signals.title: Set index on an expression: LOGICAL_ERROR "Unexpected return type from equals" when the query's expression has a Nullable operand
signals.text: ### Describe what's wrong A `SELECT` whose `WHERE` matches a `set` skip index defined on an **expression** fails with `LOGICAL_ERROR` (code 49) when the query's copy of that expression has a `Nullable` operand: ``` Unexpected return type from equals. Expected Nullable(UInt8). Got UInt8. ``` The query is valid and should return rows. In builds with assertions enabled (CI stress, debug and sanitizer jobs) the same condition aborts the server instead of raising an exception. The `Nullable` operand only has to be *constant-foldable* — `nullIf(19, 0)`, `toNullable(19)`, a scalar subquery, or `materialize(toNullable(19))` all trigger it. ### Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Yes Verified on the official release binary `26.8.1.727` (and on a `master` debug build at `5f546ba6a75338a639903081748dfb7c0fdaf231`, where it aborts rather than raising an exception). ### How to reproduce ```sql CREATE TABLE t0 (t UInt32, INDEX t_set t % 19 TYPE set(4) GRANULARITY 1) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple() SETTINGS index_granularity = 2; INSERT INTO t0 SELECT number FROM numbers(100); SELECT count() FROM t0 WHERE t % nullIf(19, 0) = 16; ``` No non-default settings beyond the `index_granularity = 2` in the `CREATE TABLE`. Reproduces via `clickhouse local` and against a server. The control case behaves correctly — removing only the `Nullable` wrapper returns `5`: ```sql SELECT count() FROM t0 WHERE t % 19 = 16; -- 5, as expected ``` `index_granularity = 2` matters only because it keeps each granule within the index's `set(4)` capacity. At the default granularity the single granule overflows `set(4)` and stores nothing, so `MergeTreeIndexConditionSet::getPossibleGranules` early-returns the whole range and never evaluates the condition. All of these fail the same way: ```sql SELECT count() FROM t0 WHERE t % toNullable(19) = 16; SELECT count() FROM t0 WHERE t % (SELECT toNullable(19)) = 16; SELECT count() FROM t0 WHERE t % nullIf(19, 0) = 16; SELECT count() FROM t0 WHERE t % materialize(toNullable(19)) = 16; ``` ### Expected behavior The query returns `5`, as the equivalent query without the `Nullable` operand does. ### Error message and/or stacktrace On release `26.8.1.727`: ``` Code: 49. DB::Exception: Unexpected return type from equals. Expected Nullable(UInt8). Got UInt8. Action: FUNCTION equals(modulo(t, 19) :: 0, 16 :: 1) -> equals(modulo(t, 19), 16) Nullable(UInt8) : 3, input block structure:modulo(t, 19) UInt8 UInt8(size = 100), 16 UInt8 Const(size = 100, UInt8(size = 1)): while executing 'FUNCTION equals(modulo(t, 19) :: 0, 16 :: 1) -> equals(modulo(t, 19), 16) Nullable(UInt8) : 3': While executing MergeTreeSelect(pool: ReadPoolInOrder, algorithm: InOrder). (LOGICAL_ERROR) ``` On a debug build, the relevant frames: ``` src/Common/Exception.cpp:60:5: DB::abortOnFailedAssertion(...) src/Interpreters/ExpressionActions.cpp:696:27: DB::executeAction(...) src/Interpreters/ExpressionActions.cpp:837:13: DB::ExpressionActions::execute(...) src/Interpreters/ExpressionActions.cpp:1003:5: DB::ExpressionActions::execute(...) src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeIndexSet.cpp:485:14: DB::MergeTreeIndexConditionSet::getPossibleGranules(...) src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataSelectExecutor.cpp:2681:83: DB::MergeTreeDataSelectExecutor::filterMarksUsingIndex(...) src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataSelectExecutor.cpp:1161:70: DB::MergeTreeDataSelectExecutor::filterPartsByPrimaryKeyAndSkipIndexes(...) ``` ### Related issues and pull requests Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113233 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/89802 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/105552 ### Additional context **Root cause.** Note that the failing action reads `equals(modulo(t, 19), 16)` — the `Nullable` operand is absent from it. That is the bug: 1. `MergeTreeIndexConditionSet` rebuilds the predicate into a small `ActionsDAG` to run against the granule block (`MergeTreeIndexSet.cpp:567` `traverseDAG` → `MergeTreeIndexSet.cpp:625` `atomFromDAG`). 2. `nullIf(19, 0)` is constant-foldable, so `getColumnName` renders the subtree as `modulo(t, 19)`, colliding with the index expression's name. `atomFromDAG` matches that name against `key_columns` and replaces the **whole** `modulo(...)` subtree with a single input bound to the granule column (`MergeTreeIndexSet.cpp:659`), discarding the `Nullable` operand. 3. The enclosing `equals` is re-added with `result_dag.addFunction(node.function_base, children, {})` (`MergeTreeIndexSet.cpp:682`), reusing the query-side resolved `IFunctionBase`. `ActionsDAG::addFunctionImpl` (`ActionsDAG.cpp:500`) takes the declared `result_type` verbatim from `function_base->getResultType()` — `Nullable(UInt8)` — while preparing the executable against the *new* arguments. Declared type and executed function now come from different resolutions. 4. `ExpressionActions::execute` binds inputs by name only, with no type check (`ExpressionActions.cpp:815`), so the granule supplies its non-`Nullable` `UInt8` column. `equals` returns `UInt8`, which no longer matches the declared `Nullable(UInt8)`, and `executeAction` raises at `ExpressionActions.cpp:695`. In short: the name-based key-column substitution erases the operand that made the expression `Nullable`, while the reused `function_base` still declares the `Nullable` return type. A fix would re-resolve the function against the granule-side argument types when rebuilding the DAG, rather than copying `function_base` and its stale return type onto a block whose types were never checked against it. Requiring the name match to also agree on type would close the same hole. **Why this does not affect a `set` index on a plain column.** With `INDEX i0 c0 TYPE set(4)` and `WHERE c0 = toNullable(16)` there is no exception: the `Nullable` operand is the comparison constant, outside the index expression, so it survives as an argument and execution genuinely produces `Nullable(UInt8)`. The defect needs the nullability *inside* the indexed expression. **CI impact.** This is the source of the `Logical error: Unexpected return type from A. Expected B. Got C. Action: (STID: 1611-4523)` bucket tracked in #113233 — 14 occurrences in the last 90 days across unrelated pull requests and every build configuration (`amd_debug`, `amd_tsan`, `amd_msan`, `amd_asan_ubsan`, `arm_tsan`, `arm_msan`, `arm_release`, `arm_asan_ubsan`, serverfuzz), plus direct `master` runs. In CI it surfaces through `tests/queries/0_stateless/01786_explain_merge_tree.sh`, whose table carries `INDEX t_set t % 19 TYPE set(4) GRANULARITY 2`, once the AST fuzzer wraps the modulus in a `Nullable` expression. #89802 is the same assertion at the same site but a different trigger (a materialized view declaring a `Nullable` column over non-`Nullable` storage). Its reproducer runs clean on current `master`, and the pull request that closed it, #105552, only added a regression test — so this path was never covered. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Resolved by: #113244 - Merged into: `26.8.1.1673` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Server shutdown hangs forever when a backup is blocked on unresponsive I/O
signals.text: 🕵️ ### Describe the situation A single `SIGTERM` never completes if a `BACKUP` is in flight and its I/O does not return. The server closes its listening sockets, then blocks in `BackupsWorker::wait()` — an unbounded `condition_variable::wait` with no timeout and no shutdown escape — and stays there indefinitely. Only a *second* signal (or `SIGKILL`) ends the process. **Both** shutdown branches reach the same wait, so no server setting avoids it: - `shutdown_wait_backups_and_restores = 1` (default) → [`waitAllBackupsAndRestores()`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/programs/server/Server.cpp#L3743) → `waitAll()` (BackupsWorker.cpp:1496) → `wait()` (BackupsWorker.cpp:1475) - `shutdown_wait_backups_and_restores = 0` → [`cancelAllBackupsAndRestores()`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/programs/server/Server.cpp#L3745) → `cancelAll(wait_ = true)` (BackupsWorker.cpp:1547) → the *same* `wait()` `cancelAll` requests cancellation and then waits for the operation to reach a final status. A thread parked in a socket read that never returns never observes the cancellation, so "cancel on shutdown" blocks exactly as long as "wait on shutdown" does. The blocking call is `status_changed.wait(lock, pred)` at [BackupsWorker.cpp:1479](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/src/Backups/BackupsWorker.cpp#L1479). It has no `wait_for`, and its predicate consults only the operation status — never a shutdown-requested flag — so nothing can wake it while the operation is stuck. This is not hypothetical: it is how ClickHouse behaves under any supervisor that sends one `SIGTERM` and then force-kills — `systemd`, `docker stop`, and the integration-test framework's `stop_clickhouse()` (30s, then `SIGKILL`) all do this. The result is a server that is always hard-killed instead of shutting down, losing whatever a clean shutdown does. ### How to reproduce * ClickHouse version: **26.8.1.1384** (also observed on 26.8.1.1 in CI) * Non-default settings: none required (the default `shutdown_wait_backups_and_restores = 1` is enough; the repro below also shows `0` fails the same way) Any destination that accepts a connection and never answers will do. A black-hole TCP listener standing in for S3 is the simplest: ```python # blackhole.py — accept connections, never reply import socket, sys srv = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) srv.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1) srv.bind(("127.0.0.1", int(sys.argv[1]))); srv.listen(128) held = [] while True: conn, _ = srv.accept() held.append(conn) # hold it open, send nothing ``` ```bash python3 blackhole.py 18999 & clickhouse-server --config-file=config.xml & # plain single-node config clickhouse-client -q "CREATE TABLE t (k UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY k" clickhouse-client -q "INSERT INTO t SELECT number FROM numbers(100000)" # Start a backup that can never finish: the endpoint accepts and never responds, # and the timeouts are long enough that the request stays in flight. clickhouse-client -q " BACKUP TABLE t TO S3('http://127.0.0.1:18999/bucket/backup1', 'key', 'secret') SETTINGS async = 1" \ --s3_request_timeout_ms=3600000 --s3_connect_timeout_ms=3600000 --s3_retry_attempts=1000 clickhouse-client -q "SELECT status FROM system.backups" # CREATING_BACKUP kill -TERM $(pgrep -x clickhouse-server) # one graceful SIGTERM ``` **Expected:** the server shuts down, abandoning or cancelling the stuck backup. **Actual:** it never exits. Still running after 2 minutes (and indefinitely): ``` <Information> BaseDaemon: Received termination signal (Terminated) <Debug> Application: Received termination signal. <Information> Application: Closed all listening sockets. <Information> BackupsWorker: Waiting for running backups and restores to finish <Information> BackupsWorker: Waiting backup S3('http://127.0.0.1:18999/bucket/backup1', 'key', '[HIDDEN]') to complete ``` Main thread: ``` #9 std::condition_variable::wait<BackupsWorker::wait(...)::$_0> #10 DB::BackupsWorker::wait src/Backups/BackupsWorker.cpp:1479 #11 DB::BackupsWorker::waitAll src/Backups/BackupsWorker.cpp:1512 #12 DB::Context::waitAllBackupsAndRestores src/Interpreters/Context.cpp:4197 #13 DB::Server::main ... $_24 programs/server/Server.cpp:3649 #15 BasicScopeGuard<...>::~BasicScopeGuard base/base/scope_guard.h:50 ``` Only a second signal ends it: ``` <Information> BaseDaemon: Received second termination signal (Terminated). Immediately terminate. ``` #### `shutdown_wait_backups_and_restores = 0` does not help Setting it and repeating the steps produces the same hang, one frame different: ``` <Information> BackupsWorker: Cancelling running backups and restores <Information> BackupsWorker: Cancelling backup S3('http://127.0.0.1:18999/bucket/backup2', 'key', '[HIDDEN]') ``` ``` #10 DB::BackupsWorker::wait src/Backups/BackupsWorker.cpp:1479 #11 DB::BackupsWorker::cancelAll src/Backups/BackupsWorker.cpp:1567 #12 DB::Context::cancelAllBackupsAndRestores src/Interpreters/Context.cpp:4203 #13 DB::Server::main ... $_24 programs/server/Server.cpp:3651 ``` Still running after 60s. So there is currently **no configuration** under which a graceful shutdown completes while a backup is stuck in a non-responsive I/O call. ### How it was found A fuzzer run on a 3-node cluster, where `BACKUP ... ON CLUSTER` / `RESTORE ... ON CLUSTER` were issued while nodes and ZooKeeper were being killed and restarted. One node never shut down and had to be force-killed; its main thread was in the same `BackupsWorker::waitAll()` frame. The single-node repro above removes the cluster, Keeper, and the fuzzer, and reduces it to "one backup whose I/O does not return". ### Suggested direction Either would fix it; the first is the smaller change: 1. Give the shutdown path a bounded wait — `status_changed.wait_for(...)` with a deadline (a new `shutdown_wait_backups_and_restores_timeout`, or reuse `shutdown_wait_unfinished`), and proceed with shutdown when it expires. 2. Make the predicate shutdown-aware, so `cancelAll` genuinely stops waiting once cancellation has been requested rather than waiting for a status the stuck thread cannot publish. `cancelAll(wait_ = true)` in particular looks like it wants to be bounded: the operation has already been told to cancel, and blocking forever for it to acknowledge defeats the purpose of the `= 0` setting.

signals.title: Wrong result: optimize_trivial_count_query makes count(arrayJoin(arr)) return the table's row count instead of the number of array elements
signals.text: ### Company or project name _No response_ ### Describe what's wrong - With the default `optimize_trivial_count_query = 1`, `SELECT count(arrayJoin(arr)) FROM t` returns the number of rows in the table instead of the number of array elements. - arrayJoin is a row-multiplying operator, so the aggregate must observe the post-expansion stream. The trivial-count optimization replaces the entire table read with a stored row counter and never evaluates count's argument, so the ARRAY JOIN expansion is silently dropped. No error, no warning. - The optimization rests on the premise "the number of rows the aggregate sees equals the number of rows stored in the table." That holds for `count()`, `count(1)` and `count(non_nullable_col)`, but arrayJoin breaks it, and nothing in the guard list checks for it. ### Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Yes ### How to reproduce - https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/a93a2cb4-e0f1-450b-a97e-0acef509da3b ``` ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬────────┬──────────┐ │ Query │ Result │ Correct? │ ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────┼──────────┤ │ count(arrayJoin(A)) │ 2 │ ✗ │ ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────┼──────────┤ │ count(arrayJoin(A)) SETTINGS optimize_trivial_count_query = 0 │ 5 │ ✓ │ ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────┼──────────┤ │ count(*) FROM (SELECT arrayJoin(A) ...) │ 5 │ ✓ │ ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────┼──────────┤ │ sum(length(A)) │ 5 │ ✓ │ └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴────────┴──────────┘ ``` ### Expected behavior - The `count(arrayJoin(A))` should return the total number of array elements across all rows, equivalent to sum(length(A)). ### Error message and/or stacktrace _No response_ ### Related issues and pull requests _No response_ ### Additional context _No response_ <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Resolved by: #115227 - Merged into: `26.8.1.1681` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Missing comma separating quota intervals silently drops the preceding interval(s)
signals.text: ```sql CREATE QUOTA q FOR INTERVAL 1 MINUTE MAX queries = 1 FOR INTERVAL 1 HOUR MAX queries = 100 TO u SHOW CREATE QUOTA q -- > FOR INTERVAL 1 hour MAX queries = 100 ``` Looks like it should be a parse error Works fine with a separating comma: ```sql CREATE QUOTA q FOR INTERVAL 1 MINUTE MAX queries = 1, FOR INTERVAL 1 HOUR MAX queries = 100 TO u SHOW CREATE QUOTA q -- > FOR INTERVAL 1 minute MAX queries = 1, FOR INTERVAL 1 hour MAX queries = 100 ``` Used version 26.7.1.1 <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Resolved by: #115320 - Merged into: `26.8.1.1679` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Weighted interpolating quantiles still route decimals through Float64
signals.text: ### Describe what's wrong **`quantileInterpolatedWeighted`, `quantileExactWeightedInterpolated` and their plural forms return values outside the input range for `Decimal*`/`DateTime64` inputs near the type limits. `quantileInterpolatedWeighted(x, 1)` over `Decimal(18,0)` values 999999999999999998/999999999999999999 returns 1000000000000000000 — not in the data and not representable in `Decimal(18,0)`. On `Decimal128` even the level-0 and level-1 quantiles return 99999999999999997752612184630461283328, which is below the minimum of the data.** - **Root cause:** Both siblings widen the decimal native value to `Float64` before interpolating and cast back. `Int64`/`Int128`/`Int256` values near their limits collapse onto the same `Float64` and the cast back lands outside the source range — the exact defect this PR removed from `QuantileReservoirSampler::get` (AggregateFunctionQuantile.cpp:59) by adding `ReservoirSampler::quantileInterpolatedDecimal`. The `NO_SANITIZE_UNDEFINED` on `interpolate` suppresses the sanitizer report but not the wrong value. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `createAggregateFunctionQuantile` dispatches `Decimal32/64/128/256` and `DateTime64` (AggregateFunctionQuantileInterpolatedWeighted.cpp:343-347, AggregateFunctionQuantileExactWeighted.cpp:423-427) -> `QuantileInterpolatedWeighted::getImpl`/`getManyImpl` -> `interpolate` (:318), and `QuantileExactWeighted::getInterpolatedImpl`/`getManyInterpolatedImpl` (:271, :294) -> `static_cast<typename Value::NativeType>(Float64)`. **Affected locations:** - [`src/AggregateFunctions/AggregateFunctionQuantileInterpolatedWeighted.cpp:318`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8b9c617362bf7/src/AggregateFunctions/AggregateFunctionQuantileInterpolatedWeighted.cpp#L318) — `interpolate` widens `lower_value`/`value_diff` to `Float64` and casts the result back to `UnderlyingType` - [`src/AggregateFunctions/AggregateFunctionQuantileExactWeighted.cpp:271`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8b9c617362bf7/src/AggregateFunctions/AggregateFunctionQuantileExactWeighted.cpp#L271) — `getInterpolatedImpl`: `Value(static_cast<typename Value::NativeType>(res))` where `res` is the `Float64` interpolation - [`src/AggregateFunctions/AggregateFunctionQuantileExactWeighted.cpp:294`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8b9c617362bf7/src/AggregateFunctions/AggregateFunctionQuantileExactWeighted.cpp#L294) — same cast in `getManyInterpolatedImpl`, used by `quantilesExactWeightedInterpolated` **Impact:** Wrong quantile values for `Decimal64`/`Decimal128`/`Decimal256`/`DateTime64` columns holding values near the type limits. The returned value can exceed the declared precision of the result type (`1000000000000000000` in a `Decimal(18,0)` result, a 77-digit value in a `Decimal(76,0)` result), which then propagates into arithmetic and comparisons downstream. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `8b9c617362bf7`). ### How to reproduce [▶ Run on ClickHouse Fiddle](https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/21f04efc-97c9-4de3-a820-cca86b516bcd) <details> <summary>Reproducer</summary> ```sql -- Test: weighted interpolating quantiles of decimal-backed values near the type limits must stay -- inside the input range instead of collapsing through Float64. SELECT quantileInterpolatedWeighted(x, 1), quantileExactWeightedInterpolated(x, 1) FROM (SELECT toDecimal64(if(number % 2 = 0, '999999999999999999', '999999999999999998'), 0) AS x FROM numbers(100)); SELECT quantilesInterpolatedWeighted(0, 0.5, 1)(x, 1), quantilesExactWeightedInterpolated(0, 0.5, 1)(x, 1) FROM (SELECT toDecimal128(if(number % 2 = 0, '99999999999999999999999999999999999999', '99999999999999999999999999999999999998'), 0) AS x FROM numbers(100)); SELECT quantileInterpolatedWeighted(x, 1), quantileExactWeightedInterpolated(x, 1) FROM (SELECT fromUnixTimestamp64Nano(if(number % 2 = 0, 9223372036854775807, 9223372036854775806), 'UTC') AS x FROM numbers(100)); ``` </details> ### Expected behavior ``` 999999999999999998 999999999999999998 [99999999999999999999999999999999999998,99999999999999999999999999999999999998,99999999999999999999999999999999999999] [99999999999999999999999999999999999998,99999999999999999999999999999999999998,99999999999999999999999999999999999999] 2262-04-11 23:47:16.854775806 2262-04-11 23:47:16.854775806 ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` 1000000000000000000 1000000000000000000 [99999999999999997752612184630461283328,99999999999999997752612184630461283328,99999999999999997752612184630461283328] [99999999999999997752612184630461283328,99999999999999997752612184630461283328,99999999999999997752612184630461283328] 2262-04-11 23:47:16.854775807 2262-04-11 23:47:16.854775807 ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> Give both siblings the same exact-domain interpolation the PR added for the reservoir path: interpolate on the native integer type (or `cpp_int`) instead of `Float64`. For `QuantileExactWeighted` that means an `is_decimal` overload of `quantileInterpolated` returning `UnderlyingType`; for `QuantileInterpolatedWeighted`, an exact-rational version of `interpolate`. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - `quantileExactWeightedInterpolated`'s cast at :271/:294 is not annotated `NO_SANITIZE_UNDEFINED` (only the inner `quantileInterpolated` at :362 is), so for `DateTime64` near `Int64` max the cast itself is UB and should also trip UBSan builds — the same signal that found the original bug. Found during automated review of [PR #114919](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114919). Severity P2 · Finding `h_pr114919_001` </details> cc @alexey-milovidov (from #114919)

signals.title: typeIsSigned omits Time/Time64: JIT zero-extends negative Time to Time64
signals.text: ### Describe what's wrong **`if`/`multiIf`/`CASE` that mixes a `Time` and a `Time64` operand returns a garbage, max-clamped value for negative `Time` inputs once the expression is JIT compiled. `SELECT if(number % 2 = 0, toTime('-100:00:00'), toTime64('50:00:00', 3)) FROM numbers(2)` yields `999:59:59.000` instead of `-100:00:00.000`. With `compile_expressions=0` the same query is correct. Both settings are on by default (`compile_expressions=true`, `min_count_to_compile_expression=3`), so a repeated query flips to the wrong answer on its 4th execution.** - **Root cause:** `typeIsSigned` (`[`src/DataTypes/Native.cpp:32-34`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8b9c617362bf7/src/DataTypes/Native.cpp#L32-L34)`) enumerates `isInt() || isFloat() || isEnum() || isDate32() || isDecimal() || isDateTime64()` and never adds `isTime()` / `isTime64()`. `WhichDataType::isDecimal()` (`[`src/DataTypes/IDataType.h:407`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8b9c617362bf7/src/DataTypes/IDataType.h#L407)`) covers only `Decimal32/64/128/256`, which is exactly why `isDateTime64()` had to be spelled out — the two time types were missed. `canBeNativeType` (`[`src/DataTypes/Native.cpp:53-59`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8b9c617362bf7/src/DataTypes/Native.cpp#L53-L59)`) does accept `isTime()` and `isTime64()`, so both reach the JIT and are widened with a zero-extend: `Time` -360000 (`Int32`) becomes 4294607296 before the x1000 scale multiply. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `FunctionIf::compileImpl` -> `nativeCast(b, {Time value, DataTypeTime}, DataTypeTime64)` -> `[`src/DataTypes/Native.cpp:180`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8b9c617362bf7/src/DataTypes/Native.cpp#L180)` (scale differs) or `:205` (scale equal) -> `b.CreateIntCast(value, i64, typeIsSigned(*from_type))` -> `typeIsSigned` at `[`src/DataTypes/Native.cpp:30`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8b9c617362bf7/src/DataTypes/Native.cpp#L30)`. **Affected locations:** - [`src/DataTypes/Native.cpp:32`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8b9c617362bf7/src/DataTypes/Native.cpp#L32) — typeIsSigned type list — missing isTime()/isTime64() - [`src/DataTypes/Native.cpp:180`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8b9c617362bf7/src/DataTypes/Native.cpp#L180) — scale-conversion widening cast for DateTime/Time family uses typeIsSigned - [`src/DataTypes/Native.cpp:205`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8b9c617362bf7/src/DataTypes/Native.cpp#L205) — generic integer-to-integer nativeCast uses typeIsSigned - [`src/DataTypes/Native.cpp:55`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8b9c617362bf7/src/DataTypes/Native.cpp#L55) — canBeNativeType admits isTime()/isTime64() **Impact:** Silent wrong results for any query that JIT-compiles a `Time`-to-`Time64` widening and can see a negative `Time` (a clock reading before midnight — `Time` is a signed second count). Reachable with stock settings via `if`, `multiIf` and `CASE` over mixed `Time`/`Time64` operands. The value is not merely off — it lands past the type maximum and prints clamped at `999:59:59`. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `8b9c617362bf7`). ### How to reproduce [▶ Run on ClickHouse Fiddle](https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/f323b20a-7a5f-4c00-96ce-23bef7bed244) <details> <summary>Reproducer</summary> ```sql -- no-fasttest: JIT compilation is not available in fasttest -- Regression test for https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/96619 -- When JIT-compiling expressions that convert DateTime to DateTime64, -- the scale multiplier was not applied, causing the value to be -- reinterpreted instead of converted (e.g., seconds treated as milliseconds). DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t; SET compile_expressions = 1, min_count_to_compile_expression = 0; SELECT '--- DateTime to DateTime64 via multiIf ---'; SELECT multiIf( number = 0, toNullable(toDateTime('2001-02-03 04:05:06')), number = 1, toNullable(toDateTime('2001-02-03 04:05:06')), '1970-01-01 00:00:00'::Nullable(DateTime64(3)) ) FROM numbers(2); SELECT '--- DateTime to DateTime64 via if ---'; SELECT if( number % 2 = 0, toNullable(toDateTime('2001-02-03 04:05:06')), '1970-01-01 00:00:00'::Nullable(DateTime64(3)) ) FROM numbers(2); SELECT '--- CASE expression ---'; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t; CREATE TABLE t (date1 Nullable(DateTime), date2 Nullable(DateTime)) ENGINE = Memory; INSERT INTO t(date1, date2) VALUES ('2001-02-03 04:05:06', NULL); SELECT CASE WHEN date2 IS NOT NULL THEN date2 WHEN date1 IS NOT NULL THEN date1 ELSE '1970-01-01 00:00:00'::Nullable(DateTime64(3)) END FROM t; DROP TABLE t; SELECT '--- Time to Time64 via if ---'; SELECT if(number % 2 = 0, toTime('-100:00:00'), toTime64('50:00:00', 3)) FROM numbers(2) ORDER BY number; SELECT '--- Time to Time64 via multiIf ---'; SELECT multiIf(number % 2 = 0, toTime('-100:00:00'), toTime64('50:00:00', 3)) FROM numbers(2) ORDER BY number; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t; ``` </details> ### Expected behavior ``` --- Time to Time64 via if --- -100:00:00.000 50:00:00.000 --- Time to Time64 via multiIf --- -100:00:00.000 50:00:00.000 ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` --- Time to Time64 via if --- 999:59:59.000 50:00:00.000 --- Time to Time64 via multiIf --- 999:59:59.000 50:00:00.000 ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> Add `|| data_type.isTime() || data_type.isTime64()` to `typeIsSigned` at `[`src/DataTypes/Native.cpp:32-34`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8b9c617362bf7/src/DataTypes/Native.cpp#L32-L34)`. Both are signed (`Int32` / `Decimal64`-derived) and both are already accepted by `canBeNativeType`. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - `src/DataTypes/Native.cpp:201` (`typeIsSigned ? CreateSIToFP : CreateUIToFP`) reads the same oracle, so a compiled `Time64`-to-float cast would be wrong the same way. I could not construct a JIT-compiled float conversion from `Time64` in SQL, so this arm is unproven — the `typeIsSigned` fix covers it regardless. Found during automated review of [PR #114168](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114168). Severity P1 · Finding `h_pr114168_001` </details> cc @groeneai @Manerone @alexey-milovidov (from #114168)

signals.title: QueryRunner pool queue_size overflows on num_threads + max_queue_size
signals.text: ### Describe what's wrong **A `QueryRunner` table created with a very large `max_queue_size` silently runs almost none of the inserted queries. With `threads = 4, max_queue_size = 18446744073709551615`, an INSERT of 100 queries executes 4 of them and discards 96; the INSERT itself reports success and the client sees no error.** - **Root cause:** `num_threads_ + max_queue_size_` at [`src/Storages/StorageQueryRunner.cpp:337`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/4b0cd9998ab10/src/Storages/StorageQueryRunner.cpp#L337) is unchecked `UInt64` arithmetic, and `max_queue_size` is validated only for `>= 1` (`:898`). For `max_queue_size > 2^64 - 1 - num_threads` the sum wraps, turning the largest requested queue into the smallest possible one. The result is also non-monotonic in `threads`: with `threads = 1` the sum wraps to exactly 0, which the pool interprets as `unlimited`, while `threads = 4` yields a capacity of 4. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `QueryRunnerDispatcher` ctor (`[`src/Storages/StorageQueryRunner.cpp:337`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/4b0cd9998ab10/src/Storages/StorageQueryRunner.cpp#L337)`) passes `num_threads_ + max_queue_size_` as the `ThreadPool` `queue_size` -> `ThreadPoolImpl` ctor (`[`src/Common/ThreadPool.cpp:311`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/4b0cd9998ab10/src/Common/ThreadPool.cpp#L311)`) stores `queue_size_ ? std::max(queue_size_, max_threads) : 0` -> `scheduleImpl` admits a job only while `scheduled_jobs < queue_size` (`[`src/Common/ThreadPool.cpp:465`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/4b0cd9998ab10/src/Common/ThreadPool.cpp#L465)`) -> `QueryRunnerDispatcher::submit` (`:345`) logs and drops everything else. **Affected locations:** - [`src/Storages/StorageQueryRunner.cpp:337`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/4b0cd9998ab10/src/Storages/StorageQueryRunner.cpp#L337) — queue_size argument passed to the ThreadPool constructor - [`src/Storages/StorageQueryRunner.cpp:898`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/4b0cd9998ab10/src/Storages/StorageQueryRunner.cpp#L898) — max_queue_size validated only for a lower bound - [`src/Common/ThreadPool.cpp:311`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/4b0cd9998ab10/src/Common/ThreadPool.cpp#L311) — queue_size member init; 0 means unlimited **Impact:** Queries handed to a `QueryRunner` table are silently discarded. The INSERT succeeds, `SYSTEM WAIT QUERY RUNNER` returns immediately, and the only trace is a rate-limited server-log line. In `mode = 'synchronous'` the INSERT also returns success for queries that never ran. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `4b0cd9998ab10`). ### How to reproduce ```sql -- A very large 'max_queue_size' must not shrink the queue. DROP TABLE IF EXISTS runner_log; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS runner_huge_queue; CREATE TABLE runner_log (n UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY n; CREATE TABLE runner_huge_queue (query String) ENGINE = QueryRunner SETTINGS threads = 4, max_queue_size = 18446744073709551615; INSERT INTO runner_huge_queue SELECT format('INSERT INTO {}.runner_log VALUES ({})', currentDatabase(), number) FROM numbers(100); SYSTEM WAIT QUERY RUNNER runner_huge_queue; SELECT count() = 100 FROM runner_log; DROP TABLE runner_huge_queue; DROP TABLE runner_log; ``` ### Expected behavior ``` 1 ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` 0 (server log) <Error> StorageQueryRunner (test_d9y1d0h3v9v4.runner_huge_queue): Cannot schedule the query (max_queue_size = 18446744073709551615), discarding it ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> Clamp instead of adding: pass `std::min<UInt64>(max_queue_size_, SOME_MAX - num_threads_) + num_threads_`, or bound `max_queue_size` in `registerStorageQueryRunner` next to the existing `max_queue_size < 1` check the way `threads` is bounded to 1024. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - The same unchecked sum makes the behaviour non-monotonic: `threads = 1, max_queue_size = 18446744073709551615` wraps to 0 and yields an unlimited queue (verified: all 100 queries ran), while `threads = 4` with the same setting yields a capacity of 4. Found during automated review of [PR #114522](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114522). Severity P2 · Finding `h_pr114522_001` </details> cc @mstetsyuk @azat (from #114522)
signals.author: clickgapai

signals.title: Uncompressed Keeper snapshots are written as 0-byte files; node cannot restart
signals.text: ### Describe what's wrong **With `compress_snapshots_with_zstd_format=false`, every snapshot Keeper writes to a local disk is 0 bytes although it logs `Created persistent snapshot N`. On the next restart Keeper dies with `Failure to load from latest snapshot ... Cannot read all data. Bytes read: 0 ... Manual intervention is necessary for recovery. Problematic snapshot can be removed but it will lead to data loss (CORRUPTED_DATA)`.** - **Root cause:** In the non-zstd branch the file buffer is wrapped BY REFERENCE (`std::make_unique<CompressedWriteBuffer>(*writer)`), so finalizing `compressed_writer` (:903) only pushes bytes into `writer`'s in-memory buffer; `compressed_writer->sync()` (:906) is the base no-op for that class and `writer.reset()` (:910) destroys the file buffer without `finalize`/`next`, discarding everything. The zstd branch passes ownership (`wrapWriteBufferWithCompressionMethod(std::move(writer), ...)`), so finalize/sync propagate — which is why only the uncompressed path is broken. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `KeeperStateMachine::create_snapshot` -> `writeSnapshotToDisk` -> `KeeperSnapshotManager::writeSnapshotFile` (KeeperStateMachine.cpp:1027, local-disk branch) -> KeeperSnapshotManager.cpp:896. **Affected locations:** - [`src/Coordination/KeeperSnapshotManager.cpp:896`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/ac58c4e749468/src/Coordination/KeeperSnapshotManager.cpp#L896) — non-owning CompressedWriteBuffer over the file write buffer - [`src/Coordination/KeeperSnapshotManager.cpp:910`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/ac58c4e749468/src/Coordination/KeeperSnapshotManager.cpp#L910) — writer.reset() without finalize/sync - [`src/Coordination/KeeperStateMachine.cpp:1027`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/ac58c4e749468/src/Coordination/KeeperStateMachine.cpp#L1027) — local-disk snapshots go through writeSnapshotFile **Impact:** Any Keeper/ClickHouse deployment with `compress_snapshots_with_zstd_format=false` silently writes empty snapshots. The node refuses to start after any restart and recovery requires deleting the snapshot, which ClickHouse's own message describes as data loss; a leader also has nothing usable to send to a recovering follower. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `ac58c4e749468`). ### How to reproduce ```python import pytest import helpers.keeper_utils as keeper_utils from helpers.cluster import ClickHouseCluster cluster = ClickHouseCluster(__file__) node_zstd = cluster.add_instance( "node_zstd", main_configs=["configs/keeper_zstd.xml"], stay_alive=True, with_remote_database_disk=False ) node_plain = cluster.add_instance( "node_plain", main_configs=["configs/keeper_plain.xml"], stay_alive=True, with_remote_database_disk=False ) SNAPSHOT_DIR = "/var/lib/clickhouse/coordination/snapshots" @pytest.fixture(scope="module") -- def started_cluster(): -- try: cluster.start() yield cluster -- finally: cluster.shutdown() @pytest.mark.parametrize("node_name", ["node_zstd", "node_plain"]) -- def test_snapshot_survives_restart(started_cluster, node_name): node = cluster.instances[node_name] keeper_utils.wait_until_connected(cluster, node) zk = keeper_utils.get_fake_zk(cluster, node.name) zk.create("/test_uncompressed_snapshot", b"somedata") idx = keeper_utils.send_4lw_cmd(cluster, node, cmd="csnp").strip() node.wait_for_log_line(f"Created persistent snapshot {idx} with path") sizes = node.exec_in_container(["bash", "-c", f"stat -c '%n %s' {SNAPSHOT_DIR}/snapshot_*"]).strip() print(f"{node_name} SNAPSHOT_FILES: {sizes}") node.restart_clickhouse() keeper_utils.wait_until_connected(cluster, node) zk = keeper_utils.get_fake_zk(cluster, node.name) assert zk.get("/test_uncompressed_snapshot")[0] == b"somedata" # configs/keeper_zstd.xml and configs/keeper_plain.xml are identical single-node keeper # configs (tcp_port 9181, server_id 1, local log/snapshot paths, four_letter_word_white_list *), -- # except that keeper_plain.xml adds inside <coordination_settings>: # <compress_snapshots_with_zstd_format>false</compress_snapshots_with_zstd_format> ``` ### Expected behavior ``` Both parameterizations pass: the snapshot file is non-empty for both settings and the node restarts and still serves /test_uncompressed_snapshot. ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` node_zstd SNAPSHOT_FILES: /var/lib/clickhouse/coordination/snapshots/snapshot_13_ebe6b90817820fc1.bin.zstd 440 -> PASSED node_plain SNAPSHOT_FILES: /var/lib/clickhouse/coordination/snapshots/snapshot_15_4d88ed92c255dd85.bin 0 -> FAILED (Exception: Cannot start ClickHouse, see additional info in logs) node_plain clickhouse-server.err.log: 2026.08.19 01:42:55.320161 <Error> void DB::KeeperDispatch ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> Finalize and sync the underlying file buffer in the non-zstd branch, e.g. after `compressed_writer->finalize()` add `writer->finalize(); writer->sync();` (or give the LZ4 branch ownership of `writer` the way the zstd branch does). </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - The same non-owning wrap exists at KeeperSnapshotManager.cpp:687 (`serializeSnapshotToBuffer`), but there the sink is `WriteBufferFromNuraftBuffer` whose `getBuffer()` finalizes, so that path is correct. Found during automated review of [PR #111715](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111715). Severity P1 · Finding `h_pr111715_001` </details> cc @al13n321 @antonio2368 (from #111715)

signals.title: Query cache on disk (RFC)
signals.text: On-disk configuration for query cache can be provided in addition to the already existing in-memory configuration. On-disk cache works almost independently of the in-memory cache. When data is written to the cache, it will be written to both of them (write-through). When data is searched inside the cache, it is searched in memory first, then on disk. If the data is found on disk, it will be also put in memory. Therefore, the on-disk cache can have independent configurations of max size, max elements, max element size, compression method, compression level, etc. The on-disk cache is organized in a directory with subdirectories named as first letters of the hexadecimal cache key, and files named like hexadecimal cache keys, similar to the filesystem cache. The files are removed by the eviction policy, while subdirectories aren't. It should be possible to have no in-memory cache, but only on-disk cache. The on-disk cache can be configured with custom disks (e.g., s3_plain), and allows co-locating inside the filesystem cache, similar to how it is done for temporary data on disk. The metadata (a set of keys existing in the on-disk cache) is loaded in memory at server startup, and the LRU information is maintained in memory. When the server is restarted, the information for the eviction policy (about last access times) is not preserved because it does not persist on disk. The server may additionally check (during the lookup) if the file suddenly appeared on disk - to support scenarios with a shared disk space between multiple servers. If there is an exception related to a wrong file size (empty) or a wrong checksum during reading, the cache entry should be discarded.

signals.title: Add assertions in IColumn::mutate to verify deep unique ownership of sub-columns
signals.text: Investigation for https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/99920 This is a draft PR with diagnostic assertions to help find a COW violation bug where columns stored in `HashJoin` have their `allocatedBytes()` change because internal sub-columns are modified by someone who treats immutable columns as mutable. ## What was found The bug manifests as `data->allocated_size != debug_allocated_size` exception in debug builds. Investigation narrowed it down to: 1. **Removing the single-chunk optimization** in `Squashing.cpp:70-72` fixes the bug — this optimization passes chunks through without `IColumn::mutate`, so columns remain shared with Memory engine blocks 2. The **modification happens between** `addBlockToJoin` calls — during pipeline processing of the next chunk 3. The mutation is a **reallocation** (reserve/grow), not a data write — `protect()` (mprotect) doesn't catch it 4. The assertions in this PR (`IColumn::mutate` deep ownership check) **do NOT fire** — meaning the mutation happens outside the `IColumn::mutate` path entirely. Someone treats an immutable column as mutable without going through `mutate`. ## Reproducer The test `04049_fix_hashjoin_shared_column_allocated_size` reproduces the exception in debug builds. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=100185&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/100185](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F100185+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Disable read-in-order when primary key selectivity is poor
signals.text: When the WHERE clause cannot use the primary key effectively (e.g., `LIKE '%...'`), the `optimize_read_in_order` optimization kills parallelism: each part is read by a single stream instead of many. This can make `ORDER BY` queries 4x slower than the same query without `ORDER BY`. Example on a 2.5B row table with `ORDER BY path` and `WHERE path LIKE '%stderr.log'`: - Without ORDER BY: ~9.5s - With ORDER BY (read-in-order): ~40s - With `optimize_read_in_order = 0`: ~9.6s The fix adds a runtime check in `ReadFromMergeTree::spreadMarkRanges`: if the primary key index selected more than a configurable fraction of all granules and there is no LIMIT, we fall back to parallel reading with per-stream `PartialSortingTransform` + `MergeSortingTransform`, so the output is still sorted as the `SortingStep` above expects. New setting `read_in_order_max_primary_key_ratio` controls the threshold. The default is 1.0, which preserves the previous behavior (never disable read-in-order based on primary key selectivity): the heuristic is opt-in until the default threshold is tuned against the performance report. Set it below 1.0 (e.g. 0.5) to enable the guard. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Add a new setting `read_in_order_max_primary_key_ratio` that can disable the read-in-order optimization when the primary key selectivity is poor (more than the given fraction of granules selected), falling back to parallel reading with sorting. This avoids severe parallelism loss for queries like `SELECT ... WHERE path LIKE '%...' ORDER BY path`. The default 1.0 preserves the previous behavior; set a lower value (e.g. 0.5) to enable the heuristic. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) New setting `read_in_order_max_primary_key_ratio` (Float, default 1.0): maximum ratio of selected to total primary key granules for `optimize_read_in_order` to stay enabled. When the ratio exceeds this value, read-in-order is disabled in favor of parallel reading with per-stream sorting. The default 1.0 preserves the old behavior. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=100377&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/100377](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F100377+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Parallelize read-in-order from a single part with PrefetchingConcatProcessor
signals.text: When a single MergeTree part is split into multiple streams for read-in-order, use the new `PrefetchingConcatProcessor` instead of relying on the downstream `MergingSortedTransform`. The key difference: - `MergingSortedTransform` marks all inputs as needed but only consumes from one stream at a time (for non-overlapping ranges), and each port can only buffer 1 block — so after initial prefetch, reading becomes sequential. - `PrefetchingConcatProcessor` marks all inputs as needed AND pulls data from non-current inputs into internal buffers, keeping upstream sources busy. It outputs data in strict input order (concatenation), which is correct because ranges from a single part are non-overlapping and pre-sorted. This avoids both the merge comparison overhead and the sort overhead, while enabling true parallel IO and filtering across range groups. Benchmark on 100M rows (4 threads, single part, poor PK selectivity): - Single-thread read-in-order: 1.57s - Parallel + sort (no read-in-order): 1.27s - PrefetchingConcat: 0.61s (2.6x faster) ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Improve the performance of queries that are reading in the order of the primary key. <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Changes read-in-order execution and introduces a new buffering processor in the query pipeline; incorrect gating or backpressure/buffering behavior could impact result ordering or memory usage in some MergeTree reads. > > **Overview** > **Adds `PrefetchingConcatProcessor`**: a new concat-like processor that keeps *all* inputs marked needed and buffers per-input chunks (bounded by `max_buffered_chunks`) to prefetch non-current streams while still outputting streams strictly in order. > > **Wires it into MergeTree read-in-order**: `ReadFromMergeTree` now conditionally replaces `MergingSortedTransform` with `PrefetchingConcatProcessor` when reading in ascending order from a *single part* split into multiple streams and only when there is filtering work (`PREWHERE` or row-level filter); it also adds `prefer_multiple_streams`/`setPreferMultipleStreams()` so aggregation-/distinct-in-order paths can opt out to avoid collapsing parallel streams. > > **Tests/bench coverage updated**: adds a new stateless test asserting `PrefetchingConcat` appears only for single-part reads and preserves sort order, adjusts an existing buffering test to force multi-part behavior, and adds a performance scenario guarding against regressions for filter-less `ORDER BY` reads. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit c0ba40d2f630976681024d2ac941261c4abdbe57. signals.title: Add leader election for non-replicated MergeTree on shared storage
signals.text: Add leader election for non-replicated MergeTree tables on shared object storage (currently `S3`; `Azure` is implemented but not yet enabled, pending test coverage), enabling active/standby failover without external coordination (no Keeper). Uses conditional writes (`If-Match` / `If-None-Match`) on object storage to maintain a lease file with JSON content `{"version":1,"leader_id":"...","timestamp":...}`. The leader renews its lease periodically; followers monitor and claim leadership when the lease expires. New MergeTree settings: - `leader_election` (Bool, default false) — enable leader election - `leader_election_heartbeat_interval` (Seconds, default 10) — lease renewal interval - `leader_election_session_timeout` (Seconds, default 30) — lease expiry threshold; must be at least 3x the heartbeat interval When not the leader, inserts, merges, mutations, and DDL are blocked; background data processing is skipped. Participating nodes should keep their clocks synchronized (NTP) to within `leader_election_session_timeout`; the conditional-write protocol always prevents split-brain, but excessive clock skew can cause leadership churn. Closes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/91613 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Add `leader_election` setting for non-replicated MergeTree tables on shared object storage, enabling active/standby failover using conditional writes without external coordination. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) Three new MergeTree-level settings are added: - `leader_election` (Bool) — When enabled on a non-replicated MergeTree table stored on an `S3` object storage disk (`Azure` is implemented but rejected at table creation until it has test coverage), multiple ClickHouse instances sharing the same data path will elect a single leader. Only the leader performs writes, merges, and mutations. Followers act as read-only replicas and automatically claim leadership when the current leader's lease expires. - `leader_election_heartbeat_interval` (Seconds, default 10) — How often the leader renews its lease and followers check for an expired lease. - `leader_election_session_timeout` (Seconds, default 30) — How long a lease remains valid without renewal. Must be at least 3x `leader_election_heartbeat_interval`. Example: ```sql CREATE TABLE shared_table (x UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY x SETTINGS leader_election = true, leader_election_heartbeat_interval = 10, leader_election_session_timeout = 30; ``` <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **High Risk** > High risk because it introduces new leader-election coordination and modifies core `MergeTree` write/DDL/drop and catalog cleanup paths; bugs could cause write unavailability or accidental deletion/incorrect visibility on shared storage. > > **Overview** > Adds a **Beta** `leader_election` mode for non-replicated `MergeTree` tables on shared S3/Azure, using a conditional-write lease file to ensure only one instance performs inserts/merges/mutations while followers remain read-only and can take over on failure. > > Introduces new MergeTree settings (`leader_election`, `leader_election_heartbeat_interval`, `leader_election_session_timeout`) with validation, new `MergeTreeLeaderElection*` metrics/events, and follower part-refresh + leader takeover sync to load new parts and advance block counters before enabling writes. > > Hardens destructive operations for shared-storage tables: blocks most `ALTER`/partition-mutation operations and `RENAME` under leader election, gates background processing on leadership, and updates drop/cleanup logic (`dropSkipsDataDirectoryCleanup`, `DatabaseCatalog`/`StorageTableProxy` fail-closed behavior) to avoid recursive deletion or hangs when tables are shared or cannot be materialized. Adds documentation and integration/stateless tests covering failover, metrics, validation, and rejection cases. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 78c1252915ba512bebf94a147932158e1bacecf0. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. signals.title: Fix correlated subquery + GROUP BY ROLLUP under group_by_use_nulls
signals.text: A correlated subquery references an outer column that is a GROUP BY key of an outer query under `group_by_use_nulls = 1` with `WITH ROLLUP`/`CUBE`/`GROUPING SETS`. The actual values fed into the inner subquery are post-rollup `Nullable`s, but the analyzer used to leave the inner column reference at its non-Nullable type. The planner then built CAST wrappers and aggregate functions with the original signature, and at header inference (after decorrelation replaced `PLACEHOLDER` nodes with `INPUT` nodes of the actual `Nullable` types) the precomputed wrappers raised `Logical error: 'Bad cast from type DB::ColumnNullable to DB::ColumnVector<...>'`. The minimal reproducer from issue #91119 hits `createUInt8ToBoolWrapper`: ```sql SELECT (SELECT c0) FROM (SELECT 1::Bool) t0(c0) GROUP BY c0 WITH ROLLUP SETTINGS group_by_use_nulls = 1; ``` The same surface bug class also appears for plain numeric types (modulo, plus), aggregate functions over correlated outer columns (e.g. `(SELECT anyLastOrDefault(number))`), correlated `HAVING`/`WHERE` filter steps, and `Nullable` source columns. The root cause is in `QueryAnalyzer::resolveExpressionNode`: the `nullable_group_by_keys` walk stops at the first enclosing `QUERY` scope, so the outer scope where the column was defined is never consulted for an inner correlated reference. This change makes the walk continue past the inner `QUERY` scope when the `node` is a column whose source table expression is registered in a deeper outer scope (i.e. the column is correlated). The aggregate-function exclusion is now evaluated against each scope's `expressions_in_resolve_process_stack`, so an outer scope's `nullable_group_by_keys` applies even when the inner subquery is currently inside an inner aggregate (the inner aggregate operates on the outer's already-`Nullable` values). For correlated matches the existing node is mutated in place instead of being replaced with a clone of the GROUP BY key. The same `shared_ptr` is referenced by the enclosing `QueryNode::correlated_columns` list (registered via `addCorrelatedColumn`); cloning would leave the planner's `correlated_columns_set` pointing to the original non-`Nullable` node, and `PlannerActionsVisitor::visitColumn` (which uses type-sensitive equality) would then fail to identify the projected column as correlated and skip the `PLACEHOLDER` step that the decorrelation pass replaces. Closes #91119. Closes #106377. Closes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/108931 Closes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109509 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `Bad cast` exception in correlated subqueries that reference an outer column promoted to `Nullable` by `group_by_use_nulls = 1` with `GROUP BY` `WITH ROLLUP`/`CUBE`/`GROUPING SETS`. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features)

signals.title: Fix `NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK` in `query_plan_convert_join_to_in` with `arrayJoin` JOIN key
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK` exception in `INNER JOIN ... ON arrayJoin(...) = ...` queries when `query_plan_convert_join_to_in` is enabled and the SELECT references the source array column. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- Not applicable -- bug fix, no new feature or API change. --> --- ### Problem With `SET query_plan_convert_join_to_in = 1` (off by default), the optimizer rewrites a hash `INNER JOIN ON arrayJoin(L.col) = R.col` into `[Expression("Calculate join left keys"), Filter("IN"), DelayedCreatingSets, Expression("Join output actions")]`. If the SELECT projection (or any post-JOIN expression) references the source array column `L.col` itself, or `arrayJoin(L.col)` again, the rewritten plan throws ``` Code: 10. DB::Exception: Not found column __table1.tags in block ... (NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK) ``` at execution (and at `EXPLAIN actions = 1` planning time). Minimal repro: ```sql CREATE TABLE lt (id UInt64, tags Array(String)) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id; CREATE TABLE rt (tag_id String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tag_id; INSERT INTO lt VALUES (1, ['a','b','c']), (2, ['d','e']); INSERT INTO rt VALUES ('a'), ('d'); -- Throws NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK: SELECT lt.id, lt.tags FROM lt INNER JOIN rt ON arrayJoin(lt.tags) = rt.tag_id SETTINGS query_plan_convert_join_to_in = 1; -- Same with arrayJoin in the projection -- also throws: SELECT lt.id, arrayJoin(lt.tags) FROM lt INNER JOIN rt ON arrayJoin(lt.tags) = rt.tag_id SETTINGS query_plan_convert_join_to_in = 1; ``` ### Root cause `tryConvertJoinToIn` builds `left_pre_join_actions = JoinExpressionActions::getSubDAG(<left join keys>)`. The output set is only the JOIN-key expressions — `arrayJoin(__table1.tags)` and `__table1.id` in the repro — **not** the source `__table1.tags` array column. Later, `cloneSubDAGWithHeader(output_header, JoinExpressionActions::getSubDAG(join_output_actions))` clones the post-JOIN expressions onto a new DAG seeded from `output_header`. `cloneSubDAGWithHeader` calls `mergeInplace(..., remove_dangling_inputs=true)`, which remaps `INPUT` nodes by name to the corresponding inputs in `output_header`. When `join_output_actions` references `__table1.tags` (because SELECT did), the source `__table1.tags` INPUT in `second_dag` has no match in `output_header` — `mergeInplace`'s `remove_dangling_inputs` only removes input nodes that collide with `first`'s inputs, not input nodes that have no counterpart at all. The non-INPUT nodes that depend on it (the cloned ARRAY_JOIN node when SELECT had `arrayJoin(lt.tags)`, or the column reference itself when SELECT had `lt.tags`) survive, and the resulting `ExpressionStep` cannot find the column at execution. ### Fix Decline the conversion in `tryConvertJoinToIn` whenever any input of `join_output_actions` is not among the outputs that `left_pre_join_actions` forwards. The check runs immediately after `left_pre_join_actions` / `right_pre_join_actions` are computed and **before** any plan mutation (`makeExpressionNodeOnTopOf` etc.), so the bail-out is safe — the query then runs through the normal JOIN path and produces the correct result. ```cpp { auto join_output_actions_subdag = JoinExpressionActions::getSubDAG(join_output_actions); std::unordered_set<std::string_view> forwarded_columns; for (const auto * out : left_pre_join_actions.getOutputs()) forwarded_columns.insert(out->result_name); for (const auto * input : join_output_actions_subdag.getInputs()) if (!forwarded_columns.contains(input->result_name)) return 0; } ``` The check mirrors the established `appendInputsForUnusedColumns` style (`ActionsDAG.cpp:1453-1461`), which is the idiomatic "verify every input is present in a sample block" pattern in this codebase. ### Related fixes for the same root cause This is the third bug in 12 months rooted in `mergeInplace` / `clone` of an ARRAY_JOIN-bearing DAG being merged into a context whose stream header does not provide a required INPUT column. The prior two are: - #96989 (prevention strategy: blacklist `ARRAY_JOIN` in the pushdown eligibility check). - #97239 (bail-out strategy: detect ghost `ARRAY_JOIN` after the merge and abandon the optimization). - #104785 (post-hoc cleanup strategy: snapshot the merged-in `ARRAY_JOIN` pointers and drop them after the merge via a new `ActionsDAG::removeNodes` helper). This PR follows the bail-out pattern of #97239 — `tryConvertJoinToIn` is an optional optimization, so declining the rewrite is safe and the query falls back to the regular JOIN path. A more invasive follow-up could forward the missing left-side columns through `left_pre_join_actions` so the optimization stays on even in these cases; left for a separate PR once we have evidence that real workloads hit the bail-out frequently. The setting `query_plan_convert_join_to_in` is off by default, so the bug is reachable only when explicitly enabled. ### Regression test `tests/queries/0_stateless/03918_convert_join_to_in_arrayjoin_dangling.{sql,reference}` — co-located with #96989's `03918_arrayjoin_function_with_join_and_where`. Four queries: 1. `SELECT lt.id ... INNER JOIN ... ON arrayJoin(lt.tags) = rt.tag_id` — the optimization stays on, returns the correct rows (validates the fix's "no-regression" guarantee for the cases it does not bail out on). 2. `SELECT lt.id, lt.tags ...` — before fix: NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK; after fix: correct result via the fallback JOIN path. 3. `SELECT lt.id, arrayJoin(lt.tags) ...` — same shape as (2). 4. Control: same as (3) with `query_plan_convert_join_to_in = 0`. Confirms the fallback path returns the same answer the fix produces in (3). Repro-first verified: queries (2) and (3) were observed to fail with NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK on un-fixed upstream master (`7bd0fa28146`) before the reference was locked. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1674` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Declarative function signatures, continuation of #3775
signals.text: This is an experimental continuation of [#3775 (2018)](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/3775) by @alexey-milovidov, which proposed a declarative way to describe function signatures so that argument validation and return-type inference can be driven by a small DSL instead of hand-written `getReturnTypeImpl` logic per function. ### What's in this branch A `getSignatureString()` method on `IFunction` and `IFunctionOverloadResolver`. When a function exposes a non-empty signature, the base `getReturnTypeImpl(ColumnsWithTypeAndName)` parses and applies it via a small grammar of type **matchers** (`UInt`, `Number`, `Array(T)`, `MaybeNullable(T)`, `Function((args), R)`, `T : Any` capture, …) and type **functions** (`leastSupertype`, `nativeNumber`, `aggregateFunctionReturnType(AggregateFunction(name, …))`, `subcolumnTypeOf`, `typeFromString`, `DateTime64(scale, tz)`, …). The DSL supports variadic positions (`…`), ellipsis grouping for repeated argument units (`T1, V1, …` repeats the pair), `OR` between alternatives, optional positions `[T]`, const-value capture (`const name String`), lambdas, etc. The grammar / parser / type matchers / type functions live under `src/DataTypes/FunctionSignature.h`, `FunctionSignature.cpp`, `TypeMatchers.cpp`, `TypeFunctions.cpp`. ### Coverage ~191 commits on top of master, each is a small per-family round titled `Function signatures: round N — …`. Current state on this branch: ``` SELECT count(*) AS total, countIf(signature != '') AS with_sig, round(countIf(signature != '') * 100.0 / count(*), 1) AS pct FROM system.functions WHERE NOT is_aggregate AND alias_to = '' AND origin = 'System'; 1416 1395 98.5 ``` (With \`allow_experimental_nlp_functions = 1\`; the few remaining unset ones are setting / config-gated functions like \`aiClassify\`, \`region*\`, \`synonyms\`, whose \`create\` throws unless the relevant config block / setting is present, so \`system.functions.tryGet\` returns null even though the signature is in source. With the right config + setting they all surface — verified in tmp/ test config.) Roughly: - **Authoritative** (DSL drives type-check and return type, the legacy `getReturnTypeImpl` is either gone or bypassed): higher-order array functions (`arrayMap`, `arrayFilter`, `arrayFirst*`, …), `toIntervalX`, comparison, `multiSearch*` / `multiMatch*`, vector L-norms / distances / dot product, `UUIDv7ToDateTime`, `arrayReduce` / `arrayReduceInRanges`, `reverse`, `mapKeys` / `mapValues`, `getSubcolumn`, the `least` / `greatest` resolver, paired-variadic `timeSeriesTagsToGroup` / `timeSeriesStoreTags`, … - **Documentation-only** (signature surfaced via `system.functions` but the legacy `getReturnTypeImpl` still runs because the result type uses promotion / widening / setting-dependent dispatch the current DSL can't express): arithmetic (`plus`, `minus`, `multiply`, `divide`, modulo / intDiv family), array widening (`arraySum` / `arrayCumSum*` / `arrayDifference`), `mapContains*Like`, `dateTrunc`, `toStartOfWeek`, `parseDateTime*`, `transform`, `range`, `toX` conversions, etc. There is a `signature_documentation` opt-in alongside `signature` in the binary-arithmetic, unary-arithmetic, FunctionArrayMapped, and FunctionMapToArrayAdapter families specifically so a function can advertise a signature without the DSL accidentally hijacking the legacy widening logic. ### Status Draft / experimental. - This is an experiment — I'm not asking for it to be merged. There's significant disruption (191 commits touching every function family), and the gain is mostly documentation: today only ~30% of the converted functions are actually DSL-authoritative; the rest are decorative. The arithmetic promotion matrix and the per-Op widening rules in particular would need a richer type-function vocabulary (or new matchers) before they can be expressed declaratively. - The branch has been kept rebased on master throughout and builds cleanly. I've run the stateless test suite on each round. The pre-existing-on-master test failures I hit are listed in commit messages of the rounds where I encountered them (none introduced by this work). - The original PR has been open since 2018 — this branch is intended as a concrete data point on \"what fraction of ClickHouse functions can be reasonably described by a declarative signature, and what would the DSL need to grow to cover the rest.\" That's the question I'd love feedback on. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=104948&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/104948](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F104948+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Add server setting `additional_memory_tracking_per_thread`
signals.text: Each thread accumulates up to `max_untracked_memory` (4 MiB by default) of allocations before reporting them to the server-wide `MemoryTracker`. With many threads, this unreported memory can sum to a large amount, causing the server's tracked memory usage to under-count actual consumption and leading to OOM. This PR introduces a server-level setting `additional_memory_tracking_per_thread` (default 4 MiB) and speculatively charges this amount to the server-wide `MemoryTracker` for each worker thread of a `PipelineExecutor`, including query, merge, and mutation pipelines. The global tracked memory becomes a tighter upper bound on actual consumption when `max_untracked_memory` for those workers does not exceed this setting; operators that permit a larger per-query value must raise the server setting accordingly. The reservation is charged on the server-wide (total) tracker only — deliberately not through the query's tracker chain. Query-level accounting feeds heuristics that compare memory deltas against byte thresholds (conversion of aggregation hash tables to two-level via `group_by_two_level_threshold_bytes`, spill-to-disk decisions), and phantom reservations of `num_threads * 4 MiB` trip those thresholds immediately: an earlier revision of this PR that charged the query tracker showed consistent slowdowns of GROUP BY queries in performance tests for exactly this reason. The reservation itself does not alter query-level or user-level accounting (`max_memory_usage`, `memory_usage` in `system.processes`); however, every pipeline worker flushes its pending real allocation reports before releasing its outermost reservation, so those counters and memory-based heuristics can become visible sooner while a worker yields, downscales, or completes. The speculative reservation uses the throwing path of the memory tracker, so when it would exceed the server memory limit the corresponding job is treated as failed with `MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` — the same behavior as if the job itself had exceeded the limit. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added a new server setting `additional_memory_tracking_per_thread` (default 4 MiB) which speculatively reserves this amount on the server-wide `MemoryTracker` for each worker thread of a `PipelineExecutor`, including query, merge, and mutation pipelines. When it is at least the workers' `max_untracked_memory`, it makes server-wide tracked memory a tighter upper bound on actual consumption and reduces the risk of OOM with many concurrent pipeline workers. The reservation does not alter query-level or user-level accounting, but workers flush pending real allocation reports before releasing their outermost reservation, so those counters can become visible sooner while a worker yields, downscales, or completes. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - signals.title: Reject CREATE TABLE ... CLONE AS SELECT / table function
signals.text: The `CREATE TABLE ... CLONE AS <source>` clause is intended to clone a real on-disk source table — the partition-attach step performed after table creation needs actual partitions to copy. The parser, however, also accepted `CREATE TABLE t CLONE AS SELECT ...` and `CREATE TABLE t CLONE AS <table_function>`. Neither shape has partitions to attach, so the `CLONE` keyword was silently ignored and the table was created as a plain `CREATE ... AS SELECT` with an inferred schema and `ORDER BY tuple()`. This PR rejects both shapes early in `getTablePropertiesAndNormalizeCreateQuery` with `BAD_ARGUMENTS`, so the user gets a clear error instead of silent misbehavior. It also fixes a related defect in `ASTCreateQuery::formatQueryImpl`: the `if (select)` branch did not call `add_clone_if_needed`, so an AST format round-trip silently dropped `CLONE` from `CLONE AS SELECT`. The randomized-settings injection in `clickhouse-test` round-trips queries through this formatter, which is how the gap surfaced. Fixes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/104994 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `CREATE TABLE ... CLONE AS SELECT ...` and `CREATE TABLE ... CLONE AS <table_function>` silently ignoring the `CLONE` keyword and creating a plain `CREATE ... AS SELECT` instead. These shapes are now rejected with `BAD_ARGUMENTS`. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is unchanged: this is a bug fix that brings behavior in line with the existing `CLONE AS` documentation, which only describes the `CLONE AS <table>` form. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=105004&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/105004](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F105004+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Reject compression_method argument for data lake engines
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/105644 Data lake engines (`Iceberg`, `DeltaLake`, `Hudi`, `Paimon`) accept a `compression_method` argument, but the on-disk file format (`Parquet`/`ORC`/`Avro`) already has its own internal codec. For `IcebergLocal`/`IcebergS3`/etc. the write path goes through `MultipleFileWriter::startNewFile`, which never wraps the buffer with `wrapWriteBufferWithCompressionMethod`, so the user's `compression='lzma'` is silently dropped and the on-disk file is raw `Parquet`. The read path in `StorageObjectStorageSource` still calls `chooseCompressionMethod(filename, configuration->compression_method)`, which with hint `'lzma'` ignores the `.parquet` extension and returns `CompressionMethod::Xz`, then wraps the read buffer with `LZMAInflatingReadBuffer`. The decoder sees raw Parquet bytes and fails with `LZMA_FORMAT_ERROR`. For `DeltaLake`/`Hudi`/`Paimon` the write path uses `StorageObjectStorageSink`, which does honor the outer codec, so the file round-trips inside ClickHouse, but the produced LZMA-wrapped Parquet is unreadable by external engines (Spark, Trino, etc.). Same class of silent corruption from an interoperability point of view. This change rejects any explicit `compression_method` (or `compression`) argument at fresh-definition time for any data lake configuration (`Iceberg`, `DeltaLake`, `Hudi`, `Paimon`), with a clear error pointing at the format-specific codec setting. Users who need to control file compression should use the format-specific settings such as `output_format_parquet_compression_method`. The default value pass-through is unchanged: the rejection only fires when the user explicitly supplied the argument, so unmodified `CREATE TABLE` statements continue to work. The rejection is gated on `LoadingStrictnessLevel == CREATE`, so it fires only for a fresh definition: a `CREATE TABLE`, or a data lake table function (which always loads with `CREATE`). Every other mode replays a definition that was already accepted when the table was created, and is deliberately exempt as a compatibility path so pre-fix tables still load after an upgrade: every `ATTACH` form (short-syntax `ATTACH TABLE name`, full-definition `ATTACH TABLE name FROM '<path>' (cols) ENGINE = ...`, and the server-startup replay paths `FORCE_ATTACH` / `FORCE_RESTORE`), and `SECONDARY_CREATE`, which covers both `RESTORE TABLE` and the replay of the stored `CREATE TABLE` text by `DatabaseReplicated::recoverLostReplica` (so a `Replicated` database created before this validation landed still recovers on an upgraded replica). Note that this includes a user-supplied full-definition `ATTACH`, which can therefore still persist a definition carrying `compression_method`; per review, the gate is intentionally kept simple rather than special-casing the `ATTACH` shapes. A fresh `CREATE` in a `Replicated` database is still rejected, because the initiator runs it as an initial query and therefore with `mode == CREATE`. Reproducer (no longer accepted after this patch): ```sql CREATE TABLE t0 (c0 Int) ENGINE = IcebergLocal('/var/lib/clickhouse/user_files/lakehouses/t0', 'Parquet', 'lzma'); -- Code: 36. DB::Exception: The `compression_method` argument is not -- supported by data lake engines. ... ``` ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Reject any explicit `compression_method` / `compression` argument for data lake engines (`Iceberg`, `DeltaLake`, `Hudi`, `Paimon`) at fresh-definition time. The outer compression codec was silently dropped on the Iceberg write path while still applied on read, producing files the engine could not read back. For other data lake formats it produced non-standard files unreadable by external engines. Users who need to control file compression should use the format-specific settings such as `output_format_parquet_compression_method`. Pre-existing tables persisted before this validation landed still load via `ATTACH`, server startup, `RESTORE`, and `Replicated`-database replica recovery. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features)
