signals.title: Fix LOGICAL_ERROR on runtime filter lookup before build finished
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a `LOGICAL_ERROR` exception "Trying to lookup values in runtime filter before building it was finished" during JOINs with `enable_join_runtime_filters` enabled when the join stops reading the build side early (for example `join_overflow_mode = 'break'` with a finite `max_rows_in_join` / `max_bytes_in_join`, or an empty/short-circuited right side). ### Description Found by the AST fuzzer (STID 2210-585c) and reproducible on master. A JOIN runtime filter is built on the right (build) side by N parallel `BuildRuntimeFilterTransform` streams. The filter becomes visible to `RuntimeFilterLookup::find(name)` after the FIRST stream's `finish()`, but `IRuntimeFilter::inserts_are_finished` only becomes true after the LAST stream merges its partial filter (`filters_to_merge` reaches 0). The probe (left) side applies the filter via `FunctionApplyFilter` -> `IRuntimeFilter::find()`. Normally the join's pull discipline guarantees the build side is fully consumed before the probe side runs. But when the join stops reading the build side early, `FillingRightJoinSideTransform` closes its input and the build-phase finish counter reaches `isLast()` before all N `BuildRuntimeFilterTransform` streams have called `finish()`. The probe side then calls `find()` on a filter whose `inserts_are_finished` is still false, and `IRuntimeFilter::find()` raised a `LOGICAL_ERROR`, crashing debug/sanitizer builds. The runtime filter is a best-effort optimization: correctness always comes from the JOIN itself, never from this pre-filter (`FunctionApplyFilter` already returns const-true when the filter is absent). The fix makes `find()` pass all rows through (return const-true) when the build side is not finished yet, instead of throwing. This is safe for both "contains" and "not-contains" filter polarities, since the JOIN drops the non-matching rows. `finishInsert()` is also reordered to finalize the underlying set/bloom filter before publishing `inserts_are_finished = true`, so a concurrent `find()` can never observe a half-built filter. Adds a functional test (`04337_runtime_filter_lookup_before_finished`) that drives a real JOIN pipeline with `join_overflow_mode = 'break'` and a tiny `max_bytes_in_join` over a multi-part build table, so the probe side reaches `find()` while the runtime filter is still unfinished. The query is repeated so the probabilistic race is hit with high probability; without the fix at least one repetition aborts the server, and with the fix the test passes. Report (AST fuzzer, amd_debug, targeted): https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=103322&sha=eeec76f833a27b148d130ef8f504ac362f26caef&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29

signals.title: Fix LOGICAL_ERROR on single-argument or() in JOIN ON
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Closes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112654 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Description `tryExtractCommonExpressions` in the `LogicalExpressionOptimizer` pass assumed every `or()` function node has at least two arguments and enforced it with `chassert(or_argument_nodes.size() > 1)`, aborting the server in debug/sanitizer builds. Release builds are not affected (the `chassert` is a no-op there and the query returns the correct empty result), hence no changelog entry. A single-argument `or()` can be resolved when its only argument has the `Nothing` type: `IFunctionOverloadResolver::getReturnTypeWithoutLowCardinality` short-circuits to `Nothing` for any `Nothing`-typed argument before the function's own `getReturnTypeImpl` runs, so the "at least 2 arguments" check in `FunctionAnyArityLogical` is skipped. An empty `ARRAY JOIN` makes a column `Nothing`-typed, so ```sql CREATE TABLE t1 (c0 Int) ENGINE = Memory; SELECT t1.c0 FROM t1 AS tx LEFT ARRAY JOIN [] AS a0 LEFT JOIN t1 ON or(a0 = t1.c0); ``` produced a single-argument `or()` in the `JOIN ON` expression and tripped the assert. Common-expression extraction across disjuncts is meaningless with fewer than two disjuncts, so the pass now returns without optimizing instead of asserting. The single-argument `or()` then falls through to normal `JOIN ON` validation, which rejects invalid cases with a clear error. Found by the AST fuzzer (STID 2508-3fad). Reproduced on two unrelated PRs: - AST fuzzer (amd_debug, targeted): https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=106981&sha=63804eccd611e475770d838739aebcfd894db406&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29 - AST fuzzer (arm_asan_ubsan): PR #106682, 2026-06-07. Added regression test `04327_single_argument_or_in_join_on`.

signals.title: Do not install standalone symlinks for multi-call-only subcommands
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/36588 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/36588 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Build/Testing/Packaging Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Stop installing standalone `clickhouse-<name>` symlinks for subcommands that no package ships. This removes useless work from the CMake install step without changing the produced packages. ### Description Step 1 of #36588. `ninja programs/install` copied a `clickhouse-<name>` symlink into the packaging root (`<build>/root/usr/bin/`) for every subcommand registered via `clickhouse_program_install`. nfpm builds every package strictly from the explicit `src:` entries in `packages/clickhouse-*.yaml` (no globs), and 14 of those symlinks are referenced by no manifest, so installing them only populated the staging tree. This splits the helper into: - `clickhouse_program_link(name lib)` - link the subcommand library into the multi-call binary and create the `clickhouse-<name>` symlink in the build directory (no install); - `clickhouse_program_install(name lib [aliases...])` - the same, plus install the standalone symlink (and aliases) for packaging. 14 subcommands are switched to `clickhouse_program_link`: `check-marks`, `checksum-for-compressed-block`, `disks`, `docker-init`, `git-import`, `oom-canary`, `packed-io`, `static-files-disk-uploader`, `su`, `zookeeper-dump-tree`, `zookeeper-remove-by-list`, `keeper-data-dumper`, `keeper-utils`, `keeper-bench`. The criterion is the packaging reference, not the invocation surface. Two of the 14, `clickhouse-disks` and `clickhouse-git-import`, are also symlinked by `clickhouse install` from its own `tools` list in `programs/install/Install.cpp`. That path is unaffected: it symlinks from the binary it has just copied itself, and never reads this staging tree. The build-tree symlinks and the multi-call dispatch table in `programs/main.cpp` are unchanged, so `clickhouse <name>` keeps working. Verified by configuring the tree with and without this change, everything else identical: the installed set drops exactly those 14 symlinks and gains none, and all 30 build-tree `create_symlink` commands are still generated. Packages are unaffected. Step 2 of the issue (dropping CMake `install` entirely in favour of direct build-directory paths in the packaging YAML) is a deliberate follow-up.

signals.title: Add query plan cache for complex queries (views, joins, subqueries)
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Add an experimental query plan cache supporting complex `SELECT` queries: views (including nested views), joins, `UNION`, `IN` subqueries and multiple tables over supported local table engines. When `allow_experimental_query_plan_cache = 1` and `enable_query_plan_cache = 1`, repeated identical queries skip query analysis and logical planning (the query is still parsed) while still executing against current data. `SYSTEM DROP QUERY PLAN CACHE` clears the cache; events `QueryPlanCacheHits`/`QueryPlanCacheMisses`/`QueryPlanCacheValidationMisses`/`QueryPlanCacheStaleMisses` and metrics `QueryPlanCacheBytes`/`QueryPlanCacheEntries` provide observability. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) --- ### Description An experimental **query plan cache** for `SELECT` queries that supports **complex queries** — views (including nested views), joins, `UNION`, `IN` subqueries and multiple tables over supported local table engines. It complements https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/99309, which covers single-table `MergeTree` queries with a universalize/materialize design; this PR takes a different approach to reach query shapes where planning cost is actually concentrated (deep view chains, many joins). Unlike the query result cache, a plan cache hit still executes the query: only query analysis and logical planning are skipped (the query is still parsed, since the cache key is built from the parsed AST), so hits are transactionally consistent and always see current data. #### Design On a miss, the plan is built in the planner's existing `build_logical_plan` mode (the machinery used by distributed plan shipping), with a new `SelectQueryOptions::cacheable_logical_plan` mode that makes the logical plan self-contained: - Leaf reads are storage-agnostic `ReadFromTable` placeholders for any eligible local engine. - **Views are expanded at plan time** (only `StorageView`; a materialized view stays a leaf and is read from its target table like an ordinary table), recursively in logical mode (propagated through `StorageView::readImpl` via `SelectQueryInfo::build_logical_plan`), so the cached plan embeds the analyzed view bodies instead of deferring the expensive expansion to execution. - Key-value direct-join lookup steps (`JoinStepLogicalLookup`), which bind live storages into the plan, are not used; a regular join is planned instead and the physical join algorithm is chosen at materialization. Distributed and parallel-replicas logical plans do not set this mode and are unaffected. - The plan is serialized with the standard query plan serialization and built with `compile_expressions = 0` (JIT-fused function nodes cannot be serialized; the JIT still applies when pipelines are built from the plan). Both hits and misses execute through `QueryPlan::resolveStorages`, which re-binds every leaf to a fresh storage snapshot. #### Cache key and invalidation The key is the normalized AST hash, a hash of plan-affecting settings, the current database, the user and the sorted role set. Each entry stores a **dependency fingerprint over every referenced storage**, discovered from the plan's `ReadFromTable` leaves plus an AST closure through view definitions (which also catches tables referenced only from scalar subqueries): UUID, metadata version (or a schema content hash including the view body), and the row policy hash. Every hit revalidates all dependencies and re-checks `SELECT` access, so `DROP`/`CREATE`, `ALTER`, view redefinition (including **nested** views), row policy changes and permission revocation are handled transparently. #### Eligibility - Non-deterministic functions anywhere — including inside expanded view bodies — make a query uncacheable (`arrayJoin` is exempt: it is multi-valued but pure). - Scalar subqueries are evaluated during analysis and baked into the plan as constants, so they are gated behind the opt-in setting `query_plan_cache_allow_scalar_subqueries`. - Table functions, temporary tables, system tables (except `system.one`), remote/`Merge` storages and views whose SQL security is not `INVOKER` (`DEFINER` and `NONE`) are rejected. - Plans containing steps without serialization support (e.g. window functions) execute normally and are simply not stored. #### Performance, proven on DOOMbench [DOOMbench](https://github.com/cedardb/doombench) is a DOOM-like raycasting engine implemented entirely in SQL; its `screen` query renders a frame through a deep chain of views over joins, unions, array joins and scalar subqueries. Ported to ClickHouse SQL, the workload is **query-analysis-bound**: profiling showed `IQueryTreeNode::getTreeHash` and analyzer resolution dominating, and `SELECT ... LIMIT 0` was as slow as the full query. With the plan cache (local server, single connection): | DOOMbench frame render | median | speedup | | --- | --- | --- | | cache off | 551-577 ms | — | | cache on (hit) | 227-246 ms | **2.4x** | | cache on, `max_threads = 4` | 148-176 ms | **3.3x** | On hits the analyzer cost disappears from profiles (`getTreeHash`: 25.8k samples → 174); the remaining time is genuine execution. Correctness validated on the same workload: frames are byte-identical between cache off/miss/hit, game-state mutations are visible on every cached render (HTAP freshness), nested view redefinition is picked up immediately, and `rand()` inside a view body refuses to cache. #### Notes - This PR includes the `ActionsDAG` input-constant serialization fix https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107124 as its first commit; it will be rebased once that PR is merged. - The miss path executes through the same logical-plan machinery as hits, so hit and miss behavior is identical by construction; storage-specific planning shortcuts (e.g. trivial `count()`) are not applied to cache-enabled queries. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/99309 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107124 <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=107125&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/107125](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F107125+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix wrong result for duplicate-named subquery columns wrapped in SELECT *
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106923 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a wrong result when a subquery has two output columns with the same name backed by different expressions (for example a constant column colliding with a starred column of the same name) and the subquery is wrapped in an outer `SELECT *`. Previously one column's value (often a constant) overwrote the other; for a non-matched `RIGHT`/`FULL JOIN` row this kept the constant's literal value instead of the default. ### Description Reproducer (deterministic, default settings): ```sql SELECT 1, * FROM (SELECT 2 AS x, 1) AS a RIGHT JOIN (SELECT 3 AS y) AS b ON y = x; -- 1 0 0 3 (correct: both left-side columns are defaulted on the non-matched row) SELECT * FROM (SELECT 1, * FROM (SELECT 2 AS x, 1) AS a RIGHT JOIN (SELECT 3 AS y) AS b ON y = x); -- before: 1 0 1 3 (wrong: the left subquery's constant column survives as 1) -- after: 1 0 0 3 (matches the unwrapped query) ``` Root cause: the planner addresses a subquery's output column purely by `source_alias + "." + column_name`, with no positional discriminator. When a subquery's projection has two columns with the same name, the outer `SELECT *` matcher resolves both to a single `ColumnNode`, only one column identifier is registered for that name, and the second column's value is replaced by the first. Fix: when a subquery has duplicate projection column names backed by non-equal expressions, the later occurrences are given unique internal names so the planner assigns each a distinct identifier. The original user-visible display names are preserved (the correct output legitimately has duplicate display names). Two cases are intentionally left unchanged: equal expressions with the same name (`SELECT number, number`), which collapse harmlessly, and a later explicit alias that redefines a same-named starred column (`SELECT *, expr AS c`), which is intentional shadowing (issue #14739). Found by the AST-fuzzer correctness oracle.

signals.title: Refresh TO-target materialized view columns when upstream tables are altered
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106919 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `DESCRIBE` and `SHOW CREATE TABLE` reporting stale column types for a materialized view created with `TO target` after the source or target table columns were changed with `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COLUMN`. Previously the view kept the types inferred at creation time, which also made `SELECT` from the view fail (for example with `UNKNOWN_ELEMENT_OF_ENUM`) when the new types were incompatible. The view's inferred columns are now refreshed on the upstream `ALTER`; explicit-column views keep their declared types. ### Description After an `ALTER` that changes a table's columns, the column metadata of dependent `TO`-target materialized views is refreshed when their stored columns are still in sync with the view's `SELECT` output (recomputed against the pre-`ALTER` schema). The refresh re-runs the same `SELECT`-output inference used at create time, so inferred-column views track the new upstream types while explicit-column views (`TO t (x String) ...`) and views whose columns intentionally diverge from the `SELECT` output (e.g. `SELECT 1 AS v2` over a wider target column) are left untouched. Existing tests `02931`, `01069`, `01182` keep their current behavior; new test: `04327_mv_to_target_columns_refresh_on_alter`.

signals.title: Throw a clear error when a marks file listed in checksums is missing on disk
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Improved the error message when a marks file that is listed in a data part's checksums is missing on disk. Reading such a column, or loading the part's index granularity, now raises `NO_FILE_IN_DATA_PART` naming the part, the missing file and the part's on-disk state, instead of an opaque `std::filesystem` `file_size: No such file or directory` error. ### Description `MergeTreeMarksLoader::loadMarksImpl()` derives the marks file path from the part's own checksums (`getStreamNameForColumn` only returns a stream name that is present in the part's checksums), so the file is expected to exist on disk. When it does not, `getFileSize()` throws an opaque ``` Code: 1001. DB::Exception: std::__1::filesystem::filesystem_error: filesystem error: in file_size: No such file or directory [".../<col>.cmrk2"] ``` with no indication of which part is affected or what its on-disk state is. This surfaces in the flaky integration test `test_rename_column::test_rename_distributed_parallel_insert_and_select` (Integration tests, amd_tsan; report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=100703&sha=e93ea3312f0d1107b3977560deafaa4241bd89b7&name_0=PR&name_1=Integration%20tests%20%28amd_tsan%2C%201%2F6%29 ) under heavy concurrent `RENAME COLUMN` + `INSERT` + `SELECT` load, where it is impossible to diagnose from the message alone. CIDB shows it on 3 unrelated PRs over the last 30 days and never on master, so it is a rare concurrency window rather than a single PR's regression. This PR does not fix the underlying race (which is not reproducible locally on a single host: 94/94 idle and CPU-jittered iterations passed). Instead it makes the next occurrence diagnosable: before calling `getFileSize()`, check whether the marks file exists, and if it does not, throw `NO_FILE_IN_DATA_PART` with the part name, path, columns, the files listed in the part's checksums, and the actual on-disk listing. The existence check runs only on the error path, so successful reads are unaffected. Example of the new message: ``` Code: 226. DB::Exception: Marks file 'b.cmrk2' does not exist in part 'all_1_1_0' at '.../all_1_1_0/', although it is listed in the part's checksums. Part columns: [...]. Checksums files: [a.bin, a.cmrk2, b.bin, b.cmrk2, ...]. Files on disk: [a.bin, a.cmrk2, b.bin, ...]. (NO_FILE_IN_DATA_PART) ``` A stateless test (`03810_missing_marks_file_error`) removes a column's marks file from a wide part and asserts the typed error is raised.

signals.title: Fix flaky test 02770_async_buffer_ignore
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/100391 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/106231 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Fixes the flaky test `02770_async_buffer_ignore`, and makes it assert the regression it was written for. Investigated at the request of alexey-milovidov on #100391, raised again on #106231. #### The flake The test asserted exact S3 read profile-event counts for a narrow-range read: ``` ProfileEvents['S3ReadRequestsCount'], ProfileEvents['ReadBufferFromS3Bytes'], ProfileEvents['ReadCompressedBytes'] ``` against the reference `4 66446 66446`. Those counts are not deterministic across CI jobs and the test cannot pin them away (it is already `no-random-settings`). Over 120 days CIDB shows 253 failures across 28 distinct observed triples, 7 of them on master, first seen 2026-03-26. The largest groups are `4 830 66446` (x174, filesystem cache hit), `6 67909 67909` (x22, parallel replicas), `4 7223260 66446` (x5, S3 read-ahead), `7 825111 569492` (x5), `4 17844 17844` (x5), and a long tail of `4 66446 679xx`/`4 66446 66533` where only `ReadCompressedBytes` drifts by tens to ~1700 bytes. The two most recent master hits are `4 66446 68063` (2026-07-26) and `4 66446 66533` (2026-07-27). #### What the test guards, and why no bound on `ReadCompressedBytes` can guard it The regression fixed together with this test was `AsynchronousBoundedReadBuffer::seek` taking the lazy-ignore branch while `file_offset_of_buffer_end` was still 0, so the buffer downloaded the whole prefix ahead of the first needed granule and discarded it. I reproduced that by removing the `file_offset_of_buffer_end &&` guard in `AsynchronousBoundedReadBuffer::seek` together with the `!current_buf ||` short-circuit in `ReadBufferFromRemoteFSGather::isSeekCheap` (the second one is required, otherwise `isSeekCheap()` returns true on the first seek and the branch is unreachable). On this fixture the narrow read then transfers 853846 S3 bytes instead of 66446, of which 787400 are discarded. `ReadCompressedBytes` does not move at all: it is incremented in `CompressedReadBufferBase` for blocks handed to the decompressor, while the ignored prefix is dropped lower down in `ThreadPoolRemoteFSReader::execute` before any block is assembled. On the buggy build `ReadCompressedBytes` is 66446, byte-for-byte equal to the healthy build. So no threshold on it can detect the over-read: not `< 1000000`, not `< 100000`, not even the exact `66446` the reference used to pin. The previous revision of this PR claimed the 1 MB bound would still catch an over-read; that claim was wrong and is retracted. Measured, narrow read, healthy vs buggy: | build | `S3ReadRequestsCount` | `ReadBufferFromS3Bytes` | `ReadCompressedBytes` | `AsynchronousReaderIgnoredBytes` | |---|---|---|---|---| | healthy | 4 | 66446 | 66446 | 0 | | guards removed | 4 | 853846 | 66446 | 787400 | #### The fix Assert the counter that actually observes the defect. The query seeks each column once, from offset 0, so a correct lazy ignore never triggers and `AsynchronousReaderIgnoredBytes` is exactly 0: ``` ProfileEvents['RemoteFSSeeks'] > 0, ProfileEvents['AsynchronousReaderIgnoredBytes'] = 0, ProfileEvents['S3ReadRequestsCount'] < 100, ProfileEvents['ReadCompressedBytes'] < 1000000 ``` `RemoteFSSeeks > 0` is an activation check. With `remote_filesystem_read_method = 'read'` there is no `AsynchronousBoundedReadBuffer` at all, so the ignored-bytes assertion would pass vacuously: on the buggy build, method `read` reports `RemoteFSSeeks` 0 and `AsynchronousReaderIgnoredBytes` 0 while `threadpool` reports 2 and 787400. `tests/clickhouse-test` does randomize `remote_filesystem_read_method` over `read` and `threadpool`, but the existing `no-random-settings` tag already suppresses that for this test, so the pin and the assertion are not guarding against the current randomizer: they guard against the default changing, the tag being dropped, or the test being edited onto the synchronous path, any of which would silently turn the ignored-bytes check into a no-op. `ReadCompressedBytes < 1000000` is kept as a granule-selection bound (a whole-column read is ~4 MB compressed), with a comment that no longer overstates what it covers. `ReadBufferFromS3Bytes` stays dropped: it is the unstable raw-transfer count (830 on a cache hit, 7.2 MB under read-ahead). #### Verification Local server over MinIO `s3_disk` (same disk definition as `tests/config/config.d/storage_conf.xml`), Build IDs recorded for each direction: - healthy build `66c6aded`: `1 1 1 1`, 10/10, and stable 15/15 on a fresh database. - guards removed, build `0c2a53f6`: `1 0 1 1`, 10/10. Only the new column reacts; the two surviving bounds print `1 1` on the buggy build, which is exactly the coverage gap this change closes. - activation mutation: dropping the read-method pin on the buggy build gives `RemoteFSSeeks` 0 / ignored 0 for method `read` (bug invisible, caught by the activation assertion) versus `RemoteFSSeeks` 2 / ignored 787400 for `threadpool`. - `AsynchronousReaderIgnoredBytes` is 0 across the regimes that made the old assertion flaky: repeated reads, prefetch off, `max_threads` 1 and 16, `remote_read_min_bytes_for_seek = 0`, parallel replicas, larger prefetch steps, larger read buffer. This flake is unrelated to #100391: the query has no `ORDER BY`, so the read-in-order path that PR changes is not exercised.

signals.title: Read the smallest on-disk column when a query reads no columns
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106597 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): When a query reads no real columns (for example `SELECT isNullable(lc) FROM t`, where the result is constant and depends only on the type), the `MergeTree` reader now picks the column that is cheapest to read from disk to carry the row count, instead of the one with the smallest in-memory value size. The previous metric mis-ranked compactly stored columns such as `LowCardinality(String)` below a `UInt64`, causing the reader to read a much larger column off disk. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106597 `SELECT isNullable(lc) FROM test_lc` is constant-folded away (`isNullable` depends only on the column type), so `ReadFromMergeTree` is left with no columns to read and must pick one column just to know the number of rows. `selectRangesToRead` picked it with `ExpressionActions::getSmallestColumn`, which ranks by the in-memory value size: a `UInt64` is 8 bytes, while a `LowCardinality(String)` falls back to a heuristic of 100. So it chose the `UInt64` column `x`, which is far more expensive to read off disk than the dictionary-encoded `lc`. This PR makes the fallback pick the column with the minimum on-disk compressed size via the existing `IMergeTreeDataPart::getColumnNameWithMinimumCompressedSize` helper. That is the same metric the read path already uses in `injectRequiredColumns`, so the two carrier-selection sites now agree. It falls back to `getSmallestColumn` only when there are no parts to measure. Verified locally with `ReadCompressedBytes` on the perf-test table (`x UInt64`, `lc LowCardinality(Nullable(String))`, 1e7 rows): | Query | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | `SELECT isNullable(lc)` | 40 MB (reads `x`) | 1.7 MB (reads `lc`) | | `SELECT 1 FROM test_lc` | 40 MB (reads `x`) | 1.7 MB (reads `lc`) | | `SELECT isNullable(big)` on `(tiny UInt8, big String)` | 85 KB (reads `tiny`) | 85 KB (reads `tiny`) | The last row is the no-regression check: when a small column is genuinely cheaper than the referenced one, the choice is unchanged. Added a regression test `04337_read_smallest_column_by_disk_size` that fails before this change and passes after it.

signals.title: Automatic LowCardinality serialization based on uniq statistics
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/85145 --> This PR adds automatic `LowCardinality` serialization for `MergeTree`, analogous to the existing automatic `Sparse` serialization. A `String` or `FixedString` column whose declared type is **not** `LowCardinality` can now be stored on disk in dictionary-encoded form when it has a `uniq` statistic with a low cardinality estimate. The encoding is transparent: the column keeps its declared data type, flows through the query pipeline as a (non-native) `ColumnLowCardinality`, and is materialized to a full column at the boundaries that require it. **Motivation:** save disk space and read I/O for low-cardinality string columns without requiring users to declare the column type as `LowCardinality(...)`. **How it works** - A new per-part serialization kind `LOW_CARDINALITY` (shown as `LowCardinality` in `system.parts_columns.serialization_kind`). - The decision is made at write time from the **existing** `uniq` statistic — there are **no changes to statistics serialization**. In `MergeTreeDataWriter`, a `String`/`FixedString` column whose `uniq` estimate does not exceed the new `MergeTree` setting `max_uniq_number_for_low_cardinality` (default `0` = disabled), and which was not already chosen for `Sparse`, is stored with `SerializationLowCardinality`. The column must therefore declare `STATISTICS(uniq)` and have `materialize_statistics_on_insert` enabled. - A new `is_native` flag on `ColumnLowCardinality` makes `getDataType` report the nested type, so the "column class matches data type" invariant holds while such a column flows through the pipeline. It is materialized to a full column in `removeSpecialRepresentations` (aggregation, joins, squashing, blocks), in the merge-input step of `IMergingAlgorithm`, in the sorting and sparse-removing transforms, and in `IFunction`. The `optimize_functions_to_subcolumns` pass skips columns stored as non-native `LowCardinality`, since the dictionary encoding does not expose the data type's regular subcolumns. - The kind is independent of sparse serialization: `SerializationInfo` entries for eligible columns are created in the writer, in merges, in mutations and in the per-table serialization hints even when `ratio_of_defaults_for_sparse_serialization = 1` disables `Sparse` entirely. **Notes** - Opt-in: disabled by default and requires an explicit `uniq` statistic, so existing tables are unaffected. Requires `allow_experimental_statistics`. - Reading a subcolumn of an encoded column (for example `s.size`) is not supported and reports `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`: the subcolumn's streams do not exist in a dictionary-encoded part. Making it read the full column and extract the subcolumn in memory needs a dedicated serialization and is left for a separate change. - Extracts and reimplements the automatic `LowCardinality` part of the draft #85145 against current `master`, without the statistics-serialization refactoring. That refactoring is still unmerged (#85145 and #109128 are open drafts). Validated locally with a server built from this branch: kind selection for `Wide` and `Compact` parts, `String` and `FixedString`, query correctness, functions, `GROUP BY`/`ORDER BY`/`DISTINCT`/`LIMIT BY`/window functions, joins, `IN` subqueries, `INSERT SELECT`, `UNION ALL`, `OPTIMIZE FINAL` (LowCardinality preserved through merges), mutations, `ALTER RENAME`/`MODIFY COLUMN`, `DETACH`/`ATTACH`, `PREWHERE`, input/output formats with and without `allow_special_serialization_kinds_in_output_formats`, and tables with mixed `Default` and `LowCardinality` active parts. The three tests also pass with `ratio_of_defaults_for_sparse_serialization` forced to `0.0` and `1.0`, with `enable_block_offset_column`/`enable_block_number_column`, with compact parts, and over repeated fully randomized runs. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added automatic `LowCardinality` serialization: a `String`/`FixedString` column that has a `uniq` statistic and low cardinality can be stored in dictionary-encoded form on disk while keeping its declared data type. Controlled by the new `MergeTree` setting `max_uniq_number_for_low_cardinality` (disabled by default). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=107436&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/107436](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F107436+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix build flag with new detection mode.
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107399 --> Fixes a build failure on AArch64 CPUs that are advertised as ARMv8.2-A but lack an optional feature of ClickHouse's "modern" ARM profile — for example the HiSilicon Kunpeng 920, which has no `rcpc` and faults with `SIGILL` on the `ldapr` instruction. Such CPUs must be built with `-DNO_ARMV81_OR_HIGHER=1`, but that profile previously failed to compile the Rust components. Root cause: the compatibility profile passed `target_feature=+crc,-neon` to Rust. NEON (Advanced SIMD) is part of the AArch64 baseline and is enabled by default for the `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` target. The `ring` crate (pulled in by `chdig` and `delta-kernel-rs`) statically asserts that NEON is available on little-endian aarch64 and fails to compile when it is disabled. Dropping the `-neon` lets the compatibility profile build `ring`, so `chdig` and `delta-kernel-rs` no longer need to be force-disabled under `NO_ARMV81_OR_HIGHER`. An earlier revision of this pull request auto-detected CPU features from `/proc/cpuinfo` at build time. That approach was reverted following review: ClickHouse always builds for an explicitly specified target platform and must not depend on the host machine (one can build on a coffee machine while targeting an AVX-512 server and vice versa). The pre-existing build-time `/proc/cpuinfo` "best-effort" guard on the AArch64 path is removed for the same reason. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107399 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Build/Testing/Packaging Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed building with `-DNO_ARMV81_OR_HIGHER=1` on AArch64: the compatibility profile no longer disables NEON for Rust, so `ring`-based components (`chdig`, `delta-kernel-rs`) compile and stay enabled. This unblocks building for ARMv8.2-A CPUs that lack `rcpc` (e.g. HiSilicon Kunpeng 920). ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features)

signals.title: Parallelize listing of globbed `s3` table function paths
signals.text: Speeds up listing files for the `s3` table function over globbed paths, in two complementary ways. The listing was a single serial stream of `ListObjectsV2` requests paginated by a continuation token, bound by the per-request latency of S3 (~75 ms measured against `clickhouse-public-datasets`); this dominates queries over buckets with many objects. An earlier attempt (#66504) used speculative keyspace splitting with fixed split points assuming a uniform key distribution and a fixed character set, and was closed as fragile. Controlled by the new setting `s3_list_object_parallelism` (default `1` = the previous serial behavior). **1. Hierarchical layouts** — walk the "directory" tree formed by the `/` delimiter with several worker threads in parallel, pruning subtrees that cannot contain a matching key (so for partitioned layouts like `year=*/month=*/` fewer objects are fetched, not merely listed in parallel). Recursive globs (`**`) keep serial listing. **2. Big flat directories** (e.g. files named by hash/UUID — `musicbrainz/mlhdplus-complete/<uuid>.txt.zst`, ~600k files in one prefix) — when a listed prefix is truncated but has no sub-directories, split it by keyspace: tile the remaining range into contiguous `(start_after, end]` sub-ranges listed concurrently, with boundaries derived from the byte alphabet observed in the listed page. Because the sub-ranges are contiguous they tile the interval **with no gaps** — a key whose byte is absent from the sampled alphabet still falls into the range that brackets it — so the split is complete regardless of the key distribution or character set. The split is a single level and is **probe-gated**: before splitting, one cheap `ListObjectsV2` checks whether any key exists beyond the current bucket; if not (keys share a common prefix, e.g. `pageviews-YYYYMMDD-HH`), the directory is paginated serially instead of issuing a fan of empty boundary probes. This is the robust counterpart to #66504 — it never regresses for clustered keys. On S3 Express / directory buckets — which reject `StartAfter` and only allow the `/` delimiter — keyspace splitting is disabled automatically (detected via `isS3ExpressBucket`), so flat ranges are paginated serially while hierarchical layouts are still listed in parallel. Correctness of glob matching is guaranteed by the existing per-file `RE2::FullMatch`, so the directory pruning only needs to be conservative. **Measured against real S3** (`clickhouse-public-datasets`, ~75 ms/list-request) across ~16 datasets — all return identical results (same count, no duplicates, identical path checksum), serial vs parallel: - Big flat, uniform keys — `musicbrainz/mlhdplus-complete` (594415 files): **37s → 3.7s (~10x)**. - Big flat, clustered keys — `wikistat` (97529) / `gharchive` (100091): probe sends them serial; parallel matches serial (no regression). - Hierarchical — `web/store`: ~2.5x (bounded by its small directory count; scales toward the parallelism factor for larger trees). - Small/medium directories (`nyc-taxi`, `ontime`, `hits/native`, `sensors`, `tranco`, `youtube`, `adsblol`, `bluesky`, …): correct, no regression. A unit test (`gtest_object_storage_parallel_listing`) asserts every key is produced exactly once across parallelism 1–64, including adversarial cases (bytes outside the sampled alphabet, shared long prefixes, boundary keys, mixed hierarchical+flat). Stateless tests (`04339_s3_parallel_glob_listing`, `04340_s3_parallel_flat_listing`) verify parallel and serial listing return identical results. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/65572 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/66504 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added a setting `s3_list_object_parallelism` to list the files of the `s3` table function over a globbed path in parallel. Hierarchically partitioned layouts are listed by walking the tree of common prefixes concurrently; a single big flat directory is listed by splitting its keyspace into contiguous sub-ranges. This speeds up queries over buckets with many objects (e.g. ~10x for a directory of 600k files). <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=107567&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/107567](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F107567+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Add ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY ENGINE to change a MergeTree-family table's engine
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107551 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY ENGINE = ...MergeTree(...)` to change the engine of a MergeTree-family table in place (for example `MergeTree` into `ReplacingMergeTree` or `SummingMergeTree`). Gated behind the experimental setting `allow_experimental_alter_modify_engine`. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107551 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107481 Requested by @ alexey-milovidov. `ALTER TABLE t MODIFY ENGINE = <engine>` changes a MergeTree-family table's engine in place. Only the merge semantics (`MergingParams`) change: columns, keys and settings are kept, and data is not rewritten. Existing parts re-merge under the new semantics via background merges and `OPTIMIZE ... FINAL`, as with the part-level reset in #107481. A new `MODIFY_ENGINE` alter command rewrites the engine clause in the CREATE query (`StorageInMemoryMetadata::new_engine` -> `applyMetadataChangesToCreateQuery`); `MergingParams::parseFromEngineAST` builds and validates the new merge params against the columns and final settings, so a rejection never leaves an unloadable CREATE on disk. Supported targets: `Replacing`, `Summing`, `Aggregating`, `Collapsing`, `VersionedCollapsing`, `Coalescing`, `Graphite`. A required column may be added in the same statement, before `MODIFY ENGINE`. Non-replicated tables only; old-syntax tables are rejected, their keys being positional engine arguments. Because data is not rewritten, a transition is refused when existing parts could not satisfy the target's invariants: a nullable or unreadable `Graphite` path/time column (the rollup reads them with `getDataAt`/`getUInt`), and `VersionedCollapsing` with the version column outside the sorting key, whose reload widens the key under existing parts. **Two questions for review:** 1. Reload-only, rather than a live swap: `merging_params` is read lock-free from hot paths and often bound by const reference for a whole query, and an exclusive lock cannot be taken there (the query holds `drop_lock` in read mode). An immediate swap needs either a `MultiVersion` `merging_params` or recreating the storage. Which do you prefer? 2. The coordinated `Replicated*MergeTree` switch (decision 3 on the issue) is not implemented. `ReplicatedMergeTreeTableMetadata` already persists the merge mode, so that is the natural next step. Tests: `04340_alter_modify_engine` (the gate, each transition's merge semantics under `FINAL`, the validation errors, the AST JSON round trip), `04341_alter_modify_engine_access` and `04342_alter_modify_engine_replicated`. Docs: `docs/reference/statements/alter/engine.mdx`.

signals.title: Fix "No set is registered for key" for a subquery used as both FROM source and IN argument
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a `LOGICAL_ERROR` "No set is registered for key" that could abort the server (or fail the query in release builds) for a query where a subquery is used both as a `FROM` table expression and as the right argument of an `IN` / `NOT IN` / `GLOBAL IN` function, for example `SELECT y FROM (SELECT y FROM t QUALIFY 1) AS s QUALIFY globalNotIn((SELECT 1), s)`. ### Description Found by the AST fuzzer (`AST fuzzer (arm_asan_ubsan)`). Example report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=104939&sha=d224ae20875bb869add720814dd4c5e5fd4604e8&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28arm_asan_ubsan%29 (STID 0250-04e2). The crash is a pre-existing trunk bug, unrelated to the PR it happened to fire on. When a subquery is referenced both as a `FROM` table expression and as the right argument of an `IN` / `NOT IN` / `GLOBAL IN` function (the right argument being an alias of that `FROM` table expression), the analyzer resolves both references to the same shared query-tree node. `collectSets()` registers the `IN` set in `PreparedSets` keyed by that node's tree hash. When the node is later planned as the `FROM` source, `Planner::buildPlanForQueryNode()` mutates it in place (constant-true `WHERE` removal, or the `QUALIFY -> HAVING -> WHERE` rewrite). That changes its tree hash, so the later set lookup in `PlannerActionsVisitor::makeSetForInFunction()` recomputes the hash from the mutated node and fails to find the set, aborting with `LOGICAL_ERROR` "No set is registered for key ...". Fix: when the `IN` set source is a `QUERY`/`UNION` node that is shared with another part of the query tree (`use_count() > 1`), resolve the `IN` argument against an independent copy. The set source is then no longer aliased to the `FROM` table expression, so planning the `FROM` source cannot mutate the node behind the set key. This is the same root-cause class as #80757 (a set key drifting between registration and lookup), here caused by an in-place planner mutation of a shared node rather than by CTE-name decoration. No open issue was found for this error. A stateless regression test `04338_in_set_source_aliases_from_table` is added; all four queries it contains abort on master and pass with this fix. #### Follow-up commit: copy `column_name` in `SortNode::cloneImpl` The new `clone()` of the `IN` set source exposed a latent defect: `SortNode::cloneImpl` did not copy `column_name` (a member derived from the original AST identifier in the constructor, not a child node, so the base clone machinery cannot reproduce it). A clone of any subtree containing a resolved `ORDER BY <identifier>` lost the name. This is visible in `EXPLAIN QUERY TREE` (`SORT` prints `EXPRESSION` instead of `EXPRESSION <name>`) and is read by the planner: `PlannerSorting` builds `SortColumnDescription::alias` from it, and that alias is used by `FillingTransform` for `WITH FILL ... INTERPOLATE` column matching. `InterpolateNode::cloneImpl` already copies its analogous `expression_name`; this mirrors that. The pre-existing test `03165_order_by_duplicate` (an `EXPLAIN QUERY TREE` of an `IN` subquery with `ORDER BY`) regressed to `EXPRESSION` and is restored by this commit.

signals.title: Fix flaky 01169_old_alter_partition_isolation_stress: orphaned client at teardown
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/99018 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Flaky in `Stateless tests (..., parallel)`. `thread_insert` and `thread_select` were stopped with `kill -TERM $PID`, which kills only the bash subshell, not the `clickhouse-client` in flight. The orphan is reparented and runs its query after the final `DROP TABLE`, printing `Table ... src does not exist` or `Database ... does not exist` to the shared stderr, reported as "having stderror". `wait_for_queries_to_finish` misses it: a client still in connect/auth is not yet in `system.processes`. The loops now stop via a flag file, exiting after their current client finishes. The name uses `CLICKHOUSE_TEST_UNIQUE_NAME`, so the test stays parallel-safe. #98280 and #99018 worked around this race without removing its source. Two error-path defects found during review are fixed as well: - The flag was raised only after `wait $PID_3 && wait $PID_4`, unreachable on either failure. Under `errexit` a nonzero `wait $PID_3` does not abort (left operand of `&&`), it only skips `wait $PID_4`, so a failed worker was reported as success and teardown began while the other was still mutating `src` / `dst`. If `wait $PID_4` failed instead, `errexit` fired before the flag was raised and the loops ran past the end of the test. The flag now comes from an `EXIT` trap, and each worker is waited for separately so the first failure is the exit status. - `wait $PID_1 ||:` discarded a real failure of `thread_insert` / `thread_select`. `thread_select` is the only check of transient isolation violations during the run, so the test could pass after it had exited on a `throwIf`. The orphan is timing dependent and does not reproduce on an idle host, so the evidence is a deterministic A/B rather than a rerun. <details><summary>Validation and CI evidence</summary> A harness mirroring the final region, with a heartbeat file detecting a loop that outlives the script. Old code: exits 0 on a `PID_3` failure, leaves the loop running on a `PID_4` failure, exits 0 on a `thread_insert` failure. Fixed: 3, loop stopped, 9. Each element is load-bearing -- removing the trap re-orphans the loop, restoring `&&` or `||:` re-swallows the failures. Against a real server the test passes 5/5 with the reference matched and no surviving clients. Genuine hits with reruns passing, last 30 days: - PR #101514, `Stateless tests (amd_debug, distributed plan, s3 storage, parallel)`: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=101514&sha=8ef111d9&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_debug%2C%20distributed%20plan%2C%20s3%20storage%2C%20parallel%29 (UNKNOWN_TABLE `src`) - PR #106203, `Stateless tests (amd_tsan, parallel, 2/2)`: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=106203&sha=1ab8ccf4f8982a98d856d7e6086616ffdff80de1&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_tsan%2C%20parallel%2C%202%2F2%29 (UNKNOWN_DATABASE) The sibling `01169_alter_partition_isolation_stress.sh` still uses `kill -TERM`, but none of its recent failures carry this signature, so it is left for a separate change. </details>

signals.title: Fix flaky hang in ThreadPool.GlobalFull1/GlobalFull2 unit tests
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `ThreadPool.GlobalFull1` (and its sibling `GlobalFull2`) can hang the entire `unit_tests_dbms` binary on slow builds, surfacing as `Thread 1 "unit_tests_dbms" received signal SIGINT, Interrupt.` after the 45-minute gdb watchdog fires. Observed on the `msan`, `tsan` and `amd_llvm_coverage` unit-test jobs; the test has never failed on master. No related open issue found. **Root cause.** Each worker job runs a hand-rolled spin-barrier over a monotonically-increasing atomic counter: ```cpp auto func = [&] { ++counter; while (counter != num_jobs) {} }; ``` The test depends on the counter reaching *exactly* `num_jobs` (= `capacity + 1` = 6): the 5 scheduled jobs each increment it once, and the main thread increments it once more after the 6th `scheduleOrThrowOnError` is rejected (the global pool is saturated at 5 threads). If, on a slow build, the schedule that *should* be rejected instead succeeds and its job runs, an extra `++counter` drives the counter past `num_jobs`. Because the counter only ever increases, `counter != num_jobs` then never holds again, so the worker threads spin forever and the binary hangs until the watchdog interrupts whatever test is running (which the report attributes to `GlobalFull1`). **Fix.** Use `counter < num_jobs` instead of `counter != num_jobs`. The normal path is unchanged (the spin still stops the instant the counter reaches the target); an overshoot now terminates the spin too, so the test finishes and reports its `EXPECT_THROW` / `EXPECT_EQ` assertions instead of hanging CI. This is a test-robustness fix only; no production code changes. Found via the `Unit tests (msan)` / `Unit tests (tsan)` / `Unit tests (amd_llvm_coverage)` jobs on commit a282a393d6f4afce3b7c601e5890081e51c8f24f. CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=107357&sha=a282a393d6f4afce3b7c601e5890081e51c8f24f&name_0=PR&name_1=Unit%20tests%20%28msan%29

signals.title: Fix LOGICAL_ERROR in parallel replicas for window function over a constant subquery
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/103695 --> Related: #103695 (same `Invalid number of columns in chunk pushed to OutputPort` family) ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `LOGICAL_ERROR` (`Invalid number of columns in chunk pushed to OutputPort`) that crashed the server for a query with a window function over a subquery projecting a constant (e.g. `SELECT count(*) OVER () FROM (SELECT 0 FROM t)`) when executed with parallel replicas and the analyzer. ### Description Found by the AST fuzzer: `AST fuzzer (amd_debug, targeted, old_compatibility)`, STID `2270-3258`. CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=85138&sha=bb9b5684191b897d5a0dc9aca64b2a4e6929557b&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%2C%20old_compatibility%29 #### Reproducer ```sql CREATE TABLE t (s String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY s; INSERT INTO t SELECT toString(number) FROM numbers(2000); SELECT count(*) OVER () FROM (SELECT 0 FROM t) SETTINGS enable_parallel_replicas = 1, max_parallel_replicas = 2, cluster_for_parallel_replicas = 'test_cluster_one_shard_three_replicas_localhost', parallel_replicas_for_non_replicated_merge_tree = 1, parallel_replicas_local_plan = 0, prefer_localhost_replica = 0, enable_analyzer = 1; ``` #### Root cause When parallel replicas read up to `WithMergeableState`, the coordinator computes the expected `RemoteSource` header from an `only_analyze` plan. In that path the inner subquery is replaced by a `ReadNothingStep` whose columns were built from the projection types only, so a projected literal constant became a plain (non-constant) column. A real replica instead emits a `ColumnConst` for it. That difference matters because `ActionsDAG` (`duplicate_const_columns`) keeps an unused `ColumnConst` flowing through a later step (e.g. the `Before WINDOW` expression, whose own outputs are empty for `count(*) OVER ()`) while a plain column is projected away. As a result the analyze header dropped the unused constant column while the replica kept it, so the coordinator built the `RemoteSource` with too few columns and the chunk pushed by the replica did not match the output port. The fix preserves the constant in the `only_analyze` `ReadNothingStep` header so it matches real execution. Non-constant projections keep the previous behavior. A regression test was added: `04365_parallel_replicas_window_over_const_subquery`. It crashes the server before the fix and passes after.

signals.title: Avoid copying data for the NONE compression codec when writing
signals.text: Avoid copying data for the `NONE` compression codec when writing. For `CODEC(NONE)` the compressed block on disk is byte-identical to the input, so the payload does not need to be copied between the compressor's working buffer and the output buffer. When a `CompressedWriteBuffer` exclusively owns its output buffer, the working buffer is now pointed directly into the output buffer (reserving room for the checksum and header in front of the data), so the caller writes the uncompressed data straight to where it will be flushed; `nextImpl` only fills in the header and checksum in place, with no payload copy. The header is written by a new `ICompressionCodec::writeHeader` helper factored out of `compress`. When the output buffer is too small, the writer falls back to the previous owned-buffer copy path. This is the same zero-copy buffer-aliasing technique that `HashingWriteBuffer` already uses. The zero-copy path (`out_buffer_is_exclusive`) is enabled only where the compressor is the sole, sequential writer of its output buffer: the wide-part column data streams, the primary-index stream, and the temporary-data buffer. It is intentionally left off where the output buffer is shared and written interleaved — the per-column streams of compact parts (which share one `plain_hashing`) and the network protocol buffer (interleaved with raw packet framing) — because there the reserved window could be overwritten by another writer. It is also left off for the marks streams of wide and compact parts: their `marks_file` has a small fixed-size buffer (4096 bytes), so the direct path would clamp `NONE`-coded mark blocks to it instead of the configured `marks_compress_block_size`; the regression test `04539_marks_compression_codec_none_block_size` covers this. Note: for `NONE`, compressed block sizes become bounded by the output buffer size, so the on-disk byte layout can differ slightly from before (an occasional shorter block at buffer boundaries). This is deterministic and does not affect reads. The read side already decompresses `NONE` data directly into the destination column via `readBig`, so no change is needed there. ### Performance evidence Measured with two `clickhouse` binaries built from the same base commit, differing only by this PR (cherry-picked onto the same parent), so the comparison isolates exactly this change. Isolated write-path microbenchmark — 4 GiB through a `CompressedWriteBuffer` with the `NONE` codec into a discarding sink (no disk), 1 MiB blocks and output buffer, toggling only `out_buffer_is_exclusive`: | `out_buffer_is_exclusive` | throughput | |---|---| | `false` (old copy path) | ~8.5–9.2 GB/s | | `true` (zero-copy path) | ~13.6–14.0 GB/s | | **speedup** | **~1.5–1.6x** | End-to-end `INSERT` of 8 wide `String CODEC(NONE)` columns (3M rows, single insert thread, no dedup/squashing/sparse, merges stopped; baseline = exact parent commit; median of interleaved reps): **2.96s → 2.62s (~1.13x, ~13% faster)**. The end-to-end gain is below the disk-free microbenchmark because disk I/O and data generation (equal in both binaries) dominate the rest of the insert. A focused performance test, `tests/performance/codec_none_read.xml`, is added. It scans `CODEC(NONE)` columns, so in the PR-vs-master comparison the table is filled by each side's own write path (old vs new block layout) and then read by the identical read code. This guards against a read regression from the slightly changed `NONE` block layout, and tracks `NONE` read throughput in general (relevant for incompressible data such as vector embeddings). Measured read time is unchanged before/after (~0.62s vs ~0.61s for 100M rows, single thread), confirming the write-path change is read-neutral. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Avoid an extra data copy when writing columns and temporary data compressed with the `NONE` codec by writing the data directly into the output buffer. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=108096&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/108096](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F108096+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Restore O(1) reserve in MergeSorter::mergeBatchImpl (fix ORDER BY perf regression)
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106599 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a performance regression in `ORDER BY` (merge sort) introduced in #100963. Queries with a sort followed by `LIMIT` were slightly slower because of redundant per-output-block work in the result-block reservation. ### Description Reported by egor-click in #106599: `jit_sort` perf test query `12` regressed on ARM/aarch64 (Neoverse-V2) by about +18% `client_time` (`SELECT WatchID FROM hits_100m_single ORDER BY WatchID ASC, CounterID DESC, ClientIP ASC LIMIT 2000000`). Public history: https://performance.ci.clickhouse.com/history/jit_sort/12?metric=client_time&arch=arm **Root cause.** Bisecting the issue's controlled window (baseline `bd123fed28c5` -> affected `d8dd2c3a1a82`) leaves a single functional source change: #100963, in `MergeSorter::mergeBatchImpl`. It replaced the reservation size ``` min(chunks[0].getNumRows(), max_merged_block_size) ``` with a sum over all input chunks, capped at `max_merged_block_size`: ``` size_to_reserve = 0; for (auto & chunk : chunks) size_to_reserve += chunk.getNumRows(); size_to_reserve = min(size_to_reserve, max_merged_block_size); ``` This both walks the whole `chunks` vector on every output block (in front of the hot k-way merge loop) and reserves a larger, cap-saturated size. Matches the issue's profile (`MergeSortingTransform` +10.88%). **Fix.** Restore the pre-#100963 O(1) reservation `min(chunks[0].getNumRows(), max_merged_block_size)`. This is the prototype egor-click validated on ARM Neoverse-V2 (affected-vs-patched about -13.96%, 9/9 runs). egor-click's validation also showed the win needs the smaller reserve, not only dropping the per-block loop: a variant that stays O(1) but reserves the full input-row sum (saturating the cap) did not recover the regression (+0.59%). `reserve()` is a capacity hint only, so it never changes results or the final allocation size; the bare `chunks[0]` estimate reserves the least and cannot over-allocate. Locally verified the merge-sort output for a mixed-direction multi-column `ORDER BY` is byte-identical to an independent reference sort. ARM perf is validated by the reporter's Neoverse-V2 pipeline and by the CI Performance Comparison.

signals.title: Avoid per-row heap allocations in blocked Myers edit distance
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106595 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Improved the performance of `levenshteinDistance` (and `editDistance`) for medium-length strings on ARM by avoiding per-row heap allocations in the blocked Myers code path. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106595 Fixes the ARM regression reported in #106595: `string_similarity` query `0` (`SELECT avg(levenshteinDistance(randomString(300), randomString(300))) FROM numbers(10000)`) was about +12.6% slower on Neoverse-V2. Root cause: the blocked Myers path (`BlockMyersEditDistance`, used for byte needles of 257..8192 bytes) allocated its per-row scratch buffers on the heap once per row through `VectorWithMemoryTracking`: the pattern-mask table `tbl` and the `VP`/`VN`/`HP`/`HN`/`D0` bit vectors. Each allocation pairs a `malloc`/`free` with a `CurrentMemoryTracker` atomic update. On ARM those atomic updates are comparatively expensive, so this per-row churn showed up as the regression. Only this path was affected: the single-word Myers widths (`ByteEditDistanceMyersImpl`, needles up to 256 bytes) already use fixed stack scratch, which is why the other `string_similarity` queries did not regress. Fix: hold the per-row buffers in `PODArrayWithStackMemory`. It keeps an allocation up to its inline capacity in an inline buffer (no heap allocation, no `CurrentMemoryTracker` atomics) and transparently spills to a tracked allocation above it. The per-row allocation is therefore eliminated across each buffer's inline range, and the buffer management is a single idiomatic type instead of a hand-rolled stack-array + tracked-vector + raw-pointer split (suggested by @ nikitamikhaylov). The inline range differs per buffer because their shapes differ: - `VP`/`VN`/`HP`/`HN`/`D0` hold one `Word` per block (1 KB each), so a 128-block inline buffer covers the full 8192-byte blocked-Myers range. - `tbl` is the ASCII pattern table, `256 * num_blocks` words (one row per byte value), so it is 256x larger per block. Its inline buffer covers needles up to 8 blocks (512 bytes, 16 KB); a full-range inline table would be about 256 KB, so longer needles transparently spill `tbl` to a tracked allocation while the bit vectors stay inline. The reported regression (300-byte needles, 5 blocks) is fully on the inline path for every buffer. Correctness: distances are unchanged. `02884_string_distance_function`, `03369_function_arrayLevenshtein` and `04125_array_levenshtein_types` pass, and a differential check of `editDistance` and `editDistanceUTF8` against a brute-force DP reference (1392 random pairs) matches exactly, including the block and inline/spill boundary lengths (64/128/192/256/512/8192).
signals.author: groeneai

signals.title: Prune non-output left columns when a join spill threshold is set
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106603 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106602 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a performance regression in hash joins introduced by enabling `max_bytes_ratio_before_external_join` by default. Left-side columns absent from the join output (for example the join key in `SELECT count() ... LEFT JOIN ...`) are now pruned again when only a spill threshold is configured, instead of being carried through the pipeline. ### Description `join_squashing_blocks` (queries `0` and `1`) regressed by ~10-20% on aarch64 (#106602, #106603). The regression window points to enabling `max_bytes_ratio_before_external_join` by default (`0.0` -> `0.5`). Root cause: `HashJoin::canRemoveColumnsFromLeftBlock()` is gated on `isUsedByAnotherAlgorithm()`, which now returns `true` for every hash join because of the `maxBytesBeforeExternalJoin() > 0` clause. That disabled pruning of left-side columns that are not in the join output. For the benchmark query the left key column (a 300M-row column not needed by `count()`) was no longer pruned, flowed through `JoiningTransform`, and forced an extra `ColumnPermuteTransform` even though the join never spills. Fix: only keep left columns when the join may switch to an algorithm that does not prune them, i.e. `auto` (`JoinSwitcher` -> `MergeJoin`) and explicit `grace_hash`. A spill threshold alone selects `SpillingHashJoin`, which only ever switches `HashJoin` -> `GraceHashJoin`; both produce results through the same `HashJoinResult` path with identical pruning, so the result structure stays consistent. `isUsedByAnotherAlgorithm()` is left unchanged, so right-side key columns are still saved for spilling/switching. EXPLAIN PIPELINE of the benchmark query no longer contains `ColumnPermuteTransform` under the default settings. Results are bit-identical across no-spill, default, forced `grace_hash` spill, forced `SpillingHashJoin` spill, and `auto`, for `LEFT`/`INNER`/`RIGHT`/`FULL` joins. Added a regression test (`04401_join_left_column_pruning_with_spill_threshold`).

signals.title: Deny mergeTreeProjection and mergeTreeIndex reads that bypass a SELECT row policy
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> No related public open issue found. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Critical Bug Fix (crash, data loss, RBAC) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Reading projection data with the `mergeTreeProjection` table function no longer bypasses a SELECT row policy defined on the parent table. Such a read is now denied with `ACCESS_DENIED` when a non-trivial SELECT row policy exists. The `mergeTreeIndex` table function is likewise denied when the row policy references one of the index columns being read. ### Description `mergeTreeProjection(db, table, projection)` reads a projection's parts directly. Projection parts contain materialized rows of the parent table, so the read returned rows that a SELECT row policy on the parent is meant to hide. Any user with `SELECT` on the table could read hidden rows. `mergeTreeIndex` had the same gap, exposing per-granule index metadata (marks, primary key and column min/max). PR #95480 added the missing `SELECT` grant check to these functions but did not consider row policies. Reproduction (before this PR the last query returns all 4 rows): ```sql CREATE TABLE users (id UInt64, name String, department String, salary UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id; INSERT INTO users VALUES (1,'Alice','engineering',100000),(2,'Bob','finance',120000), (3,'Carol','engineering',110000),(4,'Dave','hr',90000); ALTER TABLE users ADD PROJECTION proj (SELECT id, name, salary ORDER BY id); ALTER TABLE users MATERIALIZE PROJECTION proj; OPTIMIZE TABLE users FINAL; CREATE USER restricted NOT IDENTIFIED; GRANT SELECT ON default.users TO restricted; CREATE ROW POLICY rp ON users FOR SELECT USING department = 'engineering' TO restricted; -- as restricted: returns only Alice, Carol (policy enforced) SELECT * FROM users; -- as restricted, before this PR: returns all 4 rows (policy bypassed) SELECT * FROM mergeTreeProjection('default', 'users', 'proj'); ``` Fix: - `StorageFromMergeTreeProjection::read()` denies the read when a non-trivial SELECT row policy exists on the parent. The policy cannot be re-applied here: a projection may aggregate rows or omit the policy's filter columns entirely (as in the example above, where `department` is absent from the projection), so hidden rows still leak even when those columns are absent. A column-overlap check is therefore insufficient for projections; a full deny is required. - `StorageMergeTreeIndex::readImpl()` exposes only index metadata, so it gets the narrower column-overlap guard already used by `mergeTreeTextIndex`: deny only when the policy filter references one of the storage columns whose index data is being read. An always-true policy (`isAlwaysTrue()`) does not trigger the deny, and reads without a row policy are unaffected. Test: `tests/queries/0_stateless/04401_mergetree_projection_row_policy.sh`.

signals.title: Fix SQL injection in PostgreSQL wire protocol parameter binding
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110760 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed SQL injection in the PostgreSQL wire protocol emulation. Prepared-statement parameters — the `Parse`/`Bind`/`Execute` extended-query path used by `psycopg2`, JDBC, `node-postgres`, Npgsql and others, and the simple-query `EXECUTE` path — were substituted into the executed SQL by raw string splicing, so a crafted parameter could break out of its value position and inject SQL. Parameters are now bound as data. This also fixes string parameters that previously failed with `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER` when a client sent them unquoted. ### Description The PostgreSQL wire-protocol emulation assembled SQL by raw string substitution of client-supplied values. `PreparedStatemetsManager::getStatement` replaced the placeholders `$1`, `$2`, ... in the prepared-statement body with the raw parameter values. Two paths feed it: - **Extended-query path** (`Parse`/`Bind`/`Execute`), the default for `psycopg2`, JDBC, `node-postgres`, Npgsql and others. `BindQuery::deserialize` read the parameter bytes straight off the wire and they were spliced into the SQL text verbatim, so a parameter like `x' UNION ALL SELECT ... --` broke out of its string literal. As a side effect, a correctly written client that sends `WHERE name = $1` without client-side quoting failed with `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER`, because the value was substituted unquoted. - **Simple-query `EXECUTE` path**, where arguments were formatted with `fieldToString`, which drops the quotes around string literals, so it had the same problem. Every argument is now turned into a SQL literal before substitution: - `Bind` uses the parameter type OIDs the client declared in `Parse`. An OID that maps to a ClickHouse type is emitted as `accurateCast('<escaped value>', '<type>')`, which delegates parsing and range checking to ClickHouse while keeping the declared type (`int4` rejects `3.14` and `2147483648`, `numeric` keeps full precision, `bool`/`date`/`uuid` stay their declared type). Any other OID becomes a quoted and escaped string literal. Both forms keep the value inside a quoted literal, so it cannot break out of the value position. Because the declared type is honoured, a numeric parameter stays numeric and `LIMIT $1` or `SELECT $1 + 1` keep working. - The protocol NULL sentinel (length -1) maps to the SQL keyword `NULL`. `BindQuery::parameters` becomes `std::optional<String>` so a NULL parameter is no longer ambiguous with the text `"NULL"`. - `EXECUTE` uses `FieldVisitorToString` (strings quoted and escaped, numbers left bare) and rejects a non-literal argument. Previously a non-literal such as `now()` reached `child->as<ASTLiteral>()->value` and dereferenced a null pointer; splicing the expression's SQL text also changes results (`$1 * 10` with `1 + 1` assembles `1 + 1 * 10` = 11, not 20). Binding values as data exposed several protocol contracts that the emulation did not keep, each of which is needed for the fix to be usable by real clients: - **Arity** is checked against the statement's true parameter count (the highest `$N` in the body), not against the number of declared OIDs — `Parse` may declare fewer. Otherwise a short `Bind` left `$2` literally in the executed SQL and a long one was silently ignored. - **The portal snapshots its statement at `Bind`.** Re-resolving at `Execute` meant a later `Parse` that redefined the statement changed what `Execute` ran, and a `Close` between `Bind` and `Execute` turned it into `Execute without prior Bind`. - **`ReadyForQuery` is emitted once per protocol boundary** (startup, a completed simple query, `Sync`) instead of at the top of every idle loop iteration, which used to emit it twice around a standalone `Describe`/`Sync`. - **An extended-query error skips to the next `Sync`** instead of rethrowing, which dropped the connection before the client could read the `ErrorResponse`. - Negative count fields in `Parse`/`Bind` are rejected; binary-format *parameters* are rejected after the message is fully consumed (so the stream stays aligned); binary *result* format requests are accepted and answered with text, which is what the `RowDescription` advertises. #### Scope Identifier quoting for `COPY` was part of this PR and has been removed: #110760 fixed the same injection in `ParserCopyQuery`, which now stores the table and column names already rendered as valid SQL (each part of a compound `database.table` name separately back-quoted). Quoting them again in the handler would double-quote them. The integration test for `COPY` identifier injection is kept here, since #110760 added no test for it. #### Tests `tests/integration/test_postgresql_protocol` drives the extended-query path with injection payloads and asserts the parameter is treated as data (the targeted secret table is never read), while normal string, numeric, quote-containing and NULL parameters keep working; it also covers the arity, portal-snapshot, `ReadyForQuery` and error-recovery contracts above at the wire level. `src/Core/tests/gtest_postgresql_protocol.cpp` covers message deserialization and parameter formatting directly. The pre-auth `CancelRequest` path (`KILL QUERY WHERE query_id = 'postgres:{:d}:{:d}'`) was reviewed: `process_id` and `secret_key` are `Int32` formatted with `{:d}`, so they cannot carry SQL and are not injectable. No change there.
