signals.title: Make storage key and skip-index expression types independent of type-affecting session settings
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109181 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `Bad cast` logical error (for example `Bad cast from ColumnVector<UInt32> to ColumnDecimal<DateTime64>`) that broke the next `INSERT` or mutation on a `MergeTree` table whose `ORDER BY`, `PRIMARY KEY`, `PARTITION BY` or skip index uses a function whose result type depends on a session setting (`enable_extended_results_for_datetime_functions`, `cast_keep_nullable`, `function_date_trunc_return_type_behavior`, `geo_distance_returns_float64_on_float64_arguments`, `function_json_value_return_type_allow_nullable`, `least_greatest_legacy_null_behavior`, `h3togeo_lon_lat_result_order`, `allow_lossy_numeric_supertype`, `use_variant_as_common_type`), after any metadata-changing `ALTER` ran with that setting at a different value. Key and skip-index expression types are now resolved against the server settings baseline, so they stay consistent with the data the storage writes. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109181 ### Description A `MergeTree` key or skip-index expression's result type must not depend on the transient session settings that happen to be set when someone (re)builds the metadata. Several settings change the result type of a key expression, for example `enable_extended_results_for_datetime_functions` (`toStartOf*`/`toMonday`/... on `Date32`/`DateTime64` return `DateTime64`/`Date32` instead of `DateTime`/`Date`) and `cast_keep_nullable` (`CAST` and `to<T>OrDefault` over a `Nullable` argument return `Nullable(T)` instead of `T`). `KeyDescription::data_types` is recomputed with whatever context runs `CREATE`/`ALTER`, so running any metadata-changing `ALTER` (even `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COMMENT`) with such a setting flipped changes the in-memory key type. The storage keeps producing the key column through `getCombinedIndicesExpression`, which analyzes the same AST with the storage's own context, so the produced column type diverges from the serializer's expected type and the primary-index writer aborts with `Bad cast ...` on the next `INSERT` or mutation, leaving the table broken until the server reloads its metadata. Reproducer from the issue (aborts in debug/sanitizer builds, throws in release): ```sql CREATE TABLE t0 (c1 Date, c2 DateTime64) ENGINE = MergeTree() ORDER BY (toStartOfTenMinutes(c2)); SET enable_extended_results_for_datetime_functions = 1; INSERT INTO TABLE t0 (c2, c1) VALUES ('2118-08-18 18:05:25', '1998-10-21'); ALTER TABLE t0 CLEAR COLUMN c1; ``` The same divergence through `cast_keep_nullable`, which is how `MasterCI` `BuzzHouse (amd_debug)` hits it (STID 3520-704a, `Bad cast from type DB::ColumnVector<unsigned long> to DB::ColumnNullable`, report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=d5011f599b4c9c13bf17baaf58e53d84fd09eac3&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=BuzzHouse%20%28amd_debug%29). `toUInt64OrDefault` is a `FunctionCastOrDefault`, so its return type follows `cast_keep_nullable`; BuzzHouse reaches the metadata recompute through `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COLUMN ... MODIFY SETTING` and needs `allow_nullable_key = 1`, which its fuzzer server config sets: ```sql SET cast_keep_nullable = 0; CREATE TABLE t (a Int32, b Nullable(Int32)) ENGINE = MergeTree() ORDER BY (a, toUInt64OrDefault(b)) SETTINGS allow_nullable_key = 1; ALTER TABLE t MODIFY COLUMN a MODIFY SETTING max_compress_block_size = 16 SETTINGS cast_keep_nullable = 1; INSERT INTO t VALUES (2, 2); ``` Fix: analyze key and skip-index expressions in a context where every enumerated type-affecting setting is pinned to the server settings baseline (the global default/system profile, including any `compatibility`), via the new `createKeyExpressionContext` used by `KeyDescription::getKeyFromAST`, `IndexDescription::initExpressionInfo`, `IndicesDescription::getSingleExpressionForIndices` and `getCombinedIndicesExpression`. The key type then does not depend on the session that (re)builds the metadata, and it matches what a fresh metadata reload resolves, because the reload path already runs under that same baseline. The explicit `toStartOf*Extended` function family (#108002) is the supported way to define an intentionally extended key. Keys whose expression is re-analyzed in the query context at read time must not be canonicalized, otherwise validation would accept a configuration the runtime filter then breaks. `KeyDescription::getKeyFromAST` therefore takes a `canonicalize_key_types` flag, set to false for the sampling key (its read-time filter is built in `MergeTreeDataSelectExecutor`), for the `parallel_replicas_custom_key` validator, and for object-storage hive-style partitioning (the partition value is a path string produced and parsed back under the query context, not a persisted binary key file). Note for reviewers on compatibility: a table declared with e.g. `ORDER BY toStartOfTenMinutes(dt64)` under `enable_extended_results_for_datetime_functions = 1` never had a persistable `DateTime64` key anyway (the type reverts to `DateTime` on restart, and the on-disk primary index is always written with the baseline type), so this makes an already-inconsistent state consistent rather than removing a working configuration. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109196&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/109196](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F109196+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix LOGICAL_ERROR when a column transformer sets an alias on an asterisk
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109214 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109214 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a `LOGICAL_ERROR` ("Can't set alias of ... of QualifiedAsterisk", server abort in debug and sanitizer builds) when a column transformer that assigns a name (`APPLY` with a name prefix, or `REPLACE`) is applied to an expression that expands to an asterisk or `COLUMNS` matcher, for example `SELECT * APPLY (x -> t.*, 'p_')`. Such queries now return a clear `BAD_ARGUMENTS` error. Also fixes wrong column names when an `APPLY` name prefix and a second matcher appear in one `SELECT`, and makes the analyzer honour the name prefix consistently with the old analyzer. ### Description Found by the AST fuzzer (`AST fuzzer (amd_debug, targeted)`, STID `1493-3ccb`) on the query `SELECT DISTINCT * APPLY (x -> compound_value.*, 'f_') FROM test_table__fuzz_23 FINAL PREWHERE ...`: report https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109082&sha=62139e418dccb913277c31a483b2547ed4e230e7&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29 Root cause of the abort: `ASTColumnsApplyTransformer::transform` and `ASTColumnsReplaceTransformer::transform` call `setAlias` on the transformer's result node, but only `ASTWithAlias` nodes support aliases. When the `APPLY` lambda body (or the `REPLACE` replacement) expands to an `ASTAsterisk` / `ASTQualifiedAsterisk` / `ASTColumnsMatcher`, the default `IAST::setAlias` throws `LOGICAL_ERROR`. A `setTransformerAlias` helper now checks for `ASTWithAlias` first and otherwise throws `BAD_ARGUMENTS`, mirroring the existing precedent for asterisks with column aliases in `CREATE VIEW`. That path is the old analyzer. The default analyzer silently dropped the `APPLY` name prefix instead, so it also had to learn the old analyzer's naming, and the same bare-matcher case had to be rejected there. Two further naming cases fixed while implementing that: - A name prefix must stay inside its own transformer chain. Matched column nodes are shared (one node per column), so publishing the prefixed name on the matched node leaked it into a later matcher: `SELECT * APPLY (x -> x, 'p_'), *` reported `p_a p_a`, and the same query with the two matchers swapped reported `a p_a`. The prefixed name now goes on a private copy. Values were never affected. - A chained prefix accumulates onto the previous transformer's display name (`q_p_a`, `q_identity(a).1`) rather than the original column name. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109223&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/109223](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F109223+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix wrong results with parallel_hash JOIN and read-in-order-through-join
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109216 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110671 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed wrong results (silently dropped or mis-grouped rows) when `join_algorithm = 'parallel_hash'` is combined with a sorted consumer such as `optimize_aggregation_in_order`, `optimize_distinct_in_order` or `LIMIT BY`. With several join slots and a single-level hash map, `ConcurrentHashJoin` scatters the left block across slots, so the read-in-order-through-join optimization must no longer advertise the left sort order in that case. ### Description The `partial_merge` / `prefer_partial_merge` half of this PR has since been fixed on master by #110671, which added `IJoin::preservesLeftBlockOrder()` (defaulting to `true`) plus the `MergeJoin` / `JoinSwitcher` overrides and the `findReadingStep` gate. What remains here is a different carrier, and it is still a live wrong result on master. **`parallel_hash` (`ConcurrentHashJoin`) with several slots and a single-level map.** It inherits the `true` default from master, but `chooseMethod` leaves a key that materializes to one or two bytes (`key8` / `key16`) single-level - wider keys, including string and fixed-string ones, get a two-level variant. For a single-level map `joinBlock` scatters the left block across slots and `ConcurrentHashJoinResult` emits slot 0, then slot 1, and so on, so equal left-key values stop being contiguous while `findReadingStep` still installs the ordered read. Measured on master (`54dee101`, which contains #110671) against a debug build of this branch: ```sql CREATE TABLE t3 (a UInt32, j UInt8) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY (a, j); CREATE TABLE t4 (j UInt8, v UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY j; INSERT INTO t3 SELECT intDiv(number, 8)::UInt32, (number % 8)::UInt8 FROM numbers(64); INSERT INTO t4 SELECT (number % 8)::UInt8, number FROM numbers(8); SET join_algorithm = 'parallel_hash', max_threads = 8, optimize_aggregation_in_order = 1, max_bytes_before_external_join = 0, max_bytes_ratio_before_external_join = 0; SELECT a, count() FROM t3 LEFT ALL JOIN t4 ON t3.j = t4.j GROUP BY a ORDER BY a; ``` Master returns `1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 57`; the correct answer is 8 per group, which this branch returns. Ground truth was confirmed three independent ways (`optimize_aggregation_in_order = 0`, `join_algorithm = 'hash'`, `query_plan_read_in_order_through_join = 0`). The fix flips the `IJoin::preservesLeftBlockOrder()` default from `true` (fail-open) to `false` (fail-closed) and makes each join that really does stream the left side through once opt in: `HashJoin`, `DirectKeyValueJoin`, `ConstantJoin`, `PasteJoin` unconditionally, and `ConcurrentHashJoin` only when it does not scatter (`slots == 1 || twoLevelMapIsUsed()`). Flipping the default is what makes the contract hold by property rather than by accident. On master `FullSortingMergeJoin` has no override, so it inherits `true` - it is safe today only because `JoinStepLogical` inserts a `Sorting (Sort Left before JOIN)` step that `findReadingStep` does not descend through. That is a property of the current plan shape, not of the join, so any future plan change would silently reintroduce a wrong result. Under the fail-closed default it is safe by property. Precision was verified in both directions, so the stricter default does not cost the optimization anywhere it was previously correct: a two-level `UInt64` key still reads in order, a single-slot (`max_threads = 1`) `parallel_hash` join still reads in order, and `hash` / `direct` are unchanged. `GraceHashJoin` and `SpillingHashJoin` remain excluded through `hasDelayedBlocks()` as before. `topKThroughJoin.cpp` keeps its explicit `FullSortingMergeJoin` type check for its own mode 2 (a pre-JOIN `Sort` on the preserved input); its comment is updated to say the `preservesLeftBlockOrder()` read already covers that join and the type check is now belt-and-braces. Tests: `04498_distinct_in_order_partial_merge_join` fails on current master on exactly the `parallel_hash` block and passes here, so it is a live regression test rather than a restatement of #110671. `04500_read_in_order_through_constant_join` covers the `ConstantJoin` and `DirectKeyValueJoin` opt-ins, and `04500_limit_by_in_order_partial_merge_join` guards the `LIMIT BY` consumer. Each assertion was verified by mutation: with the corresponding override removed the assertion flips. All of them pin the whole read-in-order trio (`optimize_read_in_order`, `query_plan_read_in_order`, `query_plan_read_in_order_through_join`), since the stateless runner randomizes all three and a drawn `0` would make the plan assertions blind. #109216 is downgraded to `Related:` because the shape it reports (`prefer_partial_merge` + `optimize_distinct_in_order`) no longer reproduces on master after #110671; its reproducer now returns the correct 6 rows over repeated runs. This PR covers the sibling `parallel_hash` carrier of the same class, so it should not auto-close that issue.

signals.title: Respect `date_time_overflow_behavior` for numeric temporal casts
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/101131 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110459 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/101512 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Makes `date_time_overflow_behavior` take effect for numeric casts to `Date`, `Date32`, `DateTime` and `Time`. The `throw` and `saturate` paths were dead code for these targets, so an out-of-range value was always silently reinterpreted or truncated. Four results also change under the default `ignore` mode, where the previous value came from a code path that could not be reached: an out-of-range numeric `INSERT ... VALUES` expression for a `Date` or `Date32` column now clamps to the boundary instead of storing `1970-01-01`; a wide integer (`Int128`/`UInt128`/`Int256`/`UInt256`) cast to `DateTime` or `Time` now saturates instead of being truncated, so `toDateTime32(toInt128(99999999999999999999999999))` gives the maximum rather than `1970-02-04 08:19:58`; `inf` and `NaN` cast to `Date32` now raise `CANNOT_CONVERT_TYPE` as they already did for the other three targets, instead of saturating to a boundary date; and an out-of-range literal for an exact target such as `DROP PARTITION` or a strict `IN` raises `ARGUMENT_OUT_OF_BOUND` rather than addressing a clamped partition. ### Description `ConvertImpl` instantiated the numeric-to-temporal transforms with the compile-time constant `default_date_time_overflow_behavior` (`ignore`) instead of the runtime setting, so their `throw` and `saturate` branches were never instantiated. Threading the runtime value in makes them reachable, exposing three latent defects there: the rejected value was formatted with a narrowing `static_cast<Int64>`, undefined for a huge, infinite or `NaN` float (floats are now widened to `double`); `NaN` passed every range comparison into a narrowing cast, so it is guarded explicitly; and the clamp narrowed to `time_t` before `std::min`, so a `UInt64` above `INT64_MAX` wrapped negative and gave `1970` instead of the maximum. Three further paths ignored the setting and account for the default-mode changes above. The wide integer types missed every branch of the `DateTime` dispatch and fell through to `convertNumericGeneral`, which truncates. `convertFieldToType` (the `VALUES`/`IN` coercion path) serves two kinds of caller, so in `ignore` mode it keys on the exactness flag: an exact target gets the canonical storage value, while value materialization clamps like `CAST`. `values()` is the exception: built with a default `FormatSettings`, it keeps clamping while `CAST` raises under `throw`, and the test pins that divergence. `Date32` was the only target that accepted a non-finite float. The numeric `Time` dispatch and its bounds already landed on the base as a714d76b341fa8c from an earlier round here. PR 110459 (merged) is reconciled in this branch.

signals.title: Fix EmbeddedRocksDB backup to include table data
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109213 --> Closes: #109213 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `BACKUP` of `EmbeddedRocksDB` tables. Previously only the table metadata was stored in the backup and the actual data was silently dropped, so `RESTORE` produced an empty table. The backup now includes all key-value pairs and restores them correctly. ### Description `StorageEmbeddedRocksDB` did not override `backupData()` / `restoreDataFromBackup()`, so it fell through to the no-op `IStorage` defaults: `BACKUP` captured only `metadata/<db>/<table>.sql` and no data files, and `RESTORE` reported success while producing an empty table (silent data loss). Reproduction on the current binary before the fix: ```sql CREATE TABLE rdb (k UInt64, v String) ENGINE = EmbeddedRocksDB PRIMARY KEY k; INSERT INTO rdb SELECT number, 'val_' || toString(number) FROM numbers(1000); BACKUP TABLE rdb TO File('rdb_backup'); -- backup contains only metadata/default/rdb.sql DROP TABLE rdb SYNC; RESTORE TABLE rdb FROM File('rdb_backup'); SELECT count() FROM rdb; -- 0 (data lost) ``` #### Fix Implement the two backup entrypoints as a logical dump, following the existing `StorageKeeperMap` / `StorageMemory` pattern: - `backupData()` iterates every key-value pair (under a shared lock, over an implicit RocksDB snapshot for a consistent view) and writes them as length-prefixed binary records into a single compressed `data.bin` backup entry, produced lazily via `IBackupEntriesLazyBatch`. - `restoreDataFromBackup()` reads `data.bin` back and re-inserts the pairs with a `rocksdb::WriteBatch`. Restoring into a non-empty table is rejected unless `allow_non_empty_tables` is set, matching the other engines. RocksDB already stores keys and values as raw serialized strings, so the bytes are copied verbatim; every primary-key layout (single or composite) and value type (including `Nullable`, `Array`, `Map`) round-trips with no type-specific handling. This integrates with the whole backup ecosystem (File/S3/Disk, compression, encryption, incremental backups). A stateless regression test (`04401_rocksdb_backup_restore`) covers the round-trip, the non-empty-table guard, composite primary keys, complex value types, and empty tables.

signals.title: Enforce TABLE ENGINE grant in table functions
signals.text:
### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a privilege-escalation gap where the `executable`/`executablePool` table functions did not enforce the `TABLE ENGINE ON Executable` grant. With `table_engines_require_grant` enabled, a user denied `CREATE TABLE ... ENGINE = Executable` could still run the same server-side script via `SELECT ... FROM executable(...)`. These table functions now require `GRANT TABLE ENGINE ON Executable`, matching `CREATE TABLE`. ### Description `executable`/`executablePool` run a server-side script under the ClickHouse OS user. Table functions checked only source access (`READ`/`WRITE ON S3`/`URL`/...) and `CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE`, never the `TABLE ENGINE` grant `CREATE TABLE` enforces via `InterpreterCreateQuery`. So with `table_engines_require_grant = true`, a user without `GRANT TABLE ENGINE ON Executable` was correctly denied `CREATE TABLE ... ENGINE = Executable(...)` but could still reach the same `StorageExecutable` capability via `SELECT * FROM executable('sh -c ...', ...)`. Bounded, not RCE: needs `table_engines_require_grant = true` plus a pre-existing executable under `user_scripts_path`, and runs as the ClickHouse OS user; not exploitable on Cloud (setting force-disabled, no write primitive there). It is a prerequisite for enabling the setting, which otherwise denies `ENGINE = Executable` while leaving `executable` open. **Fix.** New `ITableFunction::checkEngineAccess`, called from both `execute` and `getActualTableStructureWithAccess`, so `SELECT`, `DESCRIBE` and `CREATE TABLE AS` are gated when the table function is named directly. It is scoped by a new opt-in virtual `requiresTableEngineGrant`, `true` only on `TableFunctionExecutable` (engine `Executable`, which also backs `executablePool`), and is a no-op when the setting is off. Deliberately **not** gated: wrapper/proxy engines (`merge`, `loop`, `dictionary`, `view`, `remote`), already gated by delegated data access (`SELECT`/`SHOW COLUMNS` on the wrapped table, dictionary access, row policies) - gating them would be a new requirement and breaks `03680_loop_table_function_access_check`, `04411_loop_table_function_describe_access_check`, `03928_loop_row_policy` and `03273_dictionary_rbac`; pseudo-engines (`numbers`, `values`), which have no storage engine; and source functions (`s3`, `url`, `file`), gated on the source axis by the filter-aware `checkSourceAccess`.
One structure-only path deliberately left out of scope (viewIfPermitted) One structure-only path is out of scope: `viewIfPermitted` resolves its `ELSE` branch through the fallback's raw `getActualTableStructure` (`TableFunctionViewIfPermitted.cpp:92-95`), so `DESCRIBE viewIfPermitted(... ELSE executable(...))` answers without the grant check. It discloses nothing (`executable` takes its structure as an explicit literal argument, so the answer is what the caller typed) and never reaches the script - execution goes via `else_table_function->execute`, which does check, so nested `SELECT` and `CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT` are denied. That path bypasses master's own `checkSourceAccess` identically, verified against a pristine-master build, so it is pre-existing and belongs in its own PR.
Tests in `tests/integration/test_grant_and_revoke/test_with_table_engine_grant.py`: `executable` `SELECT`/`DESCRIBE` denied without the grant, allowed with it, plus a regression asserting wrapper (`null`, `merge`), pseudo (`numbers`, `values`) and source (`url` with a source grant) table functions stay ungated on `TABLE ENGINE`.

signals.title: Add PCAP input format for reading packet captures
signals.text: # Add PCAP input format for reading packet captures ## (Human) Introduction As someone who works with ClickHouse but also occasionally opens a pcap in Wireshark, I've always had a wish to be able to do some quick stats on a pcap using ClickHouse SQL. Especially for large files, I always thought it would also be nice to be able to persist them in a MergeTree, so they don't have to be re-scanned every time. So this is my first draft at making this a reality: adding PCAP as an (experimental) input format which can be read by Clickhouse directly (and consequently be ingested, as well). It currently only parses very basic stuff (mostly L2-L4), but this could be extended in the future (imagine having all Wireshark dissectors 😍 ) I realize this may be considered "unfinished" (in the sense: lacking features), but I wanted to open a PR and get feedback on the idea early on, to see if it was worth pursuing. Full transparency: this is basically 100% vibe-coded -- ideas and some design decisions are mine, but I didn't really write any code. Thanks Claude. In that spirit, here's the Claude-generated description including some notes that may be relevant to reviewers: ## AI-generated Overview Adds a `PCAP` input format that reads packet capture files (classic `pcap` and `pcapng`) and produces one row per packet with decoded L2–L4 fields — timestamp, lengths, link type, the ordered protocol chain, Ethernet/IPv4/IPv6/TCP/UDP header fields, the L4 payload, and the raw frame. Modelled structurally on the `DWARF` format. Parsing uses `libtins` for dissection and `libpcap` for reading the capture container, added as contrib submodules behind a new `USE_PCAP` flag (`libpcap` built offline-only with pre-generated BPF grammar/scanner; WPA2/ACK-tracking disabled to avoid OpenSSL and Boost.ICL). Includes documentation and a stateless test with small Wireshark sample captures. > Transparency note: this PR was vibe-coded with Claude (Anthropic `claude-opus-4-8`) in an agentic workflow, with human review and direction. The AI co-authorship is recorded via `Co-authored-by` trailers on the commits. ### Notes for reviewers - **New contrib submodules:** `libtins` (v4.5) and `libpcap` (1.10.5), gated behind `ENABLE_PCAP`/`USE_PCAP` (on by default with `ENABLE_LIBRARIES`). They use the upstream repositories directly (not ClickHouse forks). - **libpcap build:** built offline-only using the `null` capture backend (no live capture / remote / optional backends). Its BPF grammar/scanner are pre-generated with bison/flex and checked in under `contrib/libpcap-cmake/generated/` so the build needs no flex/bison. A hand-written `config.h` targets Linux/glibc. - **libtins build:** hand-written `config.h`; WPA2 decryption and ACK tracking are disabled to avoid pulling in OpenSSL and Boost.ICL for now. Deeper protocol dissection can be layered on later. - **Disabled-build safety:** the format is wrapped in `#if USE_PCAP` with empty registration stubs, so linking succeeds when the feature is off (e.g. fasttest builds with `ENABLE_LIBRARIES=0`). The stateless test is tagged `no-fasttest` for the same reason. - **Test fixtures license:** the capture files under `tests/queries/0_stateless/data_pcap/` are sample captures from the Wireshark test suite (GPL-2.0); provenance is recorded in that directory's `README.md`. Happy to swap them for self-authored synthetic captures if the GPL-2.0 provenance is a concern. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): New input format `PCAP` for reading network packet captures (`pcap` and `pcapng`), producing one row per packet with decoded Ethernet/IP/TCP/UDP fields, the protocol chain, payload, and raw frame.

signals.title: Require a join subquery alias only when it removes a real ambiguity
signals.text: `joined_subquery_requires_alias = 1` (the default) rejected every unaliased subquery, table function or union used in a multi-table join, even when the missing alias could not cause any ambiguity. That is stricter than necessary: an alias only serves to qualify a column, so it is only needed when the unaliased table expression exposes a column whose name also occurs in another table expression of the same join. `validateJoinTableExpressionWithoutAlias` now throws `ALIAS_REQUIRED` only on such a name collision (computed with the existing `getColumnsFromTableExpression` helper over the sibling table expressions), and otherwise allows the missing alias. Genuine ambiguities involving non-sibling table expressions are still caught later by the normal `AMBIGUOUS_IDENTIFIER` resolution, exactly as they are for ordinary tables. This lets standard queries such as TPC-DS q14 (whose `cross_items` derived table has no correlation name) run without setting `joined_subquery_requires_alias = 0`: ```sql SELECT i_item_sk FROM item, (SELECT iss.i_brand_id AS brand_id FROM store_sales, item AS iss ...) WHERE i_brand_id = brand_id; -- no shared column name -> no alias needed ``` Notes: - Validation in `resolveJoin`/`resolveCrossJoin` is moved to run after all table expressions of the join are resolved, so sibling columns are known when the collision is checked. - The change is purely permissive: it never turns a previously-succeeding query into an error. When the columns of any side cannot be determined it falls back to the old strict behavior. - Only the analyzer is affected; the deprecated non-analyzer path keeps the stricter behavior. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): With `joined_subquery_requires_alias = 1` (the default), the analyzer now rejects an unaliased subquery or table function in a join only when the missing alias would make one of its columns unreachable, for example because the name collides with another joined table expression or is shadowed by an in-scope alias; otherwise the query is allowed. If the analyzer cannot determine the exposed names up front, it keeps the old strict behavior. Unambiguous queries, such as some standard TPC-DS queries, no longer require adding an alias. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109368&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/109368](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F109368+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Size parallel replicas mark_segment_size by active replica count
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107805 --> Related: #107805 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Parallel replicas now size the automatic `parallel_replicas_mark_segment_size` by the number of active replicas, consistent with the reading coordinator, so registered-but-inactive replicas no longer skew segment sizing. ### Description Follow-up to #107805 (the optional `total_nodes_count` / `mark_segment_size` alignment noted in review). #107805 made the parallel replicas reading coordinator size itself by the number of *active* replicas (excluding registered-but-inactive ones), so mark segments are not assigned to replicas that never participate. The automatic `mark_segment_size` heuristic in `ReadFromMergeTree`, however, still derived its work-distribution denominator from `getAllNodeCount()` (the *registered* count via `ParallelReadingExtension::total_nodes_count`). When a replica was registered but inactive the two sizings disagreed. This sources `ParallelReadingExtension::total_nodes_count` from the active replica count through a shared `ClusterProxy::getActiveReplicasCountForParallelReplicas` helper that mirrors the coordinator's sizing exactly: the active count when liveness is known, the registered count when it is not (or when it does not line up with the cluster definition), and a zero-active safety net that falls back to the registered count. `total_nodes_count` feeds only `chooseSegmentSize`, whose result is clamped to `{128, 1024, 16384}` and is never used for indexing, so this cannot go out of range (replica numbering stays bounded by the registered count) and can only make segments smaller, which balances work no worse. The existing integration test `test_parallel_replicas_skip_inactive_replicas` is extended to assert the segment-sizing heuristic sees the active replica count (2), not the registered count (3), when one of three replicas is stopped. Verified the added assertion fails before this change and passes after; the `all_groups` sibling test is unaffected. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109377&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/109377](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F109377+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix LOGICAL_ERROR in full_sorting_merge JOIN when sharding stream counts diverge
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> No related open issue found. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `LOGICAL_ERROR` ("Join is supported only for pipelines with one output port") that could abort the server in debug/sanitizer builds (and raise an exception in release builds) for a `full_sorting_merge` JOIN when `query_plan_join_shard_by_pk_ranges` is enabled and the two join sides end up with a different number of streams. ### Description Found by the CI stress / serverfuzz jobs. Recurs on current master code across several unrelated runs. CI reports (canonical URLs, exact commit + check): - master serverfuzz (first sighting): https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=5e67948f8fe5c3dd9003dac755192b4ea62b24e3&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28experimental%2C%20serverfuzz%2C%20arm_asan_ubsan%2C%20s3%29 - 26.6 release branch, `Stress test (arm_msan)`: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=26.6&sha=3babd82fe36c262d5aa12a71cd4823d118f7e894&name_0=ReleaseBranchCI&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_msan%29 - `Stress test (amd_msan)` (sha 33a66e1c6316): https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=104431&sha=33a66e1c6316109534074c05689611c3dd0f0a28&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_msan%29 Error: `Logical error: Join is supported only for pipelines with one output port, got N and M`. Stack: `QueryPipelineBuilder::joinPipelinesYShaped` <- `JoinStep::updatePipeline` <- `QueryPlan::buildQueryPipeline` <- `executeQueryImpl` (plain query path). Root cause: with `query_plan_join_shard_by_pk_ranges = 1`, a `full_sorting_merge` JOIN whose keys are a primary-key prefix is planned for sharding. The pre-join `SortingStep` becomes `PartitionedFinishSorting`, which keeps several per-shard streams on each side. `JoinStep::updatePipeline` uses sharding only when both sides have the same number of streams (`use_sharding = !primary_key_sharding.empty() && streams(L) == streams(R)`). When the sides diverge in stream count (e.g. a `PREWHERE` changes how one side is split into layers, or an inner sharded join feeds a non-sharded outer join), it falls back to the plain YShaped pipeline. `joinPipelinesYShaped` required exactly one stream per side and threw. The comment there ("regular join pipeline handles different stream counts") is only true for `joinPipelinesRightLeft` (hash), not the YShaped merge-join path. Fix: in the fallback, merge each side back into a single sorted stream with a `MergingSortedTransform` keyed by the join keys before building the `MergeJoinTransform`. The inputs are already sorted by the join keys (Sort ... before JOIN), so a sorted merge preserves the order the merge join requires and the result is correct. The sharded fast path (equal stream counts) is unchanged. Deterministic reproducer: ```sql CREATE TABLE t (c0 UInt64, c1 UInt64, s String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY (c0, c1) SETTINGS index_granularity = 8; INSERT INTO t SELECT number, number % 10, 'x' FROM numbers(100); INSERT INTO t SELECT number + 100, number % 10, 'x' FROM numbers(100); INSERT INTO t SELECT number + 200, number % 10, 'x' FROM numbers(100); SELECT count() FROM t AS a ALL INNER JOIN t AS b ON b.c0 = a.c0 PREWHERE isNull(a.s) SETTINGS enable_analyzer = 1, join_algorithm = 'full_sorting_merge', query_plan_join_shard_by_pk_ranges = 1, max_threads = 8; ``` Verified: the reproducer aborts the server before the fix and returns cleanly after; results match the hash join (full row-by-row comparison, including the divergent 3-way case); existing sharding tests (03357, 03774, 04065, 03668) still pass. Regression test added: `04501_full_sorting_merge_join_shard_stream_divergence`.

signals.title: Fix force_index_by_date/force_primary_key INDEX_NOT_USED reading through a view with parallel replicas (serialize_query_plan = 0 stopgap)
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/108266 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a false-positive `INDEX_NOT_USED` error thrown when a query with `force_index_by_date` or `force_primary_key` reads through a view (or subquery) with parallel replicas enabled, even though the predicate covers the partition/primary key. The fix covers the default query transport (`serialize_query_plan = 0`); with `serialize_query_plan = 1` a follower can still throw — fixing that lane is deferred to plan-based parallel replicas. ### Description Closes: #108266 Reading through a view under parallel replicas threw `INDEX_NOT_USED` for `force_index_by_date` / `force_primary_key` even when the predicate covered the key: ```sql CREATE TABLE nginx (timestamp DateTime) ENGINE = MergeTree PARTITION BY toYYYYMMDD(timestamp) ORDER BY timestamp; CREATE VIEW v_nginx AS SELECT * FROM nginx; SELECT count() FROM v_nginx WHERE timestamp >= '2026-06-05 12:00:00' SETTINGS enable_parallel_replicas = 1, max_parallel_replicas = 3, cluster_for_parallel_replicas = 'default', parallel_replicas_for_non_replicated_merge_tree = 1, force_index_by_date = 1; -- Code: 277. INDEX_NOT_USED ``` Reading the base table directly, or the view without parallel replicas, worked. **Root cause.** `force_index_by_date` / `force_primary_key` are enforced on the MergeTree reading step (`MergeTreeDataSelectExecutor::filterPartsByPartition`, `ReadFromMergeTree::selectRangesToRead`), which must see the query's filter. When a table is read through a view under parallel replicas, the view is planned as its own inner query, so the outer `WHERE` stays in a `FilterStep` above the view boundary and never reaches the inner reading step. The key condition is then always unknown there, so both guards throw even though the outer filter is valid (the result was always correct, only the index-usage check was at the wrong layer). An explicit subquery does not hit this because the analyzer inlines it into a single plan; a view stays a separate reading step. **Fix.** The existing `parallel_replicas_filter_pushdown` mechanism already pushes the filter through the view boundary into the reading step. This change enables it automatically in `buildContext` when parallel replicas is used on the initiator and either guard is set, unless the user set the setting explicitly. The index is then genuinely used, the guards are enforced correctly (a covered predicate passes, and a genuinely unused index still throws), and parallel replicas stays enabled (no fallback, no no-op). **Scope and known limitation (`serialize_query_plan = 1`).** A follower receives the pushed filter only through the shipped query AST (`ReadFromParallelRemoteReplicasStep::initializePipeline` injects it via `addFilters`). With `serialize_query_plan = 1` (the "distributed plan" transport) the initiator ships a query plan that was serialized before the filter is pushed, and the follower runs that plan and ignores the rewritten AST — so a follower's reading step still does not see the predicate and the guards can still throw a false-positive `INDEX_NOT_USED` in that mode. Per review, this fix must not override `serialize_query_plan`, and force-carrying the predicate into the serialized plan would be new transport machinery out of scope for a stopgap. So this PR is explicitly a **`serialize_query_plan = 0` stopgap**: it fixes the default AST transport; the `serialize_query_plan = 1` lane is deferred to plan-based parallel replicas, where index pushdown into a view works automatically. The regression test pins `serialize_query_plan = 0` and documents the limitation in its header. The regression test covers positives (base table as a control; view, view-over-view, and aliased view, with each guard and both; view without parallel replicas as a control) and negatives (a predicate that does not use the key must still throw `INDEX_NOT_USED` through views, including nested views). Verified on a 3-replica loopback cluster: with `serialize_query_plan = 0` all positives pass and negatives throw; with `serialize_query_plan = 1` a follower still throws the documented false positive.

signals.title: Materialize sparse sort-key columns in FinishSortingTransform
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/106024 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a `Bad cast from type DB::ColumnSparse to DB::ColumnVector` logical error in `FinishSortingTransform` when reading in order and sorting by a key column that is serialized as `ColumnSparse` in some parts and dense in others. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) ### Description `FinishSortingTransform::consume()` accumulates chunks and, for each new chunk, binary-searches the previously stored chunk with `less()` (a raw `IColumn::compareAt`). It materialized only `ColumnReplicated` sort-key columns, unlike the base `SortingTransform`, which materializes sparse, const and replicated columns before building cursors. When read-in-order reads parts with mixed serialization, one chunk can carry a dense sort-key column and the next the same key as `ColumnSparse`. The cross-chunk compare then calls `ColumnVector<T>::doCompareAt` with a `ColumnSparse` rhs, whose `assert_cast` aborts in debug/sanitizer builds (a release build silently reads wrong memory): ``` Logical error: 'Bad cast from type DB::ColumnSparse to DB::ColumnVector<unsigned short>'. ColumnVector<unsigned short>::doCompareAt src/Columns/ColumnVector.h:157 (assert_cast.h:43) less<...> src/Core/SortCursor.h:756 FinishSortingTransform::consume(Chunk) src/Processors/Transforms/FinishSortingTransform.cpp:94 SortingTransform::work() src/Processors/Transforms/SortingTransform.cpp:385 ``` The fix materializes sparse sort-key columns alongside replicated ones in `consume()`, mirroring `IMergingAlgorithm::removeConstAndSparse` (applied at every merge site) and the base `SortingTransform`, which already does `convertToFullIfSparse` / `convertToFullIfConst` / `convertToFullColumnIfReplicated` before building sort cursors. Found by the AST fuzzer (STID 1499-2393) on `Stress test (amd_msan)`, mutating `tests/queries/0_stateless/02149_read_in_order_fixed_prefix.sql`. The crashing query was `SELECT toStartOfMonth(date) as d, i FROM t_read_in_order ORDER BY d DESC, -i LIMIT 5` where the read-in-order sort prefix `toStartOfMonth(date)` is a `Date` (UInt16); a part with an all-default `date` serialized it as `ColumnSparse`. CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=108944&sha=1d5aad9342028b0763311a57933f04087f43a6cd&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_msan%29 This is the `ColumnSparse` sibling of the `ColumnReplicated` case in #106024. Unlike that one, this reproduces deterministically: `src/Processors/tests/gtest_finish_sorting_sparse.cpp` aborts with the exact error above without this change and passes with it. There is no SQL regression test: the read-in-order plan always inserts a `MergingSortedTransform` before `FinishSortingTransform`, and that merge densifies every sort-key column (`IMergingAlgorithm::removeConstAndSparse`), so the mixed dense/sparse cross-chunk state cannot be reached from a query. No related open issue was found.

signals.title: Reserve memory for merges up front
signals.text: Add proactive memory reservation for background merges, enhancing the existing `merges_mutations_memory_usage_soft_limit` mechanism. `background_memory_tracker` measures memory that background tasks have *already* allocated, so `canEnqueueBackgroundTask` is purely reactive: when many merges are scheduled at the same time — for example right after a mutation produces many parts — their IO buffers are not allocated yet, all of them pass the gate, and only then grow their memory usage and collide. Every merge now estimates the memory of its input and output IO buffers (`CompactionStatistics::estimateNeededMemoryForMerge`) as the number of input column streams (over all source parts) times the read IO buffer size, plus the number of output column streams (of the result part) times the write IO buffer size. Object storage (S3) write buffers are large and double-buffered, so they are accounted separately. Since IO buffers only ever hold data that flows through them, the estimate is capped by the data volume of the merge (beyond the eagerly allocated per-stream compressor and file buffers, which honor adaptive write buffers): without this cap, a merge of tiny parts in a many-column table on object storage would reserve gigabytes it can never touch, and concurrent merges would saturate the soft limit and starve each other. The merge reserves this amount at start (`MergeMemoryReservation`) and releases it when it finishes. A merge that will certainly run the vertical algorithm is priced by the streams that are alive at once (the merging columns, one gathering column at a time, and up to `max_merge_delayed_streams_for_parallel_write` delayed streams) rather than all output streams concurrently, and a stream whose data volume is not derivable from the source parts (a rebuilt projection, a `DEFAULT`-filled column of variable size) is priced at the buffers its writer allocates before any data flows through it (its compressor block and file buffer) plus a projected-volume bound, rather than at any multipart upload size - a multipart writer starts from the buffer size its caller passes and grows it only with the data written into it, leaving further growth to the reactive tracker — over-reservation starves all merges, while under-reservation merely degrades to the reactive behavior of the current code for that stream. `canEnqueueBackgroundTask` now consults both the actual usage and the reservation: - a non-replicated background merge reserves at selection and is not scheduled when the reservation would exceed the limit (it retries later); once `CurrentlyMergingPartsTagger` chooses the actual destination disk, the reservation is corrected if the pre-selection guess made from the source parts was wrong, and a merge that waited in the background queue re-prices its reservation at task start against the destination disk's live multipart upload settings (a config reload could have raised them), as the replicated path does. Whether a background merge runs as a `ReplacingMergeTree` cleanup merge is decided at selection and carried to the scheduler, so a row-reducing cleanup merge is priced as one; - a replicated merge, already committed to run locally, reserves unconditionally at execution so the reservation still throttles selection of further merges; - a user-initiated merge (`OPTIMIZE`) also reserves unconditionally, so it is throttled by the gate for other merges but can never be silently skipped by it. A single merge whose estimate exceeds the whole limit is always allowed to proceed alone, so progress is never blocked. Adds the `MergesMutationsMemoryReservation` metric for observability, a `gtest` for the reservation accounting, and stateless tests: a smoke test and a regression test that `OPTIMIZE TABLE ... FINAL` merges everything down to a single part under a pathologically small soft limit instead of silently doing nothing. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Background merges now reserve the memory of their input/output IO buffers up front against `merges_mutations_memory_usage_soft_limit`, so that scheduling many merges at once (for example right after a mutation) can no longer oversubscribe memory as they all start. A user-initiated `OPTIMIZE` is never silently skipped by this mechanism. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109433&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/109433](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F109433+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix split-dependent hash of JSON/Object columns
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109428 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `JSON`/`Object`/`Dynamic` columns hashing logically equal values differently depending on their physical layout: how `JSON`/`Object` paths were split between dynamic subcolumns and shared data, or whether a `Dynamic` value sat in a typed or the shared variant. Hash-based joins on such a key silently missed matches, and a `grace_hash` spill could raise a `LOGICAL_ERROR` ("Invalid state transition"). A `JSON` key needed no non-default setting; `Dynamic` also required `allow_dynamic_type_in_join_keys`. ### Description **The implementation changed since the earlier approval here, so please treat it as needing a fresh look.** The approved version hashed canonical `serializeValueIntoArena` bytes and cost up to +568% CPU; this one produces none. Both measured below. `computeHashInto` is the per-row weak hash behind the in-memory scatter paths (sharded aggregation, `grace_hash` bucketing, window `PARTITION BY`, join scatter). For `JSON`/`Object` and `Dynamic` it hashed the physical layout: `ColumnDynamic` forwarded to `ColumnVariant`, which hashes a shared-variant value by its serialized blob but a typed one by the column's representation; `ColumnObject` chained sub-columns in section order, so a path's contribution moved with it. Both splits follow insertion history and can change across a temp-file round-trip, while `compareAt` already treats the representations as equal. `JSON` hits this at default settings, since `hasDynamicType` misses its inner `Dynamic`. `ColumnDynamic::computeHashInto` forwards to `ColumnVariant` as master does, then overwrites only shared-discriminator rows with the leaf hash the value would have when typed. `ColumnObject::computeHashInto` folds `(path, value)` over the sorted union of the dynamic paths and `shared_data`, one cursor per row. `updateHashFast` and `updateHashWithValueRange` stay layout-dependent. `04505_json_object_hash_split_invariance` checks that equal values with different layouts match under the three hash joins, collapse under `GROUP BY`/`DISTINCT`/`uniqExact`, and that a spill flushes real payload rather than only constructing buckets: six assertions fail on master, all pass here. Three `ComputeHashInto` gtests cover the per-row hash and scratch state SQL cannot see. `ShuffleSendStep` shuffles rows to remote workers with this hash and marks no basis in its serialized step, so mixed versions could disagree on a shuffle key. Capability gate, or unsupported anyway? <details><summary>Provenance and performance</summary> Found by the AST fuzzer on #109428 as `Invalid state transition, expected WRITING_BLOCKS, got JOINING_BLOCKS` in `GraceHashJoin::FileBucket`, STID 3913-4579 ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109428&sha=15a6faf088a1b097b3ed56c69ec1fb4d5d602d17&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%29)): a key re-hashing into an earlier bucket mid-spill violates that state machine. Release-shaped build, three arms from one revision (master with these files reverted; the approved implementation; this one), `UserTimeMicroseconds` min over 11 alternating reps; all arms agreed on all 12 workloads first. | workload | vs master | vs appr. | |---|---|---| | JSON `grace_hash`, no shared | +2.8% | -61.2% | | JSON `grace_hash`, mixed | +8.2% | -33.8% | | JSON `grace_hash`, all shared | +11.7% | +6.5% | | window JSON, no shared | +12.8% | -88.3% | | window JSON, mixed | **-10.6%** | -1.7% | | window JSON, 4 shared | +51.5% | -46.8% | | `Dynamic` `grace_hash` | +44.3% | -34.3% | | `Dynamic`, 100% shared | +70.3% | -1.2% | Non-JSON controls are flat and `ArenaAlloc*` matches master. Making a byte-producing basis cheap failed three times: even hoisting the buffer so the block allocated almost nothing still cost +1253%. The residual tracks the shared representation only: each shared value pays one decode, one leaf hash, one fresh scratch column. Of the worst arm's +70.3%, about +30.4% is that scratch reset (+24.9%, +18.5% on the next two). It uses `cloneEmpty()` rather than `popBack` because `popBack` is a row operation: `ColumnLowCardinality::popBack` drops indexes but not the dictionary, which `computeHashInto` re-hashes in full per row, and `ColumnVariant` nests the shape. Conditioning it on a measured property of the scratch column did not survive review, so it stays unconditional. The cliff is bounded per `computeHashInto` call, not by the table; a 5k-40k ladder is linear. </details>

signals.title: Native Google Cloud Storage integration (google-cloud-cpp)
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added an experimental native Google Cloud Storage integration built on the Google Cloud C++ SDK (`google-cloud-cpp`, the GCS JSON API), as an alternative to the existing S3-compatibility path. Enable it with the new `use_native_gcs` setting for the `gcs` table function and dynamic `disk(...)` definitions, or configure a MergeTree storage disk with `object_storage_type: gcs`. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes Documented in `docs/reference/functions/table-functions/gcs.mdx` (new "Native GCS integration" section). --- ## Description ClickHouse currently talks to GCS **only through its S3-compatible XML API** (the AWS SDK against a `storage.googleapis.com` endpoint, plus a cluster of GCS quirk-toggles in the S3 client). This PR adds a first-class native backend on top of the already-vendored `google-cloud-cpp` storage client. **Opt-in, non-breaking.** The `gcs()` table function and dynamic disks select the native backend only with the new experimental `use_native_gcs` setting (default `false`); otherwise they retain S3 compatibility and HMAC keys. `ENGINE = GCS` remains on the existing compatibility path. ### What's added - `ObjectStorageType::GCS` + `GCSObjectStorage : IObjectStorage` (`src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/ObjectStorages/GCS/`), with `ReadBufferFromGCS`/`WriteBufferFromGCS` over the SDK's `ObjectReadStream`/`ObjectWriteStream` (ranged seeks, resumable uploads), native listing, `RewriteObject`-based copy, `DeleteObject`, `GetObjectMetadata`. - Registered as the `gcs` object-storage type + a `gcs` disk-type alias, so MergeTree data can live natively on GCS (`type: object_storage, object_storage_type: gcs`). - `StorageGCSConfiguration` (reuses `StorageS3Configuration`'s argument parsing) and a `TableFunctionGCS` selector that picks native vs S3-compat by the `use_native_gcs` setting. - Auth mirrors the compat surface on the native side: Application Default Credentials, service-account JSON, the `google_adc_*` OAuth refresh-token flow (reusing `IO/GCPOAuth`), anonymous / `NOSIGN`, and a REST endpoint override for the GCS emulator. - `USE_GOOGLE_CLOUD` is now exposed in `system.build_options`. ### Testing - Every changed/new translation unit compiles against the real headers and the vendored SDK (`USE_GOOGLE_CLOUD=1`, `USE_AWS_S3=1`). - Unit test for endpoint parsing (`gtest_gcs_endpoint`). - Stateless test for the setting wiring (`04502_use_native_gcs_setting`). - Integration test `test_native_gcs` runs against a `fake-gcs-server` emulator (a new `with_gcs` helper in `cluster.py`): `gcs()` INSERT/SELECT + glob with `use_native_gcs=1`, and a MergeTree-on-GCS-disk round trip. Note: `fake-gcs-server` speaks the GCS API (unlike minio, which is S3-only). The module is skipped on builds without the SDK. ### Known follow-ups - `GCSObjectStorage::iterate()` currently materializes the full listing (a lazy paginating iterator like S3's is a future optimization). - The `google_adc_*` refresh-token access token is minted eagerly (no auto-refresh yet for long-lived disks). - `readSmallObjectAndGetObjectMetadata` uses the base default (relevant only for a future native Iceberg-over-GCS path, which is not wired here). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109455&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/109455](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F109455+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Log tolerated connection failures to remote MySQL/PostgreSQL databases as warnings instead of errors
signals.text: Fix CI upgrade test failure: Example failing report — Upgrade check (amd_release) on the unrelated PR https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108255: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=108255&sha=28ca539bd4bf66de37e388238de45d840bc30c52&name_0=PR&name_1=Upgrade%20check%20%28amd_release%29 (`Error message in clickhouse-server.log (see upgrade_error_messages.txt)` with the `getTablesIterator` line above; the report shows green now because the check passed on a later rerun — which is exactly the flaky-victim pattern). **Problem.** A `DatabasePostgreSQL` or `DatabaseMySQL` pointed at an unreachable server writes the connection failure to the server log at `<Error>` level on code paths that explicitly tolerate and retry the failure. A temporarily unavailable remote server is a normal operational state on these paths, yet it floods the log with error-level messages. Concretely: - every `system.tables` / `system.columns` scan that touches the database logs an error (`DatabasePostgreSQL::getTablesIterator`: `Code: 614. DB::Exception: ... Connection to ... failed`); - the background cleaner logs one more error every rescheduling cycle; - `ATTACH DATABASE ... ENGINE = MySQL(...)` logs three error lines for a single tolerated probe failure. This also trips the Upgrade check (which fails on any unexpected error message in `clickhouse-server.log`) on unrelated PRs: the stateless test `04210_show_remote_databases_in_system_tables` (added in #104416) leaves `PostgreSQL`/`MySQL` databases pointed at the unroutable `192.0.2.1` during the check's restart window, and since #109082 made remote databases visible to `system.tables` scans by default, the check failed on 137 distinct PRs in 14 days, and 0 times on master. **Root cause.** Seven log sites report a caught-and-tolerated (or caught-and-propagated) connection failure at error level: the catches in `DatabasePostgreSQL::getTablesIterator` (kept non-throwing so `system.tables` scans do not fail) and `DatabasePostgreSQL::removeOutdatedTables` (the cleaner reschedules and continues) use `tryLogCurrentException` with the default `LogsLevel::error`; the same for the `DatabaseMySQL` constructor catch on `ATTACH` and `DatabaseMySQL::getCreateTableQueryImpl` with `throw_on_error = false`; and the connection-pool layers (`mysqlxx::Pool::allocConnection`, `mysqlxx::PoolWithFailover::get`, `postgres::PoolWithFailover::get`) log at error level before propagating the exception to the caller — who is the one deciding how severe the failure actually is. **Fix.** Downgrade those seven sites to warning. Exception propagation is unchanged everywhere: a non-tolerated failure (e.g. `CREATE DATABASE` with an unreachable host) still reaches the client as an error through the normal query-error path. The new test `04506_remote_database_unreachable_no_error_log` attaches `PostgreSQL` and `MySQL` databases pointing at an unreachable host, exercises the tolerated paths (attach probe, `system.tables` scan, background cleaner), and asserts through `system.text_log` that each path produced a warning (proving the failure path fired) and no error-level lines at all for the corresponding queries. ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109472&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/109472](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F109472+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix text index direct read with patch parts (lightweight updates)
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106460 (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/99543 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106460 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/99543 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed wrong results (and an `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER` error for `MATERIALIZED` indexed columns) when a query reads from a `text` index together with a column updated by a lightweight update (patch parts). Direct reading from the text index is now disabled for parts that have patch parts. ### Description Direct reading from a `text` index (`query_plan_direct_read_from_text_index`, enabled by default) produces the search result as a virtual column via a dedicated index-read step prepended to the reader chain. That step reads no physical data, so it cannot anchor patch application, which aligns patches to the block by `_part_offset`. When a queried part has patch parts (from a lightweight `UPDATE`) and a patch-applied column is read together with the direct-index virtual column, the direct-read path and the patch-application path do not line up. The result was either dropped rows (wrong results) or, when the indexed column was `MATERIALIZED`, an `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER` error while evaluating the virtual column's default expression. This happens even when the patched column is unrelated to the indexed column, so the existing per-index `canUseIndex` check was not sufficient. The fix disables direct text-index reading for the whole query when any queried part has patch parts, falling back to regular index reading (identical to `query_plan_direct_read_from_text_index = 0`, which always produced correct results). Bisected to #99543. Reproducer from the issue (`json_title String MATERIALIZED data_as_json.title::String` with a `text` index) plus a plain-column variant are added as `03100_lwu_51_text_index_patched_column`.

signals.title: Use bloom filter skip index for arrayJoin(col) IN (set) and arrayJoin(col) = const
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109516 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109844 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): A `bloom_filter` skip index on an `Array` column is now used for `arrayJoin(column) IN (set)`, `arrayJoin(column) GLOBAL IN (set)` and `arrayJoin(column) = const`, the same way it was already used for `hasAny(column, set)` and `has(column, const)`. Previously these `arrayJoin ...` forms fell back to a full scan. ### Description `MergeTreeIndexConditionBloomFilter` only accepted the argument of `IN` / `=` when it was an indexed column directly or one of a small set of wrappers (`tuple`, map subcolumns, JSON paths). `arrayJoin(tags)` matched none of them, so the atom became `FUNCTION_UNKNOWN` and no granules were skipped, while `hasAny(tags, ...)` / `has(tags, ...)` already pruned. This PR recognizes `arrayJoin(indexed_array_column)` on the left side and maps: - `arrayJoin(arr) IN (set)` (and `GLOBAL IN`) to the same granule test as `hasAny(arr, set_elements)` (`traverseTreeIn`); - `arrayJoin(arr) = const` to the same granule test as `has(arr, const)` (`traverseTreeEquals`). `arrayJoin` only multiplies rows, so a granule can produce a row matching the predicate only if at least one array element in the granule belongs to the set / equals the constant, which is exactly what the bloom filter evaluates for `hasAny` / `has`. `NOT IN` / `!=` are intentionally not handled: a granule containing a set element / the constant can still yield `arrayJoined` rows whose value is outside the set / differs, so no granule can be safely skipped. The derived condition is used for granule pruning only; the original filter still runs afterwards, so results are unchanged. Verified with `EXPLAIN indexes = 1` that the `arrayJoin ...` forms prune to the same granule count as `hasAny` / `has`, that `NOT IN` / `!=` do not prune, and that query results are identical with the skip index on and off (including the LEFT ARRAY JOIN default-value case). Test: `04365_bloom_filter_arrayJoin_in`.

signals.title: Fix the streaming-insert block wait not expiring under the query profiler
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109592 Related: https://jira.mariadb.org/browse/CONC-834 **Problem.** The file-descriptor poll timeout can silently never expire on a query thread. `ReadBufferFromFileDescriptor::poll` restarts the interrupted `poll` with the full original timeout after `EINTR`, resetting the deadline on every signal. Query threads receive periodic sampling-profiler timer signals (`query_profiler_real_time_period_ns`, default 1 s; the handler's `SA_RESTART` does not apply — per `signal(7)`, `poll` is never auto-restarted), so whenever the signal period does not exceed the timeout, the wait becomes unbounded while the fd stays silent. The user-visible path is the streaming-insert block wait: `IRowInputFormat::read` calls `poll` with the remaining `input_format_max_block_wait_ms` budget over a `StorageFile` fd/file or stdin buffer. With the profiler active, a stalled input source delays the partial-block flush indefinitely instead of flushing when the wait limit is reached. (All socket paths use `ReadBufferFromPocoSocket*::poll`, which is already deadline-aware, and are not affected.) **Root cause.** Same defect class as the MySQL `connect_timeout` fix in #109592 (mariadb-connector-c, upstream [CONC-834](https://jira.mariadb.org/browse/CONC-834)): an `EINTR` retry loop that passes the original timeout instead of the remainder. This was the last such site in `src/` — a sweep of all timed waits (`poll`/`epoll_wait`/`select`/`nanosleep`/`sigtimedwait`/io_uring/timerfd) found every other one deadline-aware (Poco sockets, `Epoll`, `KeeperTCPHandler`, `ShellCommandSource`, `base/sleep`). **Fix.** Re-poll with the remaining time computed **in microseconds from a single monotonic anchor**, reporting a timeout once the budget is exhausted. Per-retry whole-millisecond accounting (as in some existing call sites) would truncate a sub-millisecond retry interval to zero and make no progress under a sub-millisecond signal cadence, so the remainder is derived from the untouched anchor instead. The unit test (`gtest_fd_read_buffer_poll_under_signals.cpp`) waits on a pipe with no writer while a per-thread kernel timer (`timer_create` + `SIGEV_THREAD_ID`, the query profiler's own mechanism, so delivery deterministically targets the polling thread) interrupts the poll at two cadences: 10 ms (the classic deadline reset) and 0.5 ms (pins the microsecond-precision accounting). A watchdog thread disarms the timer after 3 s so a regressed build fails the elapsed assertion at ~3.2 s instead of hanging; the fixed poll returns in ~200 ms. Verified in both directions: the naive loop fails both cadences, a millisecond-accounting variant fails exactly the sub-millisecond one. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed the block-wait timeout of streaming inserts (`input_format_max_block_wait_ms`) potentially never expiring while the query profiler is active: the file-descriptor poll restarted with the full timeout after every profiler signal, so a stalled input source could delay the partial-block flush indefinitely instead of flushing when the wait limit is reached. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109602&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/109602](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F109602+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Implement SESSION window frame for window functions (experimental)
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/56099 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/45311 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Add a new `SESSION` window frame for window functions (`window w AS (ORDER BY time SESSION 60)`). Rows are grouped into the same frame while the gap between consecutive values of the ordering column does not exceed the given threshold. The feature is experimental and gated behind the `allow_experimental_session_window_frame` setting. ### Description Continuation of #56099 (original author @garcher22, who handed the PR over and is credited via `Co-authored-by`). Related to #45311. A `SESSION` frame groups consecutive rows into disjoint sessions: a new session starts when the gap on the single `ORDER BY` key exceeds the threshold. Every row of a session shares one frame, so an aggregate returns the same value across it. Gated behind `allow_experimental_session_window_frame` in both analyzers, with a `SettingsChangesHistory` entry. The branch was based on a 2023 commit. Merging current master surfaced defects that this PR also fixes: - Sessions merged across input block boundaries. The frame end compared each row against one remembered from the previous call, which is not the immediate predecessor once execution resumes on a newly arrived block, so a gap landing on a boundary was never examined. It now compares adjacent rows, and results no longer depend on `max_block_size`. - Two unnamed windows differing only in threshold received the same projection name, producing duplicate `JSONEachRow` keys and making `CREATE VIEW` over such a `SELECT` fail with `ILLEGAL_COLUMN`. - The threshold was not attached to the AST as a child, so tree hashing and generic traversal could not see it and the same query had different AST shapes depending on whether it was parsed or cloned. - Threshold and key types now match what `RANGE OFFSET` accepts (`isNativeNumber`, `convert_inexact_floats`), so a fractional threshold on a `Float32` key works and a `Decimal` one is rejected up front instead of failing later as `TYPE_MISMATCH`. - Wired the frame into the `clickhouse_json` AST dialect and query plan serialization, both added to master after this branch was opened; the latter also re-checks the experimental setting, which a client-supplied plan otherwise bypasses. Each fix has a case in `02891_session_window` that fails when only that fix is reverted.

signals.title: Label docker-daemon-death job truncation as infra for auto-retry
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109096 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description When the host docker daemon dies mid-run, the main test container returns exit code 125 and the job is truncated: every already-executed test is `[ OK ]`, but the run never ends, so `runner.py` marks the job `ERROR`. That is a runner-host infrastructure event, not a test or code failure. The hourly `retry_infra_failures` workflow re-runs jobs labeled `infra`, but this path recorded only a generic `"Job killed, exit code [125]"` and set no label, so such jobs were never retried and the Mergeable Check stayed red despite all tests passing. A truncated, non-timeout run is now labeled `infra` when the exit code is `125` and the log tail contains both `Error waiting for container: Canceled` and `grpc: the client connection is closing`. Both appear together only when a live container's daemon connection is torn down mid-run. A deterministic `Cannot connect to the Docker daemon at unix:///var/run/docker.sock` regression also exits 125 unfinished, so requiring the conjunction keeps it red rather than retrying a broken runner forever. Timeouts keep their own handling. The label is appended as the bare string `"infra"` rather than through `set_label()`, which stores `{"name": "infra", ...}`. `retry_infra_failures.yml` matches with `(.ext.labels // []) | any(. == "infra")`, comparing each element to a string, so the dict form would never match and this would be a no-op end to end. The other readers (`Result._label_name`, `normalizeLabels`, `gh.py`) already accept strings; the only cost is the hover tooltip, and no `workflow` scope is needed. `ci/tests/test_runner_docker_daemon_death_infra.py` pins the detector in both directions and asserts on the persisted result JSON the retry workflow reads, including once end to end through `_run` with a no-Docker job that exits 125. #109096 fixed the sibling 9000s timeout-cleanup-hang. This signature caused 107 job errors over 21 days, all on PRs and 0 on master; one report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/PRs/109536/887a2f0e48f223cde20a674e2c9dac31cc8eb483/result_stateless_tests_amd_tsan_s3_storage_parallel_2_2.json
