signals.title: EXPLAIN SYNTAX: return the pretty-printed query as a single multi-line record
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/80410 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107925 --> Closes: #80410 Related: #107925 (closed, superseded by this PR) ### Changelog category (leave one): - Backward Incompatible Change ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `EXPLAIN SYNTAX` now returns the pretty-printed (multi-line) query as a single result record instead of one record per line. The `oneline` option (`EXPLAIN SYNTAX oneline = 1`) still collapses the output to a single physical line. Queries that consumed the previous per-line output should treat the result as one row whose value contains embedded newlines. ### Description `EXPLAIN SYNTAX <query>` formatted the reformatted query and split it into one result row per physical line. This PR emits the whole formatted, copy-pasteable query as a single record with newlines preserved (issue #80410). Only the `AnalyzedSyntax` code path is changed; `PLAN`, `PIPELINE`, `AST` and the `oneline` option are unchanged. The previous attempt (#107925) was closed because it flipped the `oneline` default to `1`, collapsing the query to a single physical line rather than keeping the multi-line pretty form. This PR keeps `oneline = false` by default and only changes the result shape from N rows to one multi-line record. Reference files for tests consuming EXPLAIN SYNTAX output (including `.oldanalyzer.reference` variants) were regenerated. A regression test (`04545_explain_syntax_single_record`) asserts the single-record multi-line default and the `oneline = 1` collapse.

signals.title: Fix MaterializedPostgreSQL database/table with ON CLUSTER
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/58726 A `MaterializedPostgreSQL` database or table created with `ON CLUSTER` gets the *same* ClickHouse UUID on every replica, because the UUID is generated once on the initiator and shipped in the DDL. With `materialized_postgresql_use_unique_replication_consumer_identifier = 1` the replication slot name was derived from that UUID and the publication name from the PostgreSQL database/table name, so every replica computed the same names and fought over one PostgreSQL slot and publication: a single replica replicated, the others failed in the background with `pqxx::unique_violation` or could not hold the slot, leaving divergent data. The fix hashes the persistent per-server `ServerUUID` together with the object UUID (via `makeUUIDv4FromHash`, which keeps the result within PostgreSQL's identifier length limit) and derives both the slot and the publication name from it, so each replica gets its own pair and replicates independently. Both UUIDs are persistent, so `ATTACH` keeps reusing the same slot. The default behaviour (setting disabled) is unchanged, and since the change is in the shared `PostgreSQLReplicationHandler` it covers both the database and the table engine. A user-managed `materialized_postgresql_replication_slot` has one fixed name that every replica would share, so combining it with this setting is contradictory and is now rejected for a freshly supplied engine definition — a `CREATE`, or an `ATTACH` that carries a full definition, so it cannot be bypassed through `ATTACH ... ON CLUSTER`. A replay of an already stored definition (startup, `RESTORE`, short-syntax `ATTACH`) still accepts it, so existing deployments keep starting. ## Upgrade of existing deployments Salting the names is a rename of the generated identity, so `adoptLegacyReplicationIdentityIfNeeded` — the mechanism that already handles the schema-aware rename — now also adopts the pre-salt slot and publication when the salted ones do not exist. Replication resumes from the same slot position: no re-snapshot into the already-populated nested tables, nothing orphaned. The pre-salt slot name embeds the object's own ClickHouse UUID, so its existence proves ownership. The publication name is schema-blind and does not, so it is adopted only when it publishes *exactly* the tables this engine replicates: the configured `materialized_postgresql_tables_list`, or otherwise the tables the engine actually replicated in the previous run (their nested tables exist on disk) — not the live PostgreSQL schema, which may have grown since `CREATE DATABASE` with tables that are never replicated without an explicit `ATTACH TABLE`. Adoption is skipped for a database that never materialized a single nested table: there is nothing to preserve and its empty on-disk set cannot prove any publication's ownership, so it synchronizes under the current identity and the legacy objects are named in the log for the operator. ## Fail-closed attach paths `pgoutput` resolves publication membership from the historic catalog snapshot at each change's LSN, so streaming through a publication that was created or narrowed after those changes were written silently drops them — unrecoverably, once `confirmed_flush_lsn` advances. Attach therefore no longer papers over a broken PostgreSQL-side state; it fails with a retryable error, so startup keeps retrying and an operator can repair the conflict or rebuild the replica. This holds for every identity, not only for the pre-salt rename: - **Publication gone behind a surviving slot** — previously recreated silently, skipping every change committed while it was missing. - **Slot gone behind a surviving publication**, as after `pg_upgrade` (it keeps publications but not replication slots) or an operator dropping the slot — previously an in-place re-snapshot, whose rows are materialized with `_sign = 1` and `_version = 1` and therefore neither delete rows that disappeared from PostgreSQL nor override rows already at a higher version, silently leaving the replica stale. A clean rebuild recovers every row. A user-managed slot is excluded, since a missing one is already reported as a configuration error. - **Both gone** while the replica already holds data from a previous run. - **Publication drift under the current identity** — `ALTER PUBLICATION ... DROP TABLE`, an altered `publish` set (`CREATE PUBLICATION` defaults to `insert, update, delete, truncate`), or, on PostgreSQL 15 and newer, a row filter or a column list on a published table. The published set is compared by exact `(schema, table)` pair, because in the single-schema modes both the publication table list and the WAL consumer key tables by bare name, so a publication rewritten from `foo.a` to `bar.a` would otherwise resume and replay `bar.a`'s changes into the ClickHouse table for `foo.a`. Extra published tables stay tolerated — the identity already owns the publication name — unless a foreign-schema table's bare name collides with a replicated one. A database that has not materialized a single nested table is exempt throughout: there is nothing a snapshot could make stale, so it bootstraps through whatever survived. If an interrupted first synchronization left both the publication and the slot behind, the leftover slot is dropped so the initial synchronization can run instead of resuming and then failing forever with `UNKNOWN_TABLE` on a nested table that was never created (a user-managed slot, which this engine may not recreate, is refused with an explicit message). Relatedly, the set of tables to materialize on attach now comes from the existing publication — the engine's persisted table set, which the code always claimed to assume correct — instead of the live schema. Previously a PostgreSQL table created after `CREATE DATABASE` made every attach retry fail with `UNKNOWN_TABLE` on its missing nested table, so a whole-schema database could never resume replication after a restart; this reproduces on master with the setting disabled. Published-but-not-materialized tables are reported in a warning that names the recovery (`ATTACH TABLE`), because that state is indistinguishable from a table that was in the original definition but never completed its first snapshot; persisting the configured table set is deferred to the separate persistent-replication-state change, together with the `rebuild required` marker discussed in the review. ## Tests The new `test_postgresql_replica_database_engine_on_cluster` suite covers the fix — two-node `ON CLUSTER` databases and tables, each replica getting its own slot and publication and synchronizing independently, and both removed by `DROP ... ON CLUSTER` — the adoption of a reconstructed pre-salt identity (including a whole-schema database whose PostgreSQL schema has grown, and foreign publications that must not be adopted), every fail-closed case above, the bootstrap paths for never-synchronized runs and for a fresh full-definition `ATTACH TABLE`, and the rejection of a user-managed slot on `CREATE` and on a full-definition `ATTACH ... ON CLUSTER` of either engine. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `MaterializedPostgreSQL` databases and tables created with `ON CLUSTER`. When `materialized_postgresql_use_unique_replication_consumer_identifier` is enabled, the PostgreSQL replication slot and publication names are now unique per server, so replicas no longer collide on a shared replication slot and publication, which previously left all but one replica unable to replicate. Also fixed a whole-schema `MaterializedPostgreSQL` database failing to resume replication after a server restart when a new table had been created in PostgreSQL, and made the attach fail closed instead of silently losing changes when the publication or the replication slot is missing. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110493&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/110493](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F110493+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix toDateTime64 saturation doc example (9999 not 2282)
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110478 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Documentation (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description The embedded `toDateTime64` documentation example for the saturation case `SELECT toDateTime64(1546300800000, 3)` showed `2282-12-31 00:00:00.000`, a stale legacy DateTime64 maximum. The actual output is `9999-12-31 23:59:59.000` (DateTime64 upper saturation is year 9999). Verified against a real server: ``` SELECT toDateTime64(1546300800000, 3) AS value, toTypeName(value) 9999-12-31 23:59:59.000 DateTime64(3) ``` Note: the `toDateTime32` doc block in the same file also contains a mislabeled copy of this example (showing `2299-12-31 23:59:59.000`); that block is being rewritten separately in #110459, so this PR only touches the genuine `toDateTime64` example.

signals.title: Do not flatten a Set-engine array table on the right of IN
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110505 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `Code: 48. NOT_IMPLEMENTED: Method read is not supported by storage Set` when a `Set`-engine table, or a `Alias` table pointing at one, is used on the right side of `IN`. Such tables are now always consumed as a prepared set instead of being read, in the analyzer, the legacy `IN` implementation, and the serialized-plan path. Closes #110505. ### Description Closes: #110505 A single-`Array`-column table on the right of `IN` is rewritten into a `SELECT column FROM table` subquery so its elements become the set elements. A `Set`-engine table matches that shape but has no `read` method: it is meant to be consumed natively as a prepared set. So the rewrite made `IN` over set-backed tables fail with `Code: 48. NOT_IMPLEMENTED: Method read is not supported by storage Set`. The three places that decide "is this a set-backed table" each looked only at the immediate storage, so a `Alias` wrapper (whose `read` delegates to its target) was never recognized. This adds a shared helper, `getSetStorageFromTable`, that resolves through an alias chain and matches `StorageSet` including derived types, and routes all three call sites through it: the analyzer (`Analyzer/Resolve/resolveFunction.cpp`, `Planner/CollectSets.cpp`), the legacy implementation (`Interpreters/ActionsVisitor.cpp`, reached with `enable_analyzer = 0`), and plan deserialization (`Processors/QueryPlan/SetsSerialization.cpp`, reached in distributed-plan execution). Reproduces on released versions, so this is not master-only: ```sql CREATE TABLE t (arr Array(UInt8)) ENGINE = Set; INSERT INTO t VALUES ([1, 2, 3]); CREATE TABLE a ENGINE = Alias('t'); SELECT [1, 2, 3] IN a; -- 26.5/26.6/26.7: NOT_IMPLEMENTED; now 1 SELECT 2 IN t; -- 26.7: NOT_IMPLEMENTED; now TYPE_MISMATCH ``` `ENGINE = Alias` is generally available in all three (`allow_experimental_alias_table_engine` is obsolete), and the same query over an `Alias` to a readable table always worked, so the failure was specific to set-backed targets. Access checking is unchanged from before the rewrite: a set-backed alias on the right of `IN` requires the same grants as an equivalent `Alias` to a `MergeTree` table, verified across 5 grant combinations in both analyzer modes and on the serialized-plan path. Regressions: `04512_in_function_array_subquery_right_argument` (direct, alias, legacy mode, access) and `04652_in_set_alias_serialized_query_plan` (serialized plan).

signals.title: Do not abort server startup when a URL table's named collection is missing
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/105045 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed the server failing to start (`Cannot start clickhouse-server`) when a `URL` table references a named collection that no longer exists. A collection can be legitimately dropped while a dependent `URL` table exists (with `check_named_collection_dependencies = false`), and the `ATTACH` replayed at startup then threw `NAMED_COLLECTION_DOESNT_EXIST`. The table now attaches and the error is reported at query time. ### Description Reported on #105045 but unrelated to it: `Stress test` on `03822_named_collection_drop_dependency_check` fails to restart the server, with `ATTACH TABLE ... ENGINE = URL(...)` hitting `NAMED_COLLECTION_DOESNT_EXIST`. Reproduces on master. Root cause: the `URL` engine resolves its named collection eagerly at attach time (`StorageURL::getConfiguration`), but `check_named_collection_dependencies = false` lets a collection be dropped while dependent `URL` tables exist. The persisted `ATTACH` replayed at startup then aborts the server under synchronous loading. Fix: when replaying a definition stored on this server, a missing collection attaches a lazy proxy instead of aborting; it is re-resolved on first read/write, and if still missing the query fails `NAMED_COLLECTION_DOESNT_EXIST`. A definition the user supplies now (`CREATE`, full-definition `ATTACH`, `RESTORE`, Replicated DDL) still fails its own DDL instead of persisting an unusable table, gated on the predicate `StorageDistributed` uses. Also fixed while under review, every case where `StorageProxy` answers through `getNested()` (which materializes), so the proxy reported the missing collection where eager `URL` answers directly: the engine classification (`isObjectStorage`/`isDataLake`/`isMessageQueue`/`isExternalDatabase`), read by `InterpreterInsertQuery` before the materializing `write()`, so an object-storage-backed `URL(nc)` was rejected `QUERY_IS_PROHIBITED` under `disable_insertion_and_mutation` where the eager form inserted; and `checkAlterPartitionIsPossible`, `alterPartition`, `getCheckTaskList`, `getActionLock`, `supportsReplication`, `getColumnSizes`, where partition DDL and `CHECK TABLE` reported `NAMED_COLLECTION_DOESNT_EXIST` instead of `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` and the last three are swept over every table, so one unresolvable table made `system.tables`, `system.columns` and bulk `SYSTEM STOP MERGES` throw. Validated in both directions with `04540_url_named_collection_missing_on_attach` and `tests/integration/test_disable_insertion_and_mutation`, including a real restart with the collection still missing. `S3`/`Azure`/`HDFS` resolve collections in their own `fromAST` path and may share this.
signals.author: groeneai

signals.title: Add experimental PCO compression codec (linking the pcodec Rust crate)
signals.text: Adds an experimental `PCO` compression codec that links the [pcodec](https://github.com/pcodec/pcodec) (`pco`) Rust crate — the reference implementation — rather than reimplementing it. `pco` is a lossless codec specialized for sequences of fixed-width numbers; on numeric columns with smooth, multimodal, or high-entropy distributions (measurements, timings, counters, identifiers) it often beats `Gorilla`/`FPC`/`ZSTD`/`ALP` on ratio. This is the Rust-library counterpart to the native C++ port explored in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/106222. Instead of maintaining a C++ reimplementation, it links the upstream crate. ### Runtime CPU dispatch `pco` has no explicit SIMD: it relies on the compiler autovectorizing its per-batch loops, which only happens when the crate is compiled with the relevant instruction sets enabled (its `build.rs` warns to build with `-C target-feature=+avx2,+bmi1,+bmi2`). That does not work for ClickHouse, which compiles all Rust once at a fixed baseline micro-architecture level for a binary that must run on a range of CPUs. So `pco` is taken from a ClickHouse fork patched to add runtime CPU-feature dispatch of its hot loops — the same mechanism ClickHouse's C++ uses via `TargetSpecific.h`. The vectorizable loop bodies (decode `read_offsets`; encode `write_short_uints`/`write_uints`/`set_offsets`) are compiled at the crate baseline and again for `x86-64-v3` (AVX2 + BMI1/2 + FMA) and `x86-64-v4` (AVX-512), and the widest variant the running CPU supports is selected once and cached. On aarch64 the baseline already includes NEON, so the baseline body is used directly. Verified at baseline `-C target-cpu=x86-64`: the `read_offsets` v3 trampoline emits AVX2 (`ymm`) and v4 emits AVX-512 (`zmm`). The patch is merged into `ClickHouse/pcodec` (a fork of pcodec/pcodec in the ClickHouse organization) via its own PR: https://github.com/ClickHouse/pcodec/pull/1. The crate is added as the `contrib/pcodec` submodule and linked through a thin FFI wrapper crate (`rust/workspace/pco`). Its one not-yet-vendored dependency, `rand_xoshiro`, was added to `contrib/rust_vendor` in https://github.com/ClickHouse/rust_vendor/pull/72. ### Codec Supported types are all fixed-width numerics of 1/2/4/8 bytes via their underlying integer/float representation: `Int8`..`Int64`, `UInt8`..`UInt64`, `Float32`/`Float64`, and the types backed by them (`Date`, `DateTime`, `Decimal32`/`Decimal64`, `IPv4`, `Enum`, ...). The on-disk block stores a 2-byte header (element width + partial-tail byte count) followed by a raw partial-value tail (as in `Gorilla`/`FPC`) and the payload. The payload is a standalone `.pco` stream, wire-compatible with the reference pcodec implementation; when compression would not shrink a block the raw bytes are stored instead (a per-block "stored" flag), so the output never expands by more than the 2-byte header and `getMaxCompressedDataSize` is tight. The codec is gated behind `allow_experimental_codecs`. Because it needs the column type, it can only be specified per column: it is rejected in `TTL ... RECOMPRESS` and in the untyped compression settings that resolve codecs without a type. `CompressionCodecMultiple` propagates the experimental / column-type-requiring properties so a chain such as `CODEC(Delta, PCO)` is still gated, and a codec-only `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COLUMN x CODEC(PCO)` validates against the existing column type. Tests: `04512_pco_codec` round-trips every supported numeric and backed type (per-element verification, edge cases, codec chaining, compression-ratio check) and `04513_pco_codec_gating` covers the experimental gate, the `TTL RECOMPRESS` rejection, and the codec-only `ALTER`. The FFI wrapper has its own Rust unit tests (round-trip of all types, the no-expansion fallback, and fail-closed handling of malformed/mismatched streams). ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added a new experimental compression codec `PCO`, which links the [pcodec](https://github.com/pcodec/pcodec) library (patched for runtime CPU dispatch), specialized for fixed-width numeric columns. It is wire-format compatible with pcodec `.pco` streams and is enabled with `allow_experimental_codecs`. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes: - [x] Documentation is written (the `PCO` codec is documented in `docs/en/sql-reference/statements/create/table.md`, and the compression-frame method byte in `docs/en/interfaces/specs/NativeFormat.md`). <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110613&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/110613](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F110613+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Speed up wide-table sorting by skipping per-row replicated-column check in merge
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107611 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Speed up sorting of wide tables (`ORDER BY` over many columns) by skipping a per-row `ColumnReplicated` check in the merge step when no column can be replicated. This removes overhead that was noticeable on ARM. ### Description Addresses https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107611 (ARM regression on `sort_wide_table` query `1`: `SELECT * FROM sort_wide_16 ORDER BY k1, k2 FORMAT Null`). The reported regression scope is the `ColumnReplicated` wrapping added to `MergedData` by #101036. That change added a per-row, per-column `raw_columns[i]->isReplicated()` check to `MergedData::insertRow` / `insertRows`, wrapping the destination in `ColumnReplicated` when a source is replicated. That wrapping is only needed when the merge is fed by a JOIN with `enable_lazy_columns_replication = 1`. For a plain sort with no JOIN, no column is ever `ColumnReplicated`, so the virtual call runs once per column per row (18 columns x ~500K rows for `sort_wide_16`) as pure overhead in the hot row-by-row insertion loop. Fix, aligned with the existing design (keep the wrapping where it is genuinely needed): - Add a `may_have_replicated_columns` hint to `MergedData`, default `true`, so every algorithm keeps the current wrapping behavior unless it explicitly opts out. When the hint is `false`, `insertRow` / `insertRows` take a tight loop identical to the pre-#101036 behavior; when `true`, the wrapping path is byte-for-byte unchanged. - `MergingSortedAlgorithm` lowers the hint to `false` in `initialize` when no input column is `ColumnReplicated`, and raises it back to `true` monotonically in `consume` if a late-arriving chunk brings a replicated column — always before those rows can reach `insertRow`. A replicated source can only enter the merge through `initialize` or `consume`, so the wrapping is never skipped when it is needed. - Other algorithms that reuse `MergedData` (Aggregating, Summing, Collapsing, Replacing, VersionedCollapsing, GraphiteRollup) leave the hint at its default `true` and are unaffected. Validation on x86 (the ARM Neoverse-V2 numbers must come from the arm_release Performance Comparison job, which is the authoritative measurement): - New unit tests `MergedDataReplicated.FastPathSkipsWrappingForRegularColumns` and `RestoringFlagReenablesWrapping`, plus all 5 pre-existing `MergedDataReplicated` regression tests, pass. - A JOIN with `enable_lazy_columns_replication = 1` followed by `ORDER BY` (forces `ColumnReplicated` into the merge) produces results identical to `enable_lazy_columns_replication = 0` and stays correctly sorted. - Stateless tests `03580_external_merge_sort_with_lazy_columns`, `03709_replicated_columns_right_join`, `03701_replicated_column_short_circuit_filter`, `03352_lazy_column_filter_by_uint8` pass.

signals.title: Fix logical error in optimize_or_like_chain with aggregate/window function on LIKE LHS
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a logical error (`Function node with name '...' is not resolved as ordinary function`) that could occur with `optimize_or_like_chain` enabled when an aggregate or window function appeared on the left-hand side of a `LIKE`/`ILIKE`/`match` inside an `OR` chain. ### Description Found by the BuzzHouse fuzzer (STID 3477-117d) on [this CI run](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=107567&sha=16ccfffe167f14e51996ce4ec16384f92e4d15d0&name_0=PR&name_1=BuzzHouse%20%28amd_msan%29). Not caused by that PR — it is a trunk analyzer bug the fuzzer happened to surface there. `isExpressionNonDeterministic` in `ConvertOrLikeChainPass` guarded its `getFunctionOrThrow()` call with `FunctionNode::isResolved()`. `isResolved()` returns true for aggregate and window functions too (it only checks that the function pointer is set), but `getFunctionOrThrow()` throws `LOGICAL_ERROR` when the function kind is not `ORDINARY`. So a resolved aggregate (e.g. `count()`) or window function nested under a `LIKE` argument in an `OR` chain tripped the assertion — an exception in release builds, an abort in debug/sanitizer builds. Fix: guard with `isOrdinaryFunction()` instead, matching the existing correct guard in `PlannerExpressionAnalysis`. Aggregate/window functions are never non-deterministic-in-scope-of-query at this point, so recursing into their children is sufficient. Minimal reproducer (aborts before the fix on a debug build): ```sql SET optimize_or_like_chain = 1; SELECT toString(count()) LIKE '%1%' OR toString(count()) LIKE '%2%' FROM numbers(3); ``` Covered by `tests/queries/0_stateless/04545_optimize_or_like_chain_aggregate_lhs.sql` (aggregate and window variants, plus an ordinary-function control that must still collapse).

signals.title: Fix doubled written_rows for INSERT into Distributed with local shards
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106361 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106361 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `written_rows` being reported as twice the actual value in `system.query_log` and `system.view_refreshes` for an `INSERT` into a `Distributed` table that writes to local shards (for example a Refreshable Materialized View appending to a `Distributed` target). ### Description `INSERT` into a `Distributed` table over local shards reported `written_rows` at 2x the real value. Reported in #106361 for a Refreshable Materialized View whose target is a `Distributed` table (`system.view_refreshes.written_rows` = 180052 while `system.query_log` = 90026 and only 90026 rows were actually written), but the same doubling happens for a plain `INSERT INTO dist SELECT ...`. Root cause: the nested per-shard local `InterpreterInsertQuery` in `DistributedSink` ran with a context that still carried the parent query's progress callback and process-list element. Its own `CountingTransform` therefore re-counted rows that the top-level `CountingTransform` of the distributed `INSERT` had already accounted, feeding both `system.query_log.written_rows` (via the process-list element) and `system.view_refreshes.written_rows` (via `RefreshTask`'s progress callback). The `RemoteSink` path (`prefer_localhost_replica=0`) does not share the parent's accounting, so only the local-shard path doubled. Fix: detach the nested local insert from the parent's write-progress accounting in both the synchronous (`runWritingJob`) and asynchronous (`writeToLocal`) local-write paths. Verified locally against the reproducer from the issue and a plain distributed `INSERT`: `written_rows` and `view_refreshes.written_rows` now report 1000 (was 2000). Added stateless regression test `04500_distributed_insert_written_rows_not_doubled`.
signals.author: groeneai

signals.title: Pin patch parts in MUTATE_PART log entries for deterministic mutations
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/100493 (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/100493 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `CHECKSUM_DOESNT_MATCH` errors and a stuck mutation loop that could occur on `ReplicatedMergeTree` tables using lightweight updates (`enable_block_number_column`/`enable_block_offset_column`) under concurrent `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE`. A `MUTATE_PART` replicated log entry now records the exact set of patch parts to apply, so all replicas produce a byte-identical mutated part. ### Description Fixes [#100493](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/100493). Unlike `MERGE_PARTS`, a `MUTATE_PART` replicated log entry did not record the set of patch parts (produced by lightweight updates) that must be applied while producing the mutated part. Each replica derived the applicable patches from its own local visible state (`MutateTask::prepare` -> `getMutationsSnapshot(need_patch_parts=true)`). When a patch part was committed on the replica that assigned the mutation but not yet replicated to another replica, the two replicas executing the same `MUTATE_PART` entry applied different patch sets and produced byte-different mutated parts. This raised `CHECKSUM_DOESNT_MATCH` ("Data after mutation is not byte-identical to data on another replicas"), and the losing replica got stuck fetching the part, hanging the cluster under load. This matches the reporter's setup exactly: same-version 2-node cluster, `ReplicatedReplacingMergeTree` with block-number/offset columns, concurrent `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE`. The fix mirrors how merges already pin patch parts: - `createLogEntryToMutatePart` records the applicable patch parts (partition match + `data_version < mutation_version`) into `entry.patch_parts`. - `ReplicatedMergeTreeLogEntry` serializes/parses them for `MUTATE_PART` (field `mutation_patches:`; distinct leading character from the other mutate fields because `checkString` consumes a matching prefix). - `MutateFromLogEntryTask::prepare` resolves the pinned patch parts locally, waiting for exactly that set and falling back to fetching the mutated part if one is missing (mirrors `MergeFromLogEntryTask`). - `MutateTask::prepare` applies exactly the pinned set instead of deriving from local visible state. The new log-entry field is written only when patch parts exist, i.e. only for tables using lightweight updates, so behavior is unchanged for existing setups. **Validation** (single server, two co-located `ReplicatedMergeTree` replicas, block columns on, 200k rows, concurrent mixed lightweight `UPDATE`+`DELETE` + `OPTIMIZE FINAL`, identical config): - Without the fix (master): 26 `CHECKSUM_DOESNT_MATCH` ("Data after mutation is not byte-identical") on `MutateFromLogEntryTask`. - With the fix: 0 mismatches, 0 parse errors. The pinned-patch wait/fetch-fallback path was confirmed firing on the lagging replica. Note: the added integration test (`test_lwu_replicated_mutation_pins_patches`) was authored to exercise the divergent-patch window deterministically, but I was unable to run the Docker-based integration suite locally in this environment; the fix itself was validated with the stress reproducer above.

signals.title: Fix wrong count() result with custom key parallel replicas
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/50593 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/50593 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed wrong results for aggregation queries over a cluster/Distributed table with custom key parallel replicas (`parallel_replicas_mode = 'custom_key_sampling'`/`'custom_key_range'`) when the custom key is not a function of the `GROUP BY` keys. For example `SELECT count()` previously returned one partial row per replica instead of the merged total; now the initiator merges the partial results. ### Description Custom key parallel replicas skip the merging step on the initiator by setting `distributed_group_by_no_merge = 2`, so per-replica results are concatenated as-is. This is only correct when every row that shares a `GROUP BY` key is processed by a single replica, i.e. when the custom key is a function of the `GROUP BY` keys. Previously `distributed_group_by_no_merge = 2` was set unconditionally for a Distributed/cluster table with a custom key, so a query with aggregation whose `GROUP BY` does not cover the custom key (including plain aggregation without `GROUP BY`, e.g. `SELECT count()`) returned one partial row per replica. The fix keeps the no-merge fast path only when the custom key references only columns that are themselves plain `GROUP BY` keys (and the query has no `WITH ROLLUP`/`CUBE`/`TOTALS`/`GROUPING SETS`). Otherwise the merge is left enabled and the initiator produces the correct result. Applied on both the old and the new analyzer code paths. This is antonio2368's suggested first step from the issue thread ("not enable `distributed_group_by_no_merge` if custom key doesn't contain expression from `GROUP BY`"). The suitable-`GROUP BY` case (custom key is a function of the grouping keys) still uses the fast no-merge path.

signals.title: Fix LOGICAL_ERROR on constant-folded comparison under group_by_use_nulls + GROUPING SETS
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110551 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a logical error (server abort in debug/sanitizer builds) when a constant-folded comparison appears in the SELECT list together with `group_by_use_nulls = 1` and `GROUP BY GROUPING SETS`. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110551 `group_by_use_nulls` promotes a `FunctionNode`'s declared result type to `Nullable` via `FunctionNode::wrap_with_nullable`, while the un-wrapped base function used for constant folding still returns the non-`Nullable` type. When such a node is constant-folded in `tryFoldFunctionToConstant` (`ActionsDAG.cpp`), the folded `Const(UInt8)` diverges from the declared `Nullable(UInt8)`, so the node result-type consistency check throws `LOGICAL_ERROR: Unexpected return type from equals. Expected Nullable(UInt8). Got Const(UInt8)`. In debug/sanitizer builds this aborts the server; release tolerates it (the check is an assert), and `group_by_use_nulls = 0` is unaffected. The fix reconciles the folded constant to the declared node result type in exactly this case (the declared type equals `makeNullableOrLowCardinalityNullableSafe(base_result_type)`) instead of weakening the check. The strict `LOGICAL_ERROR` check is kept as a fallback for genuine mismatches. Regression test: `04545_group_by_use_nulls_grouping_sets_const_fold_equals` (the issue's repro plus a minimal variant). Found by the AST fuzzer.
signals.author: groeneai

signals.title: Filter LLVM Profile Error noise from cancel-insert-when-client-dies tests
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108343 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ### Description Four cancel-insert tests (02434, 02435, 04365, 04366) fail on `Stateless tests (amd_llvm_coverage_per_test, per_test_coverage)` with `result differs with reference`, where the diff's added lines are `LLVM Profile Error:` messages rather than wrong test output. The cancellation counts are correct. Root cause: `thread_cancel` SIGKILLs coverage-instrumented `clickhouse-client` processes mid-insert. On abnormal death those clients emit `LLVM Profile Error: ...` to stderr (profraw merge-pool contention, see #97020). `clickhouse-test` strips those lines from a client's *stderr* only; `thread_insert` merges client stderr into stdout via `2>&1` and filtered just `Killed` (plus session noise in 02435), so the lines survived into the test's stdout and broke the reference diff. Fix: extend each `thread_insert` filter with `grep -Fav "LLVM Profile Error:"`. A repo-wide sweep of stateless `.sh` tests that signal-kill processes and merge output with `2>&1` confirms these four are the complete carrier set: the other candidates either capture into a variable and positively `grep` for `Received from` (01169 pair), redirect client output to a file or `/dev/null` (03776, 03803, 04003, 04051, 04052), or filter on `Exception:` (02443). 02435 was added after `clickhouse-gh[bot]` pointed it out on this PR; it has 3 master failures of this exact signature (2026-06-15, 2026-07-16, 2026-07-17). Validation: this check runs only in `NightlyCoverage` (`ci/workflows/nightly_coverage.py`, `Event.SCHEDULE`, master), so it cannot run on this PR. Instead, each test's committed filter chain was extracted from the file and driven against the verbatim CI-captured stdout: post-fix output matches the reference byte-for-byte; removing the new filter reproduces the failure (so it is load-bearing); and a real `DB::Exception` line is preserved, confirming only the profiler noise is dropped. 12/12 assertions pass across the four tests. Report (04365, 2026-07-28 master): https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=4a44dcefc451d3da3f7a9e7c8a38f74180b34ebc&name_0=NightlyCoverage&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_llvm_coverage_per_test%2C%20per_test_coverage%2C%208%2F8%29 Prior PR #108343 widened the final cancel-message matcher (a separate genuine gap); the recurrence was this stdout pollution.

signals.title: Fix Block structure mismatch after liftUpUnion with divergent aggregate state types
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> No related open issue found. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a `LOGICAL_ERROR` "Block structure mismatch in after optimization liftUpUnion" (server abort in debug and sanitizer builds) that could occur for a query with an expression or preliminary `DISTINCT` above a `UNION ALL` whose branches produce aggregate-function state columns that share the same state representation but different type names (for example `quantileExactTupleState` and `quantilesExactTupleState`). ### Description `tryLiftUpUnion` pushes the parent `Expression`/`Distinct` step into each union branch, assuming the union forwards every branch unchanged. That assumption breaks when a branch column matches the union output only loosely: two `AggregateFunction` columns can share the same state representation yet print different type names (e.g. `quantileExactTuple` vs `quantilesExactTuple(0.9)`), so `blocksHaveEqualStructure` treats them as equal and the union output takes the first branch's type. The union coerces the diverging branch at runtime via a converting step; pushing the parent down bypasses that coercion and produces branch headers that no longer match, tripping the post-optimization `checkHeaders` assertion. The fix lifts the parent only when every branch input header is identical (same name and same type name) to the union output. The optimization still fires for genuine same-type unions. Found by the AST fuzzer (Stress test, amd_tsan; CIDB STID 0993-23fd).
signals.author: groeneai

signals.title: Fix text index LOGICAL_ERROR with constant folding and partition key
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a `LOGICAL_ERROR` ("Query builder not found for text search query with function") when a query filters a column that has a `text` index and is also the partition key, with the setting `use_constant_folding_in_index_analysis` enabled. ### Description The text index direct-read path registers its virtual columns against the unsubstituted condition at plan time (the virtual column name embeds the unsubstituted search-query hash), and the reader looks them up via `generateUnsubstituted()`. When `use_constant_folding_in_index_analysis` is on and the text-indexed column is also the partition key, the granule analyzer was built from the per-partition constant-folded condition instead, whose search queries hash differently. The reader could not find the query builder and threw the logical error (server abort in debug/sanitizer builds). The fix keeps constant folding off for `text` index condition templates, so the granule analyzer and the reader always use the same unsubstituted set of search queries. Other index types are unaffected. Found by the AST fuzzer (STID 3694-54bc), report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=100173&sha=e196b05a52cdcdcdf80b1f6c6a41071b5deec053&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%29

signals.title: Fix logical error on DISTINCT-in-order over ARRAY JOIN with stale sort property
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109216 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a logical error `Equal values are not contiguous within the range assumed to be sorted` (and potential wrong `DISTINCT` results) when `optimize_distinct_in_order` is enabled and an `ORDER BY` over an `arrayJoin`-derived column is followed by another `ARRAY JOIN` that reproduces a column of the same name. ### Description `applyActionsToSortDescription()` returned early whenever the expression it was pushing the sort description through contained an `ARRAY JOIN`, leaving the sort description unchanged. When such an expression re-applies an `ARRAY JOIN` that produces an output column named identically to the sorted input column, the output stream is no longer sorted by that column, yet the stale `... ASC` sort property survived and propagated up to the `DISTINCT` step. That step then ran distinct-in-order (`DistinctSortedStreamTransform`) over genuinely unsorted data and aborted with the logical error (or, in a release build, could return wrong `DISTINCT` results). Removing the blanket early-return lets the existing chain-tracing logic handle `ARRAY JOIN` correctly: the monotonic chain breaks at an `ARRAY JOIN` node, so array-join-derived sort columns are dropped, while genuinely order-preserving columns (array join only replicates rows in place) are kept. The failing shape is produced, for example, by decorrelating a correlated scalar subquery whose body is `SELECT DISTINCT ... ORDER BY <arrayJoin column> SETTINGS optimize_distinct_in_order = 1`. This is the no-JOIN variant of the `DistinctSortedStreamTransform` invariant family; it is not covered by #109225 (which gates read-in-order propagation through non-order-preserving JOINs). Found via the AST/BuzzHouse fuzzers (CIDB STID 2508-348f), reproduced deterministically on debug and asan builds. Regression test `04550_distinct_in_order_array_join_phantom_sort` fails (aborts) without the fix and passes with it.

signals.title: Serialize an empty polygon with zero rings (canonical WKB)
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110701 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110701 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed non-canonical WKB serialization of an empty polygon: `wkb(POLYGON EMPTY)` now emits `numRings = 0` instead of a spurious single zero-point ring, so a WKB round-trip of a standard empty polygon is identity-preserving. ### Description An empty polygon is stored internally with one empty outer ring (`[[]]`), so `wkb()` emitted `numRings = 1` with a zero-point `LinearRing`, producing a non-canonical form (`01030000000100000000000000`) that stricter WKB consumers may reject. Other empty geometries (LineString, MultiLineString, MultiPolygon) already serialized with a zero element count. `WKBPolygonTransform::dumpObject` (src/Common/WKB.cpp) now emits zero rings for a single-empty-ring polygon, matching the canonical form `010300000000000000`. This canonicalizes only the `wkb()` bytes and covers both freshly parsed values and rows already stored as `[[]]` by older builds. The in-memory Polygon value is left unchanged, so `readWKTPolygon('POLYGON EMPTY')` still returns `[[]]` and SQL value equality, joins, and `GROUP BY` over empty polygons are unaffected. This PR is scoped to WKB. `wkt()` streams through `boost::geometry::wkt` and prints `POLYGON()` for a zero-ring polygon (the same shape it uses for other empty geometries, e.g. `MULTIPOLYGON()`); making `wkt()` emit `POLYGON EMPTY` is a separate concern and is not addressed here. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110796&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/110796](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F110796+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Encode nulls-action variant in -Tuple aggregate state type name
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110073 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107951 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111580 --> Related: #110073 Related: #107951 Related: #111580 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a server crash when merging aggregate states of a `-Tuple` combinator function (e.g. `anyLastTuple(...) RESPECT NULLS`) whose declared type differs from the actual type, for example over a `Distributed` table under `GROUP BY ... WITH CUBE` / `WITH TOTALS`. ### Description Investigation of the crash reported on #110073: `AST fuzzer (amd_debug, targeted)` `Segmentation fault (STID: 4281-3dd7)` in `TotalsHavingTransform::addToTotals` -> `ColumnAggregateFunction::insertMergeFrom` -> `SingleValueData`. CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110073&sha=25d3ba356582bfc4bb86b97482278932468c00f2&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29 Root cause: the `-Tuple` aggregate combinator's serialized state type name was not injective with respect to the nulls-action variant of its nested functions. `anyLastTuple(...) RESPECT NULLS` resolves nested `anyLast_respect_nulls` (state layout `AggregateFunctionAnyRespectNullsData`), while the plain form resolves `anyLast` (`SingleValueDataGeneric`) - two different, byte-incompatible state representations. But `getName()` was composed from the pre-resolution nested name, so both produced the identical type name `AggregateFunction(anyLastTuple, Tuple(...))`. When that name round-trips - over the distributed wire, from disk, or when the totals/cube path reconstructs the accumulator - the reader resolves the wrong nested variant from the shared name and reinterprets the state bytes, dereferencing a bad vtable in `assert_cast<SingleValueDataGeneric &>`. This is expressible on master with the classic `Distributed` form (declared `UInt128` over a `UInt64` source), no table-function feature required: ```sql CREATE TABLE src (number UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY number; INSERT INTO src SELECT number FROM numbers(10); CREATE TABLE dist (number UInt128) ENGINE = Distributed(test_cluster_two_shards_localhost, currentDatabase(), src, number); SELECT last_valueTupleOrNull(tuple( tuple(* APPLY lambda(tuple(x), isNull(x)) EXCEPT '.*' REPLACE (2147483647 AS `e`)), tuple(* APPLY (lambda(tuple(x), isNull(x)), 'f_') EXCEPT '.*' REPLACE (1024 AS `e`)))) RESPECT NULLS FROM dist GROUP BY ALL WITH CUBE; -- SIGSEGV before this change ``` Fix: derive the `-Tuple` base name from a resolved non-placeholder nested function, matching how `-Array` / `-If` / `-OrNull` compose their names from `nested_func->getName()`. This makes the serialized name injective (`anyLast_respect_nullsTupleOrNull` vs `anyLastTupleOrNull`), so a state can only ever be reconstructed as the variant that produced it. Only-null tuple elements collapse to a `nothing*` placeholder with an empty, variant-less state and carry no naming information, so they are skipped; the pre-resolution name is used only as a fallback when every element is a placeholder. The `-Tuple` combinator is new in this version (`introduced_in {26, 7}`), so no released build persisted states under the old name and there is no on-disk compatibility concern. Also closes #111580 (`AST fuzzer (amd_debug, targeted, old_compatibility)` `Segmentation fault (STID: 2470-2cc1)`), the same crash class reached through a combinator-wrapped nested function. `anyRespectNullsArgMinTupleOrNull(...) IGNORE NULLS` over a `Distributed` table `WITH TOTALS` resolves the nested `anyRespectNullsArgMin` down to `anyArgMin` under `IGNORE NULLS` (a smaller `ArgMin` state, different key offset), while the action-less declared type name reconstructs `any_respect_nullsArgMin` on the initiator - the key offset then mismatches and the totals merge dereferences a wild pointer in `SingleValueDataNumeric`. Deriving the `-Tuple` name from the resolved nested function encodes the action here too, so the type name is injective and the state is reconstructed correctly. Reproducer verified to SIGSEGV on `master` and to be fixed by this change; a regression test covering it is added. While covering that case, the placeholder skip is also extended to a nested `-Tuple` element: `isOnlyNullPlaceholder` on a `-Tuple` holds only when all of its elements are placeholders (the base predicate unwraps only a single-nested combinator chain), so an all-only-null inner tuple no longer lends its pre-resolution name to the outer tuple.

signals.title: Compare stored table definition expressions by AST instead of formatted text
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/92340 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110840 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108590 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed cross-version metadata compatibility for tables whose keys and other definition expressions were written with redundant parentheses (`PARTITION BY (a)`, `ORDER BY (b, c)`, `DEFAULT (a + 1)`, `TTL (d + INTERVAL 10 YEAR)`, `INDEX ix (b * c)`, `CONSTRAINT c CHECK (a > 0)`, `PROJECTION p (SELECT (b) ...)`) or with an explicit single-element `tuple(a)`. #92340 started preserving these parentheses in stored metadata, so `ATTACH`/`REPLACE`/`MOVE PARTITION FROM` between two such tables failed with `Tables have different ...` even on a single server version, and a replica reading metadata written by another version failed with `METADATA_MISMATCH`. Stored table definition expressions are now compared by their ASTs (`getTreeHash`), not by their formatted text. ### Description #92340 started to preserve redundant parentheses in the stored definition ASTs. Older versions stored the canonical form without them, so the metadata serialized by the two versions differs, and every comparison (`ReplicatedMergeTree` replica join, `ATTACH`/`REPLACE`/`MOVE PARTITION FROM`) rejected definitions that are actually equal. Two sub-cases with different affected ranges: - Redundant parentheses (`PARTITION BY (a)` vs `PARTITION BY a`). This is the #92340 regression: measured on released binaries, 25.8, 26.3 and 26.4 accept `ATTACH PARTITION FROM` between the two forms while 26.5, 26.6 and 26.7 reject it, matching the branches that contain `b38a892dfbfab6`. It does **not** require an upgrade or a mixed-version cluster: both tables created by the same 26.7 binary already fail, because the comparison is between two in-memory ASTs of which only one carries the `parenthesized` flag. - An explicit single-element `tuple(a)` vs `a`. This one fails on every version tried, 25.8 included, so it is a long-standing bug rather than a #92340 regression. It is fixed here as well because `extractKeyExpressionList` unwraps the optional `tuple(...)`. Following https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110833#issuecomment-5040213065, this replaces the earlier text-canonicalization approach entirely: - Expressions are compared by their ASTs using `getTreeHash`, not as text or reformatted text. Comparing formatted text is wrong because the text depends on the formatting logic, which can change for unrelated (e.g. aesthetic) reasons, while the stored form may have been written by any past server version. - The comparison method is reusable: `sameAST` in `src/Parsers/IAST.h` (aliases significant, `nullptr`-tolerant overload for optional expressions). - It is applied at every place where serialized, stored expressions are compared to check whether the table was altered or changed unexpectedly: - `ReplicatedMergeTreeTableMetadata::checkImmutableFieldsEquals` / `checkEquals` / `checkAndFindDiff` (replica join, `ALTER` application). The stored strings are parsed purely syntactically (without resolving against any column set), so the fields of an `ALTER` log entry that adds a column and changes a key in one go compare safely; the `columns`/`context` parameters are gone. Keys additionally go through `extractKeyExpressionList`, so `a`, `(a)` and `tuple(a)` are the same single-column key while `a DESC` stays different. - `MergeTreeData::checkStructureAndGetMergeTreeData` (the `ATTACH`/`REPLACE`/`MOVE PARTITION FROM` structure gate): sorting/partition/primary keys and the secondary-index/projection definition sets. - `StorageReplicatedMergeTree::checkTableStructureAttempt`: the columns comparison (`ColumnsDescription`/`ColumnDescription`/`ColumnDefault` equality now compares the default/codec/TTL expressions as ASTs). The column-by-column comparison also has to ignore in-memory-only state that is never serialized (implicit statistics and the auxiliary `data_type` of `ColumnStatisticsDescription`, hence the new `hasSameExplicitStatistics`), otherwise every replicated `CREATE` would report `INCOMPATIBLE_COLUMNS` against the columns it had just written to ZooKeeper. - `StorageReplicatedMergeTree::alter`: detection of which metadata fields an `ALTER` actually changed. The changed fields are also written back to Keeper through the same backward-compatible serializers the `ReplicatedMergeTreeTableMetadata` constructor uses (`formatDefinition` / `formatDefinitionList`), so an `ALTER` never publishes a parenthesized definition that an older replica would reject. - `AlterCommand::isTTLAlter` (whether restating a TTL schedules a `MATERIALIZE TTL` mutation) and the `MODIFY ORDER BY` no-op detection in `AlterCommands::prepare`. - `ProjectionDescription::operator==`. - For `getTreeHash` to be a faithful identity of a definition, AST nodes that keep semantic state outside of `children` now hash that state (`updateTreeHashImpl` overrides): `ASTTTLElement` (mode, destination, `GROUP BY` keys/assignments, recompression codec), `ASTIndexDeclaration` (name, granularity), `ASTConstraintDeclaration` (name, `CHECK`/`ASSUME`), `ASTProjectionDeclaration` (name), `ASTProjectionSelectQuery` (which clause each child belongs to, previously `SELECT a GROUP BY b` and `SELECT a ORDER BY b` hashed equally), `ASTWindowDefinition` (frame type and boundary kinds). - Since a member that is not a child and is not hashed silently makes two different definitions compare equal, `getTreeHash` documents the requirement, and the classes whose member set is the whole point of the override (`ASTTTLElement`, `ASTIndexDeclaration`, `ASTConstraintDeclaration`, `ASTProjectionDeclaration`, `ASTWindowDefinition`, `ASTSetQuery`, `ASTWithElement`, `ASTWindowListElement`) carry a `sizeof` `static_assert`, so adding a member there fails to compile until it is considered. `ASTSelectQuery`, `ASTProjectionSelectQuery` and `ASTOrderByElement` instead iterate the clause/child-role enumerators, so a newly added one is hashed with no code change. The remaining overrides are not asserted: `ASTColumnsApplyTransformer` (which reaches the `parameters` and `lambda` subtrees) and `ASTSelectWithUnionQuery` hash more than one member, `ASTWithAlias` and `ASTSelectIntersectExceptQuery` one each. Measured: the `static_assert` fires for a new `String`, `UInt64` or pointer member; a lone `bool` can still fit in tail padding, which the comment covers. The negative tests found five ways the comparison was too permissive, each of which master rejects. They are fixed here and each is covered by a test that fails if the fix is reverted: - `ColumnDescription::operator==` used `IDataType::equals`, which ignores the `SimpleAggregateFunction` wrapper (as `MergeTreeData::sortingKeyChanged` already documents), so a replica declaring a plain `UInt64` joined a table whose column is `SimpleAggregateFunction(sum, UInt64)`. It compares `getName` now. - `hasSameExplicitStatistics` kept only the `StatisticsType`, so `STATISTICS(tdigest(1))` and `STATISTICS(tdigest(2))` compared equal although the parameters are a part of the stored definition and survive `SHOW CREATE`. The declaration ASTs are compared as well. - `parameters` and `lambda` of `ASTColumnsApplyTransformer` are not children and were hashed with `updateTreeHashImpl`, which stops at the node itself, so a projection using `APPLY quantile(0.5)` and one using `APPLY quantile(0.9)` hashed equally. `stripArtificialParens` could not reach them either. Both now descend. - The alias was hashed without a length prefix, so `fooIdentifier_bar` and `bar AS Identifier_foo` produced the same byte stream and two projections with different output columns compared equal. - `ASTWindowDefinition` keeps its frame type and boundary kinds outside `children` and did not hash them, so a projection aggregating over `ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` compared equal to one over `ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND CURRENT ROW`. The frame offsets are children and were already covered. One latent bug became reachable and is fixed too: `ASTTTLElement::clone` left `recompression_codec` shared with the source, and `formatDefinition` clones the metadata AST specifically in order to canonicalize it, so `stripArtificialParens` would have written into the live metadata snapshot of a `RECOMPRESS` TTL. No parser or formatter changes and no on-disk/`SHOW CREATE` changes: what the user wrote is preserved; only comparisons became insensitive to formatting. Genuinely different definitions still differ (`a` vs `b`, `a` vs `a DESC`, different index granularity, `CHECK` vs `ASSUME`, different TTL destination). The comparison of whole `CREATE` queries during `RESTORE` (`compareRestoredTableDef`) still compares text: it is a whole-query comparison rather than an expression comparison, and its failure direction is safe (refuses the restore). Tested with a real previous-version server (`clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.4`): `tests/integration/test_backward_compatibility/test_parenthesized_keys.py` exercises a new replica joining an old table and vice versa, an old replica applying parenthesized `ALTER` log entries written by the new version plus restarts of both replicas, and upgrade + `ATTACH PARTITION FROM`. Unit test `src/Storages/MergeTree/tests/gtest_replicated_metadata_compare.cpp` locks the comparison semantics including the negative cases. Stateless tests: `03471_replace_partition_tuple_key_normalization`, `04604_parenthesized_partition_key_attach_from`, `04612_parenthesized_index_projection_attach_from`, `04622_modify_ttl_parenthesized_no_mutation`, `04646_projection_ttl_parenthesized_zk_metadata`, `04648_alter_parenthesized_zk_metadata`, `04650_replica_column_definition_mismatch_rejected`, `04693_projection_apply_function_name_case` (the function name of a projection's `COLUMNS(...) APPLY` transformer is canonicalized for the comparison only, so `APPLY SUM` and `APPLY sum` compare equal while the stored definition keeps the as-written spelling that older replicas compare byte-for-byte). <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110833&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/110833](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F110833+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Add introspection TCP port
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ClickHouse server now has an introspection port. This is a native protocol TCP listener that starts before the server begins attaching tables and stops only after the tables' detach completes. During these windows, an operator can connect to it with `clickhouse client` and run queries such as `SHOW PROCESSLIST`, `SELECT * FROM system.stack_trace`, or `SYSTEM INSTRUMENT ADD 'QueryMetricLog::startQuery' SLEEP ENTRY 0.5`. Additionally, the default value of the `shutdown_wait_unfinished` server setting is increased from 5 to 120 seconds. The previous default was smaller than the connection poll interval, so the server could force exit in the middle of shutdown instead of waiting for outstanding connections to finish. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110838&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/110838](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F110838+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Validate engine features before rewriting metadata on ATTACH AS REPLICATED
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110854 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `ATTACH TABLE ... AS REPLICATED` leaving a table unloadable after restart when the source table used an unsupported clause for the target engine (e.g. a `MergeTree` table with a `UNIQUE KEY` clause, which `ReplicatedMergeTree` does not support). The conversion is now validated before the on-disk metadata is rewritten, so a rejected `ATTACH ... AS REPLICATED` keeps the stored metadata intact. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110854 `ATTACH TABLE ... AS REPLICATED` rewrote the on-disk metadata to the Replicated engine (`convertMergeTreeTableIfPossible` in `InterpreterCreateQuery.cpp`) before the engine-feature validation ran. Feature support is only checked later in `StorageFactory::get` when the storage is instantiated, where `ReplicatedMergeTree` rejects the `UNIQUE KEY` clause. So the query returned `Code 36 BAD_ARGUMENTS`, but the metadata file had already been replaced with an invalid `ReplicatedMergeTree(...) ... UNIQUE KEY (...)` combination and there was no rollback. On the next server start the load job for the table failed with `Code 36`, surfaced to clients as `Code 722 ASYNC_LOAD_WAIT_FAILED`. Repro (from the issue): ```sql SET allow_experimental_unique_key = 1; CREATE TABLE t0 (c0 Int) ENGINE = MergeTree() ORDER BY tuple() UNIQUE KEY (c0); DETACH TABLE t0; ATTACH TABLE t0 AS REPLICATED; -- returns Code 36, but rewrites the metadata anyway -- after restart: SELECT * FROM t0; -- Code 722 ASYNC_LOAD_WAIT_FAILED ``` The fix validates that the target engine supports the `UNIQUE KEY` clause in `convertMergeTreeTableIfPossible` before any side effect (before clearing transaction metadata and before writing the new metadata file). `UNIQUE KEY` is the only DDL clause whose support differs between the `MergeTree` family and `ReplicatedMergeTree`, so this fully covers the conversion. The rejected conversion now keeps the clean `Code 36` error, leaves the stored metadata untouched, and the table remains loadable after restart. Added stateless regression test `04545_attach_as_replicated_unique_key`.

signals.title: Disable TopK dynamic filtering when a sorting projection makes the read in-order
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110862 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a performance regression where `use_top_k_dynamic_filtering` installed a redundant `__topKFilter` prewhere for `ORDER BY ... LIMIT` queries served in-order by a sorting projection, causing the sort column to be read twice. ### Description Closes: #110862 `optimizeTopK` disables `use_top_k_dynamic_filtering` when the `ORDER BY` column is a prefix of the read's sorted order: there the dynamic prewhere filter is counterproductive, because once the running threshold stabilizes it rejects all remaining rows in sorted order, defeating the early pipeline cancellation that `LIMIT` relies on and forcing a full scan. That guard only checked the base table's sorting key. When a sorting projection whose `ORDER BY` differs from the base table is selected, the read is `ReadType: InOrder` with respect to the projection's sort key, but the guard never matched, so the redundant `__topKFilter` prewhere was installed on top of the projection read, re-reading the sort column that in-order reading already provided. `tryOptimizeTopK` runs in the first plan pass, before projection selection and read-in-order (both second pass), so the guard is predictive. It now also disables dynamic filtering when a normal sorting projection whose `ORDER BY` starts with the sort column and which stores every read column is available and projection optimization is enabled — the exact condition under which such a projection is later chosen to serve the read in-order. Results were correct in all cases; this is a performance-only fix. Verified with `EXPLAIN` that the redundant `__topKFilter` is no longer installed while the projection is still selected and the read stays `InOrder`, and that dynamic filtering is still applied when no projection can serve the order.
signals.author: groeneai

signals.title: Harden 00965_send_logs_level_concurrent_queries against async trace-log delivery race
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/101039 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110035 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Description Follow-up to #110035 for `00965_send_logs_level_concurrent_queries`. The positive check asserts that a trace-level query streams at least one `<Trace>` line. Trace logs are delivered asynchronously, so under heavy load (sanitizer builds, slow or remote object storage, high concurrency) a query occasionally closes its client stream before the first trace line is flushed. That yields zero `<Trace>` lines and a false `Fail` while the server behaves correctly. This is the residual flakiness observed after #110035 (which fixed the deterministic positional field-8 fragility of the same test). The trace query is now retried a bounded number of times. The assertion still fails permanently if no trace line is ever delivered, so the test keeps its ability to catch a real regression, but it tolerates a transient delivery miss. Local verification (debug build): the hardened test prints 10x `OK` and matches the reference; a controlled fake client that returns zero trace lines on the first attempts still yields `OK` via retry, whereas the old single-shot form would print `Fail` on the same transient miss.
signals.author: groeneai

signals.title: Do not abort server when loading a view without columns in metadata
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/60708 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a server abort (`LOGICAL_ERROR: Invalid storage definition in metadata file`) on startup when a `VIEW` is stored without a column list in its metadata. Such a view now fails to load with a normal exception instead of terminating the whole server. ### Description `createTableFromAST` (`src/Databases/DatabaseOnDisk.cpp`) threw a `LOGICAL_ERROR` ("Invalid storage definition in metadata file") whenever a table had no column list and no storage engine. That premise does not hold for views: an ordinary view has no storage engine by design (`StorageFactory` explicitly forbids one), and its stored column list may legitimately be absent. Only parameterized views were exempted (added in #60708), so any other columnless view definition found in on-disk metadata (produced by the AST fuzzer, an upgrade, or manual intervention) hit the throw during async table loading and aborted the entire server on startup. The fix skips this throw for all views. A columnless view now fails to load with a catchable `EMPTY_LIST_OF_COLUMNS_PASSED` exception, and the server stays up. Found by the Stress test (amd_asan_ubsan) job: the server crashed during the restart phase while loading the fuzzer-created parameterized view `test_5.prewhere_bug_view__fuzz_4` (from `04227_prewhere_parameterized_view_join_102074.sql`). Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=107091&sha=5e31ccb31390e87186ca0a7a5a047aec6968c392&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_asan_ubsan%29 Stack: ``` DB::createTableFromAST (src/Databases/DatabaseOnDisk.cpp:127) DB::DatabaseOrdinary::loadTableFromMetadata (src/Databases/DatabaseOrdinary.cpp:386) DB::AsyncLoader::worker -> <Fatal> Received signal 6 (Aborted) ```

signals.title: Fix LOGICAL_ERROR in OPTIMIZE ... DRY RUN racing a concurrent merge
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107114 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114399 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a `LOGICAL_ERROR` exception (`Temporary part ... already added`) when `OPTIMIZE ... DRY RUN` runs concurrently with a real merge, or with another `DRY RUN`, on the same parts. ### Description `MergeTreeData::optimizeDryRun` executes a real `MergeTask` but, unlike the real optimize/merge paths, takes no `CurrentlyMergingPartsTagger` and no merge lock, so it never registers its source parts as "being merged". A concurrent real merge on the same parts computes the same result part name and reserves the same `tmp_merge_<result>` directory. The second reservation trips `TemporaryParts::add` -> `LOGICAL_ERROR "Temporary part ... already added"`, aborting the server on debug and sanitizer builds. Seen on 17 unrelated PRs over the 30 days to 2026-08-11 (CIDB `default.checks`, 17 rows / 17 distinct PRs), never on master. The dry-run part is throwaway, so its directory need not be named after the result part. It is now `tmp_merge_dry_run_<uuid>`, making the collision impossible on both `MergeTree` and `ReplicatedMergeTree`. A UUID rather than a counter, because the directory can live on storage shared with other servers, where a process-local counter restarts and repeats itself. Leaving the part name out also avoids a length trap: appending a token to it can exceed the 255-byte filename limit while the real merge of the same parts still succeeds. Part names are not length-capped (an all-integral partition key spells its values out, so ten `Int64` fields plus an `IPv4` reach 226 bytes) and `MergeTree` prepends `delete_tmp_` before removal, leaving 8 bytes. The new name has a fixed size. It is never parsed back into a part name and still starts with `tmp_merge_`, which the cleaner and the startup skip logic select by. Only a `dry_run_` suffix takes the new path, so top-level and projection merges keep byte-identical names. Not a duplicate of the `DRY RUN` fix linked above (rows_sources under a soft timeout). Tracking issue: #114399. Test `03823_optimize_dry_run_merge_race` races two `DRY RUN`s on the same parts via a new failpoint pausing after the directory is reserved, at part-name lengths 7, 9 and 226, asserting the real merge succeeds at 226 and each `DRY RUN` really merged.
