signals.title: Restore Parquet column pruning for Iceberg schema-evolved reads
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110897 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Restore Parquet column pruning for Iceberg data files written under an older schema. After schema evolution (e.g. `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN`), reading an old data file decoded every physical column even when the query needed only one; now only the columns the query requires are read. ### Description Fixes #110897. When an Iceberg table's schema evolves, `IcebergMetadata::getInitialSchemaByPath` returns the full underlying (old) file schema for data files whose schema id differs from the current one. In `StorageObjectStorageSource::createReader` this full schema became the Parquet reader's `initial_header`, so the reader decoded every physical column of the old file; the schema-transform DAG only ran afterwards. Adding one unrelated nullable column turned `SELECT sum(id)` from decoding just `id` into also decoding the table's wide string columns (reporter measured ~23x more selected bytes, ~5x peak memory). The Iceberg schema-transform DAG maps old-schema input names to new-schema output names (by field name), so pruning its unused actions against the query's required columns yields exactly the old-schema physical columns to read. This is the same pruning the Delta path already does; here it is applied to the Iceberg `getSchemaTransformer()` path and the pruned transform is reused so the read header and the transform stay consistent. Pruning is applied only when there are no equality-delete files: equality deletes are applied by name on the old-schema block before the schema transform runs, so their key columns must remain in the read header even if the query does not select them. When any needed column is not a transform output the full schema is kept, so unusual column shapes fall back to current behavior rather than failing. Regression test `04545_iceberg_schema_evolution_column_pruning_110897` asserts an id-only read decodes far fewer bytes than a read that needs the wide column, and that results (including reads of the added and renamed columns, and filters on non-selected columns) stay correct.

signals.title: Fix Bad cast for GROUP BY ALL WITH ROLLUP scalar subquery under group_by_use_nulls
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110915 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `Bad cast` error (abort in debug/sanitizer builds) when a scalar subquery aggregates over a derived table that uses `GROUP BY ALL WITH ROLLUP`/`CUBE`/`GROUPING SETS` under `group_by_use_nulls = 1`. ### Description `GROUP BY ALL` is expanded into the GROUP BY key list only at the very end of query resolution (`expandGroupByAll` needs the resolved projection). Under `group_by_use_nulls = 1` that is too late: `resolveGroupByNode` runs earlier, gated by `hasGroupBy()`, which is false while the GROUP BY list is still empty. So the keys were never registered in `nullable_group_by_keys` and the inner projection kept its non-`Nullable` type, while `WITH ROLLUP` execution produces `Nullable`. In a scalar subquery the outer aggregate is resolved against the inner query's advertised (non-`Nullable`) projection type, so it is built without the `Null` combinator adapter and crashes at run time in `addBatchSinglePlace` with `Bad cast from type ColumnNullable to ColumnVector<...>`. Spelling the key explicitly (`GROUP BY val`) already worked. Fix: in the `group_by_use_nulls` path, when the query is `GROUP BY ALL`, resolve the projection and expand `GROUP BY ALL` before `resolveGroupByNode`, so the keys are registered and the projection is re-resolved with the `Nullable` promotion, exactly like the explicit-key path. The change is guarded by `isGroupByAll()`, so all other queries are unaffected. Reproducer (aborts on master, works with this PR): ```sql SET group_by_use_nulls = 1; SELECT (SELECT avgOrDefault(val) FROM (SELECT rand64() AS val FROM numbers(10) GROUP BY ALL WITH ROLLUP)); ``` Found by the AST fuzzer (`AST fuzzer (amd_debug)`, STID 1499-33a5) on unrelated PR #110606: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110606&sha=d9c6d9deca1e7c4fc5965f466d6beede6922b808&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%29 Closes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110915

signals.title: Fix RENAME TABLE of a Distributed table with a non-empty async-insert queue
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/92124 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `RENAME TABLE` of a `Distributed` table is now refused when it would have to move the table's asynchronous insert queue directory, which only happens in the deprecated `Ordinary` database engine. Previously the rename appeared to succeed while a file that was still queued kept being addressed by its pre-rename path, so its rows were never delivered: with `background_insert_batch = 0` `SYSTEM FLUSH DISTRIBUTED` failed with `Cannot open file ... errno: 2`, and with `background_insert_batch = 1` it reported success while delivering nothing. An `Atomic` database keys the data directory by UUID and never moves it, so renames there are unaffected. ### Description A `Distributed` table keeps one async-insert queue directory per shard under its data path. In an `Ordinary` database `RENAME TABLE` moves that path, and nothing serialises the move against concurrent work: `DistributedSink` resolves a queue directory, links the block into it and enqueues it without holding the mutex the move takes, and `SYSTEM FLUSH DISTRIBUTED` copies the queue pointers under that mutex but runs the sends after releasing it. `pause()` does not help either, since it only deactivates the scheduled task while the flush runs on a foreground pool. Rather than synchronise the move, this removes the case: `DatabaseAtomic::renameTable` never calls `IStorage::rename` at all (it moves the metadata file and calls `renameInMemory`, and the data directory is `store/<uuid>`), and `DatabaseOnDisk` is the only caller of it. So the defect is confined to `Ordinary`, which is deprecated behind `allow_deprecated_database_ordinary`, and refusing the rename there means no queue repointing, no task pause, and no filesystem work under a mutex. The refusal is skipped in three cases: no data path (a `remote()` target), `ATTACH ... FROM` (which calls `rename()` with an unchanged `StorageID` only to move data into place before the table is reachable), and the `Ordinary`-to-`Atomic` conversion, which assigns a UUID to every table during startup. That last one requires the acquired UUID, matching `StorageReplicatedMergeTree::checkTableCanBeRenamed`, since startup scripts also run before the server is completely started. Verified live: converting a database holding a `Distributed` table with a queued file succeeds and delivers that row. `01155_rename_move_materialized_view` moved such a table between the two engines by hand and now recreates it, which is what a user has to do. `test_distributed_storage_configuration` used `Ordinary` for a predictable data path and now reads the path from `system.tables`, keeping its `RENAME` coverage on `Atomic`.

signals.title: Fix LOGICAL_ERROR in ReadFromMergeTree::deserialize for empty distributed-read snapshot
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110927 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110910 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a `LOGICAL_ERROR` in experimental multistage distributed query planning (`make_distributed_plan`) when a worker deserializes a bucketed `ReadFromMergeTree` read whose local parts snapshot has become empty (parts merged away or dropped concurrently). ### Description Fixes the LOGICAL_ERROR `ReadFromMergeTree step is expected to be created by readFromParts` in `ReadFromMergeTree::deserialize`, in the multistage distributed queries feature (`make_distributed_plan`, experimental). Closes #110927. Surfaced once in 60 days on `Stress test (arm_release)` (report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110910&sha=51e6b0ddc85e666b2fcfacc3238134aeba30e55c&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_release%29). Not caused by #110910 (which only touches `randomHadamardTransform`); it is a pre-existing latent bug in the distributed-read deserialize path. Root cause: the coordinator serializes a bucketed read (`distributed_read_bucket_count > 0`) while parts exist. A worker deserializes it, but its local parts snapshot can be empty by then (parts merged away or dropped under stress churn). `readFromParts` returns a null step for an empty non-stream read, and the bucketed branch then `dynamic_cast`s it to null and throws. Fix: on the deserialize path only, `readFromParts` now builds a real (empty) `ReadFromMergeTree` step for a bucketed read even when the local snapshot is empty, so the bucket count has a step to attach to. `initializePipeline` then resolves it exactly as before at runtime: a genuinely empty bucket reads nothing, and a bucket whose coordinator-selected part is missing locally raises the existing retryable `NO_SUCH_DATA_PART` divergence error. A `ReadNothingStep` short-circuit would instead bypass that divergence check and silently drop rows, so it is deliberately not used. The other five `readFromParts` callers are unchanged.

signals.title: Promote exponentialTimeDecayed window-functions to aggregate-functions
signals.text: ## Motivation `exponentialTimeDecayedSum`, `exponentialTimeDecayedAvg`, and `exponentialTimeDecayedCount` already exist and are documented as aggregate functions, but their current implementation is a special window-function implementation in `WindowTransform`. They do not provide mergeable aggregate states that can be persisted and combined with aggregate combinators such as `-State` and `-Merge`. This prevents incremental time-decayed aggregation in engines such as `AggregatingMergeTree`: data has to be evaluated through the window path instead of being aggregated independently in multiple batches and merged later. This PR adds regular, mergeable aggregate implementations for those three names while preserving the existing window implementation and its behavior. ## What changes For the regular aggregate form, each state keeps the weighted sum and sum of weights at the greatest timestamp observed by that state, plus that timestamp. When a row or another state has an older anchor, it is moved to the newer anchor with: `exp((older_time - newer_time) / decay_length)` The existing semantics are unchanged: `decay_length` is the interval after which a contribution has weight `1/e`. It is not a half-life. With the default `exponential_time_decay_aggregate_function_calculation_budget = 0`, the state representation makes independently built states mergeable with the same calculation. Input rows do not need to be timestamp ordered, and different row orders and batch distributions produce the same mathematical result subject to normal `Float64` rounding. A positive calculation budget opts into approximate aggregation: it is the maximum contribution age measured in decay lengths. Older rows or states are discarded before evaluating `exp`, improving performance when their remaining weight is not useful. Approximate results near the cutoff can depend on row order or merge grouping. The aggregate forms accept numeric timestamps, `DateTime`, and `DateTime64`. ### Finalized decaying values The sum and count aggregate forms return the experimental parameterized type: `ExponentialTimeDecayingFloat64(decay_length)` The decay length is part of the type. Its tuple-compatible storage is canonicalized as `(sign, signed_unit_time, decay_length)`, where `unit_time = anchor_time + decay_length * ln(abs(value))` is the timestamp at which the curve has unit magnitude and `signed_unit_time = sign * unit_time`. Zero has the canonical form `(0, 0, decay_length)`. This representation makes native sorting and relative comparisons match the curve values at any common timestamp for values with the same decay length. Comparisons across different decay lengths are rejected. The redundant decay-length marker is checked against the type parameter when a value is evaluated or combined, preventing incompatible values from being silently mixed through layout-compatible custom-tuple paths. Values can be constructed/aggregated with: `exponentialTimeDecayingFloat64(decay_length)(value, time)` A finalized decaying value can be aggregated again without repeating the decay length: `exponentialTimeDecayedSum(decaying_value)` When the input is `ExponentialTimeDecayingFloat64(decay_length)`, the decay length is inferred from its type and the result has the same parameterized type. This gives the closure property required by `SimpleAggregateFunction`, so it can be stored directly in `AggregatingMergeTree`: ```sql CREATE TABLE decaying ( key UInt64, value SimpleAggregateFunction( exponentialTimeDecayedSum, ExponentialTimeDecayingFloat64(60)) ) ENGINE = AggregatingMergeTree ORDER BY key; ``` The scalar helpers are: - `exponentialTimeDecayingValueAt(value, target_time)` — evaluate the same exponential curve before, at, or after its anchor, including at `now()` / `now64()`; - `exponentialTimeDecayingDecayLength(value)` — read the decay length encoded in the type; - `exponentialTimeDecayingAdd(a, b)` — combine two values at their greatest anchor. The `+` operator uses the same addition logic for two decaying values. Different decay lengths are rejected. `exponentialTimeDecayedAvg` continues to return `Float64`. All new regular-aggregate and decaying-value behavior is experimental and disabled by default behind `allow_experimental_time_decay_aggregate_functions`. ## Effect on the existing window functions The existing window-function implementation remains in place. Window calls continue to use the previous frame-based implementation, retain their `Float64` result, and do not require `allow_experimental_time_decay_aggregate_functions`. This PR also corrects the function documentation to consistently call the parameter `decay_length` and describe the existing `1/e` decay semantics. ## Correctness and tests Stateless tests cover: - regular aggregation and `-State` / `-Merge`; - direct aggregation of finalized `ExponentialTimeDecayingFloat64(decay_length)` values; - direct `SimpleAggregateFunction(exponentialTimeDecayedSum, ExponentialTimeDecayingFloat64(decay_length))` storage and merging in `AggregatingMergeTree`; - different input orders and batch distributions, including reproducibly generated randomized inputs; - numeric, `DateTime`, and `DateTime64` time arguments; - the experimental setting in enabled and disabled forms; - forward and backward value evaluation, addition, decay-length lookup, and rejection of inconsistent/mixed decay lengths; - native sorting and all relative comparison operators, including negative, zero, and positive values; - exact-default, bounded-cutoff, and state-merge calculation-budget behavior; - signed values, empty input, nullable paths, canonical reconstruction, and large-time decay/underflow cases. The implementation uses `Float64` accumulation. As with other floating-point reductions, large signed values that nearly cancel can expose order/grouping-dependent rounding. Stronger reproducibility for that case is intentionally left for a separate improvement if feedback shows it is important in practice. ## Benchmark status There are no end-to-end ClickHouse benchmark results yet. The benchmark already posted in the PR discussion is a standalone C++ microbenchmark of the decay formulas. It showed the expected benefit from avoiding redundant `exp` evaluations in the merge/value paths, but it excludes ClickHouse aggregation, column access, serialization, scheduling, and `AggregatingMergeTree` overhead and therefore is not evidence of end-to-end query throughput. An end-to-end benchmark, preferably a ClickHouse performance test covering state creation and state merging, is still pending. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Add experimental mergeable `exponentialTimeDecayedSum`, `exponentialTimeDecayedAvg`, and `exponentialTimeDecayedCount` aggregate forms, including a parameterized decaying-value type that can be stored directly with `SimpleAggregateFunction` in `AggregatingMergeTree`, while preserving the existing window-function behavior. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110934&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/110934](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F110934+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Do automatic partition pruning for mutations when it's possible
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `ReplicatedMergeTree` mutations now automatically prune the affected partitions based on the `WHERE` part of the query when possible. Also, mutation queries now accept multiple values in the `IN PARTITION` clause. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/98739 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/99933 This supersedes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/99933 by @alesapin, whose commits are preserved in this branch. The original PR became `CONFLICTING` and could not be updated because maintainer edits are disabled on the fork; the branch had also fallen ~4.5 months behind `master` (in particular, the `MutationCommand` refactor to a text-backed lazy AST required reworking how commands carry `partition`/`partitions`/`predicate`). On top of the original feature, this PR: - Merges current `master` and adapts the code to the `MutationCommand` refactor (commands are re-parsed from `ast_text` via `command.ast()`), the two-argument `getInMemoryMetadataPtr` and the three-argument `ActionsDAGWithInversionPushDown`. - Moves the `optimize_mutations_with_partition_pruning` entry to the current settings-history bucket (review thread on `SettingsChangesHistory.cpp`). - Makes the pruning analysis accept every predicate the mutation itself accepts, instead of hiding failures: the analysis follows the same analyzer selection as the mutation execution - the analysis context matches how the commands will actually be interpreted - for an `ALTER` mutation it is derived from the background context exactly like the background mutation workers derive theirs, so session-only analyzer settings cannot make the submit-time analysis and the asynchronous execution diverge (analyzer-only predicate shapes such as qualified column names work, and a predicate the background execution would reject fails fast at submit time; test `04759_mutation_pruning_background_analyzer_mode`), while a lightweight `UPDATE`, which interprets its commands in the foreground, is analyzed with the submitting context, where the session settings and the current database apply (its predicate is not qualified with the default database, unlike `ALTER` commands; covered by the existing test `03100_lwu_43_subquery_from_rmt`), the column list includes the virtual columns (e.g. `_part`, `_partition_id`) and the `ALIAS` / `EPHEMERAL` columns, and the re-parsed predicate's set operations (`UNION` / `INTERSECT` / `EXCEPT`) are normalized exactly as the mutation execution path does. There is no fallback: an analysis error propagates and fails the mutation rather than silently mutating every partition (review). Without the above, `ALTER TABLE t DELETE WHERE _part = '...'` and similar queries would fail since the setting is enabled by default. Covered by the new test `04612_mutation_pruning_exotic_predicates`. - Requires the `block_numbers` version check only for predicate-pruned commands (review thread on `StorageReplicatedMergeTree.cpp`): for explicit `IN PARTITION` the target set is exact and does not depend on the observed partition list, so the `ZBADVERSION` retry loop is not needed. - In the `ZNONODE` recovery of `EphemeralLocksInPartitions`, reports `ZBADVERSION` to the caller after creating missing partition znodes instead of silently refreshing the version, so a concurrently created partition cannot be missed. - `StorageMergeTree::mutate` validates only explicit `IN PARTITION` ids instead of running the full pruning analysis and discarding the result (on the non-replicated path, parts of unaffected partitions are skipped per part by `canSkipMutationCommandForPart`). - Documents the multi-partition `IN PARTITION` syntax and the automatic pruning behavior. - Recomputes the pruned partition set on every `ZBADVERSION` retry, so a new matching partition created by a concurrent insert on the initiating replica cannot escape the mutation (AI review blocker). Covered by the new failpoint-based test `04613_mutation_pruning_new_partition_race`. - Widens the pruned set with ZooKeeper-only partitions by comparing against the partition set the pruning analysis itself iterated (returned by the pruner from its own parts snapshot), not against a separately read local partition list: a partition the pruner analyzed and ruled out is not re-added, while a partition it could not have seen is still widened in, so a same-replica insert racing with the analysis can neither escape the mutation nor drag an unaffected partition back into it (AI review). Covered by the failpoint-based tests `04614_mutation_pruning_local_partition_race` and `04820_mutation_pruning_analyzed_partition_not_widened`. - Scopes the setting description, the documentation and the changelog entry to the `ReplicatedMergeTree` family: on plain `MergeTree`, predicate-based pruning is not wired in, and an explicit `IN PARTITION` clause should be used (AI review). - Rejects the new `alter->partitions` carrier in `StorageSystemWasmModules` (exactly like the single-partition form) and preserves it in `AlterConversions::createLightweightDeleteCommand`, so the multi-partition clause cannot be silently ignored (AI review). One design note kept as in the original: in the `ZNONODE` recovery path, missing partition znodes are created one per multi-op (create + parent version bump), matching the established pattern of the insert path in `allocateBlockNumber`; batching them into a single parent bump was considered but rejected because a partial `ZNODEEXISTS` would fail the whole multi-op and require a more complex retry. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110968&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/110968](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F110968+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Report the owner query_ids and hold count in RWLock re-entrancy errors
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110893 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): When an `RWLockImpl::getLock()` re-entrancy assertion fires (`RWLock is already locked in exclusive mode` / `Cannot acquire exclusive lock while RWLock is already locked`), the error message now names the other `query_id`s currently owning the lock and how many locks the requesting `query_id` already holds, to make such lock-ordering errors diagnosable. ### Description Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110893 The two fast-path re-entrancy assertions in `RWLockImpl::getLock()` fire when the requesting `query_id` is already present in `owner_queries`, but their messages named nothing at all - so the only artifact of a rare lock-ordering error was the bare sentence. That is the case for the `CREATE OR REPLACE MATERIALIZED VIEW ... POPULATE` re-entrant deadlock seen under stress, which has no local reproducer. Both messages now report: - the **set of owner `query_id`s**, with a count next to any `query_id` held by more than one thread - i.e. who else is holding the lock, which is not recoverable from anything else in the log; - the **number of locks the requesting `query_id` already holds** - an owner count above one shows the re-entrancy is across sibling threads of the same query rather than a single nested acquisition; - the `query_id` itself. This is the lock key passed to `getLock()`, not the ambient `query_id`: callers pass `getInitialQueryId()` on some paths (`InterpreterSelectQuery`, `InterpreterInsertQuery`), `getCurrentQueryId()` on others, and `RWLockImpl::NO_QUERY` from background threads, so it is not redundant with the log-line prefix. The requester thread id is deliberately *not* printed: `OwnPatternFormatter` already prefixes every line with `[ thread_id ]`, and the holder TID - the one worth pivoting from into a thread dump - is not tracked. Locks taken with `NO_QUERY` never enter `owner_queries`, hence the wording "owner query_ids" rather than "owners". Behaviour-neutral: two error strings, plus `getOwnerQueryIdsDescription()` refactored to share the new `formatOwnerQueryIds()` helper. No new bookkeeping on the lock hot path; the public `getOwnerQueryIds()` API is unchanged. All 8 `Common.RWLock*` unit tests pass. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1672` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Fix data race on DataTypeAggregateFunction version during Native serialization
signals.text: Related: found by the `arm_tsan` and `azure, amd_tsan` Stress tests (STID 3977-4818, ThreadSanitizer data race). No existing issue. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/94859 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112052 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Not for changelog. ### Description A single `DataTypeAggregateFunction` instance is shared across query result blocks: it lives once in the table's column description and is aliased by shallow column copies. `NativeWriter`/`NativeReader` called `setVersionToAggregateFunctions`, which walked to the leaf type and wrote its `mutable version` field in place. Two concurrent `Native` serializations of the same aggregate-function-typed column then raced on that field, and the version written for one old connection stayed on the shared type, so every later query read the states at that version - for `sumMap` over `Decimal32` that returns wrong values. Reports: * https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109496&sha=62eeb400eafe86cedff9b5a4e9a36aa722633cda&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_tsan%29 * https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=b59441bd06c2fcb6b103a30874528cc398afc723&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28azure%2C%20amd_tsan%29 **That fix has since landed on `master`** through #94859 and #112052: `setVersionToAggregateFunctions` now replaces every versioned nested type instead of mutating it, and `replaceNestedSimpleTypes` carries the custom names (`Nested`, `SimpleAggregateFunction`) over the rebuild. This branch is therefore resolved in favour of that implementation, and what it added on top of it - an `IDataType::transformChildren` override per container type, and the `unique_ptr` to `shared_ptr` switch of `DataTypeCustomNamePtr` - is dropped as duplicate machinery. What remains here is what `master` does not have, and it keeps this PR's intent - the race cannot come back, because the version can no longer be assigned in place at all: * `DataTypeAggregateFunction::setVersion` and `updateVersionFromRevision` are removed, and `version` is no longer `mutable`. Both mutators were left without callers by the rewrite on `master`; the version is now set only at construction (parsed from AST, decoded from the binary type encoding, or chosen by `setVersionToAggregateFunctions`, which builds a new type). * Unit and functional coverage of the behaviour, which `master` has only indirectly. ### Testing * `gtest_aggregate_function_version_race` (14 tests) pins the type-level behaviour: the shared type object is not mutated; a wrapper is rebuilt only when a leaf was actually replaced; the `Point`, `Nested` and `SimpleAggregateFunction` custom names survive, including a `Tuple`-backed `SimpleAggregateFunction`; a `Variant` keeps its discriminator order and throws when two alternatives would collapse; a `JSON` typed path keeps the version spelled in its own type name; and an 8-thread x 2000-iteration stress over one shared type object is race-free. * `04612_aggregate_function_version_custom_type_names` round-trips `Nested`, `SimpleAggregateFunction` and a wrapper-named type through `Native` (which assigns the version in the writer and again in the reader) and through `DETACH`/`ATTACH`, and checks that a deeply nested `Nested` stays linear in the nesting depth. * `04613_aggregate_function_version_not_sticky` asks for a `Native` response at a revision below the one that introduced versioning and then checks the column again, so a version pinned for that one response would be visible both in the values read back (`sumMap` over `Decimal32`) and in `system.columns`. The revision is pinned explicitly and the type name the response carries is asserted, so the test cannot pass without that path having run. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110997&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/110997](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F110997+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix NOT_IMPLEMENTED for correlated subqueries when join_algorithm lacks hash
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/103294 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` error ("Can't execute any of specified algorithms...") for correlated subqueries with a non-trivial correlation when `join_algorithm` did not include `hash` or `parallel_hash` (e.g. `auto`, `grace_hash`, `partial_merge`, `full_sorting_merge`). ### Description When a correlated subquery has a non-trivial correlation (e.g. an inequality), it is decorrelated into an internal join. With `correlated_subqueries_use_in_memory_buffer` enabled (the default), that internal join is restricted to hash-family algorithms so the buffered input stream is fully evaluated before the subquery runs. The restriction did this with an unconditional `std::erase_if` on the join's algorithm list: if the user's `join_algorithm` enabled neither `hash` nor `parallel_hash`, the list became empty and `chooseJoinAlgorithm` threw a misleading `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`. The internal decorrelation join must still run in that case, so it now falls back to `hash` when the restriction would otherwise empty the list. Hash join always supports this join and satisfies the in-memory buffer requirement. Reproducer (failed before, works now): ```sql SET enable_analyzer = 1, allow_experimental_correlated_subqueries = 1, join_algorithm = 'full_sorting_merge'; SELECT number FROM numbers(2) AS t WHERE exists((SELECT number FROM numbers(2) WHERE number >= t.number)); ```

signals.title: Fix optimize_distributed_group_by_sharding_key wrong result for JOIN
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111087 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111274 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111087 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111274 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a wrong result with `optimize_distributed_group_by_sharding_key` when grouping a distributed `JOIN` by a column from the other join side that shares the sharding key's name (e.g. `GROUP BY r.k` over a `LEFT JOIN` where `r.k` is not the distributed table's sharding key). Such groups can span shards, so the per-shard aggregation shortcut is no longer applied for them, avoiding duplicate group keys with split aggregate values. ### Description `optimize_distributed_group_by_sharding_key` lets `StorageDistributed` skip the cross-shard merge when the `GROUP BY` key equals the sharding key, assuming each group's rows live on a single shard. In the new analyzer, `isShardingKeySuitsQueryTreeNodeExpression` matched the grouping expression against the sharding key by column name only (table qualifiers are stripped when building the comparison DAG). So a right-side column `r.k` in a distributed `LEFT JOIN` that merely shares the left table's sharding-key name `k` wrongly triggered the shortcut. Unmatched left rows are padded with `r.k = 0` on every shard, so the `r.k = 0` group spans shards and per-shard partial aggregates were returned unmerged, producing duplicate group keys with split values (silent wrong result). The fix skips the shortcut when the grouping/DISTINCT/LIMIT BY expression references any column that is not from the distributed table's own table expression, reusing the existing `hasUnknownColumn` helper. `GROUP BY` over the distributed table's actual sharding key is unaffected. Only the new analyzer path was affected; the old analyzer compares qualified identifier names and was already correct. Issue #111274 (`optimize_skip_unused_shards = 1` duplicating every group of a distributed self-join on an expression sharding key `intHash64(k)`) is the same root cause and is fixed by the same guard: `GROUP BY negate(r.k)` over a global self-join references `r.k` from the broadcast side, whose required column matches the sharding key name after qualifier stripping. Verified locally on master: the self-join returned 1000 rows (500 groups duplicated, each with an empty aggregate copy) and returns the correct 500 with this fix.

signals.title: Fix optimize_skip_unused_shards on global distributed joins with shared column names
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111089 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111089 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `optimize_skip_unused_shards = 1` misbehaving on global distributed joins (`distributed_product_mode = 'global'`): a valid query such as `SELECT DISTINCT l.c, r.c + 2 ...` where both sides have a column of the same name threw `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT`, and grouping by a right-side column whose name matched the left table's sharding key could return unmerged per-shard partial results. ### Description `StorageDistributed::getOptimizedQueryProcessingStageAnalyzer` decides whether shards can process a `DISTINCT`/`GROUP BY`/`LIMIT BY` query all the way to `Complete` (the `optimize_distributed_group_by_sharding_key` optimization). It calls `isShardingKeySuitsQueryTreeNodeExpression`, which builds a type-checked `ActionsDAG` from the expression using **unqualified** column names (`use_column_identifier_as_action_node_name = false`) because the sharding key is defined without a table qualifier and is compared by plain name. Unqualified names are only meaningful when the expression reads a single source. In a global distributed join the same name can appear on more than one side, which breaks the optimization two ways: - **Crash** (the reported case): `l.c` (String) and `r.c` (Int64) collapse onto one action node, so `r.c + 2` is built against the wrong column and `plus(String, UInt8)` throws `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT` on the initiator during planning. `optimize_skip_unused_shards = 0` skips this probe, so the same query runs fine. - **Wrong results** (found while fixing the above): grouping by a right-side column whose name equals the left table's sharding key (e.g. left sharded by `k`, `GROUP BY r.k`) matched it to the sharding key by name and let shards process to `Complete`. A group keyed by that column can span shards, so the per-shard partials were returned unmerged. The fix restricts the optimization to the case where every column in the probed expression comes from this distributed table's own source (`query_info.table_expression`). Then the unqualified-name reasoning is valid: there is no cross-side name collision and the sharding-key match genuinely belongs to this table. Otherwise the analyzer falls back to merging on the initiator, exactly as with `optimize_skip_unused_shards = 0`. Single-table `DISTINCT`/`GROUP BY`/`LIMIT BY` by the sharding key, and joins that group by this table's own sharding key, keep the shard-local optimization. Verified locally on a 2-shard cluster: the reported query and its `LEFT JOIN`, `GROUP BY`, and comma-join variants threw `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT` before and now match `optimize_skip_unused_shards = 0`; a cross-shard `GROUP BY r.k` returned duplicated partials before and now returns the correct single merged group; single-table `DISTINCT`/`GROUP BY` by the sharding key still reaches the `Complete` stage.

signals.title: Fix UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER reading/merging a projection when a late-added column default references a non-stored column
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111076 --> Closes: #111076 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER` error when reading or merging a table with a projection after `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN c ... DEFAULT expr` where `expr` references a column not stored by the projection part, and the projection selects `c` (directly or via a re-pointed `ALIAS`). Such reads now fall back to the parent part and such merges rebuild the projection instead of failing. ### Description The projection column set is re-derived from the projection query on every table load, so an existing projection part can be missing a column the current metadata now requires. `projectionPartHasRequiredColumns` (read path) and `prepareProjectionsToMergeAndRebuild` (merge path) classify such a required column that is absent from BOTH the projection part and the parent part, but is a physical table column, as a legitimate column added after the part was written (case 4), and keep using the projection part on the assumption that its default fill is identical on either read path. That assumption breaks when the late-added column's `DEFAULT`/`MATERIALIZED` expression references a column the projection part does not store: the projection read cannot evaluate the default (the dependency is missing) and throws `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER`, while the parent read can. The merge path hits the same failure via `MergeTreeSequentialSource`, permanently blocking merges. Both guards now collect the default expression's column dependencies (as `MergeTreeBlockReadUtils` already does for missing-column reads) and, when a dependency is absent from the projection part, treat the column as drift: the read routes to the parent and the merge rebuilds the projection from the parent data. A late-add with a constant/no-dependency default is unchanged and still uses the projection part. Reproduces on `master`; deterministic. Regression coverage added to `04516_projection_part_column_drift` (both the `DEFAULT expr` and the `MATERIALIZED expr` variants). CI report / provenance: reported in [#111076](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111076) by ClickGap automated review of PR #110328 (which introduced the case-4 guard); this fixes the hole in that guard for the default-over-non-stored-column variant.

signals.title: Fix GROUP BY ALL with higher-order functions
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/56019 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111090 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/56019 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111090 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `GROUP BY ALL` with higher-order functions such as `arrayMap`/`arrayFilter`. Previously a query like `SELECT arrayFilter(x -> x > 0, groupArray(number)) ... GROUP BY ALL` failed with `Unknown function lambda` (old analyzer) or `ILLEGAL_AGGREGATION` (analyzer), because the lambda argument was incorrectly collected into the `GROUP BY` key set. The lambda (and its parameters) is no longer treated as a grouping key, while free columns and aggregates inside the lambda body are handled as they are with an explicit `GROUP BY`. ### Description `GROUP BY ALL` expands to the maximum non-aggregate SELECT sub-expressions. The key collector did not handle the lambda argument of higher-order functions: the old analyzer pushed the bare `lambda(...)` node (and its parameter) as a key, and the analyzer did not see aggregates inside the lambda body and pushed the whole higher-order function as a key. Both collectors (`QueryAnalyzer::recursivelyCollectMaxOrdinaryExpressions` and the old `recursivelyCollectMaxOrdinaryExpressions` in `TreeRewriter.cpp`) now skip lambda parameters, still collect free columns referenced in the lambda body, and propagate aggregates/window functions found in the body so the enclosing function is not collapsed into a single key. The result matches the corresponding explicit `GROUP BY`.

signals.title: Add `max_rows` setting for databases
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109355 Adds a `max_rows` setting for `Atomic` and `Ordinary` databases: a ceiling on active MergeTree rows counted toward the database limit. It is enforced on `INSERT`, `ATTACH`, and partition-import/move operations. A batch `INSERT` may overshoot, and the next `INSERT` throws `TOO_MANY_ROWS`. The counted total is exposed through the nullable `system.databases.rows` column. It intentionally excludes engines that do not participate in `max_rows` accounting. The setting can be changed at runtime with `ALTER DATABASE ... MODIFY SETTING max_rows = N`; its default value, `0`, is unlimited. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Add the `max_rows` setting for `Atomic` and `Ordinary` databases, limiting active MergeTree rows counted across a database. It is enforced on `INSERT`, `ATTACH`, and partition imports, is reconfigurable via `ALTER DATABASE ... MODIFY SETTING`, and is exposed through `system.databases.rows`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=111166&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/111166](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F111166+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Promote committed orphans in refreshDataPartsOnce for rolled-back parts
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/100992 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a read-only table refresh (background `refresh_parts_interval` task or `SYSTEM RESTART DISK`) that could re-activate a rolled-back part and hide the committed parts it covers, when a rolled-back part intersects committed ones. Follow-up to #100992, which fixed the same case on the startup part-loading path. ### Description Follow-up to #100992 (requested by @tuanpach). #100992 taught the startup part loader (`loadDataPartsFromDisk`) to promote committed descendants of a rolled-back top-level part, and reverted the tree-level `contains`-branch eviction because `loadDataPartsFromDisk` already handles containment through orphan promotion. The read-only refresh path (`refreshDataPartsOnce`, used by the background refresh task on all-read-only-disk tables and by `SYSTEM RESTART DISK`) had no such promotion: it traverses only the top-level loading-tree nodes and unconditionally commits each one. On the containment topology (a rolled-back ancestor covering committed children), a read-only refresh therefore: - committed the rolled-back top-level part: `loadDataPart` demotes it to `Outdated`, and `preparePartForCommit` then resets it to `PreActive`, re-activating a rolled-back part. This trips `assertHasVersionMetadata` (`LOGICAL_ERROR`, server abort in debug/sanitizer builds); in a release build it silently re-activates the rolled-back part; and - never surfaced the committed children, which are covered by the ancestor in the tree and so are never reached by the top-level traversal. Fix: in `refreshDataPartsOnce`, skip committing a part that loaded as `Outdated` (rolled back), and instead re-enqueue its children, mirroring the orphan promotion `loadDataPartsFromDisk` performs. The loading tree is left untouched, so this does not re-open `test_transactions::test_rollback_unfinished_on_restart{1,2}` (that regression came from tree-level eviction removing rolled-back parts from `system.parts`; here the rolled-back part is still loaded, just left `Outdated`). Regression test `04612_part_loading_tree_rollback_refresh_disk` reproduces the #100992 (04241) containment topology but makes the parts appear after the read-only reader is loaded, so they go through `refreshDataPartsOnce` via `SYSTEM RESTART DISK`. It fails on `master` (server abort) and passes with this change.
signals.author: groeneai

signals.title: Fix double free when finalizing -State aggregates under looping combinators
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110975 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a server crash (double free) that could happen when finalizing an aggregate function with the `-State` combinator nested under a looping combinator (`-Resample`, `-ForEach`, `-Map`), for example `groupArrayStateResample`, if a memory limit was reached during finalization. ### Description Reported on https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110975 (unrelated to that PR). Found by the Stress test (amd_debug): a segfault in `Aggregator::prepareChunkAndFillWithoutKey`, reached from `ConvertingAggregatedToChunksTransform::initialize`. CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110975&sha=838d0b61235b06939c8acd923ebd396f51cf5b10&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_debug%29 Root cause: the `-State` combinator transfers its result by aliasing the raw aggregate state pointer into a `ColumnAggregateFunction` (`AggregateFunctionState::insertResultInto` -> `getData().push_back(place)`); ownership passes to the column. `Aggregator::insertAggregatesIntoColumns` relies on this transfer being atomic per place: on an exception it destroys the whole place exactly once. A looping combinator nested over `-State` aliases many sub-states one at a time; the `push_back` into the column's pointer array can reallocate and, being memory-tracked, throw `MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` mid-loop. The already-transferred sub-states are then freed once by the aggregator's full `destroy()` and again by `~ColumnAggregateFunction`, i.e. a double free. Reproducer (crashes without the fix, returns a memory-limit error with it): ```sql SELECT arrayMap(x -> finalizeAggregation(x), state) FROM (SELECT groupArrayStateResample(0, 1048576, 1)(number, number % 20) AS state FROM numbers(100000)) SETTINGS max_memory_usage = 150000000, max_rows_to_read = 0; ``` Fix: reserve the destination columns before the transfer loop so the aliasing `push_back`s cannot reallocate (and therefore cannot throw) once a transfer has started. `ColumnAggregateFunction` used the no-op `IColumn::reserve`, so a real `reserve()`/`capacity()` over its state-pointer array is added. For `-Map`, the (possibly variable-width) key inserts are moved into their own loop before the value transfer, keeping the throwing work out of the aliasing loop. Reserving happens before any aliasing, so a throw there is harmless. The transfer loop is now non-throwing at the point of aliasing, restoring the atomic-per-place contract; results are unchanged. The fix covers all three looping transfer combinators (`-Resample`, `-ForEach`, `-Map`), which share the aliasing path; non-looping combinators delegate a single call and are already atomic. The added stateless test reproduces the crash deterministically via `-Resample` (empty buckets keep memory low until the finalization transfer, so a memory limit reliably lands the throw mid-transfer). `-ForEach` and `-Map` build their sub-states eagerly during aggregation, so they are not deterministically reproducible under a memory limit, but are fixed as the same class via the shared transfer path.
signals.author: groeneai

signals.title: Fix logical error joining a Merge over Distributed table with USING
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111253 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `LOGICAL_ERROR` ("query tree node does not have valid source node") when a `Merge` table wrapping a `Distributed` table is joined and a bare column of the joined-away side is used as a predicate. ### Description `ReadFromMerge` builds a separate query for each underlying table. It removes the JOIN and then strips the `WHERE`/`PREWHERE` sub-expressions that reference the joined-away table, via `removeExpressionsThatDoNotDependOnTableIdentifiers`. That helper only inspected `FunctionNode` top-level expressions; a bare-column predicate such as `WHERE r.k` (a `ColumnNode`) hit an early `return` and was left in the child query. When the `Distributed` child was re-planned to be sent to the shards, that column had a dangling source and the analyzer threw `Code: 49 ... Column k UInt32 query tree node does not have valid source node`. The fix treats any non-`and` top-level expression (bare column, constant, or single non-`and` function) uniformly: it is dropped if it references only removed tables. This is the same rule the helper already applied to single-function predicates and to each conjunct of an `and`. The single-line change covers more shapes than the reported one, so the test pins each entry path (all verified to raise the logical error without the fix and to pass with it): - `USING` and `ON`, and a self-join of the `Merge` table, which needs one table and no second fixture. Reported by zlareb1 on the issue after this PR was opened. - `QUALIFY` and `HAVING`, not only a hand-written `WHERE`. The planner folds `QUALIFY` into `HAVING` when there are no window functions and `HAVING` into `WHERE` when there is no aggregation, so such a predicate reaches the same helper. This is also the shape the AST fuzzer hit on #112931. - Left-side counterparts (`qualify_l`, `self_join_on_l`, `bare_where_l_k`), so no case can pass by dropping the predicate outright. The same helper is used to decide push-down for query-backed `MySQL`/`PostgreSQL`/`SQLite` sources, so `04341_sqlite_query_passing` pins that partition too. Measured on both arms, the only verdict this patch changes there is a bare predicate on the joined local side, which master rejected while accepting every other spelling of it. A disjunction mixing the two sides is still not rejected; that verdict is identical on both arms, so it is a pre-existing gap of testing a reconstructed AST for a surviving `WHERE`, pinned here rather than fixed.
signals.author: groeneai

signals.title: Use bloom_filter skip index for IN with transform_null_in=1 and NULL-free set
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111311 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Use the `bloom_filter` skip index for `IN` predicates on a directly indexed column when `transform_null_in = 1` and the `IN`-set contains no `NULL` value. Previously the index was skipped for such queries, forcing a full scan. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111311 With `transform_null_in = 1` the analyzer rewrites `x IN (...)` to `nullIn(x, ...)` (and `globalIn` to `globalNullIn`). The `bloom_filter` skip index condition built the predicate hashes for these but never assigned an RPN function, so the atom stayed `FUNCTION_UNKNOWN` and the index was unused, forcing a full scan. When the `IN`-set has no `NULL`, `nullIn` selects exactly the same rows as `in`, so the index can prune. The fix maps `nullIn`/`globalNullIn` to `FUNCTION_IN` when the set is single-column, `NULL`-free and type-compatible with the index, and the column is not an `Array`. With a `NULL` in the set, `nullIn` also matches `NULL` rows, so the atom is left `FUNCTION_UNKNOWN` (unchanged behavior). `x = 'abc'` already worked: `transform_null_in` does not rewrite `equals`. Scope: scalar left-hand side on a directly indexed column, which is the scope of the issue. Tuple lhs, `JSONAllPaths` and map subcolumns still recognize only `in`/`globalIn` and continue to full-scan. Those are deliberately not extended, because the checks this fix relies on cannot be evaluated there: the recursive `tuple(...)` branch matches each element against its own index and is called with `prepared_set = nullptr`, and `Set::hasNull()` returns `false` whenever `data_types.size() != 1`, so reusing the single-column guard on a tuple set is vacuous rather than merely wider. Measured with that extension applied, a 180-query parity sweep against `use_skip_indexes = 0` returned fewer rows than the truth arm for 17 queries; the sweep is clean on this PR. A test arm pins the contract, so extending the tuple branch on the single-column guard fails the test. Verified with `EXPLAIN indexes = 1` that the index prunes for `String`, `Nullable`, `LowCardinality` and `LowCardinality(Nullable)` with a `NULL`-free set, and does not prune for a set containing `NULL`, an `Array` column, a type-incompatible set or a tuple lhs. Results match `use_skip_indexes = 0` in each case.

signals.title: Fsync access entities in DiskAccessStorage to survive power loss
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/68958 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Access entities stored on local disk (users, roles, grants, quotas, row policies, settings profiles created via SQL) are now fsync'd when `fsync_metadata` is enabled, so an acknowledged `CREATE`/`ALTER`/`DROP USER` (and `GRANT`/`REVOKE`) is no longer silently lost on power loss. Previously `DiskAccessStorage` wrote and removed the `.sql` entity files without any fsync. ### Description `DiskAccessStorage` wrote access-entity `.sql` files (and the `*.list` index files), and removed them, without any fsync, so an acknowledged access change could be lost on power loss. It was the only on-disk DDL-entity store not honoring `fsync_metadata` (UDFs, named collections, workload entities and table metadata all do). Reported and reproduced 3/3 on master with a `dm-flakey` power-loss simulation in #68958: after `CREATE USER` + `GRANT` and a power cut, the `<uuid>.sql` file is gone and the user cannot authenticate (`AUTHENTICATION_FAILED`). The tmp->final rename was never forced to disk. Fix, gated on `fsync_metadata` (default `true`), matching the sibling stores: - `writeEntityFile` (create/insert and update): fsync the file content, then fsync the parent directory around the rename (a rename is durable only once the directory entry is persisted). - `deleteAccessEntityOnDisk` (`DROP USER`/`REVOKE`, and the old-file removal on rename-replace): fsync the parent directory around the unlink. - `writeListFile`: fsync the file content (the `.list` files are rebuilt from the `.sql` files, so no directory fsync). The parent-directory fsync reuses `LocalDirectorySyncGuard`. The setting is resolved from the query context (session value) and falls back to the global context for the background `.list` writer, mirroring `getWriteSettings()`. Regression test `tests/integration/test_access_storage_fsync` asserts, via `system.query_log` ProfileEvents, that `CREATE`/`GRANT`/`ALTER`/`DROP USER` take the `FileSync`/`DirectorySync` path when `fsync_metadata=1` and take neither when `fsync_metadata=0`. It is an integration test because stateless tests override the access storage to `<memory/>`.

signals.title: Fsync DETACH TABLE ... PERMANENTLY flag to survive power loss
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111322 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Make `DETACH TABLE ... PERMANENTLY` durable: the `.sql.detached` marker file (and its removal on `ATTACH`) is now persisted by fsync'ing the metadata directory, gated on `fsync_metadata`. Previously the marker's creation/removal was not synced, so a power loss right after an acknowledged `DETACH ... PERMANENTLY` could silently re-attach the table on restart (or, symmetrically, undo an acknowledged `ATTACH`). ### Description Closes #111322. `DatabaseOnDisk::detachTablePermanently` creates the empty `<table>.sql.detached` marker via `db_disk->createFile`, and `removeDetachedPermanentlyFlag` removes it via `removeFileIfExists`. Neither fsync'd the parent metadata directory. A file's existence is a directory-entry change that is not durable until the directory is fsync'd, so an acknowledged `DETACH ... PERMANENTLY` (or `ATTACH`) could be lost on power loss, silently violating the acknowledged contract. This is the same `fsync_metadata` gap as #68958, applied to a marker file. Fix: fsync the metadata directory around both the marker creation and its removal, via `IDisk::getDirectorySyncGuard` (fsyncs on local disks, no-op on object storage), gated on `fsync_metadata` (default true). On the removal path the sync is taken only when the marker actually exists, so plain `CREATE TABLE` (which always calls `removeDetachedPermanentlyFlag`) is unaffected. Covers Ordinary, Atomic, and Replicated databases. Verified with the `DirectorySync` profile event (as in `02361_fsync_profile_events.sh`): `DirectorySync` is 1 for `DETACH ... PERMANENTLY` / `ATTACH` under `fsync_metadata=1` and 0 under `fsync_metadata=0`; 0 on both before the fix. Test: `03471_detach_permanently_fsync`.

signals.title: Fsync detached directory on DROP DETACHED PART/PARTITION
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111349 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `ALTER TABLE ... DROP DETACHED PART/PARTITION` now fsyncs the `detached` directory when the `fsync_part_directory` MergeTree setting is enabled, so an acknowledged drop of a detached part is no longer rolled back by a power loss (the removed part could previously reappear). ### Description `MergeTreeData::dropDetached` renames `detached/<part>` to `detached/deleting_<part>` and then unlinks it, but never fsync'd the `detached` directory and consulted no durability setting. A rename or unlink is durable only once the parent directory is fsync'd, so after a power loss in the filesystem journal window the directory-entry changes could roll back and the acknowledged-dropped detached part reappeared intact. Reported and reproduced 3/3 with a `dm-flakey` power-loss simulation in #111349. Fix, gated on the existing `fsync_part_directory` setting (default `false`, so no behavior change by default): before the rename, acquire one directory sync guard per involved disk on the `detached` directory and hold it across the rename and the removal; the guard fsyncs the directory on destruction. The guards are declared before `PartsTemporaryRename` so they outlive it and also cover the rollback rename on the error path. This uses the disk-agnostic `IDisk::getDirectorySyncGuard` (local disks fsync; object storage is a no-op), matching the existing `fsync_part_directory` handling for part directories in `IMergeTreeDataPart::renameTo`. Test: `04620_drop_detached_part_fsync` asserts the `DirectorySync` ProfileEvent is emitted for `DROP DETACHED PART` when `fsync_part_directory = 1` and not when `0`, and that the part is removed in both cases.

signals.title: Fsync object-storage disk metadata and blobs to honor fsync settings
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111330 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Object-storage disks (`s3`, `azure_blob_storage`, `local_blob_storage`, ...) now honor the `MergeTree` fsync settings (`fsync_after_insert`, `fsync_part_directory`, `min_rows_to_fsync_after_merge`, `min_compressed_bytes_to_fsync_after_merge`). Previously these settings were silently ignored on such disks: an acknowledged `INSERT` issued zero `fsync`, so the local metadata files that commit a part could be lost on power loss even when the blobs were durable. ### Description Closes #111330. Found by the same fsync-coverage audit as #111269 / #111318 / #111320 / #111321 / #111322. On an object-storage disk the MergeTree fsync setting family was a no-op through three independent paths, each fixed at its own layer: 1. `ForkWriteBuffer` (the part's blob write buffer) did not override `sync()`, so the part's `file->sync()` landed in the base `WriteBuffer::sync()` (a plain `next()`) and never reached the underlying writers. It now forwards `sync()` to its children. For `s3`/`azure` the writer's `sync()` is a no-op (durability is on finalize); for local-file-backed object storage it performs the missing `fdatasync`. 2. The local metadata files that commit a part (the map file->blob, written on a local disk) were only `finalize()`d, never `fsync`ed. This is the fatal case for real `s3`: the blob is durable but the local metadata is lost on power loss, so the acknowledged part is gone and the blobs are leaked. `WriteBufferWithFinalizeCallback` now latches the caller's `sync()` request and `fsync`s the local metadata file once it has been written (handling both wide parts, which sync after finalize, and compact parts, which sync before finalize) via a new `IMetadataStorage::syncMetadataFile`. 3. `DiskObjectStorage` did not override `getDirectorySyncGuard`, so `fsync_part_directory` was ignored. It now delegates to the metadata storage's local disk. The metadata capabilities are forwarded through `MetadataStorageFromCacheObjectStorage`, so cache-wrapped object-storage disks are covered too. Gating is the existing `sync()` call (driven by `fsync_after_insert` / `needSyncPart` / `fsync_part_directory`), so there is no new setting and no change to default behavior: the fsync settings default off, and an object-storage insert without them still issues zero `fsync`. Verified with `strace -f -e trace=fsync,fdatasync` and the `FileSync`/`DirectorySync` ProfileEvents: on master an object-storage insert with the fsync settings issues 0 fsync; with the fix it issues the expected fsyncs, and 0 without the settings. Regression test: `tests/queries/0_stateless/04541_object_storage_disk_fsync.sh`.

signals.title: Fsync projection parts to survive power loss
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111318 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111318 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Projection parts are now fsynced together with the rest of a data part. Previously projection files (under `<part>/<projection>.proj/`) were never fsynced on `INSERT` (with `fsync_after_insert`), `ALTER TABLE ... MATERIALIZE PROJECTION`, or a row-rewriting mutation (with the `*_to_fsync_after_merge` thresholds), so a power loss right after an acknowledged operation could leave the projection as all-zero-byte files, marked broken on load and reported by `CHECK TABLE` as `BROKEN_PROJECTION`. ### Description `MergeTreeDataWriter::writeProjectionPartImpl` finalized every projection part with a hardcoded no-sync flag (`finalizePartAsync(..., false)`), while the parent part's own files received the correct sync flag. That function serves the `INSERT` path (`writeProjectionPart`) and the mutation / merge path (`writeTempProjectionPart`), so under `fsync_after_insert = 1` (INSERT) or the merge/mutation fsync thresholds (`MATERIALIZE PROJECTION`, `ALTER ... DELETE`/`UPDATE`), the projection files were written but never fsynced. After a power loss the parent rows survived but the projection directory could end up all-zero-byte, broken on load and never self-healed. Fix: propagate the caller's sync decision into `writeProjectionPartImpl` and its two wrappers. INSERT passes `fsync_after_insert`; mutation and merge pass their `need_sync` decision. When a projection sub-merge re-merges several temporary parts, the final part is produced by a nested `MergeTask`, so the parent's decision is carried through `MergeProjectionPartsTask` to that task via a `force_sync` flag; the single-temp-part case is covered by the temp write itself, since it is only renamed into place (rename preserves the fsynced content). The merge-path `need_sync` is now computed before the projection temp parts are written. Behavior only changes when a durability setting is enabled; with the settings off the behavior is unchanged, and there are no on-disk, wire, or setting format changes. Report URL for the fsync-coverage finding: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111318 Verified two ways (details in the pre-PR validation gate comment): `strace -e fsync,fdatasync` on the INSERT path shows 0 projection-file fsyncs on `master` HEAD and 10 with this fix; the new stateless test `04548_projection_fsync` reads `ProfileEvents['FileSync']` from `system.query_log` and fails on `master` HEAD (`insert projection adds file syncs 0`) and passes with the fix (`1`). Mutation and merge paths verified via `strace` (all `pr.proj` files fsynced) plus `CHECK TABLE` and `force_optimize_projection`.
signals.author: groeneai

signals.title: Fsync ALTER TABLE FREEZE snapshot to survive power loss
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111331 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `ALTER TABLE ... FREEZE` now fsyncs the snapshot it creates when the table's `fsync_part_directory` setting is enabled: the snapshot directories and the chain up to the disk root, plus the rewritten `data.packed` archive for packed part storage. Previously the freeze path fsynced nothing but `shadow/increment.txt`, so a power loss right after `FREEZE` was acknowledged could erase the whole snapshot. Default behaviour is unchanged. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111331 `ALTER TABLE ... FREEZE` builds its snapshot with `createDirectories` plus `createHardLink` (Full storage), or by rewriting `data.packed` (Packed storage), and fsyncs none of it. For a hardlink snapshot the file data is already durable but the new directory entries are not, so a power loss between the acknowledgement and the operator's archive step drops every new directory entry, i.e. the whole snapshot. The directory-fsync machinery this needs is already in master: the sibling `DETACH PARTITION` durability fix (#111426) merged the `fsync_part_directory` clone parameter, `fsyncFrozenCloneTree`, and the calls from both freeze overrides. It only wires up the `DETACH` call site, so `FREEZE` still acknowledged a non-durable snapshot. This PR is what remains: 1. `freezePartitionsByMatcher` populates `fsync_part_directory` from the table setting, resolved once from the entry snapshot so a concurrent `MODIFY SETTING` cannot split one `FREEZE` across parts. 2. For packed storage, `FREEZE` rewrites the `data.packed` archive instead of hardlinking it, so the archive contents are fsynced too, for the part and for each projection. Gated on the existing `fsync_part_directory` setting (default `false`), so no `SettingsChangesHistory` entry is needed. A no-op on remote/object disks, where `getDirectorySyncGuard` returns nullptr. Verified via `ProfileEvents` `DirectorySync` and `FileSync` on the `FREEZE` query for both layouts, including the setting-off baselines. Regression test `04621_freeze_fsync_part_directory.sh`.
signals.author: groeneai

signals.title: Fsync backup files and directories when writing a backup to local disk
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111320 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `BACKUP ... TO File(...)` / `Disk(...)` now fsyncs the backup data files, the `.backup` manifest and the containing directories before reporting `BACKUP_CREATED`, so an acknowledged backup to local storage survives power loss. The guarantee covers `backups.allowed_path` and everything the backup writes below it. Controlled by the new backup setting `fsync_backup_files` (default `true`). Object-storage destinations (`S3`/`Azure`) are unaffected. ### Description Fixes #111320. `BACKUP ... TO File()/Disk()` returned `BACKUP_CREATED` without issuing any `fsync`/`fdatasync` at the destination: not the data files, not the `.backup` manifest, not the directories (there was no `fsync` anywhere in `src/Backups/`). On power loss after the acknowledgement the backup could be lost entirely or left torn, even though `BACKUP_CREATED` is what an operator relies on before dropping the source data. Only local `File()`/`Disk()` were affected; object-storage destinations were already durable. Report URL: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111320 (reproduced 3/3 with a `dm-flakey` power-loss simulation). Fix, gated on the new backup setting `fsync_backup_files` (default `true`), following the durability audit family (#68958 -> #111346, #111269 -> #111335): - Two writer hooks with a no-op default on `IBackupWriter`, overridden only by the local `File`/`Disk` writers (`S3`/`Azure`/`Memory`/`Null` inherit the no-op): `syncFileToDisk(file_name)`, called right after each data file is written in `BackupImpl::writeFile` (each call fsyncs its own file, so the concurrent write path is safe), and `syncDirectoriesToDisk()`, which fdatasyncs every directory the backup created, deepest-first. - In `BackupImpl::finalizeWriting` the `.backup` manifest (or, for archives, the archive file) is synced last, after all data files, so a persisted manifest never precedes its payload. Directory syncing runs for every writer, including the internal writers of `BACKUP ON CLUSTER` which write their own data files. Regression test `tests/queries/0_stateless/04412_backup_to_file_fsync.sh` asserts the `FileSync`/`DirectorySync` ProfileEvents of the `BACKUP` query, present with `fsync_backup_files=1` and absent with `0`; integration coverage adds the `Disk`, archive and `ON CLUSTER` internal-writer cases. Guarantee boundary, stated rather than left implicit: `backups.allowed_path` and everything written below it are synced in a loop that propagates failures. Ancestors above it are best-effort, because `fsyncBackupDirectory` needs `O_DIRECTORY` (read permission) while writing a backup only needs them searchable: measured with the area inside a `0311` directory, writing succeeds and `open(O_DIRECTORY)` on the ancestor fails `EACCES`, so throwing there would newly fail backups that work today. So if a directory above `backups.allowed_path` was itself created without being made durable, a power loss can still take the whole tree. The setting's docs row now says this. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=111394&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/111394](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F111394+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->
