signals.title: Add the `Cluster` database engine
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114411 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/59304 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110975 Implement the `Cluster` database engine, a follow-up to the `Remote` database engine (#110975). It provides real-time access to tables in a configured cluster database. Each table is exposed as a `Distributed` proxy that forwards `SELECT` and `INSERT`, with the same local-shard visibility rules and remote-replica fallback as `Remote`. The cluster is resolved from server configuration by name on every access, supports macros, and follows configuration reloads. Connections use each replica's configured credentials, secure connections, compression, and inter-server secret; the engine stores no credentials. `SHOW CREATE TABLE` returns a re-executable `Distributed` definition where possible. `Cluster` is experimental and is enabled through `allow_experimental_database_cluster`. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added the experimental `Cluster` database engine, enabled via `allow_experimental_database_cluster`, which provides real-time access to the tables of a configured cluster database and forwards `SELECT` and `INSERT` queries to it. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114417&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114417](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114417+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix header column order after the no-rescoring vector search rewrite
signals.text: <!--- A technical description of your changes with a motivation --> The second-pass vector search optimization (`vector_search_with_rescoring = 0`) removed the distance function from the `ExpressionStep` outputs and re-appended the rewritten `_distance` alias at the end, changing the header column order. Steps created above the `Sorting` before that rewrite runs — the local top-N `Limit` and the exchange steps of a distributed plan — kept the original column order, and `makeDistributedPlan` failed to rebuild the plan fragments with a logical error: `Cannot add step Limit to QueryPlan because it has incompatible header with root step Sorting`. Non-distributed plans never re-validate step headers after optimization, which is why this only surfaced with `make_distributed_plan = 1`. The fix reinserts the rewritten output node at the original position of the distance column, so the header column order is preserved and all previously created parent steps stay consistent. Found by AST fuzzer on [#42701](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/42701) ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=42701&sha=019244e0d46b4d9029fc261a549e1c5cd79b1bbb&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%29)); the same signature also hit the unrelated #98789 on 2026-08-08. The regression test asserts only the row count: the distributed plan currently returns an incorrect top-N for vector search queries regardless of the rescoring mode — a separate, pre-existing bug. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114456 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/42701 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a logical error `Cannot add step Limit to QueryPlan because it has incompatible header with root step Sorting` when a vector search query with `vector_search_with_rescoring = 0` was executed with the experimental `make_distributed_plan` setting. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114457&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114457](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114457+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Reject a lossy codec on columns backing keys and indexes
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114406 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `CREATE TABLE` and `ALTER TABLE` now reject a lossy codec such as `SZ3` on a column used in the sorting key. Such a codec does not return the value that was written, so rows stored in sorting key order came back out of order and index analysis skipped matching rows. ### Description Closes #114406. A lossy codec does not return the value that was written. Rows are stored inside a part in sorting key order, so the stored order does not match the values a reader sees, and index analysis skips matching rows. The check is in `MergeTreeData::checkProperties`, which both `CREATE TABLE` and `ALTER TABLE` already go through, and it reuses that function's existing `attach` flag so a table stored by an earlier version stays loadable. The primary key needs no separate case: it must be a prefix of the sorting key, which is enforced a few lines above in the same function. Validation is unconditional. A table whose lossy sorting key predates the check still loads and reads normally, non-replicated and replicated alike, because the load path goes through `attach`; other `ALTER`s on such a table are refused until its codec or its key is changed. Reproducer from the issue, now rejected: ```sql CREATE TABLE t (i Float64 CODEC(SZ3('ALGO_INTERP_LORENZO', 'REL', 0.01)), f Int64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY i; ``` Validated against a control binary with the check deleted: all 7 rejection cases in `04791_lossy_codec_key_column` are accepted by the control and rejected here, and 5 lossless or non-key cases behave identically on both. Loading a table with a lossy sorting key created by the control was checked for `MergeTree` and for `ReplicatedMergeTree` whose ZooKeeper metadata records the codec: both load with no rejection. A sweep of the 103 `codec` tests fails the same set on both binaries apart from this test. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114531&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114531](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114531+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Deduplicate the final DISTINCT in parallel
signals.text: The final `DISTINCT` merged all of its input streams into one and deduplicated them on a single thread, so `SELECT DISTINCT` did not scale with `max_threads` while the equivalent `GROUP BY` did - aggregation parallelizes its merge over two-level hash tables, `DISTINCT` had nothing of the sort. This repartitions the input streams by the hash of the `DISTINCT` columns instead of merging them: equal values then land in the same stream, so every stream can be deduplicated on its own, and what is left to merge is already deduplicated. The repartitioning uses `scatterByPartition`, which `SortingStep` and `ShuffleSendStep` already use. Whether the order of the step's output is free to change is only known where the sorting properties are, so the decision is taken in `applyOrder`. The new setting `allow_parallel_distinct`, enabled by default, controls it. It is not applied when: - the input is already globally sorted, because then `DISTINCT` keeps the order of its input and the repartitioning would break it; - there is a `LIMIT`, because the transform stops early anyway and the single stream keeps `LIMIT` returning the first values of the input rather than an arbitrary subset; - the streams are already disjoint - `allow_distinct_partitions_independently` covers that case and skips the merge entirely. `max_rows_in_distinct` and `max_bytes_in_distinct` keep their global meaning: the streams hold disjoint parts of one `DISTINCT` set, so the transforms add up the sizes of their sets in a shared counter and check the limits against the total. Enforcing them in the single final transform instead would have disabled the optimization for everyone who sets them - including all of CI, where the test profile sets both to `10G`. Every input chunk is split across all partitions, so the number of partitions is capped rather than following `max_threads`. On `SELECT DISTINCT number FROM numbers_mt(4e7)` the total CPU time the scatter adds grows by 8% at 4 partitions, 20% at 16 and 96% at 96; without the cap that turned into a wall-clock regression at high `max_threads`. Wall clock, minimum of 3 runs, aarch64: | workload | `max_threads` | before | after | speedup | |---|---|---|---|---| | 20M distinct `UInt64`, `MergeTree` | 4 | 0.442 s | 0.205 s | 2.16x | | | 16 | 0.458 s | 0.148 s | 3.09x | | | 96 | 0.502 s | 0.165 s | 3.04x | | 40M distinct `UInt64`, `numbers_mt` | 4 | 0.965 s | 0.545 s | 1.77x | | | 16 | 0.929 s | 0.360 s | 2.58x | | | 96 | 0.886 s | 0.299 s | 2.96x | | 8M distinct `String`, `numbers_mt` | 4 | 0.515 s | 0.288 s | 1.79x | | | 16 | 0.517 s | 0.093 s | 5.56x | | | 96 | 0.518 s | 0.083 s | 6.24x | The measurements were taken on a busy machine, hence the minimum of several runs; the existing `distinct_in_order`, `distinct_high_cardinality` and `sorted_distinct` performance tests cover these shapes, so the performance comparison job is the authoritative check. `DISTINCT` without `ORDER BY` has no defined row order, and the repartitioning changes the order it happens to produce. Two existing tests relied on it: `04109_sort_propagation_apply_order` asserts that per-stream sortedness reaches `DISTINCT`, so it pins the setting off, and `00585_union_all_subquery_aggregation_column_removal` gets the explicit `ORDER BY` it was missing. Other tests that depend on the incidental order of a `DISTINCT` may surface in CI and should be fixed the same way. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114532 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/48988 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md): Evaluate the final `DISTINCT` on several threads by repartitioning its input by the hash of the `DISTINCT` columns, instead of merging everything into a single stream and deduplicating it on one thread. Up to 6x faster on high-cardinality `DISTINCT`. Controlled by the new setting `allow_parallel_distinct`, enabled by default. Note that this changes the order in which a `DISTINCT` without `ORDER BY` returns rows, which was never defined. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114550&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114550](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114550+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Never cancel a query before its `max_execution_time` has elapsed
signals.text: `CancellationChecker::appendTask` derived a query's cancellation deadline from the current time truncated to whole milliseconds, and then aligned it up to the 100 ms grid the worker batches deadlines on. The alignment normally hides the truncation, but when the deadline already sits on the grid - one query in a hundred - it adds no padding, and the deadline lands up to 1 ms before `now + max_execution_time`. The query is then cancelled ahead of its own timeout and fails with a self-contradictory message: ``` Code: 159. DB::Exception: Timeout exceeded: elapsed 999.672 ms, maximum: 1000 ms. (TIMEOUT_EXCEEDED) ``` The current time is now rounded up to a whole millisecond instead, which is the direction the code around it already promises: *"Tasks may be cancelled slightly later than their exact timeout, but never before"*. Only the `throw` overflow mode was affected: in `break` mode the checker re-reads the elapsed time before acting on the deadline, so an early wake-up does nothing. This is what makes `02122_join_group_by_timeout` flaky - it asserts that a `max_execution_time = 1` cancellation takes at least 1000 ms, and `query_duration_ms` is measured from a stopwatch that starts before the deadline is computed. The failure shows up as `query_duration 1` becoming `query_duration 0`, always on one of the two `throw`-mode queries and never on the `break`-mode ones. In the server logs of both `Fast test` runs below, the query was cancelled early - at 999.672 ms and at 999.630 ms of its 1000 ms timeout. The deadline computation moved into `CancellationChecker::taskDeadlineMs` so that the invariant can be tested directly: the new unit test checks every sub-millisecond phase of `now` against every phase of the grid, for a range of timeouts, and fails with the old truncation. CI reports of the flaky test: - https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=gh-readonly-queue/master/pr-113021-93e2851fddb5add7bad5b28bcef780be2f6ff7bb&sha=bef88e3d96ecb0f57a0f8d81f6b7ee2117db19fd&name_0=MergeQueueCI&name_1=Fast%20test - https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=gh-readonly-queue/master/pr-110451-2f02abe52a79c02fb554728f14d8fa847dcbc1e6&sha=2eba84a8a12a21c36516158d4fbe9530d3f0af8c&name_0=MergeQueueCI&name_1=Fast%20test The truncation is as old as the checker itself. Before deadlines were aligned to a grid in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/95563 the deadline was plainly `floor(now) + timeout`, i.e. early for every query rather than for one in a hundred; and the assertion that catches it was only sharpened from `round(query_duration_ms / 1000) BETWEEN 1 AND 60` to `query_duration_ms BETWEEN 1000 AND 60000` in daf1b4980b1, which is why the flake is recent. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): A query could be cancelled up to 1 ms before its `max_execution_time` had passed, failing with a self-contradictory `Timeout exceeded: elapsed 999.672 ms, maximum: 1000 ms`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114559&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114559](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114559+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix stale MATERIALIZED column values read through a chain while a mutation is pending
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/100613 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/50237 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/99281 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/103182 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115371 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115372 **Scope changed.** The staging half of this pull request — recomputing a chain of `MATERIALIZED` columns one dependency level at a time during a mutation — landed on master in the meantime via #103182, which also generalizes it to `APPLY PATCHES`. Everything this pull request used to change in `MutationsInterpreter.cpp` has been dropped; what remains is the read path, which master still gets wrong. The two other defects found while re-testing against master are split out into #115371 and #115372. ## Problem With a mutation still pending, reading a `MATERIALIZED` column that reaches the updated column only through another `MATERIALIZED` column returns the stale on-disk value, while reading the whole chain returns the recomputed one: ```sql CREATE TABLE t (x Int32, y Int32, m1 Int32 MATERIALIZED x + 1, m2 Int32 MATERIALIZED m1 + 1, m3 Int32 MATERIALIZED m2 + 1) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); INSERT INTO t (x, y) VALUES (10, 0); SYSTEM STOP MERGES t; SET alter_sync = 0, mutations_sync = 0, apply_mutations_on_fly = 1; ALTER TABLE t UPDATE x = 20 WHERE 1; -- stays pending ``` ``` SELECT m2 FROM t; -- 12 (stale; must be 22) SELECT m3 FROM t; -- 13 (stale; must be 23) SELECT x, m1, m2, m3 FROM t; -- 20 21 22 23 (correct) ``` - The result of a query depends on which columns it selects, so the same value read two ways disagrees. - The same happens for a `MATERIALIZED` column defined over a subcolumn (`m1 MATERIALIZED t.a + 1` with a pending `UPDATE t = ...`): `SELECT m1` returns the stale value unless the query happens to select `t` as well. - Once the mutation finishes, the values are correct — only the pending window is affected. ## Root cause Reading with `apply_mutations_on_fly` builds the pending commands into the read pipeline. `AlterConversions::addColumnsRequiredForMaterialized` decides which extra columns must be read so that the `MATERIALIZED` columns being selected can be recomputed, and it only looked one hop deep: ```cpp for (const auto & column_name : read_columns_set) if (default is MATERIALIZED) for (const auto & dependency : TreeRewriter(context).analyze(expression, source_columns)->requiredSourceColumns()) if (all_updated_columns.contains(dependency)) required_source_columns.insert(dependency); ``` For `m2 MATERIALIZED m1 + 1` the only dependency is `m1`, which is not in `all_updated_columns`, so nothing is added, `filterMutationCommands` drops the `UPDATE x` command as irrelevant to the read set, and `m2` is returned from disk. Two further details of the same analysis: - the default expression is not normalized with `replaceSubcolumnsToGetSubcolumnFunctionInQuery`, so `m MATERIALIZED t.a` is seen to depend on `t.a` rather than on `t`, and a pending `UPDATE t` is filtered out (or the analysis fails with `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER` when the subcolumn does not resolve against `source_columns`); - a `MATERIALIZED` column whose expression reads an `EPHEMERAL` column can never be recomputed outside `INSERT`, so analysing it against physical columns must be avoided rather than attempted. ## Solution Walk the dependency graph transitively: a `MATERIALIZED` column is pulled into the read set when an updated column is reachable from it through other `MATERIALIZED` columns (`reachesUpdatedColumn`), so the intermediate hops are read and the interpreter recomputes the whole chain. Dependencies are analysed after the subcolumn rewrite, matching what `MutationsInterpreter::prepare` does, and `EPHEMERAL`-derived columns are excluded instead of analysed. Regression test `04869_materialized_chain_on_fly_read` covers the three cases: the plain chain, the subcolumn default, and the `EPHEMERAL`-derived column as the must-not-act case. Verified against the master binary `26.8.1.1599`: the first two return the stale values quoted above, the third is unaffected. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed stale values of a `MATERIALIZED` column that is computed from another `MATERIALIZED` column when reading a table with a mutation still in progress. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114561&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114561](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114561+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Revert "Revert "NATS: add inline credentials setting""
signals.text: Reverts https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114178, restoring the `nats_credentials` setting of the `NATS` table engine (originally added in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110733), and fixes the reason of the original revert: the possibility of referencing arbitrary server paths through `nats_credential_file`. `nats_credential_file` is a path on the server filesystem: the server opens it with its own privileges, and during authentication the credentials are sent to `nats_url`, which comes from the same query. So a path taken from SQL lets anyone who can define a `NATS` source probe the local filesystem (the error text distinguishes a missing file, a permission error, and a file without a seed), and exfiltrate files the server can read to a NATS server they control (the part of the file before the seed line is sent verbatim in the `CONNECT` frame's `jwt` field). See the analysis in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110733#discussion_r3750203599. This hole predates #110733 (`nats_credential_file` exists since 24.2), but with the inline `nats_credentials` setting restored, the path form is no longer needed in SQL at all. The restriction, modelled on `StorageMySQL::getSSLParams` (`e700bbec4c84c585`): `nats_credential_file` is accepted only from a named collection defined in the server configuration file, or as `nats.credential_file` in the server configuration itself. Every SQL spelling — the `SETTINGS` clause, an engine-argument override `NATS(collection, nats_credential_file = ...)`, or a named collection created by `CREATE NAMED COLLECTION` — throws `BAD_ARGUMENTS` with a message directing to `nats_credentials`. It is rejected on provenance, whether the query assigned the key at all, rather than on the resulting value, so an override with the empty string cannot silently drop the credentials the operator configured. Loading from previously-validated metadata (server startup, force-restore, and short-syntax `ATTACH`) is exempt via `isLoadingFromExistingMetadata`, so existing tables keep working after an upgrade; a user-issued full `ATTACH TABLE` query is still checked. `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY SETTING` is not a bypass: the `NATS` engine does not support settings alter. Replacing a configured path with inline `nats_credentials` from the query remains allowed — the path itself is not used then — as long as the named collection permits it. Because the contents are the only spelling a query has, `nats_credentials` inherits the override permission of the path key it replaces, the same way `ssl_ca_pem` does for `ssl_ca` in `findOverrideForbiddingKey`: credentials the operator pinned with `<nats_credential_file overridable="false">` cannot be replaced through the contents form either, in either spelling, while the contents form stays usable when `allow_named_collection_override_by_default` is disabled (it is not a new key, it replaces one the collection defines). The `SETTINGS` clause is applied on top of the collection values without passing through the named-collection override check, so `resolveCredentialSource` enforces the same permission for both spellings. An empty `nats_credentials` is refused as well: it can only drop the credentials a collection carries, in either form, never replace them with other ones. Tests: a new stateless test `04891_nats_credential_file_path_restriction` covers all rejected SQL spellings and the accepted configuration-file sources, using `NATS` named collections added to the stateless-test server configuration (`tests/config/config.d/named_collection.xml`, with `nats_url = '127.0.0.1:1'`, so passing the validation surfaces as `CANNOT_CONNECT_NATS`) — one with a plain `nats_credential_file`, one where it is locked with `overridable="false"`, and one without credentials at all; `04665_nats_credentials_named_collection` is updated — the `nats_credential_file` query-override direction is now rejected. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110733 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114178 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/85213 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Backward Incompatible Change ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The `NATS` table engine accepts credentials inline in the new `nats_credentials` setting (the same payload as a `.creds` file), and no longer accepts `nats_credential_file` from SQL: the path is a reference to a file on the server filesystem, which the server opens with its own privileges, so it can only be specified in a named collection defined in the server configuration file, or as `nats.credential_file` in the server configuration itself. A query may replace such a configured path with inline `nats_credentials`, unless the operator pinned it with `<nats_credential_file overridable="false">`. Tables created before this restriction keep working after an upgrade. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114644&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114644](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114644+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Do not hold the DDL guard during TRUNCATE
signals.text: `TRUNCATE TABLE` held the table's DDL guard while removing data, and truncate can wait for running merges or for other replicas to process `DROP_RANGE`. Any DDL on that name — including background threads that need it — was blocked for that whole time. Release the guard before `IStorage::truncate` for databases with UUIDs, matching `ALTER TABLE ... DROP PARTITION`, which never took it. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `TRUNCATE TABLE` no longer blocks concurrent `DROP`, `RENAME` and other DDL queries on the same table while the data is being removed. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114672&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114672](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114672+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Precompute hashes and prefetch for fixed-size-keys aggregation methods
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114638 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104475 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/81944 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): For the `keys32`/`keys64`/`keys128`/`keys256` family of aggregation methods (several fixed-size keys packed into one integer), precompute the per-row canonical hashes in one pass over the batch-packed keys and reuse them to software-prefetch the target bucket and to skip rehashing the key in `emplace`. Previously the look-ahead prefetch computed every key and its hash twice per row. --- This extends the precomputed-hash + prefetch mechanism that #104475 introduced for the `prealloc_serialized` family to `HashMethodKeysFixed` (multi-key `GROUP BY` over numeric columns, e.g. ClickBench Q30/Q31/Q32). When the whole block of keys is batch-packed upfront (`prepared_keys`), the per-row canonical hashes are computed in one pass on the first `emplace`/`find` call and reused both for the look-ahead prefetch and for the insert itself, replacing the generic look-ahead in `Aggregator::executeImplBatch` that builds every key holder and hashes it a second time per row. Details: - The runtime gates mirror `prealloc_serialized`: batch-packed keys available, `enable_software_prefetch_in_aggregation`, and the `min_bytes_for_prefetch` hash-table size threshold (checked lazily on the first call, when `Data` is known). Nullable and low-cardinality variants never use `prepared_keys` and are excluded at compile time. - A new concept `HasPrefetchByHashMemberFunc` compiles the path out for tables without hash-addressed buckets (`FixedHashTable` behind `keys16`). Set, JOIN and `arrayUniq`-style callers of `HashMethodKeysFixed` pass no settings context, so nothing changes for them. - `HashMethodSerializedContext` carried only the settings and is now the shared `HashMethodSettingsContext`, also used by `HashMethodKeysFixed::createContext`. - `HashTable::isEmptyCell` (the `findKey` short-circuit for precomputed hashes, used in the `no_more_keys` mode) is made zero-key-aware: the zero key is stored outside the buffer, so an empty cell at the key's place proves nothing when the zero key is present. The existing user (`prealloc_serialized`) never produces empty keys, so this was latent; an all-zeros fixed key is common (the ClickBench `hits` table has a `SearchEngineID = 0, ClientIP = 0` group). Correctness was verified against an unpatched build of the same commit on the full ClickBench `hits` dataset (identical single part, 99,997,497 rows): full-result checksums for `keys32`/`keys64`/`keys128`/`keys256`, nullable keys and `prealloc_serialized`; the all-zero key group; the `no_more_keys` path (`max_rows_to_group_by` with `group_by_overflow_mode = 'any'`); and external aggregation (spill + merge). All results are identical. An honest note on measured impact, from the investigation written up in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114638#issuecomment-5285053418: in a local interleaved A/B on a (noisy, shared) 96-core aarch64 box, this change measures neutral on ClickBench Q30/Q31/Q35 — the generic look-ahead prefetch already covered these methods, so the remaining saving is one packed-key load plus one CRC per row. The issue's local reproduction numbers for these queries turned out to be dominated by an unrelated effect (the memory-based `max_threads` cap from #100383, which the pre-#100383 baseline build does not have — details in the issue). The perf tests that exercise these exact shapes (`tests/performance/clickbench.xml` Q30/Q31/Q32, `group_by_fixed_keys.xml`, `hash_table_sizes_stats.xml`) should be the arbiter on dedicated hardware. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114679&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114679](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114679+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Adaptive lazy execution of short-circuit function arguments (continues #73776)
signals.text: This continues #73776 by @lgbo-ustc, whose branch was ~17 months behind `master` and could no longer be merged mechanically (27 conflicting files in the hottest central code). The author's commits are preserved; on top of them this reconciles the change with the current `master` and reworks the plumbing. Short-circuit evaluation decides *statically* which arguments of `and`, `or`, `if` and `multiIf` are executed lazily. Lazy execution is not free: the rows which are not needed are filtered out and the result is expanded back to the original size. When the filtered out part is small, or the argument itself is cheap, this overhead is larger than the work it saves. This adds an opt-in adaptive mode: the execution of every function is profiled (elapsed time and processed rows), and every 20000 rows the decision is revisited per action - lazy execution is turned off when the estimated cost of the full execution is lower than the measured cost of the lazy execution, and turned back on when the per-row cost of the action grows significantly. Actions whose function can throw an exception on invalid input values (for example `intDiv(1, 0)`) are never switched to eager execution, so the short-circuit protection is preserved. The mode is disabled by default and enabled with the new experimental setting `enable_adaptive_short_circuit_lazy_execution`. Changes on top of the original branch: * The flag no longer travels through `ExpressionStep`/`FilterStep` constructors, the query plan optimizations, the planner and the step serialization. It lives in `ExpressionActionsSettings` next to `enable_lazy_columns_replication`, which removes ~20 files from the change and all the ripple through `QueryPlan/Optimizations`. * `ExpressionActions::execute` and `executeOnColumns` stay `const`; the free `executeAction` became a member with three virtual hooks (`shouldExecuteLazily`, `executeFunction`, `finalizeBlockExecution`) which `AdaptiveExpressionActions` overrides. * The profile plumbing follows the current `IExecutableFunction` chain, including `executeWithoutReplicatedColumns`, which did not exist when the branch was written. * `is_no_except` is computed only when the setting is enabled, so nothing changes for the default path. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md): Added an experimental setting `enable_adaptive_short_circuit_lazy_execution`, which enables dynamic evaluation of whether a short-circuit function's argument should be lazily executed. The execution of the functions is profiled at runtime, and the lazy execution of an argument is disabled when it costs more than executing the argument on all the rows. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/73776 <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114734&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114734](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114734+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Resolve the 25.8 cherry-pick conflict of #112327
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112327 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114796 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a use-after-free when a `LEFT JOIN` to a dictionary with `join_algorithm = 'direct'` had a join key that is serialized `Sparse`. `getColumnVectorData` returned a `PaddedPODArray` reference into a column owned only by a function-local `ColumnPtr`, so the dictionary lookup read freed memory. ### Description Backport of #112327 to `25.8`. The robot cherry-pick #114796 is `CONFLICTING`, so the automation cannot carry it. The conflict is in one file. `getColumnVectorData` materializes its key column with `removeSpecialRepresentations` on master and with `recursiveRemoveSparse` here; `removeSpecialRepresentations` does not exist on this branch. The resolution keeps 25.8's call and takes the fix's predicate, so the resolved change is the same 8 insertions and 7 deletions as the merged commit. On this branch the copy therefore guards `Const` and `Sparse`; `ColumnReplicated` does not exist here and is dropped from the comment's carrier list. `25.8` is affected. On the official `25.8.30.17` binary the repro (a 2M-row sparse probe joined to a `FLAT()` dictionary) segfaults in 2 of 7 runs, and with jemalloc junk filling it fails 4 of 4 with `Invalid number of rows in Chunk ... expected 65409, got 0`. The same data written densely passes. Comparing returned values alone cannot see this, because freed but intact memory still yields the correct numbers. Verified in both directions with a clang-19 Debug build, this branch's pinned compiler, asserting build ids against the running server. Pristine `25.8` aborts on the first assertion of the ported test, at `PODArray::operator[]` inside `FlatDictionary::hasKeys` reached through `IDictionary::getByKeys` and `DirectKeyValueJoin::joinBlock` - the mechanism reported on master. With the fix the test passes and the repro returns the correct result in 3 of 3 runs. One branch adaptation in the test: `enable_lazy_columns_replication` does not exist on `25.8` and is rejected as an unknown setting, so it is dropped from the `ARRAY JOIN` statement. The statement and every assertion are kept.

signals.title: Convert OUTER join to INNER join by null-rejecting join conditions
signals.text: Closes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112456 Outer join to inner join conversion works by looking if a filter above the join rejects default values, NULLs in the case of nullable columns. This change allows join conditions of enclosing joins to be used for rejecting NULLs too: 1. optimizer pass `deriveNotNullFiltersFromJoin` derives `col IS NOT NULL` filters from join conditions over bare columns and adds them to the plan. 2. these filters get pushed down and used for the conversion as usual. 3. optimizer pass `resolvePlannerOnlyFilters` either promote or removes planner derived filters to executable filters based on their estimated selectivity. #### Performance result: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Convert `OUTER JOIN` to `INNER JOIN` when a later JOIN filters out its NULL-extended rows, and filter NULL join keys directly at the table scan when column statistics show it is selective. Only join clauses over bare columns are taken into account (col1 `` col2, where `` is one of `=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`). Controlled by the new settings `query_plan_convert_outer_join_to_inner_join_by_join_predicates`, `query_plan_promote_planner_only_not_null_filters` and `query_plan_max_selectivity_for_promoting_not_null_filters` (all enabled by default). --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114817&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114817](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114817+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)]

signals.title: Fix flaky 00632_get_sample_block_cache (300s timeout under TSAN)
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/41240 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Seen under `Stateless tests (amd_tsan, parallel)`: ``` Code: 159. DB::Exception: Timeout exceeded: elapsed 300200.551 ms, maximum: 300000 ms. (TIMEOUT_EXCEEDED) (query 20, line 69) ``` [CI report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/PRs/114731/a5daee0848c43176efa72907a99ab173c49a6297/result_pr.json) **Root cause.** The bound that fires is the test's own `SET max_execution_time = 300`, and it sits at the top of the healthy distribution. Nothing else bounds the query: the server default is unlimited, and `tests/config` sets the setting only in `users.d/limits_fast.yaml`, linked for Fast test alone (`install.sh:293`). Measured on this check over the 90 days to 2026-08-14, n = 12736 passing runs: p50 23.4 s, p99 128 s, max 289.1 s, so 4% headroom. TSAN plus parallel-suite contention supplies the rest. Three CIDB timeouts share the signature, one on master. **Change.** I cut the fixture's row volume only (`LIMIT 65536` to `LIMIT 4096`); `4095` asserts the same `distinct x > 0` property `65535` did. Query-20 cost is row-linear over a fixed ~50 ms analysis floor (medians 655 ms at 65536 rows, 108 ms at 4096), and the cache under test is keyed on query text, so cutting rows removes execution noise only. All 100 `UNION ALL` branches, `max_threads = 32`, the 300 s bound and all four tags stay, and `EXPLAIN PIPELINE` is byte-identical. Sensitivity drops from ~13x the p50 to ~150x; the regression it names, its own "tens of minutes", is still caught. **Validation.** The failure is contention-driven and does not reproduce on an idle box, so I proved the mechanism deterministically: with the oracle tightened to 0.3 s, between the two medians, the unchanged file fails with the exact CI signature and the fixed file passes. 200 further runs pass across both files, randomization on and off. Side note, not fixed here: under this test's `enable_analyzer = 1` query 20 never reaches the sample-block cache, which only `InterpreterSelectWithUnionQuery` reads. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1441` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Hold the table lock across a lightweight UPDATE pipeline
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104431 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a server abort (`Logical error: Part patch-... doesn't exist`) when a `DROP TABLE` runs concurrently with a lightweight `UPDATE` on a `ReplicatedMergeTree` table. The update now holds the table's shared lock until its patch part is committed, so the `DROP` waits instead of removing it. ### Description Reported by @ alexey-milovidov on #104431: an `Upgrade check (amd_release)` abort with no fix on master, STID `3208-458f`, 4 hits on 4 unrelated PRs in 6 days ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=104431&sha=7970f08a82eaf2ad5217d57a7796ae1c5e920030&name_0=PR&name_1=Upgrade+check+%28amd_release%29)). **What breaks.** A lightweight `UPDATE` racing a `DROP TABLE` aborts the server, release builds included: `Transaction::commit`'s `modifyPartState` sits in `NOEXCEPT_SCOPE`, whose catch-all is `std::terminate`. **Root cause.** `InterpreterUpdateQuery::execute` takes `lockForShare` into a function-local holder and parks only the *storage* in the returned pipeline; `QueryPlanResourceHolder` keeps `storage_holders` and `table_locks` separately, so the lock dies when `execute()` returns, long before the sink commits the patch part. A concurrent `DROP` then takes the exclusive lock, `dropAllData()` clears `data_parts_indexes`, and the commit cannot find its own part. It needs a UUID-less database (`Memory`/`Ordinary`), where `DROP` removes data inline, hence the intermittency. **The change.** Move the already-acquired lock into the pipeline's resources, as the INSERT path does at `InterpreterInsertQuery.cpp:1297`. Three entry points: `InterpreterUpdateQuery::execute`, `InterpreterAlterQuery::executeToTable`, and `StorageAlias::updateLightweight`, which resolves a *different* storage and so needs the target's own lock, as `StorageAlias::read` does. `DELETE FROM` rewrites to `UPDATE` and is covered transitively. A concurrent `DROP` or `DETACH` now waits for an in-flight lightweight update, as it already does for `INSERT`. `TRUNCATE` takes no exclusive lock for `MergeTree`. **Validation.** New test `04905_lwu_drop_race_table_lock.sh`, one arm per fixed carrier. A pauseable failpoint parks the replicated sink between the patch-part rename and the commit, while the update still holds the lock; the arm then drops the table and waits for the drop to block on that lock. Nothing is timed, so an arm cannot miss a window or pass quietly. Aborts without the fix, passes with it, 50/50 green. <details> <summary>Both-directions matrix (every cell measured, Build IDs asserted against the running server)</summary> | binary | `UPDATE` | `ALTER ... UPDATE` | via `Alias` | |---|---|---|---| | base (fix reverted) `ea8e869d` | ABORT | ABORT | ABORT | | interpreters only `3651f11d` | pass | pass | ABORT | | full fix `1884b944` | pass | pass | pass | The middle row is the control that shows the `StorageAlias` change is necessary: with both interpreter fixes applied, the alias arm is the only one that still aborts. The lock demonstrably serializes the two queries: with the sink parked after the patch-part rename, the `DROP` becomes a waiting writer and stays one until the sink is released, then completes. Deadlock check: the change only extends the lifetime of a *Read* acquisition, and no sink on this path takes the table lock. `update_sequential_consistency = 1` and a following `OPTIMIZE TABLE ... FINAL` both complete normally. </details>

signals.title: Add a userspace page cache tier to the experimental ReaderExecutor
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/103706 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/102282 Next incremental slice of the experimental `ReaderExecutor` (split of #103706), following the merged disk-cache provider #110029. Adds the userspace page (memory) cache tier: `PageCacheProvider` implements `ICacheProvider` over `PageCache` with zero-copy hits (the arena is pinned by a shared_ptr) and whole-block first-writer-wins fills via `PageCache::getOrSet`. `ReadPipeline` wires it as the first (fastest) tier of the executor cache chain when the page cache applies, and skips it on unknown-size sources. `ReadPipeline.cpp` is the only non-verbatim file; the provider and its gtest are ports from #103706. Gated by `use_reader_executor` (default off); the legacy read path is unchanged. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added a userspace page cache tier to the experimental `ReaderExecutor` read path (`use_reader_executor`, off by default). signals.title: Do not abort the server when a loader worker cannot be spawned
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110174 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a server abort that happens when the global thread pool is momentarily saturated while tables are still loading. `AsyncLoader` now keeps running if it cannot spawn an extra loader worker and some worker will still drain the queued jobs, instead of calling `std::terminate`. ### Description `AsyncLoader::spawn` wrapped `scheduleOrThrowOnError` in `NOEXCEPT_SCOPE`, whose handler is unconditionally `std::terminate()`. A transient `CANNOT_SCHEDULE_TASK` from a saturated global thread pool therefore killed the server (`Received signal 6`) during table loading. Seen 4 times over 4 unrelated PRs and 4 build flavours in 30 days, e.g. [`Stress test (arm_tsan)`](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=108468&sha=27a154474608ee82636207020a9bd13beb8c9449&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_tsan%29), whose stack is `terminate_handler()` -> `std::terminate()` -> `AsyncLoader.cpp:908` `spawn()` -> `:744` `enqueue()`. A spawn must succeed only when nothing else will drain the pool's ready queue, so it now tells three states apart: - a worker that entered `worker()` and is not inside `wait()` drains the queue now; - a worker inside `wait()` on *another* pool's job resumes draining once that job runs; - neither of those means nobody ever will. In the first two cases `spawn` uses the non-throwing `trySchedule`, rolls back its `Pool::workers` increment on failure, warns and returns false. Only the last case keeps the fatal path, byte for byte: the queued jobs would be stranded, and throwing is not an option because `schedule` marks that region non-exception-safe. Covering it needs rollback-and-retry across the loading DAG, out of scope here. All 4 observed rows are recoverable. `BackgroundSchedulePool` narrows the same way (`929227464f9736b`). Two counters are added because `Pool::workers` also counts a worker still queued in the global pool, which drains nothing, and one blocked in `wait()`, which cannot take its own pool's jobs. A saturated pool is remembered so the failing thread creation happens once per episode, not once per queued job, counted by the new `AsyncLoaderSpawnFailures` event; entering `wait()` clears the memo. Tests are gtests asserting which branch was taken, not just that the process survived. A SQL test cannot reach the line: on master the whole call sits under `blockFaultInjections()`. Related: #110174, which removed the mask that hid this exception. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Backported to: `26.7.4.53` <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Fix AI functions embedding counters behavior on error
signals.text: `aiEmbed` and `aiSimilarity` under-report provider usage in `system.query_log` when a request fails: with the default `ai_function_throw_on_error = 1` the exception row shows `AIAPICalls = 0` and `AIInputTokens = 0`, although the provider was called and billed. Flipping only that setting records the call: | `ai_function_throw_on_error` | `AIAPICalls` | `AIRowsSkipped` | |---|---:|---:| | `1` (default) | 0 | 0 | | `0` | 1 | 1 | Same query and endpoint, with `ai_function_max_retries = 0` so exactly one attempt is made. **Cause.** `embedTexts` accumulates the counters in a local `EmbeddingResult` and returns it by value. When a failed request rethrows, `return` is never reached: the local is destroyed while unwinding and the caller's `embedding_result` is never constructed, so the caller's `ProfileEvents::increment` calls are both skipped and left with nothing to read. That defeats the intent stated at the accumulation site, which counts `api_calls` *before* issuing the request so that failed calls are still counted. **Fix.** `embedTexts` now reports `AIAPICalls` and `AIInputTokens` itself, from a `SCOPE_EXIT` guard, so the normal and throwing exits both publish them. They are plain locals rather than fields of `EmbeddingResult`, so no caller can count them twice. Callers keep their own row counters, which mean different things: texts for `aiEmbed`, pairs of texts for `aiSimilarity`. **Not covered.** Row counters are still dropped when the query throws. It delivered no rows, and preserving them would need `embedTexts` to take an out-parameter in both callers. **Tests.** Three integration tests, each verified to fail with the source reverted to `master`: one per caller for `AIAPICalls`, plus one driving the quota-exceeded throw so a batch succeeds first and `AIInputTokens` is non-zero. The failed-request tests cannot cover `AIInputTokens`, since there the first request fails and no tokens are consumed. The same defect on the text-generation path is fixed in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111830, which is what introduced a throwing path there. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111830 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `aiEmbed` and `aiSimilarity` reporting zero `AIAPICalls` in `system.query_log` when a provider request failed, and losing `AIInputTokens` already consumed by earlier successful batches. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114905&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114905](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114905+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Scope WITH aliases to the SELECT that declares them when adding the default database
signals.text: Scope WITH aliases to the SELECT that declares them when adding the default database <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/104972 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/104972 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed table names not being qualified with the default database when a `WITH` alias elsewhere in the same query happened to share the name. `ALTER TABLE other_db.t UPDATE v = (WITH RECURSIVE src AS (SELECT 7 AS id) SELECT max(id) FROM src) + (SELECT max(id) FROM src)` failed with `UNKNOWN_DATABASE`, the same expression through `UPDATE ... SET` silently read the session's `src` instead of `other_db.src`, and a view whose `UNION` branch referenced such a table could not be read from another database. Closes #104972. ### Description `AddDefaultDatabaseVisitor` records `WITH RECURSIVE` aliases so it does not qualify a name that is a CTE rather than a table. That record was one set shared by the whole visitor instance and never cleared, so an alias declared inside one `SELECT` kept suppressing qualification for every identifier seen afterwards, including a genuine physical table. The leak is forward-only: a colliding name before the CTE is fine. The set becomes a stack of scopes, one pushed per `ASTSelectQuery` and popped by a destructor, so a `SELECT`'s subtree inherits the enclosing aliases and nothing outside it does. Lookups walk it innermost-first. Three cases follow: - The `WITH` list is now walked in the non-recursive case too. A recursive alias is registered before its element is visited, since it may reference itself; a plain alias after, so inside its own definition the name still denotes a table. This mirrors `ApplyWithSubqueryVisitor`, and matters because `ApplyWithGlobalVisitor` copies a first branch's `WITH` list into later `UNION` branches without the `RECURSIVE` flag. - Enclosing scopes are searched for a plain name only when `enable_global_with_statement` is set, matching the resolver: without it the analyzer clears `allow_to_check_cte` for parent scopes. A recursive name is searched unconditionally, since its self-reference resolves inside its own definition. The setting is read per `SELECT`, by replaying the clauses reaching it as `QueryTreeBuilder` does, so a repeated setting takes its last value and `compatibility` is honoured. - `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY QUERY` and `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW` expand a plain CTE reference into a copy of its body first. Inside that copy the name denotes a table, so that binding is masked. Fixing the visitor covers all 13 construction sites at once. Validated on 40 arms, with eight mutants pinning the scope stack, the clone mask, the registration and lookup order, and the setting handling.

signals.title: Read fresh in-memory metadata at the OPTIMIZE merge-selection read
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104822 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed data loss when a `RENAME COLUMN` runs concurrently with `OPTIMIZE TABLE ... FINAL` on a `MergeTree` table: the merged part could be written with the pre-rename column list, permanently filling the renamed column with its `DEFAULT`. ### Description `26.3`-only fix for issue 80648, authorized in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113929#issuecomment-5229587902. `StorageMergeTree::optimize` calls `merge` synchronously on the query thread, so the merge-selection metadata read runs with a live query context. `MergeTreeData` overrides `getInMemoryMetadataPtr` with a per-query cache that `InterpreterOptimizeQuery` has already populated with the pre-`ALTER` snapshot, so the read returns metadata predating the rename while selection pairs it with parts that already carry the mutation. `MergeTask` takes `storage_columns` from that snapshot and never re-reads, so the merged part keeps the old column list and the renamed column stays `DEFAULT`. Passing `bypass_metadata_cache=true` makes the read honour the invariant the comment above it already states. `scheduleDataProcessingJob` keeps its bare read: its only caller is the background pool, which has no query context, so it already bypasses. `26.4` and later declare the accessor as `(ContextPtr, bool)` with no default, forcing every caller to state a context, so the read is already fresh there. `25.8` has the same bare read but ships `enable_shared_storage_snapshot_in_query` defaulting to `false`. `26.3` is the only supported branch with both the defaulted parameter and that setting `true`, which is why the backport of 104822 compiled unchanged as `getInMemoryMetadataPtr()` and took the cache-consulting path. Validation on two interleaved, load-matched servers built from this tree, setting at its default: base reddens 16 of 7000 iterations against 0 for the fix (Fisher exact p = 3.0e-05); swapping the binaries onto each other's port and data directory keeps the effect with the binary (30/7000 against 0/7000); 80 runner runs of the unmodified `04238_alter_rename_column_merge_race` per arm give 3 base failures with the exact CI signature and 80/80 on the fix. None of the 211 merge and mutation tests with a verdict in both arms regressed.

signals.title: Set the current Keeper component in TextIndexCountSource::generate
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113295 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Related: #113295 `SELECT count() FROM t WHERE hasAllTokens(str, [...])` is rewritten by the trivial-count-from-text-index optimization into a `ReadFromTextIndexCount` step (added in #111494). Its source runs on a pipeline execution thread: `TextIndexCountSource::generate` -> `computeCountForPart` -> `makeTextIndexInputStream` -> `IMergeTreeDataPart::getStreamNameOrHash(..., IDataPartStorage &)`, whose body probes the part storage with `existsFile`. On a disk that keeps part metadata in Keeper that probe is a real Keeper request, and `Coordination::ZooKeeper::pushRequest` throws `LOGICAL_ERROR` when no component is set for the scope. `generate()` is the outermost scope this step owns on that thread, and it set none: the step builds its own `Pipe`, so unlike the ordinary read path it never inherits the guard from `MergeTreeSource::tryGenerate`. This adds the one-line RAII guard at the top of `generate()`. The guard is a nesting-safe thread-local stack and every Keeper-reaching call above is a descendant of that scope, so no deeper placement is needed. Same shape as #113295 for `MergeTreeCodecBlockCountsSource::generate` and the sibling `MergeTreeTextIndexSource::generate`. Of the four callers of `makeTextIndexInputStream`, the other three already have an ancestor guard (`MergeTreeSource::tryGenerate` for both `MergeTreeReaderTextIndex` sites, the mutate/merge task guards for `MergeTextIndexesTask`); this step was the only gap. Category is `CI Fix or Improvement`, as in #113295 and #113386: the metadata-in-Keeper storage type is registered only under `#if CLICKHOUSE_CLOUD`, and `LOGICAL_ERROR` aborts only in debug and sanitizer builds, so this cannot happen in an official stable build. For the same reason no test is added: no public build reaches Keeper through `existsFile`. Validated with the existing `02346_text_index*` suite (plus 50/50 randomized runs of `02346_text_index_optimize_trivial_count`), an `EXPLAIN` assertion that the modified scope is the one the query executes, and a run with `enforce_keeper_component_tracking = 1`. Left alone: the plan-time `getDeserializedFormat` path can also reach `existsFile` for packed skip-index parts and is likewise unguarded, but it predates this step by three weeks and is not this failure's carrier.

signals.title: Fix coordination mode mismatch with a parameterized view subquery
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106039 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113622 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106039 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113622 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `Coordination mode mismatch for stream <table>: got Default, expected WithOrder` when a parameterized view is used as an `IN`-subquery of an ordered query with parallel replicas enabled. A parameterized view used this way no longer plans its inner read with parallel replicas coordination on a replica. ### Description `SELECT ... FROM t WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM pv(id = 'a')) AND id IN (SELECT id FROM pv(id = 'b')) ORDER BY id` with parallel replicas enabled aborted the server in debug and sanitizer builds, and threw in release. Root cause. A parameterized view resolves as a `TableFunctionNode`, so its arguments land in `skip_children` in `Planner/CollectSets.cpp` and the view call survives verbatim into the text sent to the replicas. The initiator plans the outer read in order from the sort key and announces `WithOrder`; each replica re-plans the view body, an unordered scan, and announces `Default`. Both key on the bare table name, so the second announcement reaches the first's coordinator and throws. `PlannerJoinTree.cpp` already guards a view planning its own read on a follower, but it compares `table_node` against the chosen `parallel_replicas_table`, and both are null, so it concludes "this is the chosen table" and leaves coordination enabled for the view. A table expression that is not a `TableNode` is now treated as not chosen, which is always correct: `parallel_replicas_table` is a `const TableNode *`, and both walks in `findTableForParallelReplicas` bail out on a table function. The union-children comparison is skipped for the same reason. A view referenced by name is a `TableNode`, so `parallel_replicas_allow_view_over_mergetree = 1` is unaffected. Validation. The test pins the five settings the divergence depends on, three of which the runner randomizes; each of the four that can vary was confirmed load-bearing by a negative control on the unfixed binary. It fails 8 of 8 randomized runs on master with the reported error and passes 100 of 100 here. Expected rows are parallel-replicas-off ground truth, so each query also asserts `ParallelReplicasHandleAnnouncementMicroseconds > 0` to show coordination was reached. The in-tree view, parameterized-view, trivial-view-pushdown and table-function tests are unchanged.

signals.title: Fix undefined behavior in DateTime64 reservoir quantiles
signals.text: The reservoir-sampling implementation of `quantile` and `quantiles` previously interpolated decimal-backed values through `Float64`. `DateTime64` ticks close to the upper `Int64` boundary, as well as `Decimal128` and `Decimal256` values near their limits, can collapse to the same `Float64` value and make conversion back to the native representation undefined or return an incorrect endpoint. Interpolate decimal-backed samples in their exact native domain instead, and cover scalar/plural `DateTime64` plus wide-decimal boundary cases with stateless regression tests. Found by the `arm_asan_ubsan` stress test: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112573&sha=762fa93f05ca081011efec5fef767e3c36be6853&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_asan_ubsan%2C%20s3%29 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114485 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107154 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed undefined behavior and incorrect boundary results in `quantile` and `quantiles` for `DateTime64` and wide `Decimal` values. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1596` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Show why a job failed when it never uploaded its own report
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113382 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Not user-facing: CI report only. ### Description Two jobs on #113382 lost their runner mid-`Run`, and both report pages render nothing, so the failure looks like a 0-second job with no output: - https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113382&sha=f7f79281458bd4558f12725868c0035cbc7b8f5d&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29 - https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113382&sha=f7f79281458bd4558f12725868c0035cbc7b8f5d&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%2C%20old_compatibility%29 praktika did detect the failure and record the reason, but three defects hide it. `_finish_workflow` reported such a job only through `env.add_workflow_error(..., source=result.name)`. `source=` sets the `from` label, not the destination, so the message landed on the workflow node while the job's own node kept an empty `info`, and the page renders notifications from the node it resolved, which is the job. The `Status.ERROR` sites in `runner.py` already call `add_error` on the job's own result; this site did not. A job uploads its own `result_<job>.json` from inside the job, so a job that dies never uploads one and S3 answers 403. The page turned that 403 into "Report does not exist or expired" and returned, discarding the workflow report it had already fetched, which does contain the job's node. That early return is gone, and the cached per-job report is now overwritten on every fetch that came back, so a page polling `sha=latest` cannot keep showing an older commit's node. Rendering that node exposed a third defect, already on master: the auto-reload predicate asked whether the per-job report was running, so a null one read as still loading and the page refetched S3 every 30 seconds forever. It now asks the node the page actually renders. The runner loss is not fixable here and this does not try to. A test drives `_finish_workflow` against a stubbed environment and asserts the reason reaches the uploaded workflow report. For the page, a script extracts the relevant functions from `json.html` and replays the measured S3 responses. Reverting any one fix alone reintroduces its symptom; the healthy and expired paths stay byte-identical.

signals.title: Make a table read by a scalar subquery in a CONSTRAINT a loading dependency
signals.text: Attaching a table analyzes its constraints in `InterpreterCreateQuery::getConstraintsDescription`, and the analysis executes the scalar subqueries of a constraint expression. The tables such a subquery reads were not registered as loading dependencies, because `DDLLoadingDependencyVisitor` only looks at functions, dictionary sources and the storage definition. Nothing prevented dropping such a table, and the server did not start afterwards - attaching the dependent table threw `UNKNOWN_TABLE` and loading the metadata failed: ```sql CREATE TABLE t1 (id UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); CREATE TABLE t2 (conversation UInt64, CONSTRAINT c CHECK (SELECT id FROM t1 LIMIT 15) IN (conversation)) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); DROP TABLE t1; -- accepted, and the server cannot start anymore ``` The referential dependency was recorded, since `DDLDependencyVisitor` visits `ASTTableExpression`, so `check_referential_table_dependencies = 1` rejected the `DROP`. But that setting is off by default, and it is the loading graph that the default `check_table_dependencies` check and the `DROP DATABASE` drop order (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/97057) use. A constraint declaration is now visited, and the tables of every subquery that the analysis executes are added to the loading dependencies. Subqueries which the analysis does not execute - the right argument of `IN` and the argument of `exists`, see `ExecuteScalarSubqueriesMatcher::visit` - are skipped, because what they read is needed only when the constraint is checked, not to attach the table. That keeps `02916_joinget_dependency`-style patterns working, in particular `02841_not_ready_set_constraints`, which drops the table read by an `x IN (SELECT ...)` constraint on purpose. Seen in CI as a `Cannot start clickhouse-server` stress failure, e.g. https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110231&sha=4de836223549fd5224ca017b8c1a28e344ce38e9&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_msan%29 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114918 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/87369 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): A table read by a scalar subquery inside a `CONSTRAINT` is now a loading dependency of the table that declares the constraint. Previously such a table could be dropped, after which the server did not start, because attaching the dependent table executes the subquery. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114923&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114923](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114923+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix server abort on a corrupt ORC stripe footer
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114674 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/orc/pull/25 Reading a corrupt ORC blob aborts a debug or sanitizer server instead of raising `INCORRECT_DATA`: ``` generated_message_tctable_lite.cc:228] Check failed: VerifyHasBitConsistency(msg, table) is OK (INTERNAL: Has bits mismatch for Type=orc.proto.StripeFooter Field=1 ``` Found by the AST fuzzer (`AST fuzzer (amd_debug, targeted)`, [report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114267&sha=08273e65417c8b6a4fe95d2c2cdad899ea17d041&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29)), and reproduced on pristine master with default settings by `SELECT c0 FROM format(ORC, 'c0 DateTime64(3)', unhex('4f524311...524317'))`, so any user-supplied ORC bytes reach it. **Root cause.** ORC's `DecompressionStream` throws where protobuf's `ZeroCopyInputStream::Next` contract requires a `false` return, so the exception originates inside protobuf's parse loop. `TcParser` keeps has-bits in a register-cached local and writes them back only on its own exit paths, so the unwind skips that write-back and leaves `StripeFooter` with the repeated field `streams` appended to and its has-bit clear. Since the v35.1 protobuf bump the generated destructor checks that invariant, so destroying it aborts. `DebugHardenCheckHasBitConsistency()` gates it on `!NDEBUG` or a sanitizer, so release builds are unaffected, hence a CI fix. **Change.** A submodule bump only. ORC's parse boundary now wraps the caller's stream in an adapter that captures anything escaping `Next`/`BackUp`/`Skip`/`ByteCount`, returns the contract's failure value, and rethrows the original exception once the parser has returned consistent. One header covers all nine `parseProtobufFromStream` call sites, including embedder streams such as ClickHouse's `ORCInputStream`. **Validation.** The blob aborts (RC 134) before the change and afterwards reports `Code: 117 ... Read past EOF in DecompressionStream::readBuffer ... (INCORRECT_DATA)`, byte-identical to master release today, so no user-visible message or code changes. New test `04856_orc_corrupt_stripe_footer` passes 50/50 randomized and fails on the unfixed binary with the has-bits tokens. A 183-case corruption sweep and the full `orc` suite show no behaviour change. `ProtobufZeroCopyInputStreamFromReadBuffer` (Prometheus remote-write) has the same shape, but is unreported and I could not reproduce a failure there, so it is untouched.

signals.title: Reduce merge write amplification in test_rabbitmq_mv_combo
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109909 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109909 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `test_rabbitmq_mv_combo` intermittently fails `Time limit of 180 seconds reached` on master, most recently on `amd_msan, 6/8` ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=236b530a8018049fb73c0417cceebbf346888949&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Integration%20tests%20%28amd_msan%2C%206%2F8%29)). The run is not stalled: consumption strictly increases at every poll, zero no-progress polls. It is too slow because `rabbitmq_max_block_size = 100` makes every consumer flush a 100-row part, so each of the 5 materialized-view targets accumulates ~2,000 level-0 parts and every merge round re-reads the growing `all_1_*` base part - ~300 times over (final merge level 295-316). In the failing job merges read 124M rows to consume the 693k reached before the deadline (~179x); locally, same signature, 122M rows for the full 1M (~122x), ~96% base-part re-reads. This raises `rabbitmq_max_block_size` to 10000 for this test's table only, matching `test_nats_overloaded_insert` (the same high-volume MV fan-out shape). It reduces the work rather than relaxing the budget: the 180s deadline is unchanged and the `parallel_view_processing` setting from #110224 is retained. `rabbitmq_flush_interval_ms` stays at 1000, so partial blocks still flush every second - measured block sizes stay between 538 and 6168 rows and never reach the new cap, so the test cannot wait on a full block. The final exact-count assertion is untouched. 10000 is still 52x below the engine default for this table (`max_insert_block_size / rabbitmq_num_consumers`). Validated with 12 interleaved A/B pairs on an MSAN build (the failing configuration, same binary both arms, order alternated). Amplification drops 122.11x -> 12.43x with non-overlapping ranges, and the consumption loop the deadline measures is faster in 12/12 pairs (median 77.2s -> 66.6s). A Debug build cannot show this: there merges use 0.23 of 384 cores, so the amplification is free. 9 tests in the module pass, including `test_rabbitmq_flush_by_block_size`; the other 31 occurrences are unchanged. One residual, not addressed here: the test's `SELECT count() FROM merge(...)` poll still scans rows (~590k per poll) rather than using the trivial-count path. <details> <summary>Per-arm measurements (12 interleaved MSAN pairs)</summary> | metric | base (n=12) | fix (n=12) | delta | |---|---|---|---| | consumption loop (s), median (range) | 77.2 (69.1-81.0) | 66.6 (52.0-71.2) | -13.8% | | merge read amplification (x) | 122.11 (120.51-124.50) | 12.43 (10.90-13.25) | -89.8% | | merge rows read | 122,101,440 | 12,430,342 | -89.8% | | max merge level | 295 (291-301) | 25 (20-27) | -91.5% | | level-0 parts per table | 2000 | 142 (117-152) | -92.9% | Level-0 part size is exactly 100 rows for 9,989 of 9,989 parts before the change; after it, sizes range 538-6168 and reach the 10000 cap in 0 of 2,090 parts. </details> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1551` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->
