signals.title: Do not run 04726_kill_undrop_table_busy_wait on database engines without UNDROP support
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/56062 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `04726_kill_undrop_table_busy_wait.sh` has no `# Tags:` line, so the stateless runner admits it into the `--replicated-database` lane. There `InterpreterUndropQuery::executeToTable` rejects the query outright with `SUPPORT_IS_DISABLED` before the busy-wait the test exists to exercise ever starts, so the test's own assertion fires with `UNDROP TABLE was not cancelled with QUERY_WAS_CANCELLED`. Deterministic, not flaky: in that check 1771 of its 1776 `OK` results carry the failure text, against 0 of the 27000+ results in every other check, continuously since the explicit assertion was added on 2026-08-09. It stays invisible because that coverage job relabels diagnosed-flaky results to `OK`; the [master report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=432b1ae96183f5b085835f4b0aece8d95ce9ce73&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_llvm_coverage%2C%20old%20analyzer%2C%20s3%20storage%2C%20DBReplicated%2C%20WasmEdge%2C%20parallel%2C%202%2F3%29) that exposed it escaped only because a concurrent server death skipped the diagnostics rerun. That relabel is pre-existing and intentional; noted as disclosure, not touched here. `Ordinary` is a second carrier: `DatabaseAtomic` is the only engine that registers dropped tables for undrop, and `Ordinary` does not override `DatabaseOnDisk::dropTable`, so nothing is put into `tables_marked_dropped` and the undrop throws `UNKNOWN_TABLE`. Both rejections verified directly against a server. All three sibling UNDROP tests already tag both engines; 04726 was the only omission. Validation on one binary: the failure reproduces 100% on the pre-fix tree through the real runner; with the tag the test is `SKIPPED` in that lane and under `--db-engine Ordinary`, and still passes in the default `Atomic` lane, 50 of 50 with randomization. Negative controls (tag names typo'd, or the reason comment kept while the `# Tags:` line is deleted) re-admit the test and it fails again, so the tag is load-bearing rather than silently inert. `Related:` is context only; this PR does not implement UNDROP for Replicated. @ alexey-milovidov reached the same conclusion from the same report in PR 114884, which was closed unmerged over its unrelated `ThreadGroup` half, so this tag never landed.

signals.title: Share one referenced input subplan across sibling correlated subqueries
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a query plan growing exponentially with the number of correlated subqueries in one expression when `correlated_subqueries_use_in_memory_buffer` is disabled, which made such a query spend minutes in planning and consume tens of gigabytes. A query with eight sibling correlated subqueries now builds 226 plan steps instead of 6895. ### Description A `WHERE`/`SELECT` expression containing several correlated subqueries decorrelates them one at a time. `addExpressionStep` validates all of them against the header captured *before* that loop, but each subquery referenced the input subplan root as it stood *during* its own iteration, so subquery `k` referenced a subtree already containing subqueries `1..k-1`. When the referenced result is not buffered, the materialization pass clones each referenced root together with the references nested inside it, and the node count doubles per subquery. Measured plan steps for N sibling subqueries (`correlated_subqueries_use_in_memory_buffer = 0`): 415 at N = 4 rising to 6895 at N = 8, i.e. exactly `2^N`, reaching 68 GB of resident memory at N = 8. The buffer is also disabled whenever `correlated_subqueries_default_join_kind = 'left'`, so the blow-up is reachable by changing that one setting alone; `make_distributed_plan = 1` forces the buffer off as well (`SettingsQuirks.cpp`). Found as a `Stress test (arm_tsan)` hung check, where a cancelled `INSERT ... SELECT` sat 426 s in plan optimization with 1,670,597 plan nodes (N of about 17, for a `SELECT` repeating one correlated alias 20 times). CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114072&sha=08c0cd1e799e63d9cf42a2402776fa2ce09c9bc7&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_tsan%29 The fix creates one referenced root per expression and reuses it for every sibling. It is used only when the in-memory buffer is not in play, because the buffer optimization replaces the referenced step in place, and only when the shared root's header already carries the subquery's correlated columns. Both cases fall back to today's per-subquery root. After the fix the same plans are 226 steps at N = 8 and grow linearly. The default buffered path is untouched, and results are unchanged over both settings values. Cancellation inside the materialization pass is still not checked; with the plan now linear that pass takes milliseconds, so it is not addressed here.

signals.title: Apply HAVING without aggregation in the old analyzer
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113760 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed wrong results with `enable_analyzer = 0` when a query has a `HAVING` clause but no aggregation: the condition was silently ignored and excluded rows were returned. `HAVING` is now merged into `WHERE` for such queries, matching the new analyzer. ### Description With `enable_analyzer = 0`, a `SELECT` that has a `HAVING` clause but no aggregation silently discarded the condition and returned rows it excludes. Over a MergeTree table holding 1, 2, 3: ```sql SELECT a FROM t HAVING a > 999 SETTINGS enable_analyzer = 0, enable_optimize_predicate_expression = 0; -- returned 1, 2, 3; the new analyzer returns nothing ``` Root cause: the old analyzer builds and executes a `HAVING` filter only in its aggregation branch (`appendHaving` is called under `if (need_aggregate)`, and `executeHaving` is reachable only from inside `else if (expressions.need_aggregate)`), so without aggregation the clause is never applied. What normally hides this is `PredicateExpressionsOptimizer` moving non-aggregate conjuncts to `WHERE`, i.e. a performance optimizer was load-bearing for correctness with no interpreter fallback. It also fails at default settings when a stateful conjunct makes `tryMovePredicatesFromHavingToWhere` bail out, so `HAVING a > 999 AND blockNumber() >= 0` reproduces with `enable_analyzer = 0` alone. This merges `HAVING` into `WHERE` in `TreeRewriter::analyzeSelect` when the query does not aggregate, the canonicalization the new analyzer already performs in `Planner.cpp:2231-2238`. The interpreter, `ExpressionAnalyzer` and `PredicateExpressionsOptimizer` are unchanged. The site sits after `getAggregates` and `getWindowFunctions` so `NOT_AN_AGGREGATE` and `ILLEGAL_AGGREGATION` keep being raised, after `PredicateExpressionsOptimizer` so the default path is a no-op, and outside the `ast_optimizations_allowed` gate so it also applies on shards. Validation: `EXPLAIN` shows no `Filter` step before; after the fix the predicate reaches the storage and prunes (`Parts: 0/1`). 33 query shapes now agree across the old analyzer, the old analyzer with the rewrite enabled and the new analyzer; 20 disagreed before. `NOT_AN_AGGREGATE`, `ILLEGAL_AGGREGATION` and the `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` for `WITH TOTALS` without aggregation are unchanged and pinned by the new test. Distributed and `remote()` queries were checked on a two-shard cluster. The 44 stateless tests setting `enable_optimize_predicate_expression` pass, 589 further `HAVING` and `*analyzer*` tests show no regression.
signals.author: groeneai

signals.title: Keep 04896_orfill_merge_group_by_overflow_any on the projection merge path at any granularity
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114740 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `04896_orfill_merge_group_by_overflow_any` fails deterministically whenever the test runner randomizes `index_granularity_bytes` small: ``` Code: 117. DB::Exception: Projection p is specified in setting force_optimize_projection_name but not used. (INCORRECT_DATA) ``` Seen at four different values (7801, 9281, 49209 and locally at 1024), so it reds unrelated PRs' CI (most recently #112889 and #76867), and the arm stops covering the null-place `mergeBatch` segfault it was added for in #114740. A throw is not coverage. The optimizer is correct here. The table declares two projections, and `p` stores four aggregate states where `p2` stores one; granule sizing charges an aggregate-state column at its serialized width, so at small `index_granularity_bytes` `p` reads more marks than the base table and than `p2`, and is dropped (`optimizeUseAggregateProjection.cpp:1036` and `:1048`). At coarse granularity every candidate floors to one granule per part, the marks tie, and `p` wins only because it is declared first. The fix removes both comparisons from the fixture rather than constraining the randomizer: `index_granularity_bytes = 0` turns off adaptive granularity on the table, so a projection's mark count no longer depends on state width. The `sumOrNull` arm, the only one where `p2` is a candidate at all, also names `p` as preferred, which reduces the candidate list to one entry before any cost comparison. `force_optimize_projection_name = 'p'` is kept, so each arm still asserts that `p` specifically was used. `index_granularity_bytes`, `min_bytes_for_wide_part` and `use_const_adaptive_granularity` stay randomized. This matches `04063` and `04365`, the other tests using this pin. Validated: all four culprit values pass; 5 arms x 36 setting combinations (Compact and Wide) pass with the pinned projection applied; 50/50 runs with and without randomization; and the pre-fix binary still segfaults in `AggregateFunctionOrFill::mergeBatch` with this fixture, so the defect stays covered. `.reference` is unchanged. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114943&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114943](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114943+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1619` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Coordinate a read with pinned block numbers in classic parallel replicas
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114263 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/97557 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix wrong results when a `SELECT` with `select_sequential_consistency = 1` on a `ReplicatedMergeTree` table runs with classic (task-based) parallel replicas. Every replica performed a complete local read clamped to the quorum boundary instead of a coordinator-assigned slice, so rows were returned once per participating replica. ### Description `StorageReplicatedMergeTree::read` routes a `select_sequential_consistency = 1` query into `readLocalSequentialConsistencyImpl`, which called `MergeTreeDataSelectExecutor::read` with `enable_parallel_reading` hardcoded to `false`. The setting is propagated to the followers, so each follower took that same branch: `read_task_callback` was never installed, the follower never announced its parts, and it read the whole pinned range locally. The initiator then merged N complete copies. On a 5-part `ReplicatedMergeTree` with a pinned boundary of 12000 rows and `max_parallel_replicas = 3`, `count()` returned 36000 and `sum()` was likewise tripled, with no exception and no warning. It scaled exactly linearly with `max_parallel_replicas`, and `uniqExact` stayed correct, confirming pure per-replica duplication. Reaching the defect requires turning off one of the optimizations that would otherwise bypass this read path: `optimize_trivial_count_query = 0` for `count()`, since at its default the planner serves the count from `totalRows()` and disables parallel replicas, or `parallel_replicas_local_plan = 0` or `parallel_replicas_prefer_local_replica = 0` for data reads. All three are documented, settable per query, and leave the wrong result silent. The fix passes `canUseParallelReplicasOnFollower()` at that call site, exactly as the sibling `readLocalImpl` already does for the non-pinned path, so the pinned read participates in coordination instead of being silently excluded from it. The boundary stays computed and applied: when it binds it comes from ZooKeeper and is identical on every replica (measured on two replicas holding different part sets, 7 and 6 active parts, both clamping to the same block), and with no quorum node it is the replica's own maximum, which excludes nothing it owns. Validation: new test `04912_pr_classic_pinned_block_numbers` fails on master and passes with the change, 50/50 green under randomized settings. Full matrix in the validation-gate comment below. Out of scope, neither introduced nor altered here: the plan-based path with `parallel_replicas_local_plan = 0` (#114263), and divergent part sets with no quorum node (#105710).

signals.title: Report RabbitMQ container recreation attempts made by the startup retry
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114415 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114434 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description #114415 made the RabbitMQ readiness waiter recreate a container that fails to start and try again, turning a 21-case module abort into a passing run. When the second attempt succeeds, every channel that could record the first failure closes at once: artifact collection is gated on a failing suite (`if failed_suits:`), the report log strips setup logs from passed tests (`--report-log-exclude-logs-on-passed-tests`), and `job.log` never carried harness logging. The recovered failure survives only as an anomalous duration on the module's first test: +123.5 s against a p99 of 13.4 s over 7774 runs of that test and lane. So a retry-absorbed run discards exactly the diagnostics #114415 added to show where a hang is stuck. Now: - the waiter copies the failed attempt's `rabbit.log` out of the instance directory before recreating the container (that directory is removed on teardown) and emits a stable `RABBITMQ_RECREATE` token. The copy is named per process, cluster, waiter call and attempt, because S3 upload keys use the basename alone; - at job end the script counts those tokens across the per-worker pytest logs, puts the count in `Result.info` and attaches the preserved logs, whatever the outcome. The failure-gated paths are left alone. A recreation is not itself a verdict, so only `info` and `files` are touched: status and labels stay as the test results set them, and the count is appended after the job's own `Failures: N/M` summary rather than replacing it. Forcing a retry on a healthy host passes, and the count reaches `result_*.json` with the 107,336 B broker log attached. The same run with the reporting removed attaches nothing; a run that never retried writes no count; a forced-red run keeps its `Failures: 1/1`. `test_system_stop.py` is 21 passed. Both sides are unit-tested, each arm checked against a mutation of the code it pins. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114947&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114947](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114947+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Support ROLLUP, CUBE, GROUPING SETS and grouping() with make_distributed_plan
signals.text: Support `ROLLUP`, `CUBE`, `GROUPING SETS` and the `grouping` function under `make_distributed_plan`. 11 of the 99 TPC-DS queries use `ROLLUP`. - `RollupStep` and `CubeStep` are serialized (query plan serialization version 8), so they can run in a worker stage, for example below a distributed `ORDER BY`. - The `grouping` function specializations held their parameters inside the function object and could not be serialized. The new analyzer now appends them as trailing constant arguments when it resolves `grouping`, and registered `__groupingFor*` resolvers rebuild the function from them, so a serialized plan carries the function by name and arguments alone. The old analyzer keeps constructing the functions directly; such plans are not serialized. - `GROUPING SETS` aggregation uses the partial-aggregation split, the same one the shard-based distributed path uses. `WITH TOTALS` and extremes remain unsupported. The distributed results of all new stateless tests are verified against non-distributed execution of the same queries. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Support `ROLLUP`, `CUBE`, `GROUPING SETS` and the `grouping` function in queries executed with `make_distributed_plan = 1`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114950&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114950](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114950+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix an unkillable hang when dropping a low-sorting-name TimeSeries table
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114259 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a hang when dropping a `TimeSeries` table whose name sorts lexicographically below its inner tables' names, for example `` DROP TABLE `-ts` `` or dropping a materialized view declared with `ENGINE = TimeSeries`. The drop self-deadlocked on the DDL guard and could not be cancelled with `KILL QUERY`. ### Description `DROP TABLE` of a `TimeSeries` table never returned and could not be killed when the table's own qualified name sorted below its inner tables' names: ```sql SET allow_experimental_time_series_table = 1; CREATE TABLE `-ts` ENGINE = TimeSeries; DROP TABLE `-ts`; -- hung forever ``` A materialized view's inner name is `.inner_id.<uuid>`, which always sorts below `.inner_id.metrics.<uuid>`, so dropping an `MV ... ENGINE = TimeSeries` hung too. **Root cause.** `executeDropQuery` takes the DDL guard for the inner table, then synthesizes an `ASTDropQuery` for that same table without setting `no_ddl_lock`, so the nested interpreter takes the guard for the identical name again. `DDLGuard::table_lock` wraps a non-recursive `std::mutex`, so the thread deadlocks against itself. A mutex wait is not a cancellation point, so `KILL QUERY` could not land and the guard stayed held for the server's lifetime. `need_ddl_guard = true` comes from one call site, `StorageTimeSeries::dropInnerTableIfAny`, which requests the inner guard only when the parent name sorts first. That predicate is correct and is kept: guards must be taken in increasing name order. Only its comment was wrong, claiming the inner name is "almost always less", which holds for `MaterializedView` but not `TimeSeries`. **The change.** `executeDropQuery` now sets `no_ddl_lock = need_ddl_guard`, so the inner name is guarded exactly once, by the caller, across the nested execute. `InterpreterCreateQuery` sets the same field for the same reason. The fix is inert for the other ten call sites, which all take the `need_ddl_guard = false` default. The `ddl_guard` null check is pre-existing hardening. **Validation.** Both shapes time out before the fix and succeed after, while a high-sorting-name control passes on both builds. Eight concurrent drops serialize and complete and the name is reusable afterwards, so the guard is still taken and released. New test `04920` covers both shapes and asserts no inner table is left behind.

signals.title: Apply a row policy to a read shipped as a serialized query plan
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112891 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a `SELECT` row policy on a shard-local table being ignored when the read is shipped to the executing replica as a serialized query plan (`serialize_query_plan = 1`, with `process_query_plan_packet` enabled there). Reads through a `Distributed` table with `prefer_localhost_replica = 0`, and reads over parallel replicas, returned rows the policy excludes. Closes #112891. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112891 **What breaks.** With a policy `USING y < 5` on a 10-row MergeTree table, `SELECT count()` through a `Distributed` table returns 10 instead of 5 and `SELECT DISTINCT y` returns 0..9. Parallel replicas leak the same way once remote replicas get read tasks. **Root cause.** The initiator resolves the policy into `SelectQueryInfo::row_level_filter`, since a MergeTree table accepts filter push-down into the read. When the plan is built for shipping, the leaf becomes a placeholder `ReadFromTableStep`, which has no field for that filter, so it is never serialized; on the executing node `replaceReadingFromTable` rebuilds the read with a hand-built `SelectQueryInfo` that never sets it. Each side assumes the other applied the policy. **The change.** Such a read is now rebuilt through the reconstructed-query path `resolveStorages` already uses for remote and `Merge` storages. That path runs the ordinary planner, so the policy is resolved in the executing node's own access context, and the read-column widening, the `FINAL` deferral and the PREWHERE ordering come with it. No wire format change and no version bump. Reads without a policy keep the direct path. The initiator cannot make this decision: effective policies resolve per node. **Residual, pre-existing and not introduced here.** A policy existing only on the receiver is still missed where the initiator pushes no policy into the read: storages without PREWHERE support (`Memory`, `View`) and those whose PREWHERE-column contract is not `nullopt` (`Buffer`, `File`, data lakes). Those behave exactly as on master. Replanning them would double-apply the filter step the initiator already shipped, and telling the two apart needs the plan to carry whether that step was emitted. So the fix assumes the shards behind one `Distributed` table use engines with the same PREWHERE contract. **Validation.** Three stateless tests (`Distributed`, parallel replicas, column grants), all failing on master. <details> <summary>Arms run on both binaries</summary> Measured on a debug build of base `63b0a472f4b62ac2` and of this branch. | arm | base | fix | |---|---|---| | `count()` / `sum(x)` / `sum(y)` / subquery, `serialize_query_plan = 1` | 10 / 45 / 45 / 10 | 5 / 10 / 10 / 5 | | `SELECT DISTINCT y` | 0..9 | 0..4 | | parallel replicas `sum(x)` / `count()` / `max(y)` | 548895757384 / 1046417 / 1111952 | correct on all three | | explicit `PREWHERE` + policy | 8 | 3 | | policy on `LowCardinality` / `Nullable` / `Array` / `ALIAS` / `MATERIALIZED` column | 10 each | matches the non-serialized result | | always-false policy | 10 | 0 | | `FINAL`, both `apply_row_policy_after_final` values | disagrees with the non-serialized path | agrees | | policy on `Memory` (push-down refused, must keep the direct path) | 5 | 5, and a nondeterministic policy is applied exactly once | | `additional_table_filters` on the read table, nondeterministic | applied once | applied once | | `additional_table_filters` on a table only the policy's subquery reads | n/a, policy not applied at all | applied, agreeing with `serialize_query_plan = 0` | | policy on the `Distributed` table itself | `ILLEGAL_PREWHERE` | same code and outcome; the message drops its now-stale `serialize_query_plan` advice | | `max_rows_to_read = 1` | returns 10 silently | `TOO_MANY_ROWS`, matching the non-serialized path | | no policy, `serialize_query_plan` 1 and 0 | 10 / 10 | 10 / 10 | Existing row-policy and serialized-plan tests pass unchanged, including `03743_apply_row_policy_after_final_safety`, `04652_prewhere_final_move_skipped_when_deferred`, `03006_parallel_replicas_prewhere` and `03302_analyzer_distributed_filter_push_down`. The new `Distributed` test is 50/50 stable under randomized settings. </details>

signals.title: Honour do_not_block_pipeline_on_failure for every non-ok job status
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107115 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109071 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description A job that sets `do_not_block_pipeline_on_failure` still blocked its whole downstream closure whenever it ended `ERROR` rather than `FAIL`. The two consumers disagreed. `hook_html.py:224` gates on `not result.is_ok()`, so dependees were correctly not marked `DROPPED`. `runner.py:910` gated on `result.is_failure()`, which is `FAIL`/`XPASS` only, so an `ERROR` was never exempted and the job emitted `pipeline_status=failure`. Every dependent job's guard is `!contains(needs.*.outputs.pipeline_status, 'failure')` over a transitive `needs`, so that one token skips the entire closure. The case that hits it: an integration shard exhausts its 7200 s parallel-phase budget and appends a synthetic `Timeout` child while every real test passes. One non-ok child means `force_ok_exit = True`, so the job declares itself non-blocking, but the same timeout sets the error flag and `set_error()` makes the status `ERROR`. That skipped 107 of 175 results on #107115 and 112 of 177 on #109071, including all five `Bugfix validation (*)` jobs. Because those never ran, `new_tests_check.py` read them as `PENDING` and failed `Finish Workflow` with "it's not actually a regression test for the fix", reporting a timeout in an unrelated shard as a verdict on the author's regression test. 8 occurrences across 8 PRs and 5 of the 6 shards in 30 days. `runner.py` now uses the same predicate as `hook_html`, extracted so it is reachable from a test. They have been asymmetric since the `runner.py` consumer was added in `b35b5fd41f28412`. `functional_tests.py:1527` passes the same flag after a path that can also end `ERROR`, so it is fixed by the same line. **Merge-blocking is unchanged.** `ready_for_merge` is computed from `job.allow_failure` alone (`native_jobs.py:1102-1117`) and never reads this flag; all six shards are `allow_failure=False`, so a failing shard still blocks the merge and still reports red. Only downstream dispatch changes. `new_tests_check.py` is left as it is: its strict check is correct once the jobs actually run. <details> <summary>Validation</summary> Every mutation below was applied to production code and the suite re-run. | arm | mutation | result | |---|---|---| | 0 | the fix | 45 passed | | A | predicate reverted to `is_failure()` (pre-fix behaviour) | 11 failed, incl. the end-to-end shard shape | | B | exemption made unconditional, flag ignored (negative control) | 14 failed (every `flag=False` row) | | C | `hook_html` predicate drifted to `is_failure()` | 1 failed (the agreement pin) | | D | output site re-derives the status inline, helper left unused | 1 failed (the delegation pin) | | E | merge gate made to read the flag | 1 failed (the merge-gate pin) | | F | emitted token hardcoded, or overridden after the call | 1 failed each (the emit pin) | Arm B is what rules out a vacuous oracle: a test that ignored the flag would stay green. Arms D, E and F each redden exactly one test, pinning the seams nothing else covers: the call site the extraction created, the token actually emitted, and the merge computation the paragraph above rests on. The new test parametrizes every non-ok member of `Result.Status` (`FAIL`, `ERROR`, `XPASS`, `DROPPED`, `UNKNOWN`, `PENDING`, `RUNNING`) and all three ok members against flag on/off, asserts the two consumers reach the same verdict, reproduces the measured production shape (903 `OK` + 17 `SKIPPED` + 1 `Timeout`), and pins `allow_failure=False` on the six shards. Full `ci/tests`: 972 passed / 31 skipped / 8 failed with the fix, versus 927 / 31 / 8 on pristine `runner.py`. The same 8 pre-existing environment failures on both arms (`clickhouse was not found in PATH`); the delta is the new tests. Exactly two production `complete_job(` call sites pass this flag, and both are covered by this one line. The only other writer of `pipeline_status` is the config job's unconditional `success`. The remaining `is_failure()` uses are test-level row filtering or rendering, not job-level gating. </details>

signals.title: Bound the waits in 02932_refreshable_materialized_views_1 and report refresh state on expiry
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/105987 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/105987 Requested by @ alexey-milovidov in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/105987#issuecomment-5302349211, after a private-sync run of `Stateless tests (amd_asan_ubsan, distributed cache, meta in keeper, s3 storage, parallel, 2/2)` hung in this test with the active query `select * from rmv_a order by x`. ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description **The problem.** Every wait in this test is an unbounded loop with no deadline and no diagnostic, and some predicates can never become true: the first waits for a refresh to succeed, but with `refresh every 2 second` a failing refresh retries forever, so the predicate never holds and the `exception` column that says why is never read. The test just times out, naming nothing. `-- $LINENO` was also single-quoted at two of the three sites emitting `select * from rmv_a order by x`, and the third had no marker, so the one query a report can quote was untraceable. **The change.** One `wait_for` helper for all ten client-side waits and the unguarded read. Each poll is capped by the budget remaining, a failing client fails the wait rather than being retried as a mismatch, and on expiry the test prints the awaited query, expected and actual values, why the wait expired and `system.view_refreshes` including `exception`, then exits 1. All three `order by x` sites now carry a line number. I bound every wait, not just the two loops I first offered on that thread: the observed hangs pin lines 42, 91 and 145. One wait costs at most 30s (20s polling, then SIGKILL grace and the bounded dump), inside the 60s Fast test cap, against a slowest measured wait of 2.65s on ASAN. It bounds one wait, not the script, since the harness timer is per-test. `SYSTEM WAIT VIEW` is left alone: `RefreshTask::wait` has no deadline and no cancellation check, so bounding it client-side would park a server thread. **Validation.** With a failing refresh armed, the test previously spun silently until killed; it now reports in 20s with the pinned line and the exception. Passing-path stdout is byte-identical to the unchanged `.reference`; 50/50 runs pass on debug and ASAN.

signals.title: Do not regenerate part names from part infos for tables with the deprecated syntax
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/87206 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/103537 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112457 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `BAD_DATA_PART_NAME` ("Trying to get part name in new format for old format version") on a `ReplicatedMergeTree` created with the deprecated positional syntax under `allow_deprecated_syntax_for_merge_tree`. A mutation could be reported as done on a replica that had not applied it, and the table could stay readonly after a restart. ### Description Reported by @ alexey-milovidov on #112457 ([`Upgrade check (amd_release)` report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112457&sha=f888781eb610bfabdc8c8675d835b99482bec8a2&name_0=PR&name_1=Upgrade%20check%20%28amd_release%29)). No related open issue found. A table created with `ENGINE = ReplicatedMergeTree(date, key, granularity)` uses date-based (V0) part names. `MergeTreePartInfo::getPartNameAndCheckFormat` cannot produce one, because the min/max dates it needs are not part of a `MergeTreePartInfo`, so it throws. Two `ActiveDataPartSet` entry points take only an info and regenerate the name that way; each had exactly one caller, and both callers already held the name and threw it away. This change passes the name at both call sites, as in `536b611c96a757e`, which fixed the `ATTACH PARTITION` instance of this bug. V0 name formatting is untouched, and current-format tables are unaffected because the name-taking overload re-parses to the same info and runs the same insertion code. The linked report contains both failures: - `ReplicatedMergeTreeQueue::getPartNamesToMutate` builds `mutation.parts_to_do`. The throw left it empty, so a mutation reported `is_done` on a replica that never mutated its part, and `mutations_sync = 2` returned success while that replica still served pre-mutation values. Regressed by #87206, which changed `produced_parts` to hold infos instead of names. - `StorageReplicatedMergeTree::checkPartsImpl` builds the set of empty unexpected parts. The throw aborted `ReplicatedMergeTreeAttachThread`, leaving the table readonly. Regressed by my own #103537, which replaced a name-based call with an info-based one. The V0 gap in `MergeTreeData::restorePartFromBackup` that the throw-site comment describes is a different code path, absent from both stacks, and is not addressed. A new stateless test asserts `parts_to_do` on the frozen replica: it fails on master (`parts to do 0`) and passes here (`parts to do 2`), and 50/50 randomized runs pass. `checkPartsImpl`'s state needs parts fabricated on disk, so that half is covered by three V0 cases added to `gtest_active_data_part_set.cpp`, all of which fail with this change reverted. `00062_replicated_merge_tree_alter_zookeeper_long` and `00652_replicated_mutations_zookeeper` still pass.

signals.title: Do not drop the whole GROUP BY when unwrapping injective functions of constants
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/104863 (same logical error, closed earlier without this cause identified) ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix wrong results for a `GROUP BY` whose only key is an injective function of constants, for example `SELECT 1 FROM t GROUP BY materialize(NULL)`. Such a key was removed by `optimize_injective_functions_in_group_by`, which left the query with no `GROUP BY` and no aggregation at all, so it returned one row per input row instead of one row per group. Over a `Merge` table that mixes a local and a remote child the same cause also raised the logical error `Chunk info was not set for chunk in GroupingAggregatedTransform`. ### Description `unwrapInjectiveFunctionsInKeys` unwraps an injective function to its arguments and skips constant arguments, so a key that is an injective function *of a constant* unwraps to nothing and is dropped. `OptimizeGroupByInjectiveFunctionsPass` assigned that result unconditionally: when such a key was the only one and the query had no aggregate function, `GROUP BY` became empty and the query stopped aggregating. Under a `Merge` table mixing a child that aggregates with one that does not, the un-aggregated child's raw chunks reach a merge transform that requires aggregate state; both wordings of the message occur, `GroupingAggregatedTransform` and `MergingAggregatedTransform`, depending on `distributed_aggregation_memory_efficient`, and one fix closes both. Found by the fuzzers, e.g. [AST fuzzer (amd_debug)](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=94148&sha=8eb1df1331f7fd5dcf93b4b0e975e56685b6f732&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%29). The fix assigns the unwrapped list only when it is non-empty, which is what `OptimizeLimitByInjectiveFunctionsPass` already does for `LIMIT BY` and what the non-analyzer `TreeOptimizer::optimizeGroupBy` does via `appendUnusedGroupByColumn`. Of those three sibling paths only the analyzer's `GROUP BY` pass lacked the guard. The shared helper is unchanged, so `LIMIT BY` is unaffected. A per-key variant was deliberately not used: it would weaken the optimization when another key survives, and it is the branch added in 462445c2c201a5f and removed the next day in 355909eb3a415b7. `GROUP BY materialize(NULL), k` still groups by `k` alone. Affected queries now return a different row count, which is the point of the fix. Across 25 shapes the patched default is byte-identical to running with `optimize_injective_functions_in_group_by = 0`, where before it diverged on 7 of them; `enable_analyzer = 0` and a plain `GROUP BY NULL` key agree. The old behaviour stays reachable with that setting. The new test fails on master and passes here.
signals.author: groeneai

signals.title: Fix logical error for IN with an identical non-constant tuple on both sides in the old analyzer
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Description Found by the AST fuzzer, `AST fuzzer (arm_asan_ubsan)`, STID 2508-3457: ```sql EXPLAIN PIPELINE graph = 0, graph = 0, compact = 1 SELECT 'null', (SELECT tuple(materialize(NULL), NULL) GLOBAL IN (materialize(NULL), NULL)) GROUP BY ALL SETTINGS transform_null_in = 1 ``` Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=111552&sha=38215c1758332de1ea8a4b5a620ba8364586f6c6&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28arm_asan_ubsan%29 It reaches the old interpreter through a scalar subquery, and reduces to `SELECT (materialize(1), 2) IN (materialize(1), 2) SETTINGS enable_analyzer = 0`. Release builds catch the exception but still reject the query with an empty identifier name: `Code: 47 ... Unknown identifier: ; there are columns: dummy, 1, materialize(1), 2, ...`. Root cause: a literal's `unique_column_name` is assigned lazily, only when `ActionsMatcher::visit(const ASTLiteral &)` runs, and `getNameAndTypeFromAST` requires it. The old interpreter's row-wise `IN` rewrite visits the left argument first, and here the right-hand `tuple` renders to the same column name as the left one, so `visit(right_argument, data)` takes the common-subexpression early return and never descends into the right-hand children. The loop that follows then asks for the name and type of each raw child, and a literal child is still unnamed. The fix visits each child before naming it. That call site was the only one of the eight `getNameAndTypeFromAST` callers in the file not already preceded by a `visit()` of the node it names. `visit` is idempotent, so the added call is a no-op when the child is already indexed. The abort is gone after the change, with the result now matching `enable_analyzer = 1` on 20 shapes (including `NULL` with `transform_null_in`, `nullIn`, `GLOBAL IN`, `LowCardinality`, array and tuple literal children, `indexHint`, and the query above). 13 shapes that already worked are unchanged, with byte-identical `EXPLAIN actions = 1` output. Removing the added line reinstates the abort. Introduced by #104993 and present only on master, so no backport is needed. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104993
signals.author: groeneai

signals.title: Fix data race and silent data loss on the object-storage path list
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/90967 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed silent data loss when several `INSERT`s run concurrently into one non-partitioned `s3`, `azure` or `hdfs` table with `s3_create_new_file_on_insert = 1` or its per-storage equivalent, once the base object exists: the writers could derive the same new file name and overwrite each other's rows with no error. Also fixed the data race on the shared path list caused by the same sequence. ### Description Found by `La Casa Del Dolor (amd_tsan)`, STID `3437-4fb8`, on an unrelated PR: [report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=94148&sha=8eb1df1331f7fd5dcf93b4b0e975e56685b6f732&name_0=PR&name_1=La%20Casa%20Del%20Dolor%20%28amd_tsan%29), [log](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/PRs/94148/8eb1df1331f7fd5dcf93b4b0e975e56685b6f732/la_casa_del_dolor_amd_tsan/stderr0.log) `StorageObjectStorage::write()` read the configuration's path list, derived the next file name from it and published the result, unsynchronized. The configuration is created once per table and shared by every query, so two INSERT pipelines ran that sequence on one vector, which ThreadSanitizer reported in `std::vector::operator=`. The race is only the visible half. The new name is `<base>.<N>`, N from the length of the list the caller was handed, so the list is the name allocator: two concurrent INSERTs derive the same name, find it free, and open it with `WriteMode::Rewrite`, so one writer's rows silently replace the other's. With eight writers, two of nine rows survived. Fix: the concurrency moves into the class owning the state. `getPaths`/`setPaths` become non-virtual base methods taking a shared mutex and delegating to protected `*Impl` virtuals, so all five subclasses and the twelve `DataLakeConfiguration` instantiations inherit it, and `getPaths()` returns by value, since a reference into mutex-protected state protects nothing. Allocate-derive-publish becomes `allocatePathForWrite()` under a second, writer-only mutex, keeping the existence probes off the list's lock so a slow remote request cannot stall `SELECT`s. Three cases are left, so they are not mistaken for fixed: with no base object yet, nothing is reserved and both writers use the base path; wildcard-partitioned writes derive their name in the sink, so writers into one partition can still collide; and two `INSERT INTO FUNCTION s3(...)` queries build a configuration each, so there is no shared list. All three need an in-flight reservation, not a lock, as creating a sink creates no object to probe for. The new tests fail on master and pass 50/50 with the fix.

signals.title: Fix reading a tuple element through a positional Tuple structure hint
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114991 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114991 Reading a tuple element through a positional structure hint returned default values instead of the file's data. Over a Parquet file written as `t Tuple(x UInt64, y String)`: ```sql SELECT tupleElement(t, 1) FROM file('p.parquet', Parquet, 't Tuple(UInt64, String)'); -- returned 0, 0, 0 instead of 0, 1, 2 ``` `WHERE tupleElement(t, 1) = 1` matched no rows, and with `input_format_parquet_allow_missing_columns = 0` the query failed with `THERE_IS_NO_COLUMN`. Silent wrong results, on default settings. Root cause: an unnamed tuple names its elements `1`, `2`, ..., so `optimize_functions_to_subcolumns` rewrote `tupleElement(t, 1)` to the subcolumn `t.1`. The existing guards there consult the storage snapshot, which is built from the structure argument and does contain `t.1`. The Parquet reader then resolves a flattened element name by string against the file's real field names `t.x`, `t.y`, found no match, and substituted a missing column filled with defaults. The fix suppresses the rewrite when the element name is a bare ordinal and the source resolves subcolumn names against a file schema. Named hints keep their pushdown, and storages serving subcolumns from their own metadata (MergeTree and friends) are unaffected. This regressed in #113383 and is master-only: that merge is an ancestor of no release branch and is in no release tag, hence `Not for changelog`. That category also skips `Bugfix validation`, so the reddening check below is the evidence. Validated on a Debug build, with a regression arm added to `04706_tuple_subcolumn_pushdown_parquet`: - Reddening: removing only the new guard term makes the new arm fail while the pre-existing arms stay green. - Preservation: `t.x` pushdown survives for a named hint by name and by ordinal, and `t.1` still pushes down for MergeTree's unnamed tuple. - `04706`, `04707`, `04708`, `04873` pass; a `subcolumn`/`tuple_element`/`functions_to_subcolumns` sweep has no failure absent from an unmodified-master control; 50 randomized runs pass.

signals.title: Support `Merge` tables with plan-based parallel replicas
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/67770 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110972 Lets a `Merge` table be read with parallel replicas, implemented on top of the plan-based parallel replicas (`parallel_replicas_plan_based`). `ReadFromMerge` is opaque to the parallel-replicas plan transformation: it unites the pipelines of its per-table subplans instead of their plans, so the underlying `MergeTree` reads do not exist yet while the plan is transformed. An eligible `ReadFromMerge` is therefore expanded into a plan-level `UnionStep` over those child reads, right before the reads to distribute are collected. A `Merge` then has exactly the shape the transformation already distributes - a union of `MergeTree` reads - so the reads are coordinated across the replicas, and the steps above the `Merge` (aggregation, joins) are distributed as well, without any `Merge`-specific code in the coordinator, in the serialization or in the local plan. The expansion is off by default, gated by the new setting `parallel_replicas_allow_merge_tables`, and takes effect only together with `parallel_replicas_plan_based`. A `Merge` is read by a single replica when one of its children is not a plain `MergeTree` read, when the read is `FINAL`, or when no table matches its regexp. This is an alternative to https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110972, which implements the same feature on the legacy (query-tree-based) path. There, the query text is reshipped and every replica re-analyzes it, which needs a fail-close handshake (`parallel_replicas_designated_table`, `_freshness_checked_tables`, `_merge_child_tables`) to guard against the set of underlying tables differing across replicas or changing between planning and reading. The plan-based path ships a serialized plan fragment with the tables already resolved, so none of that is needed. Tests: three new stateless tests - the core feature and its negative cases (`04907`), the query shapes a `Merge` can be read with, including the `merge` table function, a filter on the `_table` virtual column and reading in order with a limit (`04908`), and `Merge` tables inside JOINs on either side of the join (`04909`). Each of them checks the results against non-parallel execution and asserts through the plan how the query was distributed. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): A `Merge` table can now be read with parallel replicas: the reads from the underlying `MergeTree` tables are coordinated across the replicas, and the aggregations and joins above them are distributed too. Enabled by the new setting `parallel_replicas_allow_merge_tables`, which takes effect together with `parallel_replicas_plan_based`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115001&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115001](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115001+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix a lambda argument taking the type of a table column with the same name
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/103584 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/103627 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes `LOGICAL_ERROR: Unexpected return type from FunctionExpression` when a higher-order function in `PREWHERE` has a lambda parameter named after a table column of a different type and the body reads that column before the parameter. The parameter took the column's type. A parameter whose name is also a generated expression name in the body is not covered. ### Description A lambda parameter named after a table column takes the column's type when the body reads the column first: ```sql CREATE TABLE t (v UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); INSERT INTO t SELECT 10 UNION ALL SELECT 20; SELECT v FROM t PREWHERE arrayExists(v -> (t.v != 0) AND (v = 7), [toNullable(toUInt64(7))]) ORDER BY v; -- Code: 49. Unexpected return type from FunctionExpression. Expected Nullable(UInt8). Got UInt8. ``` Renaming the parameter, or swapping the `AND` operands, returns `10, 20`. Reproduced on master 26.8.1.1454; debug builds abort. Found by the AST fuzzer, STID 2458-5396: [report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114721&sha=39164d61335228645d86f6613ff2bb2bfff00280&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%2C%20old_compatibility%29). Root cause: `ActionsScopeNode::addInputColumnIfNecessary` is a name-keyed get-or-create, called by `visitColumn` with the unqualified name (`use_column_identifier_as_action_node_name` is false in `PREWHERE`, mutations and `Merge`). The first visitor to reach the lambda scope decides its type. With the column first, the argument's INPUT takes the column's type, so the body yields `UInt8` while the declared return type stays `Nullable(UInt8)`. #103627 fixes the capture name, but runs later. Fix: before visiting the body, declare the arguments the body reads as a column as INPUTs of the lambda scope, so the name-keyed lookup finds them. The old interpreter does this in `ScopeStack::pushLevel`, so `enable_analyzer = 0` is unaffected. One scope map is shared by all node kinds, so the declaration is narrow: a candidate is matched through the same `calculateActionNodeName` the visitor uses, and a name bound by another lambda, or computed by the body, is left alone. A parameter whose name is also a generated expression name in the body is not covered, and still fails as on master. Validation: `arrayExists`, `arrayMap`, a `tuple()` body, nested lambdas, `LowCardinality(String)` and the inverted case failed before and pass now; `EXPLAIN actions = 1` is unchanged elsewhere.

signals.title: Anchor the Build profile diff master baseline windows on the run's own event
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `Build profile diff` fails closed with `No master baseline with build profile data found - cannot compare` when CI is re-run days after it was triggered, even though the baseline rows are present. Failing run: [PR #113672 @ `494760825`](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113672&sha=494760825526a945d48dd1b90c9965dfd8721df9&name_0=PR&name_1=Build%20profile%20diff). `find_baseline` intersects two sets measured from different origins: the candidates are the frozen first-parent chain of the head's master parent (`master_track_commits_sha`, chain relative), while the row filter was `date >= today() - BASE_DAYS` (wall-clock relative). A re-run replays the frozen event payload, so the chain stays anchored on the old merge base while `today()` moves on, and once the gap exceeds `BASE_DAYS` the intersection is empty by construction. On the run above, `created_at` is `2026-08-06T13:03:49Z` against a `run_started_at` of `2026-08-16T01:28:41Z`: ten days, seven-day window. Eight more sites share the mismatch, so fixing only `find_baseline` relocates the error. Every master-side window now derives from `info.event_time`, frozen with the event, as a closed interval `[anchor - N, min(anchor + 4 days, today)]`. The first-parent walk takes the same anchor and stops a whole upload day further back, so the chain it returns is a superset of what those windows can match. Closed rather than half-open because `date` leads the primary key of the profile tables: the width is then fixed however old the event is, so the window slides rather than grows. The upper bound allows for profiles uploaded after their commit, measured at 4 hours p99 and 85 hours max over 673 master `arm_release` builds. Pull request side windows keep `today() - PR_DAYS`: those rows are uploaded by the run itself. An anchor at today emits the same windows as before, a local run keeps the wall-clock ones, and both fail-closes stand. Driving the job with that run's real values reproduces the error on the current module and resolves the baseline here. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1528` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Do not alias pre-aggregation states of a zero-size aggregate in arrayReduceInRanges
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108781 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108781 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `arrayReduceInRanges` over an array whose elements are all NULL aborts a debug or sanitizer build with `Logical error: 'IAggregateFunction::merge called with the same source and destination state'`: ```sql SELECT arrayReduceInRanges('groupArray', [(1, 64)], arrayMap(x -> (x + NULL), range(64))); ``` Found by the AST fuzzer: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114747&sha=95a67283e1b33c000dba21cddefcd4418c4a2c94&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29 An all-NULL argument collapses the aggregate to `AggregateFunctionNothing`, whose `sizeOfData()` is 0. `Arena::alignedAlloc` advances the arena by `size`, so every zero-byte allocation returns the same address. The function allocates one pre-aggregation state per 64 rows plus one state per range from a single arena, so all of those states alias and both the pairwise level merge and the per-range merge become `merge(p, p)`. The fix allocates `max(sizeOfData(), 1)` bytes for the pre-aggregation states, so they are distinct and every merge still runs. The per-range state needs no padding: that merge only runs when the range spans a whole 64-row block, which is also the condition for a pre-aggregation state to exist, and its one-byte allocation has already advanced the arena. For an aggregate with a non-empty state the allocation is byte-identical to before. I deliberately did not suppress the merge for zero-size states. `sizeOfData() == 0` does not imply that merging is a no-op: `StatelessWindowFunction` is also zero-size and its `mergeImpl` throws. Since the aggregate is caller-supplied, a genuinely empty state cannot be told apart from one whose merge enforces a contract, so skipping the call could drop that enforcement. Two further places with the same allocation pattern are left alone. `ColumnAggregateFunction` can hold zero-size states (the test builds one via `nothingState`) but its `insertMergeFrom` merges across two different arenas. The `Aggregator` merge paths have one reported sighting of the sibling assertion (`mergeAndDestroyBatch`, on #111459) that 15 probes did not reproduce. Release behaviour is unchanged - the assertion compiles out and `Nothing::mergeImpl` is empty.

signals.title: Commit the recorded file sizes of a Log family write atomically
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/101796 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed an `INSERT` into a `Log`, `TinyLog` or `StripeLog` table that fails while committing the recorded file sizes. Such an insert could keep its rows in the table even though it reported an error, or leave the data files of an array column inconsistent with each other. Reading a `Log` or `TinyLog` table whose array column holds no elements while its offsets claim some now raises an error naming the column instead of reading past the end of the elements. A partially written elements column was already rejected. ### Description **The write commit was not atomic.** `StorageLog::saveFileSizes` recorded each stream's size separately, and each `FileChecker::update` does IO that can throw. A throw partway through left new sizes for some streams and old ones for the rest. The insert had not finished, so the sink destructor calls `FileChecker::repair`, which truncates every file to its recorded size, leaving adjacent streams of one array column at different generations: the outer offsets then described more elements than the inner ones held. A throw inside `save` instead left the files appended but the sizes unchanged, so a failed insert kept its rows. `FileChecker::updateAndSave` now collects the sizes into a candidate map, persists it, and adopts it only on success. `StorageStripeLog` is fixed likewise. The marks file is one of the recorded files, so a rollback truncates it while `num_marks_saved` stayed advanced, leaving in-memory marks that `removeUnsavedMarks` would not trim. The counter is now restored when the size commit fails, on both the insert and restore paths. **Reads no longer trust inconsistent array streams.** `LogSource::readData` already checked the deserialized column's type; it now also checks at every nesting level that the last offset matches the element count, raising `INCORRECT_DATA` naming the column. A short but non-empty elements column was already rejected with `CANNOT_READ_ALL_DATA`, so the empty case is the one that reached the pipeline and the one this check catches. I found the first defect while investigating a `ColumnArray::indexImpl` assertion failure in `BuzzHouse (amd_tsan)` (STID 2508-2944, [report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=101796&sha=628da3c387736525f6398b025afb900437a4f11a&name_0=PR&name_1=BuzzHouse%20%28amd_tsan%29)), where a sort indexed an array column whose offsets claimed more elements than it held. How that table reached the state is still unknown: the failing run's log shows no truncation by `repair`, so this commit path is not shown to have produced it. That is why the read side is hardened too. <details> <summary>Validation</summary> `tests/queries/0_stateless/04931_log_family_insert_commit_rollback.sh` covers the write half over `Log`, `TinyLog` and `StripeLog` and both failure windows, using two failpoints conditioned so they fire on the commit at the end of the insert and not on the empty baseline commit the sink makes when it starts. Reverting either half of the fix reddens it, with distinct symptoms: reverting the atomic commit aborts on `Invalid number of rows in Chunk`, while reverting only the counter restore leaves the table reporting 180 rows where 140 were written. `tests/integration/test_storage_log_damaged_array/` covers the read half for `Log` and `TinyLog`, over three damage shapes: a missing inner offsets stream, which the top-level check catches; a missing leaf elements stream, which only the recursion into nested levels catches; and a partially written elements stream, which fails earlier with `CANNOT_READ_ALL_DATA`. Deleting the recursion leaves the first and third passing and reddens the second. It edits the data files directly, so it cannot be a functional test. The new check was run against 1405 existing tests over `log`, `tinylog`, `stripelog`, `nested`, `array`, `object` and `json`; it did not fire once on data written normally. </details>

signals.title: Give Poco::Net::SocketAddress a noexcept move constructor
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110479 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Appending to a system log queue no longer deep-copies the whole queue when it grows. `Poco::Net::SocketAddress` had no move constructor, which made `QueryLogElement` and three other element types not nothrow-move-constructible, so a `std::vector` reallocation copied every element (allocating per address) while the queue mutex was held, blocking every query that writes to `system.query_log`. ### Description Found while investigating a server that accepted and planned queries but executed none for 3.5 minutes on `Stateless tests (amd_tsan, flaky check)`: [CI report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110479&sha=038667a9c024695126415fe5f37b76f7a06662fa&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_tsan%2C%20flaky%20check%29). The sampling profiler shows one thread inside `SystemLogQueue<QueryLogElement>::push` for 177 of 181 seconds, in `vector::__emplace_back_slow_path`, with 31 threads blocked on `std::mutex::lock()` in the same call. `push()` appends under `mutex`, so a `std::vector` reallocation happens in the critical section. libc++ relocates with `std::move_if_noexcept`, which falls back to **copying** every element when the type is not nothrow-move-constructible. `QueryLogElement` was not, for one reason: `Poco::Net::SocketAddress` declared copy operations only, and its copy heap-allocates a new `SocketAddressImpl`. `ClientInfo` holds three of those. The fix belongs in Poco because that is where the cause is: a refcounted-pointer wrapper whose move is nothing but a pointer transfer. The moves of `ClientInfo` and the log elements stay implicit, so their trait is derived. `AutoPtr::swap` is used because `AutoPtr` also declares no move, so assignment would bump the refcount and leave the source non-null. Measured over one reallocation of 8192 elements: 32769 allocations before, 1 after. Four element types were affected (`QueryLog`, `QueryThreadLog`, `SessionLog`, `ZooKeeperLog`); a `static_assert` in `SystemLogQueue` now enumerates every element type at build time (30 here, 32 in a cloud build) and fails on the unpatched tree. A moved-from `SocketAddress` has a null `_pImpl`; all seven accessors already route through `pImpl()`, which throws `NullPointerException`, so that state stays defined. Left out deliberately: the slow `query_log` flush that triggered the reallocation is a separate question, and a move on `Poco::AutoPtr` would be the broader fix. This is one mechanism proven on one artifact, not a claim about every `Server died` report. No SQL test, because a C++ relocation trait is not observable from SQL.

signals.title: Read all summed columns for SELECT FINAL from SummingMergeTree
signals.text: `SELECT ... FINAL` from a `SummingMergeTree` table returned wrong results when the query read only a subset of the columns of the summation. A merge removes a row when the values in **all** of the columns of the summation are zero after summing. The FINAL read applied the same rule, but only over the columns the query happened to read. Two ways to misbehave follow from that: - A query reading a subset of the summed columns removed every group whose visible columns summed to zero, even though an unread summed column made the row survive a real merge — rows silently disappeared. The most common victim is bare `count()`, which reads a single smallest column (plus the internally added sorting key): on a table `(c0 Int8, c1 Int32, c3 UInt64) ENGINE = SummingMergeTree ORDER BY c3` with two overlapping parts where `c0` sums to zero for some keys, `SELECT count() FROM t FINAL` returned 10 instead of 15, and `SELECT c0, c3 FROM t FINAL` lost the same 5 rows. - A query reading none of the summed columns (e.g. only the sorting key) never removed anything, keeping rows that a real merge deletes. The fix always includes all columns that a merge would aggregate into the FINAL read set (and into the set protected from plan-level column pruning), so the removal decision is taken over the same set of columns as in a real merge. This makes `SELECT ... FINAL` agree with `OPTIMIZE TABLE ... FINAL` followed by a plain `SELECT`. Note that queries over `SummingMergeTree FINAL` that previously read a subset of the summed columns now read all of them, which is the price of the correct result. Found by the nightly SQLancer `FinalMerge` oracle (`SELECT count() FROM t0 FINAL` returned 9947 before `OPTIMIZE TABLE t0 FINAL` and 9999 after it on the same data): https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=5c9f28ed5a2c585ad46bf74d6600cdcf3aa07a9e&name_0=NightlySQLancer&name_1=SQLancer%20%28arm_asan_ubsan%29&name_1=SQLancer ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix wrong results of `SELECT ... FINAL` from `SummingMergeTree` when the query reads only a subset of the columns of the summation: the decision to remove a row whose sums are all zero is now taken over all columns of the summation, as in a real merge, instead of only the columns the query reads. Previously, rows could silently disappear from the result (for example, `SELECT count() FROM table FINAL`). ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115032&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115032](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115032+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix an adaptive aggregator abort on lazily replicated columns
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111459 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `Aggregator::sealPendingChunks` coalesces several staged mini-chunks into one, concatenating each aggregate argument column across the minis. It clones the destination from the first source and then calls `prepareForSquashing` and `insertRangeFrom`, both of which `assert_cast` every source to the destination's class. That assumes all minis share one physical representation per position. They do not. Lazy column replication is decided per block: a join materializes a block whose replication does not grow the output and leaves the others wrapped in `ColumnReplicated` (`HashJoinResult.cpp`), so one stream legitimately mixes wrapped and dense blocks for the same column. `recursiveRemoveSparse` in the staging path deliberately preserves the wrapper, so the mix reaches the seal and the cast aborts: ``` Logical error: 'Bad cast from type DB::ColumnReplicated to DB::ColumnVector<unsigned long>' Received signal Aborted (6) ``` Two sites abort, both reproduced locally: `insertRangeFrom` for the numeric vectors, which do not override `prepareForSquashing` (the signature above), and `prepareForSquashing` itself for String, Nullable, Array, Map, Tuple, Variant, Dynamic and Object. The fix normalizes the whole `sources` vector, including the front, before the destination is cloned, so one gate covers both sites and destination and sources stay drawn from the same normalized set. The `structureEquals` gate keeps the homogeneous case allocation-free, so lazy replication keeps its benefit where it is uniform, and mirrors what `Squashing.cpp` already does for the identical hazard. Reachable from ordinary SQL: a `JOIN` feeding a `GROUP BY` with `enable_adaptive_aggregator = 1` and `enable_lazy_columns_replication = 1`, both defaults. In a release build `assert_cast` degrades to `static_cast`, so the same input reads a `ColumnReplicated` through a `ColumnVector` layout and copies from a bogus data pointer instead of failing loudly. `AdaptiveAggregation.cpp` was added by #111459 and is on no release branch, so no backport applies. Found by CI in `Stress test (arm_msan)` on an unrelated pull request: [report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110838&sha=db62fd0ad673a4eaf5411e8b75df5b1750bdcb93&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_msan%29), [fatal.log](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/PRs/110838/db62fd0ad673a4eaf5411e8b75df5b1750bdcb93/stress_test_arm_msan/fatal.log). <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1525` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Fix out-of-bounds read in pointInPolygon on an unbounded bounding box
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/11375 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/11375 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed an out-of-bounds read in `pointInPolygon` with a constant polygon whose bounding box is unbounded, for example when a coordinate reaches `+-DBL_MAX`. Such a polygon is now rejected with `BAD_ARGUMENTS`, and a polygon with an empty ring is treated as having no interior. Previously the query could return a wrong result, or abort the server in builds with hardening or sanitizers enabled. ### Description `SELECT pointInPolygon((1e308, 1.), [(-1.7976931348623157e308, 0.), (1.7976931348623157e308, 0.), (0., 2.)])` reads a `cells` element out of range, on default settings and with no elevated privileges. With libc++ hardening or a sanitizer it aborts (`vector[] index out of bounds`); otherwise it switches on a garbage cell type. Found by the targeted AST fuzzer: [report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112930&sha=27e32067e2142071df32a1cd106e533e54ae645e&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29) (the carrier PR is unrelated to this code). **Root cause.** `calcGridAttributes` validated the derived scales for finiteness but tested the bounding-box span only for `== 0`. `1 / +-inf` is `+-0.0`, which is finite, so an infinite span passed validation; `contains` then computed `inf * 0.0 = NaN`, which compared false against both range guards, `static_cast<int>(NaN)` gave `INT_MIN`, and the cell index overflowed. **Change.** Classify the span where it is computed: non-positive means no interior (`has_empty_bound`), non-finite is rejected with `BAD_ARGUMENTS`. Six lines in the only writer of the grid scales, so every reader is covered at once. `<= 0` rather than `!(span > 0)` keeps a NaN span throwing, as it does today. **Scope.** Only the preprocessed grid used for constant polygons is changed. A non-constant polygon column takes the on-the-fly ray-casting path, which builds no grid and cannot reach this out-of-bounds read; it does lose precision on an unbounded span (`inf/inf` in the edge formula), a separate pre-existing issue deliberately left alone here. **Validation.** Measured against pristine HEAD. Three carriers stop aborting: the wide polygon above, an empty ring, and an empty ring inside a multipolygon (which tripped a boost R-tree assertion). A fourth, an unbounded span on the y axis, silently returned **wrong** answers (`1` where an affine analogue proves `0`). Wide but finite polygons (`1e200`) keep their results. 3 existing tests extended, each verified to fail before the change; the `polygon` suite is green. <details> <summary>Behavior matrix (pristine HEAD vs this PR)</summary> `01940_point_in_polygon_ubsan` changes expectation from `0` to `BAD_ARGUMENTS`: its polygon has an `inf` vertex, so the span is now rejected before `contains` runs, where its `0` came from the query point guard. That guard stays covered by `00500_point_in_polygon_nan`. | statement | settings | HEAD | this PR | |---|---|---|---| | `(1e308,1.)` vs `[(-M,0.),(M,0.),(0.,2.)]` | default | abort | `BAD_ARGUMENTS` | | same, multipolygon / with a hole | default | abort | `BAD_ARGUMENTS` | | empty ring, large point | `validate_polygons=0` | abort | `0` | | `[[[]]]` multipolygon | `validate_polygons=0` | boost assertion | `0` | | y-unbounded `[(0.,-M),(1.,M),(2.,0.)]`, `(1.,-1e308)` | `validate_polygons=0` | **`1` (wrong)** | `BAD_ARGUMENTS` | | NaN span `[(inf,0.),(inf,0.1),(inf,0.2)]` | `validate_polygons=0` | `BAD_ARGUMENTS` | `BAD_ARGUMENTS` | | `1e200` span, `(0.,1.)` / `(1e199,0.5)` | default | `1` / `1` | `1` / `1` | | zero span, point polygon | `validate_polygons=0` | `0` | `0` | | issue #11375 NaN-point repro | default | `0` | `0` | `M = 1.7976931348623157e308`. </details> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1524` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->
