signals.title: Do not treat an unaccounted skip-index file as a materialized index
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109595 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104431 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a query failure on a part that carries both a `skp_idx.packed` archive and a leftover standalone skip-index file with no `checksums.txt` entry. The leftover file was counted as a materialized index, so a valid query was rejected with a `file_size` filesystem error. ### Description Reported on https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104431#issuecomment-5306256247, on the corrupted-part shape of https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109595 `indexFileExistsInChecksums` says whether a skip-index substream is materialized in a part. When the part carried `skp_idx.packed` it fell through to `storage->existsFile`, which tries the archive and then does a raw disk stat, and that one answer served two callers needing different ones. A read-time probe must not accept a file that neither `checksums.txt` nor the archive accounts for: it is an orphan, its index already dead, and counting it as materialized fails a valid query with `Code: 1001 ... in file_size: No such file or directory`. Mutation cleanup does need the wider answer, to strip the orphan from inherited checksums and keep it out of the hardlink loop; narrowing it there leaks the stale file forward and `CHECK TABLE` fails with `UNEXPECTED_FILE_IN_DATA_PART`. Each caller now asks by mode. One behaviour delta: read-time no longer calls generic part storage. The union answer is unchanged on every part, so nothing new reaches cleanup or `system.data_skipping_indices`. On a Keeper-backed metadata disk that stat reached Keeper with no component set, so the server threw `Current component is empty, please set it for your scope using Coordination::setCurrentComponent`. That is the private-sync failure in `Stress test (amd_tsan, SharedCatalog, meta in keeper)`, whose frames end in `DataPartStorageOnDiskFull::existsFileImpl`: the generic fallback, not the archive probe. I worked from those frames and cannot read the private logs. Asking the archive directly needs no new guard, since its loader already sets a component. This covers every unguarded probe of the class, not just the frame above: the rest of `getDeserializedFormat` is in-memory type comparison. Reachable on defaults: `packed_skip_index_max_bytes` is on and text indices are never packed. Building the shape needs a write into a part directory, so the test is `tests/integration/test_packed_skip_index_orphan`; each case fails on exactly the binary it targets.

signals.title: Spill the adaptive aggregator's learning-phase tables under memory pressure
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114987 --> Closes: #114987 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Requested by @ nihalzp in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114987#issuecomment-5307798148. **The problem.** `Aggregator::executeOnBlock` ends in a baseline tail that converts the table to two-level, checks limits and spills past `max_bytes_before_external_group_by`. The adaptive block returns before that tail. Its thaw arm stands down first and its frozen arm runs a drain valve, but the learning arm returned with no memory response at all. A producer leaves learning only by freezing at `adaptive_aggregator_freeze_threshold` keys or by giving up after 16x that many rows, so with the threshold raised neither bound fires inside one query and the table grows in RAM with no byte bound. **The change.** A learning table has no frozen twin to pair with and nothing staged, so under pressure it can stand down for good and spill through the branch that already exists below. Gating it on the pressure trigger matters: the tail can convert the table to two-level, after which `isConvertibleToTwoLevel()` is false and the producer could never freeze again, so an unconditional fall-through would disable the feature rather than fix it. **Reachability is narrower than the report implies.** At the default `adaptive_aggregator_freeze_threshold = 16384` the spill still works, so this needs a raised threshold, not stock settings. The reporter agreed on the issue. **Validation.** On the report's query with the threshold raised, `ExternalAggregationWritePart` goes from 0 to 46, matching the feature-off arm, and under `max_memory_usage = 700000000` the query changes from `MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` to completing. Each new defect cell fails on the unfixed binary, the freeze counters are byte-identical on the fast path, and the two files passed 100 randomized runs. Left alone deliberately: the stand-down reuses `Reason::TooFewDistinctKeys` rather than adding a `MemoryPressure` enumerator, since that field has no readers today; and a frozen local table stays unbounded in bytes for growing states such as `groupArray`, which the issue raises separately. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1521` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Fix the lost wakeup that hangs the BackgroundSchedulePool schedule tests
signals.text: Fix the lost wakeup that hangs the BackgroundSchedulePool schedule tests <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `TEST(BackgroundSchedulePool, Schedule)` can block forever. The unit tests run sequentially in a single binary, so one hang consumes the job's whole 90 minute budget and the binary is killed before it writes `gtest.json`: the job reported 2 rows instead of the usual ~20,285, losing every other gtest's result. `ScheduleAfter` has the same defect. Root cause: the task callback called `condvar.notify_one()` without holding the mutex the waiter uses, and the waiter's `condvar.wait` was unbounded. If the last iteration increments the counter and notifies after the waiter evaluated its predicate but before it blocked, the notification is dropped. That iteration is also the one that stops re-scheduling, so the pool goes idle and nothing can notify again; the wait is permanent rather than slow. The fix takes the mutex around the increment and the notify, closing that window, and bounds the wait at 60 seconds. `pool->join()` now runs before the assertions, because the pool's destructor requires `join()` and a fatal assertion before it would abort the binary on the timeout path. The bound waits on the wait's status, not on the predicate: the predicate overload of `wait_for` re-evaluates the predicate after the deadline and returns its value, so a dropped notification, which leaves the counter complete, would report success and keep the test green on the very regression the bound exists to catch. Validated by injecting a delay inside the waiter's predicate to force the losing interleaving: before the change the test hangs with a backtrace matching the reported one, after it the probe passes, and against that state the predicate overload passes in 301 ms while the status loop fails at the deadline. 50 repetitions of both arms pass in Debug and under TSan. Found on a private-repo `Unit tests (tsan)` run, so there is no public CI report to link. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1526` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Do not abort server startup when a database's named collection is missing
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110529 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed the server refusing to start when a database created with `S3`, `Remote`, `RemoteSecure`, `MySQL` or `PostgreSQL` referenced a named collection that no longer exists. Such a database is now skipped with a logged error and the server starts; recreating the collection and restarting brings the database back. ### Description A database whose engine arguments name a missing named collection stops the whole server from starting: `Caught exception while loading metadata: Code: 669 ... There is no named collection 'nc_cfg': while loading database 'db_cfg'`, then `shutting down`. Retiring a `config.d/*.xml` collection and restarting reaches this. Recovery meant moving `metadata/<db>.sql` aside by hand, since the collection cannot be recreated with the server down. A **table** in the same state does not: the server boots and only that table's load job fails, so an admin recovers with a plain `CREATE NAMED COLLECTION`. That asymmetry is the bug. `loadDatabase` runs with `create = true`, so `setForceAttach` is never called and databases derive `ATTACH` rather than the `FORCE_ATTACH` that gives tables their tolerance. The two startup loops in `loadMetadata` now skip such a database instead of aborting, under four conditions that must all hold: the process is `clickhouse-server`, the error is exactly `NAMED_COLLECTION_DOESNT_EXIST`, the database is not the configured default, and its engine is in an audited list of engines owning no local table metadata (`S3`, `Remote`, `RemoteSecure`, `MySQL`, `PostgreSQL`). Everything else is unchanged: other error codes still stop startup, `Replicated` and `MaterializedPostgreSQL` still do because they own local tables, `clickhouse-local` still fails, and `ATTACH DATABASE` still fails loudly. The metadata file is untouched, so recreating the collection and restarting restores the database. The *default* database is excluded because `assertDatabaseExists(default_database)` runs right after. Validated both directions on identical on-disk state: the pre-fix binary exits 157, the fixed one starts and logs the skip. `test_named_collections` passes 29/29 with 13 new cases, plus a `clickhouse-local` stateless test. Each of the four conditions has its own test that fails on a build with that one condition removed, so none is vacuous. The related PR fixes this class for URL **tables**, not databases.

signals.title: Tag functional tests averaging over 60s under MSan with `no-msan`
signals.text: MSan stateless jobs are the slowest functional-test jobs in CI and sit right at the edge of the 9000 s job timeout. In a recent run the private `Stateless tests (amd_msan, distributed cache, meta in keeper, s3 storage, sequential, 2/2)` job spent 8324 s of its 9000 s budget on tests and was then killed during teardown, even though all 526 tests had passed. MSan is ~5.8× slower than release on the same tests, and the cost is concentrated in a long tail: under MSan, 8 tests take over 180 s each, and the 30 slowest account for ~48% of a sequential shard's runtime. This tags every functional test whose mean duration under MSan exceeds 60 s with `no-msan`, except two tests that would otherwise lose all sanitizer coverage. ### How the set was chosen From `play.clickhouse.com`, over the public MSan stateless checks (`Stateless tests (amd_msan, WasmEdge, parallel, N/M)` and `Stateless tests (amd_msan, WasmEdge, sequential, N/2)`, excluding the flaky-check and selected-tests flavors): ```sql SELECT test_name, count() AS runs, avg(test_duration_ms)/1000 AS avg_s FROM checks WHERE check_name LIKE 'Stateless tests (amd_msan, WasmEdge, %' AND check_name NOT LIKE '%flaky%' AND check_name NOT LIKE '%selected%' AND test_status = 'OK' AND check_start_time >= now() - INTERVAL 30 DAY GROUP BY test_name HAVING runs >= 20 AND avg_s > 60 ORDER BY avg_s DESC ``` 351 tests matched. 30 of them no longer exist in `master` (reverted, split into smaller tests, or removed), leaving 321. One of those, `04062_text_index_json_all_values_ghdata`, already carried `no-msan`; two more remain under MSan to retain their only sanitizer coverage, so 318 files change here. Only `OK` runs are counted, so timeouts and failures do not inflate the averages. ### Initial expected effect The following estimates were calculated before retaining the two sanitizer-coverage tests. | Flavor | MSan test time per commit | Removed | Share | |---|---|---|---| | parallel | 129025 s | 24766 s | 19.2% | | sequential | 11236 s | 4108 s | 36.6% | ### 25 slowest of the tagged tests | Test | Mean under MSan | Runs | |---|---|---| | `03988_cached_read_big_at` | 384.6 s | 9014 | | `03008_deduplication_insert_several_blocks_replicated` | 337.2 s | 9116 | | `03008_deduplication_several_mv_into_one_table_nonreplicated` | 308.8 s | 9118 | | `03008_deduplication_insert_several_blocks_nonreplicated` | 282.6 s | 9118 | | `04039_merge_tree_snapshot_teardown_race` | 275.2 s | 9347 | | `01195_formats_diagnostic_info` | 234.6 s | 9278 | | `02475_bson_each_row_format` | 206.1 s | 9264 | | `00626_replace_partition_from_table_zookeeper` | 202.5 s | 9323 | | `01019_alter_materialized_view_atomic` | 192.5 s | 9340 | | `04062_text_index_json_all_values_ghdata` | 190.4 s | 1806 | | `01721_join_implicit_cast_long` | 182.8 s | 9339 | | `00746_sql_fuzzy` | 180.5 s | 9340 | | `03755_large_primary_key_explain` | 180.2 s | 9337 | | `02943_variant_type_with_different_local_and_global_order` | 180.2 s | 9284 | | `02448_clone_replica_lost_part` | 177.4 s | 9263 | | `02372_analyzer_join` | 176.3 s | 9345 | | `04327_cluster_functions_huge_num_streams_no_crash` | 171.8 s | 9261 | | `01721_join_implicit_cast_long_oldanalyzer` | 168.9 s | 9346 | | `01079_bad_alters_zookeeper_long` | 166.8 s | 9322 | | `01747_system_session_log_long` | 165.9 s | 9014 | | `03208_array_of_json_read_subcolumns_1` | 165 s | 9339 | | `00429_long_http_bufferization` | 160.9 s | 9277 | | `04411_deep_nested_field_to_type` | 156.8 s | 9262 | | `01383_log_broken_table` | 156.4 s | 9340 | | `03326_protobuf_schemas_race` | 155.1 s | 9279 | (318 tests are tagged in total; the full list is the diff.) ### Trade-off A large share of these are the ZooKeeper, replication, mutation and race tests — precisely where MSan is most likely to find real uninitialized-memory bugs. They continue to run under ASan, UBSan and TSan, but this is a genuine reduction in MSan coverage rather than a pure win. An alternative that keeps the coverage is duration-aware sharding of the sequential jobs: the split is currently `crc32(test filename) % total_batches`, which gave one recent shard 8248 s against its sibling's 5514 s (1.50×), so balancing alone would have reclaimed ~23 min on the shard that timed out. ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115050&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115050](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115050+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Record an index's absent columns when materializing it on a wide part
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114990 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112484 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes an unreleased regression from #112484 (`master` only): `ALTER TABLE ... MATERIALIZE INDEX` produced an index that never prunes when the indexed column had been added by a metadata-only `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` and the part is wide. No stable release carries #112484, so no changelog entry and no backport are owed. ### Description Reported by @ clickgapai. #112484 merged on 2026-08-15 and is an ancestor of no release branch, so only `master` is affected. **What breaks.** `ADD COLUMN c ... DEFAULT ...` on a wide part is metadata-only, so the part holds no bytes for `c`. A following `MATERIALIZE INDEX idx` writes the index files but does not add `c` to the part's column list, and since #112484 the reader refuses an index whose columns the part does not describe. The index occupies disk and never prunes: `Granules: 16/16` on the reporter's fixture versus `1/16` before, results correct both ways. **Root cause.** `splitAndModifyMutationCommands` has two branches. The compact one turns an index's required-but-absent columns into `READ_COLUMN` commands; the wide one had no such step, so `c` never enters `updated_header` and `getColumnsForNewDataPart` erases it. The missing type is the defect, so the fix belongs on the write side. **The change.** On a wide part, `MATERIALIZE INDEX` now also reads the index's absent columns, so the part records them at the type the granules were built from. The column list belongs to the part, so it records the column only when every other index holding files there either does not read it or has its granules rebuilt by this same mutation: a carried-over granule keeps its build-time type, so recording the column now would hand the reader a matching type for a stale granule. What the mutation rebuilds is decided from its own commands, and an undecidable index counts as carried over, keeping the pre-fix behaviour. Compact parts and the reader are untouched, so every #112484 refusal holds. **Cost.** The mutation now writes column data: +247 bytes before, +806,931 after on a 200k-row wide fixture; the next merge writes it anyway. No format, serialization or default change, so no `SettingsChangesHistory.cpp` entry. <details> <summary>Validation, rejected alternative, known-unfixed shape</summary> **Rejected alternative:** recording build-time types in a new per-part file - a format change needing ~9 seams, a protocol bump and upgrade/downgrade paths. **Known-unfixed:** on a part with orphan index files (#109595) `hasSecondaryIndex` is true, so the read is suppressed and the index stays inert - the status quo, never wrong results. | arm | absent arm | control arm | |---|---|---| | pristine master | `16/16` (inert) | 1/16 | | this PR | `1/16` | 1/16 | Counts identical with and without `use_skip_indexes` in every cell; the control prunes on both. Four mutation arms cover the restriction, each red on the build missing its guard: without it, a hardlinked granule's column is rewritten at the new type and the next read attempts a 4 EiB allocation; keyed to the index named in the command rather than the column, a second index over that column has its stale granules re-enabled and the next read aborts; without the rebuilt-sibling exemption, a batched update that does rebuild the sibling still suppresses it, leaving the new index inert - covered both for a sibling reached by a named column and for one reached via a TTL target. Tests: `04869_skip_index_stale_type_absent_column` gains cases 26 (the regression), 26b (subcolumn index, absent parent recorded), 27, 28 (two indices, one absent column), 29 and 30 (rebuilt sibling). Cases 11/22/23/24 moved from `ADD COLUMN` to a column TTL expiry, since the fix makes the old route no longer leave a column absent; each gained an `EXPLAIN indexes = 1` refusal assertion, and every such assertion now pins the granule count rather than matching a substring. `04246_materialize_index_force_recalc` (the #104872 compact tripwire), `04165`, `04870` and `04871` pass unchanged; 250/250 across a 50-run randomized loop. Unrelated columns stay hardlinked (by inode), so the mutation does not escalate to a full part rewrite. </details>

signals.title: Reject invalid event numbers and durations in sequenceMatch patterns
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed an `out_of_range` exception raised as an internal `Code: 1001` error when a `sequenceMatch`, `sequenceCount` or `sequenceMatchEvents` pattern contains the event number `0`, for example `sequenceMatch('(?0)')`. Such a pattern is now rejected with `BAD_ARGUMENTS`. A temporal condition holding a lone sign, such as `sequenceMatch('(?1)(?t>+)(?2)')`, was silently treated as `(?t>0)` and is now rejected with `SYNTAX_ERROR`. ### Description Event numbers are 1-based, but the bound check validated only the upper bound, so `(?0)` passed it. The conversion to a 0-based condition index then underflowed `UInt64` to `SIZE_MAX`, and `std::bitset<32>::set()` rejected that with `std::out_of_range`. Thrown from the aggregate function constructor during analysis, it surfaced as an internal `Code: 1001` error and aborted the server in debug and sanitizer builds. Two further inputs reached the same state: an event number overflowing `UInt64`, and a sign with no digits, `(?+)`. In each case `tryReadIntText` fails after consuming a byte while its pointer overload discards the boolean, so the existing "Could not parse number" check does not fire and the output keeps its initialiser `0`. Adding the missing lower bound validates the parsed value and covers all three at once, error code and message unchanged. The sibling temporal branch shared that parse-success defect and is fixed here too, after review automation raised it: `(?t>+)` was accepted as `(?t>0)`. The duration is now read through the `ReadBuffer` overload so the boolean is available, and rejected when it is false. The position check is kept, because `tryReadIntText` also succeeds while consuming nothing for a leading non-digit, which is what rejects `(?t>)`. Only the sign form leaked; `(?t>-)` and an overflowing duration were already rejected, and `(?t>+5)` still equals `(?t>5)`. All three functions share this parser and were affected; all are covered by new assertions in `00222_sequence_aggregate_function_family`, which fail on an unfixed binary. One imprecision is left as is: an overflowing event number is reported as event number `0`. Found by `AST fuzzer (amd_tsan)`, `bitset set argument out of range` (STID 2508-34fb): https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115019&sha=7be817c59e288cab7aa329a76ed1ba65b9d555e9&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_tsan%29. Also seen on `Stress test (arm_tsan)`. signals.title: A single test's timeout no longer aborts the whole clickhouse-test run
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/86768 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description **The problem.** `Fast test` on #86768 reported `Failed: 0, Passed: 73, Skipped: 23` yet failed with a synthetic `Server died` leaf. No core, no sanitizer report. [Report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=86768&sha=0927f057854f5e533b8ff833cf200e17db8005c5&name_0=PR&name_1=Fast%20test) | [job log](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/actions/runs/31943974132/job/95177622132) **Root cause.** The server saturated rather than died, so all 24 workers hit the 126 s alarm at once. The first into `timeout_handler` called `stop_tests()`, which `killpg`s our *own* group, shared by every worker and the parent. One test's deadline thus SIGTERMed the whole run, exiting -15, which `ABORTED_RUN_EXIT_CODES` makes the job side relabel `Server died`. The `Code: 76` on `run_r0/status` and the `Code: 159` from `SYSTEM FLUSH LOGS` are downstream of it. **The change.** `timeout_handler` now kills only the timing-out test's own out-of-group clients, via a per-child loop extracted from `cleanup_child_processes`. That broadcast is unchanged, so the whole-run callers are unaffected, as the `--max-failures` paths document. A surviving worker must then report the test, which needs a result built and stamped. The alarm can land before either, so the recovery arm completes what is missing, and `SIGALRM` is blocked across stamping so it cannot run twice: a doubled description matches the leaf pattern too, reporting a nonexistent test. Fast test just has the shortest fuse. This does not fix the saturation. **Validation.** Not SQL-observable. The new `ci/tests/` test drives the real handler and `run_tests_array`, faking `killpg`/`pgrep`: own-group broadcasts 0, the test's own client still killed, `cleanup_child_processes` still broadcasting, one parseable leaf per alarm window. No wall clock. `ci/tests/` is 663/665, both failures pre-existing. **Residuals.** A timed-out test's database and temporary directory survive into the worker's next test, as when the alarm killed the worker outright. An alarm can also be swallowed by an unrelated broad `except Exception`, after which saturation reports `SERVER_DIED`, as master did on every per-test timeout. Both want a private signal type, a larger change. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115061&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115061](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115061+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Do not pop hints on a line displayed programmatically
signals.text: When a query is displayed at once rather than typed — recalled from the history with Up/Down/Ctrl-P/Ctrl-N, found by the incremental (Ctrl-T) or fuzzy (Ctrl-R) history search, pasted, brought back from the external editor, or preloaded — the as-you-type hints no longer appear at its end. With hints visible, the next Up/Down press would navigate the hints instead of the history, so navigating the history quickly was impossible. The hints are shown again as soon as the line is edited. The suppression is armed before the navigation action because replxx repaints (and regenerates the hints) inside `history_move` itself, and the displayed text is additionally pinned afterwards because replxx may throttle that repaint and replay it after the key handler returns (its "rapid refresh" of e.g. a held-down Up key). Verified with a new pty regression test (`04909_client_hints_history_navigation`, 6 cases), including duplicate-history and unchanged-editor same-text redisplays; the existing `04402_clickhouse_client_autocomplete_inline_hints` (11 cases) and the hint-related expect tests still pass. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114043 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The command line client no longer shows the as-you-type hints on a query recalled from the history (or otherwise displayed at once, e.g. pasted), so pressing Up/Down continues to navigate the history instead of the hint list. The hints appear again as soon as the line is edited. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115065&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115065](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115065+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Answer text-index materialization from the index read task
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109595 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115037 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109595 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115037 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a text index query silently returning too few rows when a part carries a `skp_idx_<index>.idx` file that `checksums.txt` does not account for. The read path decided which columns to read from file existence while the index reader was assigned from checksum accounting, so the affected part contributed no matches. Both are now answered by the same predicate. ### Description ```sql CREATE TABLE t (k UInt64, s String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY k; INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 'alpha'); ALTER TABLE t ADD INDEX tx s TYPE text(tokenizer = 'splitByNonAlpha') GRANULARITY 1; INSERT INTO t VALUES (2, 'alpha'); -- in all_1_1_0/: echo garbage > skp_idx_tx.idx DETACH TABLE t SYNC; ATTACH TABLE t; SELECT count() FROM t WHERE hasToken(s, 'alpha'); -- master: 1, expected 2 SELECT count() FROM t WHERE NOT hasToken(s, 'alpha'); -- master: 1, expected 0 ``` Default settings. The unaccounted file is the corrupted-part shape of #109595; its content is never decoded. Three read-path sites answer whether a text index is materialized in a part. `optimizeDirectReadFromTextIndex` and `getIndexReadTaskForReadStep` ask the index object via `getDeserializedFormat`, which requires the file to be accounted for and decodable. `hasMaterializedTextIndex` instead asked the part for a file on disk via `hasSecondaryIndex`, whose fallback is an unconditional `existsFile` with no accounting gate. An unaccounted file therefore reads as materialized only at that third site: `injectRequiredColumnsRecursively` takes its early return and never injects the base column, no index reader is created, and the virtual column's default expression is evaluated with its input missing. `getReadTaskColumns` already receives `index_read_tasks`, keyed by index name and carrying the index object the reader-assignment site uses. Threading the map through makes the two agree via a map lookup, with no index construction on the read path. `hasSecondaryIndex` is left alone: its mutation and merge callers want the file-existence answer. The reproducer needs one file write, so the test is an integration test (#111922 forbids fabricating part contents in a functional test). I found no pure-SQL carrier: `getDeserializedFormat`'s other two false routes are `isPartTypeCompatible`, where five SQL routes returned ground truth, and `isSystemColumnInvalidated`, which only covers `_block_number` / `_block_offset`, neither referenceable by a text index. The carrier test fails on master and passes with the fix. The `02346_text_index*` and `00990_hasToken*` families are unchanged.

signals.title: Do not attach a cache writer to a detached file segment
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110029 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a `LOGICAL_ERROR` (`Cache file segment is in detached state`) when reading through the filesystem cache with the experimental `use_reader_executor` setting. The regression was introduced by #110029 and is not in any release, so no backport is owed. ### Description Related: #110029 **The problem.** `BuzzHouse` aborts the server with `Cache file segment is in detached state, operation not allowed`, on two unrelated PRs, first seen 8h41m after #110029 merged. CIDB STID `4043-43b7`, [report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113382&sha=97396ecebc7bcb7ee4d4921c71d1cfdd071a2895&name_0=PR&name_1=BuzzHouse%20%28arm_asan_ubsan%29). **Root cause.** `FileCache::getOrSet` can hand back a synthetic `DETACHED` placeholder rather than a real segment: `getImpl` fabricates one when the covering segment is being evicted or removed, and another when the range exceeds `bypass_cache_threshold`. Such a placeholder is outside the cache metadata, holds no bytes, and the downloader role cannot be acquired on it. `DiskCacheProvider::resolve` classified it as a *writable* miss, because `segmentCommittedEnd` falls back to the write offset, which for a placeholder equals the segment start. It attached a `DiskCacheWriter`, and `ReaderExecutor::readThroughCaches` then called `claimLeadRole` on it, whose `getOrSetDownloader` hit `assertNotDetachedUnlocked`: a `LOGICAL_ERROR`, aborting the server in debug and sanitizer builds. **The change.** `resolve` now emits a writer-less miss for a detached segment, so those bytes are read from source and nothing is cached. The legacy paths already do this: `CachedOnDiskReadBufferFromFile` dispatches `State::DETACHED` to a cache bypass before acquiring any role, and `CachedOnDiskWriteBufferFromFile` skips write-through caching on `isDetached()`. `claimLeadRole` was the only one of the five non-test `getOrSetDownloader` callers reachable with a detached segment; the assertion is a correct caller contract and stays. **Reachability.** `src/IO/DiskCacheProvider.cpp` exists on no active release branch (25.8, 26.3-26.7), and #110029 is an ancestor of none of them, so no released version can reach this. `use_reader_executor` is experimental and off by default; the abort affects the `BuzzHouse` checks, which randomize it as a session setting, plus anyone opting into the experimental path. **Validation.** Deterministic, no fuzzer needed: the test arms the existing failpoint `file_cache_simulate_evicting_segment`, which makes every segment the cache reports a placeholder. Without the fix the server dies with the CI stack; with it the test passes, 50/50 randomized.

signals.title: Look up the SSH key and support ssh-agent in clickhouse-client
signals.text: `--ssh-key-file` can now be specified without a value. In that case the key is looked up the same way as `ssh` does it: - the identity files configured for this host in `~/.ssh/config` and in `/etc/ssh/ssh_config`; - the default identity files, such as `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`; - the keys held by the `ssh-agent`. A key held by the `ssh-agent` is preferred, because it does not need a passphrase. It is also used when `--ssh-key-file` names a key file that the agent holds - an encrypted key that was added with `ssh-add` no longer asks for the passphrase. Signing with the agent is implemented in `SSHAgent`, a small client of the agent protocol, which produces the same `SSHSIG` signature as `SSHKey::signString` does for a local key (for RSA keys it asks the agent for `rsa-sha2-256`, because agents sign with SHA-1 by default and the server rejects that). The client reports the key it has chosen: ``` $ clickhouse-client --user abcuser --ssh-key-file Using the SSH key 'the key of abcuser' from the ssh-agent. ``` Two related changes of the existing behavior: the passphrase is now asked only if the key file is really encrypted (before, `--ssh-key-file` always asked for it), and the message about a key that cannot be imported now names the file. Tests: a new stateless test `04908_ssh_key_file_lookup` covers the default identity file, an `ed25519` key from the `ssh-agent`, and an `ssh-rsa` key from the `ssh-agent` with an empty `~/.ssh`. The existing `test_ssh_keys_authentication` integration tests pass. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `clickhouse-client` accepts `--ssh-key-file` without a value: the key is looked up the same way as `ssh` does it - the identity files configured for the host in `~/.ssh/config`, the default identity files, such as `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`, and the keys held by the `ssh-agent`. Authentication with a key held by the `ssh-agent` is now supported, and it does not need a passphrase. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115072&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115072](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115072+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Let the promql dialect keep tokens the SQL lexer rejects
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed PromQL queries with regex label matchers (`=~`, `!~`) being rejected under `--dialect promql`. Closes #115071. --- Under `--dialect promql`, `ParserPrometheusQuery` reads the raw query text and hands it to the PromQL grammar; it walks the SQL tokens only to find where the statement ends. But `tryParseQuery` scans those tokens for lexer errors *before* the parser runs, and `~` is not a SQL token, so the query was rejected before it ever reached the PromQL grammar: ``` $ clickhouse local --dialect promql -q 'up{instance="host1"}' Code: 471. ... The name of a TimeSeries table to use with promql dialect is not specified $ clickhouse local --dialect promql -q 'up{instance=~"host2|host3"}' Code: 62. ... Unrecognized token: Syntax error: failed at position 13 (~) ``` The equality matcher gets through to a missing-setting error; the regex matcher dies at the `~` with a **SQL** lexical error. It is not specific to `-q` — stdin and `--queries-file` fail identically. The grammar itself already has the tokens (`PromQLLexer.g4`: `RE : '=~'`, `NRE : '!~'`), and the same expression works when passed as a string to the table function, which is what makes the limitation easy to miss. `IParser` gains `consumesRawText()`, false by default and overridden by `ParserPrometheusQuery`. `tryParseQuery` skips its two lexical-error rejections for such parsers, since a token the SQL lexer does not recognise is not an error for a parser that reads the text itself. No call site changes, and any future dialect parser in the same position gets the behaviour by overriding one method. This is safe because the lexer does not stop at an unrecognised character — it consumes it and returns an `Error` token (`Lexer.cpp:546`), so statement-boundary detection still finds the terminating semicolon. Kusto solves the same problem with an entire parallel `parseKQLQuery.{h,cpp}`; PromQL needs only the boundary scan, so a virtual on `IParser` seemed proportionate. Happy to go the separate-entry-point route instead if maintainers prefer the consistency. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115073&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115073](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115073+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix gRPC and Arrow Flight listeners for wildcard listen hosts
signals.text: `gRPC` treats `::` and `0.0.0.0` as one family-agnostic wildcard: for either of them it binds a dual-stack `::` socket, and falls back to `0.0.0.0` only on a host without IPv6 (see `add_wildcard_addrs_to_server` in `contrib/grpc`). Listing both wildcard addresses in `listen_host` therefore made ClickHouse create two listeners that bind the very same socket address, and the second one either - failed with `EADDRINUSE`, because the Arrow Flight transport disables `SO_REUSEPORT`, and the exception terminated the whole server: ``` <Error> grpc: Failed to add port to server: No address added out of total 1 resolved for '0.0.0.0:9110' (Failed to add any wildcard listeners: Error in bind for address '[::]:9110': Address already in use Error in bind for address '0.0.0.0:9110': Address already in use) <Error> Application: Code: 1002. DB::Exception: Failed init Arrow Flight Server: Unknown error: Server did not start properly. ``` - or silently shared the port with the first one, because plain gRPC keeps `SO_REUSEPORT` enabled, so each of the two independent servers ended up serving a random half of the connections, and a listener configured for `0.0.0.0` accepted IPv6 connections as well: ``` <Information> Application: Listening for gRPC protocol: [::]:9100 <Information> Application: Listening for gRPC protocol: 0.0.0.0:9100 LISTEN 0 4096 *:9100 users:(("clickhouse",pid=3851032,fd=55)) LISTEN 0 4096 *:9100 users:(("clickhouse",pid=3851032,fd=56)) ``` Only one gRPC and one Arrow Flight listener is created for a group of wildcard `listen_host` values now, which is what the transport does internally anyway. Also, `listen_try` is honored for the protocols that bind their listening socket when they are started rather than when they are created. `EADDRINUSE` from gRPC or Arrow Flight was reported from the plain `server.start()` loop, outside of the `createServer` handler that implements `listen_try`, so it was fatal even with `listen_try` (and with `listen_reuse_port`) enabled - which contradicts the documented behavior of listening to at least one of the addresses without quitting. Not addressed here: plain gRPC still keeps `SO_REUSEPORT` enabled, so a gRPC port that is already taken by a different process is silently shared instead of reported. Making that consistent with `listen_reuse_port` for both gRPC and Arrow Flight is a possible follow-up. For the record, gRPC and Arrow Flight are not available as composable protocols (the `protocols` section): the composable stack is a Poco `TCPServer` with a chain of `TCPServerConnectionFactory` layers that receive an already accepted socket, while gRPC and Arrow Flight own the listening socket, the HTTP/2 framing, TLS and their own event loop, so they can neither be a layer nor sit under `tls` / `proxy1`. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix the server failing to start when `listen_host` contains both `::` and `0.0.0.0` and `arrowflight_port` is configured, and fix two gRPC listeners silently sharing one port in the same configuration. `listen_try` now also covers the gRPC and Arrow Flight protocols, which bind their listening socket when they are started. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115074&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115074](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115074+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Do not report "Server died" when only the liveness check failed
signals.text: Do not report "Server died" when only the liveness check failed <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110479 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110479 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `Stateless tests (amd_tsan, flaky check)` on #110479 @ `038667a9c024` reported a single failing leaf `Server died` while its own aggregate said `Failed: 0, Passed: 3872`. The server did not die: no `<Fatal>` line, no sanitizer report, empty `dmesg`, clean shutdown. The `--hung-check` liveness probe failed and the run was aborted. Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110479&sha=038667a9c024695126415fe5f37b76f7a06662fa&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_tsan%2C%20flaky%20check%29 Root cause: `tests/clickhouse-test` collapses every in-band abort cause into `STOP_TESTING_EXIT_CODE = 2`, and the job side appends `Server died` for that code unconditionally. Master already carved two causes out of code 2 for this reason; this is the third. This adds `HUNG_CHECK_EXIT_CODE = 5` and `FailureReason.LIVENESS_CHECK_FAILED`, with the leaf `Server liveness check failed` at status FAIL. All four sites that conclude `SERVER_DIED` from a failed probe are changed; the site concluding it from a `<Fatal>` line is untouched, and its neighbour becomes an `elif` of it so fatal evidence is never downgraded. The stop cause travels through one locked first-writer-wins carrier, replacing a `global_time_limit_reached` flag. The leaf names the observation, not a diagnosis: `check_server_liveness` also fails on a non-200 *response*. It is a NEW CIDB `test_name`. The aggregate stays FAIL, so bugfix validation still counts a hang as a repro. Not claimed: a remaining `Server died` row still does not prove a death. Code 2 is generic, and a worker seeing a `<Fatal>` line reaches the parent through `stop_tests()`, exiting 143 - correct there, but decided outside the carrier. Validation: +50 tests asserting the process exit code end to end - the same command exits 2 on master and 5 here. Each changed site has a mutation arm reddening a named case. `ci/tests`: 705 passed, 655 on master. Successor to #112952, not an extension: that PR deliberately excludes exit code 2. Both touch the same region of `functional_tests_results.py`, so the second to merge needs a rebase.

signals.title: Announce the connection endpoint once when the client asks for a password
signals.text: `clickhouse-client` printed `Connecting to ...` twice whenever it had to ask for a password: ``` $ clickhouse client --host clickhouse.new --secure --user alexey-milovidov ClickHouse client version 26.8.1.1. Connecting to clickhouse.new:9440 as user alexey-milovidov. Password for user (alexey-milovidov): Connecting to clickhouse.new:9440 as user alexey-milovidov. Connected to ClickHouse server version 26.8.1. ``` Neither `--password` nor `--ask-password` was given, so the client did not know whether the user has a password at all and connected without one. The server answered `REQUIRED_PASSWORD`, and the retry loop in `Client::main` set `ask-password` and called `connect` again, which prompted for the password and announced the very same endpoint a second time. Now an endpoint is announced only when it differs from the one announced last, and the announcement is forgotten after a successful connection, so a fallback to another port and a reconnect later in the session are still announced. Added `04909_client_password_prompt_announces_endpoint_once.expect`, which fails on the current `master` binary with `The endpoint was announced twice.` and passes with this change. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `clickhouse-client` no longer prints the `Connecting to ...` message twice when it asks for a password interactively. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115081&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115081](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115081+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Report cancellation instead of leaving an in-place set unbuilt
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114463 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107619 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `Not-ready Set is passed as the second argument for function 'in'` error when a query with `partial_result_on_first_cancel = 1` was cancelled while the set of an `IN (subquery)` was still being built. ### Description Follow-up to https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114463, asked for in its review. That pull request makes a cancelled mutation report `ABORTED` instead of stopping its nested pipelines silently; the review asked whether the same silent stop is still reachable through the other two interactive-cancel callbacks. I measured both. One is, one is not. **Reachable: `partial_result_on_first_cancel`.** For the first cancel, `TCPHandler::processCancel` only sets `stop_read_return_partial_result` and deliberately does not cancel the query through the process list, so the callback returns a bare `true` (`TCPHandler.cpp:897-898`). `CompletedPipelineExecutor::execute` then cancels the nested set-build pipeline and its poll loop returns normally, so `CreatingSetsTransform::generate` never runs `Set::finishInsert`, while `FutureSetFromSubquery::build` has already moved the source plan out. A caller that evaluates its filter in the same call passes the unbuilt set to `FunctionIn`. On master (`f45871c7cfa`), one cancel during ```sql SELECT count() FROM t WHERE 1 IN (SELECT number FROM numbers(10000000) WHERE sleep(1) = 0) SETTINGS partial_result_on_first_cancel = 1, optimize_use_implicit_projections = 1, optimize_trivial_count_query = 0 ``` reports ``` Code: 49. DB::Exception: Not-ready Set is passed as the second argument for function 'in' ... (LOGICAL_ERROR) ``` through `FunctionIn` (`in.cpp:116`) <- `VirtualColumnUtils::filterBlockWithExpression` (`:162`) <- `MergeTreeData::getMinMaxCountProjectionBlock` (`:10463`) <- `optimizeUseAggregateProjections` (`:630`). A debug or sanitizer build aborts on it. **Not reachable: `clickhouse-local`.** Its callback cancels the query through the process list element (`LocalConnection.cpp:191-194`), so the nested pipeline fails instead of stopping silently. The same query interrupted with `SIGINT` reports `Code: 394. DB::Exception: Query was cancelled` on master, with `EXPLAIN indexes = 1` confirming the plan is the `minmax_count` projection. That installer is untouched here. `FutureSetFromSubquery::buildSetInplace` now records whether the cancel callback fired and, if the set was left uncreated, reports `QUERY_WAS_CANCELLED` instead of returning to a caller that cannot distinguish a cancelled build from a completed one. Both conditions are required on purpose, so a set build that stops for a reason other than a cancellation keeps the behaviour it has today. Measured over the routes that stop such a pipeline early: `set_overflow_mode = 'break'`, `transfer_overflow_mode = 'break'` and `read_overflow_mode = 'break'` all still reach `CreatingSetsTransform::generate`, which finishes the set, and the query returns its result; `set_overflow_mode = 'throw'` still reports `SET_SIZE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`. For `partial_result_on_first_cancel` this means such a query now fails with `QUERY_WAS_CANCELLED` rather than with the logical error. There is no partial answer to return instead: the cancellation lands during analysis, before a row is produced, and an incomplete `IN` set would silently change the result. The mutation path keeps reporting `ABORTED` as #114463 makes it: its callback throws before this check is reached, which names the mutation the way `MergeTask::checkOperationIsNotCanceled` does and covers every nested pipeline a mutation runs, not only `buildSetInplace`. The ordered variant `buildOrderedSetInplace` needs nothing: #107924 made it build against a clone of the source plan and publish only a created set, so a silently stopped ordered build just skips index analysis. Out of scope, found while measuring this and reported here rather than fixed: a *time limit* with `break` reaches the same logical error without any cancellation, because the limit stops the set-build pipeline the same way. On master, ```sql SELECT count() FROM t WHERE 1 IN (SELECT number FROM numbers(1000)) SETTINGS optimize_use_implicit_projections = 1, optimize_trivial_count_query = 0, max_execution_time = 0.0001, timeout_overflow_mode = 'break' ``` reports `Not-ready Set is passed as the second argument for function 'in'` too. The check added here deliberately does not cover it: `break` asks for a truncated result rather than an error, so what a partially built `IN` set should do - report the limit, or silently use the rows read so far, as `set_overflow_mode = 'break'` already does - is a semantic decision, and it is not what this pull request is about. Happy to open an issue or a follow-up for it. New test `04909_cancel_in_subquery_set_build_partial_result`. It asserts up front that the `minmax_count` projection is the plan for the predicate shape under test, so it cannot pass without exercising the synchronous filter evaluation, and both of its wait loops fail loudly rather than cancelling something else. The oracle is the reported outcome, not the survival of the server, so it is live on release builds too. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115083&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115083](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115083+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix PostgreSQL-protocol authentication for users that also have an ssh_key
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/76839 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix authentication over the PostgreSQL wire protocol for users with several authentication methods: a user that also had an `ssh_key` method (or any other method that stores no password) was rejected with `Invalid user or password` even when the correct password for its `scram_sha256_password` method was supplied, and a wrong SCRAM salt was sent to the client when the SCRAM method was not the last one (e.g. for a user with `scram_sha256_password` followed by `sha256_password`). A user with multiple authentication methods, one of which is `ssh_key`, could not authenticate over the PostgreSQL protocol at all (in either order of the methods), while the same user authenticated fine over the native, MySQL, and HTTP protocols. Reproduced on 26.7.3.19 and current master. Anyone who adds a public SSH key to their user (e.g. for the SSH endpoint) silently loses PostgreSQL access with a misleading "wrong password" error. Two defects, both fixed (each order of methods hits at least one of them): 1. `checkScramSHA256Authentication` did not check the type of the authentication method it verifies the client proof against, and `IAccessStorage::authenticateImpl` calls it for every method of the user. For methods that store no password hash (e.g. `ssh_key`), the empty hash was passed to `hmacSHA256` as the HMAC key; `EVP_MAC_init` fails for a null key, so the check threw `OPENSSL_ERROR` (`Authentication failed: Code: 454. DB::Exception: EVP_MAC_init failed`) instead of returning false, aborting the whole authentication instead of trying the next method of the user. Now it returns false for non-SCRAM methods, the same way `checkMySQLAuthentication` handles non-MySQL-compatible methods. 2. `ScrambleSHA256Auth::authenticate` in the PostgreSQL handler sent the salt of the *last* authentication method of the user instead of the salt of the SCRAM method, so the client derived a salted password that could never match the stored verifier: an empty salt when `ssh_key` was last, or an unrelated random salt when e.g. `sha256_password` was. Now it sends the salt of the first `scram_sha256_password` method. Verified before/after with `psql` against a local server; added an integration test covering both method orders, the `scram_sha256_password` + `sha256_password` combination, and wrong-password rejection. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115084&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115084](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115084+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Reload a persisted `url()` table with the storage its creation selected
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104437 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a server that refuses to start after a table was created with `CREATE TABLE ... AS url('http://host/**/', ...)` while `allow_experimental_url_wildcard_from_index_pages` was enabled. Loading such a table's metadata re-evaluated the experimental check and failed with `SUPPORT_IS_DISABLED`, aborting startup. ### Description Reported by @ bacek on #104437, where `Stress test (amd_tsan)` failed with `Cannot start clickhouse-server` after a fuzzer created `url('/**/', JSONEachRow, 'x int')`. No fuzzer is needed: enable the setting, create such a table, restart with the default. Root cause is one defaulted parameter. `ITableFunction::execute` declares `bool is_insert_query = false`; `CREATE ... AS url(...)` passes `true` explicitly (`InterpreterCreateQuery.cpp:2403`), while metadata replay (`DatabaseOnDisk.cpp:117`) passes nothing. `TableFunctionURL::getStorage` computes `use_web_wildcard = !is_insert_query && ...`, so the two take opposite branches for the same stored table: creation builds a plain `StorageURL` and never reaches the experimental check, replay builds `StorageObjectStorage` and does. The check is dead at creation and live only on replay, and metadata loading rethrows. The fix treats a definition arriving with stored columns as a persisted one being replayed, so it resolves to the storage creation selected. The check is not suppressed, it becomes unreachable because the correct branch is taken. Suppressing it would instead enable index-page expansion with the setting disabled and give the table a read-only storage. `ENGINE = URL` was already fixed this way in 64abbdd31d85b15 ("Gate `URL` wildcard experiment check to creation"). Behaviour change: a persisted glob `url()` table that today rebuilds as `StorageObjectStorage` after a restart now rebuilds as the `StorageURL` its creation built. Both carriers are covered by the one change and both are tested: explicit structure, and `structure = 'auto'` via `StorageTableFunctionProxy` (the surface of an earlier `test_url_wildcard_schema_inference` failure). `urlCluster` cannot persist a table. The creation-time check in `getActualTableStructure` is deliberately untouched, since a columns-less `CREATE` reaches it before `execute`. Querying `url()` directly still requires the setting. Out of scope: the check stays dead at creation, so `CREATE` with a glob still succeeds with the setting off. `ytsaurus()` has the same problem by another mechanism. CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=104437&sha=bee15ffc5ec3d2a9b5479bd1fbc197ac6458eebc&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_tsan%29 <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115095&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115095](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115095+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Emit IF EXISTS when formatting ALTER ... MATERIALIZE INDEX/STATISTICS/PROJECTION
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114171 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed the formatting of `ALTER TABLE ... MATERIALIZE INDEX`, `MATERIALIZE STATISTICS` and `MATERIALIZE PROJECTION`, which dropped the `IF EXISTS` clause, so the formatted query was not the query that was parsed. Also rejected four `ALTER ... STATISTICS` AST JSON payloads that the SQL parser cannot produce and that formatted into a different command. ### Description `ParserAlterQuery` accepts and records `IF EXISTS` for `MATERIALIZE INDEX`, `MATERIALIZE STATISTICS` and `MATERIALIZE PROJECTION`, but `ASTAlterCommand::formatImpl` never emitted it, so formatting a parsed query produced a different query than the user wrote. The 11 sibling blocks in the same function all emit the clause already. Exactly these three of the 15 scalar `ASTAlterCommand` members fail a format-and-reparse preservation probe on master. The clause is not consumed for these three today, so no execution outcome changes. It is still user-visible: `system.mutations.command` reports exactly this formatted text, and so does the mutation entry persisted to ZooKeeper and disk. It surfaced as an `Inconsistent AST formatting` logical error in `Stateless tests (amd_debug, parallel)` from `02864_statistics_ddl.sql:194` ([CI report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114171&sha=105deb1ebf1fbc5dc4c3749df97ed590c3b9b30e&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_debug%2C%20parallel%29)). That run adds a tree hash over `if_exists`, and a member that is hashed but not formatted makes the round-trip check in `executeQuery.cpp` diverge and abort in debug builds. For `MATERIALIZE STATISTICS` the emission goes inside the column-list branch: the `ALL` form carries a null `statistics_decl`, and `MATERIALIZE STATISTICS IF EXISTS ALL` would reparse as the statistic on a column literally named `ALL`. The parser reads `IF EXISTS` and `IN PARTITION` only in that column-list branch, so on the `ALL` form neither is reachable from SQL, but both are constructible in AST JSON and both format into a different command. `readJSON` now rejects them for `MATERIALIZE STATISTICS` and `DROP/CLEAR STATISTICS`. Two were already wrong on master: `if_exists` formatted as `CLEAR STATISTICS IF EXISTS ALL` and reparsed as a column named `ALL`, and a `partition` was dropped, widening the mutation from one partition to every partition. Validation: the round-trips are pinned in `04126_parser_alter_query_variants` with the `ALL` forms asserted byte-unchanged, the rejections in `04350_ast_json_parser_impossible_field_combinations`. Every new assertion fails on a pre-fix binary.

signals.title: Fix arrayROCAUC and arrayAUCPR returning order-dependent results for NaN scores
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/104763 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `arrayROCAUC` and `arrayAUCPR` (and their aliases `arrayAUC` and `arrayPRAUC`) returning a different result for the same data depending on the order of the array elements when a score was `NaN`. A `NaN` score now makes the result `NaN`. Closes [#104763](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/104763). ### Description Closes: #104763. **The problem.** These are pure functions of a set of (score, label) pairs, so permuting the pairs must not change the result. With a `NaN` score it did: `arrayAUCPR([nan, 0.5], [1, 1])` returned `nan` while `arrayAUCPR([0.5, nan], [1, 1])` returned `1`. No error was raised, so the metric was silently wrong. **Root cause.** Two independent defects in `FunctionArrayAUC::apply`, both reachable from a single `NaN`: 1. The descending-score comparator passed to `std::sort` is not a strict weak ordering when a score is `NaN` (every comparison with `NaN` is false, so incomparability is not transitive), so the sorted order, and the traversal with it, follows the input order. 2. `threshold` is seeded from the first sorted element so the first iteration never increments the area, but `nan != nan` is true, so the guard fires with `tp = fp = 0`, and the Precision-Recall precision term becomes `0 / 0`. **The change.** `apply` returns `NaN` if any score is `NaN`, before sorting. That removes both defects at once, and `std::sort`'s precondition then holds for every input reaching it. `NaN` in, `NaN` out matches `sum`, `avg`, `arraySum` and `corr`, and `arrayROCAUC` already used `NaN` for its undefined cases. Beyond the reported `arrayAUCPR` case this also fixes `arrayROCAUC`, both aliases, the `scale` argument and the 3- and 4-argument `partial_offsets` forms, all affected the same way. The intentional value change: any `NaN`-containing input now returns `NaN` instead of an order-dependent number, including the all-`NaN` case, where `arrayROCAUC` returned `1` or `0` depending on the label order. Infinities are ordered normally, so they are unaffected and have regression tests. A `NaN` label was already order independent. Rejecting `NaN` with an exception would be backward incompatible, so I did not pick it unilaterally. If a hard error is preferred, I will switch. Requested in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/104763#issuecomment-5312328708.

signals.title: Keep the crash-report channel of clickhouse-local reachable
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed missing fatal-signal diagnostics from `clickhouse-local` when neither stdin nor stderr is attached to a terminal: a crash printed nothing at all, and `--client_logs_file` was never written. ### Description `clickhouse-local` built its crash-report channel and then discarded it: a fatal signal gave exit 134 with empty stderr and no report. `ClientApplicationBase::init` creates a splitter over stderr and binds the signal listener's logger to it. `LocalServer::processConfig` later calls `buildLoggers`, whose loop re-channels every existing logger by name, including that one. The replacement has no console child unless `logger.console` is set or a tty is attached, so the listener formatted the report into a channel with nowhere to go. `local` is the only program that is both a client and a `Loggers`, leaving `clickhouse-client` unaffected. Not CI-specific: the gate keys on `isatty` over stdin and stderr, so a run with neither on a terminal lost crash diagnostics. In CI it made 27 aborts across 7 tests undiagnosable, e.g. [PR 108078](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=108078&sha=a84b136d9ac4980b5ff9457eba8f3dbd3b1d09de&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_tsan%2C%20parallel%29). The channel is now rebound after `buildLoggers`: additively, so a configured log file keeps the report; at fatal severity only, since anything more verbose would pollute the program's own output; and dropping its own stderr child only when the configured console admits fatal records, so the report appears exactly once, never zero. File destinations go last, because the splitter walks children in order without catching a throw. Also fixed, since fatal records now route through it: `OwnSplitChannel::log` evaluated `logs_queue->isNeeded(...)` under `logs_queue == nullptr &&`, selecting the dereference rather than guarding it. Reachable with `--logger.async=0` and no log destination; the guard needs the `text_log` term its async counterpart has. Validated on x86_64 debug with a deterministic abort: stderr 0 -> 8544 bytes with the symbolized report, `--client_logs_file` created, and exactly one report with a console destination, even one whose level excludes fatal. A successful `SELECT 42` still prints only `42`, which matters for the 667 stateless tests using `clickhouse-local`. New test `04916_local_fatal_signal_report` covers ten configurations: 100/100 runs, red pre-fix, every assertion mutated. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115102&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115102](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115102+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Copy a table function's AST per read of a Distributed table
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a data race when a `Remote`/`RemoteSecure` table (or a `Distributed` table over a table function) was read by several queries at once. A table function's arguments are rewritten in place while they are parsed, and every query parsed the same AST that the storage keeps for its lifetime, so a concurrent read could observe a partially rewritten argument. ### Description `StorageDistributed` keeps `remote_table_function_ptr` for the lifetime of the storage and passes it, unguarded, to `TableFunctionFactory::get` on every read. Argument parsing rewrites the argument slots in place: `TableFunctionMerge::parseArguments` assigns `args[0] = database_ast` after folding the database name to a literal. Two concurrent queries against the same table therefore write and read the same `ASTPtr` with no synchronization. The raced eight bytes are the `intrusive_ptr` pointer slot, whose `swap` and `operator->` are not atomic, so the consequence is a use-after-free rather than a torn value. `AST fuzzer (amd_tsan)` reported it as `ThreadSanitizer: data race (STID: 3616-438e)` between `StorageMerge::evaluateDatabaseName` (read, `intrusive_ptr::operator->`) and `TableFunctionMerge::parseArguments` (write, `intrusive_ptr::swap`), both under `SelectStreamFactory::createForShardImpl`: [CI report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112928&sha=06fd0bae7343ee9366f79bc6f2563e9f35f8432d&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_tsan%29). That commit touches none of the racing files and the mutation predates it, so it only exposed a latent race. The shard loop is sequential and already clones the query AST per shard, so the racing threads are two concurrent queries, not two shards. I fixed it at the owner: `StorageDistributed::read` takes one copy of the member per call and passes it to all three consumers, and `distributedWriteBetweenDistributedTables` does the same for the source storage's member. That covers every table function reachable through these paths, so no individual `parseArguments` changes. Parsing still rewrites its arguments in place, because that normalization is what a `CREATE` persists: `merge(currentDatabase(), '^t')` is still stored as `merge('db', '^t')`. Reachable from ordinary SQL: create `ENGINE = Remote('127.0.0.1', merge(currentDatabase(), '^t'))` and read it concurrently. Validated under ThreadSanitizer with four separately built binaries: 32 concurrent readers reproduce the race without the change and the run is clean with it, and each copy is witnessed on its own by reverting just that one. The new test covers concurrent reads and a concurrent parallel `INSERT SELECT` whose optimized route is asserted, not assumed.

signals.title: Bound the storage read output resize by the number of threads that consume it
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed excessive memory usage when reading from `File`, `URL`, object storage or any storage using the generic read path with a large `max_streams_to_max_threads_ratio`. The number of output ports created after reading is now bounded by `max_threads`, so a query over a tiny table no longer allocates tens of gigabytes while building the pipeline. ### Description A `SELECT` over a three-row table can exhaust server memory: ```sql CREATE TABLE t (n UInt64) ENGINE = File(TabSeparated); INSERT INTO t VALUES (1), (2), (3); SELECT sum(n) FROM t SETTINGS max_threads = 4, max_streams_to_max_threads_ratio = 1000000; -- Code: 241 ... would use 36.33 GiB ``` Uncapped, the server is OOM-killed. Found via a ThreadSanitizer out-of-memory report inside `ResizeProcessor` plus a `Server died` / `OOM in dmesg` storm, STID 3538-49e6 ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113382&sha=222f1691027d9ce7299c3ee404e9eea1a603a0d8&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_tsan%2C%20parallel%29)) -- not caused by that pull request, it reproduces on pristine master. **Root cause.** The planner computes the stream request as `max_threads * max_streams_to_max_threads_ratio`, checked only for `size_t` representability. Each storage read that parallelises its output passes that value verbatim to `pipe.resize()`, and `ResizeProcessor` builds one `OutputPort` list node per stream, so the allocation happens while building the pipeline, before any row is read. The ratio over-requests *sources*; it must not over-allocate *output ports*. **The change.** Bound each post-read resize target by the thread width, `min(requested_streams, max_threads)`, at the four sites that decide it: `ReadFromFile`, `ReadFromURL`, `ReadFromObjectStorageStep` and the generic `IStorage::read` (reached by e.g. `Join`, which discards `num_streams` and returns one source). The guard tests the clamped value, so no pointless resize is emitted. `clampClusterFunctionNumStreams` already bounds the same resize for the `*Cluster` table functions. At `ratio = 1` (the default) the pipeline is byte-identical; above 1 the surplus ports were already discarded immediately (table below). One case narrows: a remote read through `IStorage::read` with `async_socket_for_remote = 0`, where the planner requests `max_distributed_connections` (default 1024), now resizes to `max_threads`. That is `MongoDB` / `YTsaurus` / `BigQuery` only; `Distributed` and `Merge` override the plan-level `read()`. <details> <summary>Pipeline widths, before and after</summary> `EXPLAIN PIPELINE SELECT sum(n) FROM t`, `Resize` rows only: | max_threads | ratio | before | after | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | 1, 3 | *(no resize)* | *(no resize)* | | 2 | 1 | `Resize 2 → 2 ; Resize 1 → 2` | identical | | 2 | 3 | `Resize 6 → 2 ; Resize 1 → 6` | `Resize 2 → 2 ; Resize 1 → 2` | | 4 | 1 | `Resize 4 → 4 ; Resize 1 → 4` | identical | | 4 | 3 | `Resize 12 → 4 ; Resize 1 → 12` | `Resize 4 → 4 ; Resize 1 → 4` | </details>
