signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111378 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115088 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `04550_restore_fsync_after_insert.sh` (added by #111378) read the `files` column of `system.parts` to size the encrypted-incremental-restore fsync assertion. That column was added by 476e9fcb3bb3f26 in January, after 25.8 forked, so the automated 25.8 backport #115088 fails at runtime even though the cherry-pick applied cleanly and the script is byte-identical: ``` Code: 47. Unknown expression identifier `files` in scope SELECT files FROM system.parts WHERE ... AND (`table` = 't_restore_fsync_enc'). (UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER) Code: 32. Attempt to read after eof: value cannot be parsed as UInt64 for query parameter 'files'. ``` CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115088&sha=980e9739e2ff0687cec113ed6460d38af75034f6&name_0=BackportPR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_asan%2C%20distributed%20plan%2C%20parallel%2C%201%2F2%29 The count the assertion wants is how many files RESTORE copies and must therefore fsync. The test already measures exactly that for its first table, with `SELECT path FROM system.parts` plus `find`. This drops the `system.parts.files` read and feeds the encrypted arm the same count. The two tables have identical schema, data and part-layout settings, so their parts hold the same file set; the assertion gets stronger, since the physical count also covers `checksums.txt`, `columns.txt` and the zero-byte `arr.bin` that the checksums map does not enumerate. `.reference` is unchanged. Validation: on the official 25.8 binary the old test reproduces both errors above and the new one runs to completion. On master the encrypted restore performs 20 `FileSync` events against a required 18, and the two arms' part file lists are identical on both branches (18 files on master, 15 on 25.8), so the reuse does not depend on a master-specific layout. Disabling `fsync_after_insert` on the encrypted table still fails the test, so the assertion is not vacuous. 50/50 runs green with randomized settings. Note that #115088 cannot pick this up by regeneration: the backport tree is built from #111378's merge commit, so a regenerated backport carries the same broken line. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1602` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Disable distributed index analysis with projections (wrong results)
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Disable distributed index analysis with projections (wrong results) Parts are identified by name, but projection parts share the projection's name across all parent parts, so analysis collapsed them into one entry and then filtered out valid parent parts, dropping rows. Skip distributed index analysis for projection parts (analyze locally); proper support needs parent part name + projection name on the wire. Note, that the problem not only for applied projections: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/7604e8de0caf5940d9e66872bcfb8dffcc602c5b/src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/optimizeUseNormalProjection.cpp#L617-L637 But for any tables with usable projections, since we try to filter out parts based on the analysis from projections as well: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/7604e8de0caf5940d9e66872bcfb8dffcc602c5b/src/Processors/QueryPlan/Optimizations/projectionsCommon.cpp#L418 <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115132&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115132](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115132+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Backported to: `26.7.4.58` <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Accept LowCardinality(UInt64) as a dictionary simple primary key
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/104539 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `CREATE DICTIONARY` failing with `Incorrect type of ID column: must be UInt64, but it is LowCardinality` when the simple primary key is declared as `LowCardinality(UInt64)` and `dictionary_validate_primary_key_type` is enabled. Closes #104539. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/104539 With `dictionary_validate_primary_key_type = 1`, declaring a simple primary key as `LowCardinality(UInt64)` is rejected: ``` Code: 36. DB::Exception: Incorrect type of ID column: must be UInt64, but it is LowCardinality. (BAD_ARGUMENTS) ``` With the setting off (the default) the same dictionary is created, loads, and answers `dictGet`/`dictHas`/`SELECT *` correctly, with the key normalized to plain `UInt64`. So valid input is rejected. **Root cause.** `StorageDictionary::getNamesAndTypes` compared the raw outer `TypeIndex` of the declared key type against `TypeIndex::UInt64`. For `LowCardinality(UInt64)` that yields the wrapper's index, not the payload's. `LowCardinality` is a physical-representation wrapper, not a distinct logical type, so the validator answered a logical question with a physical predicate. **The change** unwraps one `LowCardinality` level before the comparison, for both the test and the message. The declared simple-key type is already advisory everywhere else: `getKeyTypes()` returns `{UInt64}` unconditionally and every other simple-key site constructs `DataTypeUInt64` directly, which is why the setting-off path already worked. This is the only site in `src/` that type-tests the declared key type. **Exactly one type changes behaviour:** `LowCardinality(UInt64)` becomes accepted. `Nullable(UInt64)` and `LowCardinality(Nullable(UInt64))` stay rejected, since a NULL key is meaningless for a lookup; one-level unwrap gives that for free, and the new test pins it so a later switch to `removeLowCardinalityAndNullable` cannot silently widen it. `LowCardinality(String)` also stays rejected, as a plain `String` key is rejected by design; its message now names the payload. The setting's default (`false`) is unchanged and nothing valid today becomes invalid, so no `SettingsChangesHistory.cpp` entry applies. Noted, not addressed here: `LowCardinality` keys are only constructible on `LAYOUT(FLAT())`, because `DictionaryStructure::getAttributes` strips `Nullable` but not `LowCardinality` and `AttributeUnderlyingType` has no `LowCardinality` member, so other layouts fail earlier with `UNKNOWN_TYPE` regardless of this setting.

signals.title: perf(promql): Fuse identical agg(X) op agg(X) into one PromQL aggregation pass
signals.text: When both sides of a math binary operator are one-argument aggregations over the same expression and grouping, scan once and compute both aggregates together instead of joining two identical grids. This is admittedly pretty niche, so let me know if this isn't worth it. Produced a cold speedup of 0.163 s → 0.127 s (-22%) for: ```promql sum(namespace_cpu:kube_pod_container_resource_requests:sum{cluster="bench"}) - (sum(kube_node_status_allocatable{job="kube-state-metrics", resource="cpu", cluster="bench"}) - max(kube_node_status_allocatable{job="kube-state-metrics", resource="cpu", cluster="bench"})) > 0 ``` <details> <summary>SQL diff</summary> ```diff --- master (unfused) +++ fused @@ -7,30 +7,8 @@ FROM prometheus_query_step_1 GROUP BY group), prometheus_query_step_3 AS ( - SELECT CAST(0, 'UInt64') AS new_group, sumForEach(`values`) AS `values` + SELECT CAST(0, 'UInt64') AS group, arrayMap(lambda(tuple(x, y), minus(x, y)), sumForEach(`values`), maxForEach(`values`)) AS `values` FROM prometheus_query_step_2 - HAVING notEmpty(`values`)), -prometheus_query_step_4 AS ( - SELECT timeSeriesIdToGroup(id) AS group, timestamp, value - FROM timeSeriesSelector('default', 'prometheus', 'm', toDateTime64(toDecimal128('-169.999', 3), 3), toDateTime64(toDecimal128('130', 3), 3))), -prometheus_query_step_5 AS ( - SELECT group AS original_group, group AS join_group, `values` - FROM prometheus_query_step_8), -prometheus_query_step_11 AS ( - SELECT join_group AS group, arrayMap(lambda(tuple(x, y), minus(x, y)), prometheus_query_step_9.`values`, prometheus_query_step_10.`values`) AS `values` - signals.title: Fix compiled `if`/`multiIf` on a negative `Time` value
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `if` and `multiIf` returning a large positive value instead of a negative one when a `Time` branch is combined with `Time64`, `DateTime` or `DateTime64` and the expression is JIT-compiled. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115381 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114168 (found there in review; a separate mechanism) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/103390 A negative `Time` value read through a JIT-compiled `if`/`multiIf` comes back as a huge positive number: ```sql SELECT if(number % 2 = 0, toTime('-01:00:00'), toTime64('00:00:00', 3)) FROM numbers(1); -- executions 1-3: -01:00:00.000 -- execution 4+: 999:59:59.000 ``` No `SETTINGS` clause is needed to hit this: `compile_expressions` defaults to `1` and `min_count_to_compile_expression` to `3`, so the 4th execution of the expression in a session silently changes the answer. `enable_time_time64_type` also defaults to `1`. The wrong value is ticks `4294963696` = `2^32 - 3600`, i.e. the negative `Int32` tick count zero-extended to 64 bits. Root cause: `typeIsSigned` in `src/DataTypes/Native.cpp` did not list the `Time` family, so the widening cast emitted by `FunctionIfBase::compileImpl` asked whether `Time` is signed, got `false`, and LLVM emitted `zext` where `sext` was required. `Time` is `DataTypeNumberBase<Int32>` and is the only member of the date/time family that widens on this path, which is why the defect is specific to it. `Time64` is included in the same predicate for correctness of the contract: `isDecimal()` matches only `TypeIndex::Decimal32..256` and so does not cover `TypeIndex::Time64` - the same reason `isDateTime64()` is listed separately. No wrong-result carrier reaches the `Time64` half today, so it is not given a test that could not fail. Validation: five wrong-result carriers plus a `Nullable(Time)` case are covered by the new test. The reference values were taken from the non-compiled path on an unpatched binary, so the oracle is independent of this change. With the predicate token removed the test fails on 7 of 13 lines; non-negative `Time`, large-negative `Time`, and `DateTime64` controls are unchanged. 50/50 runs under settings randomization pass.

signals.title: Fix THERE_IS_NO_COLUMN for DISTINCT with an aggregate projection
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112168 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `THERE_IS_NO_COLUMN` ("Cannot find column in source stream") for `SELECT DISTINCT expr(k) ... ORDER BY k` on a table that has an aggregate projection grouped on `k`. Closes #112168. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112168 `SELECT DISTINCT v * 2 FROM t ORDER BY v` works on an ordinary table, but throws as soon as `t` carries an aggregate projection grouped on `v`: ``` Code: 8. Cannot find column `__table1.v` in source stream, there are only columns: [multiply(__table1.v, 2_UInt8)]. (THERE_IS_NO_COLUMN) ``` **Root cause.** `DistinctStep` passes its input header through (`updateOutputHeader` assigns `input_headers.front()`), so that header carries the DISTINCT columns *plus* anything a later step needs, here the `ORDER BY` source column. The aggregate-projection matcher was handed only `DistinctStep::getColumnNames()`, so `foldActionsByProjection` emitted a subtree without the extra column, and the splice that must reproduce the step's full header then failed inside `ActionsDAG::makeConvertingActions`. Only `optimize_use_projections = 0` worked around it, because this pass is gated on `optimize_projection` rather than on `query_plan_enable_optimizations`. **The change** passes the step's output header names, the set the replacement subtree is actually required to produce. Matching then declines by itself when a required column is not computable from the projection keys, so those queries fall back to the ordinary read; queries whose extra column is a function of the projection keys keep using the projection. Names are taken verbatim without de-duplication, since `makeConvertingActions` consumes one input position per result column and `checkBlockStructure` compares positionally. **Validation.** Both directions on a debug build. Each arm compares the `optimize_use_projections = 1` result against the `= 0` result, asserting the value set rather than an ordering that `ORDER BY` on a column outside the DISTINCT list leaves ambiguous. Arms cover the reported query, a filter, an `ORDER BY` column the projection cannot produce, a two-key projection, partial projection data, `LowCardinality` and `Nullable` keys, and a repeated DISTINCT expression. Each also asserts via `EXPLAIN` that the projection is still selected where usable and declined where not, so a silent fallback cannot pass as a correct result.

signals.title: Web terminal: do not connect before the host page supplies the credentials
signals.text: A `/webterminal` page embedded in a host page - `play.html`, or the ClickHouse Cloud console - is loaded without credentials in its URL and receives them from the host page over `postMessage`, on the iframe's `load` event. It nevertheless opened a connection of its own at startup, before that message could arrive, so every embedded terminal authenticated twice: first with an empty password, which can only succeed for a passwordless user, and then, a moment later, with the credentials from the host page, after the first WebSocket had been closed and replaced. The visible symptom is `Connecting...` printed twice - `attemptConnect` announces every attempt, and whether the first line is erased before the second is printed depends on timing. Behind it are a wasted WebSocket, a guaranteed-failing authentication, and, for a passwordless user, an established session that gets torn down right away. The page now waits for the credentials instead of connecting on its own. A host page that never sends them - it does not implement the protocol, or its origin is not trusted - would leave a terminal that neither connects nor prompts, so the page says that it is waiting and Enter hands the login over to the interactive prompt; credentials arriving after that no longer hijack what the user is typing. The pages opened as a normal tab, or with a `user` URL parameter, keep connecting immediately. The wait became a state of the page's own state machine, which makes the `waitingForCredentials` and `initialAutoAuth` flags, and the `ws.onclose` branch they served, unnecessary. The new `tests/integration/test_webterminal_startup` follows the existing `test_play_reconcile_startup`: it fetches `/webterminal` from a real server and runs the page's real script in a Node `vm` with a stubbed terminal and `WebSocket`, then drives each flow and asserts which connections were opened and what was displayed. Against this branch all 34 checks pass; against `master` 23 fail, including `announces the attempt exactly once -- actual: 2`. It also pins the paths that must keep connecting immediately, the prompt after a rejected password, and that credentials from an untrusted origin, from a trusted host over plain HTTP, or from a window that is not the parent are ignored - the wait is now the only way into an embedded session, so a hole in either check would hand the terminal to a foreign page. Reported by a user of clickhouse.new, where the console drives the terminal through exactly this embedded flow. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/105191 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115067 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): A web terminal embedded in another page, such as the SQL console or `play.html`, receives its credentials from that page and no longer opens a connection of its own before they arrive. Previously it connected twice - once with an empty password, then again with the real credentials - and printed `Connecting...` twice. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115148&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115148](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115148+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Reduce the per-arm work of 04895_parquet_dictionary_source_prefetch_lifetime
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114668 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114668 (the use-after-free this test guards). @ PedroTadim asked for the per-arm work of this test to be trimmed. `04895` runs at 93.5% of the flaky check's 180 s per-arm cap on `Stateless tests (amd_asan_ubsan, flaky check)`: p50 141.5 s, p99 165.9 s, max 168.3 s over 50 arms in 21 days of public CIDB, so about 12 s of headroom. No duration breach yet, so this is headroom rather than a live failure. The fixture is larger than the mechanism needs. The detector requires many concurrent queued read ranges alive at throw time, and what supplies them is the row group count plus `input_format_parquet_local_file_min_bytes_for_seek = 1` and the 32 download / 32 parsing threads. None of that depends on payload size. Scaling `numbers()` and `output_format_parquet_row_group_size` by the same factor of 10 keeps the row group count at exactly 397 while cutting the file from 19,785,515 to 2,356,314 bytes. I did not shrink `repeat('y', 400)`: it is a single distinct value, so it is RLE_DICTIONARY encoded to about 0.25 B/row. `key` is 97.5% of the file and `val` 2.5%, and cutting the string width from 400 to 40 moves total bytes by only 18%. Validation. Against a binary with the `resetReadBuffer` override removed, the trimmed test fails 20/20 with the pure-virtual abort at `Prefetcher.cpp:116` in `readSync`, and passes 20/20 with the fix. Because both the trimmed and the untrimmed fixture saturate at 20/20 there, I lowered the thread counts until redness became fractional to get resolution: at 8 threads the trimmed fixture reddens 30/40 versus 4/40 untrimmed, so the trim makes the detector more sensitive, not less. All three oracles are unchanged and were each shown able to redden, `.reference` is untouched, and 50 randomized runs pass. <details> <summary>Measured duration, ASAN, trimmed vs current</summary> `tests/clickhouse-test`, randomized settings, 12 arms each against the same server: | arm | min | p50 | p90 | max | |---|---|---|---|---| | trimmed | 20.03 s | 20.84 s | 21.34 s | 21.90 s | | current | 21.14 s | 22.90 s | 23.49 s | 23.65 s | The serial gain is about 9% because the roughly 2000 row group reads per arm are deliberately kept. The gain grows with concurrency, which is the regime the flaky check runs in, since `allow_oversubscription` is False there and every worker runs the same test: | concurrent copies | trimmed p50 | current p50 | saving | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | 11.43 s | 12.51 s | 8.6% | | 8 | 12.31 s | 15.16 s | 18.8% | | 16 | 12.87 s | 19.44 s | 33.8% | | 20 | 13.66 s | 22.67 s | 39.7% | Server side, reload phase IO drops from 54.24 MiB to 13.99 MiB at an identical 1985 row group reads. These are local numbers on one box and do not predict a contended CI runner, so there is no timing assertion in the test. </details> <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115149&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115149](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115149+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1623` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Do not serve min/max from an unusable minmax_count projection bound
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111938 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `min` and `max` returning a wrong value when the implicit `_minmax_count_projection` answered them from a part-level bound that is not a real row value: a `NULL` in a `Nullable` sorting key, a `NaN` in a float key, or a `Tuple` bound assembled component-wise. Such a query now reads rows instead of using the projection. ### Description `getMinMaxCountProjectionBlock` answers `min(col)`/`max(col)` from part-level bounds, feeding each straight into an aggregate state. That is only correct when the bound is a real row value, ordered as the aggregate orders it. Three ways it is not: - **NULL** (as reported): keys sort NULLS LAST so the top index entry is a NULL while `max` skips NULLs, and the `POSITIVE_INFINITY` pruning sentinel materializes as a SQL NULL. - **NaN**, no `Nullable` involved: the writer sorts NaN above every number while `max` skips it, so `Float64 ORDER BY k` over `(1),(200),(nan)` gives `nan`. - **Component-wise synthesis**, no NULL or NaN: `getExtremes` runs per column, so a `Tuple` bound envelopes each component's extreme and need not be any row. This breaks `min` too. Worse than the reported `NULL` is the silent shape: when the true maximum shares a part with a NULL, `max` returns the largest of the other parts, `4` instead of `200`. The fix declines the implicit projection for such a query, reusing the escape hatch this function already has earlier (`return {}` when a part has no final mark). A part whose bound pair is one repeated degenerate value stays exempt, since skipping it is the right contribution; for an index bound that exemption also requires a final mark, without which the index samples granule starts only and a repeated pair proves nothing. I rejected skipping only the poisoned part, which is the silent shape above, and changing the write path, since the sentinel is needed for `IS NULL` pruning and existing parts would stay broken. The new test covers each class across nullable, low-cardinality, tuple and float keys, ASC and DESC, one and several parts, and a part with no final mark. Issue #104412 is a different defect here, verified unaffected.

signals.title: Fix wrong count and wrong DELETE when a NULL expression sits under NOT
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112242 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112242 Requested by @ nihalzp in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112242#issuecomment-5312306258 (reported by @ zlareb1). ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed wrong results when a `WHERE` clause contained a `NULL` expression under a `NOT`, for example `SELECT count() FROM t WHERE NOT (id >= 20 AND NULL)`. Index analysis treated such a condition as provably true for the whole range, so the filter was skipped: `count()` returned rows the query rejects, and `ALTER TABLE ... DELETE` with that condition removed rows it should have kept. ### Description ```sql CREATE TABLE t (id UInt32) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id; INSERT INTO t SELECT number FROM numbers(40); SELECT count() FROM t WHERE NOT (id >= 20 AND NULL); -- returned 40, correct is 20 ``` Reading the rows returned 20, so `count()` and the row set disagreed on one predicate. A mutation was worse: `ALTER TABLE t DELETE WHERE NOT (id >= 38 AND NULL)` deleted all 40 rows, although the predicate is `NULL` for `id` 38 and 39, so those two had to survive. **Root cause.** `cloneDAGWithInversionPushDown` pushes `NOT` to the leaves. For `NOT (id >= 20 AND NULL)`, De Morgan turns the `and` into an `or` and pushes the inversion into both children; the all-NULL leaf is not recognized, so the tail wraps it in a literal `not()`, which `RPNBuilder` complements classically into "provably true for every row". Both steps hold only in two-valued logic: `NOT NULL` is `NULL`, which `WHERE` must reject. **The change.** Before the node dispatch, an all-NULL node absorbs the inversion instead of receiving a `not()` wrapper, the same idiom the neighbouring `materialize` and trivial-cast branches use. It still folds to "never true" downstream, correct because `NULL` is not `TRUE`, and a non-negated `x AND NULL` keeps its exact fast path. Absorbing the inversion substitutes the operand's type for the `not()` result type, so the guard is confined to `boolean_context`, the existing flag for positions where the caller discards the value. In a value position a negation would otherwise change type and drop valid rows. The all-NULL test needs both a column and a type check: `toInt64OrNull('x')` is typed `Nullable(Int64)`, while `if(id % 2, NULL, NULL)` has no constant column. <details> <summary>Validation</summary> Debug build of the base commit vs the same build with the change. | probe | base | with change | correct | |---|---|---|---| | `count() WHERE NOT (id >= 20 AND NULL)` | 40 | 20 | 20 | | same with `toInt64OrNull('x')` | 40 | 20 | 20 | | same with `CAST(NULL, 'Nullable(UInt8)')` | 40 | 20 | 20 | | same with `if(id % 2, NULL, NULL)` | 40 | 20 | 20 | | same with `materialize(NULL)` | 40 | 20 | 20 | | `numbers(100) WHERE NOT (number = 5 AND NULL) LIMIT 10` | 9 | 10 | 10 | | minmax skip index, same predicate | 40 | 20 | 20 | | `ALTER DELETE WHERE NOT (id >= 38 AND NULL)`, survivors | `[]` | `[38,39]` | `[38,39]` | | `count() WHERE id >= 20 AND NULL` | 0 | 0 | 0 | | `numbers() WHERE number > 0 AND NULL LIMIT 10` | 0 fast | 0 fast | 0 fast | | value position, `ifNull(NOT materialize(CAST(NULL, 'Nullable(Int64)')), 0)`, rows | 40 | 40 | 40 | | same with `Nullable(Float64)`, rows | 40 | 40 | 40 | The new test fails on the base build, passes with the change, and passed 50/50 randomized runs. Deleting any one of the three parts of the guard makes it fail again on exactly the arms that part covers: the column test covers `toInt64OrNull` and `CAST`, the type test covers `if(id % 2, NULL, NULL)`, the `boolean_context` test covers the two value-position arms. The unbounded `numbers()` lines pin the positive direction, which an earlier attempt at this fix turned into a hang. The projection, `KeyCondition` and minmax test families were run on both builds: the same 23 tests fail either way, all on ZooKeeper and distributed connections unavailable in this sandbox, none mentioning the exact-count projection or `KeyCondition`. </details>

signals.title: Carry the join analyze mode into a SQL SECURITY view's context
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` losing the join statistics of a view declared `SQL SECURITY DEFINER` or `SQL SECURITY NONE` whose body contains a JOIN. In debug and sanitizer builds the query aborted with the logical error `JoinStep analyzed without the analyze mode`. ### Description The assertion is at `JoinStep.cpp:268`. In release it is compiled out, and the report is then built from statistics the join was never told to collect. `join_analyze_mode` is a `Context` member field, not a setting, and only `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` arms it. `Context::createCopy` carries it, which is why a bare JOIN, a plain view and an `INVOKER` view all report correctly. But `StorageInMemoryMetadata::getSQLSecurityOverriddenContext` rebuilds the context from the *global* one for `DEFINER` and `NONE`, then hand-carries a curated list of caller state onto it, and `join_analyze_mode` was missing from that list. The view's inner joins were planned with the mode off, and the walker then reached them. The fix carries the field across that rebuild: one line, above the `NONE` early return so it covers both branches, beside the existing `setNormalizedQueryHash` carry which exists for the same reason. It is inert unless `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` armed the outer context, and it cannot weaken the barrier the rebuild creates, because the mode selects diagnostic statistics, not identity or access rights. The failure is deterministic in six lines of SQL. New test `04926` covers `DEFINER`, `NONE`, a `DEFINER` view joining an `ENGINE = Join` table (the sibling assertion at `JoinStep.cpp:490`), and an `INVOKER` control. It asserts the statistics arrived rather than that nothing aborted, since a no-abort check passes vacuously in release. Unpatched, the first three arms abort and the control passes; with the fix all four pass, 50/50 under randomized settings. Two residuals. A second fuzzer shape reaches the same assertion through `prometheusQuery` with no view involved; it did not reproduce on either binary, so it is not root-caused. A deserialized remote plan also never sets the mode, but `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` refuses distributed plans. Found by the AST fuzzer: - https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114038&sha=cc2993d762348f09f324efc04cc1c8f43819da3e&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29 - https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114867&sha=f4c473e73f752fa079dc3caec5b0151adefe91e6&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29 <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1654` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Support the delayed set-building step when decorrelating a subquery
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113182 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` error `Cannot decorrelate query, because 'DelayedCreatingSets' step is not supported` for a correlated subquery whose body contains an `IN (SELECT ...)` set. This included queries with no explicit `IN`, because `optimize_inverse_dictionary_lookup` (enabled by default) rewrites a `dictGet(...)` comparison into such a set. ### Description A valid query failed to plan when a correlated subquery body contained an `IN` set. ``` Code: 48. DB::Exception: Cannot decorrelate query, because 'DelayedCreatingSets' step is not supported. (NOT_IMPLEMENTED) ``` **Root cause.** The correlated body is planned by a nested `Planner`, which appends a `DelayedCreatingSetsStep` whenever the body used an `IN (subquery)` set. `decorrelateQueryPlan` has one handler per step type and throws for anything else. **The reported query is one spelling of it.** `optimize_inverse_dictionary_lookup` merely rewrites `dictGet(...) >= c` into a set, planting the step. A hand-written `IN (SELECT ...)` reproduces it with no dictionary, as do `GLOBAL IN`, `NOT IN`, correlated `NOT EXISTS` and the scalar form. Guarding the pass would leave those failing, so the fix is in the decorrelator. **The change** adds a handler for that step, mirroring the existing unary handlers: recurse into the child, refresh the header, re-add the step. The step is a planning-time placeholder whose output header equals its input, and a set reaching the decorrelator cannot reference the correlated columns, since a correlated subquery on either side of `IN` is already rejected during analysis. So it stays where the planner put it, and no set is rebuilt per outer row. **Validation.** New stateless test, both directions confirmed on locally built binaries. Every expected value comes from rewriting the query with an equivalent constant `IN`, never from the fixed binary's own output; the plan is asserted with `EXPLAIN` plus a positive control, since an empty step is optimized out and rows alone cannot witness it. 50 randomized runs pass, as do the `--replicated-database` and `optimize_inverse_dictionary_lookup=0` arms. Sibling issue #112030 is not covered: same producer, unrelated carrier, no decorrelator involvement. If you want the test smaller, tell me which cases to keep and I will trim it.

signals.title: Add a preliminary DISTINCT to UNION DISTINCT
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115104 (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114550 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115104 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114550 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `A UNION DISTINCT B` now deduplicates each branch in parallel before merging them, the same way its `SELECT DISTINCT * FROM (A UNION ALL B)` rewrite already did. Previously every row funnelled through a single `DistinctTransform`, so the query did not scale with `max_threads`. ### Description `A UNION DISTINCT B` and `SELECT DISTINCT * FROM (A UNION ALL B)` are the same query but got different pipelines: the rewrite deduplicates each branch before the merge, `UNION DISTINCT` did not. **Root cause.** The union branch of `Planner::buildPlanForUnionNode` (and its old-analyzer twin in `InterpreterSelectWithUnionQuery::buildQueryPlan`) added one `DistinctStep` with `pre_distinct = false`. `DistinctStep::getTraits` sets `returns_single_stream = !pre_distinct`, so that one step both merged to one stream and deduplicated. The `SELECT DISTINCT` path adds two steps. **The change** adds a `pre_distinct = true` step before the existing one, in both planners. `liftUpUnion` then clones it into each branch, which is how the rewrite gets its per-branch distinct. No new setting, no change to `DistinctStep` or any pass. Scoped to `UNION_DISTINCT`: `INTERSECT`/`EXCEPT DISTINCT` share the `is_distinct` branch, but `IntersectOrExceptStep` already resizes every branch to one stream and `liftUpUnion` does not handle it, so a preliminary step there is overhead. Their plans are unchanged. **Measured** (release build, 8M rows/branch, 2000 distinct values, best of 7, `query_duration_ms`): | max_threads | before | after | |---|---|---| | 1 | 60 ms | 61 ms | | 8 | 44 ms | 13 ms | | 16 | 59 ms | 9 ms | The rewrite scores 13 ms / 8 ms here, so the two forms now agree. With all-distinct data the preliminary step is overhead, at the cost the rewrite already pays. A preliminary DISTINCT keeps one hash table per stream, and this one carries the same `max_rows_in_distinct` / `max_bytes_in_distinct`, so exactly as in the rewrite those limits now bind per stream as well as globally; both overflow modes measured identical to the rewrite. The new test asserts the plan shape, not timing, and checks results against the rewrite across `Nullable`, `LowCardinality`, `Array`, aggregate-state and coerced-type branches, chains, `LIMIT`/`LIMIT BY` and size limits. <details> <summary>Interaction with #114550 (measured)</summary> #114550 "Deduplicate the final DISTINCT in parallel" attacks the same bottleneck from the other side and edits the same two functions. Measured on its head `1e783f46`, same fixture and method: | arm | t1 | t8 | t16 | |---|---|---|---| | master | 60 ms | 44 ms | 59 ms | | #114550 alone | 57 ms | 22 ms | 17 ms | | this PR alone | 61 ms | 13 ms | 9 ms | | #114550 + this PR | 60 ms | 11 ms | 7 ms | #114550 parallelizes the final dedup; this PR reduces how many rows reach it. They stack, and #114550 alone does not close the reported gap. It keeps `pre_distinct = false` at the union site, so the conflict is textual only - whoever merges second rebases. </details>

signals.title: Bound submodule cache population so it cannot kill the Config Workflow job
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114811 `Config Workflow` computes the workflow matrix, so when it dies no build and no test job is scheduled. On a submodule cache miss it clones 141 submodules inside its own `timeout=600` budget, and when that does not finish praktika SIGTERMs the job, silently dropping the matrix: the public `26.5` run at `f724d2da9360` recorded 4 checks against 102-155 on healthy commits, and the run still looks finished because `Finish Workflow` reports success afterwards. 7 occurrences over 7 refs in 30 days, including a release branch and three backport PRs. This bounds the clone with `timeout -s KILL` at 600s, above p99 494.5s and the slowest population that currently succeeds (517s), and raises the job cap to `SUBMODULE_CACHE_POPULATE_TIMEOUT_SEC + 600`, 1200s by default, above the 828s worst case (600 clone + 44 tar and upload + 184 rest of the job). Deriving the cap keeps it above the step bound under a per-repository override; were the two equal the job watchdog would fire first. A test pins that ordering. Per @ maxknv's review the step now fails when the cache cannot be populated, instead of reporting `OK` and accepting a miss. Accepting it only degrades cleanly if every dependant can run its own `git submodule update`; dependants clone unauthenticated while this path can use the App installation token, so under `ENABLE_SUBMODULE_CLONE_AUTH` a private submodule is unreachable to them and continuing would schedule checkout failures whose cause is no longer visible. The bound is what makes the timeout reportable: a job-level SIGTERM leaves no result at all. `retries` is dropped because `Shell.check` applies `timeout` per retry, not as a total. Verified by driving the real function both ways: an exhausted budget fails with the hash unset and nothing uploaded, a generous one still populates the cache. YAML regeneration is unchanged.

signals.title: Build profile diff: report why a gh api call failed
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115061 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `Build profile diff` failed on #115061 with a message naming only the `gh` argv ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115061&sha=9a8c54a155a55828cef1e38c76a31aca80038099&name_0=PR&name_1=Build%20profile%20diff), [job log](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/actions/runs/32027518805/job/95431729878)): ``` CalledProcessError: Command '['gh', 'api', 'repos/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/commits?sha=a3f55f04… ``` Two things discarded the reason. `_list_commits_page` used `check=True`, and `CalledProcessError.__str__` renders only argv, so the captured `stderr`/`stdout` carrying the HTTP status were never read. The message then went through `md_code`, a table-cell *name* formatter (`MAX_NAME_LEN = 100`), which cut the tail. So 404, 403 and 5xx produced the same 102-character string, and the walk makes up to 60 calls without naming which one failed. Report it instead: exit code and endpoint first, then `stderr` and `stdout` each capped at 300 characters with an elision marker, in the field order `GH.get_output_with_retries` uses. `TimeoutExpired` is caught in the same place. `timeout=120` is kept deliberately - `gh` bounds connect and TLS handshake but not a stalled response body (measured 240 s unbounded), so the shared praktika helper, which passes no timeout, would unbound a bounded call site. `md_message` is added beside `md_code` for the comment path, bounded head+tail so the end of a message survives. `md_code` and `MAX_NAME_LEN` are untouched, so its 17 name callers are byte-identical. The bound matters beyond `gh`: a cluster query failure reaches the same handler carrying its whole inlined SQL, measured at 54952 characters against GitHub's 65536 limit. The `gh api` failure itself is environmental and out of scope: the byte-identical call succeeds 25 times out of 25 by hand. Validated with a throwaway harness, 30 assertions plus three mutation arms each reverting one hunk: 404, 403 and 5xx give three distinct messages where they gave one, and the success path, the `extend_master_shas` fail-close and the single-attempt contract are unchanged. `ci/tests/`: 711 passed, its 2 failures pre-existing on master. No committed test, per `.claude/CLAUDE.md`: `ci/tests/test_build_profile_diff_job.py` was removed in #114675. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115201&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115201](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115201+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Sum the adaptive aggregation seal normalization assertion over the three arms
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115034 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115034 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `04676_adaptive_aggregation_replicated_argument`, which I added in #115034, is flaky: as of 2026-08-17 20:00 UTC it had failed 22 times across 22 unrelated pull requests against 1341 passes, roughly 1.6%, and it is still firing. Every failure is one of three assertion lines flipping `1` to `0`, for example `+normalized nullable 0`. [Sample report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=108431&sha=61e924073e8505f78ac3e3438e2a180a07c740df&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_debug%2C%20distributed%20plan%2C%20s3%20storage%2C%20parallel%29) (`Stateless tests (amd_debug, distributed plan, s3 storage, parallel)` on #108431). The test asserted `AdaptiveAggregationSealNormalizations > 0` separately for each of its three argument representations. That counter fires in `Aggregator::sealPendingChunks` only when the batches one producer buffered together disagree at an argument position, which needs two batches buffered in one producer, both representations reachable, and one producer holding blocks of both kinds. The test pins only the second; the others are a read pool decision and thread scheduling, so a non-zero count for a single query is not an engine guarantee. Randomization is not the cause: it also reproduces with randomization off and with `enable_lazy_columns_replication 0`. This sums the counter over the three arms instead, which is the property the engine does guarantee, and changes nothing else. The three queries stay separate, so each keeps its own value comparison and its own abort site; the `sealed chunks` assertion, the six value lines and the tags are untouched. Within one run the test no longer proves that every representation reached the normalization. `04654` already asserts the sibling `AdaptiveAggregationSealedChunks` in aggregate. Validation: in one interleaved loop the old form failed twice while the new form passed 300 of 300. Of 600 runs, 6 had an arm at zero and all 6 still had a non-zero total. With #115034's fix reverted the new form aborts 20 of 20 with `Bad cast from type DB::ColumnReplicated to DB::ColumnVector` in `sealPendingChunks`. 50 runs with randomized settings and 50 without both pass. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115204&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115204](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115204+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Perf: Optimize PromQL or for exact groups
signals.text: ## What changed - add a fast path for the PromQL set operator `or` - use it when both inputs already match on the original `group` column - decide the fast path from the operator modifiers and `metric_name_dropped` flags, without building temporary match-key ASTs - send exact-group inputs directly to the existing `FULL ALL JOIN` merge - use a compact per-step presence mask in the general `or` path instead of counting every non-NULL value - keep `on(...)`, non-empty `ignoring(...)`, `on()`, and other transformed matching keys on the current general path - treat empty `ignoring()` like default matching when both groups are already exact ## Why this is safe `VECTOR_GRID` guarantees one row per `group`. The fast path is enabled only when the matching rules leave the original `group` column unchanged on both sides, so the join key is already unique and exact. This includes normal matching and empty `ignoring()` after both inputs have already dropped `__name__`. `on(...)`, `on()`, non-empty `ignoring(...)`, and other transformed matching keys keep the existing general path. The exact-group path removes the redundant per-group aggregation, the RHS masking join, the materialized left CTE, and the second left-grid read. The final merge still uses the existing element-wise left-side preference for overlapping samples. For the general path, Step 1 only needs to know whether each timestamp has any left value. `groupBitOrForEach(arrayMap(isNotNull, values))` stores that presence mask directly instead of materializing a wider count array. The masking behavior is unchanged. ## Benchmark These benchmarks use the same **8,000-series / 300-sample** workload. Higher QPS means higher throughput for the same query. ### End-to-end PromQL Setup: `tests/performance/promql_set_operators.xml`, **10 measured runs** per server. | Query | Baseline | Patch | Relative | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | exact-group `or` | 146.8 ms | 128.9 ms | **1.14x speedup (-12.2%)** | | exact-group `or`, repeat | 157.6 ms | 134.5 ms | **1.17x speedup (-14.7%)** | | `or on(instance)` control | 143.9 ms | 145.9 ms | within noise | | `or on(instance)` control, repeat | 155.5 ms | 158.1 ms | within noise | The exact-group case is **1.14x to 1.17x faster** across the two runs. The control remains on the general path and the patch adds no extra scans or joins; the measured 1.4% to 1.7% variation is within normal run-to-run noise. The compact presence mask also reduces the size of the general-path intermediate state. ### Focused SQL lowering Setup: persistent server, **20 measured runs**, `max_threads=4`, **8,000 rows / 4,000 groups / 300-step arrays**. | Workload | General full lowering | Exact full merge | Relative | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Full lowering | 28.1 QPS | 56.5 QPS | **2.01x throughput (+101%)** | Both forms returned **1,128,000** present samples. ## Tests - add grouped `or` coverage where both sides have already dropped `__name__`, including empty `ignoring()` - cover different missing timestamps and compare the result with Prometheus - add `tests/performance/promql_set_operators.xml` with an exact-group query and an `or on(instance)` control - document that the merge helper expects unique `VECTOR_GRID` groups ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): PromQL `or` expressions with an exact group key skip redundant matching stages and use compact presence masks for transformed matching. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115219&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115219](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115219+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Remove a duplicate decimal rescaling helper that did not check for overflow
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114886 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a signed integer overflow when a `Decimal` argument passed to `prometheusQuery` or `prometheusQueryRange` had to be rescaled to the table's timestamp scale. Such an argument returned an unrelated timestamp, or made the query attempt a huge allocation, instead of reporting `DECIMAL_OVERFLOW`. ### Description Found by the AST fuzzer, check `AST fuzzer (arm_asan_ubsan)`, STID `3715-3c49` ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109480&sha=480e82b8b2a16cdfa145b984a2270ef95cf3d518&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28arm_asan_ubsan%29)): ``` src/Core/DecimalFunctions.h:444:55: runtime error: signed integer overflow: 9007199254740990976 * 1000000 cannot be represented in type 'long' ``` Reached from ordinary table-function argument parsing. Root cause is duplication rather than a missing check. `DecimalUtils::convertTo(to_scale, decimal, scale)` was a second implementation of decimal-to-decimal rescaling and the weaker of the two: it multiplied by the scale multiplier with a plain `*`, and narrowed through `Decimal::convertTo` (a bare `static_cast`) before multiplying. `convertDecimals` already did this correctly, promoting to the wider native type first, guarding the multiply with `common::mulOverflow`, and range-checking when narrowing. `FunctionsConversion.h` and `KeyCondition.cpp` both document no-wrap as this helper's contract, so the unguarded overload was the outlier. It is removed here and its four call sites go through `convertDecimals`, making the `src/` diff a net reduction. Without the fix a release build silently returns a wrapped timestamp (`toDecimal64(10000000000, 3)` against a `DateTime64(9)` table gives `1702-05-02 18:12:06.290448384`); for `prometheusQueryRange` the wrapped bounds inflate the step count until the query attempts an 8 GiB allocation. Validation: the UBSan abort reproduces on master and is gone after the change; 12 in-range values covering all three scale directions, both source widths and the exact `Int64` boundary are byte-identical before and after; new test `04926`. Known residual, not addressed here: `common::mulOverflow` does not detect `Int128`/`Int256` overflow (`base/base/arithmeticOverflow.h` says so), so a `Decimal128` rescale can still wrap. That is pre-existing, unreachable from these call sites (all `Int64`-native), and not regressed here. Complements #114886, which fixes the `UInt64` argument form in the same function and touches neither `DecimalFunctions.h` nor the decimal cases. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115220&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115220](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115220+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Do not schedule Build profile diff when the profiled build is unaffected
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115163 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Requested by @ thevar1able in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115163#issuecomment-5318430318: `Build profile diff` ran on changes involving no builds. His PR changes only `utils/exclude-authors.txt`, yet the job ran, found no profile data for the head and posted nothing. `digest_config` answers two questions: which changed files affect a job, and may its result be reused. `4e62df6112628621` gave this job a focused digest; `e64133b542327753` removed it to stop a cache hit skipping the job, whose output is a comment about one concrete commit. That also made the job always affected, and `only_docs` in `filter_job.py` compensated for docs-only diffs only. This splits the two. `Job.Config` gains `enable_cache` (default True, and in `drop_fields`, so no existing job's digest changes), honoured at both cache seams. The job gets its focused digest back plus `enable_cache=False`: the digest decides whether to run it, the flag keeps every selected run running. Whether the build can produce data for this head arrives through `requires=["Build (arm_release)"]`, covering the build's sources, submodules, docker image and packaging. `only_docs` and its gate are deleted. Side effect: no longer always affected, the job stops rescuing `Build (arm_release)`, so that build is skipped on build-free diffs too. Those two jobs are the whole newly-skipped set, and this already happens on the `only_docs` path today. `Generate LLVM Coverage Diff Report`, asked about in the same comment, has no such hole: it is a `Result` inside `llvm_coverage_job.py`, already gated on build affectedness. One pre-existing limitation is widened, not fixed: a skip and a cache hit look identical to the runner, so the comment writer does not run on a skip and the comment can outlive the head it describes. That already holds for docs-only PRs. Verified: `ci/tests/` passes, `praktika yaml` produces no diff, every job's config digest is byte-identical, and each new assertion reddens under a mutation. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115221&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115221](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115221+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: PromQL/TimeSeries: materialize tags only for unique groups
signals.text: ## What changed - collect unique group IDs before looking up tags in vectorized one-input transforms - deduplicate vectorized two-input group pairs before materializing tags - materialize and transform tags once per unique group or pair - keep a simple path for near-unique pair batches, so a small number of duplicates does not trigger the extra component maps - preserve first-seen ordering and row order when remapping results ## Why Vectorized TimeSeries transforms used to materialize tag pointers for every input row before deduplicating repeated groups or group pairs. Repeated PromQL rows therefore did extra lookup and remapping work. The updated paths deduplicate first and only materialize the groups needed by the unique transforms. For two-input transforms, batches with at most roughly 10% duplicate pairs use the simpler materialization path and transform only the first occurrence of each pair. More repetitive batches keep the component-dedup path, where the extra indexing work is worth the saved tag materialization. ## Benchmark Collector-path microbenchmark on an Apple M1 Pro with `clang++ -O3`, median of 7 runs after 3 warmup runs: | Workload | Before | After | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | One-input dense repeated groups, 500,000 rows | 4.00 ms | 0.87 ms | 78% faster | | One-input sparse repeated groups, 500,000 rows | 3.85 ms | 0.84 ms | 78% faster | | One-input dense unique groups, 500,000 rows | 90.68 ms | 90.37 ms | unchanged | | Two-input repeated pairs, 200,000 rows / 32 pairs | 2.97 ms | 0.88 ms | 70% faster | | Two-input unique pairs, 200,000 rows | 80.88 ms | 77.48 ms | 4% faster | The committed performance workload also covers 100%, 99.9%, 95%, 75%, 50%, and 10% unique pair batches, plus realistic `group_left` and `group_right` PromQL matching. ## Tests - add crossed destination/source patterns instead of symmetric pair indexes - cover near-unique pairs through the simple path - cover sparse group IDs and repeated pairs whose transformed results collapse to one group - add repeated dense and sparse one-input group coverage with row order - add repeated dense and sparse two-input pair coverage with row order - add the full pair-cardinality performance curve and `group_left`/`group_right` workloads ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Avoid repeated tag materialization and extra remapping work for duplicate groups in vectorized TimeSeries transformations. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115223&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115223](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115223+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Perf: use compact presence masks for PromQL set operators
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): **Use compact presence masks for PromQL set operators.** ### Summary The PromQL `and`, `or`, and `unless` lowering only needs to know whether a value is present at each step. This targets the general set-operator path. The exact-group fast path is separate. ### Changes - Use `Array(UInt8)` presence masks instead of `Array(UInt64)` counts. - Use `groupBitOrForEach` for the per-step presence reduction. - Share the mask expression between `and`, `or`, and `unless`. - Keep the shared set-operator validation and presence-mask construction in a common lowering helper. - Keep the existing NULL filtering and join behavior. - Cover all three operators in the plan-shape test. - Keep the original 8,000-series baseline workload. - Add a sparse fan-in workload with 1,000 matching groups and four physical replicas per group, with `replica` excluded by `on(instance)`. The compact presence mask is built with: ```sql groupBitOrForEach(arrayMap(x -> isNotNull(x), values)) ``` Because `isNotNull()` produces a `UInt8` 0/1 value, bitwise OR is exactly the presence reduction needed by the set operators. The aggregate state is a zero-initialized `UInt8`, avoiding the generic `max(UInt8)` initialized-state bookkeeping. ### Benchmark The checked-in workload contains two variants, each using 300 query steps: - Baseline: 8,000 series with one series per matching group. - Sparse fan-in: 8,000 series with four replicas per matching group and staggered 50% sample presence. Queries match on `instance` while retaining `replica` in the physical labels. The second variant exercises the actual per-step presence reduction across multiple rows in each `on(...)` group. ### Benchmark result This operator-step microbenchmark runs the old `countForEach(values)` expression and the new `groupBitOrForEach(arrayMap(x -> isNotNull(x), values))` expression over the same workload shapes. - ClickHouse 26.7.3.19 - 200 iterations per case - QPS from `clickhouse-benchmark` - Memory from `system.query_log` | Workload | Before | After | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Baseline | 68.3 QPS, p50 13 ms, 40.0 MiB | 79.6 QPS, p50 11 ms, 30.1 MiB | +16.5% QPS, -24.9% memory | | Sparse fan-in | 119.4 QPS, p50 7 ms, 30.0 MiB | 122.7 QPS, p50 7 ms, 30.0 MiB | +2.8% QPS, no material memory change | ### Tests - Verified that `groupBitOr` is registered for integer inputs and that the `ForEach` combinator accepts array arguments. - Updated the plan-shape checks for `and`, `or`, and `unless` to require `groupBitOrForEach` and reject `countForEach`. - Existing end-to-end set-operator coverage continues to exercise mixed, NULL, and missing-step behavior. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115224&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115224](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115224+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: CI: report why the LLVM coverage diff report was not generated
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112832 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112832 (touches the same files, so expect a merge conflict; it is not a fix for this) ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `ci/jobs/scripts/generate_diff_coverage_report.sh` produces no report directory in four cases: no coverable C/C++ files changed, no coverage data for the changed files, current coverage empty for them, and a hard failure under `set -euo pipefail`. `llvm_coverage_job.py` inferred all four from one bit, `_diff_report_dir.exists()`, and reported three of them as "No C/C++ source files changed" at three sites. Two are green runs where C/C++ files did change, so the job states the opposite of what happened. On a tool failure it also set the `Print Uncovered Code` sub-result to `OK` for analysis that never ran. Observed on PR #115101, which changed `src/Functions/array/arrayAUC.cpp`: the `gh api` compare call returned `gh: Not Found (HTTP 404)`, and the job made both false claims. Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115101&sha=c00b1800c1fcae2cb2138af592a9b3e79b4c8275&name_0=PR&name_1=LLVM%20Coverage The script now names its outcome in `ci/tmp/diff_outcome.txt` before every `exit 0`, and the job reports the outcome it is told plus the script's exit status. It also drops a false claim that "LBC analysis will run separately" when current coverage is empty (`print_uncovered_code.py` reads only `current.changed.info`, empty in that state), and echoes each `gh api` compare endpoint, since `gh` reports a failure as a bare `HTTP 404` naming no resource. A script failure still stays RED, and no currently-green outcome becomes red. One behavioural change beyond the labels: `print_uncovered_code.py` now runs only for the two outcomes that produced this run's own coverage slice, so the others cannot report an earlier run's numbers. This does not fix the 404, which looks environmental: replaying both compare calls with 25 victims' own commit values gave 25/25 success, and OK and FAIL runs interleave in the same hours. `ci/tests/test_llvm_coverage_gate.py` grows from 12 to 70 cases: one per outcome, a harness running the real script under stubbed tools, and cases executing the job's own call site and each dispatch it selects. 48 fail on master. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115225&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115225](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115225+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Do not use the trivial count optimization when the aggregate argument contains arrayJoin
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115123 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115123 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed wrong results for `SELECT count(arrayJoin(arr))` with the default `optimize_trivial_count_query = 1`. The stored row count was returned instead of the number of array elements, and on `file()` and `url()` the query returned `0`. Closes #115123. ### Description Requested by @ PedroTadim on the issue (["the fix for this seems small. Can you do it?"](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115123#issuecomment-5315767329)); reported by @ konsta-danyliuk. `applyTrivialCountIfPossible` replaces the whole table read with the stored row counter. It checks that the aggregate is `count` by type, then never inspects `count`'s argument. `arrayJoin` multiplies rows above the source read, so the aggregate observes `sum(length(arr))` rows rather than `totalRows()`, and the expansion is dropped along with the read. Measured on 3 rows / 6 elements: `count(arrayJoin(A))` returned `3` instead of `6`. The fix refuses the optimization when the argument contains `arrayJoin`, using the same `hasFunctionNode(..., "arrayJoin")` guard six sibling optimizations already use for this property. The guard sits **before** `select_query_info.optimize_trivial_count = true`: for `file()`, `url()` and object storage `totalRows()` is `nullopt`, so the function returns `false`, but the flag has already been written and those storages count in `read()`, so they returned `0`. Placing the guard after the flag write fixes MergeTree while leaving `file()` at `0`, so the test asserts the `file()` value too. The old analyzer decides trivial count separately, in `TreeRewriter`, and is affected there too. Per @ PedroTadim's review, that path is obsolete, so this PR leaves it alone: the analyzer is the only path fixed and asserted, and the test is tagged `no-old-analyzer`. Not bundled: rewriting `count(arrayJoin(A))` to `sum(A.size0)` would be faster, but that is an optimization on top of a wrong-results fix. <details><summary>Carriers and over-guard checks (measured, base vs patched)</summary> Fixture: 3 rows, `sum(length(A))` = 6. | case | base | patched | |---|---|---| | `count(arrayJoin(A))` on MergeTree | 3 | 6 | | `count(unnest(A))` (alias) | 3 | 6 | | `count(arrayJoin(A) + 1)`, `arrayJoin(arrayMap(...))` (nested) | 3 | 6 | | `count(arrayJoin(arrayJoin([A,B])))` | 3 | 11 | | `count(arrayJoin(A))` on `file()` / `url()` | **0** | 6 | | `count(arrayJoin(M))` Map / `(T)` Array(Tuple) | 3 | 5 | | `count(arrayJoin(LC))` Array(LowCardinality) | 3 | 7 | | `count(arrayJoin(A))` via `remote()` | 3 | 6 | | `count(arrayJoin(A))` ReplacingMergeTree FINAL | 6 | 6 | Object storage reads the same flag at `StorageObjectStorage.cpp:720`, so it takes the `file()`/`url()` path; with no S3 endpoint here that row is read from the code, not measured. Unchanged, and asserted so: `count()`, `count(*)`, `count(1)`, `count(n)`, `count(nullable)`, `ARRAY JOIN` as a clause, `countIf(arrayJoin(...))`, `count(DISTINCT arrayJoin(...))`, the sparsity-filter sibling, and a `count()` whose unrelated subquery contains `arrayJoin` (both visitors stop at nested query nodes). Controls: rejecting any non-empty argument list flips `count(n)` off the optimization; moving the guard below the flag write fails the `file()` arm alone. Every stateless test referencing `optimize_trivial_count` was run. The only failures need a dataset or a listener this sandbox cannot provide (`test.hits`, `127.0.0.2:9000`) and fail identically on unpatched master. </details> <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115227&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115227](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115227+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1681` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Fix the Upgrade check silently validating against a stale previous release
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description The Upgrade check starts a previous release, then upgrades to the build under test. `tests/ci/get_previous_release_tag.py` picks that baseline, and can silently pick one far too old. On PR #114376 commit `e1cb0dee5e9` it picked `v25.1.4.53` for a `26.8.1.1` build; that old server aborted on shutdown, reported as `Received signal 6` unrelated to the PR. Two commits earlier it resolved `v26.7.3.19`. 4 of 47 recent runs were affected. Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114376&sha=e1cb0dee5e9bd972e9bbbdd8cd8d971ad1e39ee1&name_0=PR&name_1=Upgrade%20check%20%28amd_release%29 Root cause: when no candidate on a page could be used, an unbounded `while not found:` advanced to page 2, 3 and answered from there. `/releases` returns entries roughly newest-created first, not in version order, and each later page's newest release is older than the previous page's newest (measured across all 9 pages), so page 1 holds the newest release overall. The only diagnostic was `logger.debug` under `basicConfig(level=INFO)`. This resolves from the first page only. A candidate still needs an uploaded package, so a release whose packages are still publishing keeps falling back to the previous patch release, now logged at WARNING rather than DEBUG. Three cases now raise: a first page with no usable candidate, a page shorter than the 100 requested, and an answer that is its page's oldest entry, which cannot show that no newer release precedes it. `upgrade_runner.sh` turns those nonzero exits into a job failure. No C++ change is needed: the abort is a use-after-free in `25.1`, fixed in `2920d338ea4` (#81473, released in `v25.6.1.3206`), so master and every active release branch carry the fix. Tests were removed at review request. The Upgrade check's digest now lists both release helpers `upgrade_runner.sh` runs, the resolver and `download_release_packages.py`; without them a change to either leaves the job cache-skippable, the same failure mode fixed here. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112974 (hardens the API helper; edits the same digest list, so whichever merges second rebases). <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115228&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115228](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115228+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Add test: `arrayReduceInRanges` pre-aggregation loop never runs with row offset or 2+ arg arrays
signals.text: _Test-only PR. Review: are the gaps real, is the test right._ Adds test coverage for 1 untested code path, found during automated review of [PR #115008](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115008). That PR: Allocates `max(sizeOfData(), 1)` bytes for the pre-aggregation states in `FunctionArrayReduceInRanges::executeImpl` (`arrayReduceInRanges.cpp:80,186`), so states of a zero-size aggregate (`AggregateFunctionNothing`, reached when every argument collapses to `Nullable(Nothing)`) no longer alias each … **1. `arrayReduceInRanges` pre-aggregation loop never runs with row offset or 2+ arg arrays** `src/Functions/array/arrayReduceInRanges.cpp:216`, `src/Functions/array/arrayReduceInRanges.cpp:186` **Risk:** The pre-aggregation loop at `arrayReduceInRanges.cpp:210-217` indexes the flattened array data as `begin + k`, where `begin` is the previous row's offset. It only executes when the row's array has >= 64 elements (`place_offsets[0] > 0`), and every existing test that has >= 64 elements passes a … **Unique vs PR tests:** The PR's 04925 tests are all single constant arrays with one argument column, so `executeImpl` runs with `input_rows_count == 1`, `begin == 0` and `num_arguments_columns == 1`. This test drives the same pre-aggregation code with a non-constant column over 4 rows (non-zero row offset, arena reused … [Try it on ClickHouse Fiddle](https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/2549d8cf-764d-44be-b381-bc2c928e0e59) cc @groeneai (author of #115008), @PedroTadim (merged/approved #115008) — could you take a look, and add the `can be tested` label if this looks good? ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Not applicable — test-only change. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115229&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115229](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115229+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->
