signals.title: Do not build statistics for non-physical columns
signals.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114791 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes `NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK` on every `INSERT` into a table that declares `STATISTICS(...)` on an `ALIAS` or `EPHEMERAL` column, which made such tables read-only. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114791 `CREATE TABLE t (a UInt64, b UInt64 ALIAS a + 1 STATISTICS(basic)) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY a` is accepted, and then every `INSERT` fails `Code: 10 ... Not found column b in block`, so the table is read-only. `materialize_statistics_on_insert` defaulting to `true` in 26.8 exposed it. **Root cause.** The `ColumnsStatistics` constructor collects every column with a non-empty statistics description without checking how the column is stored, and the insert path builds those with `build`, which does `block.getByName`. An `ALIAS` column is computed on read and never appears in the written block, so the lookup always throws. Merges use `buildIfExists` and skip absent columns, which is why they kept working. Such statistics are already unsupported in `addImplicitStatistics` and `ALTER ... ADD STATISTICS`. **The change.** Drop non-physical columns from the collector the insert path builds, in `MergeTreeDataWriter`, using the existing `ColumnsDescription::hasPhysical`. `build` stays strict, because its type-mismatch check is a deliberate diagnostic, so an absence for any other reason is still an error. A newly issued `MATERIALIZE STATISTICS <col>` naming such a column is still rejected before enqueue. An already queued one instead skips it, so a command persisted by a pre-upgrade server drains rather than retrying forever in the background task. `ALL` skips such a column and stays usable. **Deliberately unchanged.** The declaration stays accepted but inert: every candidate rejection site is also the ATTACH/startup or replica-addition path, so a check there would stop existing affected tables from loading. `DROP STATISTICS` stays permissive and recovers such a table. Covered by `02864_statistics_ddl`, which fails on master with `Code: 10` and passes with the fix. The queued-mutation drain under the old mutation analyzer is not covered by a test: it needs the server-level `use_analyzer_for_mutations` override, which a stateless test cannot set.

signals.title: CI: do not authenticate an unused robot token in the Codex code review
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113059 The `Code Review` job died on `gh auth login` for 10 pull requests in the 24 h to 2026-08-17, losing the automated review for those heads. A fork PR cannot re-run it, so recovery needs a fresh push. ``` ERROR: Codex review failed after 3 attempts: CalledProcessError: Command '['gh', 'auth', 'login', '--with-token']' returned non-zero exit status 1. ``` - report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113059&sha=83188f6442a4f2d7e4376efe54c2bf3bad32dd50&name_0=PR&name_1=Code%20Review - log: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/PRs/113059/83188f6442a4f2d7e4376efe54c2bf3bad32dd50/code_review/job.log `_run_codex_once` authenticated a robot token before every attempt, under `check=True`, but the Codex backend never uses it: `enable_gh_auth=True` has the runner authenticate the app up front, and the prompt runs every agent `gh` call with `GH_CONFIG_DIR` unset. Across the 25 job logs that reached the agent, 246 of 246 executed `gh` calls unset it and none used the scoped robot directory, so that login could only fail the job. In those same logs `/ci/robot-ch-test-poll-copilot` answered `HTTP 401: Bad credentials` on 27 of 27 attempts, the oldest on 2026-08-03, and `/ci/robot-ch-test-poll-1-copilot` never did. Two robots over three attempts rotate as `[X, Y, X]`, so the healthy one gets a single attempt when the shuffle puts the dead one first, and one transient GraphQL 503 there fails the job. This removes that login and its temporary `GH_CONFIG_DIR` from the Codex attempt, so it runs on the app identity it already used and retries serve agent failures. `_run_copilot_once` keeps its login, which the Copilot CLI does use. New `ci/tests/test_copilot_review_codex_auth.py`: 5 tests fail on the current code with the error above and pass here; the 2 pinning unchanged behaviour were verified by mutating the code they pin. No secret, process or sleep involved. Out of scope: `/ci/robot-ch-test-poll-copilot` still needs rotating operationally (`--copilot` would still need it); and 8 further failures that window are a separate defect, `gh api -X PATCH` on `issues/comments/<id>` returning 503 after its retries. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115232&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115232](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115232+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Make the 01396 cleanup wait its own verdict
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108213 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `01396_inactive_replica_cleanup_nodes_zookeeper` failed on `Stateless tests (arm_binary, parallel)` with ``` cleanup wait did not converge: last count='49', last poll error: ``` CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115051&sha=dca080fd03ab3fd8be3a75a881ec4f6cb4c764d4&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28arm_binary%2C%20parallel%29 Root cause: the wait and the check were two independent samples of a moving value. The poll loop broke on its own observation of `49`, below the threshold of 50, then a **separate** query re-read the same node, returned `>= 50`, and that second read was the verdict. No query failed (the poll error was empty): inserts and merges append to `/log` while the cleanup thread trims it, and a burst landed in the gap. Cleanup was working; the test mis-sampled it. The fix makes the observation that ends the wait the verdict and deletes the second read, removing the gap rather than narrowing it. The threshold, the 120 s budget, the reference and the tags are unchanged. An observation counts only if the read both completed successfully and returned a number. The numeric test is the existing guard (`[[ "" -lt N ]]` is true in bash); the exit-status test is new here: the client can flush a data block and then fail, so a delivered row alone is not a successful read. The verdict therefore accepts the count having been observed below the threshold at any point in the wait, rather than at the end. Since `/log` moves, that is the property the test can assert. If cleanup does not run, no iteration observes it and the test still fails. Validated on release binary 26.8.1.1585 (`no-debug` skips on a debug build). Recreating the window deterministically: the old logic fails 16/16 with the CI signature, the new one passes 16/16. The fixed test still fails with cleanup suppressed, with every poll erroring, and with a poll returning a low number then failing. 50/50 green under randomization. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115234&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115234](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115234+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1651` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Report which destination made the macOS self-extracting copy fail
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `Fast test (arm_darwin)` fails a few times a day on unrelated PRs with `Permission denied` on `ci/tmp/clickhouse`: [job 95461613722](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/actions/runs/32041145440/job/95461613722) ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114125&sha=88ab20e7768865da5426a0aaa8a204f6ad43e6f5&name_0=PR&name_1=Fast%20test%20%28arm_darwin%29)), also jobs `95537845886`, `95306463154`, `95222719292`, across three unrelated PRs. The binary is the self-extracting bundle and it destroys itself. In `decompressor.cpp` `unlink(self)` succeeds, the Darwin-only `std::filesystem::copy_file(tmp -> self)` then fails `EEXIST`, and the error return happens before the `chmod` restoring the executable bit, so the process exits having removed its own binary. The progress dots appear exactly once in the log, immediately followed by that `copy_file`'s `File exists`. Why the destination exists after a successful `unlink` is not established, and I could not reproduce it: this is macOS-only and I have no macOS host. Two mechanisms remain possible (path resolution through `_NSGetExecutablePath`/`realpath`/APFS naming a different entry than `unlink` removed, or a symlink-following equivalence match); an unlabelled `File exists` cannot tell them apart. So instead of guessing at a fix, this reports the destination's identity and keeps the failure closed: `lstat` and symlink-following `stat` for destination and source, the equivalence flag from the followed pair (what libc++ compares before returning `EEXIST`), and the original wrapper's dev/inode. It is confined to that failure branch plus an `OS_DARWIN`-only helper; one real occurrence identifies the mechanism. Two candidate fixes were dropped on measurement: `copy_options::overwrite_existing` is a no-op against the equivalence case and truncates an unknown object otherwise; staging the temp file executable would publish a partial executable. Validated by an oracle harness compiling this code verbatim over three destination shapes that must differ (they collapse without the change), a `-DOS_DARWIN` type-check with an injected-error control, byte-identical Linux `.text`, and a standalone self-extracting round trip unchanged before and after. A green `Fast test (arm_darwin)` here is not evidence the diagnostic works, since it only fires on failure: this makes the next occurrence diagnosable, not rarer. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115236&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115236](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115236+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix Arrow export of JSON, Dynamic, QBit and AggregateFunction
signals.text:
Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115023 Caused by: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/91170 The `output_format_arrow_unsupported_types_as_binary` fallback wrote a column with no first-class Arrow mapping by calling `IColumn::getDataAt` per row. That method exposes a column's contiguous in-memory bytes, which most of the types reaching the fallback do not have: - `ColumnObject` (`JSON`), `ColumnVariant` (hence `ColumnDynamic`) and `ColumnQBit` throw `Method getDataAt is not supported`, so `SELECT ... FORMAT Arrow` failed on them — after the schema message had already been written, leaving the client with a truncated stream; - `ColumnAggregateFunction::getDataAt` returns the `AggregateDataPtr` itself, so exporting an aggregate state silently wrote raw heap addresses instead of the state, both corrupting the data and disclosing server addresses. Before the fallback existed these types were rejected with a clear `UNKNOWN_TYPE`, so both are regressions introduced together with the setting: ``` -- 26.4, before #91170 SELECT '{"a":1}'::JSON FORMAT Arrow; -- Code: 50. The type 'JSON' of a column 'j' is not supported for conversion into Arrow data format. (UNKNOWN_TYPE) SELECT sumState(number) FROM numbers(3) FORMAT Arrow; -- Code: 50. The type 'AggregateFunction(sum, UInt64)' ... (UNKNOWN_TYPE) -- 26.5 .. 26.8 SELECT '{"a":1}'::JSON FORMAT Arrow; -- Code: 48. Method getDataAt is not supported for Object(max_dynamic_paths=1024, max_dynamic_types=32). (NOT_IMPLEMENTED) SELECT sumState(number) FROM numbers(3) FORMAT Arrow; -- succeeds, writes 00D0A9C9D37F0000 ``` The fallback now serializes each value through `ISerialization`, whose `serializeText`/`serializeBinary` are pure virtual and therefore defined for every type, so the "do not fail a `SELECT *`" property that motivated the setting holds by construction instead of depending on an unrelated method's implementation status. The aggregate state written in binary mode is the `RowBinary` encoding and deserializes back into the original `AggregateFunction` type. `output_format_arrow_unsupported_types` (`throw` / `text` / `binary`) replaces the boolean, adding a `text` mode that writes what `CAST(col AS String)` would produce — useful for the BI clients that drive `SELECT *` over Arrow Flight SQL, and the workaround users had to apply by hand for `JSON`. Its default, `binary`, is the previous behavior, and its `SettingsChangesHistory` entry has identical previous and new values so `compatibility` never marks it changed. The boolean keeps working with full effect (`0` means `throw`, `1` means `binary`) and is only consulted while the new setting is left at its default, so an explicit mode wins whichever order the two are set in. Both writers — the native Arrow IPC one behind `FORMAT Arrow`/`ArrowStream` and the Apache-Arrow-library one behind Arrow Flight SQL — make the accept/reject decision in the schema converter, before the schema message is written, so a rejected type can no longer abort a stream whose schema the reader has already accepted. Both serialize the values with the query's own `FormatSettings`, so a setting the serialization depends on (`output_format_binary_write_json_as_string`, `output_format_json_quote_64bit_integers`, …) produces the same payload whichever writer serves the query. An opaque column is tagged in both writers with the `clickhouse.opaque` Arrow extension name and the original ClickHouse type name in `ARROW:extension:metadata`, so a consumer can tell it apart from a genuine string or binary column. Per the Arrow extension-type convention a reader that does not know the extension name ignores the metadata and sees the plain storage type, so no existing consumer changes behavior. `StorageArrowFlight::ArrowFlightSink` built its converter settings from scratch and never consulted the setting, so it always used the struct default. It now resolves the mode from the query context like the other Arrow Flight call sites, which makes `INSERT INTO ... ENGINE = ArrowFlight` of an `AggregateFunction` column follow the setting; `throw` reproduces the previous behavior exactly. `JSON` and `Dynamic` cannot reach that sink, because the storage rejects a dynamic-structure column when the table is created and the table function takes its header from the remote schema. Verified against a local ClickHouse Arrow Flight server as well as `FORMAT Arrow`: `SELECT *` over a table with `JSON` and `AggregateFunction` columns returns them as `clickhouse.opaque`-tagged `binary` fields carrying the ClickHouse type name, with a neighbouring `String` column left untagged; `output_format_arrow_unsupported_types = 'text'` switches them to tagged `string` fields holding the text; and the payloads match the native writer byte for byte under the serialization settings above. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `SELECT ... FORMAT Arrow` failing with `Method getDataAt is not supported` for `JSON`, `Dynamic` and `QBit` columns, and silently exporting heap addresses instead of the aggregate state for `AggregateFunction` columns. Added the `output_format_arrow_unsupported_types` setting (`throw` / `text` / `binary`, default `binary`) which supersedes `output_format_arrow_unsupported_types_as_binary`.
  
--- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115250&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115250](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115250+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)]

signals.title: Record the read wait-for-write span and histogram in the new Keeper dispatcher
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115017 (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/101757 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115017 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/101757 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix the histogram metric `keeper_read_wait_for_write_time_milliseconds` and the OpenTelemetry span `keeper.read.wait_for_write` always reading zero and never being emitted when `use_new_dispatcher` is enabled, which is the default. Both are now recorded for read requests that wait for an in-flight write, as they were before the new request dispatcher. ### Description Requested by @ al13n321 on #115017: record the histogram and the span for late and intermediate reads in the commit callback. `KeeperRequestDispatcherOld` initializes the `ReadWaitForWrite` span when it parks a read and finalizes it when the write commits. The new dispatcher replaced that queue with two carriers in `InFlightBatch`, `intermediate_reads` (parked mid-batch) and `late_reads` (parked after the last request), and instrumented neither. The wait still happens; only its measurement was lost. This initializes at both park sites and finalizes both carriers in `onCommit`. `maybeFinalize` observes the histogram before checking for a span, so one pair feeds both surfaces. `dropInFlightRequests` is deliberately not finalized: those reads never saw their write complete, so timing them would mix stream-recreation timeouts into a latency metric, and `Old` does not finalize its error path either. A test arm pins it. The initialize in `LateReads::add` runs under the lock `add` already holds, before the read is visible to `onCommit`, and adds no lock, atomic or ordering edge. `onCommit` finalizes only the first group it takes per batch: the write is applied before the commit callback runs, so a read attached while that batch's reads are already draining waited for those reads, not for the write. A test arm pins this by adding a read from inside the drain. No setting, ordering or state transition changed. Validated on an embedded-keeper server: before, the histogram stays at 0 and the span is absent while sibling keeper spans are recorded; after, the count advances and the span carries the attributes `Old` emits. Two test gaps. Parking cannot be forced deterministically from a client, so the integration test keeps its assertion tolerating the span's absence rather than gaining a flaky one. No unit test reaches the `dispatchThread` initialize, which needs a started raft stream; the server run above covers it. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115252&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115252](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115252+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Report the exception that killed a praktika native job
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/90117 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description On [this report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=90117&sha=cbac4cec7c4dac888f916ef80f163e63e810af37&name_0=PR&name_1=Config%20Workflow), `Config Workflow` errored and 174 jobs were `DROPPED`, so nothing ran on that head. The report shows a `JSONDecodeError` from `get_pr_title_body_labels`, which is handled and returns `("", "", [])`. The job ran on for another 62 seconds and died at `native_jobs.py:635` with `Failed to set both GH commit status and PR comment with Workflow Status, cannot proceed`, after GitHub answered 503 to three further calls. The fatal exception never reached the report. `Info.store_traceback` collects *handled* tracebacks into `env.TRACEBACKS`, and `Runner._post_run` renders those as the job's info. The only frame holding the fatal traceback, the `__main__` handler, built its `Result` with `info=` commented out, assuming `runner._run()` fills it in. It does not here: the log-tail fallback is gated on `not result.is_completed()`, and an ERROR result is already completed. So such a job reports whichever handled traceback was stored earlier, or nothing. I pass that `info=`, truncated, since an exception message can embed command output of any size. A raising `workflow_filter_hook` loses its cause too, for a different reason: it is caught inside `_config_workflow`, so it never reaches that handler, and its info was `f"{traceback.print_exc()}"`, which is the string `"None"`. That has already voided a matrix: on [#109746 at 007bf36](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109746&sha=007bf36920f1c15fd079b5f0279410ee68b6ba70&name_0=PR&name_1=Config%20Workflow) a hook raised `AttributeError`, `Filter Hooks` is `ERROR` with info `"None"`, and 168 jobs were `DROPPED`. It now uses `format_exc()`, as the cache-lookup result below it does. Reporting only. The retry budget is untouched, and so is `res1 or res2` at the fatal site: whether losing the commit status is survivable when the report comment landed is a design question I am not deciding here. <details> <summary>How often this hides a cause</summary> 24 PRs took a `Config Workflow` error on 2026-08-17, 12 of them at this line. Of the 8 reports I read, none showed the fatal error: 5 show the misleading `JSONDecodeError` and 3 an empty info, and each dropped 174 jobs. One of the 12 got there with no 503 at all (`gh` exited 4 for a missing `GH_TOKEN`), so this reports whatever the cause was rather than assuming a 5xx. signals.title: Validate skip_degree when reading a uniq aggregate state
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed silently incorrect results and undefined behavior when reading a malformed `AggregateFunction(uniq, ...)` state. The `skip_degree` field of the serialized state was used as a shift exponent without validation, so an out-of-range value produced an arbitrary cardinality instead of an error. Such states are now rejected with `INCORRECT_DATA`. ### Description Found by the AST fuzzer on an unrelated PR; the defect is in trunk. `UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer: shift exponent 128 is too large for 64-bit type` at `UniquesHashSet<>::size()`, STID 3207-4f9c. https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=107943&sha=1a89f6f2660c232730fd45bc1878d5d8443f7350&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28arm_asan_ubsan%29 `skip_degree` is the first byte of a serialized `uniq` state and `read()` accepted any value for it. Three sites shift by it: `size()` shifts a `UInt64` twice and `good()` a `UInt32`, so 32 or more is undefined. Such a value can only arrive by deserializing a state, ordinary user input. The exponent wrapped modulo 64, so a release build returned a wrong answer with no error: ```sql SELECT finalizeAggregation(CAST(unhex('8003FF6321D0F2F6B3C3E0A35D4C') AS AggregateFunction(uniq, UInt64, UInt64))); -- 3 ``` Thinning leaves at most `2 ^ (32 - skip_degree)` hashes and `shrinkIfNeed()` raises the degree only while more than `UNIQUES_HASH_MAX_SIZE` remain, so one past that budget is the last degree it can produce. `read()` rejects anything above it. The same bound now holds at the other writer, as in `ReservoirSamplerDeterministic.h`: a buffer repeating one maximally divisible hash keeps a count thinning cannot reduce, so `shrinkIfNeed()` would otherwise raise the degree without limit. It has no SQL route, so it carries no separate test. That last accepted degree still admits a count which saturates the hash space, where the systematic-error correction underflows its subtraction and casts a negative double to `size_t`. `write()` serializes such a state, so rejecting it would refuse ClickHouse's own output; `size()` saturates the count instead. `UNIQUES_HASH_MAX_SIZE_DEGREE` has been 17 for this file's whole history, so no released version could write a rejected degree. No format change, no new setting. Not addressed here: the file's three pre-existing `Poco::Exception` throws surface as the opaque `Code: 1001`, and `reinsertImpl()` does not dedupe. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115276&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115276](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115276+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1680` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Fix flaky test 03100_lwu_22_detach_attach_patches
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110178 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Not for changelog. ### Description `03100_lwu_22_detach_attach_patches` hits the 60 second per-test cap in `Fast test` (`Timeout! Killing process group`). Measured over 30 days: 7 failures across 7 distinct pull requests, 0 on master. Example report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115234&sha=3d3a0b0cfb7379259dd3158099a5035c6d7099fe&name_0=PR&name_1=Fast%20test Root cause. Every merge-selection round that selects nothing multiplies the table's merge-selecting interval by `merge_selecting_sleep_slowdown_factor`, up to `max_merge_selecting_sleep_ms` (default 60000). Externally woken rounds count too, and `mutate()` schedules one for every `UPDATE` and `APPLY PATCHES`, so the interval saturates at the 60 second ceiling within a second of `CREATE TABLE`. Any later statement that has to wait for the next selection round then pays that interval. This test issues `APPLY PATCHES` under `mutations_sync = 2`, so a single such wait consumes the whole 60 second budget. Measured locally on one server, reading the interval the engine itself logs (`Scheduling next merge selecting task after Nms`): unpinned, the interval reaches 60000 ms and the longest observed wait between selection rounds is 54832 ms; with the pin the interval never exceeds 200 ms and the longest wait is 121 ms. Over 20 unpinned randomized runs, 7 took more than 30 seconds (max 57.51 s, i.e. a near miss of the cap); with the pin, 100 runs all finished in under 3 seconds. The fix pins `merge_selecting_sleep_ms` and `max_merge_selecting_sleep_ms` on the test's two tables, which is what the merged #110178 did for `02676_optimize_old_parts_replicated` and what `03047_on_fly_mutations_basics_rmt` already does. Test only, no product code change. I did not change the engine here. That the interval grows on externally woken rounds is a scheduling policy question that affects merge latency and Keeper load for every replicated table, and justifying a change to it needs multi-replica measurements this PR does not have. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115279&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115279](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115279+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Enforce allow_non_metadata_alters on the mutation path, and document what it blocks
signals.text:
Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115058 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `allow_non_metadata_alters = 0` now also rejects the `ALTER` commands that reach a `MergeTree` table as explicit mutations: `UPDATE`, `DELETE WHERE`, the five `MATERIALIZE` forms, `APPLY DELETED MASK`, `APPLY PATCHES` and `REWRITE PARTS`. Previously only column-payload alters were rejected, so these rewrote parts anyway. `DELETE FROM` and `UPDATE` stay permitted, including `ON CLUSTER`. The setting description now lists what is refused, and that the check is `MergeTree`-only. ### Description The setting was only read in `MergeTreeData::checkAlterIsPossible`. The commands listed above go into a `MutationCommands` segment, which calls `checkMutationIsPossible`, whose `Settings` parameter `MergeTreeData` declared unused. The fix names it and rejects when `hasNonEmptyMutationCommands()` holds, the predicate that already decides whether the mutation runs, so guard and execution cannot drift. Plain `DELETE FROM` needed care: under the default `lightweight_delete_mode` it synthesizes `ALTER TABLE ... UPDATE _row_exists = 0`, indistinguishable at the storage from the user-written form. Exempting by shape would reopen the hole, so the synthesizing interpreter grants it on a private context. `StorageWindowView::cleanup()` is the only other such call site in `src/`. A setting cannot carry that provenance across nodes: the worker re-clamps shipped settings against its own profile. So `DELETE FROM ... ON CLUSTER` now dispatches the `DELETE` itself, as `InterpreterUpdateQuery` does. Two consequences: - `DDLWorker` now leader-routes `ASTDeleteQuery`, so a replicated shard runs it once, not once per replica; this covers multi-shard `Replicated` databases too, by the same predicate that already covers `ALTER ... DELETE WHERE`. Mid-upgrade, an old and a new worker can both execute one entry: measured on a mixed two-node cluster, both initiator directions, that is two identical completed mutation entries and convergent rows, i.e. duplicated work that converges. The two closest precedents for widening this list also shipped ungated. - `InterpreterDeleteQuery` now inlines SQL user-defined functions, as the interpreters it used to re-enter did. That store is not replicated by default, so an unexpanded body either failed with `UNKNOWN_FUNCTION` on the other hosts or, if defined differently there, silently deleted different rows there. Refusals happen only where the setting is 0. The two bullets above are not gated on it: clustered `DELETE FROM` changes dispatch and inlining at any value of the setting, including the default. @PedroTadim, the compatibility question is open if you prefer the docs half.
Validation, allow_non_metadata_alters = 0 on a debug build Three binaries: base, the guard without the caller exemption, and the fix. | Statement | base | guard only | fix | |---|---|---|---| | the mutation commands listed above | OK | 524 | 524 | | user-written `ALTER ... UPDATE _row_exists = 0`, local and `ON CLUSTER` | OK | 524 | 524 | | `DELETE FROM` (default mode) | OK | 524 | OK | | `DELETE FROM ... ON CLUSTER`, profile constrains the setting to 0 | OK | 524 | OK | | `DELETE FROM` (`lightweight_update` mode) | OK | OK | OK | | lightweight `UPDATE ... SET` | OK | OK | OK | | `DROP COLUMN` of an `ALIAS`, `ADD COLUMN`, `COMMENT COLUMN`, `MODIFY SETTING` | OK | OK | OK | | the alters already refused before this change | 524 | 524 | 524 | | every refused statement again under `= 1` | OK | OK | OK | 524 is `ALTER_OF_COLUMN_IS_FORBIDDEN`, the code the existing alter-path guard already throws. The middle column is why the exemption sits in the interpreter: `DELETE FROM` is the only cell that differs from the fix, so the relaxation is exactly one statement wide. `01413_allow_non_metadata_alters` is extended with these cases and fails without the fix; each new expected-error line was justified against the base binary first, where all of them succeed. The clustered cases need a settings profile, which a stateless test cannot set, so they live in `test_allow_non_metadata_alters_on_cluster` (10 arms). One asserts a replicated shard records a single mutation entry; `lightweight_deletes_sync` is 2 and the DDL output mode is `THROW`, so that read happens after every host finished, with no polling or sleep. Two define a function on one host only, and differently on each host: without the inlining they fail with `UNKNOWN_FUNCTION` and with divergent surviving keys respectively.

signals.title: Restructure the Cascades optimizer code following the review of #86353
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/86353 Restructures the Cascades optimizer code to address the review comments on #86353. No behavior changes: every plan-shape reference is byte-identical, and the Cascades gtests and the distributed-plan test suite pass unchanged. - `CascadesOptimizer` now owns the search engine: the memo, the rule registries, the task stack, costing, and plan extraction. The former `OptimizationEnvironment` fields become the new `OptimizerContext`, a plain per-query settings struct stored in the memo. - One rule per file: `LocalRead`, `ParallelRead`, `ReplicatedRead`, `TopN`, and `TwoStageTopN` each moved into their own source file. The helpers shared by the rules moved to `RuleUtils`, and the fixed model constants (task budget, fallback selectivities, row-width defaults) moved to `OptimizerDefaults.h`. The per-operator cost constants stay in `CostConfig` because a query can override them. - Implementation strategies are stateless, so they became per-type singletons (`strategySingleton<T>`), and expressions compare them by pointer instead of by name. - `EnforcerAxis` is renamed to `EnforcedProperty`. - Optimization tasks are owned by `std::unique_ptr` instead of `std::shared_ptr`. - Logical expressions in a group now get the same structural deduplication as physical ones, so a transformation that derives an already-known alternative does not grow the group. Covered by a new case in `gtest_cascades_group_dedup`. - Small cleanups from the review: the eligibility check in `Group::selectInputImplementation` is inlined into the selection lambda, `DistributionPassthrough` rejects an impossible variant before it copies the `GroupExpression`, and the repeated input-requirement construction in `DistributionEnforcer` is extracted into `inputAtSourceDistribution`. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115293&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115293](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115293+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Remove the redundant cross-thread cancel of the Keeper leader-metrics timer
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113334 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `KeeperServer::stopLeaderMetricsPolling()` cancelled the leader-metrics timer from the main thread at shutdown, while a NuRaft asio worker re-armed the same `asio::steady_timer` from `collectLeaderMetrics()`. Both touch `deadline_timer_service::implementation_type::might_have_pending_waits` outside `leader_unavailable_metrics_mutex`, so nothing orders them. `basic_waitable_timer` is documented `Shared objects: Unsafe`, so the defect is at these two call sites, not in NuRaft or boost. TSan reports it on any amd_tsan job tearing a Keeper-enabled server down, attaching to whichever test is shutting the cluster down, hence three test names: - [amd_tsan integration 5/6](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109368&sha=51444071bc4587932301117674fde5f44a6f2f84&name_0=PR&name_1=Integration%20tests%20%28amd_tsan%2C%205%2F6%29), `test_keeper_max_request_size` - [amd_tsan stateless flaky check](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=101841&sha=b493a5015808fdf65e1592623e56165c0bb1d44b&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_tsan%2C%20flaky%20check%29) - [amd_tsan integration 1/6](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115039&sha=a9798769f07c415c69b43a74a2547ce96291fb15&name_0=PR&name_1=Integration%20tests%20%28amd_tsan%2C%201%2F6%29), `test_keeper_opentelemetry_tracing` I delete the cancel rather than add synchronization, because `f473bc8825cfb3b` deliberately hoisted `schedule()` out of that mutex under the subject "deadlock hazard". The cancel is also redundant: resetting the optional under the mutex is already a complete stop signal, since `collectLeaderMetrics()` re-checks it as the first statement inside its own lock before re-arming, so a late callback schedules nothing and the poll chain ends on its own. `asio_service->stop()` then joins the workers. One writer remains, no lock held across a boost call. Validated on a TSan build, since the defect is invisible in debug and release. A gdb breakpoint on `nuraft::asio_service::cancel_impl` reaches it via `stopLeaderMetricsPolling` on the main thread in 3 of 3 runs before the change and 0 of 3 after, with a positive control confirming the shutdown path ran in all six. I did not observe the TSan report itself locally, expected at three hits in 45 days. `test_keeper_max_request_size` passed 144/144 over 12 repeats; `test_keeper_back_to_back` and `test_keeper_four_word_command` passed with no `Failed to shutdown RAFT server` warning, the signal that the drain still bounds a pending expiry. Introduced by #113334 and master-only, so there is nothing to backport. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115305&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115305](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115305+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111025 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113649 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description **Do not merge this until NightlyFuzzers is green on this branch.** Dispatching it needs admin rights on the repository, so I am asking for a manual run first. Validated against a real binary: `update_dict.sh` aborts under a UTF-8 locale before the fix and succeeds after. 35 new `ci/tests` functions cover the four fixes, each with a mutation arm that reddens without its fix. Residual: `runner.py` still infers "fuzzer target" from the execute bit, so it is unchanged. signals.title: Do not admit non-clonable read steps into the MergeTree direct join
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/103473 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `Cannot clone ReadFromPreparedSource plan step` (`NOT_IMPLEMENTED`) when joining against a `Buffer` table with `join_algorithm = 'direct'`. Such a right side is now declined with the same message as any other unsupported storage. ### Description `tryMakeDirectJoinWithMergeTree` admitted `ReadFromPreparedSource` as a right-side read step, then cloned the right plan unconditionally. That step has no `clone()` override, so the clone reached the throwing base `IQueryPlanStep::clone()`: ```sql CREATE TABLE t_left (id UInt64, name String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id; CREATE TABLE t_right_mt (id UInt64, val String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id; CREATE TABLE t_right_buf AS t_right_mt ENGINE = Buffer(currentDatabase(), t_right_mt, 1, 1000, 1000, 10000, 10000, 10000000, 10000000); INSERT INTO t_left VALUES (1, 'A'); SELECT * FROM t_left AS l LEFT JOIN t_right_buf AS r ON l.id = r.id SETTINGS enable_analyzer = 1, join_algorithm = 'direct'; -- Code: 48. DB::Exception: Cannot clone ReadFromPreparedSource plan step. (NOT_IMPLEMENTED) ``` That arm never had a working case: `typeid_cast` matches the exact type, and neither `ReadFromPreparedSource` nor its subclasses implement `clone()`, so every plan it admitted threw. This removes it. The other two arms are kept, and `ReadNothingStep` (which does implement `clone()`) carries the empty-MergeTree case from #95935. The query now takes the pre-existing refusal for unsupported right-side storages, `Can't execute any of specified algorithms ...`, which is what a `Memory` or `StripeLog` right side already returns. This is the "make the exception message better" change @ vdimir asked for when he closed #103473 as not planned: `direct` does not support `Buffer`, so the right behaviour is the ordinary unsupported-storage refusal rather than a clone failure. It deliberately does not make `Buffer` work with `direct`. Two notes beyond the report. The failure is not limited to an empty underlying table as the issue title suggests: it also reproduces with a non-empty `Buffer` and with `INNER JOIN`. And it does not touch the second entry point @ zlareb1 reported, where correlated-subquery decorrelation clones the same step: that path does not go through this allow-list. Hence `Related:` below rather than `Closes:`. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/103473 <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115309&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115309](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115309+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix silently dropped quota intervals when the separating comma is missing
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115282 (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `CREATE QUOTA` and `ALTER QUOTA` silently discarding all but the last `FOR INTERVAL` block when the separating comma between intervals was omitted. Such a statement succeeded while installing none of the earlier limits. The intervals now accumulate again, as they did before 2020. Closes #115282. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115282 `CREATE QUOTA q FOR INTERVAL 1 MINUTE MAX queries = 1 FOR INTERVAL 1 HOUR MAX queries = 100 TO u` succeeded and created a quota holding only the `1 hour` limit. The `1 minute` rate limit the operator wrote, and got no error for, was never installed and never enforced; only `SHOW CREATE QUOTA` revealed the loss. Root cause: in `ParserCreateQuotaQuery.cpp`, `parseIntervalsWithLimits` parses a comma-separated list into a local vector and then *assigned* it over the caller's vector. Its call site in the option loop is deliberately unguarded, so a comma-less continuation makes the loop match a second time and the assignment discards everything parsed earlier. That assignment is a regression from `6146766` (2020-06-06), which replaced an append with an assign while leaving the loop unguarded. The comma-less spelling parsed correctly before it. I restored the append via `insertAtEnd`, which is what the sibling `ParserCreateRowPolicyQuery` already does for the same situation. This covers `CREATE`, `ALTER` and `ATTACH QUOTA`, which share `parseImpl`. Nothing that parses today changes: `insertAtEnd` onto an empty vector is the previous behaviour, so the single-block and comma-separated forms are byte-identical before and after. Only inputs that silently lost data now keep it, so this is not a backward incompatible change. Persisted and replicated definitions are unaffected because the formatter always emits the separating comma. Validation: new stateless test `04926_quota_interval_missing_comma` asserts every affected block kind (`MAX`, `TRACKING ONLY`, `NO LIMITS`, `RANDOMIZED`), two and three intervals, an interleaved `KEYED BY`, duplicate durations and `ALTER`, plus the comma form as an unchanged control and the two existing rejection boundaries. Its fix-proving assertions all fail on unpatched master; 50/50 randomized runs pass. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115320&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115320](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115320+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1679` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Fix flaky 04005_correlated_column_in_lambda by pinning row order
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114550 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `04005_correlated_column_in_lambda` fails `Fast test` with `result differs with reference`. The last query has no `ORDER BY`: ```sql SELECT (SELECT arrayMap(x -> c0 * x, [1, 2])) FROM (SELECT number AS c0 FROM numbers(3)); ``` Its correlated scalar subquery is decorrelated into a JOIN, and the resulting pipeline is multi-stream (`EXPLAIN PIPELINE` shows the expression chain repeated once per stream, resized down to one), so row order depends on which stream finishes first. The test never pinned it. The failure is a pure permutation, never a value change. From the report below: ``` [1] [11,12,13] -[0,0] -[1,2] [2,4] +[1,2] +[0,0] ``` Two *different* permutations occurred on the same commit `9cf364a8`, which rules out a deterministic result change. I reproduced it on a build of pristine master carrying none of #114550: under `max_block_size = 1` an interleaved 200-run A/B on one binary gave 4 distinct permutations (20.5% deviation) without the fix and 200/200 identical output with it. Fix: append `ORDER BY c0` to that one query. `c0` is unique across the three rows, so the order is total. The `.reference` file is unchanged, because the pinned order is the order it already records. This test guards #98285 (PLACEHOLDER nodes for correlated columns in lambdas, closes #85460), so I verified the `ORDER BY` does not hide that regression: with `visitCorrelatedColumn` reverted to its pre-#98285 form the fixed test still aborts and produces no output; restoring it makes the test pass again. Validation: 50/50 runs with randomization, 50/50 with `--no-random-settings` (the `Fast test` shape), 25/25 via `clickhouse-test`. Control arm: the unfixed query under the same conditions fails 9 of 60 runs. Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114550&sha=b5b2d025522dbb54b351249c588220b7311221c3&name_0=PR&name_1=Fast%20test No related open issue found. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115324&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115324](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115324+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix wrong results from compiled `if`/`multiIf`/`CASE` mixing `Date`/`Date32` with `DateTime`/`DateTime64`
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115272 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115146 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed wrong results from `if`, `multiIf` and `CASE` when one branch is a `Date` or `Date32` and the result type is `DateTime` or `DateTime64`. With `compile_expressions = 1` (the default) the compiled expression copied the date's day count into the timestamp column without converting days to seconds, so `if(cond, toDate32('1900-01-01'), toDateTime64('1970-01-01', 3))` returned `1969-12-31 23:59:34.433`. Closes #115272. ### Description Reported by @ PedroTadim in [#115272](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115272), who asked me to fix it and have @Manerone review. **Root cause.** `FunctionIfBase::isCompilableImpl` already intends to refuse these expressions -- its comment reads *"It's difficult to compare Date and DateTime - cannot use JIT compilation."* -- but it tested `WhichDataType::isDate()` and `isDateTime()`, which are exact `TypeIndex` equality, so it refused only `Date`+`DateTime` and admitted `Date32`+`DateTime64`, `Date`+`DateTime64` and `Date32`+`DateTime`. Those reach `nativeCast`, which correctly finds no scale for day-count types and falls through to a plain `CreateIntCast`: `-25567` days becomes `-25567` milliseconds. The predicates were never widened when `Date32` and `DateTime64` were added. **The change** widens both predicates to `isDateOrDate32()` and `isDateTimeOrDateTime64()`, so the guard covers the whole family and the interpreted path runs. `if.cpp` and `multiIf.cpp` inherit this base, so one change covers all three. These expressions lose JIT, as the comment intended and as `Date`+`DateTime` always did. The commit message covers the rejected IR alternative. **Validation.** New test `04930_jit_compiled_if_date_to_datetime` asserts the compiled result equals the `compile_expressions = 0` result over the reported matrix: scales 0/3/6/9, both date and both datetime types, both branch orders, constant and column dates, `if`/`multiIf`/`CASE`, `Nullable(Date32)`, pre/post-1970. 12 of its 14 comparison rows fail without the fix and all pass with it (50/50 runs). The 2 exceptions are controls green both ways: `Date`+`DateTime`, already refused, and same-unit `Date32`+`Date`, which must keep compiling. Those rows are 1-vs-0 parity checks, so they would pass even if compilation stopped. Two further rows pin which shapes compile, via `ProfileEvents['CompiledFunctionExecute']`: it counts executions of an already-compiled node, so it needs no cache drop and the test stays parallel-safe. The mixed-unit row fails on an unpatched binary, so it tracks this change rather than asserting a constant. They are also why the test carries `no-fasttest, no-msan`: those builds have no embedded compiler. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115325&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115325](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115325+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Do not leave metadata referencing a dropped named collection
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/77366 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112805 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Three stateless tests briefly leave table metadata on disk referencing a named collection that no longer exists. The stress test kills and restarts the server at arbitrary points and randomizes `async_load_databases=false`; in that mode `loadMetadata` waits every table load job and rethrows, so the server cannot boot: ``` Caught exception while loading metadata: Code: 722 ... Code: 695 ... Code: 669 ... There is no named collection `nc_missing_sk_test_3`: Cannot attach table ... ENGINE = Remote(...) ``` Measured: 16 occurrences across 13 PRs and 2 master runs in 30 days. Changes, copying the pattern already in `04626_s3_base_setting.sh`: - `04512_remote_missing_named_collection.sh` detaches `PERMANENTLY`. Startup skips a permanently detached table without constructing its storage, while `ATTACH TABLE` still replays the on-disk definition, so every assertion is unchanged and the `.reference` file is untouched. - `04320_url_engine_dispatch_partition_and_format.sh` and `04327_s3queue_server_credentials.sh` create the collection before dropping a possible leftover table, and chain the two teardown drops so the collection outlives the table. Validation. A restart injected where the stress kill lands reproduces the abort deterministically on master and boots cleanly with the change; restarting at every statement boundary of the changed regions shows two boundaries dying before and none after. Each change was reverted one at a time and each reverted half reddens on its own oracle, and pointing an arm at a live collection makes it fail, so the arms are not vacuous. 200/200 randomized runs of these tests plus `04626` pass. Server startup behaviour is unchanged, so the underlying gap remains: dropping a collection while a dependent table is detached still leaves an unstartable server when `async_load_databases = 0`. That was reported in #77366 and closed in favour of a drop-side guard (#96181), which #112805 is extending to detached tables. Tests only: no setting, default or serialization change, so no `SettingsChangesHistory.cpp` entry. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115326&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115326](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115326+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Block disabling the analyzer in the Stress test and fuzzers more tightly
signals.text: The Stress test and the AST fuzzer (and BuzzHouse, which installs the same profile) already constrain `enable_analyzer` to `<min>1</min>` so that neither a test nor a fuzzed query spends the run on the old interpreter. A constraint only rejects an *explicit* setting change though. `compatibility` set below 24.3 — the version where the analyzer became the default — rewrites every setting that is not marked `changed`, so it reverts `enable_analyzer` to 0 without an explicit change and the constraint never fires. With the Stress test profile as it is now: ``` SET compatibility = '23.2'; SELECT getSetting('enable_analyzer') --> false /?compatibility=23.2&query=SELECT getSetting('enable_analyzer') --> false ``` The AST fuzzer profile is immune because it also pins the value (`<enable_analyzer>1</enable_analyzer>`), which keeps the setting `changed` so that `applyCompatibilitySetting` skips it. The Stress test profile had no such pin and relied only on the client-side `enable_analyzer=1` that `stress.py` passes, while `stress.py` randomizes `compatibility` down to 20.1. This pins the value in the Stress test profile too, and documents in all four places why both halves are needed, so that neither is later removed as redundant. The comment in `ast_fuzzer_job.py` still described a `readonly` constraint that was replaced with `min` in 03782060870. The new test builds the same pinned and constrained profile in SQL and checks that: - every explicit way of disabling the analyzer is rejected (`SET`, an in-query `SETTINGS` clause, the `allow_experimental_analyzer` alias, the client command line, settings stored in a view); - a no-op `enable_analyzer = 1` sent together with `compatibility` is still accepted — a `CONST` constraint rejects it, which is why `min` is used; - a pre-24.3 `compatibility` does not revert the pinned value. Not addressed here: `SET <setting> = DEFAULT` is not checked against constraints at all (`resetSettingsToDefaultValue`), so `SET compatibility = '23.2'; SET enable_analyzer = DEFAULT` still gets through. That is a server-side bypass of settings constraints in general and is fixed separately. ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115328&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115328](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115328+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1675` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signals.title: Fix timezoneOffset losing the whole-day component of the UTC offset
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115281 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `timezoneOffset` (alias `timeZoneOffset`) returning an offset wrong by exactly one day for time zones whose UTC offset differs from their 1970-01-01 offset by a whole day, such as `Pacific/Kiritimati` and `Pacific/Apia` after they crossed the international date line, and for most zones before 1970. This also fixes `parseDateTime`, `parseDateTimeOrNull`, `parseDateTime64`, `parseDateTimeInJodaSyntax`, `EXTRACT(TIMEZONE_HOUR / TIMEZONE_MINUTE ...)`, `formatDateTime`'s `%z`, `toUTCTimestamp` and `fromUTCTimestamp`, which consume that offset. Closes #115281. ### Description Reported by @ PedroTadim in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115281#issuecomment-5327580058. `timezoneOffset` did not read the offset, it reconstructed it as `(lut[index].date - lut[epoch].date) % 86400` plus `offset_at_start_of_epoch`. That difference is `days * 86400 - (offset_now - offset_epoch)`, so the modulo keeps only the sub-day part of the change since the epoch and discards any whole-day part; the date-line zones stayed pinned at their pre-jump offset, correct before the jump and wrong after. Separately, `%` takes the sign of the dividend, so on a pre-epoch day the remainder is negative, the `res > 43200` wrap never fired, and the result came out near `+86400` instead of a small negative offset. The fix computes the offset directly as `day_number * 86400 - lut[index].date`: local midnight is that many seconds of local time from the epoch, and `date` is the UTC instant of the same midnight. Exact for either sign, no modulo, no wrap branches. The same-day `amount_of_offset_change` correction is unchanged. All 12 in-tree call sites checked. Seven were wrong and are repaired by this one change: the function itself, the `parseDateTime` family (including a zone named in the format string), `EXTRACT(TIMEZONE_HOUR / TIMEZONE_MINUTE ...)`, `formatDateTime`'s `%z`, and `toUTCTimestamp` / `fromUTCTimestamp`. The other five reduce the offset modulo a day (`CAST ... AS Time` / `Time64`, `localtime`), so an exact one-day error already cancelled; the test pins those as controls. Over all 597 rows of `system.time_zones` at 14 instants from 1900 to 2300, against Python `zoneinfo` as an independent oracle: 500 wrong samples across 307 zones before, 18 after, all 18 being `tzdata` differences between the bundled 2025a and the system 2026a. All 488 changed samples differ by exactly one day, so nothing sub-day moved. <details> <summary>Validation</summary> Both directions through `tests/clickhouse-test`: on the base master debug snapshot (build id `09e3d57a4bbe30cd`) `01252_weird_time_zone` fails with a 39-line reference diff; with the fix (build id `485b33ed0bf6e99c`) it passes, including 50 of 50 randomized runs. `unit_tests_dbms --gtest_filter='*DateLUT*:*DateTime*:*Date*'` passes 7906 tests, so no calendar component moved. The `timezone` stateless suite passes 42 of 42. Six failures in the wider `datetime` and `extract` suites are pre-existing gaps in my local environment (no `remote()` cluster config, no parquet/iceberg fixtures, no `test.hits`) and reproduce identically on the base binary. New arms: the seven reported zones after their jump; the same zones before it and `Pacific/Chatham` (+13:45) as controls that must not move; the pre-1970 class; agreement between `parseDateTime*` and `toDateTime`; the other offset consumers; the modulo-a-day consumers as regression controls; DST transition days; agreement between the in-range and out-of-range paths; and a sweep over `system.time_zones` with no zone list hardcoded, comparing the reported offset to rendering the instant as local text and reading it back as UTC. </details> <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115332&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115332](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115332+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Allow Map data type for asynchronous metrics
signals.text: <!--- A technical comment, you are free to remove or leave it as it is when PR is created The following categories are used in the next scripts, update them accordingly utils/changelog/changelog.py tests/ci/cancel_and_rerun_workflow_lambda/app.py --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Backward Incompatible Change ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md): Asynchronous metrics can now have the `Map` data type, and the per-CPU-core and per-device metrics were converted to single key-value metrics: `OSUserTimeCPU0`, `OSUserTimeCPU1`, ... became a single `OSUserTimeCPU` metric with a map from the CPU core number to the value (and similarly for the other `OS*TimeCPU*` metrics, `CPUFrequencyMHz_*`, `Temperature*`, `EDAC*`, `Block*_*`, `Network(Receive|Send)*_*`, `Disk*_*`, `*BlobsQueueEstimate`, and `AsyncLogging*QueueSize`). `system.asynchronous_metrics` has a new `key_values Map(String, Float64)` column (the `value` column is `NaN` for such metrics), `system.asynchronous_metric_log` logs them as one row per key using a new `key` column, the Prometheus endpoint exports them with a label (e.g. `ClickHouseAsyncMetrics_BlockReadBytes{device="sda"}`), and the Graphite `MetricsTransmitter` sends them as `<prefix>.<Metric>.<key>`. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115321 Some metrics are per CPU core or per device (block device, network interface, disk, temperature sensor, EDAC memory controller, logging channel), and they were published as separate metrics with the entity name mangled into the metric name (`CPUFrequencyMHz_0`, `BlockReadBytes_sda`, `DiskTotal_default`, ...). This pollutes the metric namespace (hundreds of metrics on large machines), makes the set of metric names unstable across servers, and makes aggregation across entities awkward. Now each such family is a single key-value metric. ### Details **Data model.** `AsynchronousMetricValue` gains `key_values` (an ordered map from the entity name to the value) and `key_label` (what the key means: `cpu`, `device`, `interface`, `disk`, `sensor`, `mc`, `channel`; it is also used as the Prometheus label name). A metric is either scalar or key-value. **`system.asynchronous_metrics`.** A new column `key_values Map(String, Float64)` holds the values of a key-value metric; the `value` column is `NaN` for them (an aggregate across entities like a sum is not meaningful for every metric, e.g. `CPUFrequencyMHz` or `Temperature`, so none is invented). Example: ``` SELECT metric, key_values FROM system.asynchronous_metrics WHERE metric = 'CPUFrequencyMHz' ``` I considered making the `value` column `Dynamic` (holding either `Float64` or `Map(String, Float64)`), but it breaks the most common query patterns: `WHERE value > 0` throws `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT` as soon as any row holds a Map, and `avg(value)` stops working. **`system.asynchronous_metric_log`.** A key-value metric is logged as one row per key via a new `key LowCardinality(String)` column (empty for scalar metrics). This keeps `value Float64` (and its compression), and time-series aggregation stays natural: `WHERE metric = 'BlockReadBytes' AND key = 'sda'`, or `sum(value) ... GROUP BY key`. The default `ORDER BY` of the table is now `metric, key, event_date, event_time`. On upgrade, the old table is renamed and a new one is created by the standard system-log schema-mismatch mechanism. **Prometheus.** Key-value metrics are exported as one line per key with a proper label instead of a mangled name: `ClickHouseAsyncMetrics_BlockReadBytes{device="sda"} 123` (merged with the configured constant labels; label values are escaped). **Graphite (`MetricsTransmitter`).** Key-value metrics are sent one path component deeper: `<prefix>.BlockReadBytes.sda`. **Converted metric families** ("change it where reasonable"): - `OS{User,Nice,System,Idle,IOWait,Irq,SoftIrq,Steal,Guest,GuestNice}TimeCPU<n>` → `OS*TimeCPU` keyed by the core number (the all-core sums `OSUserTime` etc. are unchanged) - `CPUFrequencyMHz_<n>` → `CPUFrequencyMHz` - `Temperature<n>` (thermal zones, numeric keys) and `Temperature_<hwmon>[_<sensor>]` (name keys) → a single `Temperature` metric - `EDAC<n>_{Correctable,Uncorrectable}` → `EDAC{Correctable,Uncorrectable}` keyed by the memory controller number - all 17 `Block*_<device>` families → `Block*` keyed by the device name - all 8 `Network{Receive,Send}*_<interface>` families → keyed by the interface name - `Disk{Total,Used,Available,Unreserved}_<disk>` and `Disk{Put,Get}ObjectThrottler{RPS,Available}_<disk>` → keyed by the disk name - `<disk>DeadBlobsQueueEstimate`, `<disk>MissingBlobsQueueEstimate` → `DeadBlobsQueueEstimate`, `MissingBlobsQueueEstimate` keyed by the disk name - `AsyncLogging<Channel>QueueSize` → `AsyncLoggingQueueSize` keyed by the channel name Left as-is (small bounded sets rather than per-device breakdowns): `PSI_*`, `NetworkTCPSockets_<STATE>`, per-protocol thread/rejected-connection metrics, `HTTPConnectionPool<Group>*`, jemalloc arena metrics. **Dashboards.** The only dashboard queries that used suffixed names are the four "Network receive/send bytes/sec" charts of the Cloud overview dashboards, which use `metric LIKE 'NetworkReceiveBytes%'` with `sum(value)` per time point. They are left unchanged deliberately: the `LIKE` pattern matches both the old suffixed rows and the new per-key rows, so the charts stay correct and continuous across the upgrade. The Web UI dashboard (`dashboard.html`) does not hardcode any metric names. **Docs.** The metric list in `docs/reference/system-tables/asynchronous_metrics.mdx` is regenerated by `utils/generate-async-metrics-docs`; the columns of both system tables are documented. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115333&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115333](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115333+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Do not let SET <name> = DEFAULT bypass the settings constraints
signals.text: `SET <name> = DEFAULT` resets a setting rather than assigning to it, so it does not produce a `SettingChange` and never reached `SettingsConstraints`. Any constraint could therefore be escaped by resetting the setting instead of assigning to it: ```sql CREATE SETTINGS PROFILE p SETTINGS max_query_size = 1000 MAX 1000; SET max_query_size = 2000; -- SETTING_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION, as expected SET max_query_size = DEFAULT; -- silently restored the default of 262144 ``` A `CONST` constraint was just as escapable, and so was readonly mode, which is enforced by the same check: ```sql SET readonly = 2; SET readonly = 0; -- READONLY, as expected SET readonly = DEFAULT; -- silently left readonly mode ``` This describes the reset as the change it effectively is — to the value declared in the source code, which is what `Context::resetSettingsToDefaultValue` restores — and runs the usual check on it before anything is applied, so that a violation leaves the whole statement without effect. The in-query `SETTINGS <name> = DEFAULT` form goes through the same interpreter and is covered too. A reset that does not change the value is still allowed, because the check drops changes whose new value equals the current one. Resetting a setting that was never touched therefore keeps working under a `CONST` constraint and in readonly mode — which is what CI profiles that pin a setting to its declared default rely on (`max_parser_backtracks` in `limit-recursion-settings.xml`, for example). Settings without a declared default are unaffected: a custom setting is dropped rather than reset and cannot carry a constraint, and an unknown name stays silently ignored. The client only mirrors the reset into its own settings when the server accepted the statement, so its view does not drift. One consequence worth calling out: a profile that caps `max_threads` below the machine's core count now rejects `SET max_threads = DEFAULT`, because the declared default resolves to `auto(<cores>)`. That is the intended reading of the constraint, but it means the CI profiles that cap `max_threads` at 128 would reject that reset on a machine with more than 128 cores. Verified locally against a build of this change: the four rejection paths above are rejected, the rejected statement leaves the value alone, and the no-op reset, custom-setting reset and unknown-setting reset all keep working. `04202_set_default_preserves_max_threads_auto` and `04078_settings_constraints_compatibility_const` still pass, and a sweep of every stateless test that uses `= DEFAULT` plus every test whose name mentions constraints/readonly/settings profiles produced no constraint or readonly error attributable to this change. signals.title: CI: do not store a failed gh api response as the docs merge base
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104437 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): A failed `gh api .../compare` response is no longer stored as the merge base commit id, so `Docs check (Mintlify)` no longer fails with `fatal: invalid refspec` on a transient API error. ### Description `Docs check (Mintlify)` reds with `fatal: invalid refspec '{"message":"Not Found",...}'` instead of comparing revisions: 16 failures across 9 PRs in the 30 days to 2026-08-18, the most recent that day, in two API classes (15 x 404, one 500 outside any incident). Root cause: `Shell.get_output` defaults to `strict=False` and returns stdout on the failure path too (`ci/praktika/utils.py:196-202`), and `gh api` prints its error body there. A non-2xx `compare` response was therefore stored under `merge_base_commit_sha`, and `docs_job_mintlify.py:144` interpolates it into a `git fetch` refspec whose guard rejects only an empty value. It is `shlex.quote`d, so there is no injection: git gets JSON where a ref belongs, and fails closed. It is sticky too: the key is written once by the `Config Workflow` pre-hook and inherited by every job, so a re-run re-reads it. Over the 12 affected (pr, sha) pairs the check has 123 failed rows and no successful one, one head failing all 3 attempts over 7h46m, cleared only by a new head. And since the job reaches its `Run` step, `retry_infra_failures.yml` sees a non-infra verdict and skips the run's rerun. The fix is at the one call site that stores the key: retry the read and raise rather than return its body, then require a full commit id before storing. On failure the key is simply absent, which the reader's existing guard already reports honestly, so the reader is unchanged. Both halves earn their place: every recorded occurrence exits non-zero, so retry-and-raise alone stops the body being stored, and validation covers `gh api -q` exiting 0 with a non-id. Deliberately not changed: the same shape at `store_data.py` (`master_commits`), `llvm_coverage_job.py:133` and `job_hooks/promql_compliance_s3.py:93`, none with a recorded occurrence and none reaching a refspec (the value only selects an S3 URL or `gh api` path). Carrier: [run 32036646118](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/actions/runs/32036646118/job/95482258798), on #104437. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115338&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115338](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115338+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->
