signals.title: Resume a NATS JetStream subscription after a reconnect
signals.text: A `NATS` table reading from a JetStream stream can stop consuming for good after the NATS server restarts, while still looking subscribed and healthy. An asynchronous JetStream pull subscription asks for more messages only when one is delivered, and when the NATS client reconnects it re-sends the `SUB` line but not the pull request the broker was holding. A broker that goes away without answering that request - a hard kill, a network partition, or a graceful restart that lands in the milliseconds between a re-subscribe and its request being parked - leaves the table subscribed and permanently silent. That is what `test_nats_restore_failed_connection_without_losses_on_write` hits when the consumer is still behind at the moment the broker is stopped: all 100000 rows were published and acknowledged into the stream, but the ones not yet delivered are never fetched again, so the view stays short of them and the test fails with `ClickHouse lost some messages: 92807`. It fails this way on about 0.2% of runs since the NATS tests came back on 2026-07-30, and at the same rate before and after #112828 recovered the closed-subscription case on 2026-08-13 (88 of 46693 runs before, 27 of 15428 after), which is what points at the window that fix leaves open. CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=c260929910ea94be9a359bb69bf5e33d7b3a40e4&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Integration%20tests%20%28arm_binary%2C%20distributed%20plan%2C%204%2F4%29 Recovery so far keyed only on a subscription the NATS client had closed, which is what a graceful shutdown produces by answering the outstanding pull request. This reports a reconnect as well, by comparing the reconnect count the client keeps for the connection against the one taken when we subscribed, and re-subscribes through the same path. Only JetStream consumers do this: a core NATS subscription really is restored by the `SUB` line, and re-subscribing it would drop buffered messages nothing redelivers. The window this closes is the residual documented in #112828, so `_restart_nats` no longer retries until a restart lands outside it, and a new test reaches that state deterministically with `SIGKILL`, which answers nothing and so leaves no closed subscription to fall back on. Verified locally with a release build, running the module through `ci.praktika`: - new test with the fix: passed twice (65 s, 146 s); - new test with `src/Storages/NATS` reverted to `master` and everything else unchanged: `AssertionError: consumption did not resume, view holds 10 of 20 keys` - the messages published after the restart never arrive; - the five existing restart tests plus `test_nats_restore_failed_connection_without_losses_on_write`, all six passed with the fix. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112828 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `NATS` engine table reading from a JetStream stream (`nats_stream`) silently stopping to consume messages after the NATS server restarted or the connection was re-established.

signals.title: Do not widen a Variant result type for an alternative that is NULL for every row
signals.text:
### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `LOGICAL_ERROR` (`Bad cast from type DB::ColumnVariant to DB::ColumnNullable`) when inserting into a MergeTree table whose sorting or primary key applies a function to a `Variant` column, such as `ORDER BY max2(v, v)`. Where the function's common result type can be inside `Nullable`, its declared type no longer depends on `variant_throw_on_type_mismatch` and so can no longer disagree with the column produced. ### Description Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112469 Found by the `BuzzHouse (amd_tsan)` fuzzer: [CI report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=102039&sha=0cb4588fe9c8c2e1a8bb292786f16269e537f09f&name_0=PR&name_1=BuzzHouse%20%28amd_tsan%29), STID 3520-704a. The `LOGICAL_ERROR` is thrown at `SerializationNullable.cpp:216` from `calculateAndSerializePrimaryIndexRow` (`:235`), aborting debug and sanitizer builds. PR 102039 is only the carrier. `FunctionBaseVariantAdaptor` composed its declared return type by a different rule than its own execution uses. Execution drops an alternative that is NULL for every row (`:530`); type construction counted it, so one such alternative widened the type to `Variant(...)`. Such an alternative arises through recursion: when another argument is still a `Variant`, the per-alternative build returns a nested adaptor, and one matching none of its own alternatives differs per strictness mode. Under the default it throws and the alternative is skipped, so `max2` over a `Variant` declares `Nullable(Float64)`, which the Variant-in-key check accepts and records as the key type; leniently it returns `Nullable(Nothing)` and the type widens. The part writer picks `SerializationNullable` from the recorded type and serializes the runtime column unconverted, so a strict `CREATE` plus a lenient `INSERT` handed it a `ColumnVariant` and the cast threw. The composition now skips such an alternative, so the declared type describes the column the adaptor builds; storage is fixed as a consequence. The discriminator is where the alternative came from, not what its type looks like: a `Nothing` or `Nullable(Nothing)` a function genuinely returns is kept, since `arrayElementOrNull` over an `Array(Nothing)` alternative produces one in both modes, and dropping it would move the declared type of a key or skip index accepted today. Collapsing is also skipped when the common type cannot be inside `Nullable`, which would turn those NULL rows into defaults. An alternative whose build *throws* still leaves the strict type bare for `Array` and `Map`: pre-existing, unchanged.
Declared type of max2 over a Variant, before and after | expression | before, strict | before, lenient | after, both | |---|---|---|---| | `Variant(UInt8)` | `Nullable(Float64)` | `Nullable(Float64)` | `Nullable(Float64)` | | `Variant(UInt8, Int128)` | `Nullable(Float64)` | `Variant(Float64)` | `Nullable(Float64)` | | `Variant(UInt8, String)` | `Nullable(Float64)` | `Variant(Float64)` | `Nullable(Float64)` | Values are unchanged: rows of an incompatible alternative are NULL before and after. When the common type cannot be inside `Nullable`, the declared type and both row values are untouched: | expression | common type | before and after | |---|---|---| | `mapFromArrays` over two Variants | `Map(UInt8, String)` | `Variant(Map(UInt8, String))`, rows `{1:'x',2:'y'}` / `NULL` | | `arrayConcat` over a Variant | `Array(UInt8)` | `Variant(Array(UInt8))`, rows `[1,2,1,2]` / `NULL` | New test covers compact and wide writers, two pruning skip indices, `OPTIMIZE FINAL` and `DETACH`/`ATTACH`, and pins the paths that must not change, including `arrayElement` and `arrayElementOrNull` over a `Nothing` alternative in both modes. A set index written by the pre-fix binary over such an expression is read back with values and pruning intact. 50/50 randomized runs passed.

signals.title: Use the text index when a tokenizer argument matches the index tokenizer
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115275 (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): A `text` index is now used for `hasAnyTokens`, `hasAllTokens` and `hasPhrase` called with an explicit tokenizer argument, when that argument denotes the same tokenizer as the index and the index has no `preprocessor` or `postprocessor`. Previously the three-argument form always fell back to a full scan. Closes #115275. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115275 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/108808 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107186 `MergeTreeIndexConditionText::traverseAtomNode` rejected any function node that was not binary before it looked at the function name, so a three-argument `hasAnyTokens` / `hasAllTokens` / `hasPhrase` never reached `isSupportedFunction` (which already lists all three). The predicate became an unknown atom: no granule pruning and no direct read. This mattered because the three-argument form is the documented workaround for #108808, so users of a non-`splitByNonAlpha` tokenizer had no option that was both correct and indexed. The gate now admits three arguments for those three functions when the argument's tokenizer canonicalizes to the index tokenizer. Equality compares `ITokenizer::getDescription()`, which is the form the direct-read pass already synthesizes for the two-argument case, so registered aliases and spelling variants compare equal while parameters still discriminate (`ngrams(3)` is not `ngrams(4)`). Everything else keeps full-scanning, by design and per @ rschu1ze's ruling on the issue: a different tokenizer, a non-constant or invalid argument, and an index carrying a `preprocessor` or `postprocessor` option (there the index stores tokens of a transformed value that the argument's bare tokenizer never produces, so the two cannot answer the same predicate). No error is raised on a mismatch. `hasPhrase` is included at @CurtizJ's request (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115275#issuecomment-5328448695). The direct-read pass is kept argument-count-preserving: it now assigns the tokenizer argument in place when one is already present rather than appending, because that pass can legitimately run over the same node twice and would otherwise build a four-argument call. `02346_text_index_function_hasPhrase{,_positions}` asserted the old full-scan behavior for this exact case. Those sections are retitled and regenerated, and a mismatching-tokenizer sibling case is added at the same site so the full-scan boundary keeps a pinned oracle. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115348&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115348](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115348+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Support the short ATTACH syntax for views
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115259 (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114747 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `ATTACH VIEW <name>` and `ATTACH MATERIALIZED VIEW <name>` now re-attach a previously detached view from its stored metadata, like `ATTACH TABLE` and `ATTACH DICTIONARY` already did. Previously only `DETACH VIEW` was accepted and the matching `ATTACH` was a syntax error. Closes #115259. ### Description Requested by @ PedroTadim in #115259, who reported it and offered to review; [acknowledged here](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115259#issuecomment-5327133729). `VIEW` was the only object kind where `DETACH X <name>` had no matching `ATTACH X <name>`. `ParserCreateTableQuery` has a short-attach shortcut (`ParserCreateQuery.cpp:858`) and `ParserCreateDictionaryQuery` skips its body clauses when attaching, but `ParserCreateViewQuery` required the body unconditionally and died at the mandatory `AS`. I added the same shortcut there, keeping the view flags on the AST so the interpreter routes it as a view. Two interpreter changes follow. I proved each on a parser-only build first. `createTable` synthesized an empty `sql_security` for any AST whose `supportSQLSecurity()` is true, which the new branch sets, and `has_dropped_clauses` then threw `BAD_ARGUMENTS` about a clause the user never wrote. I suppress the synthesis for the body-less ATTACH shape rather than reordering the defaulting, so a stored view is never re-defaulted on re-attach. `getRequiredAccess()` authorizes from the typed keyword before metadata is read, and `CREATE TABLE` implies `CREATE VIEW`, so the parser change alone let a user holding only `CREATE VIEW` attach a detached ordinary table via `ATTACH VIEW t` (measured). I reject a VIEW-spelled short ATTACH whose stored metadata is not a view. The `TABLE` spelling stays permissive: it requires the stronger `CREATE TABLE`, and `ATTACH TABLE` on a detached view is the workaround the issue documents. `ATTACH WINDOW VIEW` has the same gap, left alone while #114747 removes `WINDOW VIEW` from this file. `DETACH MATERIALIZED VIEW` is also a syntax error, but `DETACH VIEW mv` already works, so nothing is user-visible there. Validation: three new stateless tests (syntax, access, `sql_security` suppression) plus a converted arm of `01600_detach_permanently`, each verified to fail without its change; those four and five further existing tests around this path pass; 200/200 green over 50 randomized runs each. <details> <summary>Sibling and edge-case matrix</summary> | statement | before | after | |---|---|---| | `ATTACH VIEW v` | `SYNTAX_ERROR` | re-attaches | | `ATTACH MATERIALIZED VIEW mv` | `SYNTAX_ERROR` | re-attaches | | `ATTACH VIEW IF NOT EXISTS v` | `SYNTAX_ERROR` | re-attaches, idempotent | | `ATTACH VIEW v ON CLUSTER c` | `SYNTAX_ERROR` | resolves the cluster | | `ATTACH VIEW db.v` | `SYNTAX_ERROR` | re-attaches | | `ATTACH VIEW v UUID '...'` | `SYNTAX_ERROR` | `BAD_ARGUMENTS`, as `ATTACH TABLE t UUID '...'` | | `ATTACH TEMPORARY VIEW v` | `SYNTAX_ERROR` (parser) | `SYNTAX_ERROR` (interpreter), as `ATTACH TEMPORARY TABLE` | | `ATTACH VIEW <a table>` | n/a | `INCORRECT_QUERY`, "it is a Table" | | `ATTACH WINDOW VIEW wv` | `SYNTAX_ERROR` | unchanged, see #114747 | | `ATTACH OR REPLACE VIEW v` | `SYNTAX_ERROR` | unchanged | | `ATTACH SQL SECURITY INVOKER VIEW v` | `SYNTAX_ERROR` | unchanged | | `ATTACH DEFINER = u VIEW v` | `SYNTAX_ERROR` | unchanged | | `DETACH MATERIALIZED VIEW mv` | `SYNTAX_ERROR` | unchanged, out of scope | | `ATTACH TABLE <a detached view>` | works | works | | `ATTACH TABLE t` / `DICTIONARY d` / `DATABASE db` | works | works | </details> <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115351&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115351](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115351+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Keep one output port per shard when a JOIN side reads nothing
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115057 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109393 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `LOGICAL_ERROR` (`Join is supported only for pipelines with one output port`) for a `full_sorting_merge` JOIN with `query_plan_join_shard_by_pk_ranges` enabled when one of the two sides is pruned to no parts at all - by the primary key, by column statistics, or because the table is empty. ### Description A JOIN sharded by primary-key ranges pairs the shards of its two sides positionally, so both sides have to produce exactly one output port per layer. `optimizeJoinByShards` builds the layers from the parts of all the sources at once and hands every source the same number of them, and `ReadFromMergeTree::readByLayers` keeps the port of an empty layer occupied by substituting a `NullSource` for it. That invariant did not hold for a source that reads nothing at all: `ReadFromMergeTree::initializePipeline` replaced the whole side with a single `NullSource` before it ever reached the layers. A side pruned to zero parts therefore arrived at the JOIN with one port while the other side kept its layers, the stream counts disagreed, `JoinStep` stopped using sharding, and the `YShaped` pipeline it went to instead accepts only a single port per side: ``` Logical error: 'Join is supported only for pipelines with one output port, got 1 and 2' ``` The fix emits one `NullSource` per layer, so the number of ports stays what the plan says it is. The layers are only ever set by `optimizeJoinByShards` (gated by `query_plan_join_shard_by_pk_ranges`, off by default) and are ignored for a read coordinated across parallel replicas, so for every other query the pipeline is unchanged. The comment at the `JoinStep` fallback claimed that the regular pipeline handles diverging stream counts. That is true for `joinPipelinesRightLeft` (hash) but not for the merge-join path, and it is what made the missing invariant look intentional, so it is corrected as well. This replaces the approach in #109393, which merged the diverging streams back together inside `joinPipelinesYShaped`; @vdimir asked there for the invariant to be fixed at its source instead, which is what this pull request does. The throw in `joinPipelinesYShaped` is left in place. Reproducer (the second query is the shape from the CI report - the sharded side keeps its layers while the other side is pruned away): ```sql CREATE TABLE t_l (k UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY k SETTINGS index_granularity = 128; CREATE TABLE t_r (k UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY k SETTINGS index_granularity = 128; INSERT INTO t_l SELECT number FROM numbers(1000); INSERT INTO t_r SELECT number FROM numbers(1000); SET query_plan_join_shard_by_pk_ranges = 1, join_algorithm = 'full_sorting_merge', max_threads = 4; SELECT count() FROM t_l AS l JOIN (SELECT * FROM t_r WHERE k > 1000000) AS r ON l.k = r.k; SELECT count() FROM (SELECT * FROM t_l WHERE k > 1000000) AS l LEFT JOIN t_r AS r ON l.k = r.k; ``` ### How the CI report maps onto this The failing test in the report is `03447_analyzer_correlated_subqueries_tpc_h` (TPC-H Q2), run by the settings randomizer with `query_plan_join_shard_by_pk_ranges = 1` and `join_algorithm = 'full_sorting_merge'`. Replaying that query with the report's own settings, `EXPLAIN PLAN indexes=1` shows the sharded join with one side gone: ``` Join (JOIN YShaped) part ⋈ partsupp Join conditions: p_partkey = ps_partkey Sharding: [(p_partkey = ps_partkey)] ├── ReadFromMergeTree (part) Parts: 0 | Granules: 0 <- pruned by the statistics on p_size └── ReadFromMergeTree (partsupp) Parts: 1 | Granules: 1 ``` `part` is pruned to `Parts: 0` and collapses to a single port; `partsupp` keeps one port per layer. CI report this starts from: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=172d9bf947f5081ddd3288073fe0cf6be664b924&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_debug%29 The stack is one of the most frequent stress and AST-fuzzer failures at the moment: 57 hits of this exact `STID 4488-4e11` since 2026-05-27 (5 of them on master), plus 21 more of the two sibling stacks `4488-4590` and `4488-4a91`. ### Verification - The reproducer above, the one from #115057, and the new test `05019_join_shard_by_pk_ranges_pruned_side` all abort on a master binary (`got 4 and 1`) and pass with the fix. - The new test also compares the sharded result against `join_algorithm = 'hash'` with `count()` plus a `cityHash64` checksum for the `LEFT`/`RIGHT` cases, where every row of the surviving side reaches the output. This covers the semantics of the padded pipeline, not only the disappearance of the exception. - TPC-H Q2 from `03447_analyzer_correlated_subqueries_tpc_h` with the report's full settings passes. - All 1061 local stateless tests matching `join`, and the primary-key-sharding tests (`03357`, `03668`, `03774`, `04065`, `04251`, `04517`, `04655`, `04812`), pass. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115352&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115352](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115352+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Test that a normal projection is used through the Merge engine
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/63445 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/63445 Issue #63445 asked whether a `Merge` table can use a projection defined on its subtables. It works on master, so this pins it with a test. Requested by @ rienath (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/63445#issuecomment-5329931686). Nothing in-tree covered this: no test under `tests/queries/0_stateless` both creates a `Merge` table and mentions projections. The test reads two `MergeTree` tables through a `Merge` table and asserts that `system.query_log.projections` names the projection of *both* subtables, plus the query result. Asserting the result alone would not catch a silent loss of projection usage, which is what the issue is about. I verified the assertion can redden: with the projections dropped, or with `optimize_use_projections = 0`, the column becomes `[]` while the result is unchanged. `index_granularity = 8` is pinned because at a large granularity the whole fixture is one granule and no projection is selected. Two notes on what this does not cover. The projection name is not printed by `EXPLAIN` through a `Merge` table, so the obvious `EXPLAIN` assertion would fail on working behaviour; hence `query_log`. `force_optimize_projection_name` is also unusable here: it throws `INCORRECT_DATA` through `ENGINE = Merge` even when the projection is used, because the child plan is optimized a second time when the pipeline is built. Aggregate projections are still not used through `Merge` (#34968, open), so this test deliberately pins only the normal-projection case. The `duplicate #34968` comment on #63445 is not accurate: the two cases behave differently on master. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115353&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115353](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115353+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix `clickhouse-local` printing TSV instead of PrettyCompact in interactive mode
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/105249 Interactive `clickhouse-local` on master renders query results as `TSV` instead of the terminal default `PrettyCompact`. `applyCmdOptions` seeds the `default_format` setting on `global_context` as the fallback format of the sessions of the embedded protocol listeners (`SYSTEM START LISTEN`), where it must match a real `clickhouse-server` (`TabSeparated`). `client_context` is copied from `global_context` and inherits the seed, and the per-query output-format resolution introduced in #105249 treats a non-empty `default_format` setting as the fallback format, so the seed overrode the interactive display default. (#105249 guarded `--vertical` against exactly this failure mode, but the plain interactive default slipped through: it is the one case where `is_default_format` stays true.) The fix clears the seeded value on `client_context`, in `makeFormatOptionsPrivateToTheClient`, which already handles the mirror image of this problem for the `format` / `input_format` / `output_format` settings. This client renders results from its own `ClientBase::default_output_format`, so the seed is not needed there. Explicit choices keep working: an explicit `--default_format` on the command line is left in place (guarded by `cmd_settings->isChanged`), and a later `SET default_format = ...` or an in-query `SETTINGS` clause lands on `client_context` after the clearing. The served sessions still get the fallback through `global_context`. Verified against the master CI binary (26.8.1.1658, where the regression reproduces): emulating the fix by forcing an empty `default_format` on the client restores `PrettyCompact`, while `SET default_format = 'JSONEachRow'` and `SETTINGS default_format = 'CSV'` continue to be honored. The added `04927_local_interactive_default_format.expect` test fails on current master and passes with the fix emulated; the listener-side default is already covered by `04501_local_http_default_format.expect`. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a regression on master (not present in any release): interactive `clickhouse-local` rendered query results as `TSV` instead of `PrettyCompact`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115360&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115360](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115360+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Performance test for ARRAY JOIN lazy replication over serialized plans
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112330 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112330 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description The performance test @ alexey-milovidov asked for on #112330, which made `ArrayJoinStep` carry `enable_lazy_columns_replication` in its serialized flags. Before it, a shard running a serialized plan fragment fell back to the plan default `false` and replicated ARRAY JOIN payloads eagerly. That path had no performance coverage. One query: `remote('127.0.0.{2,3}', view(...))` with ARRAY JOIN and `serialize_query_plan = 1`, so the shard really runs `ArrayJoinStep::deserialize` (`EXPLAIN distributed=1` shows `ArrayJoin` under `ReadFromRemote`). Two constraints decide whether this measures anything. The payload must be a wide `String`, because `isLazyReplicationUseful` declines fixed-width columns of 8 bytes or less (also why `tests/performance/array_join.xml` could not be extended). And no function may touch it, since that converts the replicated column to a full one in both arms, hence the bare `SELECT wide`. Four settings gate the measured path, so all four are pinned: flipping any one collapses the pre-fix/post-fix ratio from 68x to about 1x while the test still passes. Also adds `process_query_plan_packet` to the perf harness config: it defaults to `false` here, so without it the query fails with `SUPPORT_IS_DISABLED` rather than running slower. It predates every active release base, so the reference binary accepts it. Measured with `perf.py` between release builds `f61ce92` (pre-fix) and `fbf131e`: median 0.762 s versus 0.016 s, about 49x, p = 4.1e-12; peak memory on the initiator 1677 MiB versus 12.5 MiB. Scope: on a pull request both sides carry the fix, so this reports parity and acts as a regression guard. The 49x is my own before/after measurement between those builds, not something this PR's run will show. The `release_base` job reverts `tests/performance` to the release base, so it skips this test rather than comparing across the fix. Worst gated per-run figure 0.47 s against a 2 s limit. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115364&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115364](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115364+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix mutation failing on CLEAR COLUMN when a MATERIALIZED column reads an EPHEMERAL column
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/103182 ## Problem `ALTER TABLE ... CLEAR COLUMN` fails on a table that has a `MATERIALIZED` column whose expression reads an `EPHEMERAL` column: ```sql CREATE TABLE t ( x Int32, y Int32, e Int32 EPHEMERAL 0, me Int32 MATERIALIZED x + e, me2 Int32 MATERIALIZED me + 100, mk Int32 MATERIALIZED x + 1 ) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple() PARTITION BY tuple(); INSERT INTO t (x, y, e) VALUES (1, 0, 7); ALTER TABLE t CLEAR COLUMN x IN PARTITION tuple(); ``` ``` Code: 341. DB::Exception: Exception happened during execution of mutation 'mutation_2.txt' with part 'all_1_1_0' reason: 'Code: 47. DB::Exception: Missing columns: 'e' while processing: 'x + e', required columns: 'x' 'e', available columns: 'me2' 'mk' 'me' 'y' 'x'. (UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER)' ``` - The mutation stays in the queue and keeps retrying, so with `mutations_sync = 2` the `ALTER` either throws or waits indefinitely. - `mk`, which does need recomputing after the clear, keeps its stale value (`2` instead of `1`). - Only the presence of the `EPHEMERAL`-derived column matters; the cleared column itself is unrelated to it. The code being fixed was added to master in #103182 and is not part of any release, so no released version is affected. ## Root cause `MutationsInterpreter::prepare` builds the set of `MATERIALIZED` columns that a `CLEAR COLUMN` recomputes (`clear_affected_materialized`). It used the reachability closure only as a non-emptiness test and then inserted **every** `MATERIALIZED` column of the table: ```cpp if (!clear_column_names.empty() && !affected_materialized_closure(clear_column_names).empty()) { for (const auto & column : columns_desc) if (column.default_desc.kind == ColumnDefaultKind::Materialized && column.default_desc.expression) clear_affected_materialized.insert(column.name); } ``` That set drives `emit_materialized_recompute_stages`, so the recompute also covered `me`, whose expression mentions the `EPHEMERAL` column `e`. `EPHEMERAL` columns exist only during `INSERT`, which is why the dependency analysis earlier in the same function deliberately skips such columns — so `e` is not in the stage's available columns and evaluating `x + e` throws `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER`, killing the mutation. ## Solution Use the closure itself as the recompute set. It contains exactly the `MATERIALIZED` columns reachable from a cleared column, and because the analysis skips `EPHEMERAL`-derived columns, it never contains a column that cannot be recomputed. This also stops `CLEAR COLUMN` from rewriting `MATERIALIZED` columns that have nothing to do with the cleared one. Regression test `04926_clear_column_ephemeral_materialized`: the case above (`mk` recomputed, `me` and `me2` left alone) plus a must-not-act case where the cleared column is read by no `MATERIALIZED` column, so no recompute may be emitted at all. On master the first case dies with the exception above. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115371&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115371](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115371+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix MATERIALIZED column value depending on the selected columns while a mutation is pending
signals.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/103182 ## Problem While a mutation is pending, the value of a `MATERIALIZED` column can depend on which columns the query selects: ```sql CREATE TABLE t (id UInt64, x Int32, z Int32, m1 Int32 MATERIALIZED x + z, m2 Int32 MATERIALIZED m1 + 1) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id SETTINGS enable_block_number_column = 1, enable_block_offset_column = 1; INSERT INTO t (id, x, z) VALUES (1, 10, 100); SYSTEM STOP MERGES t; SET alter_sync = 0, mutations_sync = 0, enable_lightweight_update = 1, apply_patch_parts = 1; ALTER TABLE t UPDATE x = 20 WHERE 1; -- stays pending SET apply_mutations_on_fly = 0; UPDATE t SET z = 500 WHERE 1; -- lightweight update, creates a patch part SET apply_mutations_on_fly = 1; ``` ``` SELECT m2 FROM t; -- 511 (consistent with m1 = 510, the value in the patch) SELECT x, z, m1, m2 FROM t; -- 20 500 520 521 ``` Both reads see the same data, so both must return the same `m1` / `m2`. The expected result is `20 500 510 511`: `m1` in the patch part was computed from `x = 10`, the value visible when the lightweight update ran. The code being fixed was added to master in #103182 and is not part of any release, so no released version is affected. ## Root cause After an `UPDATE`, `MutationsInterpreter::prepare` emits one stage per dependency level to recompute the `MATERIALIZED` columns derived from the updated ones (`emit_materialized_recompute_stages`). Those stages were created with a plain `stages.emplace_back(context)`, leaving `Stage::mutation_version` unset, while the `UPDATE`'s own stage carries `command.mutation_version` (via `addStageIfNeeded`). On-fly reads derive the patch-visibility window from consecutive stages' versions (`AlterConversions::getMutationSteps`, `MergeTreeReadersChain`), so a version-less stage leaves that window unbounded above: a patch part created *after* the pending `UPDATE` becomes visible to the recompute stages, which then recompute `m1` from the patched `z` and override the value the patch carries itself. Whether that happens depends on which columns the read requests, hence the two different answers above. ## Solution Pass the command's version into the recompute stages, so they are fenced exactly like the stage of the command they belong to. The patch-materialization and `CLEAR COLUMN` call sites keep the current behaviour (`std::nullopt`): the stages they follow carry no version either, and choosing a version for them is a separate question, out of scope here. Regression test `04927_materialized_recompute_stage_mutation_version`, which on master returns `20 500 520 521` / `520` instead of `20 500 510 511` / `510`. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115372&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115372](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115372+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Perf: Optimize PromQL and for exact groups
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): PromQL `and` expressions with an exact group key skip redundant matching stages. ## What changed - add a fast path for the PromQL set operator `and` - use it when both inputs already match on the original `group` column - join the unique left and right `VECTOR_GRID` inputs directly - keep the left-hand values and filter them by right-side sample presence - keep `on(...)`, non-empty `ignoring(...)`, `on()`, and other transformed matching keys on the existing general path - add exact-output coverage for grouped `and` expressions - cover empty `ignoring()` when both inputs already have exact groups - add a performance fixture with an exact-group query and an `and on(instance)` control ## Why this is safe `VECTOR_GRID` guarantees one row per `group`. The fast path is enabled only when the matching rules leave the original `group` column unchanged on both sides, so the join key is already unique and exact. The exact-group path removes the right-side per-group count aggregation and the transformed-key join. It returns the left value only when the corresponding right value is present, which is the existing `and` masking behavior. `on(...)`, non-empty `ignoring(...)`, and other cases that transform the matching key keep the current general lowering. Empty `ignoring()` is treated like default matching when both inputs already have exact groups. ## Benchmark Ran `tests/performance/promql_set_operators_and.xml` on Apple Silicon with the Release build from this PR. - 8,000 series - 4,000 matching groups - 300 samples per series - 7 measured runs per query on each of two local server instances The table shows the average of the two per-server medians. Both queries are equivalent for this fixture. The default query uses the new exact-group fast path. The `and on(instance)` query keeps the existing generic implementation. | Query | Median | | --- | ---: | | exact-group `and` | 130.2 ms | | equivalent `and on(instance)` query | 139.8 ms | The exact-group query took 130.2 ms versus 139.8 ms for the existing implementation, which is 6.9% faster in this test. ## Tests - add grouped exact-output coverage for `and` - add exact-output coverage for empty `ignoring()` - keep the existing ungrouped and transformed-key `and` coverage - compile the changed translation unit with the ClickHouse warning set and `-Werror` Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115219

signals.title: Bound the shutdown wait for cancelled backups and restores
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115105 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): With `shutdown_wait_backups_and_restores = 0`, a `BACKUP` or `RESTORE` whose I/O did not return kept the server from terminating on a single `SIGTERM`, because shutdown waited for it to reach a final status with no timeout. That wait is now bounded by `shutdown_wait_unfinished`, and new backups and restores are refused once shutdown has begun. ### Description Related: #115105 Reported by @ PedroTadim, who [asked me to take it](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115105#issuecomment-5326577830). The issue stays open. **Cause.** Shutdown waits with `status_changed.wait` - no timeout, predicate on the operation status only, so it lasts as long as the operation. `cancelAll` does not help: cancellation is polled per file (`checkTimeLimit()` before `writeFile`), and within a file `BackupImpl` uses the `copyData` overload with no cancellation hook, so a thread parked in a read never sees it. **Change**, all inside the `shutdown_wait_backups_and_restores = 0` branch of `Server.cpp`: refuse new operations, bound the wait at `shutdown_wait_unfinished`, and on non-convergence feed the forced exit that already handles `!joined_refresh_tasks`. That exit is `_exit`, so the unbounded `thread_pools->wait()` in `BackupsWorker::shutdown()` is never reached rather than bounded. `addInfo` refuses after its dedup early-return: `UNFINISHED` for internal operations (retriable in `DDLWorker`), `QUERY_WAS_CANCELLED` otherwise. **Not fixed here.** The default `= 1` branch is untouched, so the hang is still reachable with stock settings: that setting is documented as waiting for backups to *finish*, so capping it changes the guarantee and is your call. Also unchanged: the per-file cancellation granularity, and `BackupsWorker::shutdown()` reached without this guard (failed startup script), where bounding its status waits just moves the block to the pool join. An abandoned backup keeps its `CREATING_BACKUP` row and can leave partial files. **Validation.** The new tests wedge a backup with the existing `backup_pause_on_start` failpoint, which parks the thread upstream of both `checkTimeLimit()` polls, so the operation never sees its own cancellation. The oracle is whether `stop_clickhouse()` escalated to `SIGKILL`, not elapsed time and not a log line (`_exit` discards the async log queue). One arm requires self-exit and fails on master; a second raises the setting to 600 and requires the server to keep waiting, so a hardcoded deadline fails it. 50/50 stable; sibling shutdown and on-cluster cancel tests pass. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115377&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115377](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115377+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Add a notebook mode to the Web UI
signals.text: Adds a notebook mode to the Web SQL UI (`/play`): a tab can become an ordered sequence of cells, each either a query with its own result or a block of Markdown text — the shape of document Jupyter, Observable, Hex and Deepnote use, and for the same purpose: keeping a chain of queries, and the reasoning between them, on one page. ## How it works A tab starts as a single query cell and looks exactly as it always has — no headers, no cell chrome, no notebook. Once a query has produced a result, a large muted `[+]` appears under it and expands into the two kinds of cell that can be added, query or text. Adding the second cell is what turns notebook mode on, and it is per tab: one tab can be a notebook while another stays a plain single-query editor, and each tab remembers its own notebook across reloads. From two cells on, each cell gets a header with its position and kind (`1. Query`, `2. Text`) and the editing actions: run, edit, insert a cell before, move up/down, delete. There is still exactly one query editor on the page — the full one, with its highlighting backdrop, autocompletion and query-parameter inputs. In notebook mode it is docked into whichever query cell is active, and shown only while it has the focus; as soon as focus leaves, that cell collapses to its query on a single line, syntax highlighted, whitespace runs reduced to one space, fading out on the right. The Run / progress / copy / download row docks under the query being edited, between it and its result, and appears and disappears with the editor. Results are more compact: a smaller font with the cell padding scaled to match, and a table of at most a quarter of the viewport that is its own scroll container on both axes, so its (thin) scrollbars sit at its own edges and a long or wide result neither pushes the notebook down the page nor widens it. Results and Markdown editors can be resized by dragging their bottom edge, as the query editor already could. A text cell shows its Markdown source with the markers highlighted while it is being edited, and the rendered result once editing finishes. Raw HTML is escaped and link targets are restricted to `http`, `https`, `mailto` and relative URLs. ## Implementation The query text, parameters and result snapshot moved from the tab to a cell. `tab.query` / `tab.result` / `tab.resultEl` and the rest are now accessors onto the cell the editor is docked in, so the editor, history, URL and persistence code is unchanged and always means "the cell in front of the user". A run captures its own cell, so moving on to another cell mid-run does not redirect the response. The Logs/Metrics view and the resource meters follow the cell whose result they describe. The whole notebook is persisted in IndexedDB alongside the rest of the workspace, and history entries record the cell they belong to so Back/Forward cannot push one cell's query into another. A tab holding a single cell renders exactly as before — verified by screenshot diff against `master`: 51 pixels differ, all on one row, all by 1 in a single channel. ## Testing Driven in headless Chrome against a local server: cell creation and deletion, moving and inserting cells, collapsing and expanding, per-tab independence, tab duplicate/close with a docked editor, query parameters inside a cell, per-cell errors, reload restore from IndexedDB, "Run all" inside a cell, the Logs and Metrics views per cell, column and result resizing, the theme switch and download menu inside the docked Run row, Markdown rendering and backdrop alignment, and light and dark themes. Two pre-existing issues were fixed along the way: the download drop-down positioned itself without accounting for `#main`'s scroll offset, and the `#run` submit button needed `form="controls"` once it could be moved out of the form's subtree. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added a notebook mode to the Web UI (`/play`). After a query is run, a `[+]` button under the result adds further cells, each either a query with its own result or a block of Markdown text, turning the tab into a notebook in the style of Jupyter or Observable. Cells can be run, reordered, inserted and deleted individually; the query editor collapses to a single line when it is not focused, results are bounded and scroll inside themselves, and the whole notebook is restored on reload. Notebook mode is per tab, so a tab that has only one cell looks and behaves exactly as before. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115378&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115378](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115378+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Add a `bucketed` schema for `system.metric_log`: a single Map column with Enum keys and 128 buckets
signals.text: Adds a new `schema_type` option `bucketed` for `system.metric_log` (the default `wide` and the `transposed` schemas are unchanged): ```xml <metric_log> <schema_type>bucketed</schema_type> </metric_log> ``` With this schema, all profile events and current metrics are stored in a single `metrics` column of type `Map(Enum16(...), Int64)`, where the `Enum16` value is the global metric index and zero values are not stored (a lookup of a missing key in a `Map` returns `0`). The default table definition uses the bucketed `Map` serialization with a constant number of 128 buckets: ``` SETTINGS map_serialization_version = 'with_buckets', map_serialization_version_for_zero_level_parts = 'basic', max_buckets_in_map = 128, map_buckets_strategy = 'constant', map_buckets_min_avg_size = 0 ``` Parts created by inserts keep the basic serialization to avoid creating many small files on every flush; merged parts are always split into 128 buckets. Every metric is also exposed through an `ALIAS` column, e.g. `ProfileEvent_Query UInt64 ALIAS metrics['ProfileEvent_Query']`, so all queries, dashboards, and tests written for the `wide` schema continue to work. Reading a single metric goes through the `Map` key subcolumn (`metrics.key_ProfileEvent_Query`), which reads only the bucket containing the key: in a local test it reads ~100 times less data than reading the whole map (616 vs 60716 bytes on the same rows). Supporting changes: - `arrayElement` on a `Map` with `Enum` keys now accepts the string name of the enum value (`m['name']`): the index is cast to the key type, so an unknown name throws the `UNKNOWN_ELEMENT_OF_ENUM` exception, while a name that is in the `Enum` but absent from the map returns the default value. This previously threw `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT`. - The rewrite of `m['key']` to a key subcolumn in `FunctionToSubcolumnsPass` now supports `Enum`-keyed maps indexed by the name of the enum value, so both the aliases and ad-hoc queries prune buckets. - System logs can declare additional default engine settings via `getDefaultEngineSettings`, merged with the `settings` from the server configuration when no custom `engine` is specified. - An unknown `metric_log.schema_type` value is now rejected with an error instead of silently disabling the table. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Add a new `bucketed` schema type for `system.metric_log`, which stores all metrics in a single `Map(Enum16(...), Int64)` column using the bucketed `Map` serialization with 128 buckets, plus a per-metric `ALIAS` column for compatibility: the table consists of a few columns instead of thousands, zero values are not stored, and reading a single metric reads only one of the 128 buckets. In addition, a `Map` with `Enum` keys can now be indexed by the string name of the enum value, e.g. `map['name']`. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: Query cache on disk, backed by the filesystem cache
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115361 The query cache can now additionally store its entries on disk, backed by a preconfigured filesystem cache (an entry of the `filesystem_caches` section of the server configuration), selected per query with the new setting `query_cache_on_disk_cache_name`. Compared to the in-memory query cache, this gives the entries more space, makes them survive server restarts, and (with a distributed filesystem cache) provides a way to share them between servers. Design, following the RFC in the issue: - The entries are ordinary filesystem cache entries, indistinguishable from other data in the same filesystem cache: they are not held from deletion, they are evicted by the same rules, and there are no specific limits on their total size or number other than the limits of the filesystem cache itself. The keys are hashed with a salt so that they cannot intersect with other keys in the filesystem cache. - No extra in-memory state is kept: all metadata needed to validate an entry (TTL, user id, roles, the shared flag) is serialized into the entry itself, followed by the result payload in `Native` format, compressed with the codec from the new setting `query_cache_on_disk_codec` (default `ZSTD(3)`; reading is independent of the setting because the compressed frames are self-describing). - The on-disk cache works independently of the in-memory cache and can separately be enabled for reads and/or writes with the new settings `enable_reads_from_query_cache_on_disk` and `enable_writes_to_query_cache_on_disk` (both `true` by default, activated by setting `query_cache_on_disk_cache_name`). If both caches are enabled for reads, the lookup is attempted first from memory and only on a miss from disk. If both caches are enabled for writes, the result is written to both. A result served from memory is not written to disk. - A stale (expired TTL), partially evicted, corrupt, or inaccessible (another user's non-shared) entry is treated as a cache miss; stale entries are overwritten on the next write. - Introspection of the on-disk entries in `system.query_cache` is out of scope, per the issue. New profile events: `QueryCacheOnDiskHits`, `QueryCacheOnDiskMisses`, `QueryCacheOnDiskReadBytes`, `QueryCacheOnDiskWrittenBytes`. Tests: `05019_query_cache_on_disk_local` proves persistence across process restarts (separate `clickhouse-local` invocations sharing one filesystem cache directory, including a cached non-deterministic result, TTL expiry, and disabled reads); `05020_query_cache_on_disk` covers the server path with user isolation, sharing via `query_cache_share_between_users`, and error cases (unknown cache name, invalid codec). ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The query cache can now store its entries on disk, backed by a preconfigured filesystem cache: this gives the entries more space, makes them survive server restarts, and (with a distributed filesystem cache) provides a way to share them between servers. Select the filesystem cache with the new setting `query_cache_on_disk_cache_name`; see also the new settings `query_cache_on_disk_codec`, `enable_writes_to_query_cache_on_disk`, and `enable_reads_from_query_cache_on_disk`. Closes [#115361](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115361). <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115382&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115382](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115382+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Add the experimental Trino SQL dialect
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added an experimental `trino` value of the `dialect` setting (gated by `allow_experimental_trino_dialect`): queries written in Trino SQL are translated to ClickHouse SQL, including Trino-specific syntax (`ARRAY[...]` literals, `TRY_CAST`, `UNNEST`, `ROW` constructors and types, `VALUES` tables, `OFFSET` before `LIMIT`, `FETCH`) and a mapping of several hundred Trino function names and argument conventions to their ClickHouse equivalents. Since Trino SQL is close to ClickHouse SQL (which already parses `AT TIME ZONE`, `FILTER (WHERE ...)`, `IS DISTINCT FROM`, `DATE`/`TIMESTAMP` literals, `GROUPING SETS`, `NULLS FIRST/LAST`, `WITH RECURSIVE`, ...), the dialect is not a separate grammar. It works in three stages in `src/Parsers/Trino/`: 1. **Token-level syntax translation** (`TrinoSyntaxTranslator`): `ARRAY[1, 2]` -> `[1, 2]`, `TRY_CAST(x AS t)` -> `accurateCastOrNull(x, 't')`, `ROW(...)` -> `tuple(...)` / `Tuple(...)`, `UNNEST` in `FROM` -> `ARRAY JOIN` (`LEFT JOIN UNNEST ... ON TRUE` -> `LEFT ARRAY JOIN`, `WITH ORDINALITY` -> `arrayEnumerate`, maps -> `mapKeys`/`mapValues`), `(VALUES ...)` -> a subquery over `SQLStandardValues`, `OFFSET n LIMIT m` -> `LIMIT m OFFSET n`, `FETCH FIRST n ROWS ONLY/WITH TIES` -> `LIMIT`, `TIMESTAMP(p) [WITH TIME ZONE]` type -> `DateTime64(p)`, lambdas are parenthesized (the ClickHouse parser cannot parse a lambda after a literal argument), and backslashes in string literals are escaped (in Trino a backslash is a regular character). 2. **The standard ClickHouse parser** parses the result. If nothing needed translation, the original buffer is parsed directly, and `INSERT` statements with inline data (`VALUES`/`FORMAT`) are always delegated as-is so that the zero-copy data pointers stay valid. 3. **AST-level function mapping** (`TrinoFunctionMapper`): ~100 renames plus ~50 structural rewriters built from a review of all ~340 functions in the Trino documentation. This includes argument reordering for every higher-order function (Trino passes lambdas last, ClickHouse first: `transform(arr, f)` -> `arrayMap(f, arr)`), parametric-aggregate conversion (`approx_percentile(x, p)` -> `quantileTDigest(p)(x)`, `listagg(x, sep)` -> `groupConcat(sep)(x)`), and — most importantly — the names that resolve in ClickHouse with **different semantics** and would silently return wrong results if passed through: `to_unixtime` (an alias of `parseDateTime` in ClickHouse), `date_diff` (boundary crossings vs complete units -> `age`), `week` (non-ISO mode 0 -> `toISOWeek`), `from_unixtime(u, x)` (format string vs time zone), `rand`/`random` -> `randCanonical`, `transform`, `repeat`, `histogram`, `map(karr, varr)` -> `mapFromArrays`, `format` -> `printf`, and the varchar family (`length`, `substr`, `upper`, `lower`, `strpos`, `lpad`, ...) which is code-point-based in Trino and byte-based in ClickHouse (-> `...UTF8` variants). The feature gate follows the `polyglot` pattern: `SET` queries are handled before the gate inside the parser, so a misconfigured profile can always be recovered with `SET dialect = 'clickhouse'`. ClickHouse functions whose names do not collide with Trino names remain accessible from the dialect. Unsupported constructs (`TABLESAMPLE`, `TRY(...)`, comparator `array_sort`, ...) throw explicit `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`/`BAD_ARGUMENTS` errors instead of misbehaving, and semantics that cannot be fixed by translation at the query level (integer division `/`, `round` banker's rounding on Float, `greatest`/`least` NULL handling) are documented. The translation is observable with `EXPLAIN SYNTAX`. Note: `polyglot_dialect = 'trino'` already exists via the `polyglot` transpiler, but it performs no function mapping and passes `ARRAY[...]` through untranslated; this first-class dialect provides a much more complete translation. `BETWEEN SYMMETRIC` is translated to `BETWEEN least(a, b) AND greatest(a, b)`, and the Trino `JSON` type family is mapped to the ClickHouse `JSON` type, accepting that only objects are supported: `JSON '...'` literals and `json_parse` become casts to `JSON`, `json_format` becomes `toJSONString`, and `json_extract`, `json_extract_scalar`, `json_value`, `json_query`, `json_exists`, `json_size`, `json_array_contains` and `is_json_scalar` are translated to the ClickHouse JSON functions (the string-based JSONPath functions do not accept the `JSON` type, so casts flowing directly into them are unwrapped back to the JSON text; non-object documents are rejected when materialized as `JSON` values). Validation: besides the stateless tests, the translation was run against a corpus of 294 `SELECT`-with-expected-result examples extracted from the official Trino function documentation, and against the 22 TPC-H queries in Trino dialect from `trinodb/trino/testing/trino-benchmark-queries` (all 22 parse and translate). Of the 294 examples, 142 produce results matching the documentation (plus a few that differ only by printing the current time or the session time zone); most of the rest use deliberately unsupported constructs (SQL:2016 `MATCH`/`UNIQUE` predicates, `U&'...'` literals, functions with no ClickHouse counterpart, non-object `JSON` documents per the design above). <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115383&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115383](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115383+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Do not let an alias give `randConstant` a second value in one query
signals.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112938 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `randConstant` returning two different values in one query when its calls carry different aliases. `randConstant` is documented to hold a single value for the whole query, and `SELECT randConstant() = randConstant()` already returned `1`, but adding aliases as in `SELECT randConstant() AS a, randConstant() AS b` produced two unrelated values. ### Description ```sql SELECT randConstant() = randConstant() -- 1 SELECT a = b FROM (SELECT randConstant() AS a, randConstant() AS b) -- 0 <-- wrong ``` `randConstant` is documented to return "a single random value that remains constant across all rows in the current query execution", and its argument is documented as existing only "to prevent common subexpression elimination when the same function call is used multiple times in a query". So two bare calls must agree, and asking for a second value is spelled `randConstant(1), randConstant(2)`. `RandomConstantOverloadResolver::buildImpl` draws a new value on every call, so identical calls have to share one built `FunctionBase` to fold to one constant. `resolveFunction` arranges that with `functions_cache`, keyed by `getTreeHash`. That hash covers the alias, so the two aliased calls missed each other in the cache, each folded to its own literal, and no later common subexpression elimination could bring them back together — by then they were two different literals. With `enable_analyzer = 0` the same query returns `1`, so this is analyzer-only. The key now ignores aliases. An alias renames an expression and never changes the value the `FunctionBase` captures, so aliased calls share what bare calls share. What separates two calls is still their arguments, which the hash covers. The change is narrower than the cache's reach suggests. Only a function folded through its own `FunctionBase` can be split this way; anything evaluated per row, such as `rand` or `generateUUIDv4`, is deduplicated later by ordinary common subexpression elimination, which already ignored aliases — `SELECT rand() AS a, rand() AS b, a = b` reads `1` on `master` today. To bound it rather than argue it, I swept all 57 zero-argument non-deterministic functions, comparing each one aliased and bare, before and after: `randConstant` is the only function whose result changes, from `0` to `1`, and no bare result moves at all. Test `05023` fails on exactly its four aliased rows without the change. Its five controls — the bare comparison, the distinct-argument row (four arguments rather than two, so it cannot flake on a value collision), the across-rows row, and the `now` and `rand` rows — pass either way. Verified by building and running against the branch build: `05023` plus the five existing tests that read `randConstant` (`03611`, `01418`, `00912`, `04327` across shards, `03047` under mutations) all pass. The 382-test `analyzer` family was run on both arms of an exact A/B on the same tree — the one-line change reverted, rebuilt, rerun — and the two arms are identical: 352 pass and the same 18 fail on both, all of them for missing fixtures in my local server rather than for this change. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115384&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115384](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115384+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Command get xdbc type info
signals.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115015 Generic Flight SQL clients rely on `CommandGetXdbcTypeInfo` to discover the data types supported by a server. It is used, for example, by Power BI's built-in ADBC Flight SQL path and by the Flight SQL JDBC driver's `DatabaseMetaData.getTypeInfo()`. Until now the command fell through to the `NotImplemented` catch-all in `commandSelectorImpl`, so those clients could not resolve column types. Adds a handler that builds the ODBC/JDBC type metadata table directly with the schema from `arrow::flight::sql::SqlSchema::GetXdbcTypeInfoSchema()`, so the 19-column result (including nullability) matches exactly what Flight SQL clients expect. The table covers 25 ClickHouse types: `Bool`, `UUID`, `Int8`-`UInt64`, the wide integers `Int128`/`Int256`/`UInt128`/`UInt256`, `Decimal`, `Float32`/`Float64`, `String`/`FixedString`, `Enum8`/`Enum16`, `Date`/`Date32`, and `DateTime`/`DateTime64`. Rows are ordered by `(data_type, type_name)` as the protocol requires, and the optional `data_type` filter is honored; an unknown code returns an empty table with the full schema. The metadata follows the semantics documented in `FlightSql.proto`: - Datetime rows report the generic `XDBC_DATETIME` (9) in `sql_data_type` and the concrete type in `datetime_subcode` (`XDBC_SUBCODE_DATE` = 1, `XDBC_SUBCODE_TIMESTAMP` = 3). - `create_params` is NULL for types without parameters and lists the parameter keywords otherwise (`FixedString` -> `length`, `Decimal` -> `precision,scale`, `DateTime` -> `timezone`, `DateTime64` -> `scale,timezone`). - Exact numeric types report their maximum precision in `column_size` and `num_prec_radix` = 10; approximate numeric types use `num_prec_radix` = 2. The direct-table approach (same pattern as `CommandGetSqlInfo`) was chosen over building the result from SQL because it lets the result schema match `SqlSchema::GetXdbcTypeInfoSchema()` exactly; Flight SQL clients compare the returned schema against that canonical schema. Also includes: - `FlightSQLClient.get_xdbc_type_info()` in the integration test client, with a hand-built protobuf descriptor for `CommandGetXdbcTypeInfo`, and two integration tests covering the unfiltered table, the ordering, the metadata values (`sql_data_type`, `datetime_subcode`, `create_params`, `num_prec_radix`), and the `data_type` filter (including the empty result for an unknown code). - A row in the Arrow Flight SQL documentation listing `CommandGetXdbcTypeInfo` as supported. The two integration scenarios were exercised end-to-end against a locally built server: the unfiltered call returns 25 rows in `(data_type, type_name)` order, and the `data_type` filter returns only the matching rows. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry: Added support for `CommandGetXdbcTypeInfo` in the Arrow Flight SQL server, so generic Flight SQL clients can retrieve ODBC/JDBC type metadata for ClickHouse data types, including the optional `data_type` filter.

signals.title: Sync `BackupImpl` lock-file handling and the Cloud-only resume state
signals.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-private/pull/69709 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-private/pull/69709 This is the public side of the private pull request above, and most of it is that sync. The shared files both touch -- `BackupImpl.h`, `BackupImpl.cpp`, `BackupFactory.h` -- are identical here and there, down to the blank lines, so `Check public build` can overlay the private ones unchanged and later syncs have nothing to reconcile in them. What stays private is where the resume path lives, because nothing outside ClickHouse Cloud resumes a backup. The part that changes this build is the lock-file handling. `createLockFile` creates the lock with `writeFileIfNotExists`, so two backups racing for the same destination cannot both believe they own it. When the create fails it compares what is there against what it would have written: its own contents mean a concurrent backup, a completed `.backup` means the backup already exists, and a lock that has since disappeared rethrows the original failure rather than guessing. `removeLockFile` now reports whether the destination still holds the lock. `checkLockFile(false)` is false both for a foreign lock and for one it could not read, so a caller could not tell "not ours" from "unknown" while the lock was still there; `tryRemoveAllFiles` reports that as a failure rather than claiming the destination is clean. `open` also removes a lock it created when the verification that follows throws. Otherwise the lock outlives the failed attempt and fences the destination against every later one, which cannot match it either: a retry picks a fresh backup UUID, so the orphaned lock belongs to nobody. The rest is state that only ClickHouse Cloud reads. `BackupImpl` is where continuing an interrupted backup is implemented, so what it keeps for one belongs here: whether this attempt is a continuation, the timestamp text the earlier attempt wrote into `.backup`, the ownership check to run before publishing anything, and whether `.backup` is already published. All of it, the two helpers that reconcile an already-published manifest, and every place the shared implementation reads or reports it, are behind `CLICKHOUSE_CLOUD`, so this build behaves as it did: it writes its own timestamp and always publishes metadata. The parameters that fill the state in stay out, along with the code that reads them. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Build/Testing/Packaging Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `BACKUP` now creates the lock file in its destination atomically, and removes it when the attempt that created it fails before writing anything. A failed backup no longer leaves behind a lock that no later backup can match, and concurrent backups writing to one destination are reported as such instead of failing with whatever the storage returned.

signals.title: [ClickHouse-58380] Implement Retries in distributed queries when server stopped during queries
signals.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md): Add settings `distributed_query_retries` and `distributed_query_retry_interval_ms` (disabled by default): when enabled, a query to a `Distributed` table or to the `remote` table function is retried after a network error (`NETWORK_ERROR`, `SOCKET_TIMEOUT`, `ATTEMPT_TO_READ_AFTER_EOF`, e.g. when the remote server is stopped while the query is running). signals.title: Feature: Enable overlay databases for server.
signals.text: Enables server-side `Overlay` databases. An `Overlay` database is a read-only facade that exposes the union of the tables of several underlying databases, resolving each table name through the listed sources in order (the first source that has the table wins). DDL on the facade is rejected — it has no storage of its own — while `SELECT` and pass-through `INSERT` resolve to the underlying source table. Reading or writing through the facade requires the corresponding grant on both the facade database and the underlying source, and the facade's row policies are combined with the source's. Previously an `Overlay` database existed only as the implicit default database of `clickhouse-local`. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/52764 <!--- A technical comment, you are free to remove or leave it as it is when PR is created The following categories are used in the next scripts, update them accordingly utils/changelog/changelog.py tests/ci/cancel_and_rerun_workflow_lambda/app.py --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Allow creating `Overlay` databases. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=86768&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/86768](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F86768+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signals.title: Fix hang in `--queries-file` / `-q` when stdin is a pipe with no data
signals.text: `ClientBase` eagerly called `isStdinNotEmptyAndValid` to check for trailing stdin data on every `INSERT`. That helper calls `!std_in.eof()`, which performs a blocking `read(0, ...)`. When stdin is a pipe that is open but has no data and no `EOF` (common in CI, Docker, stress tests, and `--queries-file` invocations), the read blocks indefinitely and the client hangs until it is killed by timeout. Concretely, this caused an exception (signal 11 after timeout) in the stress test `03538_analyzer_scalar_correlated_subquery_fix`: the process hung on `read(0, ...)` and was killed. The fix replaces the eager blocking probe with a non-blocking one: `poll(timeout=0)` first asks "does stdin appear to have data right now?", and only when it does we fall through to `isStdinNotEmptyAndValid` to confirm and consume it. This: - avoids the hang on open empty pipes — `poll` returns 0 immediately; - preserves deterministic rejection of `inlined data + stdin` mixed input — when stdin actually contains data (the case asserted by `04064_inline_insert_data`), `poll` returns `POLLIN` and we still throw `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`; - is best-effort by design: a slow producer pipe (e.g. `(sleep 1; echo) | clickhouse-client ...`) may not have written by the time `poll` runs, in which case the trailing stdin payload is ignored. This is preferable to the alternative of a hard hang, and is documented in the helper. Covered cases (`is_async_insert_with_inlined_data`, `is_inline_insert_data`, and the appending-stdin path in `sendData`) all go through the same probe so the hang is closed for `--queries-file`, `-q`, and `--inline-insert-data` modes. CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=b9e68f4b9b0b33c7db43b00afb3eff4ff2050694&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_debug%29 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a hang in `clickhouse-client` for `INSERT` queries in `--queries-file`/`-q`/`--inline-insert-data` mode when stdin is an open pipe with no data and no `EOF` (common in CI, Docker, and stress tests). ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=96494&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/96494](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F96494+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

ORDER BY ... LIMIT` and `GROUP BY ... LIMIT` queries by maintaining a bounded heap during aggregation to prune groups that cannot appear in the result, significantly reducing memory usage and execution time for high-cardinality grouping. Controlled by the `enable_group_by_top_k_optimization` setting. Based on the initial implementation by [Dmitriy Terenichev](https://github.com/Dmitry909) ([#78553](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/78553)). Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/72610 Query shapes that benefit from this optimization: - `SELECT key, agg() FROM t GROUP BY key ORDER BY key ASC LIMIT N` -- single key, full ORDER BY match - `SELECT key, agg() FROM t GROUP BY key LIMIT N` -- single key, no ORDER BY - `SELECT k1, k2, agg() FROM t GROUP BY k1, k2 ORDER BY k1, k2 ASC LIMIT N` -- composite keys, full ORDER BY match - `SELECT k1, k2, k3, agg() FROM t GROUP BY k1, k2, k3 ORDER BY k1, k2, k3 ASC LIMIT N` -- 3+ keys, full match - `SELECT k1, k2, agg() FROM t GROUP BY k1, k2 ORDER BY k1 ASC LIMIT N` -- composite keys, ORDER BY is a prefix of GROUP BY - `SELECT k1, k2, k3, agg() FROM t GROUP BY k1, k2, k3 ORDER BY k1 ASC LIMIT N` -- prefix 1 of 3 - `SELECT k1, k2, k3, agg() FROM t GROUP BY k1, k2, k3 ORDER BY k1, k2 ASC LIMIT N` -- prefix 2 of 3 - `SELECT k1, k2, agg() FROM t GROUP BY k1, k2 LIMIT N` -- composite keys, no ORDER BY - `SELECT URL, count() FROM t GROUP BY URL ORDER BY URL ASC LIMIT N` -- String keys - `SELECT URL, count() FROM t GROUP BY URL LIMIT N` -- String keys, no ORDER BY Not supported (optimization is skipped): - `ORDER BY agg()` (ORDER BY aggregate function, not a GROUP BY key) (handled by [another PR](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/98607)) - `WITH TOTALS`, `HAVING`, `GROUPING SETS`, `CUBE`, `ROLLUP` - `LIMIT WITH TIES` - ~~Non-final aggregation (distributed partial aggregation)~~ - `max_rows_to_group_by` is set - `rows_before_limit_at_least` mode (exact count) - a COLLATE on any of the matched GROUP BY keys (a COLLATE on a later ORDER BY column past the full key prefix cannot affect which groups qualify and does not disable the optimization) - ORDER BY columns that are not a leading prefix of GROUP BY keys <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=96630&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/96630](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F96630+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->
