signal.title: Deduplicate the final DISTINCT in parallel
signal.text: The final `DISTINCT` merged all of its input streams into one and deduplicated them on a single thread, so `SELECT DISTINCT` did not scale with `max_threads` while the equivalent `GROUP BY` did - aggregation parallelizes its merge over two-level hash tables, `DISTINCT` had nothing of the sort. This repartitions the input streams by the hash of the `DISTINCT` columns instead of merging them: equal values then land in the same stream, so every stream can be deduplicated on its own, and what is left to merge is already deduplicated. The repartitioning uses `scatterByPartition`, which `SortingStep` and `ShuffleSendStep` already use. Whether the order of the step's output is free to change is only known where the sorting properties are, so the decision is taken in `applyOrder`. The new setting `allow_parallel_distinct`, enabled by default, controls it. It is not applied when: - the input is already globally sorted, because then `DISTINCT` keeps the order of its input and the repartitioning would break it; - there is a `LIMIT`, because the transform stops early anyway and the single stream keeps `LIMIT` returning the first values of the input rather than an arbitrary subset; - the streams are already disjoint - `allow_distinct_partitions_independently` covers that case and skips the merge entirely. `max_rows_in_distinct` and `max_bytes_in_distinct` keep their global meaning: the streams hold disjoint parts of one `DISTINCT` set, so the transforms add up the sizes of their sets in a shared counter and check the limits against the total. Enforcing them in the single final transform instead would have disabled the optimization for everyone who sets them - including all of CI, where the test profile sets both to `10G`. Every input chunk is split across all partitions, so the number of partitions is capped rather than following `max_threads`. On `SELECT DISTINCT number FROM numbers_mt(4e7)` the total CPU time the scatter adds grows by 8% at 4 partitions, 20% at 16 and 96% at 96; without the cap that turned into a wall-clock regression at high `max_threads`. Wall clock, minimum of 3 runs, aarch64: | workload | `max_threads` | before | after | speedup | |---|---|---|---|---| | 20M distinct `UInt64`, `MergeTree` | 4 | 0.442 s | 0.205 s | 2.16x | | | 16 | 0.458 s | 0.148 s | 3.09x | | | 96 | 0.502 s | 0.165 s | 3.04x | | 40M distinct `UInt64`, `numbers_mt` | 4 | 0.965 s | 0.545 s | 1.77x | | | 16 | 0.929 s | 0.360 s | 2.58x | | | 96 | 0.886 s | 0.299 s | 2.96x | | 8M distinct `String`, `numbers_mt` | 4 | 0.515 s | 0.288 s | 1.79x | | | 16 | 0.517 s | 0.093 s | 5.56x | | | 96 | 0.518 s | 0.083 s | 6.24x | The measurements were taken on a busy machine, hence the minimum of several runs; the existing `distinct_in_order`, `distinct_high_cardinality` and `sorted_distinct` performance tests cover these shapes, so the performance comparison job is the authoritative check. `DISTINCT` without `ORDER BY` has no defined row order, and the repartitioning changes the order it happens to produce. Two existing tests relied on it: `04109_sort_propagation_apply_order` asserts that per-stream sortedness reaches `DISTINCT`, so it pins the setting off, and `00585_union_all_subquery_aggregation_column_removal` gets the explicit `ORDER BY` it was missing. Other tests that depend on the incidental order of a `DISTINCT` may surface in CI and should be fixed the same way. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114532 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/48988 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md): Evaluate the final `DISTINCT` on several threads by repartitioning its input by the hash of the `DISTINCT` columns, instead of merging everything into a single stream and deduplicating it on one thread. Up to 6x faster on high-cardinality `DISTINCT`. Controlled by the new setting `allow_parallel_distinct`, enabled by default. Note that this changes the order in which a `DISTINCT` without `ORDER BY` returns rows, which was never defined. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114550&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114550](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114550+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Perf: use compact presence masks for PromQL set operators
signal.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): **Use compact presence masks for PromQL set operators.** ### Summary The PromQL `and`, `or`, and `unless` lowering only needs to know whether a value is present at each step. This targets the general set-operator path. The exact-group fast path is separate. ### Changes - Use `Array(UInt8)` presence masks instead of `Array(UInt64)` counts. - Use `groupBitOrForEach` for the per-step presence reduction. - Share the mask expression between `and`, `or`, and `unless`. - Keep the shared set-operator validation and presence-mask construction in a common lowering helper. - Keep the existing NULL filtering and join behavior. - Cover all three operators in the plan-shape test. - Keep the original 8,000-series baseline workload. - Add a sparse fan-in workload with 1,000 matching groups and four physical replicas per group, with `replica` excluded by `on(instance)`. The compact presence mask is built with: ```sql groupBitOrForEach(arrayMap(x -> isNotNull(x), values)) ``` Because `isNotNull()` produces a `UInt8` 0/1 value, bitwise OR is exactly the presence reduction needed by the set operators. The aggregate state is a zero-initialized `UInt8`, avoiding the generic `max(UInt8)` initialized-state bookkeeping. ### Benchmark The checked-in workload contains two variants, each using 300 query steps: - Baseline: 8,000 series with one series per matching group. - Sparse fan-in: 8,000 series with four replicas per matching group and staggered 50% sample presence. Queries match on `instance` while retaining `replica` in the physical labels. The second variant exercises the actual per-step presence reduction across multiple rows in each `on(...)` group. ### Benchmark result This operator-step microbenchmark runs the old `countForEach(values)` expression and the new `groupBitOrForEach(arrayMap(x -> isNotNull(x), values))` expression over the same workload shapes. - ClickHouse 26.7.3.19 - 200 iterations per case - QPS from `clickhouse-benchmark` - Memory from `system.query_log` | Workload | Before | After | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Baseline | 68.3 QPS, p50 13 ms, 40.0 MiB | 79.6 QPS, p50 11 ms, 30.1 MiB | +16.5% QPS, -24.9% memory | | Sparse fan-in | 119.4 QPS, p50 7 ms, 30.0 MiB | 122.7 QPS, p50 7 ms, 30.0 MiB | +2.8% QPS, no material memory change | ### Tests - Verified that `groupBitOr` is registered for integer inputs and that the `ForEach` combinator accepts array arguments. - Updated the plan-shape checks for `and`, `or`, and `unless` to require `groupBitOrForEach` and reject `countForEach`. - Existing end-to-end set-operator coverage continues to exercise mixed, NULL, and missing-step behavior. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115224&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115224](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115224+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Bound the shutdown wait for cancelled backups and restores
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115105 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): With `shutdown_wait_backups_and_restores = 0`, a `BACKUP` or `RESTORE` whose I/O did not return kept the server from terminating on a single `SIGTERM`, because shutdown waited for it to reach a final status with no timeout. That wait is now bounded by `shutdown_wait_unfinished`, and new backups and restores are refused once shutdown has begun. ### Description Related: #115105 Reported by @ PedroTadim, who [asked me to take it](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115105#issuecomment-5326577830). The issue stays open. **Cause.** Shutdown waits with `status_changed.wait` - no timeout, predicate on the operation status only, so it lasts as long as the operation. `cancelAll` does not help: cancellation is polled per file (`checkTimeLimit()` before `writeFile`), and within a file `BackupImpl` uses the `copyData` overload with no cancellation hook, so a thread parked in a read never sees it. **Change**, all inside the `shutdown_wait_backups_and_restores = 0` branch of `Server.cpp`: refuse new operations, bound the wait at `shutdown_wait_unfinished`, and on non-convergence feed the forced exit that already handles `!joined_refresh_tasks`. That exit is `_exit`, so the unbounded `thread_pools->wait()` in `BackupsWorker::shutdown()` is never reached rather than bounded. `addInfo` refuses after its dedup early-return: `UNFINISHED` for internal operations (retriable in `DDLWorker`), `QUERY_WAS_CANCELLED` otherwise. **Not fixed here.** The default `= 1` branch is untouched, so the hang is still reachable with stock settings: that setting is documented as waiting for backups to *finish*, so capping it changes the guarantee and is your call. Also unchanged: the per-file cancellation granularity, and `BackupsWorker::shutdown()` reached without this guard (failed startup script), where bounding its status waits just moves the block to the pool join. An abandoned backup keeps its `CREATING_BACKUP` row and can leave partial files. **Validation.** The new tests wedge a backup with the existing `backup_pause_on_start` failpoint, which parks the thread upstream of both `checkTimeLimit()` polls, so the operation never sees its own cancellation. The oracle is whether `stop_clickhouse()` escalated to `SIGKILL`, not elapsed time and not a log line (`_exit` discards the async log queue). One arm requires self-exit and fails on master; a second raises the setting to 600 and requires the server to keep waiting, so a hardcoded deadline fails it. 50/50 stable; sibling shutdown and on-cluster cancel tests pass. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115377&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115377](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115377+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Add a `bucketed` schema for `system.metric_log`: a single Map column with Enum keys and 128 buckets
signal.text: Adds a new `schema_type` option `bucketed` for `system.metric_log` (the default `wide` and the `transposed` schemas are unchanged): ```xml <metric_log> <schema_type>bucketed</schema_type> </metric_log> ``` With this schema, all profile events and current metrics are stored in a single `metrics` column of type `Map(Enum16(...), Int64)`, where the `Enum16` value is the global metric index and zero values are not stored (a lookup of a missing key in a `Map` returns `0`). The default table definition uses the bucketed `Map` serialization with a constant number of 128 buckets: ``` SETTINGS map_serialization_version = 'with_buckets', map_serialization_version_for_zero_level_parts = 'basic', max_buckets_in_map = 128, map_buckets_strategy = 'constant', map_buckets_min_avg_size = 0 ``` Parts created by inserts keep the basic serialization to avoid creating many small files on every flush; merged parts are always split into 128 buckets. Every metric is also exposed through an `ALIAS` column, e.g. `ProfileEvent_Query UInt64 ALIAS metrics['ProfileEvent_Query']`, so all queries, dashboards, and tests written for the `wide` schema continue to work. Reading a single metric goes through the `Map` key subcolumn (`metrics.key_ProfileEvent_Query`), which reads only the bucket containing the key: in a local test it reads ~100 times less data than reading the whole map (616 vs 60716 bytes on the same rows). Supporting changes: - `arrayElement` on a `Map` with `Enum` keys now accepts the string name of the enum value (`m['name']`): the index is cast to the key type, so an unknown name throws the `UNKNOWN_ELEMENT_OF_ENUM` exception, while a name that is in the `Enum` but absent from the map returns the default value. This previously threw `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT`. - The rewrite of `m['key']` to a key subcolumn in `FunctionToSubcolumnsPass` now supports `Enum`-keyed maps indexed by the name of the enum value, so both the aliases and ad-hoc queries prune buckets. - System logs can declare additional default engine settings via `getDefaultEngineSettings`, merged with the `settings` from the server configuration when no custom `engine` is specified. - An unknown `metric_log.schema_type` value is now rejected with an error instead of silently disabling the table. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Add a new `bucketed` schema type for `system.metric_log`, which stores all metrics in a single `Map(Enum16(...), Int64)` column using the bucketed `Map` serialization with 128 buckets, plus a per-metric `ALIAS` column for compatibility: the table consists of a few columns instead of thousands, zero values are not stored, and reading a single metric reads only one of the 128 buckets. In addition, a `Map` with `Enum` keys can now be indexed by the string name of the enum value, e.g. `map['name']`. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signal.title: Add leader election for non-replicated MergeTree on shared storage
signal.text: Add leader election for non-replicated MergeTree tables on shared object storage (currently `S3`; `Azure` is implemented but not yet enabled, pending test coverage), enabling active/standby failover without external coordination (no Keeper). Uses conditional writes (`If-Match` / `If-None-Match`) on object storage to maintain a lease file with JSON content `{"version":1,"leader_id":"...","timestamp":...}`. The leader renews its lease periodically; followers monitor and claim leadership when the lease expires. New MergeTree settings: - `leader_election` (Bool, default false) — enable leader election - `leader_election_heartbeat_interval` (Seconds, default 10) — lease renewal interval - `leader_election_session_timeout` (Seconds, default 30) — lease expiry threshold; must be at least 3x the heartbeat interval When not the leader, inserts, merges, mutations, and DDL are blocked; background data processing is skipped. Participating nodes should keep their clocks synchronized (NTP) to within `leader_election_session_timeout`; the conditional-write protocol always prevents split-brain, but excessive clock skew can cause leadership churn. Closes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/91613 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Add `leader_election` setting for non-replicated MergeTree tables on shared object storage, enabling active/standby failover using conditional writes without external coordination. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) Three new MergeTree-level settings are added: - `leader_election` (Bool) — When enabled on a non-replicated MergeTree table stored on an `S3` object storage disk (`Azure` is implemented but rejected at table creation until it has test coverage), multiple ClickHouse instances sharing the same data path will elect a single leader. Only the leader performs writes, merges, and mutations. Followers act as read-only replicas and automatically claim leadership when the current leader's lease expires. - `leader_election_heartbeat_interval` (Seconds, default 10) — How often the leader renews its lease and followers check for an expired lease. - `leader_election_session_timeout` (Seconds, default 30) — How long a lease remains valid without renewal. Must be at least 3x `leader_election_heartbeat_interval`. Example: ```sql CREATE TABLE shared_table (x UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY x SETTINGS leader_election = true, leader_election_heartbeat_interval = 10, leader_election_session_timeout = 30; ``` <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **High Risk** > High risk because it introduces new leader-election coordination and modifies core `MergeTree` write/DDL/drop and catalog cleanup paths; bugs could cause write unavailability or accidental deletion/incorrect visibility on shared storage. > > **Overview** > Adds a **Beta** `leader_election` mode for non-replicated `MergeTree` tables on shared S3/Azure, using a conditional-write lease file to ensure only one instance performs inserts/merges/mutations while followers remain read-only and can take over on failure. > > Introduces new MergeTree settings (`leader_election`, `leader_election_heartbeat_interval`, `leader_election_session_timeout`) with validation, new `MergeTreeLeaderElection*` metrics/events, and follower part-refresh + leader takeover sync to load new parts and advance block counters before enabling writes. > > Hardens destructive operations for shared-storage tables: blocks most `ALTER`/partition-mutation operations and `RENAME` under leader election, gates background processing on leadership, and updates drop/cleanup logic (`dropSkipsDataDirectoryCleanup`, `DatabaseCatalog`/`StorageTableProxy` fail-closed behavior) to avoid recursive deletion or hangs when tables are shared or cannot be materialized. Adds documentation and integration/stateless tests covering failover, metrics, validation, and rejection cases. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 78c1252915ba512bebf94a147932158e1bacecf0. signal.title: Add mutation completion time `finish_time` to `system.mutations`
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/89216 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/105255 Adds a `finish_time` column to `system.mutations` reporting when a mutation was completed; `0` means the mutation is not finished yet or its completion time is unknown. This is a rework of #105255 that avoids any new persistent state: no mutation-file format changes and no new Keeper znodes, so there is no upgrade path, no cleanup changes, and no retry/idempotency concerns. For non-replicated `MergeTree` tables the value is tracked in memory (like `latest_fail_time`) and stamped only when the completion is observed by the event that caused it: the commit of the last mutated part, or the creation of a mutation that has no parts to process. Mutations whose completion moment was not observed (entries loaded at startup, parts removed by `DROP PARTITION`) report `0` instead of a fabricated timestamp. For `ReplicatedMergeTree` tables the value is per-replica and equals the modification time of the replica's `mutation_pointer` znode — the write that marks mutations done on the replica. After the replica state is reloaded (e.g. server restart), the completion time of the mutation the pointer points at is restored from the znode `mtime`; older completed mutations report `0`. A cluster-wide completion time can be obtained with `max(finish_time)` grouped by `mutation_id` across replicas. Note for the CH Inc sync: `SharedMergeTree` constructs `MergeTreeMutationStatus` positionally and will need a follow-up to populate `finish_time`. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added a `finish_time` column to `system.mutations` that records when a mutation was completed. Unfinished mutations and mutations whose completion time is unknown report zero. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113474&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/113474](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F113474+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix data race in shared format init exception rethrow
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a data race (and rare crash) when a parsing/analysis error is reported while reading a file/object storage table. A parse error raised during lazy `KeyCondition` initialization was shared as a single exception object across reader threads, and two threads could concurrently append `(in file/uri ...)` to its message, racing on the exception message string. ### Description The race is in the lazy, `std::call_once`-guarded init of the shared format filter, not in `ParallelParsingInputFormat` (that class has a single reader thread per its header and the `IProcessor` no-parallel-work rule). `FormatFilterInfo::initKeyConditionOnce` builds a `KeyCondition` under `call_once`; if that throws (e.g. `convertFieldToType` failing to parse a `DateTime64` literal, `readDateTimeTextFallback`), the exception is stored in `init_exception` and rethrown to every later reader via `std::rethrow_exception(init_exception)`. `std::rethrow_exception` hands out the SAME managed `DB::Exception` object. Up the stack, `IInputFormat::generate()` mutates it in place in its catch block via `e.addMessage(...)` -> `Poco::Exception::extendedMessage()`, which appends to the exception's `_msg` `std::string`. Two `StorageObjectStorageSource::generate()` readers therefore race on `_msg` (TSan report STID 2427-2c05, allocation stack in `FormatFilterInfo::initKeyConditionOnce`; the same class was seen as a segfault). Fix both `call_once` init sites (`FormatFilterInfo::initKeyConditionOnce` and the symmetric `FormatParserSharedResources::initOnce`): keep the stored `init_exception` an immutable template that is only ever read, and hand each caller - the first thrower and every later rethrower - a private copy via `copyMutableException()`. Both reads of the stored `exception_ptr` happen inside `call_once`, so the copies are race-free. `Common/Exception.h` documents that returning a reference to a mutable `DB::Exception` is unsafe for exactly this reason; @ azat applied the same helper to the Parquet reader in f6025e3. The earlier `ParallelParsingInputFormat` change is reverted - it was not the racing path. CI report (STID 2427-2c05, Stress test (amd_tsan)): https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=108469&sha=aef76155cf7a0af8fe890077cbea2598f0a521d9&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_tsan%29

signal.title: Add early short-circuit evaluation for OR/AND in the analyzer to prevent unnecessary scalar subquery execution
signal.text: <!--- Disable AI PR formatting assistant: true --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): You can now enable early short-circuit folding for builtin `and` and `or` during analysis with the `enable_function_early_short_circuit` setting. This can skip executing dead single-row `count()` scalar subqueries while preserving normal type inference and semantic validation. Resolves #83017 ### Details When `enable_function_early_short_circuit` is enabled (and `short_circuit_function_evaluation` is not disabled), the analyzer detects decisive constants in builtin `and` / `or` expressions. The optimization is deliberately conservative. It is attempted only for expressions without outer-scope Identifier/Column dependencies and only for scalar subqueries of the statically single-row forms `SELECT count()` or `SELECT count(*)` without GROUP BY/window/HAVING/QUALIFY/LIMIT BY. All other scalar forms use normal analysis and execution. A dedicated temporary `QueryAnalyzer` resolves a clone in type-only mode using an isolated, cache-disabled scope. It never mutates the live resolver state. Scalar values are represented by non-constant type placeholders, and expressions containing aggregate/`arrayJoin` semantic carriers outside scalar-subquery boundaries are not replaced. signal.title: Fix build flag with new detection mode.
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107399 --> Fixes a build failure on AArch64 CPUs that are advertised as ARMv8.2-A but lack an optional feature of ClickHouse's "modern" ARM profile — for example the HiSilicon Kunpeng 920, which has no `rcpc` and faults with `SIGILL` on the `ldapr` instruction. Such CPUs must be built with `-DNO_ARMV81_OR_HIGHER=1`, but that profile previously failed to compile the Rust components. Root cause: the compatibility profile passed `target_feature=+crc,-neon` to Rust. NEON (Advanced SIMD) is part of the AArch64 baseline and is enabled by default for the `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` target. The `ring` crate (pulled in by `chdig` and `delta-kernel-rs`) statically asserts that NEON is available on little-endian aarch64 and fails to compile when it is disabled. Dropping the `-neon` lets the compatibility profile build `ring`, so `chdig` and `delta-kernel-rs` no longer need to be force-disabled under `NO_ARMV81_OR_HIGHER`. An earlier revision of this pull request auto-detected CPU features from `/proc/cpuinfo` at build time. That approach was reverted following review: ClickHouse always builds for an explicitly specified target platform and must not depend on the host machine (one can build on a coffee machine while targeting an AVX-512 server and vice versa). The pre-existing build-time `/proc/cpuinfo` "best-effort" guard on the AArch64 path is removed for the same reason. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107399 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Build/Testing/Packaging Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed building with `-DNO_ARMV81_OR_HIGHER=1` on AArch64: the compatibility profile no longer disables NEON for Rust, so `ring`-based components (`chdig`, `delta-kernel-rs`) compile and stay enabled. This unblocks building for ARMv8.2-A CPUs that lack `rcpc` (e.g. HiSilicon Kunpeng 920). ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features)

signal.title: Support ROLLUP, CUBE, GROUPING SETS and grouping() with make_distributed_plan
signal.text: Support `ROLLUP`, `CUBE`, `GROUPING SETS` and the `grouping` function under `make_distributed_plan`. 11 of the 99 TPC-DS queries use `ROLLUP`. - `RollupStep` and `CubeStep` are serialized (query plan serialization version 8), so they can run in a worker stage, for example below a distributed `ORDER BY`. - The `grouping` function specializations held their parameters inside the function object and could not be serialized. The new analyzer now appends them as trailing constant arguments when it resolves `grouping`, and registered `__groupingFor*` resolvers rebuild the function from them, so a serialized plan carries the function by name and arguments alone. The old analyzer keeps constructing the functions directly; such plans are not serialized. - `GROUPING SETS` aggregation uses the partial-aggregation split, the same one the shard-based distributed path uses. `WITH TOTALS` and extremes remain unsupported. The distributed results of all new stateless tests are verified against non-distributed execution of the same queries. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Support `ROLLUP`, `CUBE`, `GROUPING SETS` and the `grouping` function in queries executed with `make_distributed_plan = 1`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114950&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114950](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114950+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix `bloom_filter` index skipping granules for a `FixedString` constant
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112693 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes `hasAny`, `hasAll`, `has`, `indexOf`, `mapContainsKey`, `mapContainsValue` and `mapContains` returning too few rows, or failing with `TOO_LARGE_STRING_SIZE`, when a `bloom_filter` index is queried with a `FixedString` constant. The index hashed the padded form of the constant while the function compares the unpadded one, so a matching granule was skipped. ### Description A `bloom_filter` skip index silently returns too few rows when the constant is a `FixedString`, and in four cases raises `TOO_LARGE_STRING_SIZE` on a query that succeeds without the index: ```sql CREATE TABLE k (id UInt64, v Array(String), INDEX idx v TYPE bloom_filter GRANULARITY 1) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id SETTINGS index_granularity = 1; INSERT INTO k VALUES (0,['V0']),(1,['V0\0']),(2,['X']); SELECT count() FROM k WHERE hasAny(v, [toFixedString('V0',3)]); -- 0, wrong SELECT count() FROM k WHERE hasAny(v, [toFixedString('V0',3)]) SETTINGS use_skip_indexes=0; -- 1 ``` Root cause: the array-search functions coerce the constant with CAST before comparing it to the elements (`hasAny`/`hasAll`, and `has`/`indexOf` over a `FixedString` element, cast both sides to the least supertype; `has`/`indexOf` over a `LowCardinality` element cast the constant straight to the dictionary type), and a CAST of `FixedString` to `String` strips the trailing zero padding. The index instead converted the constant with `convertFieldToType`, which keeps the padding, so it hashed a value the function never compares and pruned granules that match. The error cases are the same cause: an oversized `Field` passed through unchanged and reached a column `insert` during index analysis. The fix replicates the coercion at the `Field` level, which is exact because the string casts involved are fully predictable: strip the padding of a `FixedString` constant, re-pad it to the width of the element type (the stored form of every element the function can match), and decline the index when the constant has no stored representation, so a runtime `TOO_LARGE_STRING_SIZE` stays reachable instead of becoming a silent empty result. The direct cast to a dictionary type rejects an over-wide `FixedString` constant before stripping, while the supertype cast strips first - that one ordering difference is the only divergence between the two coercions, so it is a `bool` rather than a second code path. `has`/`indexOf` over a plain `String` element compare the constant's raw padded bytes (`executeString`) and keep the old conversion, as does `has(<constant array>, <indexed scalar>)`, whose runtime compares `Field`s directly. #### `Map` predicates `mapContainsKey`, `mapContainsValue`, `mapContains` and `has` over a `Map` are adapters of the same `arrayIndex.h` machinery, so a `bloom_filter` index on `mapKeys`/`mapValues` needs the same coercion - and it needs to pick the mode from the `Map` type rather than from the index header, because the `mapKeys`/`mapValues` index expression strips `LowCardinality` from the key/value type while the `mapContains*` adapters run over the keys/values subcolumn, which keeps it. Reading the mode from the stripped header alone would still prune a matching granule on `Map(LowCardinality(String), ...)`, which is broken on `master` today independently of the constant's width. `has` over a `Map` is the one exception, and it goes the other way: `FunctionArrayIndex::executeMap` rewrites the map to an array of its keys and calls `recursiveRemoveLowCardinality` on both arguments before `executeArrayImpl`, so it compares the raw padded bytes exactly like `has` over an `Array(String)`, unlike `mapContainsKey` on the same column. Its element type is therefore stripped of `LowCardinality` before the mode is read. The direct array spellings `has(mapKeys(m), ...)` / `indexOf(mapValues(m), ...)` need no special handling: `mapKeys`/`mapValues` return a full `Array` with `LowCardinality` stripped from the type, so the index header type is already the type the runtime compares against. This supersedes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112693 with a smaller implementation of the same semantics (one `Field`-level helper instead of a two-mode column-cast round-trip through `getLeastSupertype` plus a batched clone of `createColumnFromConstantArray`). The array test - 115 assertions over the full element-type/function/constant-width matrix, including granule-pruning and `TOO_LARGE_STRING_SIZE` reachability assertions - is taken unchanged from that pull request and passes byte-identically, so the two implementations are behaviorally equivalent on the covered surface. Three further tests cover the `Map` predicates, the direct `mapKeys`/`mapValues` array spellings, and `has` over a `Map` with `LowCardinality` keys; each compares the indexed answer against an unindexed oracle. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114089&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114089](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114089+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1677` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: Fix flaky 04005_correlated_column_in_lambda by pinning row order
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114550 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `04005_correlated_column_in_lambda` fails `Fast test` with `result differs with reference`. The last query has no `ORDER BY`: ```sql SELECT (SELECT arrayMap(x -> c0 * x, [1, 2])) FROM (SELECT number AS c0 FROM numbers(3)); ``` Its correlated scalar subquery is decorrelated into a JOIN, and the resulting pipeline is multi-stream (`EXPLAIN PIPELINE` shows the expression chain repeated once per stream, resized down to one), so row order depends on which stream finishes first. The test never pinned it. The failure is a pure permutation, never a value change. From the report below: ``` [1] [11,12,13] -[0,0] -[1,2] [2,4] +[1,2] +[0,0] ``` Two *different* permutations occurred on the same commit `9cf364a8`, which rules out a deterministic result change. I reproduced it on a build of pristine master carrying none of #114550: under `max_block_size = 1` an interleaved 200-run A/B on one binary gave 4 distinct permutations (20.5% deviation) without the fix and 200/200 identical output with it. Fix: append `ORDER BY c0` to that one query. `c0` is unique across the three rows, so the order is total. The `.reference` file is unchanged, because the pinned order is the order it already records. This test guards #98285 (PLACEHOLDER nodes for correlated columns in lambdas, closes #85460), so I verified the `ORDER BY` does not hide that regression: with `visitCorrelatedColumn` reverted to its pre-#98285 form the fixed test still aborts and produces no output; restoring it makes the test pass again. Validation: 50/50 runs with randomization, 50/50 with `--no-random-settings` (the `Fast test` shape), 25/25 via `clickhouse-test`. Control arm: the unfixed query under the same conditions fails 9 of 60 runs. Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114550&sha=b5b2d025522dbb54b351249c588220b7311221c3&name_0=PR&name_1=Fast%20test No related open issue found. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115324&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115324](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115324+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix silently dropped quota intervals when the separating comma is missing
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115282 (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `CREATE QUOTA` and `ALTER QUOTA` silently discarding all but the last `FOR INTERVAL` block when the separating comma between intervals was omitted. Such a statement succeeded while installing none of the earlier limits. The intervals now accumulate again, as they did before 2020. Closes #115282. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115282 `CREATE QUOTA q FOR INTERVAL 1 MINUTE MAX queries = 1 FOR INTERVAL 1 HOUR MAX queries = 100 TO u` succeeded and created a quota holding only the `1 hour` limit. The `1 minute` rate limit the operator wrote, and got no error for, was never installed and never enforced; only `SHOW CREATE QUOTA` revealed the loss. Root cause: in `ParserCreateQuotaQuery.cpp`, `parseIntervalsWithLimits` parses a comma-separated list into a local vector and then *assigned* it over the caller's vector. Its call site in the option loop is deliberately unguarded, so a comma-less continuation makes the loop match a second time and the assignment discards everything parsed earlier. That assignment is a regression from `6146766` (2020-06-06), which replaced an append with an assign while leaving the loop unguarded. The comma-less spelling parsed correctly before it. I restored the append via `insertAtEnd`, which is what the sibling `ParserCreateRowPolicyQuery` already does for the same situation. This covers `CREATE`, `ALTER` and `ATTACH QUOTA`, which share `parseImpl`. Nothing that parses today changes: `insertAtEnd` onto an empty vector is the previous behaviour, so the single-block and comma-separated forms are byte-identical before and after. Only inputs that silently lost data now keep it, so this is not a backward incompatible change. Persisted and replicated definitions are unaffected because the formatter always emits the separating comma. Validation: new stateless test `04926_quota_interval_missing_comma` asserts every affected block kind (`MAX`, `TRACKING ONLY`, `NO LIMITS`, `RANDOMIZED`), two and three intervals, an interleaved `KEYED BY`, duplicate durations and `ALTER`, plus the comma form as an unchanged control and the two existing rejection boundaries. Its fix-proving assertions all fail on unpatched master; 50/50 randomized runs pass. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115320&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115320](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115320+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1679` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: Convert OUTER join to INNER join by null-rejecting join conditions
signal.text: Closes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112456 Outer join to inner join conversion works by looking if a filter above the join rejects default values, NULLs in the case of nullable columns. This change allows join conditions of enclosing joins to be used for rejecting NULLs too: 1. optimizer pass `deriveNotNullFiltersFromJoin` derives `col IS NOT NULL` filters from join conditions over bare columns and adds them to the plan. 2. these filters get pushed down and used for the conversion as usual. 3. optimizer pass `resolvePlannerOnlyFilters` either promote or removes planner derived filters to executable filters based on their estimated selectivity. #### Performance result: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Convert `OUTER JOIN` to `INNER JOIN` when a later JOIN filters out its NULL-extended rows, and filter NULL join keys directly at the table scan when column statistics show it is selective. Only join clauses over bare columns are taken into account (col1 `` col2, where `` is one of `=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`). Controlled by the new settings `query_plan_convert_outer_join_to_inner_join_by_join_predicates`, `query_plan_promote_planner_only_not_null_filters` and `query_plan_max_selectivity_for_promoting_not_null_filters` (all enabled by default). --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114817&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114817](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114817+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)]

signal.title: Support the Vortex file format
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/87327 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/rust_vendor/pull/74 ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added support for reading and writing the [Vortex](https://github.com/vortex-data/vortex) columnar file format (the `Vortex` input and output format). This closes [#87327](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/87327). ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes The implementation uses the Rust `vortex` crate (v0.83.0) through a new C FFI crate `rust/workspace/vortex` (`_ch_rust_vortex`), following the same pattern as `prql` and `polyglot`. Data crosses the FFI boundary through the Arrow C Data Interface and is converted with the same `ArrowColumnToCHColumn`/`CHColumnToArrowColumn` code as the `Arrow` format. IO is delegated back to ClickHouse through callbacks: reads go through ClickHouse's own read buffers (range reads for seekable inputs, whole-file buffering otherwise), and the produced file is streamed into the output buffer. All work is driven by a single-threaded runtime on the calling thread — the library spawns no threads, and Rust panics are caught at the FFI boundary and turned into exceptions. Features: - Reading with projection pushdown: only the columns used by the query are read from the file. - Schema inference and `count()`-only queries answered from file metadata without reading data. - Writing with the library's default adaptive compression (BtrBlocks-style cascading encodings + zstd), including a valid empty file for empty results. - Graceful errors on malformed and truncated files (fuzzer-friendly: no aborts, Rust panics become exceptions). Limitations (documented in `docs/reference/formats/Vortex.mdx`): - `Map`, `Int128`/`UInt128`/`Int256`/`UInt256`, `IPv6`, and `Interval` columns cannot be written (no corresponding Vortex type). - `String` and `FixedString` are written as Vortex `Binary` (ClickHouse strings are arbitrary bytes, while Vortex requires `Utf8` to be valid UTF-8). - The format is disabled in MSan builds: the MSan-instrumented library (with origin tracking) is so large that linking `unit_tests_dbms` overflows the 2 GiB `R_X86_64_PC32` relocation range (same approach as `wasmtime` and `delta-kernel-rs`). - Reading and writing are single-threaded in this first version: the whole scan (I/O, decompression, and decoding) runs on one thread, so on ClickBench reads are significantly slower than `Parquet`, which ClickHouse decodes with multiple threads (see the [benchmark results](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112950#issuecomment-5274283519) and [the explanation](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112950#issuecomment-5274483899)). Filter pushdown (added in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114373, `input_format_vortex_filter_push_down`, on by default) reduces the amount of data decoded by selective queries, but does not parallelize the scan. Writes are also slower than `Parquet` (the adaptive compressor samples many encodings per column) — parallelism can be added later. The 127 new vendored Rust crates are added in https://github.com/ClickHouse/rust_vendor/pull/74 (the `contrib/rust_vendor` submodule is bumped to that branch). <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112950&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/112950](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F112950+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Do not build statistics for non-physical columns
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114791 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes `NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK` on every `INSERT` into a table that declares `STATISTICS(...)` on an `ALIAS` or `EPHEMERAL` column, which made such tables read-only. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114791 `CREATE TABLE t (a UInt64, b UInt64 ALIAS a + 1 STATISTICS(basic)) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY a` is accepted, and then every `INSERT` fails `Code: 10 ... Not found column b in block`, so the table is read-only. `materialize_statistics_on_insert` defaulting to `true` in 26.8 exposed it. **Root cause.** The `ColumnsStatistics` constructor collects every column with a non-empty statistics description without checking how the column is stored, and the insert path builds those with `build`, which does `block.getByName`. An `ALIAS` column is computed on read and never appears in the written block, so the lookup always throws. Merges use `buildIfExists` and skip absent columns, which is why they kept working. Such statistics are already unsupported in `addImplicitStatistics` and `ALTER ... ADD STATISTICS`. **The change.** Drop non-physical columns from the collector the insert path builds, in `MergeTreeDataWriter`, using the existing `ColumnsDescription::hasPhysical`. `build` stays strict, because its type-mismatch check is a deliberate diagnostic, so an absence for any other reason is still an error. A newly issued `MATERIALIZE STATISTICS <col>` naming such a column is still rejected before enqueue. An already queued one instead skips it, so a command persisted by a pre-upgrade server drains rather than retrying forever in the background task. `ALL` skips such a column and stays usable. **Deliberately unchanged.** The declaration stays accepted but inert: every candidate rejection site is also the ATTACH/startup or replica-addition path, so a check there would stop existing affected tables from loading. `DROP STATISTICS` stays permissive and recovers such a table. Covered by `02864_statistics_ddl`, which fails on master with `Code: 10` and passes with the fix. The queued-mutation drain under the old mutation analyzer is not covered by a test: it needs the server-level `use_analyzer_for_mutations` override, which a stateless test cannot set.

signal.title: Remove the redundant cross-thread cancel of the Keeper leader-metrics timer
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113334 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `KeeperServer::stopLeaderMetricsPolling()` cancelled the leader-metrics timer from the main thread at shutdown, while a NuRaft asio worker re-armed the same `asio::steady_timer` from `collectLeaderMetrics()`. Both touch `deadline_timer_service::implementation_type::might_have_pending_waits` outside `leader_unavailable_metrics_mutex`, so nothing orders them. `basic_waitable_timer` is documented `Shared objects: Unsafe`, so the defect is at these two call sites, not in NuRaft or boost. TSan reports it on any amd_tsan job tearing a Keeper-enabled server down, attaching to whichever test is shutting the cluster down, hence three test names: - [amd_tsan integration 5/6](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109368&sha=51444071bc4587932301117674fde5f44a6f2f84&name_0=PR&name_1=Integration%20tests%20%28amd_tsan%2C%205%2F6%29), `test_keeper_max_request_size` - [amd_tsan stateless flaky check](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=101841&sha=b493a5015808fdf65e1592623e56165c0bb1d44b&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_tsan%2C%20flaky%20check%29) - [amd_tsan integration 1/6](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115039&sha=a9798769f07c415c69b43a74a2547ce96291fb15&name_0=PR&name_1=Integration%20tests%20%28amd_tsan%2C%201%2F6%29), `test_keeper_opentelemetry_tracing` I delete the cancel rather than add synchronization, because `f473bc8825cfb3b` deliberately hoisted `schedule()` out of that mutex under the subject "deadlock hazard". The cancel is also redundant: resetting the optional under the mutex is already a complete stop signal, since `collectLeaderMetrics()` re-checks it as the first statement inside its own lock before re-arming, so a late callback schedules nothing and the poll chain ends on its own. `asio_service->stop()` then joins the workers. One writer remains, no lock held across a boost call. Validated on a TSan build, since the defect is invisible in debug and release. A gdb breakpoint on `nuraft::asio_service::cancel_impl` reaches it via `stopLeaderMetricsPolling` on the main thread in 3 of 3 runs before the change and 0 of 3 after, with a positive control confirming the shutdown path ran in all six. I did not observe the TSan report itself locally, expected at three hits in 45 days. `test_keeper_max_request_size` passed 144/144 over 12 repeats; `test_keeper_back_to_back` and `test_keeper_four_word_command` passed with no `Failed to shutdown RAFT server` warning, the signal that the drain still bounds a pending expiry. Introduced by #113334 and master-only, so there is nothing to backport. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115305&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115305](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115305+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Web terminal: do not connect before the host page supplies the credentials
signal.text: A `/webterminal` page embedded in a host page - `play.html`, or the ClickHouse Cloud console - is loaded without credentials in its URL and receives them from the host page over `postMessage`, on the iframe's `load` event. It nevertheless opened a connection of its own at startup, before that message could arrive, so every embedded terminal authenticated twice: first with an empty password, which can only succeed for a passwordless user, and then, a moment later, with the credentials from the host page, after the first WebSocket had been closed and replaced. The visible symptom is `Connecting...` printed twice - `attemptConnect` announces every attempt, and whether the first line is erased before the second is printed depends on timing. Behind it are a wasted WebSocket, a guaranteed-failing authentication, and, for a passwordless user, an established session that gets torn down right away. The page now waits for the credentials instead of connecting on its own. A host page that never sends them - it does not implement the protocol, or its origin is not trusted - would leave a terminal that neither connects nor prompts, so the page says that it is waiting and Enter hands the login over to the interactive prompt; credentials arriving after that no longer hijack what the user is typing. The pages opened as a normal tab, or with a `user` URL parameter, keep connecting immediately. The wait became a state of the page's own state machine, which makes the `waitingForCredentials` and `initialAutoAuth` flags, and the `ws.onclose` branch they served, unnecessary. The new `tests/integration/test_webterminal_startup` follows the existing `test_play_reconcile_startup`: it fetches `/webterminal` from a real server and runs the page's real script in a Node `vm` with a stubbed terminal and `WebSocket`, then drives each flow and asserts which connections were opened and what was displayed. Against this branch all 34 checks pass; against `master` 23 fail, including `announces the attempt exactly once -- actual: 2`. It also pins the paths that must keep connecting immediately, the prompt after a rejected password, and that credentials from an untrusted origin, from a trusted host over plain HTTP, or from a window that is not the parent are ignored - the wait is now the only way into an embedded session, so a hole in either check would hand the terminal to a foreign page. Reported by a user of clickhouse.new, where the console drives the terminal through exactly this embedded flow. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/105191 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115067 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): A web terminal embedded in another page, such as the SQL console or `play.html`, receives its credentials from that page and no longer opens a connection of its own before they arrive. Previously it connected twice - once with an empty password, then again with the real credentials - and printed `Connecting...` twice. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115148&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115148](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115148+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Perf: Optimize PromQL and for exact groups
signal.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): PromQL `and` expressions with an exact group key skip redundant matching stages. ## What changed - add a fast path for the PromQL set operator `and` - use it when both inputs already match on the original `group` column - join the unique left and right `VECTOR_GRID` inputs directly - keep the left-hand values and filter them by right-side sample presence - keep `on(...)`, non-empty `ignoring(...)`, `on()`, and other transformed matching keys on the existing general path - add exact-output coverage for grouped `and` expressions - cover empty `ignoring()` when both inputs already have exact groups - add a performance fixture with an exact-group query and an `and on(instance)` control ## Why this is safe `VECTOR_GRID` guarantees one row per `group`. The fast path is enabled only when the matching rules leave the original `group` column unchanged on both sides, so the join key is already unique and exact. The exact-group path removes the right-side per-group count aggregation and the transformed-key join. It returns the left value only when the corresponding right value is present, which is the existing `and` masking behavior. `on(...)`, non-empty `ignoring(...)`, and other cases that transform the matching key keep the current general lowering. Empty `ignoring()` is treated like default matching when both inputs already have exact groups. ## Benchmark Ran `tests/performance/promql_set_operators_and.xml` on Apple Silicon with the Release build from this PR. - 8,000 series - 4,000 matching groups - 300 samples per series - 7 measured runs per query on each of two local server instances The table shows the average of the two per-server medians. Both queries are equivalent for this fixture. The default query uses the new exact-group fast path. The `and on(instance)` query keeps the existing generic implementation. | Query | Median | | --- | ---: | | exact-group `and` | 130.2 ms | | equivalent `and on(instance)` query | 139.8 ms | The exact-group query took 130.2 ms versus 139.8 ms for the existing implementation, which is 6.9% faster in this test. ## Tests - add grouped exact-output coverage for `and` - add exact-output coverage for empty `ignoring()` - keep the existing ungrouped and transformed-key `and` coverage - compile the changed translation unit with the ClickHouse warning set and `-Werror` Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115219

signal.title: Log tolerated connection failures to remote MySQL/PostgreSQL databases as warnings instead of errors
signal.text: Fix CI upgrade test failure: Example failing report — Upgrade check (amd_release) on the unrelated PR https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108255: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=108255&sha=28ca539bd4bf66de37e388238de45d840bc30c52&name_0=PR&name_1=Upgrade%20check%20%28amd_release%29 (`Error message in clickhouse-server.log (see upgrade_error_messages.txt)` with the `getTablesIterator` line above; the report shows green now because the check passed on a later rerun — which is exactly the flaky-victim pattern). **Problem.** A `DatabasePostgreSQL` or `DatabaseMySQL` pointed at an unreachable server writes the connection failure to the server log at `<Error>` level on code paths that explicitly tolerate and retry the failure. A temporarily unavailable remote server is a normal operational state on these paths, yet it floods the log with error-level messages. Concretely: - every `system.tables` / `system.columns` scan that touches the database logs an error (`DatabasePostgreSQL::getTablesIterator`: `Code: 614. DB::Exception: ... Connection to ... failed`); - the background cleaner logs one more error every rescheduling cycle; - `ATTACH DATABASE ... ENGINE = MySQL(...)` logs three error lines for a single tolerated probe failure. This also trips the Upgrade check (which fails on any unexpected error message in `clickhouse-server.log`) on unrelated PRs: the stateless test `04210_show_remote_databases_in_system_tables` (added in #104416) leaves `PostgreSQL`/`MySQL` databases pointed at the unroutable `192.0.2.1` during the check's restart window, and since #109082 made remote databases visible to `system.tables` scans by default, the check failed on 137 distinct PRs in 14 days, and 0 times on master. **Root cause.** Seven log sites report a caught-and-tolerated (or caught-and-propagated) connection failure at error level: the catches in `DatabasePostgreSQL::getTablesIterator` (kept non-throwing so `system.tables` scans do not fail) and `DatabasePostgreSQL::removeOutdatedTables` (the cleaner reschedules and continues) use `tryLogCurrentException` with the default `LogsLevel::error`; the same for the `DatabaseMySQL` constructor catch on `ATTACH` and `DatabaseMySQL::getCreateTableQueryImpl` with `throw_on_error = false`; and the connection-pool layers (`mysqlxx::Pool::allocConnection`, `mysqlxx::PoolWithFailover::get`, `postgres::PoolWithFailover::get`) log at error level before propagating the exception to the caller — who is the one deciding how severe the failure actually is. **Fix.** Downgrade those seven sites to warning. Exception propagation is unchanged everywhere: a non-tolerated failure (e.g. `CREATE DATABASE` with an unreachable host) still reaches the client as an error through the normal query-error path. The new test `04506_remote_database_unreachable_no_error_log` attaches `PostgreSQL` and `MySQL` databases pointing at an unreachable host, exercises the tolerated paths (attach probe, `system.tables` scan, background cleaner), and asserts through `system.text_log` that each path produced a warning (proving the failure path fired) and no error-level lines at all for the corresponding queries. ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109472&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/109472](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F109472+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Let the promql dialect keep tokens the SQL lexer rejects
signal.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed PromQL queries with regex label matchers (`=~`, `!~`) being rejected under `--dialect promql`. Closes #115071. --- Under `--dialect promql`, `ParserPrometheusQuery` reads the raw query text and hands it to the PromQL grammar; it walks the SQL tokens only to find where the statement ends. But `tryParseQuery` scans those tokens for lexer errors *before* the parser runs, and `~` is not a SQL token, so the query was rejected before it ever reached the PromQL grammar: ``` $ clickhouse local --dialect promql -q 'up{instance="host1"}' Code: 471. ... The name of a TimeSeries table to use with promql dialect is not specified $ clickhouse local --dialect promql -q 'up{instance=~"host2|host3"}' Code: 62. ... Unrecognized token: Syntax error: failed at position 13 (~) ``` The equality matcher gets through to a missing-setting error; the regex matcher dies at the `~` with a **SQL** lexical error. It is not specific to `-q` — stdin and `--queries-file` fail identically. The grammar itself already has the tokens (`PromQLLexer.g4`: `RE : '=~'`, `NRE : '!~'`), and the same expression works when passed as a string to the table function, which is what makes the limitation easy to miss. `IParser` gains `consumesRawText()`, false by default and overridden by `ParserPrometheusQuery`. `tryParseQuery` skips its two lexical-error rejections for such parsers, since a token the SQL lexer does not recognise is not an error for a parser that reads the text itself. No call site changes, and any future dialect parser in the same position gets the behaviour by overriding one method. This is safe because the lexer does not stop at an unrecognised character — it consumes it and returns an `Error` token (`Lexer.cpp:546`), so statement-boundary detection still finds the terminating semicolon. Kusto solves the same problem with an entire parallel `parseKQLQuery.{h,cpp}`; PromQL needs only the boundary scan, so a virtual on `IParser` seemed proportionate. Happy to go the separate-entry-point route instead if maintainers prefer the consistency. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115073&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115073](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115073+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Report cancellation instead of leaving an in-place set unbuilt
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114463 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107619 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `Not-ready Set is passed as the second argument for function 'in'` error when a query with `partial_result_on_first_cancel = 1` was cancelled while the set of an `IN (subquery)` was still being built. ### Description Follow-up to https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114463, asked for in its review. That pull request makes a cancelled mutation report `ABORTED` instead of stopping its nested pipelines silently; the review asked whether the same silent stop is still reachable through the other two interactive-cancel callbacks. I measured both. One is, one is not. **Reachable: `partial_result_on_first_cancel`.** For the first cancel, `TCPHandler::processCancel` only sets `stop_read_return_partial_result` and deliberately does not cancel the query through the process list, so the callback returns a bare `true` (`TCPHandler.cpp:897-898`). `CompletedPipelineExecutor::execute` then cancels the nested set-build pipeline and its poll loop returns normally, so `CreatingSetsTransform::generate` never runs `Set::finishInsert`, while `FutureSetFromSubquery::build` has already moved the source plan out. A caller that evaluates its filter in the same call passes the unbuilt set to `FunctionIn`. On master (`f45871c7cfa`), one cancel during ```sql SELECT count() FROM t WHERE 1 IN (SELECT number FROM numbers(10000000) WHERE sleep(1) = 0) SETTINGS partial_result_on_first_cancel = 1, optimize_use_implicit_projections = 1, optimize_trivial_count_query = 0 ``` reports ``` Code: 49. DB::Exception: Not-ready Set is passed as the second argument for function 'in' ... (LOGICAL_ERROR) ``` through `FunctionIn` (`in.cpp:116`) <- `VirtualColumnUtils::filterBlockWithExpression` (`:162`) <- `MergeTreeData::getMinMaxCountProjectionBlock` (`:10463`) <- `optimizeUseAggregateProjections` (`:630`). A debug or sanitizer build aborts on it. **Not reachable: `clickhouse-local`.** Its callback cancels the query through the process list element (`LocalConnection.cpp:191-194`), so the nested pipeline fails instead of stopping silently. The same query interrupted with `SIGINT` reports `Code: 394. DB::Exception: Query was cancelled` on master, with `EXPLAIN indexes = 1` confirming the plan is the `minmax_count` projection. That installer is untouched here. `FutureSetFromSubquery::buildSetInplace` now records whether the cancel callback fired and, if the set was left uncreated, reports `QUERY_WAS_CANCELLED` instead of returning to a caller that cannot distinguish a cancelled build from a completed one. Both conditions are required on purpose, so a set build that stops for a reason other than a cancellation keeps the behaviour it has today. Measured over the routes that stop such a pipeline early: `set_overflow_mode = 'break'`, `transfer_overflow_mode = 'break'` and `read_overflow_mode = 'break'` all still reach `CreatingSetsTransform::generate`, which finishes the set, and the query returns its result; `set_overflow_mode = 'throw'` still reports `SET_SIZE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`. For `partial_result_on_first_cancel` this means such a query now fails with `QUERY_WAS_CANCELLED` rather than with the logical error. There is no partial answer to return instead: the cancellation lands during analysis, before a row is produced, and an incomplete `IN` set would silently change the result. The mutation path keeps reporting `ABORTED` as #114463 makes it: its callback throws before this check is reached, which names the mutation the way `MergeTask::checkOperationIsNotCanceled` does and covers every nested pipeline a mutation runs, not only `buildSetInplace`. The ordered variant `buildOrderedSetInplace` needs nothing: #107924 made it build against a clone of the source plan and publish only a created set, so a silently stopped ordered build just skips index analysis. Out of scope, found while measuring this and reported here rather than fixed: a *time limit* with `break` reaches the same logical error without any cancellation, because the limit stops the set-build pipeline the same way. On master, ```sql SELECT count() FROM t WHERE 1 IN (SELECT number FROM numbers(1000)) SETTINGS optimize_use_implicit_projections = 1, optimize_trivial_count_query = 0, max_execution_time = 0.0001, timeout_overflow_mode = 'break' ``` reports `Not-ready Set is passed as the second argument for function 'in'` too. The check added here deliberately does not cover it: `break` asks for a truncated result rather than an error, so what a partially built `IN` set should do - report the limit, or silently use the rows read so far, as `set_overflow_mode = 'break'` already does - is a semantic decision, and it is not what this pull request is about. Happy to open an issue or a follow-up for it. New test `04909_cancel_in_subquery_set_build_partial_result`. It asserts up front that the `minmax_count` projection is the plan for the predicate shape under test, so it cannot pass without exercising the synchronous filter evaluation, and both of its wait loops fail loudly rather than cancelling something else. The oracle is the reported outcome, not the survival of the server, so it is live on release builds too. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115083&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115083](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115083+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Detect when tables behind a query have changed
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/108713 Adds a way to detect when the data behind a query has changed, and uses it to make the query cache consistent and to skip unnecessary refreshes of materialized views. A new virtual method `getModificationHash` on `IStorage` returns an optional `UInt128` that changes whenever the data behind the table changes (similar to an HTTP ETag). It is not a hash of the data and the way it is computed is engine-specific. It returns `NULL` when the engine cannot give a usable value, so callers fail closed. Implemented for engines that can expose a loop-free (no-ABA) value - one that never returns to an earlier value across a change-and-change-back (an `A -> B -> A` transition): - `MergeTree` family: the block-number ranges of the active data parts, their content checksums, the table structure/key metadata, a per-lifetime counter that advances on every active-part-set change (so a drop that restores an identical part set does not reproduce an earlier hash), and a per-lifetime metadata version that advances on every metadata change (so a metadata `ALTER` and back does not either). Changes on insert, merge, mutation, `ALTER`. - `Memory`: identity of the current set of blocks plus the row count and a monotonic version. - `Log`, `TinyLog`, `StripeLog`: total rows and bytes plus structure and a monotonic version. - `Merge` and `Distributed`: combine the hashes of the underlying tables (`Distributed` asks each shard through `system.tables`), folding each table's identity (database, name, UUID) so two different tables with the same hash are distinguished; they fail closed if any underlying table does. - `View` and `MaterializedView` are looked through: a view hashes the tables behind its stored `SELECT` (plus its own UUID, columns, and security metadata), a materialized view hashes its target table. They fail closed for parameterized views and in databases without table UUIDs (`Ordinary`), where incarnations of a re-created view cannot be told apart. `URL` and object storage (`S3`, ...) trust the resource's strong (non-weak) `ETag` when one is exposed, and fail closed (report `NULL`) otherwise - for glob/failover patterns, a weak or absent `ETag`, or an unreachable source. The `ETag` is loop-free for content (the same `ETag` denotes the same content), but unlike the engines above there is no monotonic version to fold, so an `A -> B -> A` rewrite back to byte-identical content within a single query's read window can in principle repeat it. That residual is narrow and both consumers below are opt-in, so we keep these engines in the feature rather than drop them. `File` fails closed: its only change signals are size and modification time, both weak. It is exposed as a lazily-computed `modification_hash` column in `system.tables`, and used for two features: - New setting `query_cache_use_only_when_data_was_not_changed`: when enabled, the combined modification hash of the tables referenced by a query is folded into the query cache key, so a cached result is reused only while none of those tables changed. If consistency cannot be guaranteed (e.g. a query calling a non-deterministic function, whose result can change while every referenced table is unchanged; a table function; a `File` table; a `URL`/object-storage table without a strong `ETag`; an object-storage read pruned by a `_path`/`_file`/Hive-partition filter, where the consumed subset cannot be compared with the full listing; a query inside a transaction, which reads the transaction's snapshot while the hash samples the live table state; or a referenced table with an active row policy for the current user, which changes what the user reads while every referenced table is unchanged - row policies existing only on remote shard servers of a `Distributed` table cannot be seen and remain part of the best-effort window), the query cache is bypassed for that query. - `REFRESH ... IF CHANGED` for refreshable materialized views: a scheduled refresh is skipped when none of the tables the view reads from changed since the last refresh that rebuilt the view (e.g. `REFRESH EVERY 1 MINUTE IF CHANGED`). It always rebuilds when a source table cannot prove it is unchanged. The `clickhouse` binary was built and all new tests pass locally, including a functional check that `Distributed.modification_hash` changes when a remote table changes and that `IF CHANGED` skips refreshes while the source is unchanged. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added a `modification_hash` column to `system.tables` that changes whenever the data behind a table changes. Based on it, added a setting `query_cache_use_only_when_data_was_not_changed` to make the query cache consistent (a cached result is reused only while the referenced tables are unchanged) and a `REFRESH ... IF CHANGED` option for refreshable materialized views to skip refreshes when the source data did not change. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=108721&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/108721](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F108721+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.text: When both sides of a math binary operator are one-argument aggregations over the same expression and grouping, scan once and compute both aggregates together instead of joining two identical grids.
