signal.title: Add `sorted_merge` and `parallel_sorted_merge` join algorithms
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109005 Implements the two algorithms planned in [this discussion](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109005#discussion_r3694159098): `full_sorting_merge` and `parallel_full_sorting_merge` are always supported, so anything listed after them in `join_algorithm` is unreachable — listing them is an unconditional choice, not a preference. The new `sorted_merge` and `parallel_sorted_merge` algorithms execute the same merge join, but are **available only when both join inputs can be efficiently read in the order of the join keys** (e.g. MergeTree tables whose primary key starts with the join keys), so the pre-join sorts become cheap `FinishSorting` or disappear. When the tables' order cannot be exploited, the selection falls through to the next algorithm in the list. That makes them meaningful as a high-priority preference: `join_algorithm = 'sorted_merge,parallel_hash'` uses the streaming, low-memory merge join exactly when it is certainly beneficial, and a hash join otherwise. `sorted_merge` runs a single in-order merge join. `parallel_sorted_merge` additionally shards the join by ranges of the tables' common primary-key prefix into independent per-shard merge joins running in parallel — the same source-side sharding `query_plan_join_shard_by_pk_ranges` applies, enabled for this join by the algorithm itself; the in-order reads stay intact (no scatter, no re-sort). When the sharding cannot apply (e.g. an `ASOF` join), it degrades to a single `sorted_merge`. Implementation notes: - Eligibility is decided during plan physicalization, where the input subplans are visible: `JoinStepLogical::inputsCanBeReadInJoinKeyOrder` finds the `ReadFromMergeTree` below each input (mirroring `findReadingStep` of `optimizeReadInOrder`, without descending through nested joins) and probes the actual read-in-order matcher (`wouldReadInOrderBeUseful`, the same side-effect-free probe `topKThroughJoin` uses) with the join-key sort description. The predicted decision degrades gracefully in both directions: a false positive runs like `full_sorting_merge` (with a full sort), a false negative falls through to the next algorithm. - The same memoized predicate makes `tryAddJoinRuntimeFilter` keep its hands off an eligible join listed before the first hash-family algorithm. Without this, planting a runtime filter erases the merge algorithms from the list (a merge join reads both sides concurrently and cannot use a runtime filter), silently overriding the priority order — the defining feature of these algorithms. For non-eligible joins the runtime filter (and the erasure) stays, because those algorithms are not selectable anyway. When `applyParallelReplicas` later breaks the eligibility (a join input becomes a distributed read), the filter pass is re-run for exactly the joins it had skipped, so the `hash` fall-through gets its runtime filter back. - `FullSortingMergeJoin` now carries the selected algorithm (`getSelectedAlgorithm`) instead of an `is_parallel` flag; the hash-scatter rewrite (`optimizeParallelFullSortingMergeJoin`) stays exclusive to `parallel_full_sorting_merge`, and `optimizeJoinByShards` runs in a restricted mode (only `parallel_sorted_merge`-selected joins, with a cheap pre-scan bail-out) when `query_plan_join_shard_by_pk_ranges` is off. When the sharded stream counts diverge at pipeline-building time (e.g. a data-dependent `PREWHERE` prunes one side to a single empty stream), `JoinStep` merges each side's per-shard sorted streams back into one sorted stream and runs the single-stream merge join instead of failing (the same approach as #109393, applied at the sharding fallback). - The `CreateSetAndFilterOnTheFlyStep` pair (`max_rows_in_set_to_optimize_join`) is not added for sorted-merge joins: it sits between the read and the sort and would defeat the in-order read the algorithm was selected for. - The old analyzer has no query plan at selection time, so there the algorithms are never selected and the list falls through (documented). With only `sorted_merge` listed and no exploitable order, the query fails with `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`, like other unsupported single-algorithm configurations. - The known lower-priority-fallback side effects of listing merge algorithms (stricter `USING` key-type inference, `topKThroughJoin` deferral) extend to the new values and are documented in the `join_algorithm` setting description. Tests: `04669_sorted_merge_join_selection` pins the selection gating via `EXPLAIN PIPELINE` (selected on a primary-key join with no re-sort, falls through on non-key joins / disabled read-in-order / old analyzer, priority order respected, error when listed alone without exploitable order) and correctness against `hash` for `INNER`/`LEFT`/`RIGHT`/`FULL`/`ANY`/`join_use_nulls`. `04670_parallel_sorted_merge_join` pins the primary-key-range sharding (`Sharding:` marker with `query_plan_join_shard_by_pk_ranges = 0`, no `ScatterByPartitionTransform`, no `MergeSortingTransform`), the `ASOF` degradation, and correctness. `04824_sorted_merge_join_parallel_replicas_fallthrough` and `04894_sorted_merge_join_parallel_replicas_runtime_filter` pin the parallel-replicas edge (fall-through to `hash` with the runtime filter restored), `04895_parallel_sorted_merge_join_shard_stream_divergence` pins the diverged-shard degradation, `04896_sorted_merge_join_null_safe_equals` pins the ineligibility of a nullable null-safe (`<=>`) join (whose keys are compared wrapped into `tuple(...)`, so they cannot be read in table order), and `04760`/`04850` pin the `join_use_nulls` and `query_plan_join_shard_by_pk_ranges` contracts. The PR #109005 regression tests and the join runtime filter tests pass unchanged. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added new `join_algorithm` values `sorted_merge` and `parallel_sorted_merge`: merge-join algorithms that are available only when both join inputs can be efficiently read in the order of the join keys (so the join benefits from the tables' order instead of sorting), and otherwise fall through to the next algorithm in the list. `parallel_sorted_merge` additionally shards the join by primary-key ranges into independent per-shard merge joins running in parallel. Listing them first, e.g. `join_algorithm = 'sorted_merge,parallel_hash'`, uses the streaming low-memory merge join exactly when it is certainly beneficial. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112973&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/112973](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F112973+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Add --dump-schema option to clickhouse-client and clickhouse-local
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/60681 Adds a `--dump-schema[=<db1,db2,...>]` option that dumps `CREATE DATABASE`/`CREATE TABLE`/`CREATE DICTIONARY`/`CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW`/`CREATE VIEW` statements for one or more databases, or all non-system user databases if no value is given, to stdout, then exits — similar to `pg_dump --schema-only`. Tables are ordered (via `TablesDependencyGraph`, the same class `DatabaseCatalog` uses to load tables at startup and backups use to order their restore; ties within a level broken by `(database, name)` for determinism) using every dependency signal `system.tables` exposes, combined: `loading_dependencies_*` (dictionaries), inverted `dependencies_*` (a materialized view's source — recorded only on the source row, not the view), `target_database`/`target_table` (a materialized view's `TO` target, explicit or implicit), and — since the server tracks none of this for plain views at all (`DROP TABLE` on a view's source succeeds even with the view still referencing it) — a best-effort scan of each view's stored, server-formatted `SELECT` text for other dumped tables' names. A genuine dependency cycle is a clear error rather than being silently reordered. This is entirely a client-side feature: `system.tables.create_table_query` and `SHOW CREATE DATABASE` already give the server-computed DDL text, so no server-side or wire-protocol changes are needed — the new code (`src/Client/SchemaDumper.{h,cpp}`) just issues a couple of queries over the existing connection (same pattern as `Suggest.cpp`) and prints the results in dependency order. `--dump-schema` also accepts a comma-separated database list (`--dump-schema=db1,db2`), and two modifiers: - `--dump-schema-exclude=db1,db2` dumps all user databases except the listed ones (rejected if combined with an explicit database list — the two are mutually exclusive ways of selecting the same thing). - `--dump-schema-dir=<path>` writes one `<database>.sql` file per dumped database into that directory (created if it doesn't exist, e.g. `mkdir clickhouse-lab && clickhouse-client --dump-schema --dump-schema-exclude=... --dump-schema-dir=clickhouse-lab`) instead of writing everything to stdout. Database names are escaped with `escapeForFileName` before being used as filenames; two target databases whose escaped names collide case-insensitively are rejected unconditionally (regardless of the destination filesystem's actual case sensitivity — reliably probing that portably isn't worth it when the point of a dump is to be replayed somewhere else later anyway), rather than one silently overwriting the other's file. Per-database write failures are detected instead of reported as success, and when a table in one dumped database depends on a table in another, the files (and their confirmation lines) are ordered — and a note printed — so replaying them in the printed order works; a database-level circular dependency (distinct from, and not implied by, a table-level cycle) is rejected with a clear error since no file order could satisfy it. A few things worth calling out for review: - Implicit materialized-view storage tables are excluded from the dump (recreated automatically by their owning `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW` statement) — but only when confirmed to be a *live* materialized view's own target with the generated-name shape (`.inner_id.*`/`.inner.*`), not merely name-shaped like one, so a real user table literally named `` `.inner.foo` `` stays in the dump. Orphaned mid-refresh leftovers (`.tmp.inner_id.*`/`.tmp.inner.*`) are filtered by name, since they're never any live target. - `--dump-schema` forces non-interactive mode (like `--query`/`--queries-file`) and is rejected if combined with either of them, so its stdout is never mixed with an interactive banner, warnings, or another query's output. For `clickhouse-local`, it's also rejected combined with `--file`/`--structure`. `--dump-schema-exclude`/`--dump-schema-dir` are rejected if `--dump-schema` itself isn't given — all validated in `processConfig()`, before `connect()`, so a plain argument mistake fails fast instead of after a connection attempt (which could otherwise block on an interactive password prompt). - Verified end-to-end via real replays into a fresh `clickhouse-local` instance: a source table with a materialized view (implicit storage), a dictionary, a plain view, a view-on-view chain, and an explicit `TO` target, named so that alphabetical order alone would produce an unreplayable dump without the fix; single/list/exclude/all-databases selection; `--dump-schema-dir` output with a genuine cross-database dependency; the case-insensitive filename collision guard (using a case-sensitive APFS volume to stand in for a Linux source, confirming both that `Foo`/`foo` coexist there and that the guard fires when dumping them); and all the rejection cases (unknown database, combined with `--query`/`--file`/`--structure`, list + exclude together, dir without `--dump-schema`). ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added a `--dump-schema[=<db1,db2,...>]` option to `clickhouse-client` and `clickhouse-local` that dumps `CREATE DATABASE`/`CREATE TABLE`/`CREATE DICTIONARY`/`CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW`/`CREATE VIEW` statements for the given database(s), or all user databases if no value is given, to stdout in dependency order, then exits — similar to `pg_dump --schema-only`. `--dump-schema-exclude=<db1,db2,...>` skips the listed databases when dumping all of them, and `--dump-schema-dir=<path>` writes one `<database>.sql` file per dumped database into that directory instead of stdout. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114098&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114098](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114098+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Add experimental PCO compression codec (linking the pcodec Rust crate)
signal.text: Adds an experimental `PCO` compression codec that links the [pcodec](https://github.com/pcodec/pcodec) (`pco`) Rust crate — the reference implementation — rather than reimplementing it. `pco` is a lossless codec specialized for sequences of fixed-width numbers; on numeric columns with smooth, multimodal, or high-entropy distributions (measurements, timings, counters, identifiers) it often beats `Gorilla`/`FPC`/`ZSTD`/`ALP` on ratio. This is the Rust-library counterpart to the native C++ port explored in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/106222. Instead of maintaining a C++ reimplementation, it links the upstream crate. ### Runtime CPU dispatch `pco` has no explicit SIMD: it relies on the compiler autovectorizing its per-batch loops, which only happens when the crate is compiled with the relevant instruction sets enabled (its `build.rs` warns to build with `-C target-feature=+avx2,+bmi1,+bmi2`). That does not work for ClickHouse, which compiles all Rust once at a fixed baseline micro-architecture level for a binary that must run on a range of CPUs. So `pco` is taken from a ClickHouse fork patched to add runtime CPU-feature dispatch of its hot loops — the same mechanism ClickHouse's C++ uses via `TargetSpecific.h`. The vectorizable loop bodies (decode `read_offsets`; encode `write_short_uints`/`write_uints`/`set_offsets`) are compiled at the crate baseline and again for `x86-64-v3` (AVX2 + BMI1/2 + FMA) and `x86-64-v4` (AVX-512), and the widest variant the running CPU supports is selected once and cached. On aarch64 the baseline already includes NEON, so the baseline body is used directly. Verified at baseline `-C target-cpu=x86-64`: the `read_offsets` v3 trampoline emits AVX2 (`ymm`) and v4 emits AVX-512 (`zmm`). The patch is merged into `ClickHouse/pcodec` (a fork of pcodec/pcodec in the ClickHouse organization) via its own PR: https://github.com/ClickHouse/pcodec/pull/1. The crate is added as the `contrib/pcodec` submodule and linked through a thin FFI wrapper crate (`rust/workspace/pco`). Its one not-yet-vendored dependency, `rand_xoshiro`, was added to `contrib/rust_vendor` in https://github.com/ClickHouse/rust_vendor/pull/72. ### Codec Supported types are all fixed-width numerics of 1/2/4/8 bytes via their underlying integer/float representation: `Int8`..`Int64`, `UInt8`..`UInt64`, `Float32`/`Float64`, and the types backed by them (`Date`, `DateTime`, `Decimal32`/`Decimal64`, `IPv4`, `Enum`, ...). The on-disk block stores a 2-byte header (element width + partial-tail byte count) followed by a raw partial-value tail (as in `Gorilla`/`FPC`) and the payload. The payload is a standalone `.pco` stream, wire-compatible with the reference pcodec implementation; when compression would not shrink a block the raw bytes are stored instead (a per-block "stored" flag), so the output never expands by more than the 2-byte header and `getMaxCompressedDataSize` is tight. The codec is gated behind `allow_experimental_codecs`. Because it needs the column type, it can only be specified per column: it is rejected in `TTL ... RECOMPRESS` and in the untyped compression settings that resolve codecs without a type. `CompressionCodecMultiple` propagates the experimental / column-type-requiring properties so a chain such as `CODEC(Delta, PCO)` is still gated, and a codec-only `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COLUMN x CODEC(PCO)` validates against the existing column type. Tests: `04512_pco_codec` round-trips every supported numeric and backed type (per-element verification, edge cases, codec chaining, compression-ratio check) and `04513_pco_codec_gating` covers the experimental gate, the `TTL RECOMPRESS` rejection, and the codec-only `ALTER`. The FFI wrapper has its own Rust unit tests (round-trip of all types, the no-expansion fallback, and fail-closed handling of malformed/mismatched streams). ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added a new experimental compression codec `PCO`, which links the [pcodec](https://github.com/pcodec/pcodec) library (patched for runtime CPU dispatch), specialized for fixed-width numeric columns. It is wire-format compatible with pcodec `.pco` streams and is enabled with `allow_experimental_codecs`. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes: - [x] Documentation is written (the `PCO` codec is documented in `docs/en/sql-reference/statements/create/table.md`, and the compression-frame method byte in `docs/en/interfaces/specs/NativeFormat.md`). <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110613&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/110613](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F110613+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Reject CREATE TABLE ... CLONE AS SELECT / table function
signal.text: The `CREATE TABLE ... CLONE AS <source>` clause is intended to clone a real on-disk source table — the partition-attach step performed after table creation needs actual partitions to copy. The parser, however, also accepted `CREATE TABLE t CLONE AS SELECT ...` and `CREATE TABLE t CLONE AS <table_function>`. Neither shape has partitions to attach, so the `CLONE` keyword was silently ignored and the table was created as a plain `CREATE ... AS SELECT` with an inferred schema and `ORDER BY tuple()`. This PR rejects both shapes early in `getTablePropertiesAndNormalizeCreateQuery` with `BAD_ARGUMENTS`, so the user gets a clear error instead of silent misbehavior. It also fixes a related defect in `ASTCreateQuery::formatQueryImpl`: the `if (select)` branch did not call `add_clone_if_needed`, so an AST format round-trip silently dropped `CLONE` from `CLONE AS SELECT`. The randomized-settings injection in `clickhouse-test` round-trips queries through this formatter, which is how the gap surfaced. Fixes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/104994 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `CREATE TABLE ... CLONE AS SELECT ...` and `CREATE TABLE ... CLONE AS <table_function>` silently ignoring the `CLONE` keyword and creating a plain `CREATE ... AS SELECT` instead. These shapes are now rejected with `BAD_ARGUMENTS`. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is unchanged: this is a bug fix that brings behavior in line with the existing `CLONE AS` documentation, which only describes the `CLONE AS <table>` form. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=105004&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/105004](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F105004+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix AI functions embedding counters behavior on error
signal.text: `aiEmbed` and `aiSimilarity` under-report provider usage in `system.query_log` when a request fails: with the default `ai_function_throw_on_error = 1` the exception row shows `AIAPICalls = 0` and `AIInputTokens = 0`, although the provider was called and billed. Flipping only that setting records the call: | `ai_function_throw_on_error` | `AIAPICalls` | `AIRowsSkipped` | |---|---:|---:| | `1` (default) | 0 | 0 | | `0` | 1 | 1 | Same query and endpoint, with `ai_function_max_retries = 0` so exactly one attempt is made. **Cause.** `embedTexts` accumulates the counters in a local `EmbeddingResult` and returns it by value. When a failed request rethrows, `return` is never reached: the local is destroyed while unwinding and the caller's `embedding_result` is never constructed, so the caller's `ProfileEvents::increment` calls are both skipped and left with nothing to read. That defeats the intent stated at the accumulation site, which counts `api_calls` *before* issuing the request so that failed calls are still counted. **Fix.** `embedTexts` now reports `AIAPICalls` and `AIInputTokens` itself, from a `SCOPE_EXIT` guard, so the normal and throwing exits both publish them. They are plain locals rather than fields of `EmbeddingResult`, so no caller can count them twice. Callers keep their own row counters, which mean different things: texts for `aiEmbed`, pairs of texts for `aiSimilarity`. **Not covered.** Row counters are still dropped when the query throws. It delivered no rows, and preserving them would need `embedTexts` to take an out-parameter in both callers. **Tests.** Three integration tests, each verified to fail with the source reverted to `master`: one per caller for `AIAPICalls`, plus one driving the quota-exceeded throw so a batch succeeds first and `AIInputTokens` is non-zero. The failed-request tests cannot cover `AIInputTokens`, since there the first request fails and no tokens are consumed. The same defect on the text-generation path is fixed in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111830, which is what introduced a throwing path there. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111830 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `aiEmbed` and `aiSimilarity` reporting zero `AIAPICalls` in `system.query_log` when a provider request failed, and losing `AIInputTokens` already consumed by earlier successful batches. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114905&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114905](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114905+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Add VALID FOR clause for users and credentials
signal.text: We support `VALID UNTIL` for users and credentials. This adds `VALID FOR <interval>` as a convenience shorthand. Instead of an absolute date and time, `VALID FOR` accepts an interval, and the expiration deadline is computed as the current time plus that interval at the moment the query is executed. The result is stored in the `VALID UNTIL` form, so `SHOW CREATE USER` always displays the resolved absolute deadline. It can be used everywhere `VALID UNTIL` can - at the user level and per authentication method, in both `CREATE USER` and `ALTER USER`. Examples: ```sql CREATE USER u1 VALID FOR INTERVAL 1 DAY; CREATE USER u2 IDENTIFIED WITH plaintext_password BY 'x' VALID FOR INTERVAL 3 MONTH; ALTER USER u1 VALID FOR INTERVAL 1 DAY + INTERVAL 12 HOUR; ``` Implementation notes: the current time is injected as a literal (rather than using `now`, which is non-deterministic and would not fold to a constant expression), and the deadline is computed with `toDateTime64` so that large intervals saturate at the `DateTime64` upper bound instead of overflowing the year-2106 boundary of `DateTime`. Note on the system table schema: to represent deadlines beyond the year 2106 exactly, the `valid_until` column of `system.users` changes from `Array(DateTime)` to `Array(DateTime64(0))`. This is a backward-incompatible change of a documented system table for tooling that introspects the column type; the values themselves keep second precision. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Backward Incompatible Change ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added the `VALID FOR <interval>` clause to `CREATE USER` and `ALTER USER` as a shorthand for `VALID UNTIL`. The expiration deadline is computed as the current time plus the given interval at query execution time and stored in the `VALID UNTIL` form. The `valid_until` column of the `system.users` table now has the type `Array(DateTime64(0))` instead of `Array(DateTime)`, so that deadlines beyond the year 2106 are represented exactly; tooling that reads this column should handle the new type. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110171&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/110171](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F110171+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Validate IN tuple/subquery column count mismatch in analyzer
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/74442 The analyzer (`resolveFunction`) now validates that the number of elements on the left side of `IN` matches the number of columns in the right-side subquery. Previously, constant folding could optimize away the `IN` expression and silently hide the mismatch: for example, `(1, 1) IN (SELECT 1)` wrapped in a subquery with a constant-false outer `WHERE` succeeded silently. Now it correctly throws `NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS_DOESNT_MATCH` during analysis. A single `Tuple` column on the right side is still accepted, since `FunctionIn` compares the whole left-side value against it; `LowCardinality` and `Nullable` wrappers are unwrapped before the check. Covered by the new test `03380_in_tuple_subquery_column_count`, including the original reproducer from the issue. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Detect column count mismatch between a tuple and a subquery in the `IN` clause during analysis, preventing constant folding from silently hiding the error. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=97540&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/97540](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F97540+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Make a table read by a scalar subquery in a CONSTRAINT a loading dependency
signal.text: Attaching a table analyzes its constraints in `InterpreterCreateQuery::getConstraintsDescription`, and the analysis executes the scalar subqueries of a constraint expression. The tables such a subquery reads were not registered as loading dependencies, because `DDLLoadingDependencyVisitor` only looks at functions, dictionary sources and the storage definition. Nothing prevented dropping such a table, and the server did not start afterwards - attaching the dependent table threw `UNKNOWN_TABLE` and loading the metadata failed: ```sql CREATE TABLE t1 (id UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); CREATE TABLE t2 (conversation UInt64, CONSTRAINT c CHECK (SELECT id FROM t1 LIMIT 15) IN (conversation)) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); DROP TABLE t1; -- accepted, and the server cannot start anymore ``` The referential dependency was recorded, since `DDLDependencyVisitor` visits `ASTTableExpression`, so `check_referential_table_dependencies = 1` rejected the `DROP`. But that setting is off by default, and it is the loading graph that the default `check_table_dependencies` check and the `DROP DATABASE` drop order (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/97057) use. A constraint declaration is now visited, and the tables of every subquery that the analysis executes are added to the loading dependencies. Subqueries which the analysis does not execute - the right argument of `IN` and the argument of `exists`, see `ExecuteScalarSubqueriesMatcher::visit` - are skipped, because what they read is needed only when the constraint is checked, not to attach the table. That keeps `02916_joinget_dependency`-style patterns working, in particular `02841_not_ready_set_constraints`, which drops the table read by an `x IN (SELECT ...)` constraint on purpose. Seen in CI as a `Cannot start clickhouse-server` stress failure, e.g. https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110231&sha=4de836223549fd5224ca017b8c1a28e344ce38e9&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_msan%29 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114918 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/87369 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): A table read by a scalar subquery inside a `CONSTRAINT` is now a loading dependency of the table that declares the constraint. Previously such a table could be dropped, after which the server did not start, because attaching the dependent table executes the subquery. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114923&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114923](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114923+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix `clickhouse-local` printing TSV instead of PrettyCompact in interactive mode
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/105249 Interactive `clickhouse-local` on master renders query results as `TSV` instead of the terminal default `PrettyCompact`. `applyCmdOptions` seeds the `default_format` setting on `global_context` as the fallback format of the sessions of the embedded protocol listeners (`SYSTEM START LISTEN`), where it must match a real `clickhouse-server` (`TabSeparated`). `client_context` is copied from `global_context` and inherits the seed, and the per-query output-format resolution introduced in #105249 treats a non-empty `default_format` setting as the fallback format, so the seed overrode the interactive display default. (#105249 guarded `--vertical` against exactly this failure mode, but the plain interactive default slipped through: it is the one case where `is_default_format` stays true.) The fix clears the seeded value on `client_context`, in `makeFormatOptionsPrivateToTheClient`, which already handles the mirror image of this problem for the `format` / `input_format` / `output_format` settings. This client renders results from its own `ClientBase::default_output_format`, so the seed is not needed there. Explicit choices keep working: an explicit `--default_format` on the command line is left in place (guarded by `cmd_settings->isChanged`), and a later `SET default_format = ...` or an in-query `SETTINGS` clause lands on `client_context` after the clearing. The served sessions still get the fallback through `global_context`. Verified against the master CI binary (26.8.1.1658, where the regression reproduces): emulating the fix by forcing an empty `default_format` on the client restores `PrettyCompact`, while `SET default_format = 'JSONEachRow'` and `SETTINGS default_format = 'CSV'` continue to be honored. The added `04927_local_interactive_default_format.expect` test fails on current master and passes with the fix emulated; the listener-side default is already covered by `04501_local_http_default_format.expect`. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a regression on master (not present in any release): interactive `clickhouse-local` rendered query results as `TSV` instead of `PrettyCompact`. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115360&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115360](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115360+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Reimplement the KQL (Kusto) dialect on a lexer, an AST and AST translation
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/61742 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Reimplemented the experimental KQL (Kusto) dialect. It now has its own lexer and parser and builds an AST directly, instead of translating a token stream into SQL text and reparsing it. This fixes an expression-injection hole in the string operators (`contains`, `has`, ...), several results that silently disagreed with Kusto (`7 / 2`, `substring` with a negative start, `bin`), and 28 functions that were registered but did nothing. The supported subset is smaller and documented; anything outside it is now rejected by name instead of being mistranslated. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes `docs/guides/clickhouse/kusto-query-language.mdx` --- ## Why The dialect was contributed in 2022 and abandoned by its authors; the rewrite they promised in #62668 was closed unmerged. Since then it has been emergency-disabled once (#59305) and gated behind `allow_experimental_kusto_dialect` (#74224), and #61742 ("Remove KQL support if this code will not be fixed") has stayed open. The implementation translated a KQL token stream directly into ClickHouse SQL **text** and reparsed it — 298 `fmt::format` sites, 41 places that re-lexed generated text, and no AST anywhere in the function layer. Everything below follows from that: | | before | after | |---|---|---| | `T \| where s contains "x') OR 1 = 1 OR ilike(s, 'y"` | injected the expression | needle is an `ASTLiteral`; no injection is representable | | `'50x' contains '50%'` | `true` — needle was pasted into a LIKE pattern | `false` | | `substring('abcdefg', -3, 2)` | `'ab'` | `'ef'` | | `7 / 2` | `3.5` | `3` | | `format_timespan(col, 'hh:mm')` | `stoi: no conversion` — `std::stoi` on generated SQL | rejected by name | | `series_fir(...)` | `Function series_fir does not exist` (one of 28 stubs) | rejected by name | | `search 'x'` | `Unknown table expression identifier 'search'` | `'search' is not a supported KQL operator` | | `let` bindings | `static thread_local`, leaked between queries | scoped to one parse | ## What is here Two commits: the removal, then the reimplementation. ``` src/Parsers/Kusto/ KQLLexer KQL's own tokens: !in, =~, .., timespans (2.5h), verbatim @'...', datetime(...). A bad literal is an Error token carrying a reason, so nothing downstream asks isValidKQLPos() — the core of #61742. KQLAST the tabular level only. Scalar expressions are ClickHouse AST directly; a parallel expression hierarchy would add only conversions. KQLParser recursive descent. `let` bindings are an ordinary member. KQLTranslator each operator fills a still-empty clause of the select being built, or wraps what exists so far in a subquery and starts a new one. KQLFunctions name -> builder returning an ASTPtr. src/Functions/Kusto/ kqlDivide `7 / 2` is 3 in KQL and 3.5 in SQL — the choice depends on operand kqlBin types, so it is made by an IFunctionOverloadResolver during analysis rather than guessed from how the argument was spelled. ``` KQL now has its own entry point (`parseKQLQuery`) and never touches the SQL tokenizer. Because `ClientBase` already catches, the parser can simply throw — so there is no `tryParseKQLQuery`, and no `catch` anywhere in the new code. **`src/Parsers/Kusto` no longer needs its carve-out from check 19** ("do not catch exceptions in src/Parsers"), and this PR deletes it. `src/Parsers/Kusto` goes from 13017 lines to 3967, plus 337 lines of runtime functions. ## Scope Deliberately smaller than before, and written down in the guide. A construct is either translated with the semantics Kusto documents, or rejected by name. Rejected in this PR: `search`, `parse`, `mv-apply`, `lookup`, `evaluate`, `invoke`, `facet`, `top-nested`, `make-series` and friends; the `series_*`, `bag_*`/`pack_*` and `ipv4_*` families; `parse_url`, `parse_csv`, `parse_json`, `toscalar`, `format_timespan`; and `dynamic` **objects** (arrays map onto ClickHouse `Array`). Three known divergences are documented rather than papered over: subtracting two datetimes yields seconds instead of a timespan, `project-rename` moves the renamed column to the end, and `union` needs compatible schemas. ## Testing `04670`–`04673` cover the pipeline, the string operators (including the injection cases), the scalar semantics that used to be wrong, and 47 constructs that must be rejected. A 2500-query random fuzz found no crashes or logical errors. The 302 conformance cases that were deleted with the old implementation are being reintroduced separately, on top of this branch. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112932&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/112932](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F112932+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix a `_table` or `_database` filter silently returning no rows over a Merge table
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/84139 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107418 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `WHERE _table = ...` or `WHERE _database = ...` filter on a `Merge` table silently returning no rows when a child table reads through another table, for example a `Distributed`, `Merge`, `Buffer` or `Alias` child. The filter now prunes only the children whose rows carry that child's own name, and is applied per row for the rest. ### Description `SELECT ... FROM merge(db, <regexp>) WHERE _table = '<name>'` silently returns zero rows whenever a child does not stamp its own name into `_table`. There is no exception, so the user gets a short answer with no signal. `_database` behaves the same; both reproduce on master. The prefilter in `ReadFromMerge::getSelectedTables` matches the predicate against the child's own name, but the value the rows carry is stamped lower down, by whichever storage produces the block. For a `MergeTree` or `View` child these agree. For a child that delegates its read they differ: the rows carry the delegate's name, the prefilter the delegator's. This dates from #102471, which made `Merge` proxy virtual columns to its children without updating the prefilter. The fix prunes a child only where its rows are guaranteed to carry that child's own `StorageID`, and admits every other child so the per-row filter decides. Admitting is safe: the predicate is still pushed down and still prunes below an admitted child, so an unrecognised engine loses only an optimisation. Streaming engines stay pruned, because reading one consumes its queue, durably for `FileLog`. That is resolved through `Alias`, `Buffer`, `MaterializedView`, `MaterializedPostgreSQL` and lazy-table-proxy hops of any depth, each using a non-throwing accessor. An unresolvable hop, a chain over sixteen deep, or a proxy whose table is not yet loaded stays pruned, as on master. Physical-column shadowing is a separate defect, #103631, left unchanged. One case is deliberate: a `Distributed` child over a streaming engine is now read rather than pruned, since the initiator cannot know the remote engine. The two tests add 77 arms, 37 of them controls. Each recognised class and each guard is pinned by a mutant reverting it, which reddens that class's arms and no others. An `EXCHANGE TABLES` racing the check is left open, as on master. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113735&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/113735](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F113735+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Allow creating a Distributed table over a table function
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/106189 Allow creating a `Distributed` table over a table function, in the same way the `remote`/`cluster` table functions already accept an arbitrary table expression. Previously `CREATE TABLE ... ENGINE = Distributed(...)` only accepted `Distributed(cluster, database, table[, sharding_key[, policy_name]])`, where `database` and `table` had to be string literals or identifiers. `StorageDistributed` itself already supported being backed by a table function (`remote_table_function_ptr`), but that capability was only reachable through the `remote`/`cluster`/`clusterAllReplicas` table functions. This change lets the engine take a table function directly: ```sql CREATE TABLE t ENGINE = Distributed(cluster, table_function()[, sharding_key[, policy_name]]); -- e.g. CREATE TABLE distributed_numbers ENGINE = Distributed(test_cluster_two_shards, numbers(100)); ``` mirroring the `cluster('cluster_name', table_function())` signature. The second engine argument is treated as a table function only when it is a call to a registered table function; any other expression is still interpreted as a database name, so the existing `Distributed(cluster, database, table, ...)` form is unaffected. The structure is inferred from the table function when the columns are omitted. `INSERT` into a table-function-backed `Distributed` table is rejected with `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`, since there is no concrete remote table to route rows to. As a side effect, `INSERT INTO FUNCTION cluster('cluster', table_function())` now fails with this clear error instead of silently building a broken `INSERT INTO <empty>` query for the shards. ### Relationship to #106189 This is complementary to #106189 (`Remote`/`RemoteSecure` storage engines): that PR adds address-based engines over an ad-hoc cluster, while this one lets the configured-cluster `Distributed` engine take a table function. The table-function `INSERT` guard in `StorageDistributed::write` is aligned with #106189 (identical exception message, guard placed only in `write`). The `read` path here additionally handles the case where the remote database/table names are empty (a table-function-backed `Distributed` stores empty names rather than the `system.one` placeholder that #106189's engines inherit from the `remote` table function); this also makes the shared `read` path robust for #106189's engines. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Allow creating a `Distributed` table over a table function, e.g. `CREATE TABLE t ENGINE = Distributed(cluster, numbers(100))`, in the same way as the `cluster`/`remote` table functions accept a table function. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110073&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/110073](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F110073+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Resume a NATS JetStream subscription after a reconnect
signal.text: A `NATS` table reading from a JetStream stream can stop consuming for good after the NATS server restarts, while still looking subscribed and healthy. An asynchronous JetStream pull subscription asks for more messages only when one is delivered, and when the NATS client reconnects it re-sends the `SUB` line but not the pull request the broker was holding. A broker that goes away without answering that request - a hard kill, a network partition, or a graceful restart that lands in the milliseconds between a re-subscribe and its request being parked - leaves the table subscribed and permanently silent. That is what `test_nats_restore_failed_connection_without_losses_on_write` hits when the consumer is still behind at the moment the broker is stopped: all 100000 rows were published and acknowledged into the stream, but the ones not yet delivered are never fetched again, so the view stays short of them and the test fails with `ClickHouse lost some messages: 92807`. It fails this way on about 0.2% of runs since the NATS tests came back on 2026-07-30, and at the same rate before and after #112828 recovered the closed-subscription case on 2026-08-13 (88 of 46693 runs before, 27 of 15428 after), which is what points at the window that fix leaves open. CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=c260929910ea94be9a359bb69bf5e33d7b3a40e4&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Integration%20tests%20%28arm_binary%2C%20distributed%20plan%2C%204%2F4%29 Recovery so far keyed only on a subscription the NATS client had closed, which is what a graceful shutdown produces by answering the outstanding pull request. This reports a reconnect as well, by comparing the reconnect count the client keeps for the connection against the one taken when we subscribed, and re-subscribes through the same path. Only JetStream consumers do this: a core NATS subscription really is restored by the `SUB` line, and re-subscribing it would drop buffered messages nothing redelivers. The window this closes is the residual documented in #112828, so `_restart_nats` no longer retries until a restart lands outside it, and a new test reaches that state deterministically with `SIGKILL`, which answers nothing and so leaves no closed subscription to fall back on. Verified locally with a release build, running the module through `ci.praktika`: - new test with the fix: passed twice (65 s, 146 s); - new test with `src/Storages/NATS` reverted to `master` and everything else unchanged: `AssertionError: consumption did not resume, view holds 10 of 20 keys` - the messages published after the restart never arrive; - the five existing restart tests plus `test_nats_restore_failed_connection_without_losses_on_write`, all six passed with the fix. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112828 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `NATS` engine table reading from a JetStream stream (`nats_stream`) silently stopping to consume messages after the NATS server restarted or the connection was re-established.

signal.title: typeIsSigned omits Time/Time64: JIT zero-extends negative Time to Time64
signal.text: ### Describe what's wrong **`if`/`multiIf`/`CASE` that mixes a `Time` and a `Time64` operand returns a garbage, max-clamped value for negative `Time` inputs once the expression is JIT compiled. `SELECT if(number % 2 = 0, toTime('-100:00:00'), toTime64('50:00:00', 3)) FROM numbers(2)` yields `999:59:59.000` instead of `-100:00:00.000`. With `compile_expressions=0` the same query is correct. Both settings are on by default (`compile_expressions=true`, `min_count_to_compile_expression=3`), so a repeated query flips to the wrong answer on its 4th execution.** - **Root cause:** `typeIsSigned` (`[`src/DataTypes/Native.cpp:32-34`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8b9c617362bf7/src/DataTypes/Native.cpp#L32-L34)`) enumerates `isInt() || isFloat() || isEnum() || isDate32() || isDecimal() || isDateTime64()` and never adds `isTime()` / `isTime64()`. `WhichDataType::isDecimal()` (`[`src/DataTypes/IDataType.h:407`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8b9c617362bf7/src/DataTypes/IDataType.h#L407)`) covers only `Decimal32/64/128/256`, which is exactly why `isDateTime64()` had to be spelled out — the two time types were missed. `canBeNativeType` (`[`src/DataTypes/Native.cpp:53-59`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8b9c617362bf7/src/DataTypes/Native.cpp#L53-L59)`) does accept `isTime()` and `isTime64()`, so both reach the JIT and are widened with a zero-extend: `Time` -360000 (`Int32`) becomes 4294607296 before the x1000 scale multiply. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `FunctionIf::compileImpl` -> `nativeCast(b, {Time value, DataTypeTime}, DataTypeTime64)` -> `[`src/DataTypes/Native.cpp:180`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8b9c617362bf7/src/DataTypes/Native.cpp#L180)` (scale differs) or `:205` (scale equal) -> `b.CreateIntCast(value, i64, typeIsSigned(*from_type))` -> `typeIsSigned` at `[`src/DataTypes/Native.cpp:30`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8b9c617362bf7/src/DataTypes/Native.cpp#L30)`. **Affected locations:** - [`src/DataTypes/Native.cpp:32`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8b9c617362bf7/src/DataTypes/Native.cpp#L32) — typeIsSigned type list — missing isTime()/isTime64() - [`src/DataTypes/Native.cpp:180`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8b9c617362bf7/src/DataTypes/Native.cpp#L180) — scale-conversion widening cast for DateTime/Time family uses typeIsSigned - [`src/DataTypes/Native.cpp:205`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8b9c617362bf7/src/DataTypes/Native.cpp#L205) — generic integer-to-integer nativeCast uses typeIsSigned - [`src/DataTypes/Native.cpp:55`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8b9c617362bf7/src/DataTypes/Native.cpp#L55) — canBeNativeType admits isTime()/isTime64() **Impact:** Silent wrong results for any query that JIT-compiles a `Time`-to-`Time64` widening and can see a negative `Time` (a clock reading before midnight — `Time` is a signed second count). Reachable with stock settings via `if`, `multiIf` and `CASE` over mixed `Time`/`Time64` operands. The value is not merely off — it lands past the type maximum and prints clamped at `999:59:59`. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `8b9c617362bf7`). ### How to reproduce [▶ Run on ClickHouse Fiddle](https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/f323b20a-7a5f-4c00-96ce-23bef7bed244) <details> <summary>Reproducer</summary> ```sql -- no-fasttest: JIT compilation is not available in fasttest -- Regression test for https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/96619 -- When JIT-compiling expressions that convert DateTime to DateTime64, -- the scale multiplier was not applied, causing the value to be -- reinterpreted instead of converted (e.g., seconds treated as milliseconds). DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t; SET compile_expressions = 1, min_count_to_compile_expression = 0; SELECT '--- DateTime to DateTime64 via multiIf ---'; SELECT multiIf( number = 0, toNullable(toDateTime('2001-02-03 04:05:06')), number = 1, toNullable(toDateTime('2001-02-03 04:05:06')), '1970-01-01 00:00:00'::Nullable(DateTime64(3)) ) FROM numbers(2); SELECT '--- DateTime to DateTime64 via if ---'; SELECT if( number % 2 = 0, toNullable(toDateTime('2001-02-03 04:05:06')), '1970-01-01 00:00:00'::Nullable(DateTime64(3)) ) FROM numbers(2); SELECT '--- CASE expression ---'; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t; CREATE TABLE t (date1 Nullable(DateTime), date2 Nullable(DateTime)) ENGINE = Memory; INSERT INTO t(date1, date2) VALUES ('2001-02-03 04:05:06', NULL); SELECT CASE WHEN date2 IS NOT NULL THEN date2 WHEN date1 IS NOT NULL THEN date1 ELSE '1970-01-01 00:00:00'::Nullable(DateTime64(3)) END FROM t; DROP TABLE t; SELECT '--- Time to Time64 via if ---'; SELECT if(number % 2 = 0, toTime('-100:00:00'), toTime64('50:00:00', 3)) FROM numbers(2) ORDER BY number; SELECT '--- Time to Time64 via multiIf ---'; SELECT multiIf(number % 2 = 0, toTime('-100:00:00'), toTime64('50:00:00', 3)) FROM numbers(2) ORDER BY number; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t; ``` </details> ### Expected behavior ``` --- Time to Time64 via if --- -100:00:00.000 50:00:00.000 --- Time to Time64 via multiIf --- -100:00:00.000 50:00:00.000 ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` --- Time to Time64 via if --- 999:59:59.000 50:00:00.000 --- Time to Time64 via multiIf --- 999:59:59.000 50:00:00.000 ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> Add `|| data_type.isTime() || data_type.isTime64()` to `typeIsSigned` at `[`src/DataTypes/Native.cpp:32-34`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8b9c617362bf7/src/DataTypes/Native.cpp#L32-L34)`. Both are signed (`Int32` / `Decimal64`-derived) and both are already accepted by `canBeNativeType`. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - `src/DataTypes/Native.cpp:201` (`typeIsSigned ? CreateSIToFP : CreateUIToFP`) reads the same oracle, so a compiled `Time64`-to-float cast would be wrong the same way. I could not construct a JIT-compiled float conversion from `Time64` in SQL, so this arm is unproven — the `typeIsSigned` fix covers it regardless. Found during automated review of [PR #114168](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114168). Severity P1 · Finding `h_pr114168_001` </details> cc @groeneai @Manerone @alexey-milovidov (from #114168)

signal.title: Fix header column order after the no-rescoring vector search rewrite
signal.text: <!--- A technical description of your changes with a motivation --> The second-pass vector search optimization (`vector_search_with_rescoring = 0`) removed the distance function from the `ExpressionStep` outputs and re-appended the rewritten `_distance` alias at the end, changing the header column order. Steps created above the `Sorting` before that rewrite runs — the local top-N `Limit` and the exchange steps of a distributed plan — kept the original column order, and `makeDistributedPlan` failed to rebuild the plan fragments with a logical error: `Cannot add step Limit to QueryPlan because it has incompatible header with root step Sorting`. Non-distributed plans never re-validate step headers after optimization, which is why this only surfaced with `make_distributed_plan = 1`. The fix reinserts the rewritten output node at the original position of the distance column, so the header column order is preserved and all previously created parent steps stay consistent. Found by AST fuzzer on [#42701](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/42701) ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=42701&sha=019244e0d46b4d9029fc261a549e1c5cd79b1bbb&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%29)); the same signature also hit the unrelated #98789 on 2026-08-08. The regression test asserts only the row count: the distributed plan currently returns an incorrect top-N for vector search queries regardless of the rescoring mode — a separate, pre-existing bug. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114456 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/42701 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a logical error `Cannot add step Limit to QueryPlan because it has incompatible header with root step Sorting` when a vector search query with `vector_search_with_rescoring = 0` was executed with the experimental `make_distributed_plan` setting. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114457&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114457](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114457+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Add `max_rows` setting for databases
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109355 Adds a `max_rows` setting for `Atomic` and `Ordinary` databases: a ceiling on active MergeTree rows counted toward the database limit. The counted total is exposed through the nullable `system.databases.rows` column. It intentionally excludes engines that do not participate in `max_rows` accounting. The setting can be changed at runtime with `ALTER DATABASE ... MODIFY SETTING max_rows = N`; its default value, `0`, is unlimited. ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Add the `max_rows` setting for `Atomic` and `Ordinary` databases, limiting active MergeTree rows counted across a database. It is enforced on `INSERT`, `ATTACH`, and partition imports, is reconfigurable via `ALTER DATABASE ... signal.title: Improve canceling queries in nested expression functions in FilterTransform
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/103705 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Improve canceling queries by `KILL QUERY` and Ctrl+C in `clickhouse-client` while a long-running function is evaluated in a filter expression: `FilterTransform` (`WHERE`, including the `FilterSortedStreamByRange` path) and `TotalsHavingTransform` (`HAVING` with `WITH TOTALS`) now forward cancellation into nested expression functions. This supersedes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/103705 by @rvasin (Roman Vasin), whose commits are preserved here — all credit for the feature goes to them. The original branch is in a fork with maintainer edits disabled, so the merge conflicts with `master` and the remaining review feedback could not be pushed there. On top of the original PR, this PR: - Merges `master` and resolves the conflicts (`FailPoint.cpp` failpoint list, `FilterTransform.cpp` includes). - Addresses the two unresolved review threads (the AI review "Request changes" verdict): - `FilterSortedStreamByRange` holds a private `FilterTransform` and calls its `transform` directly, but the pipeline cancels only the outer processor. Now `FilterSortedStreamByRange::onCancel` forwards the cancellation into the inner transform, so `cancelExecution` reaches functions of range-filter predicates from `PartsSplitter`. - `TotalsHavingTransform` evaluated the `HAVING` expression without a cancellation callback, so a long-running function in `HAVING` remained uninterruptible. It now mirrors `FilterTransform`: `onCancel` cancels function execution, `expression->execute` gets a `check_cancelled` callback, and the transform returns before the totals/filter bookkeeping when cancelled. - Adds a test `04658_kill_query_having_totals_pause` with a new `totals_having_transform_pause` failpoint, mirroring `04612_kill_query_filter_pause`. - Adds immediate pre-evaluation cancellation guards in `FilterTransform` and `TotalsHavingTransform`, with `04905_kill_query_cancelled_before_expression` covering the already-dispatched-task race. - Addresses the latest review thread: `ConvertingTransform::onCancel` now forwards cancellation into functions executing target-side conversion/default expressions, with `04909_kill_query_converting_transform_wasm` covering a cancelled `INSERT` through a `DEFAULT` WASM expression. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112705&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/112705](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F112705+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Support the short ATTACH syntax for views
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115259 (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114747 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `ATTACH VIEW <name>` and `ATTACH MATERIALIZED VIEW <name>` now re-attach a previously detached view from its stored metadata, like `ATTACH TABLE` and `ATTACH DICTIONARY` already did. Previously only `DETACH VIEW` was accepted and the matching `ATTACH` was a syntax error. Closes #115259. ### Description Requested by @ PedroTadim in #115259, who reported it and offered to review; [acknowledged here](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115259#issuecomment-5327133729). `VIEW` was the only object kind where `DETACH X <name>` had no matching `ATTACH X <name>`. `ParserCreateTableQuery` has a short-attach shortcut (`ParserCreateQuery.cpp:858`) and `ParserCreateDictionaryQuery` skips its body clauses when attaching, but `ParserCreateViewQuery` required the body unconditionally and died at the mandatory `AS`. I added the same shortcut there, keeping the view flags on the AST so the interpreter routes it as a view. Two interpreter changes follow. I proved each on a parser-only build first. `createTable` synthesized an empty `sql_security` for any AST whose `supportSQLSecurity()` is true, which the new branch sets, and `has_dropped_clauses` then threw `BAD_ARGUMENTS` about a clause the user never wrote. I suppress the synthesis for the body-less ATTACH shape rather than reordering the defaulting, so a stored view is never re-defaulted on re-attach. `getRequiredAccess()` authorizes from the typed keyword before metadata is read, and `CREATE TABLE` implies `CREATE VIEW`, so the parser change alone let a user holding only `CREATE VIEW` attach a detached ordinary table via `ATTACH VIEW t` (measured). I reject a VIEW-spelled short ATTACH whose stored metadata is not a view. The `TABLE` spelling stays permissive: it requires the stronger `CREATE TABLE`, and `ATTACH TABLE` on a detached view is the workaround the issue documents. `ATTACH WINDOW VIEW` has the same gap, left alone while #114747 removes `WINDOW VIEW` from this file. `DETACH MATERIALIZED VIEW` is also a syntax error, but `DETACH VIEW mv` already works, so nothing is user-visible there. Validation: three new stateless tests (syntax, access, `sql_security` suppression) plus a converted arm of `01600_detach_permanently`, each verified to fail without its change; those four and five further existing tests around this path pass; 200/200 green over 50 randomized runs each. <details> <summary>Sibling and edge-case matrix</summary> | statement | before | after | |---|---|---| | `ATTACH VIEW v` | `SYNTAX_ERROR` | re-attaches | | `ATTACH MATERIALIZED VIEW mv` | `SYNTAX_ERROR` | re-attaches | | `ATTACH VIEW IF NOT EXISTS v` | `SYNTAX_ERROR` | re-attaches, idempotent | | `ATTACH VIEW v ON CLUSTER c` | `SYNTAX_ERROR` | resolves the cluster | | `ATTACH VIEW db.v` | `SYNTAX_ERROR` | re-attaches | | `ATTACH VIEW v UUID '...'` | `SYNTAX_ERROR` | `BAD_ARGUMENTS`, as `ATTACH TABLE t UUID '...'` | | `ATTACH TEMPORARY VIEW v` | `SYNTAX_ERROR` (parser) | `SYNTAX_ERROR` (interpreter), as `ATTACH TEMPORARY TABLE` | | `ATTACH VIEW <a table>` | n/a | `INCORRECT_QUERY`, "it is a Table" | | `ATTACH WINDOW VIEW wv` | `SYNTAX_ERROR` | unchanged, see #114747 | | `ATTACH OR REPLACE VIEW v` | `SYNTAX_ERROR` | unchanged | | `ATTACH SQL SECURITY INVOKER VIEW v` | `SYNTAX_ERROR` | unchanged | | `ATTACH DEFINER = u VIEW v` | `SYNTAX_ERROR` | unchanged | | `DETACH MATERIALIZED VIEW mv` | `SYNTAX_ERROR` | unchanged, out of scope | | `ATTACH TABLE <a detached view>` | works | works | | `ATTACH TABLE t` / `DICTIONARY d` / `DATABASE db` | works | works | </details> <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115351&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115351](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115351+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix undefined behavior in DateTime64 reservoir quantiles
signal.text: The reservoir-sampling implementation of `quantile` and `quantiles` previously interpolated decimal-backed values through `Float64`. `DateTime64` ticks close to the upper `Int64` boundary, as well as `Decimal128` and `Decimal256` values near their limits, can collapse to the same `Float64` value and make conversion back to the native representation undefined or return an incorrect endpoint. Interpolate decimal-backed samples in their exact native domain instead, and cover scalar/plural `DateTime64` plus wide-decimal boundary cases with stateless regression tests. Found by the `arm_asan_ubsan` stress test: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112573&sha=762fa93f05ca081011efec5fef767e3c36be6853&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_asan_ubsan%2C%20s3%29 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114485 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107154 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed undefined behavior and incorrect boundary results in `quantile` and `quantiles` for `DateTime64` and wide `Decimal` values. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1596` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: Weighted interpolating quantiles still route decimals through Float64
signal.text: ### Describe what's wrong **`quantileInterpolatedWeighted`, `quantileExactWeightedInterpolated` and their plural forms return values outside the input range for `Decimal*`/`DateTime64` inputs near the type limits. `quantileInterpolatedWeighted(x, 1)` over `Decimal(18,0)` values 999999999999999998/999999999999999999 returns 1000000000000000000 — not in the data and not representable in `Decimal(18,0)`. On `Decimal128` even the level-0 and level-1 quantiles return 99999999999999997752612184630461283328, which is below the minimum of the data.** - **Root cause:** Both siblings widen the decimal native value to `Float64` before interpolating and cast back. `Int64`/`Int128`/`Int256` values near their limits collapse onto the same `Float64` and the cast back lands outside the source range — the exact defect this PR removed from `QuantileReservoirSampler::get` (AggregateFunctionQuantile.cpp:59) by adding `ReservoirSampler::quantileInterpolatedDecimal`. The `NO_SANITIZE_UNDEFINED` on `interpolate` suppresses the sanitizer report but not the wrong value. <details> <summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary> **Why we believe this is a bug:** `createAggregateFunctionQuantile` dispatches `Decimal32/64/128/256` and `DateTime64` (AggregateFunctionQuantileInterpolatedWeighted.cpp:343-347, AggregateFunctionQuantileExactWeighted.cpp:423-427) -> `QuantileInterpolatedWeighted::getImpl`/`getManyImpl` -> `interpolate` (:318), and `QuantileExactWeighted::getInterpolatedImpl`/`getManyInterpolatedImpl` (:271, :294) -> `static_cast<typename Value::NativeType>(Float64)`. **Affected locations:** - [`src/AggregateFunctions/AggregateFunctionQuantileInterpolatedWeighted.cpp:318`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8b9c617362bf7/src/AggregateFunctions/AggregateFunctionQuantileInterpolatedWeighted.cpp#L318) — `interpolate` widens `lower_value`/`value_diff` to `Float64` and casts the result back to `UnderlyingType` - [`src/AggregateFunctions/AggregateFunctionQuantileExactWeighted.cpp:271`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8b9c617362bf7/src/AggregateFunctions/AggregateFunctionQuantileExactWeighted.cpp#L271) — `getInterpolatedImpl`: `Value(static_cast<typename Value::NativeType>(res))` where `res` is the `Float64` interpolation - [`src/AggregateFunctions/AggregateFunctionQuantileExactWeighted.cpp:294`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8b9c617362bf7/src/AggregateFunctions/AggregateFunctionQuantileExactWeighted.cpp#L294) — same cast in `getManyInterpolatedImpl`, used by `quantilesExactWeightedInterpolated` **Impact:** Wrong quantile values for `Decimal64`/`Decimal128`/`Decimal256`/`DateTime64` columns holding values near the type limits. The returned value can exceed the declared precision of the result type (`1000000000000000000` in a `Decimal(18,0)` result, a 77-digit value in a `Decimal(76,0)` result), which then propagates into arithmetic and comparisons downstream. </details> ### Does it reproduce on most recent release? Yes — confirmed on current `master` (commit `8b9c617362bf7`). ### How to reproduce [▶ Run on ClickHouse Fiddle](https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/21f04efc-97c9-4de3-a820-cca86b516bcd) <details> <summary>Reproducer</summary> ```sql -- Test: weighted interpolating quantiles of decimal-backed values near the type limits must stay -- inside the input range instead of collapsing through Float64. SELECT quantileInterpolatedWeighted(x, 1), quantileExactWeightedInterpolated(x, 1) FROM (SELECT toDecimal64(if(number % 2 = 0, '999999999999999999', '999999999999999998'), 0) AS x FROM numbers(100)); SELECT quantilesInterpolatedWeighted(0, 0.5, 1)(x, 1), quantilesExactWeightedInterpolated(0, 0.5, 1)(x, 1) FROM (SELECT toDecimal128(if(number % 2 = 0, '99999999999999999999999999999999999999', '99999999999999999999999999999999999998'), 0) AS x FROM numbers(100)); SELECT quantileInterpolatedWeighted(x, 1), quantileExactWeightedInterpolated(x, 1) FROM (SELECT fromUnixTimestamp64Nano(if(number % 2 = 0, 9223372036854775807, 9223372036854775806), 'UTC') AS x FROM numbers(100)); ``` </details> ### Expected behavior ``` 999999999999999998 999999999999999998 [99999999999999999999999999999999999998,99999999999999999999999999999999999998,99999999999999999999999999999999999999] [99999999999999999999999999999999999998,99999999999999999999999999999999999998,99999999999999999999999999999999999999] 2262-04-11 23:47:16.854775806 2262-04-11 23:47:16.854775806 ``` ### Error message and/or stacktrace ``` 1000000000000000000 1000000000000000000 [99999999999999997752612184630461283328,99999999999999997752612184630461283328,99999999999999997752612184630461283328] [99999999999999997752612184630461283328,99999999999999997752612184630461283328,99999999999999997752612184630461283328] 2262-04-11 23:47:16.854775807 2262-04-11 23:47:16.854775807 ``` <details> <summary>Suggested fix</summary> Give both siblings the same exact-domain interpolation the PR added for the reservoir path: interpolate on the native integer type (or `cpp_int`) instead of `Float64`. For `QuantileExactWeighted` that means an `is_decimal` overload of `quantileInterpolated` returning `UnderlyingType`; for `QuantileInterpolatedWeighted`, an exact-rational version of `interpolate`. </details> <details> <summary>Additional context</summary> **Open risks:** - `quantileExactWeightedInterpolated`'s cast at :271/:294 is not annotated `NO_SANITIZE_UNDEFINED` (only the inner `quantileInterpolated` at :362 is), so for `DateTime64` near `Int64` max the cast itself is UB and should also trip UBSan builds — the same signal that found the original bug. Found during automated review of [PR #114919](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114919). Severity P2 · Finding `h_pr114919_001` </details> cc @alexey-milovidov (from #114919)
