signal.title: Make stress-test server crashes diagnosable: name the signal and enable core dumps
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109951 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Stress and upgrade CI jobs now name the fatal signal when the server is terminated (instead of the opaque "Unknown error") and let the server write a core dump, so the next such crash is attributable and debuggable. ### Description Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109951 A `Stress test (arm_asan_ubsan, s3)` run left the server child dead with signal 11 but no actionable evidence: no `BaseDaemon` fault stack, no sanitizer report, no core dump, nothing in `dmesg`. The only trace was one watchdog line, and CI reported it as the opaque `Unknown error`: ``` <Fatal> Application: Child process was terminated by signal 11. ``` Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109951&sha=5ec2b2ed5b6cf1fc8ede04ce6756bebc1e281cda&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_asan_ubsan%2C%20s3%29 Three independent diagnostics gaps caused this, and this PR fixes all of them. The underlying SIGSEGV itself is not addressed: with no stack, no core, and no reproducer it cannot be located, and I am not speculating an engine fix without evidence. The point of this change is that the next occurrence carries the signal number and a core dump. 1. `FuzzerLogParser.parse_failure` only matched the fault-handler stack (`Received signal`, absent here) or the literal signal `9`, so a `signal 11` watchdog line matched nothing and fell through to `Unknown error`. The Signal pattern now matches `Child process was terminated by signal N` for any `N`, anchored to the watchdog's `<Fatal> Application: ` record. The anchor keeps a live-server `ShellCommand` exception (`<Error> ... Child process was terminated by signal N`, server still alive) from being misattributed as the server dying, and also fixes that pre-existing false positive of the old unanchored pattern. 2. No core is ever produced by stress/upgrade jobs. The server starts via `clickhouse start`, i.e. through `sudo`, and `sudo` clamps `RLIMIT_CORE` to `0/0` for its child, so the server's own startup raise to `core_dump.size_limit` fails (the recurring `Cannot set max size of core file` warning) and the kernel writes nothing. A `Defaults rlimit_core="0,infinity"` sudoers drop-in in the stress-test image gives the sudo child `soft=0`, `hard=unlimited`: only the server's own startup raise takes effect, every other sudo helper keeps `soft=0` and still dumps nothing. The upgrade job uses the same image and `start_server`, so it is covered too. AST-fuzzer and BuzzHouse jobs start the server without `sudo`, so they are unaffected and their already-working core pipeline is untouched. 3. Even with the sudoers drop-in, the core destination was configured for only one of the server starts. `<core_path>/cores</core_path>` (`/cores` is the sole host-mounted directory that the job collects) was written by `configure_limits`, which the stress runner calls only just before its late-phase restart and the upgrade runner never calls at all, so upgrade-job crashes and early stress-phase crashes wrote their core into the container-local default `/var/lib/clickhouse/cores` and lost it with the container. The `core_path` config is now written by `configure` itself, which every server start in both runners goes through, so a crash at any start lands its core in the collected `/cores`. `start_server` additionally logs the effective `Max core file size` of the started server, so every stress/upgrade job now carries per-run proof that the core limit is raisable. `parse_failure` only names an already-decided failure, so no new failures are introduced anywhere, and the independent OOM allowance (a signal-9 death is still allowed as OOM) is unchanged. The 4 parser tests this PR added are dropped: master removed `ci/tests/test_log_parser.py` in 3a69545dc040 and did not restore it. All 4 were re-verified against this branch before dropping them.

signal.title: Fix server crash in text index direct read when a filter uses a derived expression
signal.text: Only affects `enable_analyzer = 0`. <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111467 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a server abort in the text index direct-read optimization when a text-search predicate is applied to a derived expression - an `ALIAS` column, or an index expression such as `mapValues(attributes)` - and the rewrite happens in the `WHERE` filter step. The optimization tried to remove a filter-expression input name that is not a physical read column, which aborted the server. Only affects `enable_analyzer = 0`. ### Description Found by the AST fuzzer (`AST fuzzer (amd_debug)`), STID 4792-5e4c. First report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109524&sha=5a447113dcb18b89e0b150c7dc4efb65ff114342&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%29 (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109524). Trunk bug, not caused by any single pull request: it has now hit 11 unrelated pull requests plus master since 2026-07-02. Most recent, on master: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=d59f2be34ed39b45665de8c5afe3b333239befeb&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%29 `ReadFromMergeTree::createReadTasksForTextIndex` removes the filter inputs that the text-search rewrite no longer needs from the reading step's read set: ```cpp for (const auto & column_name : removed_columns) { auto it = std::ranges::find(all_column_names, column_name); all_column_names.erase(it); // UB when it == end() } ``` `removed_columns` comes from the filter DAG (`TextIndexDAGReplacer::replace`): it is the set of DAG inputs required before the rewrite minus those still required after. Those names live in the filter-expression namespace and can be derived nodes such as `mapValues(attributes)`, or the expression behind an `ALIAS` column. `all_column_names` is the reading step's physical read set and holds only source columns (e.g. `attributes`, `arr`). So a derived name is not found, `std::ranges::find` returns `end()`, and `erase(end())` is undefined behavior. It aborts in debug and in release builds (release uses libc++ `_LIBCPP_HARDENING_MODE_FAST`, which keeps the `vector::erase` valid-iterator check active). The loop only needs to prune columns that are actually in the read set; a removed filter input that was never a physical read column has nothing to prune. The fix guards the erase, matching the idiom already used for every other `all_column_names` mutation in this file. It cannot change behaviour for any query that did not previously abort: when the name is found, the code path is unchanged. What the abort needs is for the text-search rewrite to land in the `WHERE` `FilterStep` rather than in `PREWHERE`, because only there is the derived expression a DAG input. Both reproducers below arrange that, in two different ways: - a `toLowCardinality` needle in `PREWHERE`, which the direct read declines, so `processAndOptimizeTextIndexFunctions` falls through to the `FilterStep` DAG - this needs no `Merge` and no `Distributed` table; - reading through `Merge` -> `Distributed` -> `MergeTree`, where `ReadFromMerge` pushes the filter into the child plan. It requires `enable_analyzer = 0`; the analyzer does not name that filter input after the expression. Reproducer 1 - plain `MergeTree`, text index on an expression (aborts on master): ```sql SET allow_experimental_full_text_index = 1, enable_full_text_index = 1; SET query_plan_direct_read_from_text_index = 1, enable_analyzer = 0; CREATE TABLE t (id UInt64, attributes Map(String, String), INDEX idx_vals mapValues(attributes) TYPE text(tokenizer = 'array') GRANULARITY 1) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id; INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, {'ip':'192.168.1.1'}); SELECT id FROM t PREWHERE has(mapValues(attributes), toLowCardinality('zzz')) WHERE has(mapValues(attributes), '192.168.1.1'); ``` Reproducer 2 - `Merge` -> `Distributed` -> `MergeTree` (aborts on master): ```sql SET allow_experimental_full_text_index = 1, enable_full_text_index = 1; CREATE TABLE logs (ts DateTime, attributes Map(String, String), INDEX attributes_vals_idx mapValues(attributes) TYPE text(tokenizer = 'array') GRANULARITY 1) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY ts; INSERT INTO logs VALUES (1, {'ip':'192.168.1.1'}); CREATE TABLE logs_dist AS logs ENGINE = Distributed(test_shard_localhost, currentDatabase(), logs); CREATE TABLE logs_merge AS logs ENGINE = Merge(currentDatabase(), '^logs_dist$'); SELECT count() FROM logs_merge PREWHERE hasAnyTokens(mapValues(attributes), toLowCardinality('0')) WHERE has(mapValues(attributes), '192.168.1.1') SETTINGS query_plan_direct_read_from_text_index = 1, enable_analyzer = 0; ``` The fuzzed query from the master report is the first shape over an `ALIAS` column: the table from `04141_text_index_alias_lambda_with_constants`, where `arr_keyword` is `arrayMap(select -> concat('-', select), arr)` with a text index on it. The server logged the derived name it then failed to erase: ``` processAndOptimizeTextIndexFunctions: Added: [__text_index_idx_kw_text_has_b747...], Removed: [arrayMap(lambda(tuple(select), concat('-', select)), arr)] ``` Both shapes are covered by tests, and both assert results rather than only non-crashing. An `EXPLAIN actions` oracle in each test keeps the fix from silently disabling the optimization: the synthetic `__text_index_*` column must be present in the plan with `query_plan_direct_read_from_text_index = 1` and absent with `0`. No related open issue found. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=111844&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/111844](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F111844+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix correlated scalar count()/uniqExact() returning NULL instead of 0 for an empty group
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111615 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a correlated scalar subquery with `count()` or `uniqExact()` returning `NULL` instead of `0` when the correlated group is empty for an outer row (e.g. `SELECT o.k, (SELECT count() FROM t AS i WHERE i.k = o.k AND i.flag = 1) FROM t AS o`). Aggregates whose value over an empty input is `NULL` (`sum`, `min`, `max`, `avg`) are unchanged. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111615 Decorrelation rewrites a correlated scalar aggregate subquery into an aggregation grouped by the correlated key. An outer row whose correlated group is empty then has no matching group, so the decorrelation outer join fills the aggregate column with `NULL`. That is correct for aggregates whose value over an empty input is `NULL` (a scalar subquery over zero rows is `NULL`, and `QueryNode::getResultType` deliberately forces the result `Nullable` so `WHERE outer > (SELECT sum(...))` filters empty groups). But `count()`/`uniqExact()` always produce a non-`NULL` value over an empty input (`0`), so the join `NULL` is wrong. Fix: after the decorrelation join, for exactly the restorable case, replace the unmatched-row `NULL` with the aggregate's empty-input value via `ifNull(result, 0)`. The restorable case is a bare aggregate projection whose `returns_default_when_only_null` property is set (`count`, `uniqExact`, ...), with no `GROUP BY`/`HAVING`/`DISTINCT`/`LIMIT`/`OFFSET` and `empty_result_for_aggregation_by_empty_set = 0` (any of which can make the empty aggregate result legitimately absent, i.e. `NULL`). Such aggregates never produce `NULL` over a non-empty group, so a post-join `NULL` is unambiguously an empty group. The declared `Nullable(T)` result type is preserved. New-analyzer only. Not addressed here (out of scope, unchanged behavior): `sum`/`min`/`max`/`avg` over an empty group stay `NULL`; a wrapped projection such as `count() + 100` stays `NULL`; `count(nullable_col)` (rewritten to `sum(NOT col.null)`) stays `NULL`. A separate pre-existing decorrelation limitation is also unchanged: the internal identity join uses plain equality, so a null-safe correlated match (`IS NOT DISTINCT FROM`) over a `NULL` key does not match its group (`sum`/`EXISTS` are affected too); for that narrow case the restored `count` reports `0` rather than the real count. cc @novikd @PedroTadim.

signal.title: Fix stale rows in a normal projection after lightweight DELETE in rebuild mode
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111791 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a bug where a lightweight `DELETE` with `lightweight_mutation_projection_mode = 'rebuild'` did not remove the deleted rows from a normal (non-aggregate) `PROJECTION` that has no `WHERE` clause. A query served by such a projection (for example an `ORDER BY` matching the projection sort key) could return already-deleted rows. ### Description A normal projection with no `WHERE` is calculated at `QueryProcessingStage::FetchColumns`, which stops before the `WHERE` step. The rebuild path injected `WHERE _row_exists = 1` into the projection query to drop the lightweight-deleted rows, but at `FetchColumns` that filter was never applied, so the projection was rebuilt from all rows including the deleted ones. The deletion mask is a data-level filter that is independent of the projection query, so for the `FetchColumns` path the deleted rows are now dropped from the input block directly (the `_part_offset` column, when present, is filtered by the same mask so surviving rows keep their original parent offsets). This keeps `FetchColumns` (the projection part is sorted afterwards by `writeTempProjectionPart`, so no `ORDER BY` is needed during calculation). Filtered and aggregate projections already ran at `WithMergeableState` and applied the injected filter correctly; that path is unchanged.

signal.title: Fix NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK for a correlated subquery referencing an outer column via a subcolumn function
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111729 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK` when a correlated subquery (with `allow_experimental_correlated_subqueries = 1`) references an outer column through a function that reads a subcolumn, such as `tupleElement(o.p, 1)` / `o.p.1`, `variantElement(o.v, 'x')`, or `o.m['key']`. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111729 `FunctionToSubcolumnsPass` rewrites `tupleElement(col, ...)` (and `variantElement`, Map `arrayElement`) into a direct subcolumn read. When such a function reads an *outer* column inside a correlated subquery, the correlated-columns metadata has already been fixed during analysis to reference the whole column (e.g. the Tuple `p`), so after the rewrite it points at a column (`p`) that the decorrelated plan no longer produces (it now needs the subcolumn `p.a`), and decorrelation fails with `NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK`. The identifier form `o.p.a` works because it resolves straight to the subcolumn during analysis, so its correlated entry already matches. Fix: in `FunctionToSubcolumnsVisitorSecondPass`, do not rewrite a function whose underlying column is a correlated reference relative to the current scope. A per-scope stack tracks the sources registered as correlated by each enclosing query/union, so only the outer correlated column is skipped; the same table's other, non-correlated columns and the inner table's columns are still optimized. This mirrors the pass's existing `outer_joined_tables` guard.

signal.title: Fix CI crash reporter naming logical errors after query-echoed text
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108735 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Related: #108735 The functional/stress crash reporter (`FuzzerLogParser` in `ci/jobs/scripts/log_parser.py`, invoked by `ClickHouseProc.check_fatal_messages_in_logs`) names a failure by running `rg -o 'Logical error.*'` over the whole `clickhouse-server.log` and taking the first match. `executeQuery` logs the full query text (SQL comments included) into the server log, and the signal handler embeds the crashing query inside a `<Fatal>` record. So when a job hits a real logical-error crash, the reporter can pick up a *different* test's comment that merely quotes `Logical error '...'` and use it as the failure name, while the STID and stack come from the actual crash. This mislabels unrelated crashes and pollutes failure tracking. Concrete example (MasterCI, `Stateless tests (amd_llvm_coverage, ParallelReplicas, s3 storage, parallel)`): the real crash was `<Fatal> : Logical error: 'Got read request from replica 1 for unknown stream ...'` (`ParallelReplicasReadingCoordinator`), but the reporter named it after a regression test's `!part.empty()` / `Bad cast ...` comment. This wrongly reopened an unrelated tracking task. Fix, in `log_parser.py`: - Match `Logical error` only as the message of a real formatted log record, anchored to the line prefix `^<date> <time> [ tid ] {query_id} <Fatal> [logger]: Logical error: ...`. A query echo, a comment continuation line, and query text embedded mid-line on a `<Fatal>` signal record all fail that anchor. The anchor also requires the `<Fatal>` level and the `Logical error:` colon, so a benign `<Warning> ...: Logical error. Not all polled messages ...` is not selected. Genuine logical errors are always emitted via `LOG_FATAL` (`abortOnFailedAssertion`), so nothing real is missed. The other patterns (sanitizer, assertion, segfault, signal, memory) are byte-for-byte unchanged. - `get_failed_query()` reuses the query id of the selected fatal record instead of re-grepping the log from the top, so the reported failing query matches the crash. An explicitly empty id (background exception with no query) reports no query rather than an unrelated one; the inline `Inconsistent AST formatting` query (which aborts before an `executeQuery` record is logged) is still extracted, scoped to the selected record; and the query id is matched inside its `{...}` delimiters and escaped, so `q2` no longer also matches `{q20}` and a metacharacter id is literal. Added regression tests in `ci/tests/test_log_parser.py`; existing tests unchanged.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Fix index granularity collapsing to 1 when mutating an adaptive part on a table with index_granularity_bytes = 0
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111626 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes index granularity collapsing to one mark per row (large mark and primary-index bloat) when a row-changing mutation rewrites an adaptive data part that lives on a table with `index_granularity_bytes = 0`. ### Description An adaptive part (a `Wide` part with `.mrk2` marks, or a `Compact` part) can end up on a table whose `index_granularity_bytes = 0` (non-adaptive) via `RESTORE ... AS ... FROM ... SETTINGS allow_different_table_def = 1`. A row-changing mutation (`ALTER ... DELETE`, TTL, or any mutation that rewrites all columns) then rewrites the part and inherits the source part's adaptive `index_granularity_info`, so the writer runs with `can_use_adaptive = true` while the table setting `index_granularity_bytes = 0`. In that state `computeIndexGranularity` reached the byte-sizing branch and computed `index_granularity_bytes / size_of_row = 0 / N = 0`, which was then clamped to 1, producing one mark per row (thousands-fold mark and primary-index bloat). Data stayed correct, so correct-result tests did not catch it. Fix: in the adaptive branch, when `index_granularity_bytes = 0` (byte-based sizing disabled) use the fixed row granularity (`index_granularity`) instead of dividing by a zero byte budget. This enforces the invariant the function already documented. The normal adaptive path (`index_granularity_bytes > 0`) and the non-adaptive path are unchanged. Reproducer (before the fix the last query returns 10000 marks for 9999 rows; after, 3): ```sql CREATE TABLE src (k UInt64, s String) ORDER BY k SETTINGS min_bytes_for_wide_part = 0, min_rows_for_wide_part = 0, index_granularity = 8192; INSERT INTO src SELECT number, toString(number) FROM numbers(10000); BACKUP TABLE src TO Disk('backups', 'b'); CREATE TABLE dst (k UInt64, s String) ORDER BY k SETTINGS index_granularity_bytes = 0; RESTORE TABLE src AS dst FROM Disk('backups', 'b') SETTINGS allow_different_table_def = 1; ALTER TABLE dst DELETE WHERE k = 0 SETTINGS mutations_sync = 2; SELECT part_type, rows, marks FROM system.parts WHERE table = 'dst' AND active; ``` Same latent bug affects the `Compact`-part variant reachable via #111626; that PR's fix consumes the same correction.

signal.title: Fix use-of-uninitialized-value in direct JOIN over a MergeTree table read with STREAM
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111492 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Improves the stability of experimental `STREAM` queries that use a `direct` join against a `MergeTree` table after `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN`. ### Description Found by the AST fuzzer under MSan on PR #111492 (unrelated to that PR's changes). The MSan report itself lost its stack (nested error while writing), so the crashing query was recovered from the fuzzer log: ```sql SELECT l.id, r.value, r.new_col FROM t_left AS l INNER JOIN t_right AS r STREAM ON l.id = r.id ``` with `join_algorithm = 'direct'`, `enable_analyzer = 1`, `enable_streaming_queries = 1`, where `r.new_col` was added by `ALTER TABLE t_right ADD COLUMN new_col String DEFAULT 'default_value'`. Root cause: `ReadFromMergeTree::initializePipeline` strips data parts from the storage snapshot (for the `enable_remove_parts_from_snapshot_optimization` / streaming path) by mutating `storage_snapshot->data` in place. `ReadFromMergeTree::clone()` copies the `storage_snapshot` shared pointer, so the original lookup plan and every clone share one `StorageSnapshot`. A `direct` JOIN rebuilds its lookup pipeline for each probe block (and the `STREAM` source rebuilds its sub-pipeline repeatedly), so one pipeline build replaced and destroyed a `SnapshotData` whose `mutations_snapshot` was still read by an overlapping build, giving MSan a use-of-uninitialized-value. Fix: rebind this step's own `storage_snapshot` to a private clone via `StorageSnapshot::clone(...)` instead of mutating the shared snapshot in place. The clone keeps the same storage and metadata, only the stripped `Data` is private, so no build observes another build's destroyed `SnapshotData`. CI report (MSan, `AST fuzzer (amd_msan)`): https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=111492&sha=1f9f9e0c14bca355fd9cf558efcb722aca37f1b9&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_msan%29 Reproduced locally on an MSan build (crash rate about 1 in 8 runs); with the fix it no longer reproduces (0 crashes over many runs) and results are unchanged for plain, `LowCardinality`, and `Nullable` added columns. Added a regression test that spawns the streaming direct-join query repeatedly and asserts the server stays alive.

signal.title: Recover an intact part from an empty columns.txt instead of losing it
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111373 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111414 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed data loss where a MergeTree part with an empty (zero-byte) `columns.txt` was detached as broken on load, discarding all of its rows. An empty `columns.txt` is now treated like a missing one: for wide parts the column list is rebuilt from the part's own metadata, matching the existing behavior for an absent file. ### Description `IMergeTreeDataPart::writeMetadata` rewrites `columns.txt` in place (no atomic rename, no fsync). An interrupted rewrite (crash, power loss, `ENOSPC` between truncate and write) can leave a zero-byte `columns.txt` in an already-committed part directory. On load, an absent `columns.txt` already self-heals: for a wide part the else-branch rebuilds the column list from the table metadata and rewrites the file. But an empty `columns.txt` was read anyway, and `NamesAndTypesList::readText` starts with `assertString("columns format version: 1\n", buf)`, which throws `CANNOT_PARSE_INPUT_ASSERTION_FAILED` on the empty stream. The otherwise-intact part is then detached as broken and every row is lost. An empty file is strictly less broken than a missing one, so bricking the part for it is illogical. This routes an empty `columns.txt` through the same rebuild path as a missing one. Emptiness is decided via `IMergeTreeDataPart::readFile`, which forces `pread`, so a zero-byte file reports `eof` cleanly instead of faulting under a randomized mmap read method. Compact and patch parts still require `columns.txt` (they cannot rebuild it), so their behavior is unchanged. The rebuild reconstructs the persistent virtual columns the part physically carries (`_row_exists`, `_block_number`, `_block_offset`), not only `getAllPhysical()`. Dropping `_row_exists` would silently discard a lightweight-delete mask (deleted rows would reappear); dropping any of them would fail `columns_substreams.txt` validation and detach the part. Column presence during the rebuild is taken from `columns_substreams.txt`, which records exactly the columns physically written, in order, independent of the on-disk serialization. A column's default serialization can enumerate different streams than were stored (a bucketed Map writes `m.buckets_info`, `m.0.keys`, ... instead of `m.keys`, ...), so probing the default serialization would misjudge such a column absent and drop it, turning recovery back into silent data loss and tripping `columns_substreams.txt` validation. Parts predating that file fall back to enumerating each column's own non-ephemeral streams (present only when every such stream exists), matching `MergeTreeDataPartWide::hasColumnFiles`. These gaps also affected the pre-existing missing-`columns.txt` path. Test `04545_empty_columns_txt_not_fatal` covers wide-part shapes: plain, `_block_number`/`_block_offset`, a lightweight-delete `_row_exists` mask, a `Tuple` and a `Map` (including bucketed serialization), a shared-offset Nested sibling added by `ALTER`, and recovery via the legacy stream-enumeration path when `columns_substreams.txt` is also absent. In each, truncating `columns.txt` to zero and reloading keeps the correct rows/values and persists a complete rebuilt file; a missing `columns.txt` still self-heals. Fails on `master`, passes with the fix.

signal.title: Fix non-atomic Keeper Raft state persistence that could lose term/vote after a crash
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113654 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111454 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113654 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Hardened Keeper Raft state persistence. On a local state disk, the `state` file (which stores the current `term` and `voted_for`) and its backup are now made durable before the file they protect is overwritten. Only a backup that reads back and verifies is written, and neither file is read through a cache that could return an earlier term. A node that recovers from the backup now also syncs it before acting on its term. ### Description #111454 is fixed on master by #113654, the first commit of this branch. What remains is the hardening the review of that window turned up, all on the same two files. `save_state`: the backup is written with an explicit `sync()` rather than `IDisk::copyFile`, which only finalizes, so it is durable before the live file is truncated. A live file that does not read back and verify may no longer become the backup, so a torn file cannot overwrite a still-valid `state-OLD`. Directory entries are synced too, best effort: `LocalDirectorySyncGuard` logs a failed `fdatasync` instead of throwing, so a lost dentry can still take a synced file with it. `read_state`: a valid state file is synced before its term is returned, since parsing only shows the bytes are complete, not that they reached the disk. That covers the backup-only branch too, as a backup written by the previous implementation was never synced. A file failing its checksum is kept rather than deleted, so a restart cannot silently end up with no state. Neither file is read through a read cache: both are rewritten in place at fixed paths and the caches key by path, so a cached read could copy an old term into `state-OLD`, the double vote this branch exists to prevent. Scope: the file syncs only bite on a local state disk. `s3` and `s3_plain` are `DiskObjectStorage`, where `syncExistingFile` returns early on `isRemote()` and `getDirectorySyncGuard` has no override, so the forgotten-term window stays open there; ordering and verification still apply. `save_state` on master has no syncs at all, so this is not a regression. Five gtests cover the ordering, the backup-only recovery, a partial write, a retry and a read failure. Each assertion was checked by removing the line it guards.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Fix logical error !raw_type->isNullable() in AND-compare chain optimization
signal.text: Keep NULL-constant and nullable-result comparisons out of AND-compare pruning <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111292 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111292 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Found by the AST fuzzer: `AST fuzzer (amd_debug, targeted)` [CI report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=111535&sha=5d41a4d4d9fe7efc9a932917ac11ac20f376ea85&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29) and `Stress test (amd_asan_ubsan)`, `Logical error: '!rhs_literal->getValue().isNull()'` (STID 2508-5318 / 2508-5717). The assertion aborts in debug/sanitizer builds; in release builds the `chassert` is a no-op, so this is a CI/sanitizer fix. This extends the original fix to two more paths in the same `Nothing`-collapsed AND, reached by fuzzing the added test: 1. A comparison whose constant side is itself NULL-valued (e.g. `expr = NULL`) hit `chassert(!literal->getValue().isNull())` in the classification loop of `tryOptimizeAndCompareNotEqualsChain`. A NULL-valued constant has no comparable value, so it is no longer treated as the constant side and the operand is kept as-is, mirroring the sibling `tryOptimizeOrEqualsChain`. 2. The `addComparisonFilter` pruning guard tested only the raw operand type via `isNullable()`, which is false for `LowCardinality(Nullable(T))` (nested nullability) and for the NULL-capable carriers `Dynamic` / `Variant`, whose comparison result is still `Nullable(UInt8)`. Those slipped past the guard and folded a contradictory chain, changing the handled exception from `ILLEGAL_COLUMN` to `TYPE_MISMATCH` depending on `optimize_redundant_comparisons`. The guard now tests the comparison node's own result type, which is the robust signal and covers all of `Nullable` / `LowCardinality(Nullable)` / `Dynamic` / `Variant`; both entry functions share `addComparisonFilter`. Verified the error is identical across `optimize_redundant_comparisons` / `optimize_and_compare_chain` for the whole wrapper matrix, non-nullable `Int32` / `LowCardinality(Int32)` are unchanged, and plain-column pruning still fires.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Fix JIT logical error 'Invalid cast from Nothing to native type'
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111485 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111485 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a logical error `Invalid cast from Nothing to native type` (an abort in debug/sanitizer builds) when `compile_expressions = 1` compiled an expression with a `Nullable(Nothing)` operand, e.g. `and(Nullable(Nothing), <native comparison>)`. ### Description `isCompilableFunction` only checked the function's declared argument types. An overload resolver can normalize a degenerate operand (an `onlyNull` argument) to a native declared type (`Nullable(UInt8)`) while the child node keeps its real result type `Nullable(Nothing)`. That non-compilable child is materialized as a JIT input carrying its real type, so `compileFunction` later called `toNativeType(Nothing)` and raised the logical error. The gate now also requires each non-skipped child node's actual result type to be native, bailing the whole expression to the interpreter. It is a type-level check in the shared gate, so it covers every function that could receive such an operand, not just `and`.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Make TRUNCATE / DROP PARTITION / DROP PART durable across power loss
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111348 --> Related: #111348 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `TRUNCATE TABLE`, `ALTER TABLE ... DROP PARTITION` and `ALTER TABLE ... DROP PART` on `MergeTree` tables on local disks silently reverting after a power loss with default settings. These operations commit an empty covering part and remove the covered parts before acknowledging, but the covering part (the operation's only on-disk commit record) was not fsynced unless `fsync_after_insert`/`fsync_part_directory` were enabled, so a power loss in the journal window could resurrect the deleted data. The covering part and the parent table directory are now synced before the operation is acknowledged. ### Description `StorageMergeTree::truncate`, `dropPartition` and `dropPart` commit one empty covering part per visible part (`initCoverageWithNewEmptyParts` -> `createEmptyPart` -> `renameAndCommitEmptyParts`) and then unlink the covered parts synchronously before the ack. The covering part is the only on-disk record of the operation, yet its contents, its directory and the commit rename were all synced only under the default-off `fsync_after_insert`/`fsync_part_directory`. So at default settings the whole operation is a single uncommitted ext4 journal transaction: a power loss reverts it and the acked-deleted rows come back (reproduced with a dm-flakey power cut in #111348: `TRUNCATE` 3/3, `DROP PARTITION`/`DROP PART` likewise). Fix: for these three operations, sync the covering part's contents and its directory (a new `force_sync` argument to `createEmptyPart`, independent of the default-off settings), then sync the parent table directory whose entry the rename changed, after the commit succeeds and before the covered parts are unlinked. Success-only syncing keeps a rolled-back DDL from durably installing partial covering parts. `DETACH PARTITION`/`DETACH PART` are excluded: their detached clone is not synced here, so making only the removal durable could lose the detached copy. Other `createEmptyPart` callers are unchanged (`force_sync` defaults to false). Scope: local disks. `DiskObjectStorage` inherits the `nullptr` `getDirectorySyncGuard` default (`IDisk.cpp:212`), so both guards are a no-op there, and its covering part commits through local metadata files that are written with `finalize()` and never fsynced (`MetadataStorageFromDiskTransactionOperations.cpp:107`). Separate mechanism, not addressed here. Test: `04623_truncate_drop_partition_covering_part_fsync` asserts, at default settings, the exact `DirectorySync` count per operation plus correct row visibility. It fails on master and passes with this change. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=111488&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/111488](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F111488+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Make Keeper cross-disk snapshot/changelog moves durable
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111339 --> Related: #111339 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a durability gap when Keeper relocates a snapshot or changelog file between configured disks (multi-disk setups, e.g. `latest_snapshot_storage_disk` plus a main disk). The cross-disk move now fsyncs the copied file content and the affected directory entries before dropping the completion marker and removing the source, so a power loss during the move can no longer leave a snapshot or changelog that looks complete but is not on stable storage. ### Description Keeper moves snapshot and changelog files across disks through the shared `moveFileBetweenDisks` helper (`src/Coordination/KeeperCommon.cpp`). Crash safety there relies on a `tmp_` marker: on restart a target with a leftover marker is deleted as an incomplete copy, and a target with no marker is accepted as complete. None of the move's filesystem operations were made durable: - `IDisk::copyFile` only `finalize()`s the target buffer, never `sync()`, so copied content can remain in the page cache. - The marker creation, marker removal, and source removal are directory-entry changes that a file fsync does not persist. On power loss the directory transaction removing the source and the marker can commit while the target's data blocks are lost. The next constructor then sees a marker-less target and accepts it as complete, corrupting the snapshot/changelog (or losing it entirely if the source was already removed). This is the cross-disk-move sibling of #111339 (the snapshot write path). Fix, in `moveFileBetweenDisks`: - fsync the marker's directory after creating the marker (its presence is durable before the copy starts); - copy with a new `IDisk::copyFile(..., sync = true)` so the content is fsynced; - fsync the marker directory and the target directory after removing the marker, before publishing; - fsync the source directory after removing the source. Directory fsyncs use `getDirectorySyncGuard`, a no-op on non-local disks; remote object storage is durable once its copy transaction commits. The new `copyFile` `sync` parameter defaults to `false`, so all existing callers are unchanged. Covered by a unit test (`KeeperMoveFileBetweenDisksTest.CrossDiskMoveIsDurable`) that fails without the fix and passes with it.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Fall back to hash for correlated-subquery decorrelation joins
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111207 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111075 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` error ("Can't execute any of specified algorithms for specified strictness/kind and right storage type") for correlated `EXISTS`/`NOT EXISTS` subqueries, and for `IN`/`NOT IN` subqueries under `rewrite_in_to_join`, when `join_algorithm` is `full_sorting_merge`, `partial_merge` or `direct`. Such subqueries decorrelate into an internal `ANY` join (and may be rewritten to `SEMI`/`ANTI`) that those algorithms cannot execute, so a query that ran with optimizations disabled would throw. The internal join now stays runnable regardless of `join_algorithm`. ### Description Correlated subquery decorrelation builds an internal join with `ANY` strictness and kind `correlated_subqueries_default_join_kind` (`RIGHT` by default). `full_sorting_merge`, `partial_merge` and `direct` cannot execute every such combination and have no fallback, and the `query_plan_convert_any_join_to_semi_or_anti_join` optimization may further rewrite the join into `SEMI`/`ANTI`. Because this internal join is an implementation detail, the user cannot pick a runnable algorithm for it, so the query failed with `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`. Two coordinated changes keep it runnable without changing any already-runnable plan: - `buildLogicalJoin` adds a hash fallback to the internal join, but only when no already-enabled algorithm can execute the join in its `ANY` shape. Adding hash unconditionally made an otherwise `full_sorting_merge`-only join runtime-filter-eligible, and the runtime-filter pass then dropped `full_sorting_merge`, silently demoting a spill-capable merge plan to an in-memory hash build under the default `enable_join_runtime_filters`. Gating the fallback on `ANY`-shape capability leaves such plans on merge. - `convert-any-join-to-semi-or-anti` only rewrites `ANY` to `SEMI`/`ANTI` when an enabled algorithm can execute the result; otherwise it keeps the runnable `ANY` join. When a capable algorithm such as `hash` is enabled the conversion is unchanged, so results are identical. The capability predicate `anyEnabledAlgorithmSupports` mirrors the per-algorithm dispatch in `PlannerJoins.cpp::tryCreateJoin` and is shared by both call sites. Supersedes #111091 (that PR fixed only the convert-pass half; this PR carries both halves so neither the `partial_merge`/`direct` `ANY` case nor the `full_sorting_merge` demotion is left uncovered). The regression test asserts, via `EXPLAIN`, that the `full_sorting_merge` plan is preserved (the join stays a full sorting merge join and is not demoted to hash), not only that results are correct.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Fix ORDER BY WITH FILL applied per shard on Distributed tables
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111212 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `ORDER BY ... WITH FILL` returning wrong results over `Distributed` tables: fill rows were generated on each shard and concatenated, so every fill row was returned once per shard and positioned per-shard instead of once over the merged result. The fill step now runs only on the initiator. ### Description For a `Distributed` non-aggregate query with `ORDER BY`, each shard is asked to process to `WithMergeableStateAfterAggregation[AndLimit]` so it can pre-sort. On the shard `isSecondStage()` is true, and the `WITH FILL` step was added unconditionally, unlike the sibling final-result-only steps (`OFFSET`, `LIMIT`, `Project names`) which are guarded by `!isToAggregationState()`. As a result `FillingStep` ran on every shard. Fix: gate the `WITH FILL` step with the same condition in both the new analyzer (`Planner.cpp`) and the old interpreter (`InterpreterSelectQuery.cpp`), so it runs only on the initiator over the merged, ordered result. Per-shard sorting is unchanged (the initiator still merge-sorts the shard streams). `distributed_group_by_no_merge=1` (shards process to `Complete`) is unaffected, since `isToAggregationState()` is false there and per-shard filling is the intended behavior.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Make on-disk SQL objects (UDFs, named collections, workloads) crash-durable
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111381 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Make on-disk SQL objects crash-durable. `CREATE`/`DROP` of user-defined functions, named collections and workload entities (`WORKLOAD`/`RESOURCE`) now fsync the parent directory after the commit rename and after the file removal (gated on `fsync_metadata`, default enabled), so an acknowledged `CREATE` no longer vanishes and an acknowledged `DROP` no longer reverts after a power loss. Also, a corrupt or torn local named-collection metadata file is now skipped and logged at startup (like user-defined functions and workload entities) instead of failing server startup. ### Description Closes: #111381 `UserDefinedSQLObjectsDiskStorage`, `NamedCollectionsMetadataStorage` (local storage) and `WorkloadEntityDiskStorage` committed a create by writing `<object>.sql.tmp` and renaming it into place, and a drop with `fs::remove`. Only the temp file content was fsynced (gated on `fsync_metadata`); the commit rename, the removal, and the first-time directory creation were never followed by a parent-directory fsync, and the drop path did not read `fsync_metadata` at all. An fsync of a file's content does not persist its directory entry, so after a power loss an acknowledged `CREATE` could disappear and an acknowledged `DROP` could revert (the object reappears at the next startup with its old definition, stale credentials or re-imposed scheduling). This wraps the commit rename, the drop unlink, and the initial directory creation in `LocalDirectorySyncGuard` (opens the parent directory with `O_DIRECTORY` and `fdatasync`s it), gated on the existing `fsync_metadata` setting. For user-defined functions and workload entities the setting is taken from the query context (the drop path now uses the previously-unused `current_context`); named collections use the global context, matching their existing content-fsync. Additionally, `NamedCollectionsMetadataStorage::getAll` only caught Keeper `ZNONODE`, so a corrupt or zero-byte local `.sql` file (which `fsync_metadata=0` can leave via delayed allocation) raised a parse error that propagated out of `NamedCollectionFactory::loadIfNot` at boot and failed server startup. It now skips and logs such a file for local storage (rethrowing for replicated storage, so ZooKeeper-backed collections are never silently dropped on transient errors), matching the behavior of the user-defined-function and workload disk storages. No setting default, on-disk format or validation change; with `fsync_metadata=0` the write behavior of user-defined functions and workload entities is unchanged. Added integration test `test_sql_objects_fsync` covering the directory fsync on create/drop for all three object families and that a corrupt local named-collection file no longer bricks startup.

signal.title: Make mutation entry lifecycle crash-durable on plain MergeTree
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111380 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a durability gap where a mutation on a plain `MergeTree` table could be lost or resurrected after a power loss. With `fsync_part_directory = 1`, the `mutation_<N>.txt` entry file's creation (rename) and its `KILL MUTATION` removal now fsync the table directory, so an acknowledged `ALTER ... DELETE`/`UPDATE` is not silently dropped and a killed mutation does not come back on restart. ### Description Closes #111380. On plain (non-replicated) `MergeTree`, `mutation_<N>.txt` is the only on-disk commit record of a mutation, and both of its lifecycle transitions were non-durable: - **Create:** `MergeTreeMutationEntry` fsyncs the entry content as `tmp_mutation_<N>.txt`, but `commit()` renamed it to `mutation_<N>.txt` without fsyncing the parent directory. A power loss could leave only the `tmp_` name, which `loadMutations` deletes at startup, silently dropping an acknowledged mutation. - **Kill:** `KILL MUTATION` removed `mutation_<N>.txt` with a bare unlink and no directory fsync. A power loss could resurrect the entry, and `loadMutations` re-loads the killed mutation. `ReplicatedMergeTree` is unaffected (mutations are Keeper transactions). Fix: gate a directory fsync behind the existing `fsync_part_directory` MergeTree setting (default off, so no behavior change by default), matching how part renames are made durable (`getDirectorySyncGuard`, as in #111375). `MergeTreeMutationEntry::commit` and `removeFile` acquire the guard before the rename/unlink. The setting is carried on the entry so the removals that compensate a durable create (orphan cleanup on a failed registration, metadata-rollback of a rename mutation) are also durable; `killMutation` applies the current setting to entries loaded from disk. The guard is a no-op on object storage. Regression test `04621_mutation_entry_fsync.sh` uses the `DirectorySync` ProfileEvent as the durability proxy (a real power loss cannot be simulated in a stateless test) and checks both directions with the setting on and off.

signal.title: Make part metadata rewrite durable to prevent data loss on power loss
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111373 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix possible data loss when a part's `checksums.txt` is repaired (recalculated and written on load, or by `CHECK TABLE`) and the server loses power afterwards. The metadata rewrite is now durable and atomic (write to a temporary file, fsync, atomically rename), and an empty `checksums.txt` is now recalculated on load instead of detaching the whole part as broken. ### Description Reported in #111373. `IMergeTreeDataPart::writeMetadata` rewrote `checksums.txt` / `columns.txt` in place with `finalize()` only, without an fsync or an atomic rename. This backs the `CHECK TABLE` checksums repair and the `checksums.txt` / `columns.txt` backfills in `loadChecksums` / `loadColumns`. On a local disk these run without an enclosing directory rename, so the write is neither atomic nor durable: after the repair is acknowledged, an unrelated durable write plus a power loss can leave a zero-byte `checksums.txt`. On the next load `loadChecksums` treated the empty file as fatal and detached the entire part as broken, losing every row of an otherwise-intact part (an absent `checksums.txt` self-heals, so the acknowledged repair made the state strictly worse). Fix: - `writeMetadata` now writes to a temporary file, fsyncs it, and atomically renames it into place (fsyncing the directory when `fsync_part_directory` is set), mirroring `VersionMetadataOnDisk::storeInfoToDataPartStorage`. The final file is never empty or partial. - `loadChecksums` treats an existing-but-empty `checksums.txt` like an absent one: it removes the empty file (and any leftover temporary file) and recalculates, which also recovers parts already left in this state. - `checkDataPart` skips temporary `*.tmp` files during its directory walk so a leftover temporary file from an interrupted rewrite cannot be checksummed and then invalidate the recalculated checksums. Reproduces deterministically on ext4/XFS (dm-flakey harness in the issue). Added a stateless regression test that truncates `checksums.txt` to zero bytes and verifies the part still loads with all rows; it fails on `master` and passes with this change.

signal.title: Fsync directory on Atomic DDL commit rename to survive power loss
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111348 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111348 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): On an `Atomic` database, the commit of `DROP`/`RENAME`/`EXCHANGE TABLE` (and the `CREATE`/`ALTER` metadata commit) is a rename of the table's `.sql` file whose parent directory was never fsync'd, so an acknowledged DDL could silently revert after a power loss (e.g. a dropped table returning with all data). The commit rename now fsyncs its parent directory when `fsync_metadata` is enabled (default `true`), the same way part commits honor `fsync_part_directory`. ### Description `DatabaseAtomic` commits a `DROP`/`RENAME`/`EXCHANGE` (and the `CREATE`/`ALTER` tmp -> `.sql`) by renaming the `.sql` metadata file via `db_disk->replaceFile`/`moveFile`/`renameExchange`. A rename only changes a directory entry, which on ext4 becomes durable when the journal commits (default `commit=5s`); the directory was never fsync'd. A power loss inside that window rolls the rename back and the acknowledged DDL undoes itself. `DROP` is the sharpest case: cleanup is deferred by `database_atomic_delay_before_drop_table_sec` (480s), so the rolled-back `.sql` finds the full `store/` and the table loads back with all data. `fsync_metadata=1` (default) only fsync'd metadata file content, never these renames. Fix (gated on `fsync_metadata`, resolved from the query context): before each commit rename, open a directory sync guard for every directory whose entry the rename changes, and let it fdatasync on scope exit. This uses `IDisk::getDirectorySyncGuard`, the same primitive the MergeTree part-commit path uses for `fsync_part_directory`; it is a no-op on disks without directory sync support (e.g. object storage). `DROP` syncs both the source (`metadata/<db>/`) and target (`metadata_dropped/`) directories, plus the disk root when `metadata_dropped` is created for the first time on a custom metadata disk. The guards are opened before the ZooKeeper commit so a rare directory-open failure cannot widen the local-vs-ZooKeeper desync window the existing `NOTE` warns about. Regression test `04545_atomic_ddl_commit_fsync.sh` asserts, via `system.query_log` `DirectorySync` ProfileEvents, that `CREATE`/`RENAME`/`EXCHANGE`/`DROP` take the directory-fsync path with `fsync_metadata=1` and take none with `fsync_metadata=0`. Verified to fail on master HEAD and pass with the fix. Part of the durability/power-loss audit family (sibling access-storage fix in #111346).

signal.title: Fsync snapshot directory in Keeper to survive power loss
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111339 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a rare Keeper data-loss window: the snapshot write path now fsyncs the snapshot directory after removing the `tmp_` marker, so a power loss can no longer drop the marker unlink while keeping the snapshot content. Previously such a crash made Keeper treat a good, fully-synced snapshot as incomplete and delete it on restart, losing acknowledged writes even with `force_sync=true`. ### Description Fixes #111339. `src/Coordination` never fsynced a directory. Each snapshot write path creates an empty `tmp_snapshot_<name>` marker, writes and fsyncs the snapshot content, then unlinks the marker. The unlink is a directory-entry change, which a file-content fsync does not make durable. On power loss inside the ext4 journal-commit window the content can persist while the marker unlink is lost. On restart the constructor treats a `snapshot_<idx>` that still has a sibling `tmp_snapshot_<idx>` as incomplete and deletes both, discarding a good snapshot; if the covering changelogs were already compacted, Keeper then aborts with `CORRUPTED_DATA`. The fix adds a `removeSnapshotMarker` helper that opens the snapshot directory's sync guard before the unlink and fsyncs it on scope exit, used at all three snapshot write sites (`writeSnapshotBufferToFile`, `finalizeSnapshotReceiveToDisk`, `writeSnapshotFile`). It is a no-op on non-local disks (`getDirectorySyncGuard` returns null), matching the existing `force_sync` + `DiskLocal` durability contract used for the changelog. The directory fsync is unconditional, matching the already-unconditional snapshot content fsync. Out of scope (one concern per PR): the constructor cleanup and cross-disk maintenance moves also unlink without a directory fsync, but those operate on already-superseded or incomplete files, so a lost unlink there is self-healing on the next restart rather than acknowledged-write data loss. Regression test `CoordinationTest.TestStorageSnapshotDirectoryFsync` (both compression variants) asserts the write path acquires a directory sync guard and leaves no `tmp_` marker behind. It fails without this change and passes with it. An end-to-end device-level power-loss reproduction (dm-flakey on the snapshot filesystem, separate from the log filesystem) reproduces the original discard.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Fsync backup files and directories when writing a backup to local disk
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111320 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `BACKUP ... TO File(...)` / `Disk(...)` now fsyncs the backup data files, the `.backup` manifest and the containing directories before reporting `BACKUP_CREATED`, so an acknowledged backup to local storage survives power loss. The guarantee covers `backups.allowed_path` and everything the backup writes below it. Controlled by the new backup setting `fsync_backup_files` (default `true`). Object-storage destinations (`S3`/`Azure`) are unaffected. ### Description Fixes #111320. `BACKUP ... TO File()/Disk()` returned `BACKUP_CREATED` without issuing any `fsync`/`fdatasync` at the destination: not the data files, not the `.backup` manifest, not the directories (there was no `fsync` anywhere in `src/Backups/`). On power loss after the acknowledgement the backup could be lost entirely or left torn, even though `BACKUP_CREATED` is what an operator relies on before dropping the source data. Only local `File()`/`Disk()` were affected; object-storage destinations were already durable. Report URL: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111320 (reproduced 3/3 with a `dm-flakey` power-loss simulation). Fix, gated on the new backup setting `fsync_backup_files` (default `true`), following the durability audit family (#68958 -> #111346, #111269 -> #111335): - Two writer hooks with a no-op default on `IBackupWriter`, overridden only by the local `File`/`Disk` writers (`S3`/`Azure`/`Memory`/`Null` inherit the no-op): `syncFileToDisk(file_name)`, called right after each data file is written in `BackupImpl::writeFile` (each call fsyncs its own file, so the concurrent write path is safe), and `syncDirectoriesToDisk()`, which fdatasyncs every directory the backup created, deepest-first. - In `BackupImpl::finalizeWriting` the `.backup` manifest (or, for archives, the archive file) is synced last, after all data files, so a persisted manifest never precedes its payload. Directory syncing runs for every writer, including the internal writers of `BACKUP ON CLUSTER` which write their own data files. Regression test `tests/queries/0_stateless/04412_backup_to_file_fsync.sh` asserts the `FileSync`/`DirectorySync` ProfileEvents of the `BACKUP` query, present with `fsync_backup_files=1` and absent with `0`; integration coverage adds the `Disk`, archive and `ON CLUSTER` internal-writer cases. Guarantee boundary, stated rather than left implicit: `backups.allowed_path` and everything written below it are synced in a loop that propagates failures. Ancestors above it are best-effort, because `fsyncBackupDirectory` needs `O_DIRECTORY` (read permission) while writing a backup only needs them searchable: measured with the area inside a `0311` directory, writing succeeds and `open(O_DIRECTORY)` on the ancestor fails `EACCES`, so throwing there would newly fail backups that work today. So if a directory above `backups.allowed_path` was itself created without being made durable, a power loss can still take the whole tree. The setting's docs row now says this. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=111394&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/111394](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F111394+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Fsync ALTER TABLE FREEZE snapshot to survive power loss
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111331 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `ALTER TABLE ... FREEZE` now fsyncs the snapshot it creates when the table's `fsync_part_directory` setting is enabled: the snapshot directories and the chain up to the disk root, plus the rewritten `data.packed` archive for packed part storage. Previously the freeze path fsynced nothing but `shadow/increment.txt`, so a power loss right after `FREEZE` was acknowledged could erase the whole snapshot. Default behaviour is unchanged. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111331 `ALTER TABLE ... FREEZE` builds its snapshot with `createDirectories` plus `createHardLink` (Full storage), or by rewriting `data.packed` (Packed storage), and fsyncs none of it. For a hardlink snapshot the file data is already durable but the new directory entries are not, so a power loss between the acknowledgement and the operator's archive step drops every new directory entry, i.e. the whole snapshot. The directory-fsync machinery this needs is already in master: the sibling `DETACH PARTITION` durability fix (#111426) merged the `fsync_part_directory` clone parameter, `fsyncFrozenCloneTree`, and the calls from both freeze overrides. It only wires up the `DETACH` call site, so `FREEZE` still acknowledged a non-durable snapshot. This PR is what remains: 1. `freezePartitionsByMatcher` populates `fsync_part_directory` from the table setting, resolved once from the entry snapshot so a concurrent `MODIFY SETTING` cannot split one `FREEZE` across parts. 2. For packed storage, `FREEZE` rewrites the `data.packed` archive instead of hardlinking it, so the archive contents are fsynced too, for the part and for each projection. Gated on the existing `fsync_part_directory` setting (default `false`), so no `SettingsChangesHistory` entry is needed. A no-op on remote/object disks, where `getDirectorySyncGuard` returns nullptr. Verified via `ProfileEvents` `DirectorySync` and `FileSync` on the `FREEZE` query for both layouts, including the setting-off baselines. Regression test `04621_freeze_fsync_part_directory.sh`.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Fsync projection parts to survive power loss
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111318 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111318 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Projection parts are now fsynced together with the rest of a data part. Previously projection files (under `<part>/<projection>.proj/`) were never fsynced on `INSERT` (with `fsync_after_insert`), `ALTER TABLE ... MATERIALIZE PROJECTION`, or a row-rewriting mutation (with the `*_to_fsync_after_merge` thresholds), so a power loss right after an acknowledged operation could leave the projection as all-zero-byte files, marked broken on load and reported by `CHECK TABLE` as `BROKEN_PROJECTION`. ### Description `MergeTreeDataWriter::writeProjectionPartImpl` finalized every projection part with a hardcoded no-sync flag (`finalizePartAsync(..., false)`), while the parent part's own files received the correct sync flag. That function serves the `INSERT` path (`writeProjectionPart`) and the mutation / merge path (`writeTempProjectionPart`), so under `fsync_after_insert = 1` (INSERT) or the merge/mutation fsync thresholds (`MATERIALIZE PROJECTION`, `ALTER ... DELETE`/`UPDATE`), the projection files were written but never fsynced. After a power loss the parent rows survived but the projection directory could end up all-zero-byte, broken on load and never self-healed. Fix: propagate the caller's sync decision into `writeProjectionPartImpl` and its two wrappers. INSERT passes `fsync_after_insert`; mutation and merge pass their `need_sync` decision. When a projection sub-merge re-merges several temporary parts, the final part is produced by a nested `MergeTask`, so the parent's decision is carried through `MergeProjectionPartsTask` to that task via a `force_sync` flag; the single-temp-part case is covered by the temp write itself, since it is only renamed into place (rename preserves the fsynced content). The merge-path `need_sync` is now computed before the projection temp parts are written. Behavior only changes when a durability setting is enabled; with the settings off the behavior is unchanged, and there are no on-disk, wire, or setting format changes. Report URL for the fsync-coverage finding: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111318 Verified two ways (details in the pre-PR validation gate comment): `strace -e fsync,fdatasync` on the INSERT path shows 0 projection-file fsyncs on `master` HEAD and 10 with this fix; the new stateless test `04548_projection_fsync` reads `ProfileEvents['FileSync']` from `system.query_log` and fails on `master` HEAD (`insert projection adds file syncs 0`) and passes with the fix (`1`). Mutation and merge paths verified via `strace` (all `pr.proj` files fsynced) plus `CHECK TABLE` and `force_optimize_projection`.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Fsync object-storage disk metadata and blobs to honor fsync settings
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111330 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Object-storage disks (`s3`, `azure_blob_storage`, `local_blob_storage`, ...) now honor the `MergeTree` fsync settings (`fsync_after_insert`, `fsync_part_directory`, `min_rows_to_fsync_after_merge`, `min_compressed_bytes_to_fsync_after_merge`). Previously these settings were silently ignored on such disks: an acknowledged `INSERT` issued zero `fsync`, so the local metadata files that commit a part could be lost on power loss even when the blobs were durable. ### Description Closes #111330. Found by the same fsync-coverage audit as #111269 / #111318 / #111320 / #111321 / #111322. On an object-storage disk the MergeTree fsync setting family was a no-op through three independent paths, each fixed at its own layer: 1. `ForkWriteBuffer` (the part's blob write buffer) did not override `sync()`, so the part's `file->sync()` landed in the base `WriteBuffer::sync()` (a plain `next()`) and never reached the underlying writers. It now forwards `sync()` to its children. For `s3`/`azure` the writer's `sync()` is a no-op (durability is on finalize); for local-file-backed object storage it performs the missing `fdatasync`. 2. The local metadata files that commit a part (the map file->blob, written on a local disk) were only `finalize()`d, never `fsync`ed. This is the fatal case for real `s3`: the blob is durable but the local metadata is lost on power loss, so the acknowledged part is gone and the blobs are leaked. `WriteBufferWithFinalizeCallback` now latches the caller's `sync()` request and `fsync`s the local metadata file once it has been written (handling both wide parts, which sync after finalize, and compact parts, which sync before finalize) via a new `IMetadataStorage::syncMetadataFile`. 3. `DiskObjectStorage` did not override `getDirectorySyncGuard`, so `fsync_part_directory` was ignored. It now delegates to the metadata storage's local disk. The metadata capabilities are forwarded through `MetadataStorageFromCacheObjectStorage`, so cache-wrapped object-storage disks are covered too. Gating is the existing `sync()` call (driven by `fsync_after_insert` / `needSyncPart` / `fsync_part_directory`), so there is no new setting and no change to default behavior: the fsync settings default off, and an object-storage insert without them still issues zero `fsync`. Verified with `strace -f -e trace=fsync,fdatasync` and the `FileSync`/`DirectorySync` ProfileEvents: on master an object-storage insert with the fsync settings issues 0 fsync; with the fix it issues the expected fsyncs, and 0 without the settings. Regression test: `tests/queries/0_stateless/04541_object_storage_disk_fsync.sh`.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Fsync detached directory on DROP DETACHED PART/PARTITION
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111349 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `ALTER TABLE ... DROP DETACHED PART/PARTITION` now fsyncs the `detached` directory when the `fsync_part_directory` MergeTree setting is enabled, so an acknowledged drop of a detached part is no longer rolled back by a power loss (the removed part could previously reappear). ### Description `MergeTreeData::dropDetached` renames `detached/<part>` to `detached/deleting_<part>` and then unlinks it, but never fsync'd the `detached` directory and consulted no durability setting. A rename or unlink is durable only once the parent directory is fsync'd, so after a power loss in the filesystem journal window the directory-entry changes could roll back and the acknowledged-dropped detached part reappeared intact. Reported and reproduced 3/3 with a `dm-flakey` power-loss simulation in #111349. Fix, gated on the existing `fsync_part_directory` setting (default `false`, so no behavior change by default): before the rename, acquire one directory sync guard per involved disk on the `detached` directory and hold it across the rename and the removal; the guard fsyncs the directory on destruction. The guards are declared before `PartsTemporaryRename` so they outlive it and also cover the rollback rename on the error path. This uses the disk-agnostic `IDisk::getDirectorySyncGuard` (local disks fsync; object storage is a no-op), matching the existing `fsync_part_directory` handling for part directories in `IMergeTreeDataPart::renameTo`. Test: `04620_drop_detached_part_fsync` asserts the `DirectorySync` ProfileEvent is emitted for `DROP DETACHED PART` when `fsync_part_directory = 1` and not when `0`, and that the part is removed in both cases.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Fsync DETACH TABLE ... PERMANENTLY flag to survive power loss
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111322 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Make `DETACH TABLE ... PERMANENTLY` durable: the `.sql.detached` marker file (and its removal on `ATTACH`) is now persisted by fsync'ing the metadata directory, gated on `fsync_metadata`. Previously the marker's creation/removal was not synced, so a power loss right after an acknowledged `DETACH ... PERMANENTLY` could silently re-attach the table on restart (or, symmetrically, undo an acknowledged `ATTACH`). ### Description Closes #111322. `DatabaseOnDisk::detachTablePermanently` creates the empty `<table>.sql.detached` marker via `db_disk->createFile`, and `removeDetachedPermanentlyFlag` removes it via `removeFileIfExists`. Neither fsync'd the parent metadata directory. A file's existence is a directory-entry change that is not durable until the directory is fsync'd, so an acknowledged `DETACH ... PERMANENTLY` (or `ATTACH`) could be lost on power loss, silently violating the acknowledged contract. This is the same `fsync_metadata` gap as #68958, applied to a marker file. Fix: fsync the metadata directory around both the marker creation and its removal, via `IDisk::getDirectorySyncGuard` (fsyncs on local disks, no-op on object storage), gated on `fsync_metadata` (default true). On the removal path the sync is taken only when the marker actually exists, so plain `CREATE TABLE` (which always calls `removeDetachedPermanentlyFlag`) is unaffected. Covers Ordinary, Atomic, and Replicated databases. Verified with the `DirectorySync` profile event (as in `02361_fsync_profile_events.sh`): `DirectorySync` is 1 for `DETACH ... PERMANENTLY` / `ATTACH` under `fsync_metadata=1` and 0 under `fsync_metadata=0`; 0 on both before the fix. Test: `03471_detach_permanently_fsync`.
