signal.title: Fsync access entities in DiskAccessStorage to survive power loss
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/68958 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Access entities stored on local disk (users, roles, grants, quotas, row policies, settings profiles created via SQL) are now fsync'd when `fsync_metadata` is enabled, so an acknowledged `CREATE`/`ALTER`/`DROP USER` (and `GRANT`/`REVOKE`) is no longer silently lost on power loss. Previously `DiskAccessStorage` wrote and removed the `.sql` entity files without any fsync. ### Description `DiskAccessStorage` wrote access-entity `.sql` files (and the `*.list` index files), and removed them, without any fsync, so an acknowledged access change could be lost on power loss. It was the only on-disk DDL-entity store not honoring `fsync_metadata` (UDFs, named collections, workload entities and table metadata all do). Reported and reproduced 3/3 on master with a `dm-flakey` power-loss simulation in #68958: after `CREATE USER` + `GRANT` and a power cut, the `<uuid>.sql` file is gone and the user cannot authenticate (`AUTHENTICATION_FAILED`). The tmp->final rename was never forced to disk. Fix, gated on `fsync_metadata` (default `true`), matching the sibling stores: - `writeEntityFile` (create/insert and update): fsync the file content, then fsync the parent directory around the rename (a rename is durable only once the directory entry is persisted). - `deleteAccessEntityOnDisk` (`DROP USER`/`REVOKE`, and the old-file removal on rename-replace): fsync the parent directory around the unlink. - `writeListFile`: fsync the file content (the `.list` files are rebuilt from the `.sql` files, so no directory fsync). The parent-directory fsync reuses `LocalDirectorySyncGuard`. The setting is resolved from the query context (session value) and falls back to the global context for the background `.list` writer, mirroring `getWriteSettings()`. Regression test `tests/integration/test_access_storage_fsync` asserts, via `system.query_log` ProfileEvents, that `CREATE`/`GRANT`/`ALTER`/`DROP USER` take the `FileSync`/`DirectorySync` path when `fsync_metadata=1` and take neither when `fsync_metadata=0`. It is an integration test because stateless tests override the access storage to `<memory/>`.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Use bloom_filter skip index for IN with transform_null_in=1 and NULL-free set
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111311 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Use the `bloom_filter` skip index for `IN` predicates on a directly indexed column when `transform_null_in = 1` and the `IN`-set contains no `NULL` value. Previously the index was skipped for such queries, forcing a full scan. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111311 With `transform_null_in = 1` the analyzer rewrites `x IN (...)` to `nullIn(x, ...)` (and `globalIn` to `globalNullIn`). The `bloom_filter` skip index condition built the predicate hashes for these but never assigned an RPN function, so the atom stayed `FUNCTION_UNKNOWN` and the index was unused, forcing a full scan. When the `IN`-set has no `NULL`, `nullIn` selects exactly the same rows as `in`, so the index can prune. The fix maps `nullIn`/`globalNullIn` to `FUNCTION_IN` when the set is single-column, `NULL`-free and type-compatible with the index, and the column is not an `Array`. With a `NULL` in the set, `nullIn` also matches `NULL` rows, so the atom is left `FUNCTION_UNKNOWN` (unchanged behavior). `x = 'abc'` already worked: `transform_null_in` does not rewrite `equals`. Scope: scalar left-hand side on a directly indexed column, which is the scope of the issue. Tuple lhs, `JSONAllPaths` and map subcolumns still recognize only `in`/`globalIn` and continue to full-scan. Those are deliberately not extended, because the checks this fix relies on cannot be evaluated there: the recursive `tuple(...)` branch matches each element against its own index and is called with `prepared_set = nullptr`, and `Set::hasNull()` returns `false` whenever `data_types.size() != 1`, so reusing the single-column guard on a tuple set is vacuous rather than merely wider. Measured with that extension applied, a 180-query parity sweep against `use_skip_indexes = 0` returned fewer rows than the truth arm for 17 queries; the sweep is clean on this PR. A test arm pins the contract, so extending the tuple branch on the single-column guard fails the test. Verified with `EXPLAIN indexes = 1` that the index prunes for `String`, `Nullable`, `LowCardinality` and `LowCardinality(Nullable)` with a `NULL`-free set, and does not prune for a set containing `NULL`, an `Array` column, a type-incompatible set or a tuple lhs. Results match `use_skip_indexes = 0` in each case.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Fix logical error joining a Merge over Distributed table with USING
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111253 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `LOGICAL_ERROR` ("query tree node does not have valid source node") when a `Merge` table wrapping a `Distributed` table is joined and a bare column of the joined-away side is used as a predicate. ### Description `ReadFromMerge` builds a separate query for each underlying table. It removes the JOIN and then strips the `WHERE`/`PREWHERE` sub-expressions that reference the joined-away table, via `removeExpressionsThatDoNotDependOnTableIdentifiers`. That helper only inspected `FunctionNode` top-level expressions; a bare-column predicate such as `WHERE r.k` (a `ColumnNode`) hit an early `return` and was left in the child query. When the `Distributed` child was re-planned to be sent to the shards, that column had a dangling source and the analyzer threw `Code: 49 ... Column k UInt32 query tree node does not have valid source node`. The fix treats any non-`and` top-level expression (bare column, constant, or single non-`and` function) uniformly: it is dropped if it references only removed tables. This is the same rule the helper already applied to single-function predicates and to each conjunct of an `and`. The single-line change covers more shapes than the reported one, so the test pins each entry path (all verified to raise the logical error without the fix and to pass with it): - `USING` and `ON`, and a self-join of the `Merge` table, which needs one table and no second fixture. Reported by zlareb1 on the issue after this PR was opened. - `QUALIFY` and `HAVING`, not only a hand-written `WHERE`. The planner folds `QUALIFY` into `HAVING` when there are no window functions and `HAVING` into `WHERE` when there is no aggregation, so such a predicate reaches the same helper. This is also the shape the AST fuzzer hit on #112931. - Left-side counterparts (`qualify_l`, `self_join_on_l`, `bare_where_l_k`), so no case can pass by dropping the predicate outright. The same helper is used to decide push-down for query-backed `MySQL`/`PostgreSQL`/`SQLite` sources, so `04341_sqlite_query_passing` pins that partition too. Measured on both arms, the only verdict this patch changes there is a bare predicate on the joined local side, which master rejected while accepting every other spelling of it. A disjunction mixing the two sides is still not rejected; that verdict is identical on both arms, so it is a pre-existing gap of testing a reconstructed AST for a surviving `WHERE`, pinned here rather than fixed.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Fix double free when finalizing -State aggregates under looping combinators
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110975 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a server crash (double free) that could happen when finalizing an aggregate function with the `-State` combinator nested under a looping combinator (`-Resample`, `-ForEach`, `-Map`), for example `groupArrayStateResample`, if a memory limit was reached during finalization. ### Description Reported on https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110975 (unrelated to that PR). Found by the Stress test (amd_debug): a segfault in `Aggregator::prepareChunkAndFillWithoutKey`, reached from `ConvertingAggregatedToChunksTransform::initialize`. CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110975&sha=838d0b61235b06939c8acd923ebd396f51cf5b10&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_debug%29 Root cause: the `-State` combinator transfers its result by aliasing the raw aggregate state pointer into a `ColumnAggregateFunction` (`AggregateFunctionState::insertResultInto` -> `getData().push_back(place)`); ownership passes to the column. `Aggregator::insertAggregatesIntoColumns` relies on this transfer being atomic per place: on an exception it destroys the whole place exactly once. A looping combinator nested over `-State` aliases many sub-states one at a time; the `push_back` into the column's pointer array can reallocate and, being memory-tracked, throw `MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` mid-loop. The already-transferred sub-states are then freed once by the aggregator's full `destroy()` and again by `~ColumnAggregateFunction`, i.e. a double free. Reproducer (crashes without the fix, returns a memory-limit error with it): ```sql SELECT arrayMap(x -> finalizeAggregation(x), state) FROM (SELECT groupArrayStateResample(0, 1048576, 1)(number, number % 20) AS state FROM numbers(100000)) SETTINGS max_memory_usage = 150000000, max_rows_to_read = 0; ``` Fix: reserve the destination columns before the transfer loop so the aliasing `push_back`s cannot reallocate (and therefore cannot throw) once a transfer has started. `ColumnAggregateFunction` used the no-op `IColumn::reserve`, so a real `reserve()`/`capacity()` over its state-pointer array is added. For `-Map`, the (possibly variable-width) key inserts are moved into their own loop before the value transfer, keeping the throwing work out of the aliasing loop. Reserving happens before any aliasing, so a throw there is harmless. The transfer loop is now non-throwing at the point of aliasing, restoring the atomic-per-place contract; results are unchanged. The fix covers all three looping transfer combinators (`-Resample`, `-ForEach`, `-Map`), which share the aliasing path; non-looping combinators delegate a single call and are already atomic. The added stateless test reproduces the crash deterministically via `-Resample` (empty buckets keep memory low until the finalization transfer, so a memory limit reliably lands the throw mid-transfer). `-ForEach` and `-Map` build their sub-states eagerly during aggregation, so they are not deterministically reproducible under a memory limit, but are fixed as the same class via the shared transfer path.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Promote committed orphans in refreshDataPartsOnce for rolled-back parts
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/100992 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a read-only table refresh (background `refresh_parts_interval` task or `SYSTEM RESTART DISK`) that could re-activate a rolled-back part and hide the committed parts it covers, when a rolled-back part intersects committed ones. Follow-up to #100992, which fixed the same case on the startup part-loading path. ### Description Follow-up to #100992 (requested by @tuanpach). #100992 taught the startup part loader (`loadDataPartsFromDisk`) to promote committed descendants of a rolled-back top-level part, and reverted the tree-level `contains`-branch eviction because `loadDataPartsFromDisk` already handles containment through orphan promotion. The read-only refresh path (`refreshDataPartsOnce`, used by the background refresh task on all-read-only-disk tables and by `SYSTEM RESTART DISK`) had no such promotion: it traverses only the top-level loading-tree nodes and unconditionally commits each one. On the containment topology (a rolled-back ancestor covering committed children), a read-only refresh therefore: - committed the rolled-back top-level part: `loadDataPart` demotes it to `Outdated`, and `preparePartForCommit` then resets it to `PreActive`, re-activating a rolled-back part. This trips `assertHasVersionMetadata` (`LOGICAL_ERROR`, server abort in debug/sanitizer builds); in a release build it silently re-activates the rolled-back part; and - never surfaced the committed children, which are covered by the ancestor in the tree and so are never reached by the top-level traversal. Fix: in `refreshDataPartsOnce`, skip committing a part that loaded as `Outdated` (rolled back), and instead re-enqueue its children, mirroring the orphan promotion `loadDataPartsFromDisk` performs. The loading tree is left untouched, so this does not re-open `test_transactions::test_rollback_unfinished_on_restart{1,2}` (that regression came from tree-level eviction removing rolled-back parts from `system.parts`; here the rolled-back part is still loaded, just left `Outdated`). Regression test `04612_part_loading_tree_rollback_refresh_disk` reproduces the #100992 (04241) containment topology but makes the parts appear after the read-only reader is loaded, so they go through `refreshDataPartsOnce` via `SYSTEM RESTART DISK`. It fails on `master` (server abort) and passes with this change.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Fix GROUP BY ALL with higher-order functions
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/56019 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111090 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/56019 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111090 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `GROUP BY ALL` with higher-order functions such as `arrayMap`/`arrayFilter`. Previously a query like `SELECT arrayFilter(x -> x > 0, groupArray(number)) ... GROUP BY ALL` failed with `Unknown function lambda` (old analyzer) or `ILLEGAL_AGGREGATION` (analyzer), because the lambda argument was incorrectly collected into the `GROUP BY` key set. The lambda (and its parameters) is no longer treated as a grouping key, while free columns and aggregates inside the lambda body are handled as they are with an explicit `GROUP BY`. ### Description `GROUP BY ALL` expands to the maximum non-aggregate SELECT sub-expressions. The key collector did not handle the lambda argument of higher-order functions: the old analyzer pushed the bare `lambda(...)` node (and its parameter) as a key, and the analyzer did not see aggregates inside the lambda body and pushed the whole higher-order function as a key. Both collectors (`QueryAnalyzer::recursivelyCollectMaxOrdinaryExpressions` and the old `recursivelyCollectMaxOrdinaryExpressions` in `TreeRewriter.cpp`) now skip lambda parameters, still collect free columns referenced in the lambda body, and propagate aggregates/window functions found in the body so the enclosing function is not collapsed into a single key. The result matches the corresponding explicit `GROUP BY`.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Fix UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER reading/merging a projection when a late-added column default references a non-stored column
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111076 --> Closes: #111076 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER` error when reading or merging a table with a projection after `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN c ... DEFAULT expr` where `expr` references a column not stored by the projection part, and the projection selects `c` (directly or via a re-pointed `ALIAS`). Such reads now fall back to the parent part and such merges rebuild the projection instead of failing. ### Description The projection column set is re-derived from the projection query on every table load, so an existing projection part can be missing a column the current metadata now requires. `projectionPartHasRequiredColumns` (read path) and `prepareProjectionsToMergeAndRebuild` (merge path) classify such a required column that is absent from BOTH the projection part and the parent part, but is a physical table column, as a legitimate column added after the part was written (case 4), and keep using the projection part on the assumption that its default fill is identical on either read path. That assumption breaks when the late-added column's `DEFAULT`/`MATERIALIZED` expression references a column the projection part does not store: the projection read cannot evaluate the default (the dependency is missing) and throws `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER`, while the parent read can. The merge path hits the same failure via `MergeTreeSequentialSource`, permanently blocking merges. Both guards now collect the default expression's column dependencies (as `MergeTreeBlockReadUtils` already does for missing-column reads) and, when a dependency is absent from the projection part, treat the column as drift: the read routes to the parent and the merge rebuilds the projection from the parent data. A late-add with a constant/no-dependency default is unchanged and still uses the projection part. Reproduces on `master`; deterministic. Regression coverage added to `04516_projection_part_column_drift` (both the `DEFAULT expr` and the `MATERIALIZED expr` variants). CI report / provenance: reported in [#111076](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111076) by ClickGap automated review of PR #110328 (which introduced the case-4 guard); this fixes the hole in that guard for the default-over-non-stored-column variant.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Fix optimize_skip_unused_shards on global distributed joins with shared column names
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111089 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111089 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `optimize_skip_unused_shards = 1` misbehaving on global distributed joins (`distributed_product_mode = 'global'`): a valid query such as `SELECT DISTINCT l.c, r.c + 2 ...` where both sides have a column of the same name threw `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT`, and grouping by a right-side column whose name matched the left table's sharding key could return unmerged per-shard partial results. ### Description `StorageDistributed::getOptimizedQueryProcessingStageAnalyzer` decides whether shards can process a `DISTINCT`/`GROUP BY`/`LIMIT BY` query all the way to `Complete` (the `optimize_distributed_group_by_sharding_key` optimization). It calls `isShardingKeySuitsQueryTreeNodeExpression`, which builds a type-checked `ActionsDAG` from the expression using **unqualified** column names (`use_column_identifier_as_action_node_name = false`) because the sharding key is defined without a table qualifier and is compared by plain name. Unqualified names are only meaningful when the expression reads a single source. In a global distributed join the same name can appear on more than one side, which breaks the optimization two ways: - **Crash** (the reported case): `l.c` (String) and `r.c` (Int64) collapse onto one action node, so `r.c + 2` is built against the wrong column and `plus(String, UInt8)` throws `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT` on the initiator during planning. `optimize_skip_unused_shards = 0` skips this probe, so the same query runs fine. - **Wrong results** (found while fixing the above): grouping by a right-side column whose name equals the left table's sharding key (e.g. left sharded by `k`, `GROUP BY r.k`) matched it to the sharding key by name and let shards process to `Complete`. A group keyed by that column can span shards, so the per-shard partials were returned unmerged. The fix restricts the optimization to the case where every column in the probed expression comes from this distributed table's own source (`query_info.table_expression`). Then the unqualified-name reasoning is valid: there is no cross-side name collision and the sharding-key match genuinely belongs to this table. Otherwise the analyzer falls back to merging on the initiator, exactly as with `optimize_skip_unused_shards = 0`. Single-table `DISTINCT`/`GROUP BY`/`LIMIT BY` by the sharding key, and joins that group by this table's own sharding key, keep the shard-local optimization. Verified locally on a 2-shard cluster: the reported query and its `LEFT JOIN`, `GROUP BY`, and comma-join variants threw `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT` before and now match `optimize_skip_unused_shards = 0`; a cross-shard `GROUP BY r.k` returned duplicated partials before and now returns the correct single merged group; single-table `DISTINCT`/`GROUP BY` by the sharding key still reaches the `Complete` stage.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Fix optimize_distributed_group_by_sharding_key wrong result for JOIN
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111087 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111274 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111087 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111274 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a wrong result with `optimize_distributed_group_by_sharding_key` when grouping a distributed `JOIN` by a column from the other join side that shares the sharding key's name (e.g. `GROUP BY r.k` over a `LEFT JOIN` where `r.k` is not the distributed table's sharding key). Such groups can span shards, so the per-shard aggregation shortcut is no longer applied for them, avoiding duplicate group keys with split aggregate values. ### Description `optimize_distributed_group_by_sharding_key` lets `StorageDistributed` skip the cross-shard merge when the `GROUP BY` key equals the sharding key, assuming each group's rows live on a single shard. In the new analyzer, `isShardingKeySuitsQueryTreeNodeExpression` matched the grouping expression against the sharding key by column name only (table qualifiers are stripped when building the comparison DAG). So a right-side column `r.k` in a distributed `LEFT JOIN` that merely shares the left table's sharding-key name `k` wrongly triggered the shortcut. Unmatched left rows are padded with `r.k = 0` on every shard, so the `r.k = 0` group spans shards and per-shard partial aggregates were returned unmerged, producing duplicate group keys with split values (silent wrong result). The fix skips the shortcut when the grouping/DISTINCT/LIMIT BY expression references any column that is not from the distributed table's own table expression, reusing the existing `hasUnknownColumn` helper. `GROUP BY` over the distributed table's actual sharding key is unaffected. Only the new analyzer path was affected; the old analyzer compares qualified identifier names and was already correct. Issue #111274 (`optimize_skip_unused_shards = 1` duplicating every group of a distributed self-join on an expression sharding key `intHash64(k)`) is the same root cause and is fixed by the same guard: `GROUP BY negate(r.k)` over a global self-join references `r.k` from the broadcast side, whose required column matches the sharding key name after qualifier stripping. Verified locally on master: the self-join returned 1000 rows (500 groups duplicated, each with an empty aggregate copy) and returns the correct 500 with this fix.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Fix NOT_IMPLEMENTED for correlated subqueries when join_algorithm lacks hash
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/103294 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` error ("Can't execute any of specified algorithms...") for correlated subqueries with a non-trivial correlation when `join_algorithm` did not include `hash` or `parallel_hash` (e.g. `auto`, `grace_hash`, `partial_merge`, `full_sorting_merge`). ### Description When a correlated subquery has a non-trivial correlation (e.g. an inequality), it is decorrelated into an internal join. With `correlated_subqueries_use_in_memory_buffer` enabled (the default), that internal join is restricted to hash-family algorithms so the buffered input stream is fully evaluated before the subquery runs. The restriction did this with an unconditional `std::erase_if` on the join's algorithm list: if the user's `join_algorithm` enabled neither `hash` nor `parallel_hash`, the list became empty and `chooseJoinAlgorithm` threw a misleading `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`. The internal decorrelation join must still run in that case, so it now falls back to `hash` when the restriction would otherwise empty the list. Hash join always supports this join and satisfies the in-memory buffer requirement. Reproducer (failed before, works now): ```sql SET enable_analyzer = 1, allow_experimental_correlated_subqueries = 1, join_algorithm = 'full_sorting_merge'; SELECT number FROM numbers(2) AS t WHERE exists((SELECT number FROM numbers(2) WHERE number >= t.number)); ```
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Fix data race on DataTypeAggregateFunction version during Native serialization
signal.text: Related: found by the `arm_tsan` and `azure, amd_tsan` Stress tests (STID 3977-4818, ThreadSanitizer data race). No existing issue. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/94859 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112052 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Not for changelog. ### Description A single `DataTypeAggregateFunction` instance is shared across query result blocks: it lives once in the table's column description and is aliased by shallow column copies. `NativeWriter`/`NativeReader` called `setVersionToAggregateFunctions`, which walked to the leaf type and wrote its `mutable version` field in place. Two concurrent `Native` serializations of the same aggregate-function-typed column then raced on that field, and the version written for one old connection stayed on the shared type, so every later query read the states at that version - for `sumMap` over `Decimal32` that returns wrong values. Reports: * https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109496&sha=62eeb400eafe86cedff9b5a4e9a36aa722633cda&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_tsan%29 * https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=b59441bd06c2fcb6b103a30874528cc398afc723&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28azure%2C%20amd_tsan%29 **That fix has since landed on `master`** through #94859 and #112052: `setVersionToAggregateFunctions` now replaces every versioned nested type instead of mutating it, and `replaceNestedSimpleTypes` carries the custom names (`Nested`, `SimpleAggregateFunction`) over the rebuild. This branch is therefore resolved in favour of that implementation, and what it added on top of it - an `IDataType::transformChildren` override per container type, and the `unique_ptr` to `shared_ptr` switch of `DataTypeCustomNamePtr` - is dropped as duplicate machinery. What remains here is what `master` does not have, and it keeps this PR's intent - the race cannot come back, because the version can no longer be assigned in place at all: * `DataTypeAggregateFunction::setVersion` and `updateVersionFromRevision` are removed, and `version` is no longer `mutable`. Both mutators were left without callers by the rewrite on `master`; the version is now set only at construction (parsed from AST, decoded from the binary type encoding, or chosen by `setVersionToAggregateFunctions`, which builds a new type). * Unit and functional coverage of the behaviour, which `master` has only indirectly. ### Testing * `gtest_aggregate_function_version_race` (14 tests) pins the type-level behaviour: the shared type object is not mutated; a wrapper is rebuilt only when a leaf was actually replaced; the `Point`, `Nested` and `SimpleAggregateFunction` custom names survive, including a `Tuple`-backed `SimpleAggregateFunction`; a `Variant` keeps its discriminator order and throws when two alternatives would collapse; a `JSON` typed path keeps the version spelled in its own type name; and an 8-thread x 2000-iteration stress over one shared type object is race-free. * `04612_aggregate_function_version_custom_type_names` round-trips `Nested`, `SimpleAggregateFunction` and a wrapper-named type through `Native` (which assigns the version in the writer and again in the reader) and through `DETACH`/`ATTACH`, and checks that a deeply nested `Nested` stays linear in the nesting depth. * `04613_aggregate_function_version_not_sticky` asks for a `Native` response at a revision below the one that introduced versioning and then checks the column again, so a version pinned for that one response would be visible both in the values read back (`sumMap` over `Decimal32`) and in `system.columns`. The revision is pinned explicitly and the type name the response carries is asserted, so the test cannot pass without that path having run. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110997&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/110997](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F110997+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix LOGICAL_ERROR in ReadFromMergeTree::deserialize for empty distributed-read snapshot
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110927 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110910 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a `LOGICAL_ERROR` in experimental multistage distributed query planning (`make_distributed_plan`) when a worker deserializes a bucketed `ReadFromMergeTree` read whose local parts snapshot has become empty (parts merged away or dropped concurrently). ### Description Fixes the LOGICAL_ERROR `ReadFromMergeTree step is expected to be created by readFromParts` in `ReadFromMergeTree::deserialize`, in the multistage distributed queries feature (`make_distributed_plan`, experimental). Closes #110927. Surfaced once in 60 days on `Stress test (arm_release)` (report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110910&sha=51e6b0ddc85e666b2fcfacc3238134aeba30e55c&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_release%29). Not caused by #110910 (which only touches `randomHadamardTransform`); it is a pre-existing latent bug in the distributed-read deserialize path. Root cause: the coordinator serializes a bucketed read (`distributed_read_bucket_count > 0`) while parts exist. A worker deserializes it, but its local parts snapshot can be empty by then (parts merged away or dropped under stress churn). `readFromParts` returns a null step for an empty non-stream read, and the bucketed branch then `dynamic_cast`s it to null and throws. Fix: on the deserialize path only, `readFromParts` now builds a real (empty) `ReadFromMergeTree` step for a bucketed read even when the local snapshot is empty, so the bucket count has a step to attach to. `initializePipeline` then resolves it exactly as before at runtime: a genuinely empty bucket reads nothing, and a bucket whose coordinator-selected part is missing locally raises the existing retryable `NO_SUCH_DATA_PART` divergence error. A `ReadNothingStep` short-circuit would instead bypass that divergence check and silently drop rows, so it is deliberately not used. The other five `readFromParts` callers are unchanged.

signal.title: Fix RENAME TABLE of a Distributed table with a non-empty async-insert queue
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/92124 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `RENAME TABLE` of a `Distributed` table is now refused when it would have to move the table's asynchronous insert queue directory, which only happens in the deprecated `Ordinary` database engine. Previously the rename appeared to succeed while a file that was still queued kept being addressed by its pre-rename path, so its rows were never delivered: with `background_insert_batch = 0` `SYSTEM FLUSH DISTRIBUTED` failed with `Cannot open file ... errno: 2`, and with `background_insert_batch = 1` it reported success while delivering nothing. An `Atomic` database keys the data directory by UUID and never moves it, so renames there are unaffected. ### Description A `Distributed` table keeps one async-insert queue directory per shard under its data path. In an `Ordinary` database `RENAME TABLE` moves that path, and nothing serialises the move against concurrent work: `DistributedSink` resolves a queue directory, links the block into it and enqueues it without holding the mutex the move takes, and `SYSTEM FLUSH DISTRIBUTED` copies the queue pointers under that mutex but runs the sends after releasing it. `pause()` does not help either, since it only deactivates the scheduled task while the flush runs on a foreground pool. Rather than synchronise the move, this removes the case: `DatabaseAtomic::renameTable` never calls `IStorage::rename` at all (it moves the metadata file and calls `renameInMemory`, and the data directory is `store/<uuid>`), and `DatabaseOnDisk` is the only caller of it. So the defect is confined to `Ordinary`, which is deprecated behind `allow_deprecated_database_ordinary`, and refusing the rename there means no queue repointing, no task pause, and no filesystem work under a mutex. The refusal is skipped in three cases: no data path (a `remote()` target), `ATTACH ... FROM` (which calls `rename()` with an unchanged `StorageID` only to move data into place before the table is reachable), and the `Ordinary`-to-`Atomic` conversion, which assigns a UUID to every table during startup. That last one requires the acquired UUID, matching `StorageReplicatedMergeTree::checkTableCanBeRenamed`, since startup scripts also run before the server is completely started. Verified live: converting a database holding a `Distributed` table with a queued file succeeds and delivers that row. `01155_rename_move_materialized_view` moved such a table between the two engines by hand and now recreates it, which is what a user has to do. `test_distributed_storage_configuration` used `Ordinary` for a predictable data path and now reads the path from `system.tables`, keeping its `RENAME` coverage on `Atomic`.

signal.title: Fix Bad cast for GROUP BY ALL WITH ROLLUP scalar subquery under group_by_use_nulls
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110915 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `Bad cast` error (abort in debug/sanitizer builds) when a scalar subquery aggregates over a derived table that uses `GROUP BY ALL WITH ROLLUP`/`CUBE`/`GROUPING SETS` under `group_by_use_nulls = 1`. ### Description `GROUP BY ALL` is expanded into the GROUP BY key list only at the very end of query resolution (`expandGroupByAll` needs the resolved projection). Under `group_by_use_nulls = 1` that is too late: `resolveGroupByNode` runs earlier, gated by `hasGroupBy()`, which is false while the GROUP BY list is still empty. So the keys were never registered in `nullable_group_by_keys` and the inner projection kept its non-`Nullable` type, while `WITH ROLLUP` execution produces `Nullable`. In a scalar subquery the outer aggregate is resolved against the inner query's advertised (non-`Nullable`) projection type, so it is built without the `Null` combinator adapter and crashes at run time in `addBatchSinglePlace` with `Bad cast from type ColumnNullable to ColumnVector<...>`. Spelling the key explicitly (`GROUP BY val`) already worked. Fix: in the `group_by_use_nulls` path, when the query is `GROUP BY ALL`, resolve the projection and expand `GROUP BY ALL` before `resolveGroupByNode`, so the keys are registered and the projection is re-resolved with the `Nullable` promotion, exactly like the explicit-key path. The change is guarded by `isGroupByAll()`, so all other queries are unaffected. Reproducer (aborts on master, works with this PR): ```sql SET group_by_use_nulls = 1; SELECT (SELECT avgOrDefault(val) FROM (SELECT rand64() AS val FROM numbers(10) GROUP BY ALL WITH ROLLUP)); ``` Found by the AST fuzzer (`AST fuzzer (amd_debug)`, STID 1499-33a5) on unrelated PR #110606: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110606&sha=d9c6d9deca1e7c4fc5965f466d6beede6922b808&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%29 Closes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110915

signal.title: Restore Parquet column pruning for Iceberg schema-evolved reads
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110897 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Restore Parquet column pruning for Iceberg data files written under an older schema. After schema evolution (e.g. `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN`), reading an old data file decoded every physical column even when the query needed only one; now only the columns the query requires are read. ### Description Fixes #110897. When an Iceberg table's schema evolves, `IcebergMetadata::getInitialSchemaByPath` returns the full underlying (old) file schema for data files whose schema id differs from the current one. In `StorageObjectStorageSource::createReader` this full schema became the Parquet reader's `initial_header`, so the reader decoded every physical column of the old file; the schema-transform DAG only ran afterwards. Adding one unrelated nullable column turned `SELECT sum(id)` from decoding just `id` into also decoding the table's wide string columns (reporter measured ~23x more selected bytes, ~5x peak memory). The Iceberg schema-transform DAG maps old-schema input names to new-schema output names (by field name), so pruning its unused actions against the query's required columns yields exactly the old-schema physical columns to read. This is the same pruning the Delta path already does; here it is applied to the Iceberg `getSchemaTransformer()` path and the pruned transform is reused so the read header and the transform stay consistent. Pruning is applied only when there are no equality-delete files: equality deletes are applied by name on the old-schema block before the schema transform runs, so their key columns must remain in the read header even if the query does not select them. When any needed column is not a transform output the full schema is kept, so unusual column shapes fall back to current behavior rather than failing. Regression test `04545_iceberg_schema_evolution_column_pruning_110897` asserts an id-only read decodes far fewer bytes than a read that needs the wide column, and that results (including reads of the added and renamed columns, and filters on non-selected columns) stay correct.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Fix LOGICAL_ERROR in OPTIMIZE ... DRY RUN racing a concurrent merge
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107114 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114399 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a `LOGICAL_ERROR` exception (`Temporary part ... already added`) when `OPTIMIZE ... DRY RUN` runs concurrently with a real merge, or with another `DRY RUN`, on the same parts. ### Description `MergeTreeData::optimizeDryRun` executes a real `MergeTask` but, unlike the real optimize/merge paths, takes no `CurrentlyMergingPartsTagger` and no merge lock, so it never registers its source parts as "being merged". A concurrent real merge on the same parts computes the same result part name and reserves the same `tmp_merge_<result>` directory. The second reservation trips `TemporaryParts::add` -> `LOGICAL_ERROR "Temporary part ... already added"`, aborting the server on debug and sanitizer builds. Seen on 17 unrelated PRs over the 30 days to 2026-08-11 (CIDB `default.checks`, 17 rows / 17 distinct PRs), never on master. The dry-run part is throwaway, so its directory need not be named after the result part. It is now `tmp_merge_dry_run_<uuid>`, making the collision impossible on both `MergeTree` and `ReplicatedMergeTree`. A UUID rather than a counter, because the directory can live on storage shared with other servers, where a process-local counter restarts and repeats itself. Leaving the part name out also avoids a length trap: appending a token to it can exceed the 255-byte filename limit while the real merge of the same parts still succeeds. Part names are not length-capped (an all-integral partition key spells its values out, so ten `Int64` fields plus an `IPv4` reach 226 bytes) and `MergeTree` prepends `delete_tmp_` before removal, leaving 8 bytes. The new name has a fixed size. It is never parsed back into a part name and still starts with `tmp_merge_`, which the cleaner and the startup skip logic select by. Only a `dry_run_` suffix takes the new path, so top-level and projection merges keep byte-identical names. Not a duplicate of the `DRY RUN` fix linked above (rows_sources under a soft timeout). Tracking issue: #114399. Test `03823_optimize_dry_run_merge_race` races two `DRY RUN`s on the same parts via a new failpoint pausing after the directory is reserved, at part-name lengths 7, 9 and 226, asserting the real merge succeeds at 226 and each `DRY RUN` really merged.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Do not abort server when loading a view without columns in metadata
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/60708 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a server abort (`LOGICAL_ERROR: Invalid storage definition in metadata file`) on startup when a `VIEW` is stored without a column list in its metadata. Such a view now fails to load with a normal exception instead of terminating the whole server. ### Description `createTableFromAST` (`src/Databases/DatabaseOnDisk.cpp`) threw a `LOGICAL_ERROR` ("Invalid storage definition in metadata file") whenever a table had no column list and no storage engine. That premise does not hold for views: an ordinary view has no storage engine by design (`StorageFactory` explicitly forbids one), and its stored column list may legitimately be absent. Only parameterized views were exempted (added in #60708), so any other columnless view definition found in on-disk metadata (produced by the AST fuzzer, an upgrade, or manual intervention) hit the throw during async table loading and aborted the entire server on startup. The fix skips this throw for all views. A columnless view now fails to load with a catchable `EMPTY_LIST_OF_COLUMNS_PASSED` exception, and the server stays up. Found by the Stress test (amd_asan_ubsan) job: the server crashed during the restart phase while loading the fuzzer-created parameterized view `test_5.prewhere_bug_view__fuzz_4` (from `04227_prewhere_parameterized_view_join_102074.sql`). Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=107091&sha=5e31ccb31390e87186ca0a7a5a047aec6968c392&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_asan_ubsan%29 Stack: ``` DB::createTableFromAST (src/Databases/DatabaseOnDisk.cpp:127) DB::DatabaseOrdinary::loadTableFromMetadata (src/Databases/DatabaseOrdinary.cpp:386) DB::AsyncLoader::worker -> <Fatal> Received signal 6 (Aborted) ```

signal.title: Harden 00965_send_logs_level_concurrent_queries against async trace-log delivery race
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/101039 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110035 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Description Follow-up to #110035 for `00965_send_logs_level_concurrent_queries`. The positive check asserts that a trace-level query streams at least one `<Trace>` line. Trace logs are delivered asynchronously, so under heavy load (sanitizer builds, slow or remote object storage, high concurrency) a query occasionally closes its client stream before the first trace line is flushed. That yields zero `<Trace>` lines and a false `Fail` while the server behaves correctly. This is the residual flakiness observed after #110035 (which fixed the deterministic positional field-8 fragility of the same test). The trace query is now retried a bounded number of times. The assertion still fails permanently if no trace line is ever delivered, so the test keeps its ability to catch a real regression, but it tolerates a transient delivery miss. Local verification (debug build): the hardened test prints 10x `OK` and matches the reference; a controlled fake client that returns zero trace lines on the first attempts still yields `OK` via retry, whereas the old single-shot form would print `Fail` on the same transient miss.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Disable TopK dynamic filtering when a sorting projection makes the read in-order
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110862 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a performance regression where `use_top_k_dynamic_filtering` installed a redundant `__topKFilter` prewhere for `ORDER BY ... LIMIT` queries served in-order by a sorting projection, causing the sort column to be read twice. ### Description Closes: #110862 `optimizeTopK` disables `use_top_k_dynamic_filtering` when the `ORDER BY` column is a prefix of the read's sorted order: there the dynamic prewhere filter is counterproductive, because once the running threshold stabilizes it rejects all remaining rows in sorted order, defeating the early pipeline cancellation that `LIMIT` relies on and forcing a full scan. That guard only checked the base table's sorting key. When a sorting projection whose `ORDER BY` differs from the base table is selected, the read is `ReadType: InOrder` with respect to the projection's sort key, but the guard never matched, so the redundant `__topKFilter` prewhere was installed on top of the projection read, re-reading the sort column that in-order reading already provided. `tryOptimizeTopK` runs in the first plan pass, before projection selection and read-in-order (both second pass), so the guard is predictive. It now also disables dynamic filtering when a normal sorting projection whose `ORDER BY` starts with the sort column and which stores every read column is available and projection optimization is enabled — the exact condition under which such a projection is later chosen to serve the read in-order. Results were correct in all cases; this is a performance-only fix. Verified with `EXPLAIN` that the redundant `__topKFilter` is no longer installed while the projection is still selected and the read stays `InOrder`, and that dynamic filtering is still applied when no projection can serve the order.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Validate engine features before rewriting metadata on ATTACH AS REPLICATED
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110854 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `ATTACH TABLE ... AS REPLICATED` leaving a table unloadable after restart when the source table used an unsupported clause for the target engine (e.g. a `MergeTree` table with a `UNIQUE KEY` clause, which `ReplicatedMergeTree` does not support). The conversion is now validated before the on-disk metadata is rewritten, so a rejected `ATTACH ... AS REPLICATED` keeps the stored metadata intact. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110854 `ATTACH TABLE ... AS REPLICATED` rewrote the on-disk metadata to the Replicated engine (`convertMergeTreeTableIfPossible` in `InterpreterCreateQuery.cpp`) before the engine-feature validation ran. Feature support is only checked later in `StorageFactory::get` when the storage is instantiated, where `ReplicatedMergeTree` rejects the `UNIQUE KEY` clause. So the query returned `Code 36 BAD_ARGUMENTS`, but the metadata file had already been replaced with an invalid `ReplicatedMergeTree(...) ... UNIQUE KEY (...)` combination and there was no rollback. On the next server start the load job for the table failed with `Code 36`, surfaced to clients as `Code 722 ASYNC_LOAD_WAIT_FAILED`. Repro (from the issue): ```sql SET allow_experimental_unique_key = 1; CREATE TABLE t0 (c0 Int) ENGINE = MergeTree() ORDER BY tuple() UNIQUE KEY (c0); DETACH TABLE t0; ATTACH TABLE t0 AS REPLICATED; -- returns Code 36, but rewrites the metadata anyway -- after restart: SELECT * FROM t0; -- Code 722 ASYNC_LOAD_WAIT_FAILED ``` The fix validates that the target engine supports the `UNIQUE KEY` clause in `convertMergeTreeTableIfPossible` before any side effect (before clearing transaction metadata and before writing the new metadata file). `UNIQUE KEY` is the only DDL clause whose support differs between the `MergeTree` family and `ReplicatedMergeTree`, so this fully covers the conversion. The rejected conversion now keeps the clean `Code 36` error, leaves the stored metadata untouched, and the table remains loadable after restart. Added stateless regression test `04545_attach_as_replicated_unique_key`.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Encode nulls-action variant in -Tuple aggregate state type name
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110073 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107951 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111580 --> Related: #110073 Related: #107951 Related: #111580 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a server crash when merging aggregate states of a `-Tuple` combinator function (e.g. `anyLastTuple(...) RESPECT NULLS`) whose declared type differs from the actual type, for example over a `Distributed` table under `GROUP BY ... WITH CUBE` / `WITH TOTALS`. ### Description Investigation of the crash reported on #110073: `AST fuzzer (amd_debug, targeted)` `Segmentation fault (STID: 4281-3dd7)` in `TotalsHavingTransform::addToTotals` -> `ColumnAggregateFunction::insertMergeFrom` -> `SingleValueData`. CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110073&sha=25d3ba356582bfc4bb86b97482278932468c00f2&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29 Root cause: the `-Tuple` aggregate combinator's serialized state type name was not injective with respect to the nulls-action variant of its nested functions. `anyLastTuple(...) RESPECT NULLS` resolves nested `anyLast_respect_nulls` (state layout `AggregateFunctionAnyRespectNullsData`), while the plain form resolves `anyLast` (`SingleValueDataGeneric`) - two different, byte-incompatible state representations. But `getName()` was composed from the pre-resolution nested name, so both produced the identical type name `AggregateFunction(anyLastTuple, Tuple(...))`. When that name round-trips - over the distributed wire, from disk, or when the totals/cube path reconstructs the accumulator - the reader resolves the wrong nested variant from the shared name and reinterprets the state bytes, dereferencing a bad vtable in `assert_cast<SingleValueDataGeneric &>`. This is expressible on master with the classic `Distributed` form (declared `UInt128` over a `UInt64` source), no table-function feature required: ```sql CREATE TABLE src (number UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY number; INSERT INTO src SELECT number FROM numbers(10); CREATE TABLE dist (number UInt128) ENGINE = Distributed(test_cluster_two_shards_localhost, currentDatabase(), src, number); SELECT last_valueTupleOrNull(tuple( tuple(* APPLY lambda(tuple(x), isNull(x)) EXCEPT '.*' REPLACE (2147483647 AS `e`)), tuple(* APPLY (lambda(tuple(x), isNull(x)), 'f_') EXCEPT '.*' REPLACE (1024 AS `e`)))) RESPECT NULLS FROM dist GROUP BY ALL WITH CUBE; -- SIGSEGV before this change ``` Fix: derive the `-Tuple` base name from a resolved non-placeholder nested function, matching how `-Array` / `-If` / `-OrNull` compose their names from `nested_func->getName()`. This makes the serialized name injective (`anyLast_respect_nullsTupleOrNull` vs `anyLastTupleOrNull`), so a state can only ever be reconstructed as the variant that produced it. Only-null tuple elements collapse to a `nothing*` placeholder with an empty, variant-less state and carry no naming information, so they are skipped; the pre-resolution name is used only as a fallback when every element is a placeholder. The `-Tuple` combinator is new in this version (`introduced_in {26, 7}`), so no released build persisted states under the old name and there is no on-disk compatibility concern. Also closes #111580 (`AST fuzzer (amd_debug, targeted, old_compatibility)` `Segmentation fault (STID: 2470-2cc1)`), the same crash class reached through a combinator-wrapped nested function. `anyRespectNullsArgMinTupleOrNull(...) IGNORE NULLS` over a `Distributed` table `WITH TOTALS` resolves the nested `anyRespectNullsArgMin` down to `anyArgMin` under `IGNORE NULLS` (a smaller `ArgMin` state, different key offset), while the action-less declared type name reconstructs `any_respect_nullsArgMin` on the initiator - the key offset then mismatches and the totals merge dereferences a wild pointer in `SingleValueDataNumeric`. Deriving the `-Tuple` name from the resolved nested function encodes the action here too, so the type name is injective and the state is reconstructed correctly. Reproducer verified to SIGSEGV on `master` and to be fixed by this change; a regression test covering it is added. While covering that case, the placeholder skip is also extended to a nested `-Tuple` element: `isOnlyNullPlaceholder` on a `-Tuple` holds only when all of its elements are placeholders (the base predicate unwraps only a single-nested combinator chain), so an all-only-null inner tuple no longer lends its pre-resolution name to the outer tuple.

signal.title: Fix logical error on DISTINCT-in-order over ARRAY JOIN with stale sort property
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109216 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a logical error `Equal values are not contiguous within the range assumed to be sorted` (and potential wrong `DISTINCT` results) when `optimize_distinct_in_order` is enabled and an `ORDER BY` over an `arrayJoin`-derived column is followed by another `ARRAY JOIN` that reproduces a column of the same name. ### Description `applyActionsToSortDescription()` returned early whenever the expression it was pushing the sort description through contained an `ARRAY JOIN`, leaving the sort description unchanged. When such an expression re-applies an `ARRAY JOIN` that produces an output column named identically to the sorted input column, the output stream is no longer sorted by that column, yet the stale `... ASC` sort property survived and propagated up to the `DISTINCT` step. That step then ran distinct-in-order (`DistinctSortedStreamTransform`) over genuinely unsorted data and aborted with the logical error (or, in a release build, could return wrong `DISTINCT` results). Removing the blanket early-return lets the existing chain-tracing logic handle `ARRAY JOIN` correctly: the monotonic chain breaks at an `ARRAY JOIN` node, so array-join-derived sort columns are dropped, while genuinely order-preserving columns (array join only replicates rows in place) are kept. The failing shape is produced, for example, by decorrelating a correlated scalar subquery whose body is `SELECT DISTINCT ... ORDER BY <arrayJoin column> SETTINGS optimize_distinct_in_order = 1`. This is the no-JOIN variant of the `DistinctSortedStreamTransform` invariant family; it is not covered by #109225 (which gates read-in-order propagation through non-order-preserving JOINs). Found via the AST/BuzzHouse fuzzers (CIDB STID 2508-348f), reproduced deterministically on debug and asan builds. Regression test `04550_distinct_in_order_array_join_phantom_sort` fails (aborts) without the fix and passes with it.

signal.title: Fix text index LOGICAL_ERROR with constant folding and partition key
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a `LOGICAL_ERROR` ("Query builder not found for text search query with function") when a query filters a column that has a `text` index and is also the partition key, with the setting `use_constant_folding_in_index_analysis` enabled. ### Description The text index direct-read path registers its virtual columns against the unsubstituted condition at plan time (the virtual column name embeds the unsubstituted search-query hash), and the reader looks them up via `generateUnsubstituted()`. When `use_constant_folding_in_index_analysis` is on and the text-indexed column is also the partition key, the granule analyzer was built from the per-partition constant-folded condition instead, whose search queries hash differently. The reader could not find the query builder and threw the logical error (server abort in debug/sanitizer builds). The fix keeps constant folding off for `text` index condition templates, so the granule analyzer and the reader always use the same unsubstituted set of search queries. Other index types are unaffected. Found by the AST fuzzer (STID 3694-54bc), report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=100173&sha=e196b05a52cdcdcdf80b1f6c6a41071b5deec053&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%29

signal.title: Fix Block structure mismatch after liftUpUnion with divergent aggregate state types
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> No related open issue found. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a `LOGICAL_ERROR` "Block structure mismatch in after optimization liftUpUnion" (server abort in debug and sanitizer builds) that could occur for a query with an expression or preliminary `DISTINCT` above a `UNION ALL` whose branches produce aggregate-function state columns that share the same state representation but different type names (for example `quantileExactTupleState` and `quantilesExactTupleState`). ### Description `tryLiftUpUnion` pushes the parent `Expression`/`Distinct` step into each union branch, assuming the union forwards every branch unchanged. That assumption breaks when a branch column matches the union output only loosely: two `AggregateFunction` columns can share the same state representation yet print different type names (e.g. `quantileExactTuple` vs `quantilesExactTuple(0.9)`), so `blocksHaveEqualStructure` treats them as equal and the union output takes the first branch's type. The union coerces the diverging branch at runtime via a converting step; pushing the parent down bypasses that coercion and produces branch headers that no longer match, tripping the post-optimization `checkHeaders` assertion. The fix lifts the parent only when every branch input header is identical (same name and same type name) to the union output. The optimization still fires for genuine same-type unions. Found by the AST fuzzer (Stress test, amd_tsan; CIDB STID 0993-23fd).

signal.title: Filter LLVM Profile Error noise from cancel-insert-when-client-dies tests
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108343 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ### Description Four cancel-insert tests (02434, 02435, 04365, 04366) fail on `Stateless tests (amd_llvm_coverage_per_test, per_test_coverage)` with `result differs with reference`, where the diff's added lines are `LLVM Profile Error:` messages rather than wrong test output. The cancellation counts are correct. Root cause: `thread_cancel` SIGKILLs coverage-instrumented `clickhouse-client` processes mid-insert. On abnormal death those clients emit `LLVM Profile Error: ...` to stderr (profraw merge-pool contention, see #97020). `clickhouse-test` strips those lines from a client's *stderr* only; `thread_insert` merges client stderr into stdout via `2>&1` and filtered just `Killed` (plus session noise in 02435), so the lines survived into the test's stdout and broke the reference diff. Fix: extend each `thread_insert` filter with `grep -Fav "LLVM Profile Error:"`. A repo-wide sweep of stateless `.sh` tests that signal-kill processes and merge output with `2>&1` confirms these four are the complete carrier set: the other candidates either capture into a variable and positively `grep` for `Received from` (01169 pair), redirect client output to a file or `/dev/null` (03776, 03803, 04003, 04051, 04052), or filter on `Exception:` (02443). 02435 was added after `clickhouse-gh[bot]` pointed it out on this PR; it has 3 master failures of this exact signature (2026-06-15, 2026-07-16, 2026-07-17). Validation: this check runs only in `NightlyCoverage` (`ci/workflows/nightly_coverage.py`, `Event.SCHEDULE`, master), so it cannot run on this PR. Instead, each test's committed filter chain was extracted from the file and driven against the verbatim CI-captured stdout: post-fix output matches the reference byte-for-byte; removing the new filter reproduces the failure (so it is load-bearing); and a real `DB::Exception` line is preserved, confirming only the profiler noise is dropped. 12/12 assertions pass across the four tests. Report (04365, 2026-07-28 master): https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=4a44dcefc451d3da3f7a9e7c8a38f74180b34ebc&name_0=NightlyCoverage&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_llvm_coverage_per_test%2C%20per_test_coverage%2C%208%2F8%29 Prior PR #108343 widened the final cancel-message matcher (a separate genuine gap); the recurrence was this stdout pollution.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Fix LOGICAL_ERROR on constant-folded comparison under group_by_use_nulls + GROUPING SETS
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110551 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a logical error (server abort in debug/sanitizer builds) when a constant-folded comparison appears in the SELECT list together with `group_by_use_nulls = 1` and `GROUP BY GROUPING SETS`. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110551 `group_by_use_nulls` promotes a `FunctionNode`'s declared result type to `Nullable` via `FunctionNode::wrap_with_nullable`, while the un-wrapped base function used for constant folding still returns the non-`Nullable` type. When such a node is constant-folded in `tryFoldFunctionToConstant` (`ActionsDAG.cpp`), the folded `Const(UInt8)` diverges from the declared `Nullable(UInt8)`, so the node result-type consistency check throws `LOGICAL_ERROR: Unexpected return type from equals. Expected Nullable(UInt8). Got Const(UInt8)`. In debug/sanitizer builds this aborts the server; release tolerates it (the check is an assert), and `group_by_use_nulls = 0` is unaffected. The fix reconciles the folded constant to the declared node result type in exactly this case (the declared type equals `makeNullableOrLowCardinalityNullableSafe(base_result_type)`) instead of weakening the check. The strict `LOGICAL_ERROR` check is kept as a fallback for genuine mismatches. Regression test: `04545_group_by_use_nulls_grouping_sets_const_fold_equals` (the issue's repro plus a minimal variant). Found by the AST fuzzer.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Fix wrong count() result with custom key parallel replicas
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/50593 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/50593 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed wrong results for aggregation queries over a cluster/Distributed table with custom key parallel replicas (`parallel_replicas_mode = 'custom_key_sampling'`/`'custom_key_range'`) when the custom key is not a function of the `GROUP BY` keys. For example `SELECT count()` previously returned one partial row per replica instead of the merged total; now the initiator merges the partial results. ### Description Custom key parallel replicas skip the merging step on the initiator by setting `distributed_group_by_no_merge = 2`, so per-replica results are concatenated as-is. This is only correct when every row that shares a `GROUP BY` key is processed by a single replica, i.e. when the custom key is a function of the `GROUP BY` keys. Previously `distributed_group_by_no_merge = 2` was set unconditionally for a Distributed/cluster table with a custom key, so a query with aggregation whose `GROUP BY` does not cover the custom key (including plain aggregation without `GROUP BY`, e.g. `SELECT count()`) returned one partial row per replica. The fix keeps the no-merge fast path only when the custom key references only columns that are themselves plain `GROUP BY` keys (and the query has no `WITH ROLLUP`/`CUBE`/`TOTALS`/`GROUPING SETS`). Otherwise the merge is left enabled and the initiator produces the correct result. Applied on both the old and the new analyzer code paths. This is antonio2368's suggested first step from the issue thread ("not enable `distributed_group_by_no_merge` if custom key doesn't contain expression from `GROUP BY`"). The suitable-`GROUP BY` case (custom key is a function of the grouping keys) still uses the fast no-merge path.
