signal.title: Pin patch parts in MUTATE_PART log entries for deterministic mutations
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/100493 (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/100493 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `CHECKSUM_DOESNT_MATCH` errors and a stuck mutation loop that could occur on `ReplicatedMergeTree` tables using lightweight updates (`enable_block_number_column`/`enable_block_offset_column`) under concurrent `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE`. A `MUTATE_PART` replicated log entry now records the exact set of patch parts to apply, so all replicas produce a byte-identical mutated part. ### Description Fixes [#100493](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/100493). Unlike `MERGE_PARTS`, a `MUTATE_PART` replicated log entry did not record the set of patch parts (produced by lightweight updates) that must be applied while producing the mutated part. Each replica derived the applicable patches from its own local visible state (`MutateTask::prepare` -> `getMutationsSnapshot(need_patch_parts=true)`). When a patch part was committed on the replica that assigned the mutation but not yet replicated to another replica, the two replicas executing the same `MUTATE_PART` entry applied different patch sets and produced byte-different mutated parts. This raised `CHECKSUM_DOESNT_MATCH` ("Data after mutation is not byte-identical to data on another replicas"), and the losing replica got stuck fetching the part, hanging the cluster under load. This matches the reporter's setup exactly: same-version 2-node cluster, `ReplicatedReplacingMergeTree` with block-number/offset columns, concurrent `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE`. The fix mirrors how merges already pin patch parts: - `createLogEntryToMutatePart` records the applicable patch parts (partition match + `data_version < mutation_version`) into `entry.patch_parts`. - `ReplicatedMergeTreeLogEntry` serializes/parses them for `MUTATE_PART` (field `mutation_patches:`; distinct leading character from the other mutate fields because `checkString` consumes a matching prefix). - `MutateFromLogEntryTask::prepare` resolves the pinned patch parts locally, waiting for exactly that set and falling back to fetching the mutated part if one is missing (mirrors `MergeFromLogEntryTask`). - `MutateTask::prepare` applies exactly the pinned set instead of deriving from local visible state. The new log-entry field is written only when patch parts exist, i.e. only for tables using lightweight updates, so behavior is unchanged for existing setups. **Validation** (single server, two co-located `ReplicatedMergeTree` replicas, block columns on, 200k rows, concurrent mixed lightweight `UPDATE`+`DELETE` + `OPTIMIZE FINAL`, identical config): - Without the fix (master): 26 `CHECKSUM_DOESNT_MATCH` ("Data after mutation is not byte-identical") on `MutateFromLogEntryTask`. - With the fix: 0 mismatches, 0 parse errors. The pinned-patch wait/fetch-fallback path was confirmed firing on the lagging replica. Note: the added integration test (`test_lwu_replicated_mutation_pins_patches`) was authored to exercise the divergent-patch window deterministically, but I was unable to run the Docker-based integration suite locally in this environment; the fix itself was validated with the stress reproducer above.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Fix doubled written_rows for INSERT into Distributed with local shards
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106361 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106361 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `written_rows` being reported as twice the actual value in `system.query_log` and `system.view_refreshes` for an `INSERT` into a `Distributed` table that writes to local shards (for example a Refreshable Materialized View appending to a `Distributed` target). ### Description `INSERT` into a `Distributed` table over local shards reported `written_rows` at 2x the real value. Reported in #106361 for a Refreshable Materialized View whose target is a `Distributed` table (`system.view_refreshes.written_rows` = 180052 while `system.query_log` = 90026 and only 90026 rows were actually written), but the same doubling happens for a plain `INSERT INTO dist SELECT ...`. Root cause: the nested per-shard local `InterpreterInsertQuery` in `DistributedSink` ran with a context that still carried the parent query's progress callback and process-list element. Its own `CountingTransform` therefore re-counted rows that the top-level `CountingTransform` of the distributed `INSERT` had already accounted, feeding both `system.query_log.written_rows` (via the process-list element) and `system.view_refreshes.written_rows` (via `RefreshTask`'s progress callback). The `RemoteSink` path (`prefer_localhost_replica=0`) does not share the parent's accounting, so only the local-shard path doubled. Fix: detach the nested local insert from the parent's write-progress accounting in both the synchronous (`runWritingJob`) and asynchronous (`writeToLocal`) local-write paths. Verified locally against the reproducer from the issue and a plain distributed `INSERT`: `written_rows` and `view_refreshes.written_rows` now report 1000 (was 2000). Added stateless regression test `04500_distributed_insert_written_rows_not_doubled`.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Fix logical error in optimize_or_like_chain with aggregate/window function on LIKE LHS
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a logical error (`Function node with name '...' is not resolved as ordinary function`) that could occur with `optimize_or_like_chain` enabled when an aggregate or window function appeared on the left-hand side of a `LIKE`/`ILIKE`/`match` inside an `OR` chain. ### Description Found by the BuzzHouse fuzzer (STID 3477-117d) on [this CI run](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=107567&sha=16ccfffe167f14e51996ce4ec16384f92e4d15d0&name_0=PR&name_1=BuzzHouse%20%28amd_msan%29). Not caused by that PR — it is a trunk analyzer bug the fuzzer happened to surface there. `isExpressionNonDeterministic` in `ConvertOrLikeChainPass` guarded its `getFunctionOrThrow()` call with `FunctionNode::isResolved()`. `isResolved()` returns true for aggregate and window functions too (it only checks that the function pointer is set), but `getFunctionOrThrow()` throws `LOGICAL_ERROR` when the function kind is not `ORDINARY`. So a resolved aggregate (e.g. `count()`) or window function nested under a `LIKE` argument in an `OR` chain tripped the assertion — an exception in release builds, an abort in debug/sanitizer builds. Fix: guard with `isOrdinaryFunction()` instead, matching the existing correct guard in `PlannerExpressionAnalysis`. Aggregate/window functions are never non-deterministic-in-scope-of-query at this point, so recursing into their children is sufficient. Minimal reproducer (aborts before the fix on a debug build): ```sql SET optimize_or_like_chain = 1; SELECT toString(count()) LIKE '%1%' OR toString(count()) LIKE '%2%' FROM numbers(3); ``` Covered by `tests/queries/0_stateless/04545_optimize_or_like_chain_aggregate_lhs.sql` (aggregate and window variants, plus an ordinary-function control that must still collapse).
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Speed up wide-table sorting by skipping per-row replicated-column check in merge
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107611 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Speed up sorting of wide tables (`ORDER BY` over many columns) by skipping a per-row `ColumnReplicated` check in the merge step when no column can be replicated. This removes overhead that was noticeable on ARM. ### Description Addresses https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107611 (ARM regression on `sort_wide_table` query `1`: `SELECT * FROM sort_wide_16 ORDER BY k1, k2 FORMAT Null`). The reported regression scope is the `ColumnReplicated` wrapping added to `MergedData` by #101036. That change added a per-row, per-column `raw_columns[i]->isReplicated()` check to `MergedData::insertRow` / `insertRows`, wrapping the destination in `ColumnReplicated` when a source is replicated. That wrapping is only needed when the merge is fed by a JOIN with `enable_lazy_columns_replication = 1`. For a plain sort with no JOIN, no column is ever `ColumnReplicated`, so the virtual call runs once per column per row (18 columns x ~500K rows for `sort_wide_16`) as pure overhead in the hot row-by-row insertion loop. Fix, aligned with the existing design (keep the wrapping where it is genuinely needed): - Add a `may_have_replicated_columns` hint to `MergedData`, default `true`, so every algorithm keeps the current wrapping behavior unless it explicitly opts out. When the hint is `false`, `insertRow` / `insertRows` take a tight loop identical to the pre-#101036 behavior; when `true`, the wrapping path is byte-for-byte unchanged. - `MergingSortedAlgorithm` lowers the hint to `false` in `initialize` when no input column is `ColumnReplicated`, and raises it back to `true` monotonically in `consume` if a late-arriving chunk brings a replicated column — always before those rows can reach `insertRow`. A replicated source can only enter the merge through `initialize` or `consume`, so the wrapping is never skipped when it is needed. - Other algorithms that reuse `MergedData` (Aggregating, Summing, Collapsing, Replacing, VersionedCollapsing, GraphiteRollup) leave the hint at its default `true` and are unaffected. Validation on x86 (the ARM Neoverse-V2 numbers must come from the arm_release Performance Comparison job, which is the authoritative measurement): - New unit tests `MergedDataReplicated.FastPathSkipsWrappingForRegularColumns` and `RestoringFlagReenablesWrapping`, plus all 5 pre-existing `MergedDataReplicated` regression tests, pass. - A JOIN with `enable_lazy_columns_replication = 1` followed by `ORDER BY` (forces `ColumnReplicated` into the merge) produces results identical to `enable_lazy_columns_replication = 0` and stays correctly sorted. - Stateless tests `03580_external_merge_sort_with_lazy_columns`, `03709_replicated_columns_right_join`, `03701_replicated_column_short_circuit_filter`, `03352_lazy_column_filter_by_uint8` pass.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Do not abort server startup when a URL table's named collection is missing
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/105045 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed the server failing to start (`Cannot start clickhouse-server`) when a `URL` table references a named collection that no longer exists. A collection can be legitimately dropped while a dependent `URL` table exists (with `check_named_collection_dependencies = false`), and the `ATTACH` replayed at startup then threw `NAMED_COLLECTION_DOESNT_EXIST`. The table now attaches and the error is reported at query time. ### Description Reported on #105045 but unrelated to it: `Stress test` on `03822_named_collection_drop_dependency_check` fails to restart the server, with `ATTACH TABLE ... ENGINE = URL(...)` hitting `NAMED_COLLECTION_DOESNT_EXIST`. Reproduces on master. Root cause: the `URL` engine resolves its named collection eagerly at attach time (`StorageURL::getConfiguration`), but `check_named_collection_dependencies = false` lets a collection be dropped while dependent `URL` tables exist. The persisted `ATTACH` replayed at startup then aborts the server under synchronous loading. Fix: when replaying a definition stored on this server, a missing collection attaches a lazy proxy instead of aborting; it is re-resolved on first read/write, and if still missing the query fails `NAMED_COLLECTION_DOESNT_EXIST`. A definition the user supplies now (`CREATE`, full-definition `ATTACH`, `RESTORE`, Replicated DDL) still fails its own DDL instead of persisting an unusable table, gated on the predicate `StorageDistributed` uses. Also fixed while under review, every case where `StorageProxy` answers through `getNested()` (which materializes), so the proxy reported the missing collection where eager `URL` answers directly: the engine classification (`isObjectStorage`/`isDataLake`/`isMessageQueue`/`isExternalDatabase`), read by `InterpreterInsertQuery` before the materializing `write()`, so an object-storage-backed `URL(nc)` was rejected `QUERY_IS_PROHIBITED` under `disable_insertion_and_mutation` where the eager form inserted; and `checkAlterPartitionIsPossible`, `alterPartition`, `getCheckTaskList`, `getActionLock`, `supportsReplication`, `getColumnSizes`, where partition DDL and `CHECK TABLE` reported `NAMED_COLLECTION_DOESNT_EXIST` instead of `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` and the last three are swept over every table, so one unresolvable table made `system.tables`, `system.columns` and bulk `SYSTEM STOP MERGES` throw. Validated in both directions with `04540_url_named_collection_missing_on_attach` and `tests/integration/test_disable_insertion_and_mutation`, including a real restart with the collection still missing. `S3`/`Azure`/`HDFS` resolve collections in their own `fromAST` path and may share this.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Do not flatten a Set-engine array table on the right of IN
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110505 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `Code: 48. NOT_IMPLEMENTED: Method read is not supported by storage Set` when a `Set`-engine table, or a `Alias` table pointing at one, is used on the right side of `IN`. Such tables are now always consumed as a prepared set instead of being read, in the analyzer, the legacy `IN` implementation, and the serialized-plan path. Closes #110505. ### Description Closes: #110505 A single-`Array`-column table on the right of `IN` is rewritten into a `SELECT column FROM table` subquery so its elements become the set elements. A `Set`-engine table matches that shape but has no `read` method: it is meant to be consumed natively as a prepared set. So the rewrite made `IN` over set-backed tables fail with `Code: 48. NOT_IMPLEMENTED: Method read is not supported by storage Set`. The three places that decide "is this a set-backed table" each looked only at the immediate storage, so a `Alias` wrapper (whose `read` delegates to its target) was never recognized. This adds a shared helper, `getSetStorageFromTable`, that resolves through an alias chain and matches `StorageSet` including derived types, and routes all three call sites through it: the analyzer (`Analyzer/Resolve/resolveFunction.cpp`, `Planner/CollectSets.cpp`), the legacy implementation (`Interpreters/ActionsVisitor.cpp`, reached with `enable_analyzer = 0`), and plan deserialization (`Processors/QueryPlan/SetsSerialization.cpp`, reached in distributed-plan execution). Reproduces on released versions, so this is not master-only: ```sql CREATE TABLE t (arr Array(UInt8)) ENGINE = Set; INSERT INTO t VALUES ([1, 2, 3]); CREATE TABLE a ENGINE = Alias('t'); SELECT [1, 2, 3] IN a; -- 26.5/26.6/26.7: NOT_IMPLEMENTED; now 1 SELECT 2 IN t; -- 26.7: NOT_IMPLEMENTED; now TYPE_MISMATCH ``` `ENGINE = Alias` is generally available in all three (`allow_experimental_alias_table_engine` is obsolete), and the same query over an `Alias` to a readable table always worked, so the failure was specific to set-backed targets. Access checking is unchanged from before the rewrite: a set-backed alias on the right of `IN` requires the same grants as an equivalent `Alias` to a `MergeTree` table, verified across 5 grant combinations in both analyzer modes and on the serialized-plan path. Regressions: `04512_in_function_array_subquery_right_argument` (direct, alias, legacy mode, access) and `04652_in_set_alias_serialized_query_plan` (serialized plan).

signal.title: Skip sharding key IN rewrite when the sharding key contains a set
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107619 --> Related: #107619 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix the `Not-ready Set is passed as the second argument for function 'in'` logical error that could be thrown when a `Distributed` table's sharding key expression itself contained an `IN`/subquery (a set) and `optimize_skip_unused_shards_rewrite_in` was enabled. ### Description Found by the AST fuzzer (STID `0250-4e52`, tracked in #107619). Reported on the arm_debug Stress test of PR #101039; per @ alexey-milovidov the failure is unrelated to that PR, so this is a separate fix. Reproducer (aborts in debug/sanitizer builds): ```sql SELECT * FROM remoteSecure('127.{1..8}', view(SELECT number AS id FROM numbers(0)), bitAnd(1025, murmurHash3_32(minus(id, (2 IN (SELECT 1)))))) WHERE id IN (2, 3) LIMIT 444 SETTINGS optimize_skip_unused_shards = 1, optimize_skip_unused_shards_rewrite_in = 1, allow_nondeterministic_optimize_skip_unused_shards = 1; ``` CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=101039&sha=8b127de6068682ddc50262e918ab1a7dd3a0a307&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_debug%29 Root cause: `OptimizeShardingKeyRewriteIn` prunes shards by executing the standalone sharding-key `ExpressionActions` on constant values (`shardContains` -> `executeFunctionOnField`). The sharding-key expression is built directly from the sharding-key AST, so an `IN`/subquery in the sharding key becomes a `FunctionIn` whose set is never populated during planning. Executing it hits `FunctionIn::executeImpl` with an unbuilt set and throws the `Not-ready Set` logical error (`OptimizeShardingKeyRewriteInVisitor.cpp:36` -> `Functions/in.cpp:116`). Fix: skip the rewrite when the sharding-key expression contains a set, and query all shards instead. This is the same safe fallback already used for non-deterministic sharding keys, and the optimization was never valid for a set-containing key anyway (it cannot be constant-folded per value). Both the analyzer and old-analyzer call sites are guarded. Distinct from the other in-flight `Not-ready Set` fixes (#109722, #102192), which address the `buildOrderedSetInplace` / `QueryPlan` path; neither touches `OptimizeShardingKeyRewriteIn`.

signal.title: Fix materialized CTE self-reference in set operation
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110176 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes two errors when a materialized CTE is named identically to a base table it reads inside its own body: a `LOGICAL_ERROR` (`Reading from materialized CTE before its materialization completed - DelayedPortsProcessor gate is missing`) when the body is a set operation, e.g. `WITH test1 AS MATERIALIZED ((SELECT i FROM test1) EXCEPT ALL (SELECT i FROM test1)) SELECT 4 AS i WHERE i IN (test1)`, and `TOO_DEEP_SUBQUERIES` when the CTE is referenced twice, e.g. `WITH test1 AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT i FROM test1) SELECT count() FROM test1, test1 AS t2`. ### Description Found by the AST fuzzer (STID 2467-2c2d), still live on master. A distinct, non-`EXPLAIN ANALYZE` manifestation of the `DelayedPortsProcessor gate is missing` site. A materialized CTE named the same as a base table it reads inside its own body must bind that self-reference to the base table (recursive CTEs are not supported here), exactly like a non-materialized CTE. The guard in `tryResolveIdentifierFromCTE` tests the node stored in `scope.cte_name_to_query_node` against `ctes_in_resolve_process`, so only that node works as a guard. The guard has three call sites, and two were passing the wrong node or none at all: 1. The expression path in `resolveExpressionNode` inserted the freshly cloned `TableNode` placeholder, which the guard never looks up. With a set-operation body the guard did not fire on the second branch, so `FROM test1` there bound to the still-unmaterialized CTE and the plan read its `StorageMemory` with no `DelayedPortsProcessor` gate, tripping the fail-fast in `ReadFromMemoryStorageStep`. 2. The reused-reference branch of `resolveQueryJoinTreeNode` (taken when another reference already created the storage) resolves this clone's own unresolved copy of the body but inserted nothing. A body reference bound back to the CTE, re-entered the same branch and recursed until `TOO_DEEP_SUBQUERIES`. Reaching it needs two consumers, not a set operation, which is why the first version of the test did not cover it; found by the AI reviewer on this PR. Both now insert the `cte_name_to_query_node` node. The scope walk that finds it was duplicated per site and is now `findCTENodeInScopes`, so the three sites cannot drift apart again. Verified against the non-materialized CTE as an oracle, plus a plan assertion that the CTE really is materialized. Genuine recursive CTEs are still rejected. No performance impact: this only changes which node a set insert/erase uses during name resolution.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Read Replicated database DDL finished node status atomically via LIST_WITH_STAT_AND_DATA
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109192 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109192 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Follow-up to #109192 requested by @alexey-milovidov (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109192#discussion_r3544661542), implementing @tuanpach's suggestion to read the `finished/<host_id>` payload atomically with the finished-node listing via Keeper's `LIST_WITH_STAT_AND_DATA`. The debug/sanitizer-only cross-check in `ReplicatedDatabaseQueryStatusSource::checkStatus` read `finished/<host_id>` with a separate `get` issued after `DistributedQueryStatusSource::generate()` had already listed the finished children. That second read could race the DDL cleaner between the listing and the get. When the connected Keeper advertises `LIST_WITH_STAT_AND_DATA`, `generate()` now lists the finished nodes together with their payloads in a single request (`with_data = true`) and caches them, so `checkStatus` reads the status from that consistent snapshot instead of a separate get. A subclass opts in through the new `wantsFinishedNodeData()` (default `false`), so the `ON CLUSTER` path (`DDLOnClusterQueryStatusSource`) keeps the plain listing unchanged. When the feature flag is not negotiated, it falls back to the existing per-host `getExecutionStatus`. The read remains `DEBUG_OR_SANITIZER_BUILD`-only, so there is no user-visible behavior change; the release path still returns success without reading the node. Verified on a debug build (embedded Keeper advertising `LIST_WITH_STAT_AND_DATA`): a normal Replicated-database DDL succeeds via the atomic read path, and the `replicated_database_status_finished_node_missing` failpoint still yields the benign absent-node success, with the server staying alive and no `LOGICAL_ERROR`/abort.

signal.title: Fix LOGICAL_ERROR in server AST fuzzer safety-limit stripping on desynced SETTINGS
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108212 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description The server-side AST fuzzer strips its safety-limit settings (`max_rows_to_read`, `max_execution_time`, ...) from each fuzzed query so a fuzzed `SETTINGS max_rows_to_read = 0` cannot lift the pinned resource caps. When stripping empties a SETTINGS clause, `removeSettingsFromQuery` detached the clause from its owner via `IAST::reset`, which hard-throws `LOGICAL_ERROR "AST subtree not found in children"` if the owner's settings slot is set but its pointer is not registered in `children`. The AST fuzzer explicitly can produce such structurally-invalid ASTs (`executeQuery.cpp` only skips them at format time, and this strip runs before that guard), so the desync aborted the server in debug/sanitizer builds instead of being skipped. Found by BuzzHouse (amd_tsan): `stripFuzzerSafetyLimitSettings` -> `removeSettingsFromQuery` (`stripQuerySettings.cpp:140`) -> `IAST::reset` (`IAST.h:269`). CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109000&sha=8b77fe6ef18a638bcbc188de2e154324262cef13&name_0=PR&name_1=BuzzHouse%20%28amd_tsan%29 Fix: detach the emptied slot tolerantly (erase the child if present, then clear the slot) in the INSERT, `ASTQueryWithOutput` and `ASTStorage` branches, matching the already-tolerant SELECT (`setExpression({})`) and BACKUP (`settings.reset()`) branches. Adds a gtest that desyncs the settings slot from `children` for each affected carrier and asserts the strip no longer aborts.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Fix wrong primary-key pruning for toStartOfDay and relative-number functions on out-of-range DateTime64
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/90461 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108018 --> Related: #90461 Related: #108018 Closes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112071 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed wrong `count()` results and dropped rows when a `DateTime64` primary-key column is filtered through `toStartOfDay`, `toRelativeSecondNum`, `toRelativeMinuteNum`, `toRelativeHourNum`, `toRelativeDayNum`, `toRelativeWeekNum`, `toMonthNumSinceEpoch` or `toYearNumSinceEpoch` with values outside the `UInt32`-seconds range (before 1970 or beyond 2106). These functions claim to be always monotonic to the primary index but their standard-precision results wrapped for out-of-range `DateTime64`, breaking primary-key pruning. ### Description The `DateTime64` sibling of #108018 (which fixed the same class for `Date32`). `toStartOfDay` and the relative-number transforms have `FactorTransform = ZeroTransform`, so `IFunctionDateOrDateTime::getMonotonicityForRange` reports them as always monotonic. Their standard-precision `DateTime64` code paths narrowed the result to `UInt32`/`UInt16` without saturating, so for arguments outside that range the value wrapped and the function stopped being monotonic. This makes primary-key range analysis produce exact ranges that extend before the selected mark range, which: - in release builds: silently drops granules holding matching rows, returning a wrong `count()`; - in debug/sanitizer builds: trips `chassert(exact_ranges[i].begin >= range.begin)` in the trivial-count projection optimization (`optimizeUseAggregateProjection.cpp`). Found by the AST fuzzer (amd_msan) on a query that mutated a `Date32` key column to `DateTime64(5)`: `SELECT count() FROM t WHERE toStartOfDay(d) >= toDateTime('2000-01-01 00:00:00','UTC') SETTINGS force_primary_key = 1`. Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/PRs/110310/e242401ecdb1e933c8646546bc2f905d4ed106cd/ast_fuzzer_amd_msan/fatal.log The fix saturates the `DateTime64` `execute` overloads to `[0, result-type max]`, matching the `Date32` fix in #108018, keeping each function monotonic over the whole `DateTime64` domain. Adds `04538_datetime64_zerotransform_monotonicity_pruning`; updates the references of `01768_extended_range`, `04408_datediff_datetime64_overflow` and `02403_enable_extended_results_for_datetime_functions`, which asserted the previous wrapped standard-precision results.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Fix LOGICAL_ERROR in KeyCondition over LowCardinality key exposed through Merge
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109699 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109699 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a `LOGICAL_ERROR` ("Arguments of 'minus'/'plus' have incorrect data types") during primary-key index analysis when a monotonic arithmetic function is applied over a `LowCardinality` key column exposed through a `Merge` table whose header declares the plain type. ### Description `KeyCondition::applyFunction` executed a monotonic key function on the raw index column while the function was resolved against the plain key type. When a `Merge` table declares a plain header (e.g. `UInt32`) over a source whose key column is `LowCardinality(UInt32)`, the index column loaded from the child part is `LowCardinality`, but the function expects the plain type. The function then received a `LowCardinality` column dispatched as its plain type and threw a `LOGICAL_ERROR` during PK index analysis (a server abort in debug and sanitizer builds). Both reported argument types are the plain type in the message because the divergence is column-representation vs declared-type. The fix strips `LowCardinality` from the argument column and its type in lockstep before executing, mirroring the sibling `applyFunctionChainToColumn` which already calls `convertToFullColumnIfLowCardinality` + `removeLowCardinality`. Found by the AST fuzzer (STID 2735-50e2). CI report: [AST fuzzer (amd_debug)](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=108325&sha=d9014f8f51d3c4aa2117437a9f6f38fc40d78d2c&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%29). Verified the regression test aborts on `master` HEAD with the exact fuzzer error and passes with this change. PK pruning results over the `LowCardinality` key match the plain-key results.

signal.title: Backfill Iceberg identity-partition columns absent from data files
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110216 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a bug where an Iceberg identity-partition column that is absent from the data files (its value stored only in the manifest partition tuple, as produced by Hive-partitioned / Microsoft Fabric tables) was read as `NULL` for every row. The column is now backfilled from the manifest partition value, so `SELECT`, `WHERE` and `GROUP BY` on it return correct results. ### Description Related issue: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110216 When an Iceberg identity-partition source column is not physically stored in the data files (its value exists only in the Iceberg manifest partition tuple, e.g. Microsoft Fabric / OneLake / Apache XTable-virtualized tables), reading the column returned `NULL` for every row. `count()` was correct (served from partition statistics) but selecting the column and any `WHERE` / `GROUP BY` on it were silently wrong. Fix: - Each data file's identity-partition values are parsed from the manifest partition spec entries whose transform is `identity`, mapped to the current schema column name, and carried to the read source (`IcebergIterator`). The read source overwrites the otherwise `NULL`-filled output column with the per-file constant (`StorageObjectStorageSource`). - Identity-partition columns are excluded from `supportedPrewhereColumns()`. Otherwise the planner pushes a filter on such a column into PREWHERE, and the format reader reads the absent column as `NULL` before the backfill runs, dropping every row. With the exclusion the condition is applied as a regular filter above the source, after the backfill. Filters on physical columns still use PREWHERE. - The manifest values are serialized to cluster workers behind a new cluster processing protocol version. Reproduction (a data file with the partition column removed, leaving the value only in the manifest): see the added test `tests/queries/0_stateless/04500_iceberg_identity_partition_backfill.sh`, which covers projection, filtering under both PREWHERE modes, `count()`, `GROUP BY`, multiple identity-partition columns of different types, and a mixed filter over an identity-partition column and a physical column.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Fix Inconsistent AST formatting for aliased IN nested in a function argument
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110223 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110223 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed an `Inconsistent AST formatting` logical error for an aliased `IN` expression whose left operand also has an alias when it is nested inside a function-argument list, e.g. `SELECT ifNull(sum((x AS a1) IN [y] AS c3 = TRUE), 0)`. ### Description The query `SELECT ifNull(sum((x AS a1) IN [y] AS c3 = TRUE), 0)` (found by BuzzHouse, `amd_debug`) aborted the server with an `Inconsistent AST formatting between 'ExpressionList' and 'ExpressionList'` logical error in debug/sanitizer builds. Root cause: the formatter was not round-trip stable. First format produced `(((x AS a1) IN [y]) AS c3)` — the alias-wrap branch in `ASTWithAlias::formatImpl` opened one pair of parens but left `current_function` set, so the descendant `IN` operator (which parenthesizes itself when it is a function argument) added a second isolating pair. The re-parse then marked the `IN` node `parenthesized`, and the second format dropped the inner pair, yielding `((x AS a1) IN [y] AS c3)` — a different AST. Fix: clear `current_function`/`list_element_index` in the alias-wrap branch (mirroring `decideParensEmission`), so the descendant `IN` sees it is already isolated by the alias wrap and does not add redundant parens. Added a regression test asserting `formatQuerySingleLine` is idempotent for this and sibling cases.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Fix LOGICAL_ERROR in join order optimizer for duplicate column names via merged expression
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a `LOGICAL_ERROR` (`Left and right columns have same names`) in the join order optimizer that could be triggered by a comma join over a multi-table view when `query_plan_merge_expression_into_join` is enabled. ### Description No related open issue found. Found by the SQLancerPP nightly on master (server abort in the sanitizer build): https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=3d31d8f59df88ee56b9b739f2eedb1b7a6acc6a4&name_0=NightlySQLancer&name_1=SQLancerPP The pre-reorder guard `joinGraphHasOverlappingColumnNames` flattens the join graph to check for duplicate qualified column names and skips reordering when it finds any. It peeled only passthrough expression steps. The optimizer's `addChildQueryGraph` also peels a non-passthrough expression step and flattens the child join beneath it when `query_plan_merge_expression_into_join` is enabled. So the guard saw one relation fewer than the optimizer produced and missed a duplicated name (`__table3.c1`); reconstructing the reordered join with `JoinExpressionActions` then threw the error. Fix: make the guard peel expression steps the same way as `addChildQueryGraph`, so it inspects the same relation set the optimizer builds and correctly skips reordering when names overlap. Known residual, not addressed here: this guard is a read-only mirror of `buildQueryGraph`, and it does not replicate the `get_exposed_columns` side-clash suppression that keeps a join boundary collapsed. That predates this PR (the mirror landed in `2ddbf356499caa5`, the clash check a week later in `69f802454c23ee6`) and can only cost a reordering, never correctness. I have not found a query where the two disagree, so I have left it for a separate change rather than adding an unexercised check here.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Apply AST size limits to the query generated by table function eval
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110132 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Apply the AST size limits `max_ast_depth` and `max_ast_elements` to the query generated by the `eval` table function, same as for a query executed directly. ### Description Follow-up to #110132 (per @ alexey-milovidov's review request on `src/TableFunctions/TableFunctionEval.cpp`). `eval` parses and stores the generated inner `SELECT` but, unlike `executeQueryImpl`, never applied the AST size limits. That made `max_ast_depth` / `max_ast_elements` ineffective for the inner query: a tiny outer `SELECT * FROM eval('...')` could smuggle a huge or very deep AST into the analyzer, even though executing the same inner query directly would be rejected. This applies `checkDepth`/`checkSize` to the generated query, reading the limits from a context that already has the generated query's own `SETTINGS` applied. The settings are resolved before the normalization visitors rewrite the query tree (which can move or drop the `SETTINGS` clause), so an inner `... SETTINGS max_ast_elements = N` controls its own limits both to tighten and to relax them, the same way it would for a standalone query. Regression tests added to `04512_eval_table_function`.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Read database metadata files synchronously to avoid file-offset assertion
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/104692 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ### Description Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/104692 `readMetadataFile()` reads a table/database `.sql` metadata file with `getReadSettingsForMetadata()`, which forces `RemoteFSReadMethod::threadpool`. On object-storage-backed metadata that produces an `AsynchronousBoundedReadBuffer`, which caches the file size at construction and asserts `file_offset_of_buffer_end <= getFileSize()` in `nextImpl()`. Metadata `.sql` files are mutable: `ALTER`/`RENAME` rewrite them in place. A concurrent rewrite that grows the object under an already-open reader makes the inner reader return bytes past the cached size, tripping the assert and aborting the server in debug/sanitizer builds. The read is a single full-file read of a tiny file, so none of the size-snapshotting stages buy anything here. The fix pins the metadata read to the plain synchronous `ReadBufferFromRemoteFSGather`, which has no cached-size assertion, by disabling the three stages the pipeline may otherwise pick: the async prefetch buffer (`RemoteFSReadMethod::read`), the reader executor, and the in-memory page cache. The fix is in the single `readMetadataFile()` free function, so it covers all metadata read sites (`DatabaseOrdinary`, `DatabaseOnDisk`, `DatabaseReplicated`, startup load). Found by the BuzzHouse (amd_msan) and stateless flaky-check fuzzers. Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110127&sha=1f4a1b8f87ea4ec3270939654c508b009bde65da&name_0=PR&name_1=BuzzHouse%20%28amd_msan%29 Reproduced deterministically on an object-storage metadata disk under ThreadFuzzer (`ENGINE = Buffer` table + concurrent `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COMMENT` with varying comment lengths + `SELECT FROM system.tables`): server aborts within ~90s without the fix; survives a 35-minute run with it.

signal.title: Use fewer stateful-prepare insert threads for regular sanitizer runs
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110152 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description The stateful data prepare step runs `INSERT INTO test.hits_s3 SELECT * FROM test.hits` with `max_insert_threads=16`. On regular sanitizer Stateless jobs this single INSERT tracks ~24 GiB and pushes ASan RSS to ~42 GiB, which memcg-OOM-kills the server (`Server died` + `OOM in dmesg`). #109954 already reduced this to 4 threads on sanitizer builds, but only for the bugfix-validation path, because `build_type` is only passed there. On regular runs `build_type` is `None`, so `is_sanitizer` was always `False` and the INSERT still used 16 threads. Fix: when `build_type` is not passed, fall back to `Info().job_name` to detect the sanitizer, mirroring the existing `limit_source` pattern in `functional_tests.py::run_tests` (which already does `build_type if build_type is not None else Info().job_name`). Same data is loaded, just a smaller peak. Example failure (amd_asan_ubsan, distributed plan, parallel): peak server MemoryTracking 24.2 GiB at 17:47:14 from the single hits_s3 INSERT; server OOM-killed at 42 GiB anon-rss. Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110152&sha=729886a3f8576eae108e6bd09bc29c4922a39212&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_asan_ubsan%2C%20distributed%20plan%2C%20parallel%29

signal.title: Fix use-of-uninitialized-value in WITH FILL suffix over a merge
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107074 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a use-of-uninitialized-value in `ORDER BY ... WITH FILL ... STALENESS` when the fill suffix generates no rows (for example when the staleness window leaves nothing to fill) and the result is read through a merge of sorted streams (such as a two-shard `Distributed` table). ### Description Found by the AST fuzzer under MSan on top of #107074. `FillingTransform`, when all input chunks are processed, may run the suffix path. If the fill constraints are satisfied but no fill rows are produced (e.g. `WITH FILL ... STALENESS` with an exhausted staleness window), `generateSuffixIfNeeded` returns `true` while the result columns are freshly `cloneEmpty()`'d and carry no data. Previously the transform still emitted a 0-row chunk built from those empty columns. A downstream `MergingSortedTransform` (as used when reading from a two-shard `Distributed` table) then built a sort cursor over that empty chunk and compared row 0, reading past the end of the empty column. Fix: do not emit the suffix chunk when it has no rows. Minimal reproducer (needs a two-shard merge on the initiator): ```sql CREATE TABLE m (key Int) ENGINE = Memory; INSERT INTO m VALUES (100); CREATE TABLE d2 AS m ENGINE = Distributed(test_cluster_two_shards_localhost, currentDatabase(), m); SELECT _shard_num FROM d2 ORDER BY _shard_num ASC WITH FILL TO 46 STALENESS 1; ``` CI finding: `AST fuzzer (amd_msan)`, report https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=107074&sha=3ec54c88d4eb535a5d644fc1ab91af31d717f9a5&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_msan%29 MSan use-of-uninitialized-value in `ColumnVector<UInt32>::doCompareAt` (`MergingSortedAlgorithm::consume`), origin `FillingTransform::initColumns` (`cloneEmpty`) via the suffix path. Verified on a local `amd_msan` build: reproduces before the fix (server aborts), clean after; the new regression test returns `1\n2`.

signal.title: Preserve parameters in aggregate functions that dropped them, fixing the `-Array` combinator assert
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104812 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a `LOGICAL_ERROR` (a server abort in debug and sanitizer builds) when the `-Array` combinator is applied with parameters to `argMin`, `argMax`, `argAndMin`, `argAndMax`, `min_by`, `max_by`, `groupArrayMovingSum`, `groupArrayMovingAvg`, `kolmogorovSmirnovTest`, `mannWhitneyUTest` or `intervalLengthSum`, for example `argMaxArray(2)([1, 2, 3], [1, 2, 3])`. These functions dropped the parameters they were given; they now preserve them, so a state type name also keeps them, e.g. `AggregateFunction(groupArrayMovingSum(42), UInt64)` instead of dropping the window size. ### Description Found by the AST fuzzer. Example abort: ``` Logical error: 'AggregateFunctionArray: parameters mismatch between Array wrapper 'groupArrayMovingSumArray' and nested function 'groupArrayMovingSum'. Wrapper has 1 parameter(s): [UInt64_42], nested function has 0 parameter(s): []'. ``` Reproducers, one per affected family: ```sql SELECT groupArrayMovingSumArray(42)([1, 2, 3]); SELECT argMaxArray(2)([1, 2, 3], [1, 2, 3]); SELECT intervalLengthSumArray('two-sided', 1)([0., 1], [10., 3]); SELECT mannWhitneyUTestArray('two-sided', 1)([1., 2, 3, 4], [0., 0, 1, 1]); ``` Root cause: each of these functions built its `IAggregateFunctionDataHelper` base with an empty parameter array instead of the parameters it was passed, so `getParameters` returned `[]`. The `-Array` combinator does not transform parameters and asserts that the wrapper's parameters equal the nested function's; with the wrapper carrying `[42]` and the nested function returning `[]`, the invariant fired. `groupArrayMovingSum`/`groupArrayMovingAvg` and `kolmogorovSmirnovTest`/`mannWhitneyUTest` are the set listed in the TODO added by #104812. `intervalLengthSum` and the `argMin`/`argMax` family instead accepted parameters and silently ignored them, so hard-rejecting them would make existing `AggregateFunction(argMin(...), ...)` metadata unreadable on upgrade; for those the parameters are preserved and normalized away in the state type via `getNormalizedStateType`, keeping legacy parameterless state columns `Merge`- and `CAST`-compatible. No performance impact: the change only forwards an already-constructed parameter array to a base constructor, with no work added on any aggregation hot path. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104812

signal.title: Push filter above INTERSECT/EXCEPT into input branches
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110113 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110113 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Push a filter above `INTERSECT` and `EXCEPT` (both `ALL` and `DISTINCT`) into the input branches, so each input can prune with its own primary key, as already happens for `UNION ALL`. ### Description A filter above `UNION ALL` is pushed into every branch. The same filter above `INTERSECT`/`EXCEPT` stayed above the set operation, so both inputs were read in full. `IntersectOrExceptStep` shares the properties the `UnionStep` case relies on (header unchanged, branches positionally aligned), so `filterPushDown` now applies the same transformation: clone the deterministic filter into each branch and remove the original. Equivalence-preserving for all set operators: values failing the predicate cannot appear in the output (INTERSECT ALL multiplicity = min(left, right); EXCEPT ALL = max(0, left - right); DISTINCT variants by the same argument on sets), so dropping them from every input is safe. The pass's existing global guard already rejects stateful/non-deterministic filters. Regression test `04401_filter_push_down_intersect_except` asserts via `EXPLAIN indexes=1` that the key condition reaches both branches for INTERSECT ALL/DISTINCT and EXCEPT ALL/DISTINCT, plus a correctness check preserving multiplicity. Reproducer from the issue: https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/4d1403c5-2a56-41dd-9401-4a84f1c52b24

signal.title: Prune partitions through identity ifNull/coalesce nested in a key expression
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110117 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109998 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110117 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109998 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed partition/primary key pruning being lost when an identity `ifNull(x, c)` or `coalesce(x, c)` over a non-Nullable column is nested inside a key expression (for example `PARTITION BY sipHash64(p)` with `WHERE sipHash64(ifNull(p, 0)) = ...` now prunes parts instead of scanning them all). Applies with the analyzer (`enable_analyzer = 1`, the default). ### Description `ifNull(x, c)` and `coalesce(x, c)` are pure identities on `x` when `x` cannot be NULL: the fallback is unreachable and the result type equals `x`. Both functions already fold their return type to the first argument, but the `FunctionNode` remained in the query tree, so `KeyCondition`'s syntactic key-expression matching failed whenever the wrapper was nested inside another key function. `WHERE sipHash64(ifNull(p, 0)) = sipHash64(3)` against `PARTITION BY sipHash64(p)` therefore scanned all parts instead of pruning to one. This adds a query tree pass (`RemoveRedundantIfNullCoalescePass`) replacing such identity calls with their first argument. It fires only when the argument cannot be NULL, the result type is unchanged, and every discarded fallback is a constant (`ifNull`/`coalesce` are not short-circuit, so a non-constant fallback must still be evaluated). It is gated on `allow_key_condition_coalesce_rewrite`, the same knob as the top-level rewrite. Pruning then sees the bare argument inside any key expression: partition key, primary key or skip index. **Scope:** being a query tree pass, this applies under the analyzer (`enable_analyzer = 1`, the default). The legacy `enable_analyzer = 0` path is unchanged and still scans all parts for the nested form. That path is being retired, and duplicating the rewrite plus its three correctness guards in `ExpressionAnalyzer` would mean keeping two implementations in sync, which is the reasoning applied in a8fd36400c95f4cf331b6f6f5644b032e57cb850 when `optimize_or_like_chain` was made analyzer-only. Regression test `03891_ifnull_coalesce_identity_nested_key_pruning` pins `enable_analyzer = 1` and covers the non-Nullable (prunes), Nullable (not simplified, correct results), setting-off and side-effect-fallback cases.

signal.title: Apply Iceberg schema evolution when compacting (OPTIMIZE)
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `OPTIMIZE` (compaction) of Iceberg tables after schema evolution (e.g. `ALTER TABLE ... RENAME COLUMN`). Data files written under an older schema were read by the current-schema column names, so the compacted file could get `DEFAULT`/`NULL` values instead of the original data, and the regenerated metadata could fail with `ICEBERG_SPECIFICATION_VIOLATION`. Requires `allow_experimental_iceberg_compaction`. ### Description `IcebergMetadata::optimize` builds the compaction reader header from the table's current schema (`getSampleBlock()`), and `Compaction.cpp` read/regenerated everything against the current schema, ignoring per-file schema ids. After schema evolution this had three consequences: 1. **Data read**: old data files were read by the current column names. The normal read path (`StorageObjectStorageSource`) handles this via `getInitialSchemaByPath` + `getSchemaTransformer`; compaction did not, so a renamed column was compacted into `DEFAULT`/`NULL`. 2. **Metadata regeneration**: `createEmptyMetadataFile` always synthesizes `schema-id 0` from the current column names with fresh field ids, rebinding `schema-id 0` to different fields (`ICEBERG_SPECIFICATION_VIOLATION` on the next read) and losing the field ids the data files reference. 3. **Snapshots**: regenerated snapshots were stamped with the current schema id while reusing the original snapshot ids, which are bound to their committed schema id on read (`snapshot already registered with schema id ...`). Fix: - `writeDataFiles` reads each data file by its own schema (`getClickhouseTableSchemaById`) and remaps it to the current schema via `getSchemaTransformationDagByIds`, mirroring the normal read path. Position deletes are applied first (they reference original file row positions), then surviving rows are remapped. - `writeMetadataFiles` carries the real `schemas`, `current-schema-id` and `last-column-id` from the source metadata, and preserves each snapshot's originally committed schema id. Added an integration regression (`test_storage_iceberg_no_spark/test_writes_optimize_after_rename.py`): INSERT, DELETE (positional delete so compaction has work), `RENAME COLUMN`, `OPTIMIZE` — asserts the renamed column keeps its original values (no `NULL`/`DEFAULT`) and the deleted row stays deleted. It fails before this change (`ICEBERG_SPECIFICATION_VIOLATION`) and passes after. Verified locally on `IcebergLocal` (format-version 2): before the fix `OPTIMIZE` leaves the table unreadable (`ICEBERG_SPECIFICATION_VIOLATION`); after the fix the renamed column reads back `hello`/`foo`, 0 NULLs, correct row count. A control run without rename confirms no change to the existing compaction path.

signal.title: Eliminate min/max/any/anyLast of LowCardinality GROUP BY keys
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110041 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `optimize_aggregators_of_group_by_keys` not eliminating `min`/`max`/`any`/`anyLast` of a `LowCardinality` `GROUP BY` key. The optimization was silently dead for `LowCardinality` columns, so a `HAVING` predicate on the key (e.g. `HAVING min(s) = 'x'`) was not pushed down to storage and could not use skip indexes, unlike the same query on a plain column. ### Description `optimize_aggregators_of_group_by_keys` (on by default) rewrites `min`/`max`/`any`/`anyLast` of a `GROUP BY` key to the key expression itself, so a `HAVING` predicate on the key can be pushed below the aggregation and prune granules via skip indexes. It never fired for `LowCardinality` keys: the pass required the aggregate's result type to be exactly equal to the argument type, but aggregate functions strip `LowCardinality` from their result (`min(LowCardinality(String))` returns `String`), so the check always failed. Fix: - Compare the aggregate result type and the argument type up to `LowCardinality` (`recursiveRemoveLowCardinality`) before deciding the aggregate can be replaced by the key. - Replacing the aggregate with its argument changes the node type (`String` -> `LowCardinality(String)`), which would break the enclosing function whose resolution was cached against the aggregate's type (and abort with a `LOGICAL_ERROR` in debug/sanitizer builds). So re-resolve the parent ordinary functions in `leaveImpl` when an argument type changed; this cascades upward and keeps predicates like `key = 'x'` operating directly on the key column, so `HAVING` pushes down and skip indexes prune as for a plain key. Verified locally (issue reproducer): `min(s)` / `any(s = 'x')` of a `LowCardinality(String)` key now eliminate the aggregate, push the `HAVING` predicate down, and prune the text index (8/128 granules, matching the plain-key behavior). Results are unchanged with the optimization on vs off across `LowCardinality(String)`, `LowCardinality(Nullable(String))`, and `LowCardinality(UInt8)`.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Use text index on map element with Nullable constant key
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110018 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): A text index defined on `mapKeys(m)` / `mapValues(m)` is now used for `m[key] = value` when the constant map key is wrapped in `Nullable` (e.g. `m[CAST('key' AS Nullable(String))]`), instead of falling back to a full scan. ### Description Closes #110018. A text index on `mapKeys(m)` / `mapValues(m)` was used for `WHERE m['key'] = 'value'` but not for the semantically equivalent `WHERE m[CAST('key' AS Nullable(String))] = 'value'`. The `Nullable` wrapper makes `arrayElement` return `Nullable(String)` and the comparison return `Nullable(UInt8)`, and the map-element analysis in the text index condition rejected both types. Fix: strip the `Nullable` wrapper in the map-element key/value analysis (`MergeTreeIndexConditionText`), mirroring what the JSON-subcolumn path already does. This is safe for a non-NULL constant key: `arrayElement(m, key)` returns the value-type default (empty string) for an absent key, not `NULL`, so the "predicate is false on the default value" invariant the map-element optimization relies on still holds. A `NULL` constant key still declines the `mapKeys` path (it would break the invariant); the value index remains a safe over-approximation there. Verified with `EXPLAIN indexes = 1`: both the `mapKeys` and `mapValues` indexes now prune granules (2/128) for a Nullable (and `LowCardinality(Nullable)`) constant key, matching the plain-key behaviour. Regression test: `02346_text_index_bug110018`.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Text index looks through positive boolean wrappers
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110012 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110012 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): The text (full-text) skip index now prunes granules for a supported search predicate even when it is wrapped in a positive boolean comparison, so `hasToken(s, 'x') = true`, `hasToken(s, 'x') != false`, `hasToken(s, 'x') IN (true)` and `hasToken(s, 'x') IS TRUE` use the index like the bare `hasToken(s, 'x')` instead of scanning every granule. Such wrappers are common in SQL generated by BI tools and ORMs. ### Description The text skip-index condition builder recognized a supported atom (`hasToken`, `equals`, `LIKE`, ...) as prunable only as a bare conjunct. When the same atom was wrapped in a semantically-equivalent positive boolean comparison the inner atom node was treated as the index column, `header.has()` failed, no index condition was built, and the query read every granule. Results were always correct; only pruning was lost. `traverseAtomNode` now looks through positive boolean wrappers by recursing into the atom: - `atom = true` / `true = atom` - `atom != false` - `isNotDistinctFrom(atom, true)` (this is also the desugaring of `atom IS TRUE`) - `atom IN (only-truthy-consts)` Only positive wrappers are handled. A positive wrapper selects a row exactly when the atom is true (under WHERE three-valued logic NULL and false rows are excluded in every case, so this holds for Nullable atoms too), hence the atom's granule mask remains a necessary condition and pruning stays sound. Negative wrappers (`= false`, `!= true`) map to the negated atom, whose NOT-of-a-granule-mask is always can-be-true and gives no pruning benefit, so they are declined. Non-boolean right-hand sides such as `= 5` are left to row-level evaluation. The recursed atom's direct-read mode is forced to `None`: the wrapper node is not shaped `[haystack, needles]`, so the direct-read / preprocessor rewrite (which assumes that shape) must not run on it. Granule pruning is mode-independent (driven by the RPN function type), so pruning is fully restored, and the bare inner atom node is still optimized for direct read independently. Regression test `04365_text_index_positive_boolean_wrapper` asserts via `EXPLAIN indexes = 1` that every positive wrapper prunes to the same single granule as the bare atom, that negative and non-boolean wrappers do not prune, and that results are unchanged. Repro from the issue: https://fiddle.clickhouse.com/33bc89bf-a740-450a-a1c8-26e7c3c59ba5
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Decide parallel replicas eligibility with the subquery's own context
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/100815 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Parallel replicas now honor a `SETTINGS` clause that changes table eligibility when it is written inside a subquery or a view body. Such a clause was ignored, so a query over a view whose body sets `parallel_replicas_for_non_replicated_merge_tree = 0` returned too many rows, and a `UNION` over a view overriding `parallel_replicas_allow_view_over_mergetree` per subquery could throw `Can't determine table for parallel replicas`. ### Description One root cause in three traversals: parallel-replicas table eligibility was decided with the OUTER query's context, while the read executes with the per-(sub)query context that `SETTINGS` applies to. Two symptoms. **Wrong results.** `StorageView::getUnderlyingMergeTreeStorageForParallelReplicas` walked a view's resolved inner query tree with a single captured outer context, so a `SETTINGS` clause in the view body was ignored and the view was still judged eligible. Each follower then read the whole table locally (its own view-body context has the setting disabled) and the initiator concatenated those results, so `SELECT count()` silently returned `max_parallel_replicas` times too many rows. Reported by an automated review comment here (3696132546). **Logical error.** In a `UNION` whose subqueries read a view over MergeTree, `getSupportingParallelReplicasQueries` decided eligibility with the outer context while `findTableForParallelReplicas` re-decided it while descending. With a per-subquery override the two disagreed: a subquery was chosen but no eligible table found, so the logical error was thrown (server abort in debug and sanitizer builds). Found by the AST fuzzer, `Stress test (amd_debug)` on master, STID 3634-4123: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=06136dac55ba4fb8544dc1697cd28b2ef769eb17&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_debug%29 The fix tracks the enclosing (sub)query context while descending, in all three traversals. Both halves ship together because neither is correct alone: with only the planner half a view whose body opts out still returns inflated counts, and with only the storage half the `UNION`-in-a-view shape reaches the pre-existing logical error the buggy helper had been suppressing. Some queries will stop using parallel replicas where they previously did; those were returning wrong answers. No new setting or default change, so no `SettingsChangesHistory.cpp` entry. Validated on a 3-replica cluster with `index_granularity = 1`, which makes the inflation deterministic: the new test `04728` fails on master on six rows and passes with the fix, over 100 randomized runs.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Use token skip indexes for LowCardinality(String) constants
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110010 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110010 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `text`, `tokenbf_v1` and `ngrambf_v1` skip indexes not being used when the searched constant has type `LowCardinality(String)` (e.g. `hasToken(s, toLowCardinality('rare'))` or `s = toLowCardinality('rare')`), which caused a silent full scan. Such predicates now prune granules like their plain `String` counterparts, matching the primary key and `bloom_filter` index behavior. ### Description The token-search index conditions checked the constant's type with `isStringOrFixedString()` before stripping wrappers. A `Const(LowCardinality(String))` needle kept its `LowCardinality` wrapper, failed the gate, produced no index condition, and the query degraded to a full scan. Since `hasToken`/text-search predicates have no fallback index type, an LC-typed needle guaranteed a full scan. `KeyCondition` (primary key) and the plain `bloom_filter` index already strip the wrapper and prune correctly. This aligns the token indexes with them: strip `LowCardinality`, then `Nullable` (only for a non-null value, mirroring `RPNBuilderTreeNode::tryGetConstant`, so a NULL needle stays rejected), before the string-type gate. The constant Field is already a plain value, so only the type wrapper needs stripping. Covers all three families (`text`, `tokenbf_v1`, `ngrambf_v1`) and the shapes `LowCardinality(String)`, `LowCardinality(Nullable(String))`, `Nullable(String)`, plus derived-LC constants (scalar subquery over an LC column). Regression test asserts pruning is preserved via `EXPLAIN indexes = 1`.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Accept fractional unix timestamp for DateTime64 in containers and JSON
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109884 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed parsing of `DateTime64` values written as an unquoted fractional unix timestamp (e.g. `1783585473.954`) when they appear as elements of `Array`, `Tuple`, `Map`, or in JSON. Previously only scalar `DateTime64` columns accepted this form; inside containers the value failed with `CANNOT_READ_ARRAY_FROM_TEXT`. A bare integer is still interpreted as a scaled tick count, unchanged. ### Description Closes #109884. Parsing CSV/TSV/JSON/Values into a container of `DateTime64(N)` (e.g. `Array(DateTime64(3))`) rejected an element written as an unquoted fractional unix timestamp such as `1783585473.954`, failing with `Cannot read array from text, expected comma or end of array, found '.'` (`CANNOT_READ_ARRAY_FROM_TEXT`). The same instant written as integer ticks (`1783585473954`) worked, and a scalar `DateTime64` column accepted both forms. Root cause: container/JSON elements go through `SerializationDateTime64::deserializeTextQuoted` / `deserializeTextJSON`, whose unquoted branch used `readIntText`, which stops at the `.`. The leftover `.` then broke the array reader. Scalar CSV/Escaped columns use `readText` (`readDateTime64Text`), which already handles the fractional form. Fix: the unquoted numeric branch now reads the integer and, if a `.` follows, treats the integer part as whole seconds and the fraction as subseconds (mirroring the scalar `readDateTimeTextImpl` logic, including negative-timestamp handling and scale truncation/padding). A bare integer with no `.` keeps its existing raw-tick interpretation, so behavior is unchanged for every previously-accepted input (no backward-incompatible change).
