signal.title: Fix Iceberg insert out-of-bounds abort on schema column-count mismatch
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109835 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a server abort (out-of-bounds read) when inserting into an `Iceberg` table whose cached ClickHouse structure has more columns than the table's current on-disk Iceberg schema. This can happen when a materialized view (whose output block is fixed at creation time) writes into an Iceberg target whose schema was shrunk out-of-band. The mismatch is now rejected with a clear `BAD_ARGUMENTS` error instead of crashing the server. Also rejects stale writes whose column names or partition layout no longer match the current schema, and no longer rejects writes whose column types only differ by an Iceberg-equivalent mapping (`UInt32`/`Int32`, `UInt64`/`Int64`, `Date`/`Date32`). ### Description Closes: #109835 `IcebergStorageSink` maps the input block's columns positionally onto the table's current schema fields when it writes per-column statistics (`DataFileStatistics`) and per-column value dumps. `DataFileStatistics::getColumnSizes()` (and the sibling getters) index `field_ids[i]`, where `field_ids` is sized from the current on-disk schema while `column_sizes` is sized from the written chunk. When the input block is wider than the current schema, these getters read past the end of `field_ids` and the server aborts (libc++ hardening `vector[] index out of bounds`). This is reachable from SQL: an Avro `IcebergLocal` table `t(3 cols)` fed by a materialized view `MV(3 cols)`; a sibling table on the same on-disk path drops a column so `t`'s current schema shrinks to 2 fields, while `t`'s cached ClickHouse structure and the MV output block stay at 3 columns. The MV pushes a 3-column block into the 2-field sink and the server aborts (AVRO data files also bypass the Parquet-only write-time field-id guard). The fix validates the column count against the current schema in the sink constructor, at the point where both the input block and the resolved current schema are available, and rejects the impossible mapping with `BAD_ARGUMENTS` rather than reading out of bounds. Reproduced frame-for-frame against the reported stack (`DataFileStatistics.cpp:97` -> `generateManifestFile` -> `IcebergStorageSink::initializeMetadata`): without the fix the `INSERT` aborts the server; with the fix it is a clean query error and the server stays alive. Fixed while reviewing this change: - A count-only check still let a same-width `RENAME`/`MODIFY COLUMN` drift through, so the guard compares names and types positionally, and it now runs for every mutation rather than only `UPDATE`. - `UPDATE`/`DELETE` are unsafe only when the partition layout changed, so the partition-spec guard resolves the manifest's embedded layout instead of rejecting on a differing spec id alone. - The name/type comparison itself was too strict. `getIcebergType` deliberately maps several ClickHouse types onto one Iceberg primitive (`UInt32`/`Int32` -> `int`, `UInt64`/`Int64` -> `long`, `Date`/`Date32` -> `date`) and the read side reconstructs the signed or wider member, so an unsigned or `Date` column with no drift at all was rejected. A materialized view is the reachable shape, because it hands the target its own unmapped header; a prior direct `INSERT` into the target refreshes the cached metadata and hides it. Types are now compared after that same mapping, so genuine drift is still rejected while an equivalent mapping is accepted. Report: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109835 (stack: signal 6, `DataFileStatistics::getColumnSizes()` OOB, build 26.7.1.644 / git 0633b44).
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Supply `_sample_factor` to the per-part read path used by mutations and merges
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/78465 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/78465 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a mutation that references the `_sample_factor` virtual column failing mid-execution with `Unexpected const virtual column: _sample_factor` and leaving the mutation stuck. A mutation now reads it as `1`, the same value a query without `SAMPLE` returns. ### Description `_sample_factor` is registered with `VirtualsMaterializationPlace::Reader`, so a reader is expected to supply its value. `ReadFromMergeTree` publishes it into `shared_virtual_fields` and the normal read pool copies that map into every read task, which is why `SELECT` resolves it. The per-part path used by mutations and merges does not: `createMergeTreeSequentialSource` seeds only `_part_index` and `_part_starting_offset`, so `fillVirtualColumns` falls through to a throw. `ALTER TABLE t UPDATE u = _sample_factor WHERE ...` therefore starts, then fails per part with `Code 341` wrapping `Code 16`, and the mutation entry stays stuck. The fix seeds the field where the sibling already does. The value is `1` because no `SAMPLE` clause reaches this path: `used_sample_factor` is declared `1.0` and is overwritten only for an actual `SAMPLE` clause, which a mutation predicate cannot carry. It is a literal constant, identical on every replica, so it is safe on ReplicatedMergeTree and SharedMergeTree. The net change against master is 3 lines of source plus one test. This replaces the analysis-time rejection this PR previously carried, so the guard it added earlier is gone and `MutationsInterpreter.cpp` is now untouched. That guard decided column identity from raw AST identifier names, which cannot distinguish an `ALIAS` over a virtual column from an `ALIAS` over a real `Tuple`, because `ColumnsDescription` deliberately omits alias subcolumns. One of the six holes measured rejected `a Tuple(_table UInt8) ALIAS tup` over a real `tup`, which master and 26.7.2 both accept, so dropping the guard also removes that regression. Scope is `_sample_factor` only, which is what the issue reports. `_table` and `_database` derive from the local storage id, and a mutation persists what it reads, so seeding them could diverge replicas, while rejecting them for every MergeTree would be a new restriction. That design is filed separately, and their current mid-execution failure is unchanged here.

signal.title: Avoid server abort on type mismatch during partial result evaluation
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110048 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/97411 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Constant folding during query planning no longer executes a function whose argument type differs from the type the function was resolved for during analysis. Such a mismatch used to raise a `LOGICAL_ERROR` while the output header was being computed, which is an assertion failure in debug and sanitizer builds. Folding is now skipped instead, and a genuinely invalid query still reports a recoverable `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT` error from the normal execution path. ### Description `ActionsDAG::updateHeader` matches header columns to DAG input nodes **by name only**, then runs `evaluatePartialResult` to compute the output header. A function node, by contrast, is resolved once during analysis: the overload is picked and the return type computed for a fixed set of argument types. If partial evaluation is handed an input column whose type differs from the one the function was resolved for, `executeActionForPartialResult` used to execute the function anyway. That trips a `LOGICAL_ERROR` inside the function body (for example `FunctionUnaryArithmetic`: "`negate`'s argument does not match the expected data type"), and because `handle_error_code` routes `LOGICAL_ERROR` to `abortOnFailedAssertion`, a debug or sanitizer build aborts the whole server process during planning rather than failing the one query. **Fix.** Before executing a `FUNCTION` node in partial evaluation, compare each argument column's type against the type recorded in `function_base->getArgumentTypes()`. If any of them differs, skip the fold: it is only an optimization, and the node's declared result type is already known from analysis. - With `input_rows_count == 0` (header computation) an empty column of the declared result type is produced, so header computation proceeds. - With `input_rows_count == 1` (the callers reached from JOIN rewrites, shard skipping and virtual-column path extraction) the column is left null. Those callers treat any non-null output as a definitive folded value, so a fabricated one could silently change a JOIN rewrite or skip the wrong shards; a null routes them through their existing "unknown value" path. The comparison is exact rather than wrapper-stripped, because `isNullable` derives its value from the argument type alone: its result type is `UInt8` either way, so a wrapper-only difference would produce a definitive but wrong value that no result-type check can catch. `ALIAS` and `ARRAY_JOIN` need the same treatment, because both used to pass a value through while keeping the declared type computed during analysis. That hid the mismatch from the check above and let a downstream function execute on an incompatible column anyway. Both now carry the argument's actual type, which is what `ExpressionActions::executeAction` already does in its own `ALIAS` and `ARRAY_JOIN` cases. One result type cannot be instantiated: `DataTypeFunction`, the result type of a captured lambda, inherits `IDataTypeDummy::createColumn`, which throws `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`. The column is left null in that one case. Since a capture is normally a child of the higher-order function consuming it, that function then reports a recoverable `NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK`, whereas executing the stale capture raises `Cannot capture column N because it has incompatible type`, another `LOGICAL_ERROR` abort. (`DataTypeNothing` and `DataTypeSet` derive from the same base but do override `createColumn`, so they are built normally.) **Scope.** In production the mismatch was produced by a concurrent `EXCHANGE TABLES`. The query does hold its table object, lock and metadata snapshot for its whole lifetime (`InterpreterSelectQuery.cpp:635-656`), so the held storage is never swapped. What drifts is that the old analyzer resolves the table name a second time for the analyzed column types (`getTableExpressions.cpp:118`, reached from `joined_tables.resolveTables()`), and an exchange changes what that second resolution returns. The per-query storage cache from #97411 is what keeps those two resolutions consistent; #108728 defeated it and #110048 restored it, which is what `03915_exchange_tables_race` races for. This change is therefore no longer the fix for that race; it hardens the planning path itself so that any argument-type mismatch degrades to "do not fold" instead of aborting the server. I left the changelog category as `Bug Fix` because the abort was user-visible on released builds before #110048, but I am happy to move it to `Not for changelog` if you prefer, given that the root cause is now fixed upstream. **Testing.** Coverage is a unit test rather than a functional one, because the race is an inherent TOCTOU and cannot be reproduced deterministically. Since `updateHeader` binds header columns by name only, the mismatch can be injected directly, single-threaded, with no race at all. `src/Interpreters/tests/gtest_actions_dag_partial_result_type_drift.cpp` covers a strict function (`Float64` resolved, `Int256` supplied), a wrapper-only difference through `materialize`, the same mismatch behind an `ALIAS` and behind an `ARRAY_JOIN`, the wrong-value hazard via `isNullable` at `input_rows_count == 1`, a captured lambda both as a terminal output and consumed by `arrayMap`, and a non-mismatched constant that must still be folded. Verified in both directions on a debug build. Against master's `executeActionForPartialResult` the first case aborts the test binary with `Logical error: 'Unexpected return type from negate. Expected Float64. Got Int256'` through `updateHeader` -> `evaluatePartialResult` -> `executeActionForPartialResult`; with the fix all eight cases pass. Each hunk was also reverted individually and fails only its own case, and forcing the guard to fire unconditionally fails only the still-folds-a-constant case. Full unit suite: 22357 tests pass. `03915_exchange_tables_race` passes 10 out of 10 runs. **Known residuals, both pre-existing on `master` and deliberately not addressed here.** I measured each one against a build with this branch's `ActionsDAG.cpp` replaced by master's, and the behaviour is identical, so neither is caused or widened by this change: - The add-time fold in `tryFoldFunctionToConstant` does not perform this check. Handing `addFunction` a `function_base` resolved for one type together with a differently typed constant child raises `Unexpected return type from negate. Expected Float64. Got Const(Int256)`. This diff does not touch that path, and adding the check there would alter DAG construction for every query on a scenario I could not reach from SQL. - At `input_rows_count == 1` with `allow_unknown_function_arguments`, a type-sensitive folder above a node whose column is unknown can still fold from the type alone. Two shapes: `identity -> isNullable` over a `Nullable(String)` yields `0` where the real chain would yield `1` (unchanged from `master`), and an `ARRAY_JOIN` whose argument stopped being an array leaves the declared nested type in place, so `isNullable` above it also folds to `0`. Closing this properly needs an explicit "unknown" marker propagated through descendants, which changes the `evaluatePartialResult` contract for every caller. I tried the two local shortcuts and neither works: clearing the type outright makes the unit-test binary abort and then segfault, because a null type in a `ColumnWithTypeAndName` breaks downstream consumers; handing up the argument's own type does not help, because the parent compares against the type it was itself resolved for. So this is a separate design decision rather than part of an abort-avoidance fix. Happy to follow up on any of these if you would like them in scope. This branch also takes master's version of `03915_exchange_tables_race` verbatim: master rewrote that test after this branch forked it (pinning `enable_analyzer` and capping concurrent clients so the flaky check does not run out of memory), and those changes belong with #110048's coverage rather than here.

signal.title: Fix Arrow flattened Tuple subcolumn read from a nullable struct
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109726 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix reading a flattened `Tuple` subcolumn (e.g. `` `s.v` ``) from an `Arrow`/`ArrowStream` file whose column is a nullable struct returning column defaults instead of the actual data when `allow_experimental_nullable_tuple_type` is enabled. ### Description Since #101272 the Arrow reader wraps a nullable struct into `Nullable(Tuple(...))`. `NestedColumnExtractHelper` reaches a subcolumn by calling `Nested::flatten` on the parent column, but `flatten` only descends into a plain `Tuple`, not `Nullable(Tuple)`, so the subcolumn was never produced and the read silently fell back to type defaults. The fix unwraps `Nullable(Tuple)` into `Tuple(Nullable(...))` (propagating the struct null map to each element via the existing `unwrapNullableTuple`) before flattening. It is a no-op for non-nullable tuples, so plain-`Tuple` reads (ORC fast decoder, Hive) are unchanged. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/101272 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109185

signal.title: Retry reference-binary download in bugfix validation
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/105139 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description The `Bugfix validation (functional tests)` job downloads the master reference ClickHouse binary via a single `wget ... strict=True` with no retry (`ci/jobs/functional_tests.py`). A transient S3 5xx (e.g. `ERROR 503: Service Unavailable`, wget exit code 8) aborts the whole job before any test runs. This is a broad transient class that reddens finish ledgers across unrelated PRs; the `aarch64` variant passing on the same head while `amd64` errors on the download is the tell that it is not code-related. Fix: use praktika's native `Shell.run` retry (`retries=5`, exponential backoff, 1s->2s->4s->... capped at 60s) around the reference-binary `wget`. It stays `strict`, so a persistently-missing artifact still fails closed and errors clearly after all attempts. Download-robustness only; `aarch64` behavior is unaffected. Same team-approved pattern as #105139 (wget retry for `.deb`/`.tgz`) and #108675 (keeper S3 retry). Verified both directions locally against `praktika.utils.Shell.run`: a command failing twice then succeeding returns 0 after retries; a persistently-failing command still raises `RuntimeError` under `strict=True` after exhausting all attempts.

signal.title: Reset adopted part level to 0 on ATTACH PART/PARTITION for non-Ordinary engines
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109674 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109674 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `SELECT ... FINAL` and `OPTIMIZE TABLE ... FINAL` returning duplicate rows after `ALTER TABLE ... ATTACH PART`/`ATTACH PARTITION` (and `FETCH PART`, restore from backup) adopted a merged part with duplicate sorting keys into a `ReplacingMergeTree`, `SummingMergeTree`, `AggregatingMergeTree` (or other `FINAL`-relying engine). The adopted part's merge level is now reset to 0 so the destination deduplicates/collapses it on the next merge and during `FINAL`. ### Description A part attached from `detached/` (via `ALTER TABLE ... ATTACH PART`/`ATTACH PARTITION`, `FETCH PART`, or restore from backup) has unknown provenance. Since commit `20e5dfc789f` the ATTACH path kept such a part's merge level clamped to 1 for non-Ordinary engines. But a level greater than 0 does not guarantee unique/collapsed ORDER BY keys when the part was merged elsewhere (for example a plain `MergeTree`, which does not collapse rows on merge). `SELECT ... FINAL`, `OPTIMIZE ... FINAL` and the `PartsSplitter` FINAL optimization treat a lone level greater than 0 part as already merged and skip the row-collapsing transform, so duplicate keys survived `FINAL` on `ReplacingMergeTree`/`SummingMergeTree`/`AggregatingMergeTree`/`VersionedCollapsingMergeTree`/`GraphiteMergeTree`/`CoalescingMergeTree`, returning wrong results silently. The fix resets the adopted part's level to 0 at both part-adoption sites: `StorageMergeTree::fillNewPartNameAndResetLevel` (ATTACH PART/PARTITION) and `ReplicatedMergeTreeSink::writeExistingPart` (replicated ATTACH and restore). The destination then re-merges the part under its own semantics. This restores the pre-`20e5dfc` behavior for these paths. The cross-table adoption path (`getLevelForAdoptedPart`) is unaffected: it already has a `hasSameMergeSemantics` uniqueness check and keeps its own level logic. This implements the approach requested by @ den-crane in the issue (mirroring PR #107481, which fixed the cross-engine CLONE/ATTACH-PARTITION-FROM/MOVE path). Test `03283_optimize_on_insert_level` asserted the old level-1 outcome after a same-table DETACH/ATTACH round-trip; that assertion encoded the bug, so its reference is updated to level 0. Reproduction (returns 3 with the fix, returned 6 before): ```sql CREATE TABLE src (a UInt32, b UInt32) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY a; INSERT INTO src VALUES (1,10),(1,20),(2,30),(2,40),(3,50),(3,60); OPTIMIZE TABLE src FINAL; -- produces a lone level-1 part with duplicate keys CREATE TABLE dst (a UInt32, b UInt32) ENGINE = ReplacingMergeTree ORDER BY a; -- copy src's part directory into dst's detached/ folder, then: ALTER TABLE dst ATTACH PART 'all_1_1_1'; SELECT count() FROM dst FINAL; -- 3 (was 6) ```
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Enable fractional RANGE OFFSET for Decimal ORDER BY columns
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/56101 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Allow fractional offsets in a `RANGE` window frame when the `ORDER BY` column is a `Decimal`. For example, subsecond `RANGE` frames over a `DateTime64` cast to `Decimal64(3)`: `range between 0.5 preceding and 0.5 following`. Fractional `RANGE` offsets are standard SQL. ### Description Continuation of #56101 (original author @garcher22, who asked us to carry it forward). Rebased onto current master and addressing the reviewer feedback that had stalled the original PR. Fractional offsets in a `RANGE` window frame were disabled for `Decimal` `ORDER BY` columns. This PR re-enables them, which lets users look at rows within a fractional distance of the current row when ordering by e.g. a subsecond timestamp cast to `Decimal64(3)`. What changed: - `QueryAnalyzer` / `WindowDescription`: accept non-native-integer numeric (Decimal) frame offsets. The integer bound check still applies to `ROWS` and `GROUPS` frames; `RANGE` offsets are coerced to the `ORDER BY` column type and validated in the window transform. - `WindowTransform`: register `ColumnDecimal<Decimal32/64>` comparators and use `NativeType<>` for the offset cast so the `DecimalField` is unwrapped to its underlying integer. - Reject a NaN `RANGE` offset explicitly in the transform constructor. The original PR relied on comparison-visitor semantics for this, which @alexey-milovidov objected to (it made the shared `FieldAccurateComparison` visitors inconsistent). Checking NaN locally keeps those shared visitors untouched and fixes an abort: with the shared-visitor change reverted, a NaN offset slipped past validation and hit `chassert(offset >= 0)` downstream (this is the `02833_window_func_range_offset` failure on the original PR). Tests: `02892_decimal_window_fractional_range` (new, the feature), and `02833_window_func_range_offset` updated (`0.0` offset is now valid; NaN still rejected with `BAD_ARGUMENTS`).
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Label docker-daemon-death job truncation as infra for auto-retry
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109096 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description When the host docker daemon dies mid-run, the main test container returns exit code 125 and the job is truncated: every already-executed test is `[ OK ]`, but the run never ends, so `runner.py` marks the job `ERROR`. That is a runner-host infrastructure event, not a test or code failure. The hourly `retry_infra_failures` workflow re-runs jobs labeled `infra`, but this path recorded only a generic `"Job killed, exit code [125]"` and set no label, so such jobs were never retried and the Mergeable Check stayed red despite all tests passing. A truncated, non-timeout run is now labeled `infra` when the exit code is `125` and the log tail contains both `Error waiting for container: Canceled` and `grpc: the client connection is closing`. Both appear together only when a live container's daemon connection is torn down mid-run. A deterministic `Cannot connect to the Docker daemon at unix:///var/run/docker.sock` regression also exits 125 unfinished, so requiring the conjunction keeps it red rather than retrying a broken runner forever. Timeouts keep their own handling. The label is appended as the bare string `"infra"` rather than through `set_label()`, which stores `{"name": "infra", ...}`. `retry_infra_failures.yml` matches with `(.ext.labels // []) | any(. == "infra")`, comparing each element to a string, so the dict form would never match and this would be a no-op end to end. The other readers (`Result._label_name`, `normalizeLabels`, `gh.py`) already accept strings; the only cost is the hover tooltip, and no `workflow` scope is needed. `ci/tests/test_runner_docker_daemon_death_infra.py` pins the detector in both directions and asserts on the persisted result JSON the retry workflow reads, including once end to end through `_run` with a no-Docker job that exits 125. #109096 fixed the sibling 9000s timeout-cleanup-hang. This signature caused 107 job errors over 21 days, all on PRs and 0 on master; one report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/PRs/109536/887a2f0e48f223cde20a674e2c9dac31cc8eb483/result_stateless_tests_amd_tsan_s3_storage_parallel_2_2.json

signal.title: Implement SESSION window frame for window functions (experimental)
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/56099 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/45311 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Add a new `SESSION` window frame for window functions (`window w AS (ORDER BY time SESSION 60)`). Rows are grouped into the same frame while the gap between consecutive values of the ordering column does not exceed the given threshold. The feature is experimental and gated behind the `allow_experimental_session_window_frame` setting. ### Description Continuation of #56099 (original author @garcher22, who handed the PR over and is credited via `Co-authored-by`). Related to #45311. A `SESSION` frame groups consecutive rows into disjoint sessions: a new session starts when the gap on the single `ORDER BY` key exceeds the threshold. Every row of a session shares one frame, so an aggregate returns the same value across it. Gated behind `allow_experimental_session_window_frame` in both analyzers, with a `SettingsChangesHistory` entry. The branch was based on a 2023 commit. Merging current master surfaced defects that this PR also fixes: - Sessions merged across input block boundaries. The frame end compared each row against one remembered from the previous call, which is not the immediate predecessor once execution resumes on a newly arrived block, so a gap landing on a boundary was never examined. It now compares adjacent rows, and results no longer depend on `max_block_size`. - Two unnamed windows differing only in threshold received the same projection name, producing duplicate `JSONEachRow` keys and making `CREATE VIEW` over such a `SELECT` fail with `ILLEGAL_COLUMN`. - The threshold was not attached to the AST as a child, so tree hashing and generic traversal could not see it and the same query had different AST shapes depending on whether it was parsed or cloned. - Threshold and key types now match what `RANGE OFFSET` accepts (`isNativeNumber`, `convert_inexact_floats`), so a fractional threshold on a `Float32` key works and a `Decimal` one is rejected up front instead of failing later as `TYPE_MISMATCH`. - Wired the frame into the `clickhouse_json` AST dialect and query plan serialization, both added to master after this branch was opened; the latter also re-checks the experimental setting, which a client-supplied plan otherwise bypasses. Each fix has a case in `02891_session_window` that fails when only that fix is reverted.

signal.title: Use bloom filter skip index for arrayJoin(col) IN (set) and arrayJoin(col) = const
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109516 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109844 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): A `bloom_filter` skip index on an `Array` column is now used for `arrayJoin(column) IN (set)`, `arrayJoin(column) GLOBAL IN (set)` and `arrayJoin(column) = const`, the same way it was already used for `hasAny(column, set)` and `has(column, const)`. Previously these `arrayJoin ...` forms fell back to a full scan. ### Description `MergeTreeIndexConditionBloomFilter` only accepted the argument of `IN` / `=` when it was an indexed column directly or one of a small set of wrappers (`tuple`, map subcolumns, JSON paths). `arrayJoin(tags)` matched none of them, so the atom became `FUNCTION_UNKNOWN` and no granules were skipped, while `hasAny(tags, ...)` / `has(tags, ...)` already pruned. This PR recognizes `arrayJoin(indexed_array_column)` on the left side and maps: - `arrayJoin(arr) IN (set)` (and `GLOBAL IN`) to the same granule test as `hasAny(arr, set_elements)` (`traverseTreeIn`); - `arrayJoin(arr) = const` to the same granule test as `has(arr, const)` (`traverseTreeEquals`). `arrayJoin` only multiplies rows, so a granule can produce a row matching the predicate only if at least one array element in the granule belongs to the set / equals the constant, which is exactly what the bloom filter evaluates for `hasAny` / `has`. `NOT IN` / `!=` are intentionally not handled: a granule containing a set element / the constant can still yield `arrayJoined` rows whose value is outside the set / differs, so no granule can be safely skipped. The derived condition is used for granule pruning only; the original filter still runs afterwards, so results are unchanged. Verified with `EXPLAIN indexes = 1` that the `arrayJoin ...` forms prune to the same granule count as `hasAny` / `has`, that `NOT IN` / `!=` do not prune, and that query results are identical with the skip index on and off (including the LEFT ARRAY JOIN default-value case). Test: `04365_bloom_filter_arrayJoin_in`.

signal.title: Fix text index direct read with patch parts (lightweight updates)
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106460 (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/99543 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106460 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/99543 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed wrong results (and an `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER` error for `MATERIALIZED` indexed columns) when a query reads from a `text` index together with a column updated by a lightweight update (patch parts). Direct reading from the text index is now disabled for parts that have patch parts. ### Description Direct reading from a `text` index (`query_plan_direct_read_from_text_index`, enabled by default) produces the search result as a virtual column via a dedicated index-read step prepended to the reader chain. That step reads no physical data, so it cannot anchor patch application, which aligns patches to the block by `_part_offset`. When a queried part has patch parts (from a lightweight `UPDATE`) and a patch-applied column is read together with the direct-index virtual column, the direct-read path and the patch-application path do not line up. The result was either dropped rows (wrong results) or, when the indexed column was `MATERIALIZED`, an `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER` error while evaluating the virtual column's default expression. This happens even when the patched column is unrelated to the indexed column, so the existing per-index `canUseIndex` check was not sufficient. The fix disables direct text-index reading for the whole query when any queried part has patch parts, falling back to regular index reading (identical to `query_plan_direct_read_from_text_index = 0`, which always produced correct results). Bisected to #99543. Reproducer from the issue (`json_title String MATERIALIZED data_as_json.title::String` with a `text` index) plus a plain-column variant are added as `03100_lwu_51_text_index_patched_column`.

signal.title: Fix split-dependent hash of JSON/Object columns
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109428 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `JSON`/`Object`/`Dynamic` columns hashing logically equal values differently depending on their physical layout: how `JSON`/`Object` paths were split between dynamic subcolumns and shared data, or whether a `Dynamic` value sat in a typed or the shared variant. Hash-based joins on such a key silently missed matches, and a `grace_hash` spill could raise a `LOGICAL_ERROR` ("Invalid state transition"). A `JSON` key needed no non-default setting; `Dynamic` also required `allow_dynamic_type_in_join_keys`. ### Description **The implementation changed since the earlier approval here, so please treat it as needing a fresh look.** The approved version hashed canonical `serializeValueIntoArena` bytes and cost up to +568% CPU; this one produces none. Both measured below. `computeHashInto` is the per-row weak hash behind the in-memory scatter paths (sharded aggregation, `grace_hash` bucketing, window `PARTITION BY`, join scatter). For `JSON`/`Object` and `Dynamic` it hashed the physical layout: `ColumnDynamic` forwarded to `ColumnVariant`, which hashes a shared-variant value by its serialized blob but a typed one by the column's representation; `ColumnObject` chained sub-columns in section order, so a path's contribution moved with it. Both splits follow insertion history and can change across a temp-file round-trip, while `compareAt` already treats the representations as equal. `JSON` hits this at default settings, since `hasDynamicType` misses its inner `Dynamic`. `ColumnDynamic::computeHashInto` forwards to `ColumnVariant` as master does, then overwrites only shared-discriminator rows with the leaf hash the value would have when typed. `ColumnObject::computeHashInto` folds `(path, value)` over the sorted union of the dynamic paths and `shared_data`, one cursor per row. `updateHashFast` and `updateHashWithValueRange` stay layout-dependent. `04505_json_object_hash_split_invariance` checks that equal values with different layouts match under the three hash joins, collapse under `GROUP BY`/`DISTINCT`/`uniqExact`, and that a spill flushes real payload rather than only constructing buckets: six assertions fail on master, all pass here. Three `ComputeHashInto` gtests cover the per-row hash and scratch state SQL cannot see. `ShuffleSendStep` shuffles rows to remote workers with this hash and marks no basis in its serialized step, so mixed versions could disagree on a shuffle key. Capability gate, or unsupported anyway? <details><summary>Provenance and performance</summary> Found by the AST fuzzer on #109428 as `Invalid state transition, expected WRITING_BLOCKS, got JOINING_BLOCKS` in `GraceHashJoin::FileBucket`, STID 3913-4579 ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109428&sha=15a6faf088a1b097b3ed56c69ec1fb4d5d602d17&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%29)): a key re-hashing into an earlier bucket mid-spill violates that state machine. Release-shaped build, three arms from one revision (master with these files reverted; the approved implementation; this one), `UserTimeMicroseconds` min over 11 alternating reps; all arms agreed on all 12 workloads first. | workload | vs master | vs appr. | |---|---|---| | JSON `grace_hash`, no shared | +2.8% | -61.2% | | JSON `grace_hash`, mixed | +8.2% | -33.8% | | JSON `grace_hash`, all shared | +11.7% | +6.5% | | window JSON, no shared | +12.8% | -88.3% | | window JSON, mixed | **-10.6%** | -1.7% | | window JSON, 4 shared | +51.5% | -46.8% | | `Dynamic` `grace_hash` | +44.3% | -34.3% | | `Dynamic`, 100% shared | +70.3% | -1.2% | Non-JSON controls are flat and `ArenaAlloc*` matches master. Making a byte-producing basis cheap failed three times: even hoisting the buffer so the block allocated almost nothing still cost +1253%. The residual tracks the shared representation only: each shared value pays one decode, one leaf hash, one fresh scratch column. Of the worst arm's +70.3%, about +30.4% is that scratch reset (+24.9%, +18.5% on the next two). It uses `cloneEmpty()` rather than `popBack` because `popBack` is a row operation: `ColumnLowCardinality::popBack` drops indexes but not the dictionary, which `computeHashInto` re-hashes in full per row, and `ColumnVariant` nests the shape. Conditioning it on a measured property of the scratch column did not survive review, so it stays unconditional. The cliff is bounded per `computeHashInto` call, not by the table; a 5k-40k ladder is linear. </details>

signal.title: Materialize sparse sort-key columns in FinishSortingTransform
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/106024 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a `Bad cast from type DB::ColumnSparse to DB::ColumnVector` logical error in `FinishSortingTransform` when reading in order and sorting by a key column that is serialized as `ColumnSparse` in some parts and dense in others. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) ### Description `FinishSortingTransform::consume()` accumulates chunks and, for each new chunk, binary-searches the previously stored chunk with `less()` (a raw `IColumn::compareAt`). It materialized only `ColumnReplicated` sort-key columns, unlike the base `SortingTransform`, which materializes sparse, const and replicated columns before building cursors. When read-in-order reads parts with mixed serialization, one chunk can carry a dense sort-key column and the next the same key as `ColumnSparse`. The cross-chunk compare then calls `ColumnVector<T>::doCompareAt` with a `ColumnSparse` rhs, whose `assert_cast` aborts in debug/sanitizer builds (a release build silently reads wrong memory): ``` Logical error: 'Bad cast from type DB::ColumnSparse to DB::ColumnVector<unsigned short>'. ColumnVector<unsigned short>::doCompareAt src/Columns/ColumnVector.h:157 (assert_cast.h:43) less<...> src/Core/SortCursor.h:756 FinishSortingTransform::consume(Chunk) src/Processors/Transforms/FinishSortingTransform.cpp:94 SortingTransform::work() src/Processors/Transforms/SortingTransform.cpp:385 ``` The fix materializes sparse sort-key columns alongside replicated ones in `consume()`, mirroring `IMergingAlgorithm::removeConstAndSparse` (applied at every merge site) and the base `SortingTransform`, which already does `convertToFullIfSparse` / `convertToFullIfConst` / `convertToFullColumnIfReplicated` before building sort cursors. Found by the AST fuzzer (STID 1499-2393) on `Stress test (amd_msan)`, mutating `tests/queries/0_stateless/02149_read_in_order_fixed_prefix.sql`. The crashing query was `SELECT toStartOfMonth(date) as d, i FROM t_read_in_order ORDER BY d DESC, -i LIMIT 5` where the read-in-order sort prefix `toStartOfMonth(date)` is a `Date` (UInt16); a part with an all-default `date` serialized it as `ColumnSparse`. CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=108944&sha=1d5aad9342028b0763311a57933f04087f43a6cd&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_msan%29 This is the `ColumnSparse` sibling of the `ColumnReplicated` case in #106024. Unlike that one, this reproduces deterministically: `src/Processors/tests/gtest_finish_sorting_sparse.cpp` aborts with the exact error above without this change and passes with it. There is no SQL regression test: the read-in-order plan always inserts a `MergingSortedTransform` before `FinishSortingTransform`, and that merge densifies every sort-key column (`IMergingAlgorithm::removeConstAndSparse`), so the mixed dense/sparse cross-chunk state cannot be reached from a query. No related open issue was found.

signal.title: Fix force_index_by_date/force_primary_key INDEX_NOT_USED reading through a view with parallel replicas (serialize_query_plan = 0 stopgap)
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/108266 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a false-positive `INDEX_NOT_USED` error thrown when a query with `force_index_by_date` or `force_primary_key` reads through a view (or subquery) with parallel replicas enabled, even though the predicate covers the partition/primary key. The fix covers the default query transport (`serialize_query_plan = 0`); with `serialize_query_plan = 1` a follower can still throw — fixing that lane is deferred to plan-based parallel replicas. ### Description Closes: #108266 Reading through a view under parallel replicas threw `INDEX_NOT_USED` for `force_index_by_date` / `force_primary_key` even when the predicate covered the key: ```sql CREATE TABLE nginx (timestamp DateTime) ENGINE = MergeTree PARTITION BY toYYYYMMDD(timestamp) ORDER BY timestamp; CREATE VIEW v_nginx AS SELECT * FROM nginx; SELECT count() FROM v_nginx WHERE timestamp >= '2026-06-05 12:00:00' SETTINGS enable_parallel_replicas = 1, max_parallel_replicas = 3, cluster_for_parallel_replicas = 'default', parallel_replicas_for_non_replicated_merge_tree = 1, force_index_by_date = 1; -- Code: 277. INDEX_NOT_USED ``` Reading the base table directly, or the view without parallel replicas, worked. **Root cause.** `force_index_by_date` / `force_primary_key` are enforced on the MergeTree reading step (`MergeTreeDataSelectExecutor::filterPartsByPartition`, `ReadFromMergeTree::selectRangesToRead`), which must see the query's filter. When a table is read through a view under parallel replicas, the view is planned as its own inner query, so the outer `WHERE` stays in a `FilterStep` above the view boundary and never reaches the inner reading step. The key condition is then always unknown there, so both guards throw even though the outer filter is valid (the result was always correct, only the index-usage check was at the wrong layer). An explicit subquery does not hit this because the analyzer inlines it into a single plan; a view stays a separate reading step. **Fix.** The existing `parallel_replicas_filter_pushdown` mechanism already pushes the filter through the view boundary into the reading step. This change enables it automatically in `buildContext` when parallel replicas is used on the initiator and either guard is set, unless the user set the setting explicitly. The index is then genuinely used, the guards are enforced correctly (a covered predicate passes, and a genuinely unused index still throws), and parallel replicas stays enabled (no fallback, no no-op). **Scope and known limitation (`serialize_query_plan = 1`).** A follower receives the pushed filter only through the shipped query AST (`ReadFromParallelRemoteReplicasStep::initializePipeline` injects it via `addFilters`). With `serialize_query_plan = 1` (the "distributed plan" transport) the initiator ships a query plan that was serialized before the filter is pushed, and the follower runs that plan and ignores the rewritten AST — so a follower's reading step still does not see the predicate and the guards can still throw a false-positive `INDEX_NOT_USED` in that mode. Per review, this fix must not override `serialize_query_plan`, and force-carrying the predicate into the serialized plan would be new transport machinery out of scope for a stopgap. So this PR is explicitly a **`serialize_query_plan = 0` stopgap**: it fixes the default AST transport; the `serialize_query_plan = 1` lane is deferred to plan-based parallel replicas, where index pushdown into a view works automatically. The regression test pins `serialize_query_plan = 0` and documents the limitation in its header. The regression test covers positives (base table as a control; view, view-over-view, and aliased view, with each guard and both; view without parallel replicas as a control) and negatives (a predicate that does not use the key must still throw `INDEX_NOT_USED` through views, including nested views). Verified on a 3-replica loopback cluster: with `serialize_query_plan = 0` all positives pass and negatives throw; with `serialize_query_plan = 1` a follower still throws the documented false positive.

signal.title: Fix LOGICAL_ERROR in full_sorting_merge JOIN when sharding stream counts diverge
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> No related open issue found. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `LOGICAL_ERROR` ("Join is supported only for pipelines with one output port") that could abort the server in debug/sanitizer builds (and raise an exception in release builds) for a `full_sorting_merge` JOIN when `query_plan_join_shard_by_pk_ranges` is enabled and the two join sides end up with a different number of streams. ### Description Found by the CI stress / serverfuzz jobs. Recurs on current master code across several unrelated runs. CI reports (canonical URLs, exact commit + check): - master serverfuzz (first sighting): https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=5e67948f8fe5c3dd9003dac755192b4ea62b24e3&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28experimental%2C%20serverfuzz%2C%20arm_asan_ubsan%2C%20s3%29 - 26.6 release branch, `Stress test (arm_msan)`: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=26.6&sha=3babd82fe36c262d5aa12a71cd4823d118f7e894&name_0=ReleaseBranchCI&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_msan%29 - `Stress test (amd_msan)` (sha 33a66e1c6316): https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=104431&sha=33a66e1c6316109534074c05689611c3dd0f0a28&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_msan%29 Error: `Logical error: Join is supported only for pipelines with one output port, got N and M`. Stack: `QueryPipelineBuilder::joinPipelinesYShaped` <- `JoinStep::updatePipeline` <- `QueryPlan::buildQueryPipeline` <- `executeQueryImpl` (plain query path). Root cause: with `query_plan_join_shard_by_pk_ranges = 1`, a `full_sorting_merge` JOIN whose keys are a primary-key prefix is planned for sharding. The pre-join `SortingStep` becomes `PartitionedFinishSorting`, which keeps several per-shard streams on each side. `JoinStep::updatePipeline` uses sharding only when both sides have the same number of streams (`use_sharding = !primary_key_sharding.empty() && streams(L) == streams(R)`). When the sides diverge in stream count (e.g. a `PREWHERE` changes how one side is split into layers, or an inner sharded join feeds a non-sharded outer join), it falls back to the plain YShaped pipeline. `joinPipelinesYShaped` required exactly one stream per side and threw. The comment there ("regular join pipeline handles different stream counts") is only true for `joinPipelinesRightLeft` (hash), not the YShaped merge-join path. Fix: in the fallback, merge each side back into a single sorted stream with a `MergingSortedTransform` keyed by the join keys before building the `MergeJoinTransform`. The inputs are already sorted by the join keys (Sort ... before JOIN), so a sorted merge preserves the order the merge join requires and the result is correct. The sharded fast path (equal stream counts) is unchanged. Deterministic reproducer: ```sql CREATE TABLE t (c0 UInt64, c1 UInt64, s String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY (c0, c1) SETTINGS index_granularity = 8; INSERT INTO t SELECT number, number % 10, 'x' FROM numbers(100); INSERT INTO t SELECT number + 100, number % 10, 'x' FROM numbers(100); INSERT INTO t SELECT number + 200, number % 10, 'x' FROM numbers(100); SELECT count() FROM t AS a ALL INNER JOIN t AS b ON b.c0 = a.c0 PREWHERE isNull(a.s) SETTINGS enable_analyzer = 1, join_algorithm = 'full_sorting_merge', query_plan_join_shard_by_pk_ranges = 1, max_threads = 8; ``` Verified: the reproducer aborts the server before the fix and returns cleanly after; results match the hash join (full row-by-row comparison, including the divergent 3-way case); existing sharding tests (03357, 03774, 04065, 03668) still pass. Regression test added: `04501_full_sorting_merge_join_shard_stream_divergence`.

signal.title: Enforce TABLE ENGINE grant in table functions
signal.text:
### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a privilege-escalation gap where the `executable`/`executablePool` table functions did not enforce the `TABLE ENGINE ON Executable` grant. With `table_engines_require_grant` enabled, a user denied `CREATE TABLE ... ENGINE = Executable` could still run the same server-side script via `SELECT ... FROM executable(...)`. These table functions now require `GRANT TABLE ENGINE ON Executable`, matching `CREATE TABLE`. ### Description `executable`/`executablePool` run a server-side script under the ClickHouse OS user. Table functions checked only source access (`READ`/`WRITE ON S3`/`URL`/...) and `CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE`, never the `TABLE ENGINE` grant `CREATE TABLE` enforces via `InterpreterCreateQuery`. So with `table_engines_require_grant = true`, a user without `GRANT TABLE ENGINE ON Executable` was correctly denied `CREATE TABLE ... ENGINE = Executable(...)` but could still reach the same `StorageExecutable` capability via `SELECT * FROM executable('sh -c ...', ...)`. Bounded, not RCE: needs `table_engines_require_grant = true` plus a pre-existing executable under `user_scripts_path`, and runs as the ClickHouse OS user; not exploitable on Cloud (setting force-disabled, no write primitive there). It is a prerequisite for enabling the setting, which otherwise denies `ENGINE = Executable` while leaving `executable` open. **Fix.** New `ITableFunction::checkEngineAccess`, called from both `execute` and `getActualTableStructureWithAccess`, so `SELECT`, `DESCRIBE` and `CREATE TABLE AS` are gated when the table function is named directly. It is scoped by a new opt-in virtual `requiresTableEngineGrant`, `true` only on `TableFunctionExecutable` (engine `Executable`, which also backs `executablePool`), and is a no-op when the setting is off. Deliberately **not** gated: wrapper/proxy engines (`merge`, `loop`, `dictionary`, `view`, `remote`), already gated by delegated data access (`SELECT`/`SHOW COLUMNS` on the wrapped table, dictionary access, row policies) - gating them would be a new requirement and breaks `03680_loop_table_function_access_check`, `04411_loop_table_function_describe_access_check`, `03928_loop_row_policy` and `03273_dictionary_rbac`; pseudo-engines (`numbers`, `values`), which have no storage engine; and source functions (`s3`, `url`, `file`), gated on the source axis by the filter-aware `checkSourceAccess`.
One structure-only path deliberately left out of scope (viewIfPermitted) One structure-only path is out of scope: `viewIfPermitted` resolves its `ELSE` branch through the fallback's raw `getActualTableStructure` (`TableFunctionViewIfPermitted.cpp:92-95`), so `DESCRIBE viewIfPermitted(... ELSE executable(...))` answers without the grant check. It discloses nothing (`executable` takes its structure as an explicit literal argument, so the answer is what the caller typed) and never reaches the script - execution goes via `else_table_function->execute`, which does check, so nested `SELECT` and `CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT` are denied. That path bypasses master's own `checkSourceAccess` identically, verified against a pristine-master build, so it is pre-existing and belongs in its own PR.
Tests in `tests/integration/test_grant_and_revoke/test_with_table_engine_grant.py`: `executable` `SELECT`/`DESCRIBE` denied without the grant, allowed with it, plus a regression asserting wrapper (`null`, `merge`), pseudo (`numbers`, `values`) and source (`url` with a source grant) table functions stay ungated on `TABLE ENGINE`.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Fix EmbeddedRocksDB backup to include table data
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109213 --> Closes: #109213 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `BACKUP` of `EmbeddedRocksDB` tables. Previously only the table metadata was stored in the backup and the actual data was silently dropped, so `RESTORE` produced an empty table. The backup now includes all key-value pairs and restores them correctly. ### Description `StorageEmbeddedRocksDB` did not override `backupData()` / `restoreDataFromBackup()`, so it fell through to the no-op `IStorage` defaults: `BACKUP` captured only `metadata/<db>/<table>.sql` and no data files, and `RESTORE` reported success while producing an empty table (silent data loss). Reproduction on the current binary before the fix: ```sql CREATE TABLE rdb (k UInt64, v String) ENGINE = EmbeddedRocksDB PRIMARY KEY k; INSERT INTO rdb SELECT number, 'val_' || toString(number) FROM numbers(1000); BACKUP TABLE rdb TO File('rdb_backup'); -- backup contains only metadata/default/rdb.sql DROP TABLE rdb SYNC; RESTORE TABLE rdb FROM File('rdb_backup'); SELECT count() FROM rdb; -- 0 (data lost) ``` #### Fix Implement the two backup entrypoints as a logical dump, following the existing `StorageKeeperMap` / `StorageMemory` pattern: - `backupData()` iterates every key-value pair (under a shared lock, over an implicit RocksDB snapshot for a consistent view) and writes them as length-prefixed binary records into a single compressed `data.bin` backup entry, produced lazily via `IBackupEntriesLazyBatch`. - `restoreDataFromBackup()` reads `data.bin` back and re-inserts the pairs with a `rocksdb::WriteBatch`. Restoring into a non-empty table is rejected unless `allow_non_empty_tables` is set, matching the other engines. RocksDB already stores keys and values as raw serialized strings, so the bytes are copied verbatim; every primary-key layout (single or composite) and value type (including `Nullable`, `Array`, `Map`) round-trips with no type-specific handling. This integrates with the whole backup ecosystem (File/S3/Disk, compression, encryption, incremental backups). A stateless regression test (`04401_rocksdb_backup_restore`) covers the round-trip, the non-empty-table guard, composite primary keys, complex value types, and empty tables.

signal.title: Respect `date_time_overflow_behavior` for numeric temporal casts
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/101131 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110459 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/101512 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Makes `date_time_overflow_behavior` take effect for numeric casts to `Date`, `Date32`, `DateTime` and `Time`. The `throw` and `saturate` paths were dead code for these targets, so an out-of-range value was always silently reinterpreted or truncated. Four results also change under the default `ignore` mode, where the previous value came from a code path that could not be reached: an out-of-range numeric `INSERT ... VALUES` expression for a `Date` or `Date32` column now clamps to the boundary instead of storing `1970-01-01`; a wide integer (`Int128`/`UInt128`/`Int256`/`UInt256`) cast to `DateTime` or `Time` now saturates instead of being truncated, so `toDateTime32(toInt128(99999999999999999999999999))` gives the maximum rather than `1970-02-04 08:19:58`; `inf` and `NaN` cast to `Date32` now raise `CANNOT_CONVERT_TYPE` as they already did for the other three targets, instead of saturating to a boundary date; and an out-of-range literal for an exact target such as `DROP PARTITION` or a strict `IN` raises `ARGUMENT_OUT_OF_BOUND` rather than addressing a clamped partition. ### Description `ConvertImpl` instantiated the numeric-to-temporal transforms with the compile-time constant `default_date_time_overflow_behavior` (`ignore`) instead of the runtime setting, so their `throw` and `saturate` branches were never instantiated. Threading the runtime value in makes them reachable, exposing three latent defects there: the rejected value was formatted with a narrowing `static_cast<Int64>`, undefined for a huge, infinite or `NaN` float (floats are now widened to `double`); `NaN` passed every range comparison into a narrowing cast, so it is guarded explicitly; and the clamp narrowed to `time_t` before `std::min`, so a `UInt64` above `INT64_MAX` wrapped negative and gave `1970` instead of the maximum. Three further paths ignored the setting and account for the default-mode changes above. The wide integer types missed every branch of the `DateTime` dispatch and fell through to `convertNumericGeneral`, which truncates. `convertFieldToType` (the `VALUES`/`IN` coercion path) serves two kinds of caller, so in `ignore` mode it keys on the exactness flag: an exact target gets the canonical storage value, while value materialization clamps like `CAST`. `values()` is the exception: built with a default `FormatSettings`, it keeps clamping while `CAST` raises under `throw`, and the test pins that divergence. `Date32` was the only target that accepted a non-finite float. The numeric `Time` dispatch and its bounds already landed on the base as a714d76b341fa8c from an earlier round here. PR 110459 (merged) is reconciled in this branch.

signal.title: Fix wrong results with parallel_hash JOIN and read-in-order-through-join
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109216 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110671 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed wrong results (silently dropped or mis-grouped rows) when `join_algorithm = 'parallel_hash'` is combined with a sorted consumer such as `optimize_aggregation_in_order`, `optimize_distinct_in_order` or `LIMIT BY`. With several join slots and a single-level hash map, `ConcurrentHashJoin` scatters the left block across slots, so the read-in-order-through-join optimization must no longer advertise the left sort order in that case. ### Description The `partial_merge` / `prefer_partial_merge` half of this PR has since been fixed on master by #110671, which added `IJoin::preservesLeftBlockOrder()` (defaulting to `true`) plus the `MergeJoin` / `JoinSwitcher` overrides and the `findReadingStep` gate. What remains here is a different carrier, and it is still a live wrong result on master. **`parallel_hash` (`ConcurrentHashJoin`) with several slots and a single-level map.** It inherits the `true` default from master, but `chooseMethod` leaves a key that materializes to one or two bytes (`key8` / `key16`) single-level - wider keys, including string and fixed-string ones, get a two-level variant. For a single-level map `joinBlock` scatters the left block across slots and `ConcurrentHashJoinResult` emits slot 0, then slot 1, and so on, so equal left-key values stop being contiguous while `findReadingStep` still installs the ordered read. Measured on master (`54dee101`, which contains #110671) against a debug build of this branch: ```sql CREATE TABLE t3 (a UInt32, j UInt8) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY (a, j); CREATE TABLE t4 (j UInt8, v UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY j; INSERT INTO t3 SELECT intDiv(number, 8)::UInt32, (number % 8)::UInt8 FROM numbers(64); INSERT INTO t4 SELECT (number % 8)::UInt8, number FROM numbers(8); SET join_algorithm = 'parallel_hash', max_threads = 8, optimize_aggregation_in_order = 1, max_bytes_before_external_join = 0, max_bytes_ratio_before_external_join = 0; SELECT a, count() FROM t3 LEFT ALL JOIN t4 ON t3.j = t4.j GROUP BY a ORDER BY a; ``` Master returns `1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 57`; the correct answer is 8 per group, which this branch returns. Ground truth was confirmed three independent ways (`optimize_aggregation_in_order = 0`, `join_algorithm = 'hash'`, `query_plan_read_in_order_through_join = 0`). The fix flips the `IJoin::preservesLeftBlockOrder()` default from `true` (fail-open) to `false` (fail-closed) and makes each join that really does stream the left side through once opt in: `HashJoin`, `DirectKeyValueJoin`, `ConstantJoin`, `PasteJoin` unconditionally, and `ConcurrentHashJoin` only when it does not scatter (`slots == 1 || twoLevelMapIsUsed()`). Flipping the default is what makes the contract hold by property rather than by accident. On master `FullSortingMergeJoin` has no override, so it inherits `true` - it is safe today only because `JoinStepLogical` inserts a `Sorting (Sort Left before JOIN)` step that `findReadingStep` does not descend through. That is a property of the current plan shape, not of the join, so any future plan change would silently reintroduce a wrong result. Under the fail-closed default it is safe by property. Precision was verified in both directions, so the stricter default does not cost the optimization anywhere it was previously correct: a two-level `UInt64` key still reads in order, a single-slot (`max_threads = 1`) `parallel_hash` join still reads in order, and `hash` / `direct` are unchanged. `GraceHashJoin` and `SpillingHashJoin` remain excluded through `hasDelayedBlocks()` as before. `topKThroughJoin.cpp` keeps its explicit `FullSortingMergeJoin` type check for its own mode 2 (a pre-JOIN `Sort` on the preserved input); its comment is updated to say the `preservesLeftBlockOrder()` read already covers that join and the type check is now belt-and-braces. Tests: `04498_distinct_in_order_partial_merge_join` fails on current master on exactly the `parallel_hash` block and passes here, so it is a live regression test rather than a restatement of #110671. `04500_read_in_order_through_constant_join` covers the `ConstantJoin` and `DirectKeyValueJoin` opt-ins, and `04500_limit_by_in_order_partial_merge_join` guards the `LIMIT BY` consumer. Each assertion was verified by mutation: with the corresponding override removed the assertion flips. All of them pin the whole read-in-order trio (`optimize_read_in_order`, `query_plan_read_in_order`, `query_plan_read_in_order_through_join`), since the stateless runner randomizes all three and a drawn `0` would make the plan assertions blind. #109216 is downgraded to `Related:` because the shape it reports (`prefer_partial_merge` + `optimize_distinct_in_order`) no longer reproduces on master after #110671; its reproducer now returns the correct 6 rows over repeated runs. This PR covers the sibling `parallel_hash` carrier of the same class, so it should not auto-close that issue.

signal.title: Fix LOGICAL_ERROR when a column transformer sets an alias on an asterisk
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109214 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109214 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a `LOGICAL_ERROR` ("Can't set alias of ... of QualifiedAsterisk", server abort in debug and sanitizer builds) when a column transformer that assigns a name (`APPLY` with a name prefix, or `REPLACE`) is applied to an expression that expands to an asterisk or `COLUMNS` matcher, for example `SELECT * APPLY (x -> t.*, 'p_')`. Such queries now return a clear `BAD_ARGUMENTS` error. Also fixes wrong column names when an `APPLY` name prefix and a second matcher appear in one `SELECT`, and makes the analyzer honour the name prefix consistently with the old analyzer. ### Description Found by the AST fuzzer (`AST fuzzer (amd_debug, targeted)`, STID `1493-3ccb`) on the query `SELECT DISTINCT * APPLY (x -> compound_value.*, 'f_') FROM test_table__fuzz_23 FINAL PREWHERE ...`: report https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109082&sha=62139e418dccb913277c31a483b2547ed4e230e7&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29 Root cause of the abort: `ASTColumnsApplyTransformer::transform` and `ASTColumnsReplaceTransformer::transform` call `setAlias` on the transformer's result node, but only `ASTWithAlias` nodes support aliases. When the `APPLY` lambda body (or the `REPLACE` replacement) expands to an `ASTAsterisk` / `ASTQualifiedAsterisk` / `ASTColumnsMatcher`, the default `IAST::setAlias` throws `LOGICAL_ERROR`. A `setTransformerAlias` helper now checks for `ASTWithAlias` first and otherwise throws `BAD_ARGUMENTS`, mirroring the existing precedent for asterisks with column aliases in `CREATE VIEW`. That path is the old analyzer. The default analyzer silently dropped the `APPLY` name prefix instead, so it also had to learn the old analyzer's naming, and the same bare-matcher case had to be rejected there. Two further naming cases fixed while implementing that: - A name prefix must stay inside its own transformer chain. Matched column nodes are shared (one node per column), so publishing the prefixed name on the matched node leaked it into a later matcher: `SELECT * APPLY (x -> x, 'p_'), *` reported `p_a p_a`, and the same query with the two matchers swapped reported `a p_a`. The prefixed name now goes on a private copy. Values were never affected. - A chained prefix accumulates onto the previous transformer's display name (`q_p_a`, `q_identity(a).1`) rather than the original column name. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109223&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/109223](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F109223+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Guard ColumnString::filter against offsets inconsistent with chars array
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107196 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a possible out-of-bounds write in `ColumnString::filter` when a `String` column arrives with `offsets` inconsistent with its `chars` array (for example `offsets.back()` not equal to `chars.size()`). Such a column now raises an `INCORRECT_DATA` exception instead of reading and writing out of bounds. ### Description `ColumnString::filter` (both the `const` and in-place overloads) passed `offsets` and `chars` straight to `filterArraysImpl` / `filterArraysImplInPlace` without checking that they are consistent. The SIMD fast path in `filterArraysImplGeneric` (`ColumnsCommon.cpp`) trusts `offsets` to size its copies: for a full-passing 64-row chunk it computes `chunk_size = offsets_pos[63] - offsets_pos[-1]`, then does `resize + memcpy` of that many bytes. If a corrupt column arrives with `offsets.back() != chars.size()`, `chunk_size` is bogus and the memcpy runs off the end of the buffer, an out-of-bounds write. This was observed in CI as a SEGV ("address not mapped to object") with the stack: ``` __asan_memcpy ColumnsCommon.cpp ResultOffsetsBuilder::insertChunk<64> / filterArraysImpl<char8_t> ColumnString.cpp ColumnString::filter ColumnNullable.cpp ColumnNullable::filter FilterDescription.cpp FilterDescription::filter FilterTransform.cpp FilterTransform::doTransform ``` while filtering a nullable `String` column produced by the Parquet reader on a metadata-cache-hit path. The inconsistent column is produced upstream and the exact producer path is not deterministically reproducible, so this change does not touch the upstream producer. Instead it guards the point where the corruption turns into memory unsafety: `ColumnString::filter` now validates the same invariant the `ColumnString` copy constructor already enforces (`offsets.back() == chars.size()`), matching the guard recently added to the sibling `ColumnString::insertRangeFrom` path (#107196). A violated invariant becomes a clean `INCORRECT_DATA` exception, which is handled normally in release builds, rather than a silent out-of-bounds write. The guard is O(1) (a single comparison on the already-loaded last offset), so there is no hot-path cost for well-formed columns. Unit tests in `gtest_column_string.cpp` build a `ColumnString` whose offsets overshoot `chars` and assert that `filter()` (both overloads) throws `INCORRECT_DATA` instead of reading/writing out of bounds. Without the guard, the large-overshoot case is an AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow. A positive test confirms a consistent column still filters correctly over both the SIMD and the tail paths. No related open issue found.

signal.title: Stress test: do not force use_query_cache for non-throw overflow-mode tests
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107907 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description The stress runner enables `use_query_cache=1` as a global per-runner client option (`ci/jobs/scripts/stress/stress.py`, probability `1/15`). The server refuses that together with a non-throw `*_overflow_mode` and raises `QUERY_CACHE_USED_WITH_NON_THROW_OVERFLOW_MODE` (error 731), because such a mode can truncate the result, which must never be cached (Bug 67476, guarded in `executeQuery.cpp`). Tests that set such a mode then fail. `00107_totals_after_having` sets `group_by_overflow_mode = 'any'`, and three consecutive failures trip `--max-failures-chain`, aborting the runner. 72 stateless tests set a non-throw overflow mode. Reported by @ alexey-milovidov while triaging a `Stress test (amd_msan)` failure on #107907 (report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=107907&sha=f7e21726f54a9&name_0=PR). That block now also pins the overflow modes to `'throw'`, but only as a client option, so it does not cover this: a test's own `SET` overrides a client option. Verified against a local server: with `use_query_cache=1` and every mode pinned to `'throw'` on the command line, a query after `SET group_by_overflow_mode = 'any'` still returns 731. Fix: detect tests that set a non-throw overflow mode and turn the forced query cache back off for exactly those, on the command line and on the HTTP carrier used in cloud mode. The trailing value wins in both. The detected settings are the ten the server guards, so `read_overflow_mode_leaf` is covered; comment-only mentions are ignored. Query-level `SETTINGS` still override the override, so the intentional 731 coverage in `02494_query_cache_bugs` is preserved, and the query-cache coverage of every other test is unchanged. Treating 731 as benign in the runner was rejected: it would let a test's queries silently abort and could mask real 731 regressions.

signal.title: Retry clickhouse-server boot in functional-test setup
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Retry the initial clickhouse-server boot in the functional-test setup so a single transient boot failure does not fail the whole job. ### Description **Problem.** During functional-test setup, `clickhouse_proc.start()` spawns the server and `wait_ready()` polls `select 1`. A transient host condition at boot (e.g. a brief memory spike from a co-tenant job on the same runner) can make the server exit a few seconds after start, **before it even creates `clickhouse-server.err.log`** (i.e. before logger file-init), so there are no diagnostics. A plain re-start then succeeds. This shows up as an opaque `Start ClickHouse Server` setup FAIL, reddening the non-blocking `Bugfix validation (functional tests)` job and, through the rollup, `Finish Workflow` / `Mergeable Check`. **Evidence it is transient, not a code/binary defect.** In one recent ~40-minute window the identical setup-phase `Start ClickHouse Server` FAIL hit four unrelated PRs. On the same commit that failed this step, every *other* server-booting check passed (Fast test, all Integration test batches, AST fuzzer, BuzzHouse, Stress) — the binary was healthy. A sibling PR re-ran the exact same commit SHA and the job passed on the retry. Example failing run: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109052&sha=f03fe3af507daaf0a255f0cdc55867bc05662e59&name_0=PR&name_1=Bugfix%20validation%20%28functional%20tests%2C%20amd64%29 (`Start ClickHouse Server`: server started pid 669, then `Server replica 0 (pid=663) exited: 115`, `err.log` never created). **Fix.** Retry the initial setup boot up to 3 times: on a failed `start()`/`wait_ready()`, `stop_server()`, `clean_logs()`, sleep briefly, and try again. A single transient boot death no longer fails the whole job. A *persistent* boot failure still fails after the last attempt with `wait_ready()`'s err-log tail preserved for triage, so a real boot regression is not masked. The first-try-success path is unchanged (no stop/clean/sleep, no extra output), and the per-build-type binary-swap boot stays fail-closed. Only `ci/jobs/functional_tests.py` changes; the retry benefits all functional-test and bugfix-validation jobs.
