signal.title: Add zero-argument year() returning the current year
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/45305 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/45305 ### Changelog category (leave one): - New Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added a zero-argument form of `year()` that returns the current year, mirroring `now()` and `today()`. `year()` is equivalent to `toYear(today())`. `year` is now a function in its own right rather than a case-insensitive alias of `toYear`, and the whole function is reported non-deterministic, so `year(<date>)` is no longer eligible for the query result cache and is rejected in mutations of `Replicated*` tables; use `toYear(<date>)` where determinism is required. Results, result types, index analysis and projection selection for `year(<date>)` are unchanged. ### Description Requested in #45305. `year` is now implemented as a proper SQL function (`src/Functions/year.cpp`), modelled on `today.cpp`, instead of the earlier parse-time rewrite. - The `year` overload resolver is variadic and non-deterministic. With arguments it forwards to the `toYear` overload resolver (`to_year->build(arguments)`, the same pattern `dateTrunc` uses for `toStartOfInterval`), so `year(<date>)` keeps `toYear`'s result type, monotonicity, preimage and index analysis. Verified that `year(d) = 2005` and `toYear(d) = 2005` produce identical granule pruning. - Without arguments it returns the current year (server timezone, evaluated once at query analysis), analogous to `today()`/`now()`. - Determinism is a per-resolver property inspected by name without argument counts (`system.functions`, the query result cache, mutation analysis), so the whole `year` function is reported non-deterministic. This is the safe choice: `year()` is correctly excluded from the query result cache (no stale-year bug at a year boundary), and `year` gets its own `system.functions` row with consistent metadata. `toYear(<date>)` remains the deterministic, fully cacheable spelling. - `year`/`YEAR` is now a real function rather than a case-insensitive alias of `toYear`; the parser is unchanged from master. `toYear()` with zero arguments still requires an argument. Per the discussion in #45305 (and the earlier #48321), only `year` gains the zero-argument form. Added a stateless test (`03480_year_current_year`) and documentation for the new form.

signal.title: Delete Iceberg table files on DROP with iceberg_delete_data_on_drop
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/108524 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `DROP TABLE` on an Iceberg table with `iceberg_delete_data_on_drop = 1` not deleting the table's files, which made re-creating a table at the same path fail with `TABLE_ALREADY_EXISTS`. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/108524 With `iceberg_delete_data_on_drop = 1`, `DROP TABLE` on an Iceberg table left the underlying files in place, so a later `CREATE TABLE` at the same path failed with `Iceberg table with path ... already exists (TABLE_ALREADY_EXISTS)`. Long-standing (reproduces at least down to v25.9), not a recent regression. Two independent bugs, both in the self-managed Iceberg drop path: 1. `IcebergMetadata::drop` listed the files to delete with the table path passed as both the listing base and the prefix (`listFiles(..., table_path, table_path, "")`). `listFiles` keys on `path / prefix`, so it looked under `table_path/table_path` and matched nothing. Fixed by using an empty prefix so everything under the table path is enumerated (this matches the existing `create` and `Hudi` callers). 2. `StorageObjectStorage::drop` runs in a background pool and read `iceberg_delete_data_on_drop` from the global context, where it is always the default `false`, so the deletion never ran even after bug 1 was fixed. The value is now captured from the query context in `checkTableCanBeDropped` (called on the drop path with the query context, on the same storage object) and applied to a copy of the global context passed to the background drop. This is the same `mutable`-flag pattern `StorageNATS`/`StorageRabbitMQ` already use for drop-time state. Both the self-managed engine path (`Iceberg`/`IcebergLocal`) and the `DataLakeCatalog` database path go through the same `checkTableCanBeDropped` -> `drop()` on one storage instance, so both are covered. With the setting off (default) files are left in place, as before. Regression test `04365_iceberg_delete_data_on_drop_108524` fails without the fix (files survive the drop, re-create fails) and passes with it; it also checks the default-off behavior is unchanged.

signal.title: Push GROUP BY key predicate to remote shards for aggregating views over Distributed
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/108284 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a performance regression in the analyzer where a predicate on a `GROUP BY` key of an aggregating query over a `Distributed` table was sent to remote shards as a `HAVING` (post-aggregation) filter instead of a `WHERE` (pre-aggregation) filter. Because remote shards run only up to `WithMergeableState`, the `HAVING` was deferred to the initiator and never pruned partitions or indexes on the shards, so every shard read and aggregated all of its local data. The predicate is now pushed to shards as `WHERE`, matching the old analyzer. ### Description Reported in #108284 (thanks @BorisTyshkevich). When reading from an aggregating view (or subquery) over a `Distributed` table, e.g. ```sql CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT date, login, sum(x) AS s FROM t GROUP BY date, login; -- t is Distributed SELECT date, sum(s) FROM v WHERE date = '2024-01-05' GROUP BY date; ``` the new analyzer sent the shard query as `... GROUP BY date, login HAVING equals(date, '2024-01-05')`, while the old analyzer sent `... WHERE date = '2024-01-05' GROUP BY date, login`. On a 2-shard cluster over 2M rows / 10 daily partitions, the remote shard read ~10x more rows under the new analyzer (2,000,000 vs 200,000); at production scale this shows up as `MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` in `AggregatingTransform` on a shard. Root cause: `ReadFromRemote::addFilters` pushes the plan-level distributed filter into the shard subquery through `PredicateRewriteVisitor::rewriteSubquery`, which always inserts the predicate as `HAVING` and relies on the receiving side to move grouping-key conjuncts back to `WHERE`. That move is performed by `PredicateExpressionsOptimizer`, which only runs under the old analyzer. Under the new analyzer the shard keeps the deferred `HAVING`, and since it stops at `WithMergeableState` (it only pre-aggregates; the initiator merges), the `HAVING` is applied on the initiator after the merge and never prunes on the shard. Fix: after `rewriteSubquery`, move the non-aggregate (grouping-key) conjuncts of the pushed `HAVING` to `WHERE`, reusing the same `PredicateExpressionsOptimizer` split the old analyzer already uses. The move is guarded against `WITH CUBE`/`ROLLUP`/`TOTALS`/`GROUPING SETS`, where a grouping key can be `NULL` in super-aggregate rows and moving the predicate to `WHERE` would change results. Aggregate-result predicates (e.g. `HAVING sum(s) > 0`) are correctly left as `HAVING`. Results are unchanged; this only enables shard-side pruning. Scope: this targets the AST predicate-pushdown path (`allow_push_predicate_ast_for_distributed_subqueries`, the default). The separate `serialize_query_plan = 1` path is not covered here, consistent with the report. A stateless regression test (`04402_analyzer_distributed_aggregating_view_filter_pushdown`) asserts the shard secondary query carries a pre-aggregation `WHERE` on the grouping key and no deferred `HAVING`. Verified it fails before the fix and passes after; existing HAVING/predicate-pushdown tests (`01798_having_push_down`, `00491_shard_distributed_and_aliases_in_where_having`, `01763_filter_push_down_bugs`, `00597_push_down_predicate_long`, `01680_predicate_pushdown_union_distinct_subquery`) still pass, and results are identical between analyzers across a query matrix. signal.title: Fix flaky test 01825_json_type_in_other_types under bucketed Map serialization
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108089 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Fixes flaky `01825_json_type_in_other_types`, requested by alexey-milovidov in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108089#issuecomment-4847672406 (CI triage on #108089). It is not caused by that PR's part-writer-fd change. The test checks a full `Tuple(String, Map(String, Array(JSON)), JSON)` row with `SELECT * ... FORMAT JSONEachRow`, and the `.reference` hard-codes the `Map` keys in insertion order. When CI randomizes `map_serialization_version_for_zero_level_parts` to `with_buckets`, `SerializationMap` places each key into bucket `SipHash(key) % buckets` (`splitMapToBuckets`) and reassembles the column by iterating buckets in ascending index order (`collectMapFromBuckets`). With the default 32 buckets `sipHash64('aa') % 32 = 28` and `sipHash64('bb') % 32 = 7`, so `bb` is emitted first and the row stops matching. That is deterministic, not a race: `Map` key order is not preserved across a bucketed round trip. Values are unaffected, only key order. The order-sensitive assertions therefore run against a table pinned to `basic`. Because that pin would otherwise have removed the only `MergeTree` round trip of a `Map` with `JSON`-typed values through the bucketed format, a second table pinned to `with_buckets` keeps that coverage and is read back only through order-independent queries (`mapSort` and key subscripts). `serialization_info_version` and `max_buckets_in_map` are pinned there as well, since either one alone (`basic`, or a single bucket) skips the split and reassembly path while leaving those queries green; the bucket count of the written part is asserted so the coverage cannot go vacuous. `01550_create_map_type` uses `mapSort` the same way, and `03237` pins `basic` for a `Map(String, Variant(...))` round trip. CI failure history (CIDB, 180 days): 6 `result differs with reference` hits across unrelated PRs, under `amd_tsan`, `amd_debug` and `arm_binary`. On the triaged instance ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=108089&sha=9bf747bfda5e62ac6b0c00797917b5a2c1cf44e3&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_tsan%2C%20parallel%2C%201%2F2%29)) the runner's minimization reports `Runs: 5, Failed: 5` with the randomized settings and `Runs: 12, Failed: 0` without them, naming the culprits `--map_serialization_version_for_zero_level_parts with_buckets --map_buckets_strategy constant --map_buckets_min_avg_size 1`. The earliest hit, on #96487 ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=96487&sha=7d955dc099ef89277f349421606ddc9413bf91b8&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_debug%2C%20parallel%29)), carries the diff: expected `{"aa":...}` first, produced `{"bb":...}` first.

signal.title: Fix logical error with correlated EXISTS and convert_query_to_cnf
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/100422 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107951 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a logical error (`Unexpected number of columns in result sample block` in `HashJoin::getNonJoinedBlocks`, leading to a server abort in debug and sanitizer builds) when a correlated `EXISTS` subquery is combined with `convert_query_to_cnf = 1`. ### Description Reopens and fixes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/100422. With `allow_experimental_correlated_subqueries = 1` and `convert_query_to_cnf = 1`, a filter such as ```sql SELECT i FROM t WHERE exists((SELECT dt)) OR (dt > 1 AND dt < 100 AND dt != 7); ``` raises ``` Code: 49. LOGICAL_ERROR: Unexpected number of columns in result sample block: 8 expected 9 ``` in `HashJoin::getNonJoinedBlocks` (debug and sanitizer builds abort). Root cause: `convert_query_to_cnf` distributes `exists(q) OR (a AND b AND c)` into `(exists(q) OR a) AND (exists(q) OR b) AND (exists(q) OR c)`, and `CNF::toQueryTree` clones the `exists(q)` subquery node into each conjunct. The clones are structurally identical, so `ActionNodeNameHelper::calculateActionNodeName` gives them all the same action node name. `PlannerActionsVisitorImpl::visitExistsFunction` then registered each clone as a separate correlated subquery, so decorrelation produced several joins all emitting a column with that one name. The duplicate same-named columns broke `HashJoin`'s column bookkeeping. The scalar correlated subquery path (`visitQuery`) already deduplicates by action node name for exactly this reason (the same correlated subquery referenced multiple times). This change applies the same guard to `visitExistsFunction`: an `EXISTS` subquery is registered only once per action node name. The input column was already deduplicated by `addInputColumnIfNecessary`. Distinct `EXISTS` subqueries get distinct action node names and are not affected. Not a regression from #99736; it reproduces on clean master. The AST fuzzer surfaced it on #99736 (STID 2980-385f). Added a stateless regression test `04490_correlated_exists_convert_query_to_cnf` that fails (server dies) without the fix and passes with it, and verifies the results match `convert_query_to_cnf = 0`.

signal.title: Reject correlated MATERIALIZED CTE reused in a JOIN at analysis time
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/105501 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a logical error (`Trying to execute PLACEHOLDER action`, server abort in debug/sanitizer builds) when a correlated `MATERIALIZED` CTE is referenced more than once inside a `JOIN`. Such a CTE is now rejected at analysis time with `UNSUPPORTED_METHOD`, consistently with the single-reference and `IN`-subquery paths. ### Description A `MATERIALIZED` CTE is materialized once and cannot depend on outer-scope columns, so its body cannot be a correlated subquery. The analyzer already rejects this on the `IN`-subquery path and on the first (storage-initializing) reference in the join tree. When a `MATERIALIZED` CTE is referenced more than once it is not inlined, so each reference is a separate `TableNode` whose body subquery is resolved independently. The storage-initializing reference can resolve non-correlated while a later reference resolves correlated. The subsequent-reference branch in `resolveQueryJoinTreeNode` only verified column structure (`verifyMaterializedCTESubqueryMatchesStorage`), not correlation, so the correlated clone slipped through. Its `PLACEHOLDER` nodes (correlated-column markers) are never decorrelated on the materialized-CTE build path and reach `ExpressionActions::execute` (`ExpressionActions.cpp:797`), aborting the server in debug builds. Reproducer (STID `1611-343c`): ```sql SET enable_analyzer = 1, enable_materialized_cte = 1, allow_experimental_correlated_subqueries = 1; CREATE TABLE users (uid Int16) ENGINE = Memory; WITH a AS (SELECT uid FROM users), b AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT database, uid FROM a) SELECT count() FROM b AS l SEMI LEFT JOIN b AS r ON l.uid = r.uid; ``` The fix adds the correlation check to the subsequent-reference branch so every reference is rejected uniformly. The shared check is extracted into a helper. A non-correlated materialized CTE reused in a JOIN keeps working. Found by `Stress test (arm_debug)`: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=107826&sha=3f6a79763dc52cd4004e8c1c177b67e1a428e7fd&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_debug%29

signal.title: Fix LOGICAL_ERROR on duplicate __join_result_dummy when deserializing a distributed join plan
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/89166 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/89166 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a `LOGICAL_ERROR` ("Left and right columns have same names: [__join_result_dummy], ...") when a distributed query plan (`make_distributed_plan = 1`, `serialize_query_plan = 1`) contains a join whose two inputs are both joins with no required output columns (for example `count()` over a CROSS join of two such joins). In debug and sanitizer builds this aborted the server on the worker that deserialized the plan. ### Description `JoinStepLogical` adds a constant marker column `__join_result_dummy` to its output whenever a join has no required output columns (e.g. a `count()` that needs no join keys). When such a join is itself an input to another join (e.g. `count()` over a CROSS join of two count-pruned joins), both of the parent join's input headers carry `__join_result_dummy`. The in-process planner builds this with the two-argument `JoinExpressionActions(left_header, right_header)` constructor, which assigns each input's source side positionally and is fine with the duplicate name. A distributed-plan worker, however, reconstructs the same step with the three-argument constructor (a serialized `ActionsDAG` plus the two child output headers) in `JoinStepLogical::deserialize`. That constructor mapped each input to its source side **by name** and rejected any name present in both headers with a `LOGICAL_ERROR`, even though the structure is valid and was produced by the initiator. Found by the AST fuzzer mutating `tests/queries/0_stateless/03394_distributed_shuffle_join.sql` (a comma join whose predicate the fuzzer neutralized into a CROSS join), `Stress test (arm_tsan)`. Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=108088&sha=39a5968c228d6a28a04328e39f27470f077d2e24&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_tsan%29 The fix keeps name-based source mapping for the common (unambiguous) case so unrelated callers are unaffected, and only for a name present in **both** headers falls back to positional mapping: the DAG inputs are ordered `[left header columns..., right header columns...]` (an invariant already relied on elsewhere in `JoinStepLogical`, which reads the first right input as `getInputs().at(number_of_left_inputs)`). Each input still maps to exactly one side, so downstream source-relation checks are unchanged. Regression test: `src/Interpreters/tests/gtest_join_expression_actions.cpp` exercises the three-argument constructor directly with two headers that both contain `__join_result_dummy` (fails with the LOGICAL_ERROR before the fix, passes after) and a control case asserting distinct names still map to their own side.

signal.title: Fix allocator abort in validateColumnOfFixedSize for huge index_granularity
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/103538 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a server abort (`Too large size passed to allocator`) in debug builds when writing a non-adaptive MergeTree part (`index_granularity_bytes = 0`) created with an extremely large `index_granularity`. ### Description The debug-only writer validator `MergeTreeDataPartWriterWide::validateColumnOfFixedSize` re-reads each granule via `deserializeBinaryBulk`, passing the per-mark granularity as the row count to read. For a non-adaptive part (`index_granularity_bytes = 0`) the per-mark granularity is the `index_granularity` setting itself, which is only rejected when `< 1`, so a value near the unsigned 64-bit range is accepted. `deserializeBinaryBulk` eagerly resizes the column to that count before reading, which trips the allocator overflow guard (`Too large size (...) passed to allocator`) and aborts the server in debug builds, long before reaching EOF. Found by the AST fuzzer (STID `1367-1ab3`) on `AST fuzzer (amd_debug, targeted, old_compatibility)`, reproduced across several unrelated PR runs, always with the same value `9223372036854775933` (2^63 + 125): - https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=107983&sha=3f0767ee825cc4ee075d3b8ec29e6a629e4cc813&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%2C%20old_compatibility%29 Stack (key frames): ``` checkSize(9223372036854775933) / Allocator::alloc / PODArray::resize SerializationNumber<char8_t>::deserializeBinaryBulk (SerializationNumber.cpp:232) MergeTreeDataPartWriterWide::validateColumnOfFixedSize (MergeTreeDataPartWriterWide.cpp:710) MergeTreeDataPartWriterWide::finishDataSerialization / finish MergedBlockOutputStream::Finalizer::Impl::finish ``` Minimal deterministic reproducer (debug build): ```sql CREATE TABLE t (x UInt8) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple() SETTINGS index_granularity_bytes = 0, index_granularity = 9223372036854775933, min_bytes_for_wide_part = 0; INSERT INTO t SELECT number FROM numbers(100000); ``` Fix: read the column in bounded batches (grow on demand) instead of resizing to the untrusted count up front. The column ends up holding only the rows actually present, which the existing `column->size() != index_granularity_rows` check still uses to detect a real mark/data mismatch, so the validator's behavior is unchanged for valid parts. Regression test added in `04412_validate_fixed_size_column_huge_granularity`. No related open issue found (the previous validator fix for non-adaptive parts was #103538, issue #98585, a distinct mismatch).

signal.title: Make SYSTEM SYNC MERGES wait for part_log to be written
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/104883 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Fixes flaky `04040_commit_order_projection_merge_levels` (first seen on master, `Stateless tests (arm_binary, parallel)`), where the `all_1_4_2` projection-merge row was occasionally missing from `system.part_log`. Root cause: `SYSTEM SYNC MERGES` returned as soon as the scheduled merges' result parts became active. A merge makes its result part active by committing the transaction (plain: `MergePlainMergeTreeTask::finish()`, replicated: `MergeFromLogEntryTask::finalize()`), which happens before the task writes its `part_log` row (`write_part_log({})`). So a `SYSTEM FLUSH LOGS part_log` issued right after `SYNC MERGES` could flush before the entry was queued, leaving the row missing. In CI only the last merge lost the race because its SYNC to FLUSH window is the tightest. Fix: `syncMerges()` returns only when the scheduled parts are covered AND no merge consuming any scheduled source part is still in the global merge list. A merge task holds its merge list entry until after `write_part_log()` in both the plain and replicated execution paths, so this guarantees the scheduled merges' `part_log` rows are queued before SYNC MERGES returns, while scoping to the scheduled source parts (and skipping mutations) avoids over-waiting on unrelated in-flight work. The existing `max_execution_time` deadline still guards the loop. A scheduled merge on a replicated table can also be satisfied by fetching the merged part instead of executing it locally (`always_fetch_merged_part`, prefer-fetch, or zero-copy contention). The fetch path commits the fetched part active in `checkPartChecksumsAndCommit()` before it queues its `DOWNLOAD_PART` `part_log` row and creates no merge list entry, so the merge list check does not cover it. `syncMerges()` therefore also waits, on a `StorageReplicatedMergeTree`, until no in-flight fetch produces a part covering a scheduled source part. The fetched result part stays in `currently_fetching_parts` from before the commit until after `write_part_log()`, so the `DOWNLOAD_PART` row is queued before SYNC MERGES returns. Plain `StorageMergeTree` is unaffected. Validation. The local-merge race was reproduced with a forced sleep between the transaction commit and `write_part_log`: the row was missing without the fix and present with it. The fetch-path race is covered by `04412_sync_merges_waits_part_log_on_fetch.sh`: replica `a` executes the merge, replica `b` (Manual selector + `always_fetch_merged_part=1`) satisfies the scheduled merge by fetching, and a new `rmt_fetch_part_sleep_before_part_log` failpoint widens the post-commit window. With the failpoint, the `DOWNLOAD_PART` row is absent right after SYNC MERGES returns without the fetch wait (count 0) and present with it (count 1). Sibling tests `04207_schedule_merge_basic` and `04208_schedule_merge_disabled` still pass.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Throw TOO_LARGE_STRING_SIZE instead of aborting on a corrupt String size stream
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107196 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107196 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a server abort when reading a `String` column stored with the separate size-stream format (`WITH_SIZE_STREAM`) from a corrupt or truncated part: a garbage per-row length in the `.size` sub-stream could trigger an out-of-bounds allocation (`Too large size ... passed to allocator`) and abort the server under assert/sanitizer builds. Such a corrupt part now raises `TOO_LARGE_STRING_SIZE` at the point of deserialization instead. ### Description `SerializationString::deserializeBinaryBulkWithSizeStream` reads per-row lengths from a separate `.size` sub-stream, accumulates them into `ColumnString` offsets, then sizes the character buffer with `data.resize(...)` **before** reading any character bytes. The accumulation had no bound on the per-row size. The size and data sub-streams are stored separately, so a corrupt part (or a desynced/seeked sizes stream) can deliver a garbage length with bit 63 set, making `bytes_to_read >= 2^63`. The pre-read `resize` reaches `Allocator::checkSize` (`size >= 0x8000000000000000`), which throws a `LOGICAL_ERROR` and aborts under assert/sanitizer builds. Top of the observed stack: ``` checkSize src/Common/Allocator.cpp:122 ("Too large size ... passed to allocator") Allocator<false,false>::realloc DB::SerializationString::deserializeBinaryBulkWithSizeStream DB::MergeTreeReaderCompact::readData ... DB::MergeTreeSource::tryGenerate ``` The existing `readBigStrict` hardening (#107196) catches the *opposite* desync (data stream short, sizes intact) but runs *after* the resize, so it does not help when the sizes stream is the corrupt one. The fix bounds the per-row size at the accumulation point in `appendStringSizesToColumnStringOffsets` and throws `TOO_LARGE_STRING_SIZE`, mirroring the bound the single-stream path already enforces in `deserializeBinaryImpl` (`max_string_size = 16_GiB`). A unit test `WithSizeStreamCorruptSizeStreamThrows` was added (symmetric to the existing `WithSizeStreamShortDataStreamThrows`): it corrupts the first `.size` entry with a bit-63 length and asserts the deserializer throws instead of aborting. Verified the test aborts (SIGABRT) on the unfixed code and passes with the fix; all existing `StringSerialization.*` unit tests still pass.

signal.title: Do not abort on block-number counter reset in ReplicatedMergeTreeSink
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/42120 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/28848 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/56524 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `LOGICAL_ERROR` exception ("Part with name ... is already written by concurrent request") on `INSERT` into a `ReplicatedMergeTree` table when the ZooKeeper block-number counter is reset while a local part at a higher block number still exists (for example after Keeper metadata loss or replica re-creation). This `LOGICAL_ERROR` aborts the server in debug and sanitizer builds and is a catchable exception in release builds. The insert now fails with a regular `DUPLICATE_DATA_PART` error and the conflicting part is enqueued for a check. ### Description `ReplicatedMergeTreeSink::commitPart` allocates a new block number, builds the part name from it, and adds the part to the working set via `renameTempPartAndAdd`. If that throws `DUPLICATE_DATA_PART`/`PART_IS_TEMPORARILY_LOCKED` (the freshly allocated name already exists locally), the sink treated it as an impossible condition and threw `LOGICAL_ERROR`. In debug and sanitizer builds (`abort_on_logical_error`) this aborts the server; in release builds it is a catchable exception. This is reachable without any bug: the ZooKeeper block-number sequential counter can be reset out from under a still-present local part (Keeper metadata loss, replica re-creation, or a `DROP`/lost-replica race). The counter then restarts and hands out a number whose part survived locally, so the next `INSERT` collides with it. `SYSTEM RESTORE REPLICA` avoids this by moving all parts to `detached/` before recreating ZooKeeper metadata (see the comment in `StorageReplicatedMergeTree::restoreMetadataInZooKeeper`), but the collision is still reachable through other paths, and it was reported historically (#28848, #42120, #56524) as a "race with DROP". The fix handles it as a recoverable replica inconsistency: it enqueues a part check to reconcile the surviving part and fails the `INSERT` with a regular `DUPLICATE_DATA_PART` error instead of raising the `LOGICAL_ERROR`. Found by the BuzzHouse fuzzer (`BuzzHouse (amd_msan)`), STID `3744-4a1b`: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=108549&sha=09e554ccedbce6d2dced89414ae256d516fb7c72&name_0=PR&name_1=BuzzHouse%20%28amd_msan%29 The crash was reproduced locally on a single-node ReplicatedMergeTree by inserting a row, recreating the partition's `/block_numbers/<partition>` ZooKeeper node (which resets its sequential counter) while the part stays in the working set, and inserting again. The added stateless test `04411_replicated_insert_block_number_counter_reset` reproduces this and asserts the `INSERT` fails cleanly while the server stays alive. Verified that the test triggers the `LOGICAL_ERROR` (aborting the server in debug/sanitizer builds) before the fix and passes after it. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signal.title: Limit concurrent bcrypt authentications to bound CPU under auth floods
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/87115 --> Related: #87115 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added a server setting `max_concurrent_bcrypt_authentications` that caps the number of `bcrypt_password` verifications running concurrently across the server. bcrypt is intentionally CPU-expensive, so a flood of authentication attempts with distinct passwords (which the bcrypt result cache cannot absorb) can saturate all CPU cores and cause a denial of service. Attempts exceeding the limit fail fast with the generic authentication error and are counted by the `BcryptAuthenticationThrottled` event in `system.events`. An attempt served from the bcrypt result cache is never throttled. The default is `0` (unlimited), preserving the previous behavior. ### Description bcrypt is deliberately CPU-expensive (work factor 12 is roughly 100ms of CPU per verification), so an unauthenticated client can force a full `bcrypt_checkpw` per attempt and saturate all cores. #87115 added an LRU cache keyed on `SHA256(password)` plus the bcrypt hash, which absorbs *repeated identical* credentials. The residual gap: the key includes the password, so an attacker sending a *different* password each request misses the cache every time, and `CacheBase::getOrSet` serializes only same-key threads, so distinct passwords all run bcrypt concurrently. The per-user `FAILED_SEQUENTIAL_AUTHENTICATIONS` quota does not cover it either (opt-in, and not applied to unknown usernames). **Approach.** A process-wide cap on concurrent bcrypt verifications, applied only on the cache-miss path inside `getOrSet`'s load function, so cache hits never touch the limiter. Admission is fail-fast rather than blocking, so a flood cannot pile up connection threads and amplify the DoS. A denied attempt is reported as a *failed bcrypt method*, identical to a wrong password: users may list several authentication methods as alternatives, and `IAccessStorage::authenticateImpl` only tries the next one when this method returns false, so throttling must not abort that loop. The denial is not cached, so a legitimate client retrying under lower load still succeeds. Rejections are counted by the `BcryptAuthenticationThrottled` profile event. This bounds worst-case bcrypt CPU to `concurrency * cost(workfactor)` no matter how many distinct passwords are tried. The limit is identity-agnostic, so unlike per-source / fail2ban-style blocking it cannot be aimed at a chosen victim. It is **not** a per-client admission guarantee: the bcrypt cache is a fixed-capacity server-wide LRU that also stores negative results, so a sustained distinct-password flood can evict a cached entry, after which the next attempt with that password is a miss the limit can reject. Documented with the setting. **Compatibility.** A server config-file key (`config.xml`) plumbed through `AccessControl::setupFromMainConfig` next to `bcrypt_workfactor`, defaulting to `0` = unlimited; with the key absent behavior is identical to today. Not a query-level `Setting`, so `SettingsChangesHistory.cpp` does not apply. Like `bcrypt_workfactor` it is read once at startup and is not re-applied by `SYSTEM RELOAD CONFIG`, so changing it needs a restart. **Tests.** `gtest_bcrypt_concurrency_limiter` covers the primitive (zero means unlimited, admission/rejection at the limit, slot release, move semantics, bound holds under 16-thread contention). `test_bcrypt_concurrency_limit` covers end-to-end behavior: repeated identical correct credentials are never throttled, a distinct-password flood is capped while every attempt returns the generic auth error, a throttled bcrypt method still falls through to a later method for multi-method users, and the default `0` preserves unlimited behavior. **Open question.** The default is `0` (unlimited) so this is strictly backward-compatible. Happy to switch to a small non-zero default (a fraction of CPU cores) if preferred.

signal.title: Make row policies follow the table on RENAME, EXCHANGE and RENAME DATABASE
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/NNNNN (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/NNNNN --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a row-policy escape: `RENAME TABLE`, `EXCHANGE TABLES` and `RENAME DATABASE` left row policies bound to the old name, so afterwards the table was readable with no filtering under the new name. Row policies now follow the table or database through these statements, and likewise through `RENAME DICTIONARY` and `EXCHANGE DICTIONARIES`. A rename is now rejected, rather than silently unfiltering the data, when a policy covering the table cannot follow it: it is defined in a read-only storage such as `users.xml`, or it is database-wide (`ON db.*`) and the table moves to another database. Recreate such a policy per table in a writable storage before renaming. On a server that has a replicated access storage configured, no policy is moved and the skip is logged, including one kept in a node-local storage there: moving only some of them could leave a name unfiltered on a server the rename does not apply to. Those names keep the policy they had. ### Description Row policies are keyed by `(database, table_name)`. `executeToTables` already re-keys every other table binding but never row policies, so the policy stayed on the old name. This PR re-keys them through `AccessControl` by UUID, so the policy follows the data. The re-key cannot be atomic with the metadata rename, so it is **preflighted before the commit point**: the rename is rejected up front when a policy cannot move (read-only storage, a name already taken, an `ON db.*` policy that cannot cross databases), because a post-commit failure would leave the table unfiltered - the escape being fixed. A replicated access storage declines the whole plan instead, so no name ends up less filtered than on master. Three internal renames replace only the *storage* behind a name and must **not** move the policy (`CREATE OR REPLACE`, a refreshable view installing its fresh target, system-log rotation); they are opted out. The `Ordinary` to `Atomic` startup conversion is handled too: it runs before the server accepts connections, so a rejection there would abort startup rather than reach a user, and it declines instead. Residuals, tracked separately: `recoverLostReplica` renames directly and never re-keys; each `Replicated` replica preflights against its own policies, so one blocking the move leaves those replicas on different table names. One open question: a multi-element `RENAME TABLE a TO b, c TO d` still commits earlier elements before a later element's policy rejection. Six narrower guards are each unsound (details in the review comment below), and the two sound options change behavior beyond this fix, so I would rather you pick one. <details><summary>Producer classification and replicated DDL</summary> Each policy moves via a unique temporary name, so an `EXCHANGE` of two policies sharing a short name cannot collide transiently. `MaskingPolicy` shares the same key and escape shape but is Cloud-only, so nothing here can move it; worth a separate look on that side. All 6 `ASTRenameQuery` producers in `src/` were classified. Moves the name, so the policy follows: `ParserRenameQuery` and the `renameInMemory` inner tables of `StorageMaterializedView`/`StorageTimeSeries`. Keeps the name (flagged): `InterpreterCreateQuery`, `SystemLog::prepareTable`, and `exchangeTargetTable`, which also needs the predicate below. The flag is not formatted into SQL text (which would make it public syntax for skipping the transition), so a rename replicated through a `Replicated` database arrives with it `false`, and there a refreshable view lost its target's policy on every refresh. `DDLLogEntry::parent_table_uuid` is a serialized field whose only producer is a non-append refresh, republished by `DatabaseReplicatedTask::makeQueryContext`; a rename is name-preserving only when it is a replayed entry **and** runs under such a refresh **and** its source name equals that view's refresh temp name. The replicated-storage skip is keyed on the server's configuration, not on the affected policies: no local predicate can bound a globally published re-key, and a replicated storage reads from its own copy, so a policy written elsewhere and not yet observed is invisible to the scan. It drops the whole plan rather than the shared entries alone - erasing per policy would still move a node-local policy onto a name whose shared policy stayed put, leaving the other name unprotected. In a `Replicated` database the preflight also runs on the initiator before the entry is enqueued, so no doomed entry is written to Keeper; each replica then applies the plan computed against its own policies. </details>

signal.title: Fix SQL injection in PostgreSQL wire protocol parameter binding
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110760 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed SQL injection in the PostgreSQL wire protocol emulation. Prepared-statement parameters — the `Parse`/`Bind`/`Execute` extended-query path used by `psycopg2`, JDBC, `node-postgres`, Npgsql and others, and the simple-query `EXECUTE` path — were substituted into the executed SQL by raw string splicing, so a crafted parameter could break out of its value position and inject SQL. Parameters are now bound as data. This also fixes string parameters that previously failed with `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER` when a client sent them unquoted. ### Description The PostgreSQL wire-protocol emulation assembled SQL by raw string substitution of client-supplied values. `PreparedStatemetsManager::getStatement` replaced the placeholders `$1`, `$2`, ... in the prepared-statement body with the raw parameter values. Two paths feed it: - **Extended-query path** (`Parse`/`Bind`/`Execute`), the default for `psycopg2`, JDBC, `node-postgres`, Npgsql and others. `BindQuery::deserialize` read the parameter bytes straight off the wire and they were spliced into the SQL text verbatim, so a parameter like `x' UNION ALL SELECT ... --` broke out of its string literal. As a side effect, a correctly written client that sends `WHERE name = $1` without client-side quoting failed with `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER`, because the value was substituted unquoted. - **Simple-query `EXECUTE` path**, where arguments were formatted with `fieldToString`, which drops the quotes around string literals, so it had the same problem. Every argument is now turned into a SQL literal before substitution: - `Bind` uses the parameter type OIDs the client declared in `Parse`. An OID that maps to a ClickHouse type is emitted as `accurateCast('<escaped value>', '<type>')`, which delegates parsing and range checking to ClickHouse while keeping the declared type (`int4` rejects `3.14` and `2147483648`, `numeric` keeps full precision, `bool`/`date`/`uuid` stay their declared type). Any other OID becomes a quoted and escaped string literal. Both forms keep the value inside a quoted literal, so it cannot break out of the value position. Because the declared type is honoured, a numeric parameter stays numeric and `LIMIT $1` or `SELECT $1 + 1` keep working. - The protocol NULL sentinel (length -1) maps to the SQL keyword `NULL`. `BindQuery::parameters` becomes `std::optional<String>` so a NULL parameter is no longer ambiguous with the text `"NULL"`. - `EXECUTE` uses `FieldVisitorToString` (strings quoted and escaped, numbers left bare) and rejects a non-literal argument. Previously a non-literal such as `now()` reached `child->as<ASTLiteral>()->value` and dereferenced a null pointer; splicing the expression's SQL text also changes results (`$1 * 10` with `1 + 1` assembles `1 + 1 * 10` = 11, not 20). Binding values as data exposed several protocol contracts that the emulation did not keep, each of which is needed for the fix to be usable by real clients: - **Arity** is checked against the statement's true parameter count (the highest `$N` in the body), not against the number of declared OIDs — `Parse` may declare fewer. Otherwise a short `Bind` left `$2` literally in the executed SQL and a long one was silently ignored. - **The portal snapshots its statement at `Bind`.** Re-resolving at `Execute` meant a later `Parse` that redefined the statement changed what `Execute` ran, and a `Close` between `Bind` and `Execute` turned it into `Execute without prior Bind`. - **`ReadyForQuery` is emitted once per protocol boundary** (startup, a completed simple query, `Sync`) instead of at the top of every idle loop iteration, which used to emit it twice around a standalone `Describe`/`Sync`. - **An extended-query error skips to the next `Sync`** instead of rethrowing, which dropped the connection before the client could read the `ErrorResponse`. - Negative count fields in `Parse`/`Bind` are rejected; binary-format *parameters* are rejected after the message is fully consumed (so the stream stays aligned); binary *result* format requests are accepted and answered with text, which is what the `RowDescription` advertises. #### Scope Identifier quoting for `COPY` was part of this PR and has been removed: #110760 fixed the same injection in `ParserCopyQuery`, which now stores the table and column names already rendered as valid SQL (each part of a compound `database.table` name separately back-quoted). Quoting them again in the handler would double-quote them. The integration test for `COPY` identifier injection is kept here, since #110760 added no test for it. #### Tests `tests/integration/test_postgresql_protocol` drives the extended-query path with injection payloads and asserts the parameter is treated as data (the targeted secret table is never read), while normal string, numeric, quote-containing and NULL parameters keep working; it also covers the arity, portal-snapshot, `ReadyForQuery` and error-recovery contracts above at the wire level. `src/Core/tests/gtest_postgresql_protocol.cpp` covers message deserialization and parameter formatting directly. The pre-auth `CancelRequest` path (`KILL QUERY WHERE query_id = 'postgres:{:d}:{:d}'`) was reviewed: `process_id` and `secret_key` are `Int32` formatted with `{:d}`, so they cannot carry SQL and are not injectable. No change there.

signal.title: Deny mergeTreeProjection and mergeTreeIndex reads that bypass a SELECT row policy
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> No related public open issue found. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Critical Bug Fix (crash, data loss, RBAC) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Reading projection data with the `mergeTreeProjection` table function no longer bypasses a SELECT row policy defined on the parent table. Such a read is now denied with `ACCESS_DENIED` when a non-trivial SELECT row policy exists. The `mergeTreeIndex` table function is likewise denied when the row policy references one of the index columns being read. ### Description `mergeTreeProjection(db, table, projection)` reads a projection's parts directly. Projection parts contain materialized rows of the parent table, so the read returned rows that a SELECT row policy on the parent is meant to hide. Any user with `SELECT` on the table could read hidden rows. `mergeTreeIndex` had the same gap, exposing per-granule index metadata (marks, primary key and column min/max). PR #95480 added the missing `SELECT` grant check to these functions but did not consider row policies. Reproduction (before this PR the last query returns all 4 rows): ```sql CREATE TABLE users (id UInt64, name String, department String, salary UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id; INSERT INTO users VALUES (1,'Alice','engineering',100000),(2,'Bob','finance',120000), (3,'Carol','engineering',110000),(4,'Dave','hr',90000); ALTER TABLE users ADD PROJECTION proj (SELECT id, name, salary ORDER BY id); ALTER TABLE users MATERIALIZE PROJECTION proj; OPTIMIZE TABLE users FINAL; CREATE USER restricted NOT IDENTIFIED; GRANT SELECT ON default.users TO restricted; CREATE ROW POLICY rp ON users FOR SELECT USING department = 'engineering' TO restricted; -- as restricted: returns only Alice, Carol (policy enforced) SELECT * FROM users; -- as restricted, before this PR: returns all 4 rows (policy bypassed) SELECT * FROM mergeTreeProjection('default', 'users', 'proj'); ``` Fix: - `StorageFromMergeTreeProjection::read()` denies the read when a non-trivial SELECT row policy exists on the parent. The policy cannot be re-applied here: a projection may aggregate rows or omit the policy's filter columns entirely (as in the example above, where `department` is absent from the projection), so hidden rows still leak even when those columns are absent. A column-overlap check is therefore insufficient for projections; a full deny is required. - `StorageMergeTreeIndex::readImpl()` exposes only index metadata, so it gets the narrower column-overlap guard already used by `mergeTreeTextIndex`: deny only when the policy filter references one of the storage columns whose index data is being read. An always-true policy (`isAlwaysTrue()`) does not trigger the deny, and reads without a row policy are unaffected. Test: `tests/queries/0_stateless/04401_mergetree_projection_row_policy.sh`.

signal.title: Prune non-output left columns when a join spill threshold is set
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106603 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106602 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a performance regression in hash joins introduced by enabling `max_bytes_ratio_before_external_join` by default. Left-side columns absent from the join output (for example the join key in `SELECT count() ... LEFT JOIN ...`) are now pruned again when only a spill threshold is configured, instead of being carried through the pipeline. ### Description `join_squashing_blocks` (queries `0` and `1`) regressed by ~10-20% on aarch64 (#106602, #106603). The regression window points to enabling `max_bytes_ratio_before_external_join` by default (`0.0` -> `0.5`). Root cause: `HashJoin::canRemoveColumnsFromLeftBlock()` is gated on `isUsedByAnotherAlgorithm()`, which now returns `true` for every hash join because of the `maxBytesBeforeExternalJoin() > 0` clause. That disabled pruning of left-side columns that are not in the join output. For the benchmark query the left key column (a 300M-row column not needed by `count()`) was no longer pruned, flowed through `JoiningTransform`, and forced an extra `ColumnPermuteTransform` even though the join never spills. Fix: only keep left columns when the join may switch to an algorithm that does not prune them, i.e. `auto` (`JoinSwitcher` -> `MergeJoin`) and explicit `grace_hash`. A spill threshold alone selects `SpillingHashJoin`, which only ever switches `HashJoin` -> `GraceHashJoin`; both produce results through the same `HashJoinResult` path with identical pruning, so the result structure stays consistent. `isUsedByAnotherAlgorithm()` is left unchanged, so right-side key columns are still saved for spilling/switching. EXPLAIN PIPELINE of the benchmark query no longer contains `ColumnPermuteTransform` under the default settings. Results are bit-identical across no-spill, default, forced `grace_hash` spill, forced `SpillingHashJoin` spill, and `auto`, for `LEFT`/`INNER`/`RIGHT`/`FULL` joins. Added a regression test (`04401_join_left_column_pruning_with_spill_threshold`).

signal.title: Avoid per-row heap allocations in blocked Myers edit distance
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106595 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Improved the performance of `levenshteinDistance` (and `editDistance`) for medium-length strings on ARM by avoiding per-row heap allocations in the blocked Myers code path. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106595 Fixes the ARM regression reported in #106595: `string_similarity` query `0` (`SELECT avg(levenshteinDistance(randomString(300), randomString(300))) FROM numbers(10000)`) was about +12.6% slower on Neoverse-V2. Root cause: the blocked Myers path (`BlockMyersEditDistance`, used for byte needles of 257..8192 bytes) allocated its per-row scratch buffers on the heap once per row through `VectorWithMemoryTracking`: the pattern-mask table `tbl` and the `VP`/`VN`/`HP`/`HN`/`D0` bit vectors. Each allocation pairs a `malloc`/`free` with a `CurrentMemoryTracker` atomic update. On ARM those atomic updates are comparatively expensive, so this per-row churn showed up as the regression. Only this path was affected: the single-word Myers widths (`ByteEditDistanceMyersImpl`, needles up to 256 bytes) already use fixed stack scratch, which is why the other `string_similarity` queries did not regress. Fix: hold the per-row buffers in `PODArrayWithStackMemory`. It keeps an allocation up to its inline capacity in an inline buffer (no heap allocation, no `CurrentMemoryTracker` atomics) and transparently spills to a tracked allocation above it. The per-row allocation is therefore eliminated across each buffer's inline range, and the buffer management is a single idiomatic type instead of a hand-rolled stack-array + tracked-vector + raw-pointer split (suggested by @ nikitamikhaylov). The inline range differs per buffer because their shapes differ: - `VP`/`VN`/`HP`/`HN`/`D0` hold one `Word` per block (1 KB each), so a 128-block inline buffer covers the full 8192-byte blocked-Myers range. - `tbl` is the ASCII pattern table, `256 * num_blocks` words (one row per byte value), so it is 256x larger per block. Its inline buffer covers needles up to 8 blocks (512 bytes, 16 KB); a full-range inline table would be about 256 KB, so longer needles transparently spill `tbl` to a tracked allocation while the bit vectors stay inline. The reported regression (300-byte needles, 5 blocks) is fully on the inline path for every buffer. Correctness: distances are unchanged. `02884_string_distance_function`, `03369_function_arrayLevenshtein` and `04125_array_levenshtein_types` pass, and a differential check of `editDistance` and `editDistanceUTF8` against a brute-force DP reference (1392 random pairs) matches exactly, including the block and inline/spill boundary lengths (64/128/192/256/512/8192).

signal.title: Restore O(1) reserve in MergeSorter::mergeBatchImpl (fix ORDER BY perf regression)
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106599 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a performance regression in `ORDER BY` (merge sort) introduced in #100963. Queries with a sort followed by `LIMIT` were slightly slower because of redundant per-output-block work in the result-block reservation. ### Description Reported by egor-click in #106599: `jit_sort` perf test query `12` regressed on ARM/aarch64 (Neoverse-V2) by about +18% `client_time` (`SELECT WatchID FROM hits_100m_single ORDER BY WatchID ASC, CounterID DESC, ClientIP ASC LIMIT 2000000`). Public history: https://performance.ci.clickhouse.com/history/jit_sort/12?metric=client_time&arch=arm **Root cause.** Bisecting the issue's controlled window (baseline `bd123fed28c5` -> affected `d8dd2c3a1a82`) leaves a single functional source change: #100963, in `MergeSorter::mergeBatchImpl`. It replaced the reservation size ``` min(chunks[0].getNumRows(), max_merged_block_size) ``` with a sum over all input chunks, capped at `max_merged_block_size`: ``` size_to_reserve = 0; for (auto & chunk : chunks) size_to_reserve += chunk.getNumRows(); size_to_reserve = min(size_to_reserve, max_merged_block_size); ``` This both walks the whole `chunks` vector on every output block (in front of the hot k-way merge loop) and reserves a larger, cap-saturated size. Matches the issue's profile (`MergeSortingTransform` +10.88%). **Fix.** Restore the pre-#100963 O(1) reservation `min(chunks[0].getNumRows(), max_merged_block_size)`. This is the prototype egor-click validated on ARM Neoverse-V2 (affected-vs-patched about -13.96%, 9/9 runs). egor-click's validation also showed the win needs the smaller reserve, not only dropping the per-block loop: a variant that stays O(1) but reserves the full input-row sum (saturating the cap) did not recover the regression (+0.59%). `reserve()` is a capacity hint only, so it never changes results or the final allocation size; the bare `chunks[0]` estimate reserves the least and cannot over-allocate. Locally verified the merge-sort output for a mixed-direction multi-column `ORDER BY` is byte-identical to an independent reference sort. ARM perf is validated by the reporter's Neoverse-V2 pipeline and by the CI Performance Comparison.

signal.title: Fix LOGICAL_ERROR in parallel replicas for window function over a constant subquery
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/103695 --> Related: #103695 (same `Invalid number of columns in chunk pushed to OutputPort` family) ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `LOGICAL_ERROR` (`Invalid number of columns in chunk pushed to OutputPort`) that crashed the server for a query with a window function over a subquery projecting a constant (e.g. `SELECT count(*) OVER () FROM (SELECT 0 FROM t)`) when executed with parallel replicas and the analyzer. ### Description Found by the AST fuzzer: `AST fuzzer (amd_debug, targeted, old_compatibility)`, STID `2270-3258`. CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=85138&sha=bb9b5684191b897d5a0dc9aca64b2a4e6929557b&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%2C%20old_compatibility%29 #### Reproducer ```sql CREATE TABLE t (s String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY s; INSERT INTO t SELECT toString(number) FROM numbers(2000); SELECT count(*) OVER () FROM (SELECT 0 FROM t) SETTINGS enable_parallel_replicas = 1, max_parallel_replicas = 2, cluster_for_parallel_replicas = 'test_cluster_one_shard_three_replicas_localhost', parallel_replicas_for_non_replicated_merge_tree = 1, parallel_replicas_local_plan = 0, prefer_localhost_replica = 0, enable_analyzer = 1; ``` #### Root cause When parallel replicas read up to `WithMergeableState`, the coordinator computes the expected `RemoteSource` header from an `only_analyze` plan. In that path the inner subquery is replaced by a `ReadNothingStep` whose columns were built from the projection types only, so a projected literal constant became a plain (non-constant) column. A real replica instead emits a `ColumnConst` for it. That difference matters because `ActionsDAG` (`duplicate_const_columns`) keeps an unused `ColumnConst` flowing through a later step (e.g. the `Before WINDOW` expression, whose own outputs are empty for `count(*) OVER ()`) while a plain column is projected away. As a result the analyze header dropped the unused constant column while the replica kept it, so the coordinator built the `RemoteSource` with too few columns and the chunk pushed by the replica did not match the output port. The fix preserves the constant in the `only_analyze` `ReadNothingStep` header so it matches real execution. Non-constant projections keep the previous behavior. A regression test was added: `04365_parallel_replicas_window_over_const_subquery`. It crashes the server before the fix and passes after.

signal.title: Fix flaky hang in ThreadPool.GlobalFull1/GlobalFull2 unit tests
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `ThreadPool.GlobalFull1` (and its sibling `GlobalFull2`) can hang the entire `unit_tests_dbms` binary on slow builds, surfacing as `Thread 1 "unit_tests_dbms" received signal SIGINT, Interrupt.` after the 45-minute gdb watchdog fires. Observed on the `msan`, `tsan` and `amd_llvm_coverage` unit-test jobs; the test has never failed on master. No related open issue found. **Root cause.** Each worker job runs a hand-rolled spin-barrier over a monotonically-increasing atomic counter: ```cpp auto func = [&] { ++counter; while (counter != num_jobs) {} }; ``` The test depends on the counter reaching *exactly* `num_jobs` (= `capacity + 1` = 6): the 5 scheduled jobs each increment it once, and the main thread increments it once more after the 6th `scheduleOrThrowOnError` is rejected (the global pool is saturated at 5 threads). If, on a slow build, the schedule that *should* be rejected instead succeeds and its job runs, an extra `++counter` drives the counter past `num_jobs`. Because the counter only ever increases, `counter != num_jobs` then never holds again, so the worker threads spin forever and the binary hangs until the watchdog interrupts whatever test is running (which the report attributes to `GlobalFull1`). **Fix.** Use `counter < num_jobs` instead of `counter != num_jobs`. The normal path is unchanged (the spin still stops the instant the counter reaches the target); an overshoot now terminates the spin too, so the test finishes and reports its `EXPECT_THROW` / `EXPECT_EQ` assertions instead of hanging CI. This is a test-robustness fix only; no production code changes. Found via the `Unit tests (msan)` / `Unit tests (tsan)` / `Unit tests (amd_llvm_coverage)` jobs on commit a282a393d6f4afce3b7c601e5890081e51c8f24f. CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=107357&sha=a282a393d6f4afce3b7c601e5890081e51c8f24f&name_0=PR&name_1=Unit%20tests%20%28msan%29

signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/99018 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Flaky in `Stateless tests (..., parallel)`. `thread_insert` and `thread_select` were stopped with `kill -TERM $PID`, which kills only the bash subshell, not the `clickhouse-client` in flight. The orphan is reparented and runs its query after the final `DROP TABLE`, printing `Table ... src does not exist` or `Database ... does not exist` to the shared stderr, reported as "having stderror". `wait_for_queries_to_finish` misses it: a client still in connect/auth is not yet in `system.processes`. The loops now stop via a flag file, exiting after their current client finishes. The name uses `CLICKHOUSE_TEST_UNIQUE_NAME`, so the test stays parallel-safe. #98280 and #99018 worked around this race without removing its source. Two error-path defects found during review are fixed as well: - The flag was raised only after `wait $PID_3 && wait $PID_4`, unreachable on either failure. Under `errexit` a nonzero `wait $PID_3` does not abort (left operand of `&&`), it only skips `wait $PID_4`, so a failed worker was reported as success and teardown began while the other was still mutating `src` / `dst`. If `wait $PID_4` failed instead, `errexit` fired before the flag was raised and the loops ran past the end of the test. The flag now comes from an `EXIT` trap, and each worker is waited for separately so the first failure is the exit status. - `wait $PID_1 ||:` discarded a real failure of `thread_insert` / `thread_select`. `thread_select` is the only check of transient isolation violations during the run, so the test could pass after it had exited on a `throwIf`. The orphan is timing dependent and does not reproduce on an idle host, so the evidence is a deterministic A/B rather than a rerun. <details><summary>Validation and CI evidence</summary> A harness mirroring the final region, with a heartbeat file detecting a loop that outlives the script. Old code: exits 0 on a `PID_3` failure, leaves the loop running on a `PID_4` failure, exits 0 on a `thread_insert` failure. Fixed: 3, loop stopped, 9. Each element is load-bearing -- removing the trap re-orphans the loop, restoring `&&` or `||:` re-swallows the failures. Against a real server the test passes 5/5 with the reference matched and no surviving clients. Genuine hits with reruns passing, last 30 days: - PR #101514, `Stateless tests (amd_debug, distributed plan, s3 storage, parallel)`: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=101514&sha=8ef111d9&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_debug%2C%20distributed%20plan%2C%20s3%20storage%2C%20parallel%29 (UNKNOWN_TABLE `src`) - PR #106203, `Stateless tests (amd_tsan, parallel, 2/2)`: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=106203&sha=1ab8ccf4f8982a98d856d7e6086616ffdff80de1&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_tsan%2C%20parallel%2C%202%2F2%29 (UNKNOWN_DATABASE) The sibling `01169_alter_partition_isolation_stress.sh` still uses `kill -TERM`, but none of its recent failures carry this signature, so it is left for a separate change. </details>

signal.title: Fix "No set is registered for key" for a subquery used as both FROM source and IN argument
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a `LOGICAL_ERROR` "No set is registered for key" that could abort the server (or fail the query in release builds) for a query where a subquery is used both as a `FROM` table expression and as the right argument of an `IN` / `NOT IN` / `GLOBAL IN` function, for example `SELECT y FROM (SELECT y FROM t QUALIFY 1) AS s QUALIFY globalNotIn((SELECT 1), s)`. ### Description Found by the AST fuzzer (`AST fuzzer (arm_asan_ubsan)`). Example report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=104939&sha=d224ae20875bb869add720814dd4c5e5fd4604e8&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28arm_asan_ubsan%29 (STID 0250-04e2). The crash is a pre-existing trunk bug, unrelated to the PR it happened to fire on. When a subquery is referenced both as a `FROM` table expression and as the right argument of an `IN` / `NOT IN` / `GLOBAL IN` function (the right argument being an alias of that `FROM` table expression), the analyzer resolves both references to the same shared query-tree node. `collectSets()` registers the `IN` set in `PreparedSets` keyed by that node's tree hash. When the node is later planned as the `FROM` source, `Planner::buildPlanForQueryNode()` mutates it in place (constant-true `WHERE` removal, or the `QUALIFY -> HAVING -> WHERE` rewrite). That changes its tree hash, so the later set lookup in `PlannerActionsVisitor::makeSetForInFunction()` recomputes the hash from the mutated node and fails to find the set, aborting with `LOGICAL_ERROR` "No set is registered for key ...". Fix: when the `IN` set source is a `QUERY`/`UNION` node that is shared with another part of the query tree (`use_count() > 1`), resolve the `IN` argument against an independent copy. The set source is then no longer aliased to the `FROM` table expression, so planning the `FROM` source cannot mutate the node behind the set key. This is the same root-cause class as #80757 (a set key drifting between registration and lookup), here caused by an in-place planner mutation of a shared node rather than by CTE-name decoration. No open issue was found for this error. A stateless regression test `04338_in_set_source_aliases_from_table` is added; all four queries it contains abort on master and pass with this fix. #### Follow-up commit: copy `column_name` in `SortNode::cloneImpl` The new `clone()` of the `IN` set source exposed a latent defect: `SortNode::cloneImpl` did not copy `column_name` (a member derived from the original AST identifier in the constructor, not a child node, so the base clone machinery cannot reproduce it). A clone of any subtree containing a resolved `ORDER BY <identifier>` lost the name. This is visible in `EXPLAIN QUERY TREE` (`SORT` prints `EXPRESSION` instead of `EXPRESSION <name>`) and is read by the planner: `PlannerSorting` builds `SortColumnDescription::alias` from it, and that alias is used by `FillingTransform` for `WITH FILL ... INTERPOLATE` column matching. `InterpolateNode::cloneImpl` already copies its analogous `expression_name`; this mirrors that. The pre-existing test `03165_order_by_duplicate` (an `EXPLAIN QUERY TREE` of an `IN` subquery with `ORDER BY`) regressed to `EXPRESSION` and is restored by this commit.

signal.title: Add ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY ENGINE to change a MergeTree-family table's engine
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107551 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Experimental Feature ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Added `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY ENGINE = ...MergeTree(...)` to change the engine of a MergeTree-family table in place (for example `MergeTree` into `ReplacingMergeTree` or `SummingMergeTree`). Gated behind the experimental setting `allow_experimental_alter_modify_engine`. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107551 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107481 Requested by @ alexey-milovidov. `ALTER TABLE t MODIFY ENGINE = <engine>` changes a MergeTree-family table's engine in place. Only the merge semantics (`MergingParams`) change: columns, keys and settings are kept, and data is not rewritten. Existing parts re-merge under the new semantics via background merges and `OPTIMIZE ... FINAL`, as with the part-level reset in #107481. A new `MODIFY_ENGINE` alter command rewrites the engine clause in the CREATE query (`StorageInMemoryMetadata::new_engine` -> `applyMetadataChangesToCreateQuery`); `MergingParams::parseFromEngineAST` builds and validates the new merge params against the columns and final settings, so a rejection never leaves an unloadable CREATE on disk. Supported targets: `Replacing`, `Summing`, `Aggregating`, `Collapsing`, `VersionedCollapsing`, `Coalescing`, `Graphite`. A required column may be added in the same statement, before `MODIFY ENGINE`. Non-replicated tables only; old-syntax tables are rejected, their keys being positional engine arguments. Because data is not rewritten, a transition is refused when existing parts could not satisfy the target's invariants: a nullable or unreadable `Graphite` path/time column (the rollup reads them with `getDataAt`/`getUInt`), and `VersionedCollapsing` with the version column outside the sorting key, whose reload widens the key under existing parts. **Two questions for review:** 1. Reload-only, rather than a live swap: `merging_params` is read lock-free from hot paths and often bound by const reference for a whole query, and an exclusive lock cannot be taken there (the query holds `drop_lock` in read mode). An immediate swap needs either a `MultiVersion` `merging_params` or recreating the storage. Which do you prefer? 2. The coordinated `Replicated*MergeTree` switch (decision 3 on the issue) is not implemented. `ReplicatedMergeTreeTableMetadata` already persists the merge mode, so that is the natural next step. Tests: `04340_alter_modify_engine` (the gate, each transition's merge semantics under `FINAL`, the validation errors, the AST JSON round trip), `04341_alter_modify_engine_access` and `04342_alter_modify_engine_replicated`. Docs: `docs/reference/statements/alter/engine.mdx`.

signal.title: Read the smallest on-disk column when a query reads no columns
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106597 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): When a query reads no real columns (for example `SELECT isNullable(lc) FROM t`, where the result is constant and depends only on the type), the `MergeTree` reader now picks the column that is cheapest to read from disk to carry the row count, instead of the one with the smallest in-memory value size. The previous metric mis-ranked compactly stored columns such as `LowCardinality(String)` below a `UInt64`, causing the reader to read a much larger column off disk. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106597 `SELECT isNullable(lc) FROM test_lc` is constant-folded away (`isNullable` depends only on the column type), so `ReadFromMergeTree` is left with no columns to read and must pick one column just to know the number of rows. `selectRangesToRead` picked it with `ExpressionActions::getSmallestColumn`, which ranks by the in-memory value size: a `UInt64` is 8 bytes, while a `LowCardinality(String)` falls back to a heuristic of 100. So it chose the `UInt64` column `x`, which is far more expensive to read off disk than the dictionary-encoded `lc`. This PR makes the fallback pick the column with the minimum on-disk compressed size via the existing `IMergeTreeDataPart::getColumnNameWithMinimumCompressedSize` helper. That is the same metric the read path already uses in `injectRequiredColumns`, so the two carrier-selection sites now agree. It falls back to `getSmallestColumn` only when there are no parts to measure. Verified locally with `ReadCompressedBytes` on the perf-test table (`x UInt64`, `lc LowCardinality(Nullable(String))`, 1e7 rows): | Query | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | `SELECT isNullable(lc)` | 40 MB (reads `x`) | 1.7 MB (reads `lc`) | | `SELECT 1 FROM test_lc` | 40 MB (reads `x`) | 1.7 MB (reads `lc`) | | `SELECT isNullable(big)` on `(tiny UInt8, big String)` | 85 KB (reads `tiny`) | 85 KB (reads `tiny`) | The last row is the no-regression check: when a small column is genuinely cheaper than the referenced one, the choice is unchanged. Added a regression test `04337_read_smallest_column_by_disk_size` that fails before this change and passes after it.
