signal.title: Fix flaky test 02770_async_buffer_ignore
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/100391 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/106231 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Fixes the flaky test `02770_async_buffer_ignore`, and makes it assert the regression it was written for. Investigated at the request of alexey-milovidov on #100391, raised again on #106231. #### The flake The test asserted exact S3 read profile-event counts for a narrow-range read: ``` ProfileEvents['S3ReadRequestsCount'], ProfileEvents['ReadBufferFromS3Bytes'], ProfileEvents['ReadCompressedBytes'] ``` against the reference `4 66446 66446`. Those counts are not deterministic across CI jobs and the test cannot pin them away (it is already `no-random-settings`). Over 120 days CIDB shows 253 failures across 28 distinct observed triples, 7 of them on master, first seen 2026-03-26. The largest groups are `4 830 66446` (x174, filesystem cache hit), `6 67909 67909` (x22, parallel replicas), `4 7223260 66446` (x5, S3 read-ahead), `7 825111 569492` (x5), `4 17844 17844` (x5), and a long tail of `4 66446 679xx`/`4 66446 66533` where only `ReadCompressedBytes` drifts by tens to ~1700 bytes. The two most recent master hits are `4 66446 68063` (2026-07-26) and `4 66446 66533` (2026-07-27). #### What the test guards, and why no bound on `ReadCompressedBytes` can guard it The regression fixed together with this test was `AsynchronousBoundedReadBuffer::seek` taking the lazy-ignore branch while `file_offset_of_buffer_end` was still 0, so the buffer downloaded the whole prefix ahead of the first needed granule and discarded it. I reproduced that by removing the `file_offset_of_buffer_end &&` guard in `AsynchronousBoundedReadBuffer::seek` together with the `!current_buf ||` short-circuit in `ReadBufferFromRemoteFSGather::isSeekCheap` (the second one is required, otherwise `isSeekCheap()` returns true on the first seek and the branch is unreachable). On this fixture the narrow read then transfers 853846 S3 bytes instead of 66446, of which 787400 are discarded. `ReadCompressedBytes` does not move at all: it is incremented in `CompressedReadBufferBase` for blocks handed to the decompressor, while the ignored prefix is dropped lower down in `ThreadPoolRemoteFSReader::execute` before any block is assembled. On the buggy build `ReadCompressedBytes` is 66446, byte-for-byte equal to the healthy build. So no threshold on it can detect the over-read: not `< 1000000`, not `< 100000`, not even the exact `66446` the reference used to pin. The previous revision of this PR claimed the 1 MB bound would still catch an over-read; that claim was wrong and is retracted. Measured, narrow read, healthy vs buggy: | build | `S3ReadRequestsCount` | `ReadBufferFromS3Bytes` | `ReadCompressedBytes` | `AsynchronousReaderIgnoredBytes` | |---|---|---|---|---| | healthy | 4 | 66446 | 66446 | 0 | | guards removed | 4 | 853846 | 66446 | 787400 | #### The fix Assert the counter that actually observes the defect. The query seeks each column once, from offset 0, so a correct lazy ignore never triggers and `AsynchronousReaderIgnoredBytes` is exactly 0: ``` ProfileEvents['RemoteFSSeeks'] > 0, ProfileEvents['AsynchronousReaderIgnoredBytes'] = 0, ProfileEvents['S3ReadRequestsCount'] < 100, ProfileEvents['ReadCompressedBytes'] < 1000000 ``` `RemoteFSSeeks > 0` is an activation check. With `remote_filesystem_read_method = 'read'` there is no `AsynchronousBoundedReadBuffer` at all, so the ignored-bytes assertion would pass vacuously: on the buggy build, method `read` reports `RemoteFSSeeks` 0 and `AsynchronousReaderIgnoredBytes` 0 while `threadpool` reports 2 and 787400. `tests/clickhouse-test` does randomize `remote_filesystem_read_method` over `read` and `threadpool`, but the existing `no-random-settings` tag already suppresses that for this test, so the pin and the assertion are not guarding against the current randomizer: they guard against the default changing, the tag being dropped, or the test being edited onto the synchronous path, any of which would silently turn the ignored-bytes check into a no-op. `ReadCompressedBytes < 1000000` is kept as a granule-selection bound (a whole-column read is ~4 MB compressed), with a comment that no longer overstates what it covers. `ReadBufferFromS3Bytes` stays dropped: it is the unstable raw-transfer count (830 on a cache hit, 7.2 MB under read-ahead). #### Verification Local server over MinIO `s3_disk` (same disk definition as `tests/config/config.d/storage_conf.xml`), Build IDs recorded for each direction: - healthy build `66c6aded`: `1 1 1 1`, 10/10, and stable 15/15 on a fresh database. - guards removed, build `0c2a53f6`: `1 0 1 1`, 10/10. Only the new column reacts; the two surviving bounds print `1 1` on the buggy build, which is exactly the coverage gap this change closes. - activation mutation: dropping the read-method pin on the buggy build gives `RemoteFSSeeks` 0 / ignored 0 for method `read` (bug invisible, caught by the activation assertion) versus `RemoteFSSeeks` 2 / ignored 787400 for `threadpool`. - `AsynchronousReaderIgnoredBytes` is 0 across the regimes that made the old assertion flaky: repeated reads, prefetch off, `max_threads` 1 and 16, `remote_read_min_bytes_for_seek = 0`, parallel replicas, larger prefetch steps, larger read buffer. This flake is unrelated to #100391: the query has no `ORDER BY`, so the read-in-order path that PR changes is not exercised.

signal.title: Throw a clear error when a marks file listed in checksums is missing on disk
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Improved the error message when a marks file that is listed in a data part's checksums is missing on disk. Reading such a column, or loading the part's index granularity, now raises `NO_FILE_IN_DATA_PART` naming the part, the missing file and the part's on-disk state, instead of an opaque `std::filesystem` `file_size: No such file or directory` error. ### Description `MergeTreeMarksLoader::loadMarksImpl()` derives the marks file path from the part's own checksums (`getStreamNameForColumn` only returns a stream name that is present in the part's checksums), so the file is expected to exist on disk. When it does not, `getFileSize()` throws an opaque ``` Code: 1001. DB::Exception: std::__1::filesystem::filesystem_error: filesystem error: in file_size: No such file or directory [".../<col>.cmrk2"] ``` with no indication of which part is affected or what its on-disk state is. This surfaces in the flaky integration test `test_rename_column::test_rename_distributed_parallel_insert_and_select` (Integration tests, amd_tsan; report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=100703&sha=e93ea3312f0d1107b3977560deafaa4241bd89b7&name_0=PR&name_1=Integration%20tests%20%28amd_tsan%2C%201%2F6%29 ) under heavy concurrent `RENAME COLUMN` + `INSERT` + `SELECT` load, where it is impossible to diagnose from the message alone. CIDB shows it on 3 unrelated PRs over the last 30 days and never on master, so it is a rare concurrency window rather than a single PR's regression. This PR does not fix the underlying race (which is not reproducible locally on a single host: 94/94 idle and CPU-jittered iterations passed). Instead it makes the next occurrence diagnosable: before calling `getFileSize()`, check whether the marks file exists, and if it does not, throw `NO_FILE_IN_DATA_PART` with the part name, path, columns, the files listed in the part's checksums, and the actual on-disk listing. The existence check runs only on the error path, so successful reads are unaffected. Example of the new message: ``` Code: 226. DB::Exception: Marks file 'b.cmrk2' does not exist in part 'all_1_1_0' at '.../all_1_1_0/', although it is listed in the part's checksums. Part columns: [...]. Checksums files: [a.bin, a.cmrk2, b.bin, b.cmrk2, ...]. Files on disk: [a.bin, a.cmrk2, b.bin, ...]. (NO_FILE_IN_DATA_PART) ``` A stateless test (`03810_missing_marks_file_error`) removes a column's marks file from a wide part and asserts the typed error is raised.

signal.title: Refresh TO-target materialized view columns when upstream tables are altered
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106919 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `DESCRIBE` and `SHOW CREATE TABLE` reporting stale column types for a materialized view created with `TO target` after the source or target table columns were changed with `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COLUMN`. Previously the view kept the types inferred at creation time, which also made `SELECT` from the view fail (for example with `UNKNOWN_ELEMENT_OF_ENUM`) when the new types were incompatible. The view's inferred columns are now refreshed on the upstream `ALTER`; explicit-column views keep their declared types. ### Description After an `ALTER` that changes a table's columns, the column metadata of dependent `TO`-target materialized views is refreshed when their stored columns are still in sync with the view's `SELECT` output (recomputed against the pre-`ALTER` schema). The refresh re-runs the same `SELECT`-output inference used at create time, so inferred-column views track the new upstream types while explicit-column views (`TO t (x String) ...`) and views whose columns intentionally diverge from the `SELECT` output (e.g. `SELECT 1 AS v2` over a wider target column) are left untouched. Existing tests `02931`, `01069`, `01182` keep their current behavior; new test: `04327_mv_to_target_columns_refresh_on_alter`.

signal.title: Fix wrong result for duplicate-named subquery columns wrapped in SELECT *
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106923 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a wrong result when a subquery has two output columns with the same name backed by different expressions (for example a constant column colliding with a starred column of the same name) and the subquery is wrapped in an outer `SELECT *`. Previously one column's value (often a constant) overwrote the other; for a non-matched `RIGHT`/`FULL JOIN` row this kept the constant's literal value instead of the default. ### Description Reproducer (deterministic, default settings): ```sql SELECT 1, * FROM (SELECT 2 AS x, 1) AS a RIGHT JOIN (SELECT 3 AS y) AS b ON y = x; -- 1 0 0 3 (correct: both left-side columns are defaulted on the non-matched row) SELECT * FROM (SELECT 1, * FROM (SELECT 2 AS x, 1) AS a RIGHT JOIN (SELECT 3 AS y) AS b ON y = x); -- before: 1 0 1 3 (wrong: the left subquery's constant column survives as 1) -- after: 1 0 0 3 (matches the unwrapped query) ``` Root cause: the planner addresses a subquery's output column purely by `source_alias + "." + column_name`, with no positional discriminator. When a subquery's projection has two columns with the same name, the outer `SELECT *` matcher resolves both to a single `ColumnNode`, only one column identifier is registered for that name, and the second column's value is replaced by the first. Fix: when a subquery has duplicate projection column names backed by non-equal expressions, the later occurrences are given unique internal names so the planner assigns each a distinct identifier. The original user-visible display names are preserved (the correct output legitimately has duplicate display names). Two cases are intentionally left unchanged: equal expressions with the same name (`SELECT number, number`), which collapse harmlessly, and a later explicit alias that redefines a same-named starred column (`SELECT *, expr AS c`), which is intentional shadowing (issue #14739). Found by the AST-fuzzer correctness oracle.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Do not install standalone symlinks for multi-call-only subcommands
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/36588 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/36588 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Build/Testing/Packaging Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Stop installing standalone `clickhouse-<name>` symlinks for subcommands that no package ships. This removes useless work from the CMake install step without changing the produced packages. ### Description Step 1 of #36588. `ninja programs/install` copied a `clickhouse-<name>` symlink into the packaging root (`<build>/root/usr/bin/`) for every subcommand registered via `clickhouse_program_install`. nfpm builds every package strictly from the explicit `src:` entries in `packages/clickhouse-*.yaml` (no globs), and 14 of those symlinks are referenced by no manifest, so installing them only populated the staging tree. This splits the helper into: - `clickhouse_program_link(name lib)` - link the subcommand library into the multi-call binary and create the `clickhouse-<name>` symlink in the build directory (no install); - `clickhouse_program_install(name lib [aliases...])` - the same, plus install the standalone symlink (and aliases) for packaging. 14 subcommands are switched to `clickhouse_program_link`: `check-marks`, `checksum-for-compressed-block`, `disks`, `docker-init`, `git-import`, `oom-canary`, `packed-io`, `static-files-disk-uploader`, `su`, `zookeeper-dump-tree`, `zookeeper-remove-by-list`, `keeper-data-dumper`, `keeper-utils`, `keeper-bench`. The criterion is the packaging reference, not the invocation surface. Two of the 14, `clickhouse-disks` and `clickhouse-git-import`, are also symlinked by `clickhouse install` from its own `tools` list in `programs/install/Install.cpp`. That path is unaffected: it symlinks from the binary it has just copied itself, and never reads this staging tree. The build-tree symlinks and the multi-call dispatch table in `programs/main.cpp` are unchanged, so `clickhouse <name>` keeps working. Verified by configuring the tree with and without this change, everything else identical: the installed set drops exactly those 14 symlinks and gains none, and all 30 build-tree `create_symlink` commands are still generated. Packages are unaffected. Step 2 of the issue (dropping CMake `install` entirely in favour of direct build-directory paths in the packaging YAML) is a deliberate follow-up.

signal.title: Fix LOGICAL_ERROR on single-argument or() in JOIN ON
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Closes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112654 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Description `tryExtractCommonExpressions` in the `LogicalExpressionOptimizer` pass assumed every `or()` function node has at least two arguments and enforced it with `chassert(or_argument_nodes.size() > 1)`, aborting the server in debug/sanitizer builds. Release builds are not affected (the `chassert` is a no-op there and the query returns the correct empty result), hence no changelog entry. A single-argument `or()` can be resolved when its only argument has the `Nothing` type: `IFunctionOverloadResolver::getReturnTypeWithoutLowCardinality` short-circuits to `Nothing` for any `Nothing`-typed argument before the function's own `getReturnTypeImpl` runs, so the "at least 2 arguments" check in `FunctionAnyArityLogical` is skipped. An empty `ARRAY JOIN` makes a column `Nothing`-typed, so ```sql CREATE TABLE t1 (c0 Int) ENGINE = Memory; SELECT t1.c0 FROM t1 AS tx LEFT ARRAY JOIN [] AS a0 LEFT JOIN t1 ON or(a0 = t1.c0); ``` produced a single-argument `or()` in the `JOIN ON` expression and tripped the assert. Common-expression extraction across disjuncts is meaningless with fewer than two disjuncts, so the pass now returns without optimizing instead of asserting. The single-argument `or()` then falls through to normal `JOIN ON` validation, which rejects invalid cases with a clear error. Found by the AST fuzzer (STID 2508-3fad). Reproduced on two unrelated PRs: - AST fuzzer (amd_debug, targeted): https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=106981&sha=63804eccd611e475770d838739aebcfd894db406&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29 - AST fuzzer (arm_asan_ubsan): PR #106682, 2026-06-07. Added regression test `04327_single_argument_or_in_join_on`.

signal.title: Fix LOGICAL_ERROR on runtime filter lookup before build finished
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a `LOGICAL_ERROR` exception "Trying to lookup values in runtime filter before building it was finished" during JOINs with `enable_join_runtime_filters` enabled when the join stops reading the build side early (for example `join_overflow_mode = 'break'` with a finite `max_rows_in_join` / `max_bytes_in_join`, or an empty/short-circuited right side). ### Description Found by the AST fuzzer (STID 2210-585c) and reproducible on master. A JOIN runtime filter is built on the right (build) side by N parallel `BuildRuntimeFilterTransform` streams. The filter becomes visible to `RuntimeFilterLookup::find(name)` after the FIRST stream's `finish()`, but `IRuntimeFilter::inserts_are_finished` only becomes true after the LAST stream merges its partial filter (`filters_to_merge` reaches 0). The probe (left) side applies the filter via `FunctionApplyFilter` -> `IRuntimeFilter::find()`. Normally the join's pull discipline guarantees the build side is fully consumed before the probe side runs. But when the join stops reading the build side early, `FillingRightJoinSideTransform` closes its input and the build-phase finish counter reaches `isLast()` before all N `BuildRuntimeFilterTransform` streams have called `finish()`. The probe side then calls `find()` on a filter whose `inserts_are_finished` is still false, and `IRuntimeFilter::find()` raised a `LOGICAL_ERROR`, crashing debug/sanitizer builds. The runtime filter is a best-effort optimization: correctness always comes from the JOIN itself, never from this pre-filter (`FunctionApplyFilter` already returns const-true when the filter is absent). The fix makes `find()` pass all rows through (return const-true) when the build side is not finished yet, instead of throwing. This is safe for both "contains" and "not-contains" filter polarities, since the JOIN drops the non-matching rows. `finishInsert()` is also reordered to finalize the underlying set/bloom filter before publishing `inserts_are_finished = true`, so a concurrent `find()` can never observe a half-built filter. Adds a functional test (`04337_runtime_filter_lookup_before_finished`) that drives a real JOIN pipeline with `join_overflow_mode = 'break'` and a tiny `max_bytes_in_join` over a multi-part build table, so the probe side reaches `find()` while the runtime filter is still unfinished. The query is repeated so the probabilistic race is hit with high probability; without the fix at least one repetition aborts the server, and with the fix the test passes. Report (AST fuzzer, amd_debug, targeted): https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=103322&sha=eeec76f833a27b148d130ef8f504ac362f26caef&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29

signal.title: Support group_by_use_nulls in WITH TOTALS
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/39574 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `GROUP BY ... WITH TOTALS` now respects the `group_by_use_nulls` setting when the analyzer is enabled (`enable_analyzer = 1`, the default): the GROUP BY keys in the TOTALS summary row are reported as `NULL` instead of their default values, consistent with `GROUPING SETS`, `ROLLUP` and `CUBE`. Keys whose types cannot be wrapped in `Nullable` (for example `Array` or `Map`) keep their default value. With the old query analyzer (`enable_analyzer = 0`) the keys keep their default value as before. ### Description Rebase and port of #39574 (original author @ novikd) on top of current master. With `group_by_use_nulls = 1`, GROUP BY keys are already reported as `Nullable` for `GROUPING SETS`, `ROLLUP` and `CUBE`, but plain `GROUP BY ... WITH TOTALS` was left out: the keys stayed non-nullable and the TOTALS summary row showed `0` (the default value) instead of `NULL`. The original PR fixed this in the old interpreter by converting the keys inside `AggregatingStep`. The analyzer is now the default, so this ports the fix to the analyzer planner: - `PlannerExpressionAnalysis`: include `WITH TOTALS` in the `group_by_use_nulls` condition so the result type of the keys is analyzed as `Nullable`. - `Planner`: insert a `toNullable` conversion for the GROUP BY keys right before the `TotalsHaving` step. The TOTALS row is filled from default values, so a `Nullable` key column yields `NULL` there. This also covers `CUBE`/`ROLLUP WITH TOTALS`, whose own nullable conversion happens after `TotalsHaving` and would otherwise leave the TOTALS row non-NULL. Keys that cannot be made `Nullable` are skipped. Example (before this change the last row was `0`): ```sql SELECT number FROM numbers(10) GROUP BY number WITH TOTALS ORDER BY number SETTINGS group_by_use_nulls = 1; -- 0 .. 9 -- -- \N ``` The behavior is analyzer-only, so the affected tests set `enable_analyzer = 1`, and the documentation/changelog qualify the behavior as applying only with the analyzer. Updated tests: `02343_group_by_use_nulls`, `02535_analyzer_group_by_use_nulls`, `03912_tuple_comparison_group_by_use_nulls`, and the new `02373_group_by_use_nulls_with_totals` (from the original PR).

signal.title: Do not terminate the server on retryable errors while loading outdated parts
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106736 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Do not terminate the server when a transient retryable error (such as `MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` or a network error) occurs while loading outdated or unexpected data parts in the background. Such errors are not a sign of an inconsistent on-disk set of parts, so the loading task is now retried instead of aborting the whole server. The existing fail-fast behaviour is preserved for genuinely inconsistent state. ### Description Closes #106736 `MergeTreeData::loadOutdatedDataParts()` and the sibling `loadUnexpectedDataParts()` wrap their whole body in a `catch (...)` that calls `std::terminate()`, to fail fast on a genuinely inconsistent on-disk set of parts. The same `catch` also fires for transient runtime errors such as `MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (including the stress test memory fault injector) or network errors, which are not on-disk corruption. This takes the whole server down in the experimental `serverfuzz` stress jobs. `loadDataPartWithRetries()` already classifies and retries such exceptions via `isRetryableException()`, but only around `loadDataPart()` itself; an exception thrown elsewhere in the loader (part removal, ZooKeeper cleanup, rename, the runner machinery, or newly memory-tracked allocations) escapes straight to the terminating `catch`. The fix reuses `isRetryableException()` in both `catch` blocks: for a retryable error in the asynchronous background loader, it logs a warning and reschedules the loading task instead of terminating, so the server stays up and retries once the transient condition clears. Non-retryable errors and the synchronous drop-table path keep the existing fail-fast behaviour. The unexpected-parts loop is made idempotent so a rescheduled retry skips already-loaded parts. A `REGULAR` failpoint `mergetree_load_outdated_parts_inject_retryable_exception` and an integration test (`test_load_outdated_parts_retryable`) inject a retryable error into the outdated-parts loader and verify the server survives and finishes loading. The retry must not requeue a part whose retryable error happened after it was already published. `loadDataPartWithRetries()` inserts a normal Outdated part into `data_parts_indexes` before its post-load cleanup (`preparePartForRemoval` writes the removal TID and can throw retryably); requeueing it as-is made the retry reload the same directory as a fresh part, hit the duplicate-part path, and `remove()` could delete the directory while the published part still referenced it. The published part is now rolled back out of the index before requeueing so the retry reloads it cleanly. The unexpected-parts loop has the same shape (its optional `broken-on-start` detach runs after the part is set), so it now uses a separate `finished` marker set only after the detach succeeds. Two more failpoints exercise these post-load paths and the integration test gains a third case asserting nothing is wrongly detached. The broken-part detach in both loaders no longer hides its errors. It used to call `renameToDetached("broken-on-start", /*ignore_error=*/ replicated)`, and `renameToDetached` swallows `ErrnoException` and `fs::filesystem_error` when `ignore_error` is set - exactly the exception types a failing rename raises, and exactly the class `isRetryableException` treats as transient. On a replicated table a transient detach failure therefore never reached the new classification: the worker continued as if the cleanup had succeeded, leaving the broken outdated part on its original path with its ZooKeeper entry already removed, or setting the unexpected part's `finished` marker so the retry skipped it. Both call sites now pass `ignore_error = false` and classify the error themselves; the tolerance `ignore_error` gave replicated tables is preserved, but only for a permanent failure and only after the retryable case has been handled. A failpoint that throws the swallowed exception type and a regression case per loader cover it. #### Provenance Surfaced on master as the `'px != 0' failed` family whose actual fatal is the `loadOutdatedDataParts` terminate. Latest master hit: `Stress test (experimental, serverfuzz, arm_release)`, commit `81a8bcef7e8ba2dae3dfdc762dde87a853f40070`, STID 3782-2f00. Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=81a8bcef7e8ba2dae3dfdc762dde87a853f40070&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28experimental%2C%20serverfuzz%2C%20arm_release%29

signal.title: Fix mapKeys bloom_filter index over-pruning for FixedString default equality
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106924 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed wrong query results and spurious errors when a `bloom_filter` index on `mapKeys(map)` or `mapValues(map)` is used with a `map[key] = const` comparison. Index analysis compared the constant against the wrong default and hashed it without converting it to the indexed type, so `map[k] = toFixedString('', N)` returned no rows, a `mapValues` index dropped a matching granule for a constant storing a different representation of the indexed string type, and a valid predicate such as `map[k] = 1.0` over a `Map(String, UInt64)` failed with `BAD_GET`. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106924 Three defects in `MergeTreeIndexConditionBloomFilter::traverseTreeEquals`, all reachable from `map[key] = const`. **1. The absent-key default was compared against the wrong type.** An absent key makes `map[key]` return the map value type default, so a granule lacking the key still matches when `default = const`. The check compared the constant byte-wise against the *constant's* own type default: for `toFixedString('', 3)` that is 3 NUL bytes against an empty `String`, so every granule without the key was pruned although `'' = toFixedString('', 3)` is true at runtime. The real `equals` now runs on a default column of the map value type. A NULL result is not a match, so a `Nullable` value type stays prunable. **2. `mapValues` hashed a constant storing a different representation.** Equality ignores trailing NUL padding, and an `Enum` constant carries its number while equality compares the name, so one constant can equal several stored values or hash to what none of them produces, dropping a matching granule. The index is now used only when the constant's primitive type equals the indexed string type. Wrappers are ignored, since a `LowCardinality(String)` constant stores the same `String`. **3. `mapValues` hashed the raw constant.** `hashWithField` reads the `Field` via `Field::safeGet`, which tolerates only `UInt64 <-> Int64`, so any other constant type threw `BAD_GET` and failed a valid query. It is converted first, as the ordinary column path and the sibling `mapContainsValue` and `IN` paths already did, and the index is declined when the constant is not representable. A resource limit, stack overflow, cancellation or internal error still reaches the caller rather than quietly disabling the index. The test asserts both directions per case: granules-read < granules-total where pruning must survive, `INDEX_NOT_USED` where it must decline. <details> <summary>Measured carriers</summary> `BAD_GET` on a valid predicate (defect 3), all on master before this change: | indexed `mapValues` type | constant type | |---|---| | `UInt64` | `Float64`, `Int128`, `Decimal64` | | `Float64` | `UInt64` | | `Date`, `Enum8` | `String` | | `Int128` | `Int64` | A matching granule dropped (defect 2), against an indexed `String`: a `FixedString` of a different width, `Enum8`, `LowCardinality(FixedString(3))`, `Variant(FixedString(3), UInt64)`. The last two also predate this PR. A resource limit, a stack overflow, a cancellation or an internal error is not a statement about the constant, so it still reaches the caller rather than quietly disabling the index. `mapKeys` needs no conversion, since `arrayElement` resolves the key constant to the map key type first. Heterogeneous integers were already sound: both signednesses share one `Field` slot and `getNumberTypeHash` casts to the indexed type. </details>

signal.title: Do not leak a correlated subquery's `TOTALS` into the outer query
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106920 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a spurious `TOTALS` block returned for a non-aggregate `SELECT` whose `WHERE` contains a correlated subquery using `GROUP BY ... WITH TOTALS`. The subquery's totals are no longer propagated as the outer query's totals. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106920 A non-aggregate `SELECT` returned an extra totals row when its `WHERE` contained a correlated scalar or `EXISTS` subquery producing a totals stream: ```sql CREATE TABLE t (id UInt32, val Int64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id; INSERT INTO t SELECT number, number * 7 FROM numbers(3); SELECT id FROM t WHERE id >= (SELECT 0 GROUP BY 1 WITH TOTALS HAVING isNull(val) = 0); -- returned 0, 1, 2 and then a spurious totals row ``` **Root cause.** A subquery's totals are not part of the value it returns; the non-correlated scalar evaluator consumes data chunks only. Decorrelation replaces the subquery with a `JOIN`, and `joinPipelinesRightLeft` propagates totals from whichever input has them. **The change.** `buildLogicalJoin` is the only place where the join's two inputs are unambiguous, so it records there which input carries the subquery (after the `correlated_subqueries_default_join_kind` swap, so one expression covers both values). `JoinStep::updatePipeline` drops that input's totals and extremes at the top, before the `swap_streams` swap and before algorithm dispatch, the only point where the pipelines still match the step's declared inputs. Only the carrier input is touched, so a legitimate totals stream on the other input still propagates (guarded by `03808_correlated_subquery_with_totals`). That side is only meaningful while the join has two inputs, so the existing swap-only `query_graph_size_limit = 2` clamp is extended to cover it, and the side is re-derived after reconstruction, reversing it when the optimizer flips the children. **Validation.** New test `04327_correlated_subquery_with_totals`, 26 assertions covering scalar and `EXISTS`, nested totals, both values of `correlated_subqueries_default_join_kind` and `correlated_subqueries_use_in_memory_buffer`, an aggregating outer query, `extremes = 1`, `WITH ROLLUP`, a cached subquery, a distributed plan. Fails on master, passes here, 50 randomized runs green. The existing correlated suite shows no reference churn: the only `.reference` this PR changes is the new one. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=107075&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/107075](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F107075+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix minmax skip index and partition pruning skipping NaN under negated float ranges
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106533 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106948 Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110266 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/106568 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix wrong results when a `MergeTree` query filters a `Float`/`Nullable(Float)` column with a negated comparison range such as `NOT ((val >= a) AND (val <= b))`. Partition pruning and the `minmax` skip index previously dropped partitions or granules containing `NaN`, even though `NaN` rows satisfy the negated predicate (since `NaN >= a` is false). Regression since v26.3. ### Description Supersedes #106568, which fixed only the partition-pruning half of #106533, and fixes the skip-index half (#106948). One root cause: range analysis over floats ignores `NaN` under a negated comparison. **1. `KeyCondition` negation rewrite (#106533).** `cloneDAGWithInversionPushDown` rewrites `not(greater(x, c))` into `lessOrEquals(x, c)`. That is invalid when an operand can be `NaN`: `not(NaN > c)` is true while `NaN <= c` is false, so pruning dropped the partition holding the `NaN`. The rewrite is now skipped for the six comparison ops when an operand is a non-constant float column or a `NaN` constant. Finite constants and non-float types are unaffected. **2. `minmax` loses `NaN` in mixed granules (#106948).** Granule extremes come from `getExtremes`, which skips `NaN`, so `[1.0, nan, 3.0]` stored a clean `[1, 3]`. Since `NaN` sorts after `+inf`, the true upper bound is `NaN`: it is now stored as the max, tripping the `NaN` guard in `checkInHyperrectangle`. Widening a range only causes conservative keeps, never wrong skips, so positive-range pruning is intact. Covers the skip index and the part-level minmax. **3. Single-sided comparison (#110266).** Same cause for `NOT(f > c)` over an all-`NaN` granule; fix 1 covers it and `04327` asserts it. **Upgrade behavior.** Both fixes are on the write path, and neither on-disk format (`.idx2`, `minmax_<col>.idx`) carries a version marker, so a reader cannot tell a pre-fix granule from a good one. Parts written before the upgrade keep the old result until rewritten via `ALTER TABLE ... REWRITE PARTS`. `MATERIALIZE INDEX` does **not** help (the mutation hardlinks an index file already present); `OPTIMIZE ... FINAL` repairs skip indexes but not the part-level minmax, which a non-row-reducing merge unions from its sources. Closes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106533 Closes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106948 Closes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/110266 <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=107074&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/107074](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F107074+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Do not connect to MySQL during startup metadata loading
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed slow server startup when a `MySQL` database engine points at a host that black-holes the connection. The MySQL database engine no longer connects to the server during startup metadata loading; tables are fetched lazily on first access, matching the `PostgreSQL` database engine. ### Description `DatabaseMySQL` connected to the MySQL server synchronously in its constructor (`empty()` -> `fetchTablesIntoLocalCache()`). The constructor runs during startup metadata loading and on `ATTACH DATABASE`, both of which happen before the server binds its listen ports. A `MySQL` database engine pointing at a host that drops connection attempts (so the connect blocks until timeout, rather than failing fast) then stalls startup for `connect_timeout * connection_max_tries` before the ports come up. `DatabasePostgreSQL` already does the right thing: its constructor does not connect, and tables are fetched lazily on access. This change makes `DatabaseMySQL` match by skipping the constructor connect when `attach` is true (server startup / `ATTACH DATABASE`). Tables are still fetched lazily by every accessor (`empty` / `getTablesIterator` / `tryGetTable`), so behavior on access is unchanged. The non-attach `CREATE DATABASE` path keeps its original probe and error semantics. The integration test in this PR (`test_restart_server_with_unreachable_mysql`) demonstrates the behavior: with the host partitioned away, without this change the server does not come up within the start window; with it, the server starts and the database is fetched lazily on first access.

signal.title: Retry tests on the "Coordination error:" rendering of transient Keeper errors
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/80416 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description The functional test runner (`tests/clickhouse-test`) retries a test when its output matches an entry in `MESSAGES_TO_RETRY`. The two transient-Keeper entries only match the socket-layer rendering `Coordination::Exception: Session expired` / `Coordination::Exception: Connection loss`. Generic Keeper operations (`exists`/`get`/`getChildren`) throw via the `Coordination::Exception(code)` / `fromPath(code, path)` constructors, which format the message as `"Coordination error: {}"`. The client then prints: ``` Code: 999. Coordination::Exception: Coordination error: Session expired, path /zookeeper/.../replicas/1/is_active. (KEEPER_EXCEPTION) ``` That string is not a substring of the existing retry entries, so the runner never retried it and the test failed instead. This is the OPTIMIZE wait path in `StorageReplicatedMergeTree` (`tryWaitForReplicaToProcessLogEntry` -> `getZooKeeper()->exists(.../is_active)`), which surfaced as a flaky failure of `03100_lwu_29_concurrent_merges` on amd_tsan during `OPTIMIZE TABLE` (reported on #80416). The same `Coordination error:` rendering also hit `test_drop_database_replica` and `test_distributed_ddl_parallel`. Fix: add the `Coordination error: ...` variants so both renderings are retried. The existing entries are kept so the socket-layer rendering stays covered. No test reference file contains these strings, so there is no false-positive risk.

signal.title: Fix crash on skip index over a column with pending ALTER MODIFY COLUMN type change
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112213 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112484 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a `LOGICAL_ERROR` exception ("Sizes of nested column and null map ... are not equal after deserialization") when querying a table with a skip index over a column that has a pending `ALTER MODIFY COLUMN` type change while `apply_mutations_on_fly` and `apply_patch_parts` are both disabled. ### Description A pending `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COLUMN` leaves old parts with skip-index data serialized using the old column type. `MergeTreeDataSelectExecutor::canUseIndex` skips such an index for a part by checking the column against `AlterConversions::getAllUpdatedColumns()`, populated from the read snapshot's `READ_COLUMN` mutations. `createStorageSnapshot` built that snapshot with `need_alter_mutations = apply_mutations_on_fly || apply_patch_parts`. With both off the pending mutation is dropped, the incompatible index is not excluded, and `filterMarksUsingIndex` deserializes an old granule with the new type. For `String` to `Nullable(UInt64)` that raises `Sizes of nested column and null map of Nullable column are not equal after deserialization` (an exception in release builds; debug and sanitizer builds abort). The implicit `count()` projection reaches the index read during planning, so a plain `SELECT count()` is enough. Neither setting relates to column type changes, so the snapshot now requests alter mutations whenever one is pending. The request is `need_alter_mutations_if_pending`, resolved against `num_alter` inside `getMutationsSnapshot`, which already holds the lock guarding the counters and already reads them for its fast-path condition. A read with no pending alter still returns the empty snapshot without scanning `current_mutations_by_version`, and adds no lock acquisition. Column data reads were already correct: `IMergeTreeReader` converts from the part's own stored type. The `supportsSkipIndexesOnDataRead` guard covers the data-read phase but not this planning-time path; both are pinned by the tests. Found by serverfuzz running `03702_alter_column_modify_secondary_index_rebuild.sh`. Repro: ```sql CREATE TABLE tg (id UInt64, value String, INDEX idx_set (value) TYPE set(0) GRANULARITY 1) ENGINE = MergeTree() ORDER BY id PARTITION BY id SETTINGS add_minmax_index_for_numeric_columns = 0, min_bytes_for_wide_part = 0; INSERT INTO tg VALUES (1, '10'), (2, '20'), (3, '300'); SYSTEM STOP MERGES tg; ALTER TABLE tg MODIFY COLUMN value Nullable(UInt64) SETTINGS alter_sync = 0, mutations_sync = 0; SELECT count() FROM tg WHERE value = 300 SETTINGS apply_mutations_on_fly = 0, apply_patch_parts = 0; ``` Related: #112213 (this fixes the pending-mutation half; the killed-mutation half is #112484).

signal.title: Fix signed integer overflow in condition_variable::wait_for with huge timeouts
signal.text: A wait-timeout setting that reaches `std::condition_variable::wait_for` unchecked overflows the chrono conversion inside it. libc++ evaluates `wait_for(d)` as `steady_clock::now() + d` in nanoseconds, multiplying a millisecond duration by 1000000: a timeout above ~9.2e12 ms overflows Int64, and one above the Int64 millisecond range even turns into a negative duration, so the wait returns at once and the caller busy-loops instead of waiting. UBSan aborts the server; a release build silently wraps. The setting that reaches it in practice is `interactive_delay`, a plain unbounded `UInt64` of microseconds: the server waits `interactive_delay / 1000` milliseconds for the next result chunk in `ConcurrentBoundedQueue::popImpl`, through the lazy output format, on both the `TCPHandler` and the `clickhouse-local` path. Found by serverfuzz on master, and again in the stress test of an unrelated pull request — https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112177&sha=e601607e228ad5d736ad491220ebf4b62d531d51&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_asan_ubsan%2C%20s3%29 (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112177): ``` /ClickHouse/contrib/llvm-project/libcxx/include/__chrono/duration.h:93:79: runtime error: signed integer overflow: 18584892780430 * 1000000 cannot be represented in type '_Ct' (aka 'long long') ... #6 ConcurrentBoundedQueue<DB::Chunk>::popImpl<true>(...) src/Common/ConcurrentBoundedQueue.h:73 #8 DB::LazyOutputFormat::getChunk(unsigned long) src/Processors/Formats/LazyOutputFormat.cpp:25 #11 DB::TCPHandler::processOrdinaryQuery(DB::QueryState&) src/Server/TCPHandler.cpp:1540 SUMMARY: UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer: undefined-behavior ``` Reproduces deterministically: ``` clickhouse-local --query "SELECT 1 SETTINGS interactive_delay = 100000000000000000" ``` Fix: clamp the timeout to one year before constructing the chrono duration, via a small shared helper `saturatedMilliseconds`. The same cap is already used for `CancellationChecker` (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/96450); it is applied here to the remaining `wait_for` sites that take a user-controlled millisecond timeout, and `saturatedSeconds`/`saturatedSecondsFrom` cover the seconds-typed timeouts and the query cache expiry built as `now() + seconds(query_cache_ttl)`. A `Milliseconds`- or `Seconds`-typed setting can no longer carry such a value in the first place: `SettingFieldTimespan` rejects a value that does not fit into Int64 microseconds, so the clamp there is only defence in depth. That check landed on master after this branch was cut and supersedes the saturating conversion this pull request originally added to `SettingsFields`, which is dropped along with its unit tests in favour of master's stricter ones. What is left for the clamp is every setting that is not a timespan — above all `interactive_delay`. Keeper has its own coordination waits with a different bound; they are handled separately in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112088. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112088 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112177 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a signed integer overflow when a wait-timeout setting, such as `interactive_delay`, was set to a huge value: the wait could time out immediately instead of waiting, and the server could abort under the Undefined Behavior Sanitizer.

signal.title: Break symlink loops in StorageFile glob expansion
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/106676 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes `Too many levels of symbolic links` errors and duplicate or missing rows when the `file()` table function expands a recursive glob (`**`) over a directory tree containing a symlink to an ancestor directory. Such a walk is now pruned per (directory, remaining pattern) frame, and matches are deduplicated by resolved parent directory, so a symlinked ancestor neither loops nor yields a file twice while a symlink to a file is still reported under its own name. ### Description Recursive glob expansion in `listFilesWithRegexpMatchingImpl` did not protect against directory symlinks that target an ancestor. `fs::directory_iterator` does not follow symlinks for iteration, but `directory_entry::is_directory` does, so the recursion descended a loop until the kernel hit `ELOOP` and surfaced a raw `std::filesystem::filesystem_error: Too many levels of symbolic links` (`STD_EXCEPTION`). The depth cap added in #106676 does not catch this because the kernel error fires first. The walk now enters each frame at most once, where a frame is the canonical directory together with the pattern still to be matched there. That pair is the whole state of the walk, so a frame repeating it can only redo what another frame already did, whether that is an enclosing frame (a cycle) or a finished sibling (an alias). Keying on the directory alone is wrong, because `**` matches zero levels: the re-application enters the current directory with a shorter suffix while the enclosing frame is still there, and directory-only keying dropped it, so `file('root/*/**/top.txt')` with `root/x/back -> ..` returned 0 rows instead of 1. Because a `**` walk can now reach one file through two frames, its match deduplication resolves the parent directory of each match; lexical forms do not resolve symlinks. The final component is deliberately left as written, so a symlink to a file and its target stay two rows, which is what the pattern selected. This is scoped to `**` expansions, since a finite glob can also name one file twice through two ancestor aliases sharing a filename, and master reports both. Deduplication only filters results, so it cannot stop the walk re-descending; a dense graph of aliased directories previously returned 109600 rows for eight real files, and now returns 8. `04325_test_storage_file_glob_symlink_loop` covers the loop, aliasing, finite-glob and write-refusal shapes above; each assertion is mutation-tested. <details> <summary>Canonicalization cost on large symlink-free trees</summary> Deduplicating by canonical path needs the canonical parent of each match. Every entry one invocation emits shares that parent, so a glob suffix resolves once per directory rather than once per file. A purely finite glob resolves nothing. Counting `readlink` against master: | pattern, tree | master | here | rows | |---|---|---|---| | `**/*.tsv`, 20 000 files in one directory | 26 | 34 | 20 000 | | `**/*.tsv`, 10 000 files in 100 dirs at depth 3 | 26 | 1 702 | 10 000 | | `**/file.txt`, 251 files in 500 dirs | 4 033 | 7 038 | 251 | A literal suffix costs more: the globstar frame resolves its directory, then applies the suffix in a fresh call that resolves the match's own parent, which for a multi-component suffix is a deeper directory. Both are bounded by directories walked, not by rows. Latency on the 10 000-file tree is 329 ms against 417 ms. Pruning cost on dense alias graphs, where every one of N sibling directories links to every other and none links to an ancestor: | aliases | frames remembered while descending only | frames remembered once walked | |---|---|---| | 6 | 0.46 s | 0.10 s | | 8 | 30.2 s | 0.10 s | | 10 | over 700 s | 0.11 s | </details>
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Allow ON CLUSTER `<db_name>` pass-through on Replicated / Shared databases for RENAME and EXCHANGE
signal.text: Closes: #106087 For non-`Replicated` databases, users can run DDL on a cluster via `ON CLUSTER`. `Replicated` and `Shared` databases already propagate DDL across the cluster themselves, so `ON CLUSTER` is redundant when the cluster name in `ON CLUSTER` matches the database's automatic cluster name (the database name itself). Today this only works for `CREATE TABLE`, `ALTER TABLE`, `DROP TABLE`, `UNDROP TABLE`, `TRUNCATE` and `DETACH / ATTACH TABLE` because `maybeRemoveOnCluster` in `executeDDLQueryOnCluster.cpp` requires the AST to derive from `ASTQueryWithTableAndOutput`. `RENAME` and `EXCHANGE TABLES` use `ASTRenameQuery` which derives from `ASTQueryWithOutput`, so the helper bailed out early and the query was sent to the DDL worker, where it then failed inside `DatabaseReplicated::tryEnqueueReplicatedDDL` with `"It's not initial query. ON CLUSTER is not allowed for Replicated database."`. This PR extends `maybeRemoveOnCluster` to handle `ASTRenameQuery`. For `RENAME` and `EXCHANGE TABLES`, every element's `from`/`to` database must be the same database, otherwise the helper conservatively bails out and the original `ON CLUSTER` path runs unchanged. `OPTIMIZE` is intentionally left out. Routing it through the `Replicated` database DDL queue throws `NOT_A_LEADER` on a non-leader initiator, because `DDLWorker` rethrows the initial-task exception instead of handing off to another replica. The existing `executeDDLQueryOnCluster` path already selects a leader correctly for `OPTIMIZE ... ON CLUSTER`, so it is kept unchanged. Behavior matrix on a `Replicated` database `db`: | Query | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | `CREATE TABLE db.t ON CLUSTER db ...` | works | works | | `ALTER TABLE db.t ON CLUSTER db ...` | works | works | | `DROP TABLE db.t ON CLUSTER db` | works | works | | `RENAME TABLE db.x TO db.y ON CLUSTER db` | rejected | works | | `EXCHANGE TABLES db.a AND db.b ON CLUSTER db` | rejected | works | | `RENAME TABLE db.a TO other.b ON CLUSTER db` (cross-database) | rejected | rejected | | `RENAME ... ON CLUSTER 'other_cluster'` | rejected | rejected | | `ignore_on_cluster_for_replicated_database=1` for the above | already worked for some | now works for `RENAME` too | For `Shared` databases (Cloud), the same code path is used via `IDatabase::shouldReplicateQuery`, so the fix extends transparently to them. Motivation: scripts written against non-`Replicated` databases (often with a literal cluster name baked in) can be ported to `Replicated` and to ClickHouse Cloud `Shared` databases without rewriting the `ON CLUSTER` clauses, as long as the cluster name matches the database name. See the SigNoz case referenced in #106087. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Allow `ON CLUSTER` clause for `RENAME TABLE` and `EXCHANGE TABLES` on a `Replicated` (or `Shared`) database when the cluster name matches the database's automatic cluster name (i.e. the database name itself). The clause is treated as a no-op and the database engine propagates the DDL as usual. This already worked for `CREATE`, `ALTER`, `DROP` and similar queries, and lets scripts written for non-`Replicated` databases be ported to `Replicated` and Cloud `Shared` databases without rewriting `ON CLUSTER` clauses. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features)

signal.title: Fix SummingMergeTree FINAL dropping rows when column pruning hides non-zero summing columns
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106125 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `SELECT FINAL` on a `SummingMergeTree` table silently dropping a physically-present row when column pruning narrowed the read set to a subset of the summing columns and the only visible summing column was zero for that row. The "drop the group's row when all summing columns are zero" rule is now evaluated over the full set of physical summing columns from the table metadata, matching real on-disk merge semantics. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) ### Description `SELECT FINAL` on a `SummingMergeTree` could silently drop a physically-present row when column pruning narrowed the read set to a strict subset of the summing columns and the only visible summing column was `0` for that row. A real on-disk merge keeps the row because another (pruned) summing column has a non-zero value. Root cause: `SummingSortedAlgorithm` applies a "drop the group's row if all summing columns are zero" rule over the summing columns present in its input header. That header is the table sample block, i.e. every physical column (ordinary plus materialized). `ReadFromMergeTree` already pins `sign_column` / `version_column` / `is_deleted_column` for `Collapsing` / `Replacing` / `VersionedCollapsing` so those algorithms see complete row state under `FINAL`; the `Summing` branch was missing the same treatment. The same gap existed in `getColumnsRequiredForMergingFinal`, used by the `removeUnusedColumns` query-plan optimization. Both read-set paths now share one helper that mirrors `SummingSortedAlgorithm::defineColumns`' membership exactly, so the on-the-fly `FINAL` path and a real merge keep/drop the same rows: - All physical columns via `getAllPhysical()`, so a materialized non-key numeric column is preserved. (An earlier revision used `getOrdinary()`, which omits materialized columns and could still drop a row whose only non-zero value lives in one.) - An explicit `columns_to_sum` entry that names a `Nested` table, e.g. `SummingMergeTree(SomeMap)` whose stored columns are `SomeMap.ID` / `SomeMap.Num`, is expanded to its physical subcolumns the way the engine matches `columns_to_sum`. A `*Map` Nested member is kept regardless of `columns_to_sum`, because the algorithm discovers and sums maps independently of the scalar `columns_to_sum` filter. - A non-summable scalar (e.g. a `String` column) is pruned: the algorithm copies it last-value and it never affects the zero-row decision, so it is not read from disk. - With `allow_tuple_element_aggregation`, the algorithm flattens `Tuple` columns (`Nested::flattenTupleRecursive`) and sums the leaves, so a `Tuple` column is kept when any flattened leaf is summable. The whole physical column is read, which gives the merge every leaf. The tuple recursion mirrors `defineColumns`' flattened-leaf gates: a `*Map`-suffixed array leaf is a summed-map candidate only when its synthesized parent is a real tuple ancestor and, with an explicit `columns_to_sum`, the leaf or an ancestor is named; otherwise it is copied last-value and not pinned, so an unlisted tuple `*Map` is not over-read. Reproducer from issue #106125: ```sql CREATE TABLE s (c0 UInt32, v_keep Int32, v_zero UInt32) ENGINE = SummingMergeTree ORDER BY c0; INSERT INTO s VALUES (0,1,0),(1,1,1),(2,1,2); INSERT INTO s VALUES (3,1,3),(4,1,4),(5,1,5); SELECT c0 FROM s FINAL WHERE v_zero >= 0 ORDER BY c0; -- before: 1,2,3,4,5 (c0=0 incorrectly dropped) -- after: 0,1,2,3,4,5 ``` Tuple-leaf reproducer (`allow_tuple_element_aggregation`): ```sql CREATE TABLE s (k UInt64, metrics Tuple(a Int64, b Int64)) ENGINE = SummingMergeTree ORDER BY k SETTINGS allow_tuple_element_aggregation = 1; INSERT INTO s VALUES (0,(0,1)),(1,(5,5)); INSERT INTO s VALUES (0,(0,0)),(2,(7,7)); SELECT k FROM s FINAL WHERE metrics.a >= 0 ORDER BY k; -- before: 1,2 (k=0 dropped though metrics.b=1) -- after: 0,1,2 ``` Validation: - New stateless test `04301_106125_summing_final_column_pruning_drops_row.sql` covers implicit, explicit, materialized, explicit-Nested-map, explicit-multi-column, non-summable-String, tuple-leaf, nested-tuple and explicit-excluded-tuple cases under `FINAL` with column pruning. It fails on the unfixed binary and passes with the fix. - Existing `SummingMergeTree`, `Coalescing`, `AggregatingMergeTree`, `allow_tuple_element_aggregation` and remove-unused-columns-under-`FINAL` stateless tests pass. - Semantic check: a row whose summing columns are all zero is still dropped by `FINAL`; the fix only restores rows whose full stored form has a non-zero summing column. Verified the on-the-fly `FINAL` result matches a real `OPTIMIZE TABLE ... FINAL` merge for the tuple case. Closes #106125
