signal.title: Fix EXECUTE AS for LDAP-backed users not yet logged in
signal.text: Fixes #99574. `EXECUTE AS <user>` failed with `UNKNOWN_USER` for users provided by an external LDAP user directory whenever the target had not yet authenticated against this server since the last restart. The LDAP storage materializes its in-memory entry on first successful login, so `AccessControl::getID` (which iterates `findImpl` over the nested storages) saw nothing. ### Approach Per @ pufit's review direction on this PR, the fix adds a `force_external_lookup` overload on `IAccessStorage::find` and `findImpl`. `MultipleAccessStorage` propagates the flag to nested storages; `LDAPAccessStorage::findImpl(..., force_external_lookup=true)` performs the upstream lookup against the LDAP server using a configured service-bind account, verifies the user via `user_dn_detection`, and materializes the in-memory entry with the resolved role mapping. `InterpreterExecuteAsQuery` resolves the target user through a two-pass lookup that preserves the existing `user_directories` precedence: first a normal `find<User>` (so a target already cached locally wins over an LDAP entry that has not yet been materialized), then the forced lookup if pass 1 missed. ### LDAP service-bind The forced lookup needs to confirm a user exists in the directory without their password. `LDAPClient` is extended with a service-bind mode (`BindMode::Service` on `openConnection`) that binds with two new configuration fields: ```xml <ldap_servers> <my_ldap_server> <host>...</host> <bind_dn>cn={user_name},ou=users,dc=example,dc=org</bind_dn> <!-- Required for force_external_lookup, optional otherwise --> <lookup_bind_dn>cn=admin,dc=example,dc=org</lookup_bind_dn> <lookup_password>...</lookup_password> <user_dn_detection> <base_dn>ou=users,dc=example,dc=org</base_dn> <search_filter>(&(objectClass=person)(cn={user_name}))</search_filter> </user_dn_detection> </my_ldap_server> </ldap_servers> ``` When `lookup_bind_dn` is empty the forced lookup is a no-op for that server, so existing deployments are unaffected. ### Why not `AlwaysAllowCredentials` The earlier commit on this branch routed the lookup through `IAccessStorage::authenticate` with `AlwaysAllowCredentials`. As @ pufit and the LLVM Coverage review flagged, `LDAPAccessStorage::areLDAPCredentialsValidNoLock` short-circuits to `true` for that credential type before any LDAP bind or search; the storage would have materialized a phantom user for any name reachable to a holder of `IMPERSONATE ON *`, and role mappings would have been empty. This redesign fixes both: nonexistent names are rejected at the `user_dn_detection` search, and resolved users get their proper role mapping. ### Reviewer-driven follow-ups * `parseLDAPServer` errors are remembered keyed by server name. `findLDAPUser` rethrows the saved error so a misconfigured server (e.g. `lookup_bind_dn` set without `user_dn_detection`) surfaces as a query-time `BAD_ARGUMENTS` instead of degrading to `UNKNOWN_USER`. Per @ tiandiwonder. * `LDAPAccessStorage::findImpl(..., force_external_lookup=true)` refreshes a cached entry whose `users_external_roles[name]` is shorter than `role_search_params`. This catches the cache-poisoning shape that distributed `EXECUTE AS` over an interserver `<secret>` cluster otherwise produces: the `AlwaysAllowCredentials` short-circuit on the receiving shard materializes the user with empty role mapping, and a subsequent local `EXECUTE AS` on that shard otherwise inherits only the common roles. Per @ tiandiwonder. * `findLDAPUser` re-validates the server and `params_hash` after the LDAP round-trip, mirroring the existing post-check in `checkLDAPCredentials`, so a concurrent `SYSTEM RELOAD CONFIG` cannot publish a result against stale lookup semantics. * `parseLDAPServer` rejects an empty `lookup_password` when `lookup_bind_dn` is set, blocking the LDAP unauthenticated simple bind path. ### Tests `tests/integration/test_ldap_execute_as/` covers eleven cases: * `test_execute_as_ldap_user_without_prior_login` -- the issue reproducer; fails on master, passes here. * `test_execute_as_ldap_user_after_login_still_works` -- regression coverage for the previously-working path. * `test_execute_as_requires_impersonate_grant` -- the `IMPERSONATE` access check still fires before any LDAP work. * `test_execute_as_unknown_ldap_user_throws` -- proves a nonexistent LDAP name returns `UNKNOWN_USER` instead of being silently materialized. * `test_execute_as_ldap_user_with_role_mapping_without_prior_login` -- the forced-lookup path applies role mapping. * `test_execute_as_local_user_takes_precedence_over_ldap` -- two-pass lookup keeps a local user from being shadowed by the forced LDAP lookup on a global normal-lookup miss. * `test_execute_as_already_materialized_ldap_user_when_ldap_first` -- when the LDAP storage is ordered first AND already has the same name cached, pass 1 returns the LDAP entry. Pins the resolution order; matches pre-PR `getID<User>` behavior. * `test_execute_as_misconfigured_lookup_throws_config_error` -- a misconfigured LDAP server surfaces a query-time error instead of `UNKNOWN_USER`. * `test_execute_as_role_mapping_user_dn_filter` -- AD-style `{user_dn}` substitution through the forced lookup. * `test_execute_as_refreshes_distributed_cache_poisoned_entry` -- two-shard cluster with `<secret>`. After a remote query under `EXECUTE AS` poisons shard2's cache via `AlwaysAllowCredentials`, a local `EXECUTE AS` on shard2 still receives the mapped role. * `test_execute_as_wrong_lookup_password_throws_ldap_error` -- invalid service-bind credentials surface as an LDAP error, not `UNKNOWN_USER`. Local run: 11/11 passed. The cache-poisoning test was verified to fail on a binary built without the refresh logic in `InterpreterExecuteAsQuery::resolveImpersonationTargetUser` (confirms both directions). ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `EXECUTE AS <user>` failing with `UNKNOWN_USER` for users from an LDAP user directory that had not yet authenticated against the server since the last restart. The LDAP server definition now accepts optional `lookup_bind_dn` and `lookup_password` for the service account used by `EXECUTE AS` to resolve the target user without the user's own password; `user_dn_detection` is required when the new fields are set. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features)
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Use text index for LIKE/ILIKE with ESCAPE
signal.text: Follow-up to #99774 (qoega's LIKE ESCAPE clause). Before this change, a query like `... WHERE col LIKE pattern ESCAPE 'c'` silently bypassed the primary key (`KeyCondition`), the text index (`TYPE text`), and the bloom-filter text indexes (`ngrambf_v1`, `tokenbf_v1`, `sparse_grams`), falling back to a full scan even on tables with such an index defined or with `col` in the sorting key. Root cause: `LIKE pattern ESCAPE 'c'` is parsed into a 3-argument function call `like(col, pattern, escape_char)`. `MergeTreeIndexConditionText::traverseAtomNode`, `MergeTreeConditionBloomFilterText::extractAtomFromTree`, and `KeyCondition::extractAtomFromTree` only accepted 2-argument forms; any 3-arg `like`/`ilike` was rejected without ever reaching the LIKE handler. The execution layer in `FunctionsStringSearch::executeImpl` already calls `likePatternWithCustomEscapeToLikePattern` to fold the custom escape into standard backslash escapes before matching, so result correctness was never affected, only performance. Apply the same fold at index-condition time: - Text index (`MergeTreeIndexConditionText`): handles 3-arg `like` and `ilike` (the same arities `isSupportedFunction` allows for the index). - Bloom-filter text indexes (`MergeTreeConditionBloomFilterText`, for `ngrambf_v1` / `tokenbf_v1` / `sparse_grams`): handles 3-arg `like` and `notLike` (the like-family forms this index supports; `ilike` is not supported by this index type). - Primary key (`KeyCondition`): handles 3-arg `like` and `notLike` (the like-family forms present in `atom_map`). Case-insensitive `ilike`/`notILike` are not in `atom_map` and continue to fall back to row-level evaluation, same as the existing 2-arg behavior. In all paths the pattern must be a constant String and the escape argument a constant String of length 1; otherwise we bail out. Invalid escape sequences cause analysis to skip the index/key so row-level evaluation throws the same error the user would have seen before. The `nextInStringLike` tokenizer used by both text-index variants drops the backslash for an unknown escape `\c` while row-level matching keeps it, so an unknown/trailing backslash is declined (the `likePatternHasUnknownBackslashEscape` guard) and falls back to row-level matching to avoid wrongly pruning a matching granule. In the bloom-filter path this guard is placed in the shared `traverseTreeEquals`, so it protects both the folded 3-argument form and the pre-existing 2-argument `like` / `notLike` / `mapContainsKeyLike` / `mapContainsValueLike` paths. Regression tests use `EXPLAIN indexes = 1` to assert that pruning now happens: - `04277_text_index_function_like_escape.sql` covers the `TYPE text` index for `LIKE`/`ILIKE`, both `splitByNonAlpha` and `array` tokenizers, and both the operator form and the functional form `like(a, p, 'c')`. - `04292_105885_primary_key_like_escape.sql` covers the primary key for `LIKE`/`NOT LIKE` (with a remaining wildcard so the perfect-prefix extraction succeeds) and the functional form. - `04351_bloom_filter_text_index_like_escape.sql` covers the `ngrambf_v1` / `tokenbf_v1` / `sparse_grams` text indexes for `LIKE`/`NOT LIKE` ESCAPE and the functional form, including a consumed escape character, `force_data_skipping_indices`, and the unknown/trailing-backslash decline for both the 2-argument and 3-argument forms. The tests FAIL on master without this change and PASS with it. Closes #105885 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `LIKE ... ESCAPE 'c'` and `ILIKE ... ESCAPE 'c'` predicates (added in #99774) now use `TYPE text` skip indexes to prune granules; `LIKE ... ESCAPE 'c'` and `NOT LIKE ... ESCAPE 'c'` additionally use the `ngrambf_v1`, `tokenbf_v1`, and `sparse_grams` skip indexes, and the primary key when the column is in the sorting key, instead of falling back to a full scan. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is unchanged (the existing text-index docs already describe LIKE-based pruning; this change only fills a coverage gap for the recently added ESCAPE clause).
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Fix FREEZE permanent failure on empty shadow/increment.txt
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/105719 ## Motivation A concurrent `ALTER TABLE ... FREEZE WITH NAME` and `ALTER TABLE ... UNFREEZE WITH NAME` race, or a writer killed between `truncate(0)` and the subsequent `writeIntText` inside `CounterInFile::add`, could leave the server-global `shadow/increment.txt` at size 0. Every subsequent FREEZE on the server then failed permanently with `ATTEMPT_TO_READ_AFTER_EOF` until an operator manually removed the file. Backup tools that issue FREEZE concurrently (clickhouse-backup, ad-hoc scripts, CI) were stuck in that broken state. Slach's deterministic reproducer (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/105719): ```bash docker exec ch bash -c ': > /var/lib/clickhouse/shadow/increment.txt' docker exec ch clickhouse-client -q "ALTER TABLE t FREEZE" # Code: 32. DB::Exception: File ... is empty. (ATTEMPT_TO_READ_AFTER_EOF) # Every subsequent FREEZE also fails. Server never recovers. ``` ## Fix 1. `CounterInFile::add` drops the TOCTOU-unsafe pre-lock `fs::exists` check, takes the exclusive `flock`, then uses `fstat` under the lock to determine state. A size-0 file is treated the same as a missing file: with `create_if_need` the counter is repaired in place; without it the call throws, a missing file is not created, and an existing empty file is left untouched. 2. `MergeTreeData::freezePartitionsByMatcher` walks `shadow/` on every configured disk for the maximum numeric subdirectory name and passes it as a lower bound for the recovered counter, so the next FREEZE without `WITH NAME` does not collide with an already-allocated `shadow/<N>/`. The scan is evaluated lazily, only on the recovery path and under the counter lock, so a healthy counter never pays for it. Healthy counter values found in a non-empty file are used as-is and are NOT clamped, so steady-state behavior is unchanged. The scan must observe every `shadow/<N>` that exists, because it is collision avoidance: a bound that is too low hands out an identifier a backup already holds. So a failure that could hide one fails the FREEZE rather than silently lowering the bound. There are two deliberate exceptions, both logged so an operator can raise the counter once: - a **broken** disk, which is a routine and possibly long-lived state that must not fail every FREEZE on the server; - a **read-only** disk whose inspection raises, i.e. one whose backing store is unreachable, such as a `web` disk whose endpoint is down. Without this, such a disk breaks every FREEZE that has to recover the counter, including the very first FREEZE on a server, where no counter file exists yet. Being read-only is deliberately NOT sufficient on its own. `DiskLocal` becomes read-only whenever write access is lost while staying fully readable and not broken, so such a disk can still hold `shadow/<N>` written while it was writable, and skipping it would hand out an identifier one of them already holds. Note that with an unreachable disk configured a recovery FREEZE now succeeds but pays that disk's connection-retry budget, rather than failing outright. ## What `FREEZE WITH NAME` does with the counter A named FREEZE takes its directory name from `WITH NAME`, never from the counter. Whether it has to touch the counter therefore depends on the name, and the two cases are split: **A numeric name is an identifier an unnamed FREEZE could allocate**, so it must be reserved or the two collide. It is taken with `create_if_need = true`, floored by the name, and recovered through the same all-disk scan. The counter ends up at or above the name: at it when the name is the highest id in play, higher when the scan found a larger existing backup. Either way the name is marked allocated, because an unnamed FREEZE hands out the stored value plus one. `shadow/0` is the one exception and needs no reservation, because a recovered counter is the bound plus one and zero is never allocated. If the scan refuses because an existing backup already holds the counter's maximum, the numeric named FREEZE fails, keeping the scan's message, which names the directory to remove. It is tempting to proceed unreserved instead, since there is no next id anyway, but that state is not durable: `SYSTEM UNFREEZE` removes a backup directory without taking the counter lock, and the named backup's own directory is created only after the lock is released. In that window an unnamed FREEZE allocates exactly the pending name and two tables silently share one backup directory. **Any other name cannot collide with an allocated id**, so it must not depend on the recovery scan: an unrelated disk whose `shadow` lookup throws would otherwise fail a query that never needs the counter to choose a name (reported by the review bot on this PR). It is taken with `create_if_need = false`, which keeps the one property it needs and drops the one it does not: - it still advances a **healthy** counter, because consuming the value is what keeps a later unnamed FREEZE from handing it out; - it never creates or repairs a **missing or empty** counter, and never runs the scan. Recovery stays pending for the next FREEZE without `WITH NAME`, the only operation that consumes the counter. Persisting a value no scan produced would instead let that FREEZE see a healthy counter, skip recovery, and reuse an existing `shadow/<N>/`; - it also proceeds when the counter is **exhausted**, i.e. parked at the value beyond which no next id exists. That state has no id for an unnamed FREEZE to allocate, so there is nothing to reserve against, and the overflow guard throws before writing, so the stored maximum is left intact (reported by the review bot on this PR: refusing here turned uniquely named backups into a permanent failure). Unlike the scan's refusal above, this state is durable, because only writing the counter file can leave it. A genuinely broken counter still fails the query: an unreadable one, a short read, content `readIntText` rejects outright, or any errno other than `ENOENT`. Content that `readIntText` accepts as a prefix (`abc`, `12x`, a value wider than `Int64`) is taken at face value here exactly as it is on master, so this PR neither improves nor regresses it; validating the committed counter format is a separate concern. The scan counts only entries an unnamed FREEZE could have produced: a directory (the iterator also yields plain files, and a numeric file is not a backup) whose name is the canonical decimal spelling within the counter's range: `09223372036854775807` is a different path from `9223372036854775807` and only `FREEZE WITH NAME` can create it, so folding it in would raise the bound over an identifier that is still free. The bound is the counter's maximum rather than one below it, because `shadow/<Int64 max>` is reachable (recovery from `max - 1` adds one) and must therefore be accounted for. That makes exhaustion reachable, where no next id exists at all, and recovery then fails with `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` naming the directory instead of overflowing the counter and reusing it. ## Regression tests `tests/queries/0_stateless/04277_105719_freeze_recover_from_empty_increment.sh` covers thirteen scenarios: an empty counter with no prior backup (A) and with a prior non-numeric backup (B); recovery above a planted numeric directory (C); no reuse of a numeric `FREEZE WITH NAME` directory (D); an oversized numeric name ignored (E); a non-canonical numeric name such as `09223372036854775807` ignored (J); a non-numeric named FREEZE leaving recovery pending (G); a named FREEZE reserving its numeric name against a healthy counter (H) and against an empty one (N); the reservation happening before the directory is created (P); a non-numeric name leaving an empty counter alone (O); a numeric plain file ignored by the scan (M); and a numeric backup living on a non-default disk (F). Each assertion was mutation-tested: reverting the corresponding part of the fix makes exactly the matching scenario fail. `tests/integration/test_freeze_recover_broken_disk/test.py` covers what a stateless test cannot safely do: - a broken disk being skipped rather than failing every FREEZE; - a numeric backup on a nested `DiskEncrypted` still counting toward the bound; - the `Int64` boundary, where a backup named `max - 1` must still allow `max` to be allocated while a backup occupying `max` itself is refused with `LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, the directory and the empty counter both surviving, a non-numeric named FREEZE still succeeding, and a numeric one refused without creating its directory or writing the counter; - the counter states the named path must tolerate (exhausted, missing, empty) or propagate (unparsable, unopenable), that a numeric name is a floor rather than the final value, and that a healthy counter is advanced by a non-numeric name too; - on its own instance, that an unreachable read-only disk does not fail recovery while a local disk that turned read-only but is still readable does raise the bound. Those cases need either a directory name that cannot be varied, an unrecoverable state written into `shadow/increment.txt` itself, or a disk configuration of their own. The stateless server's counter is shared with every other test and is deliberately never restored on cleanup, so a run killed inside such a case would leave every later FREEZE on that server failing. Each integration instance owns its own `shadow/`. The read-only cases live on a separate instance because an unreachable disk also breaks the unrelated all-disk orphaned-parts scan that a non-default storage policy performs at table load, which the other cases here rely on. `src/Common/tests/gtest_counter_in_file.cpp` pins the `CounterInFile::add` contract directly: missing and empty files with and without `create_if_need`, the lower bound and the lazy provider each applying on recovery from a missing file as well as from an empty one and never on a healthy counter, and a throwing provider aborting without writing. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `ALTER TABLE ... FREEZE` failing permanently with `ATTEMPT_TO_READ_AFTER_EOF` after `shadow/increment.txt` was left empty by a concurrent FREEZE/UNFREEZE race or an interrupted writer. The counter is now repaired in place from the maximum existing `shadow/<N>/` directory rather than requiring manual operator intervention. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is unchanged.

signal.title: Reject divergent same-named parts in parallel replicas coordinator
signal.text: The parallel replicas coordinator deduplicated parts purely by `MergeTreePartInfo` (name + version), so when two replicas announced a same-named part holding genuinely different data the second announcement was silently merged into the first. The coordinator then dispatched ranges from the first replica's snapshot to the second replica, whose local part was different, producing an exception `Trying to get non existing mark N, while size is M` inside `MergeTreeIndexGranularityConstant::getMarkRows` — or, when the layouts happened to line up, potentially incorrect results. This is reachable with `parallel_replicas_for_non_replicated_merge_tree = 1` against a cluster whose members each have independent local `MergeTree` data: block numbers of a non-replicated `MergeTree` come from a node-local `SimpleIncrement`, so each member's local first part is named `all_1_1_0` but can store different data. The fix makes the coordinator validate the identity of same-named parts across announcements: - `RangesInDataPartDescription` now carries the underlying part's total mark count, a content fingerprint (`checksums.getTotalChecksumUInt128`), and a `part_name_identity` tri-state saying whether a part name identifies the same content on every cluster member. The fields are gated on a new parallel replicas protocol version (`DBMS_PARALLEL_REPLICAS_PROTOCOL_VERSION` bumped to 10). - `part_name_identity` is `ClusterWide` when the engine coordinates block numbers through Keeper (`ReplicatedMergeTree` and descendants) *or* when all of the table's disks keep their metadata in storage shared by every cluster member (`MetadataStorageType::Plain`, `PlainRewritable`, `StaticWeb`, `WebIndex`, `Keeper`) — there every member enumerates literally the same parts. It is `NodeLocal` for a plain `MergeTree` on ordinary local or per-node remote disks. - `InOrderCoordinator` and `DefaultCoordinator` snapshot these fields from the first announcement of each part and compare later announcements against the snapshot. A fingerprint mismatch raises `BAD_ARGUMENTS` naming the diverging part and pointing the user at `ReplicatedMergeTree` or at disabling `parallel_replicas_for_non_replicated_merge_tree`. - When the fingerprint is unavailable on either side (a replica running an older server version, or a part whose checksums are not loaded) and either side reports `NodeLocal` part names, the coordinator fails closed with `BAD_ARGUMENTS` instead of weakening the identity check — such same-named parts cannot be verified, and merging them blindly could return incorrect results. For `ClusterWide` part names the part name implies identical content, so a mark-count fallback keeps mixed-version clusters working during rolling upgrades. Only analyzed-view fields (`rows`, `ranges`) are deliberately NOT compared: per-replica PK and skip-index analysis can legitimately select different mark subsets from the same underlying part, and `ranges` is consumed in place as the coordinator dispatches work. The protocol bump also required pinning one existing consumer of the serializer. The `read_bucket` task parameter of a distributed read plan (`make_distributed_plan`) embeds a `RangesInDataPartsDescription` blob but travels as an opaque query parameter with no handshake to negotiate a version on, so producer and consumer both used the build's own `DBMS_PARALLEL_REPLICAS_PROTOCOL_VERSION` and would disagree about the field layout across a rolling upgrade. The blob is now pinned to `DBMS_PARALLEL_REPLICAS_DISTRIBUTED_READ_BUCKET_VERSION = 8`, the layout in effect when it was introduced. Surfaced by the AST fuzzer (STID `4920-51f2`) on PR #105706. The 5-replica `parallel_replicas` cluster used by `tests/queries/0_stateless/02275_full_sort_join_long.sql.j2` exposes the divergence whenever local `t2` parts differ in size across replicas. CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=105706&sha=84790f83ec78aee26b08ab6e0bc6712f6e4f1745&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%29 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/105706 Coverage is via `gtest_parallel_replicas_coordinator`, which exercises both coordination modes and both announcement orderings: rejection on divergent mark counts and divergent fingerprints, acceptance of identical announcements and of divergent analyzed views over the same part, the fail-closed path for `NodeLocal` part names without a fingerprint, the mark-count fallback for `ClusterWide` part names in mixed-version clusters, and a serializer round trip across protocol versions 8, 9 and 10 that requires the reader to consume the whole buffer. ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed an exception `Trying to get non existing mark N, while size is M` and potential incorrect parallel-replica range assignment when `parallel_replicas_for_non_replicated_merge_tree = 1` is used on divergent local `MergeTree` data: the parallel replicas coordinator now validates same-named parts by a content fingerprint of the underlying part instead of merging announcements blindly, and fails closed when the fingerprint is unavailable and part names are not guaranteed to identify the same content on every cluster member. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is unchanged

signal.title: Reject compression_method argument for data lake engines
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/105644 Data lake engines (`Iceberg`, `DeltaLake`, `Hudi`, `Paimon`) accept a `compression_method` argument, but the on-disk file format (`Parquet`/`ORC`/`Avro`) already has its own internal codec. For `IcebergLocal`/`IcebergS3`/etc. the write path goes through `MultipleFileWriter::startNewFile`, which never wraps the buffer with `wrapWriteBufferWithCompressionMethod`, so the user's `compression='lzma'` is silently dropped and the on-disk file is raw `Parquet`. The read path in `StorageObjectStorageSource` still calls `chooseCompressionMethod(filename, configuration->compression_method)`, which with hint `'lzma'` ignores the `.parquet` extension and returns `CompressionMethod::Xz`, then wraps the read buffer with `LZMAInflatingReadBuffer`. The decoder sees raw Parquet bytes and fails with `LZMA_FORMAT_ERROR`. For `DeltaLake`/`Hudi`/`Paimon` the write path uses `StorageObjectStorageSink`, which does honor the outer codec, so the file round-trips inside ClickHouse, but the produced LZMA-wrapped Parquet is unreadable by external engines (Spark, Trino, etc.). Same class of silent corruption from an interoperability point of view. This change rejects any explicit `compression_method` (or `compression`) argument at fresh-definition time for any data lake configuration (`Iceberg`, `DeltaLake`, `Hudi`, `Paimon`), with a clear error pointing at the format-specific codec setting. Users who need to control file compression should use the format-specific settings such as `output_format_parquet_compression_method`. The default value pass-through is unchanged: the rejection only fires when the user explicitly supplied the argument, so unmodified `CREATE TABLE` statements continue to work. The rejection is gated on `LoadingStrictnessLevel == CREATE`, so it fires only for a fresh definition: a `CREATE TABLE`, or a data lake table function (which always loads with `CREATE`). Every other mode replays a definition that was already accepted when the table was created, and is deliberately exempt as a compatibility path so pre-fix tables still load after an upgrade: every `ATTACH` form (short-syntax `ATTACH TABLE name`, full-definition `ATTACH TABLE name FROM '<path>' (cols) ENGINE = ...`, and the server-startup replay paths `FORCE_ATTACH` / `FORCE_RESTORE`), and `SECONDARY_CREATE`, which covers both `RESTORE TABLE` and the replay of the stored `CREATE TABLE` text by `DatabaseReplicated::recoverLostReplica` (so a `Replicated` database created before this validation landed still recovers on an upgraded replica). Note that this includes a user-supplied full-definition `ATTACH`, which can therefore still persist a definition carrying `compression_method`; per review, the gate is intentionally kept simple rather than special-casing the `ATTACH` shapes. A fresh `CREATE` in a `Replicated` database is still rejected, because the initiator runs it as an initial query and therefore with `mode == CREATE`. Reproducer (no longer accepted after this patch): ```sql CREATE TABLE t0 (c0 Int) ENGINE = IcebergLocal('/var/lib/clickhouse/user_files/lakehouses/t0', 'Parquet', 'lzma'); -- Code: 36. DB::Exception: The `compression_method` argument is not -- supported by data lake engines. ... ``` ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Reject any explicit `compression_method` / `compression` argument for data lake engines (`Iceberg`, `DeltaLake`, `Hudi`, `Paimon`) at fresh-definition time. The outer compression codec was silently dropped on the Iceberg write path while still applied on read, producing files the engine could not read back. For other data lake formats it produced non-standard files unreadable by external engines. Users who need to control file compression should use the format-specific settings such as `output_format_parquet_compression_method`. Pre-existing tables persisted before this validation landed still load via `ATTACH`, server startup, `RESTORE`, and `Replicated`-database replica recovery. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [ ] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features)

signal.title: Fix correlated subquery + GROUP BY ROLLUP under group_by_use_nulls
signal.text: A correlated subquery references an outer column that is a GROUP BY key of an outer query under `group_by_use_nulls = 1` with `WITH ROLLUP`/`CUBE`/`GROUPING SETS`. The actual values fed into the inner subquery are post-rollup `Nullable`s, but the analyzer used to leave the inner column reference at its non-Nullable type. The planner then built CAST wrappers and aggregate functions with the original signature, and at header inference (after decorrelation replaced `PLACEHOLDER` nodes with `INPUT` nodes of the actual `Nullable` types) the precomputed wrappers raised `Logical error: 'Bad cast from type DB::ColumnNullable to DB::ColumnVector<...>'`. The minimal reproducer from issue #91119 hits `createUInt8ToBoolWrapper`: ```sql SELECT (SELECT c0) FROM (SELECT 1::Bool) t0(c0) GROUP BY c0 WITH ROLLUP SETTINGS group_by_use_nulls = 1; ``` The same surface bug class also appears for plain numeric types (modulo, plus), aggregate functions over correlated outer columns (e.g. `(SELECT anyLastOrDefault(number))`), correlated `HAVING`/`WHERE` filter steps, and `Nullable` source columns. The root cause is in `QueryAnalyzer::resolveExpressionNode`: the `nullable_group_by_keys` walk stops at the first enclosing `QUERY` scope, so the outer scope where the column was defined is never consulted for an inner correlated reference. This change makes the walk continue past the inner `QUERY` scope when the `node` is a column whose source table expression is registered in a deeper outer scope (i.e. the column is correlated). The aggregate-function exclusion is now evaluated against each scope's `expressions_in_resolve_process_stack`, so an outer scope's `nullable_group_by_keys` applies even when the inner subquery is currently inside an inner aggregate (the inner aggregate operates on the outer's already-`Nullable` values). For correlated matches the existing node is mutated in place instead of being replaced with a clone of the GROUP BY key. The same `shared_ptr` is referenced by the enclosing `QueryNode::correlated_columns` list (registered via `addCorrelatedColumn`); cloning would leave the planner's `correlated_columns_set` pointing to the original non-`Nullable` node, and `PlannerActionsVisitor::visitColumn` (which uses type-sensitive equality) would then fail to identify the projected column as correlated and skip the `PLACEHOLDER` step that the decorrelation pass replaces. Closes #91119. Closes #106377. Closes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/108931 Closes https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109509 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `Bad cast` exception in correlated subqueries that reference an outer column promoted to `Nullable` by `group_by_use_nulls = 1` with `GROUP BY` `WITH ROLLUP`/`CUBE`/`GROUPING SETS`. ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features)

signal.title: Set index on an expression: LOGICAL_ERROR "Unexpected return type from equals" when the query's expression has a Nullable operand
signal.text: ### Describe what's wrong A `SELECT` whose `WHERE` matches a `set` skip index defined on an **expression** fails with `LOGICAL_ERROR` (code 49) when the query's copy of that expression has a `Nullable` operand: ``` Unexpected return type from equals. Expected Nullable(UInt8). Got UInt8. ``` The query is valid and should return rows. In builds with assertions enabled (CI stress, debug and sanitizer jobs) the same condition aborts the server instead of raising an exception. The `Nullable` operand only has to be *constant-foldable* — `nullIf(19, 0)`, `toNullable(19)`, a scalar subquery, or `materialize(toNullable(19))` all trigger it. ### Does it reproduce on the most recent release? Yes Verified on the official release binary `26.8.1.727` (and on a `master` debug build at `5f546ba6a75338a639903081748dfb7c0fdaf231`, where it aborts rather than raising an exception). ### How to reproduce ```sql CREATE TABLE t0 (t UInt32, INDEX t_set t % 19 TYPE set(4) GRANULARITY 1) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple() SETTINGS index_granularity = 2; INSERT INTO t0 SELECT number FROM numbers(100); SELECT count() FROM t0 WHERE t % nullIf(19, 0) = 16; ``` No non-default settings beyond the `index_granularity = 2` in the `CREATE TABLE`. Reproduces via `clickhouse local` and against a server. The control case behaves correctly — removing only the `Nullable` wrapper returns `5`: ```sql SELECT count() FROM t0 WHERE t % 19 = 16; -- 5, as expected ``` `index_granularity = 2` matters only because it keeps each granule within the index's `set(4)` capacity. At the default granularity the single granule overflows `set(4)` and stores nothing, so `MergeTreeIndexConditionSet::getPossibleGranules` early-returns the whole range and never evaluates the condition. All of these fail the same way: ```sql SELECT count() FROM t0 WHERE t % toNullable(19) = 16; SELECT count() FROM t0 WHERE t % (SELECT toNullable(19)) = 16; SELECT count() FROM t0 WHERE t % nullIf(19, 0) = 16; SELECT count() FROM t0 WHERE t % materialize(toNullable(19)) = 16; ``` ### Expected behavior The query returns `5`, as the equivalent query without the `Nullable` operand does. ### Error message and/or stacktrace On release `26.8.1.727`: ``` Code: 49. DB::Exception: Unexpected return type from equals. Expected Nullable(UInt8). Got UInt8. Action: FUNCTION equals(modulo(t, 19) :: 0, 16 :: 1) -> equals(modulo(t, 19), 16) Nullable(UInt8) : 3, input block structure:modulo(t, 19) UInt8 UInt8(size = 100), 16 UInt8 Const(size = 100, UInt8(size = 1)): while executing 'FUNCTION equals(modulo(t, 19) :: 0, 16 :: 1) -> equals(modulo(t, 19), 16) Nullable(UInt8) : 3': While executing MergeTreeSelect(pool: ReadPoolInOrder, algorithm: InOrder). (LOGICAL_ERROR) ``` On a debug build, the relevant frames: ``` src/Common/Exception.cpp:60:5: DB::abortOnFailedAssertion(...) src/Interpreters/ExpressionActions.cpp:696:27: DB::executeAction(...) src/Interpreters/ExpressionActions.cpp:837:13: DB::ExpressionActions::execute(...) src/Interpreters/ExpressionActions.cpp:1003:5: DB::ExpressionActions::execute(...) src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeIndexSet.cpp:485:14: DB::MergeTreeIndexConditionSet::getPossibleGranules(...) src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataSelectExecutor.cpp:2681:83: DB::MergeTreeDataSelectExecutor::filterMarksUsingIndex(...) src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataSelectExecutor.cpp:1161:70: DB::MergeTreeDataSelectExecutor::filterPartsByPrimaryKeyAndSkipIndexes(...) ``` ### Related issues and pull requests Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113233 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/89802 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/105552 ### Additional context **Root cause.** Note that the failing action reads `equals(modulo(t, 19), 16)` — the `Nullable` operand is absent from it. That is the bug: 1. `MergeTreeIndexConditionSet` rebuilds the predicate into a small `ActionsDAG` to run against the granule block (`MergeTreeIndexSet.cpp:567` `traverseDAG` → `MergeTreeIndexSet.cpp:625` `atomFromDAG`). 2. `nullIf(19, 0)` is constant-foldable, so `getColumnName` renders the subtree as `modulo(t, 19)`, colliding with the index expression's name. `atomFromDAG` matches that name against `key_columns` and replaces the **whole** `modulo(...)` subtree with a single input bound to the granule column (`MergeTreeIndexSet.cpp:659`), discarding the `Nullable` operand. 3. The enclosing `equals` is re-added with `result_dag.addFunction(node.function_base, children, {})` (`MergeTreeIndexSet.cpp:682`), reusing the query-side resolved `IFunctionBase`. `ActionsDAG::addFunctionImpl` (`ActionsDAG.cpp:500`) takes the declared `result_type` verbatim from `function_base->getResultType()` — `Nullable(UInt8)` — while preparing the executable against the *new* arguments. Declared type and executed function now come from different resolutions. 4. `ExpressionActions::execute` binds inputs by name only, with no type check (`ExpressionActions.cpp:815`), so the granule supplies its non-`Nullable` `UInt8` column. `equals` returns `UInt8`, which no longer matches the declared `Nullable(UInt8)`, and `executeAction` raises at `ExpressionActions.cpp:695`. In short: the name-based key-column substitution erases the operand that made the expression `Nullable`, while the reused `function_base` still declares the `Nullable` return type. A fix would re-resolve the function against the granule-side argument types when rebuilding the DAG, rather than copying `function_base` and its stale return type onto a block whose types were never checked against it. Requiring the name match to also agree on type would close the same hole. **Why this does not affect a `set` index on a plain column.** With `INDEX i0 c0 TYPE set(4)` and `WHERE c0 = toNullable(16)` there is no exception: the `Nullable` operand is the comparison constant, outside the index expression, so it survives as an argument and execution genuinely produces `Nullable(UInt8)`. The defect needs the nullability *inside* the indexed expression. **CI impact.** This is the source of the `Logical error: Unexpected return type from A. Expected B. Got C. Action: (STID: 1611-4523)` bucket tracked in #113233 — 14 occurrences in the last 90 days across unrelated pull requests and every build configuration (`amd_debug`, `amd_tsan`, `amd_msan`, `amd_asan_ubsan`, `arm_tsan`, `arm_msan`, `arm_release`, `arm_asan_ubsan`, serverfuzz), plus direct `master` runs. In CI it surfaces through `tests/queries/0_stateless/01786_explain_merge_tree.sh`, whose table carries `INDEX t_set t % 19 TYPE set(4) GRANULARITY 2`, once the AST fuzzer wraps the modulus in a `Nullable` expression. #89802 is the same assertion at the same site but a different trigger (a materialized view declaring a `Nullable` column over non-`Nullable` storage). Its reproducer runs clean on current `master`, and the pull request that closed it, #105552, only added a regression test — so this path was never covered. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Resolved by: #113244 - Merged into: `26.8.1.1673` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: Logical error: Unexpected return type from A. Expected B. Got C. Action: (STID: 1611-4523)

signal.title: Fix hang in `--queries-file` / `-q` when stdin is a pipe with no data
signal.text: `ClientBase` eagerly called `isStdinNotEmptyAndValid` to check for trailing stdin data on every `INSERT`. That helper calls `!std_in.eof()`, which performs a blocking `read(0, ...)`. When stdin is a pipe that is open but has no data and no `EOF` (common in CI, Docker, stress tests, and `--queries-file` invocations), the read blocks indefinitely and the client hangs until it is killed by timeout. Concretely, this caused an exception (signal 11 after timeout) in the stress test `03538_analyzer_scalar_correlated_subquery_fix`: the process hung on `read(0, ...)` and was killed. The fix replaces the eager blocking probe with a non-blocking one: `poll(timeout=0)` first asks "does stdin appear to have data right now?", and only when it does we fall through to `isStdinNotEmptyAndValid` to confirm and consume it. This: - avoids the hang on open empty pipes — `poll` returns 0 immediately; - preserves deterministic rejection of `inlined data + stdin` mixed input — when stdin actually contains data (the case asserted by `04064_inline_insert_data`), `poll` returns `POLLIN` and we still throw `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`; - is best-effort by design: a slow producer pipe (e.g. `(sleep 1; echo) | clickhouse-client ...`) may not have written by the time `poll` runs, in which case the trailing stdin payload is ignored. This is preferable to the alternative of a hard hang, and is documented in the helper. Covered cases (`is_async_insert_with_inlined_data`, `is_inline_insert_data`, and the appending-stdin path in `sendData`) all go through the same probe so the hang is closed for `--queries-file`, `-q`, and `--inline-insert-data` modes. CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=b9e68f4b9b0b33c7db43b00afb3eff4ff2050694&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_debug%29 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a hang in `clickhouse-client` for `INSERT` queries in `--queries-file`/`-q`/`--inline-insert-data` mode when stdin is an open pipe with no data and no `EOF` (common in CI, Docker, and stress tests). ### Documentation entry for user-facing changes - [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features) <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=96494&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/96494](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F96494+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Parallelize read-in-order from a single part with PrefetchingConcatProcessor
signal.text: When a single MergeTree part is split into multiple streams for read-in-order, use the new `PrefetchingConcatProcessor` instead of relying on the downstream `MergingSortedTransform`. The key difference: - `MergingSortedTransform` marks all inputs as needed but only consumes from one stream at a time (for non-overlapping ranges), and each port can only buffer 1 block — so after initial prefetch, reading becomes sequential. - `PrefetchingConcatProcessor` marks all inputs as needed AND pulls data from non-current inputs into internal buffers, keeping upstream sources busy. It outputs data in strict input order (concatenation), which is correct because ranges from a single part are non-overlapping and pre-sorted. This avoids both the merge comparison overhead and the sort overhead, while enabling true parallel IO and filtering across range groups. Benchmark on 100M rows (4 threads, single part, poor PK selectivity): - Single-thread read-in-order: 1.57s - Parallel + sort (no read-in-order): 1.27s - PrefetchingConcat: 0.61s (2.6x faster) ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Improve the performance of queries that are reading in the order of the primary key. <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Changes read-in-order execution and introduces a new buffering processor in the query pipeline; incorrect gating or backpressure/buffering behavior could impact result ordering or memory usage in some MergeTree reads. > > **Overview** > **Adds `PrefetchingConcatProcessor`**: a new concat-like processor that keeps *all* inputs marked needed and buffers per-input chunks (bounded by `max_buffered_chunks`) to prefetch non-current streams while still outputting streams strictly in order. > > **Wires it into MergeTree read-in-order**: `ReadFromMergeTree` now conditionally replaces `MergingSortedTransform` with `PrefetchingConcatProcessor` when reading in ascending order from a *single part* split into multiple streams and only when there is filtering work (`PREWHERE` or row-level filter); it also adds `prefer_multiple_streams`/`setPreferMultipleStreams()` so aggregation-/distinct-in-order paths can opt out to avoid collapsing parallel streams. > > **Tests/bench coverage updated**: adds a new stateless test asserting `PrefetchingConcat` appears only for single-part reads and preserves sort order, adjusts an existing buffering test to force multi-part behavior, and adds a performance scenario guarding against regressions for filter-less `ORDER BY` reads. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit c0ba40d2f630976681024d2ac941261c4abdbe57. signal.title: Performance test for ARRAY JOIN lazy replication over serialized plans
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112330 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112330 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description The performance test @ alexey-milovidov asked for on #112330, which made `ArrayJoinStep` carry `enable_lazy_columns_replication` in its serialized flags. Before it, a shard running a serialized plan fragment fell back to the plan default `false` and replicated ARRAY JOIN payloads eagerly. That path had no performance coverage. One query: `remote('127.0.0.{2,3}', view(...))` with ARRAY JOIN and `serialize_query_plan = 1`, so the shard really runs `ArrayJoinStep::deserialize` (`EXPLAIN distributed=1` shows `ArrayJoin` under `ReadFromRemote`). Two constraints decide whether this measures anything. The payload must be a wide `String`, because `isLazyReplicationUseful` declines fixed-width columns of 8 bytes or less (also why `tests/performance/array_join.xml` could not be extended). And no function may touch it, since that converts the replicated column to a full one in both arms, hence the bare `SELECT wide`. Four settings gate the measured path, so all four are pinned: flipping any one collapses the pre-fix/post-fix ratio from 68x to about 1x while the test still passes. Also adds `process_query_plan_packet` to the perf harness config: it defaults to `false` here, so without it the query fails with `SUPPORT_IS_DISABLED` rather than running slower. It predates every active release base, so the reference binary accepts it. Measured with `perf.py` between release builds `f61ce92` (pre-fix) and `fbf131e`: median 0.762 s versus 0.016 s, about 49x, p = 4.1e-12; peak memory on the initiator 1677 MiB versus 12.5 MiB. Scope: on a pull request both sides carry the fix, so this reports parity and acts as a regression guard. The 49x is my own before/after measurement between those builds, not something this PR's run will show. The `release_base` job reverts `tests/performance` to the release base, so it skips this test rather than comparing across the fix. Worst gated per-run figure 0.47 s against a 2 s limit. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115364&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115364](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115364+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Test that a normal projection is used through the Merge engine
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/63445 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/63445 Issue #63445 asked whether a `Merge` table can use a projection defined on its subtables. It works on master, so this pins it with a test. Requested by @ rienath (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/63445#issuecomment-5329931686). Nothing in-tree covered this: no test under `tests/queries/0_stateless` both creates a `Merge` table and mentions projections. The test reads two `MergeTree` tables through a `Merge` table and asserts that `system.query_log.projections` names the projection of *both* subtables, plus the query result. Asserting the result alone would not catch a silent loss of projection usage, which is what the issue is about. I verified the assertion can redden: with the projections dropped, or with `optimize_use_projections = 0`, the column becomes `[]` while the result is unchanged. `index_granularity = 8` is pinned because at a large granularity the whole fixture is one granule and no projection is selected. Two notes on what this does not cover. The projection name is not printed by `EXPLAIN` through a `Merge` table, so the obvious `EXPLAIN` assertion would fail on working behaviour; hence `query_log`. `force_optimize_projection_name` is also unusable here: it throws `INCORRECT_DATA` through `ENGINE = Merge` even when the projection is used, because the child plan is optimized a second time when the pipeline is built. Aggregate projections are still not used through `Merge` (#34968, open), so this test deliberately pins only the normal-projection case. The `duplicate #34968` comment on #63445 is not accurate: the two cases behave differently on master. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115353&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115353](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115353+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Use the text index when a tokenizer argument matches the index tokenizer
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115275 (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): A `text` index is now used for `hasAnyTokens`, `hasAllTokens` and `hasPhrase` called with an explicit tokenizer argument, when that argument denotes the same tokenizer as the index and the index has no `preprocessor` or `postprocessor`. Previously the three-argument form always fell back to a full scan. Closes #115275. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115275 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/108808 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/107186 `MergeTreeIndexConditionText::traverseAtomNode` rejected any function node that was not binary before it looked at the function name, so a three-argument `hasAnyTokens` / `hasAllTokens` / `hasPhrase` never reached `isSupportedFunction` (which already lists all three). The predicate became an unknown atom: no granule pruning and no direct read. This mattered because the three-argument form is the documented workaround for #108808, so users of a non-`splitByNonAlpha` tokenizer had no option that was both correct and indexed. The gate now admits three arguments for those three functions when the argument's tokenizer canonicalizes to the index tokenizer. Equality compares `ITokenizer::getDescription()`, which is the form the direct-read pass already synthesizes for the two-argument case, so registered aliases and spelling variants compare equal while parameters still discriminate (`ngrams(3)` is not `ngrams(4)`). Everything else keeps full-scanning, by design and per @ rschu1ze's ruling on the issue: a different tokenizer, a non-constant or invalid argument, and an index carrying a `preprocessor` or `postprocessor` option (there the index stores tokens of a transformed value that the argument's bare tokenizer never produces, so the two cannot answer the same predicate). No error is raised on a mismatch. `hasPhrase` is included at @CurtizJ's request (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115275#issuecomment-5328448695). The direct-read pass is kept argument-count-preserving: it now assigns the tokenizer argument in place when one is already present rather than appending, because that pass can legitimately run over the same node twice and would otherwise build a four-argument call. `02346_text_index_function_hasPhrase{,_positions}` asserted the old full-scan behavior for this exact case. Those sections are retitled and regenerated, and a mismatching-tokenizer sibling case is added at the same site so the full-scan boundary keeps a pinned oracle. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115348&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115348](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115348+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a `LOGICAL_ERROR` (`Bad cast from type DB::ColumnVariant to DB::ColumnNullable`) when inserting into a MergeTree table whose sorting or primary key applies a function to a `Variant` column, such as `ORDER BY max2(v, v)`. Where the function's common result type can be inside `Nullable`, its declared type no longer depends on `variant_throw_on_type_mismatch` and so can no longer disagree with the column produced. ### Description Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112469 Found by the `BuzzHouse (amd_tsan)` fuzzer: [CI report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=102039&sha=0cb4588fe9c8c2e1a8bb292786f16269e537f09f&name_0=PR&name_1=BuzzHouse%20%28amd_tsan%29), STID 3520-704a. The `LOGICAL_ERROR` is thrown at `SerializationNullable.cpp:216` from `calculateAndSerializePrimaryIndexRow` (`:235`), aborting debug and sanitizer builds. PR 102039 is only the carrier. `FunctionBaseVariantAdaptor` composed its declared return type by a different rule than its own execution uses. Execution drops an alternative that is NULL for every row (`:530`); type construction counted it, so one such alternative widened the type to `Variant(...)`. Such an alternative arises through recursion: when another argument is still a `Variant`, the per-alternative build returns a nested adaptor, and one matching none of its own alternatives differs per strictness mode. Under the default it throws and the alternative is skipped, so `max2` over a `Variant` declares `Nullable(Float64)`, which the Variant-in-key check accepts and records as the key type; leniently it returns `Nullable(Nothing)` and the type widens. The part writer picks `SerializationNullable` from the recorded type and serializes the runtime column unconverted, so a strict `CREATE` plus a lenient `INSERT` handed it a `ColumnVariant` and the cast threw. The composition now skips such an alternative, so the declared type describes the column the adaptor builds; storage is fixed as a consequence. The discriminator is where the alternative came from, not what its type looks like: a `Nothing` or `Nullable(Nothing)` a function genuinely returns is kept, since `arrayElementOrNull` over an `Array(Nothing)` alternative produces one in both modes, and dropping it would move the declared type of a key or skip index accepted today. Collapsing is also skipped when the common type cannot be inside `Nullable`, which would turn those NULL rows into defaults. An alternative whose build *throws* still leaves the strict type bare for `Array` and `Map`: pre-existing, unchanged.
Declared type of max2 over a Variant, before and after | expression | before, strict | before, lenient | after, both | |---|---|---|---| | `Variant(UInt8)` | `Nullable(Float64)` | `Nullable(Float64)` | `Nullable(Float64)` | | `Variant(UInt8, Int128)` | `Nullable(Float64)` | `Variant(Float64)` | `Nullable(Float64)` | | `Variant(UInt8, String)` | `Nullable(Float64)` | `Variant(Float64)` | `Nullable(Float64)` | Values are unchanged: rows of an incompatible alternative are NULL before and after. When the common type cannot be inside `Nullable`, the declared type and both row values are untouched: | expression | common type | before and after | |---|---|---| | `mapFromArrays` over two Variants | `Map(UInt8, String)` | `Variant(Map(UInt8, String))`, rows `{1:'x',2:'y'}` / `NULL` | | `arrayConcat` over a Variant | `Array(UInt8)` | `Variant(Array(UInt8))`, rows `[1,2,1,2]` / `NULL` | New test covers compact and wide writers, two pruning skip indices, `OPTIMIZE FINAL` and `DETACH`/`ATTACH`, and pins the paths that must not change, including `arrayElement` and `arrayElementOrNull` over a `Nothing` alternative in both modes. A set index written by the pre-fix binary over such an expression is read back with values and pruning intact. 50/50 randomized runs passed.

signal.title: CI: do not store a failed gh api response as the docs merge base
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104437 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): A failed `gh api .../compare` response is no longer stored as the merge base commit id, so `Docs check (Mintlify)` no longer fails with `fatal: invalid refspec` on a transient API error. ### Description `Docs check (Mintlify)` reds with `fatal: invalid refspec '{"message":"Not Found",...}'` instead of comparing revisions: 16 failures across 9 PRs in the 30 days to 2026-08-18, the most recent that day, in two API classes (15 x 404, one 500 outside any incident). Root cause: `Shell.get_output` defaults to `strict=False` and returns stdout on the failure path too (`ci/praktika/utils.py:196-202`), and `gh api` prints its error body there. A non-2xx `compare` response was therefore stored under `merge_base_commit_sha`, and `docs_job_mintlify.py:144` interpolates it into a `git fetch` refspec whose guard rejects only an empty value. It is `shlex.quote`d, so there is no injection: git gets JSON where a ref belongs, and fails closed. It is sticky too: the key is written once by the `Config Workflow` pre-hook and inherited by every job, so a re-run re-reads it. Over the 12 affected (pr, sha) pairs the check has 123 failed rows and no successful one, one head failing all 3 attempts over 7h46m, cleared only by a new head. And since the job reaches its `Run` step, `retry_infra_failures.yml` sees a non-infra verdict and skips the run's rerun. The fix is at the one call site that stores the key: retry the read and raise rather than return its body, then require a full commit id before storing. On failure the key is simply absent, which the reader's existing guard already reports honestly, so the reader is unchanged. Both halves earn their place: every recorded occurrence exits non-zero, so retry-and-raise alone stops the body being stored, and validation covers `gh api -q` exiting 0 with a non-id. Deliberately not changed: the same shape at `store_data.py` (`master_commits`), `llvm_coverage_job.py:133` and `job_hooks/promql_compliance_s3.py:93`, none with a recorded occurrence and none reaching a refspec (the value only selects an S3 URL or `gh api` path). Carrier: [run 32036646118](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/actions/runs/32036646118/job/95482258798), on #104437. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115338&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115338](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115338+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/77366 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112805 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Three stateless tests briefly leave table metadata on disk referencing a named collection that no longer exists. The stress test kills and restarts the server at arbitrary points and randomizes `async_load_databases=false`; in that mode `loadMetadata` waits every table load job and rethrows, so the server cannot boot: ``` Caught exception while loading metadata: Code: 722 ... Code: 695 ... Code: 669 ... There is no named collection `nc_missing_sk_test_3`: Cannot attach table ... ENGINE = Remote(...) ``` Measured: 16 occurrences across 13 PRs and 2 master runs in 30 days. Changes, copying the pattern already in `04626_s3_base_setting.sh`: - `04512_remote_missing_named_collection.sh` detaches `PERMANENTLY`. Startup skips a permanently detached table without constructing its storage, while `ATTACH TABLE` still replays the on-disk definition, so every assertion is unchanged and the `.reference` file is untouched. - `04320_url_engine_dispatch_partition_and_format.sh` and `04327_s3queue_server_credentials.sh` create the collection before dropping a possible leftover table, and chain the two teardown drops so the collection outlives the table. Validation. A restart injected where the stress kill lands reproduces the abort deterministically on master and boots cleanly with the change; restarting at every statement boundary of the changed regions shows two boundaries dying before and none after. Each change was reverted one at a time and each reverted half reddens on its own oracle, and pointing an arm at a live collection makes it fail, so the arms are not vacuous. 200/200 randomized runs of these tests plus `04626` pass. Server startup behaviour is unchanged, so the underlying gap remains: dropping a collection while a dependent table is detached still leaves an unstartable server when `async_load_databases = 0`. That was reported in #77366 and closed in favour of a drop-side guard (#96181), which #112805 is extending to detached tables. Tests only: no setting, default or serialization change, so no `SettingsChangesHistory.cpp` entry. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115326&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115326](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115326+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix wrong results from compiled `if`/`multiIf`/`CASE` mixing `Date`/`Date32` with `DateTime`/`DateTime64`
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115272 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115146 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed wrong results from `if`, `multiIf` and `CASE` when one branch is a `Date` or `Date32` and the result type is `DateTime` or `DateTime64`. With `compile_expressions = 1` (the default) the compiled expression copied the date's day count into the timestamp column without converting days to seconds, so `if(cond, toDate32('1900-01-01'), toDateTime64('1970-01-01', 3))` returned `1969-12-31 23:59:34.433`. Closes #115272. ### Description Reported by @ PedroTadim in [#115272](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115272), who asked me to fix it and have @Manerone review. **Root cause.** `FunctionIfBase::isCompilableImpl` already intends to refuse these expressions -- its comment reads *"It's difficult to compare Date and DateTime - cannot use JIT compilation."* -- but it tested `WhichDataType::isDate()` and `isDateTime()`, which are exact `TypeIndex` equality, so it refused only `Date`+`DateTime` and admitted `Date32`+`DateTime64`, `Date`+`DateTime64` and `Date32`+`DateTime`. Those reach `nativeCast`, which correctly finds no scale for day-count types and falls through to a plain `CreateIntCast`: `-25567` days becomes `-25567` milliseconds. The predicates were never widened when `Date32` and `DateTime64` were added. **The change** widens both predicates to `isDateOrDate32()` and `isDateTimeOrDateTime64()`, so the guard covers the whole family and the interpreted path runs. `if.cpp` and `multiIf.cpp` inherit this base, so one change covers all three. These expressions lose JIT, as the comment intended and as `Date`+`DateTime` always did. The commit message covers the rejected IR alternative. **Validation.** New test `04930_jit_compiled_if_date_to_datetime` asserts the compiled result equals the `compile_expressions = 0` result over the reported matrix: scales 0/3/6/9, both date and both datetime types, both branch orders, constant and column dates, `if`/`multiIf`/`CASE`, `Nullable(Date32)`, pre/post-1970. 12 of its 14 comparison rows fail without the fix and all pass with it (50/50 runs). The 2 exceptions are controls green both ways: `Date`+`DateTime`, already refused, and same-unit `Date32`+`Date`, which must keep compiling. Those rows are 1-vs-0 parity checks, so they would pass even if compilation stopped. Two further rows pin which shapes compile, via `ProfileEvents['CompiledFunctionExecute']`: it counts executions of an already-compiled node, so it needs no cache drop and the test stays parallel-safe. The mixed-unit row fails on an unpatched binary, so it tracks this change rather than asserting a constant. They are also why the test carries `no-fasttest, no-msan`: those builds have no embedded compiler. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115325&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115325](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115325+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Do not admit non-clonable read steps into the MergeTree direct join
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/103473 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `Cannot clone ReadFromPreparedSource plan step` (`NOT_IMPLEMENTED`) when joining against a `Buffer` table with `join_algorithm = 'direct'`. Such a right side is now declined with the same message as any other unsupported storage. ### Description `tryMakeDirectJoinWithMergeTree` admitted `ReadFromPreparedSource` as a right-side read step, then cloned the right plan unconditionally. That step has no `clone()` override, so the clone reached the throwing base `IQueryPlanStep::clone()`: ```sql CREATE TABLE t_left (id UInt64, name String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id; CREATE TABLE t_right_mt (id UInt64, val String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id; CREATE TABLE t_right_buf AS t_right_mt ENGINE = Buffer(currentDatabase(), t_right_mt, 1, 1000, 1000, 10000, 10000, 10000000, 10000000); INSERT INTO t_left VALUES (1, 'A'); SELECT * FROM t_left AS l LEFT JOIN t_right_buf AS r ON l.id = r.id SETTINGS enable_analyzer = 1, join_algorithm = 'direct'; -- Code: 48. DB::Exception: Cannot clone ReadFromPreparedSource plan step. (NOT_IMPLEMENTED) ``` That arm never had a working case: `typeid_cast` matches the exact type, and neither `ReadFromPreparedSource` nor its subclasses implement `clone()`, so every plan it admitted threw. This removes it. The other two arms are kept, and `ReadNothingStep` (which does implement `clone()`) carries the empty-MergeTree case from #95935. The query now takes the pre-existing refusal for unsupported right-side storages, `Can't execute any of specified algorithms ...`, which is what a `Memory` or `StripeLog` right side already returns. This is the "make the exception message better" change @ vdimir asked for when he closed #103473 as not planned: `direct` does not support `Buffer`, so the right behaviour is the ordinary unsupported-storage refusal rather than a clone failure. It deliberately does not make `Buffer` work with `direct`. Two notes beyond the report. The failure is not limited to an empty underlying table as the issue title suggests: it also reproduces with a non-empty `Buffer` and with `INNER JOIN`. And it does not touch the second entry point @ zlareb1 reported, where correlated-subquery decorrelation clones the same step: that path does not go through this allow-list. Hence `Related:` below rather than `Closes:`. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/103473 <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115309&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115309](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115309+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Generate the fuzzer dictionary from a release binary instead of committing it
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111025 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113649 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description **Do not merge this until NightlyFuzzers is green on this branch.** Dispatching it needs admin rights on the repository, so I am asking for a manual run first. Re-land of #111025, reverted in #113649 after the nightly `libFuzzer tests` job went red for a week. The mechanism is unchanged: the dictionary is derived from the release binary's own registries instead of a committed snapshot that drifts. Four defects are fixed. The first two are what made the job red; the other two are collateral damage from dropping the committed `all.dict` that no CI job would have caught. 1. The coverage check ran `comm` under the container's `en_US.UTF-8` against `LC_ALL=C`-sorted input, so it exited 1 and `set -e` killed the script before the verdict. 2. The release binary was staged executable next to the fuzzer targets, so `runner.py` enumerated it as a target and ran it with libFuzzer arguments. 3. The `all.dict` fallback was generated only by a `POST_BUILD` step of the `fuzzers` aggregate target, which the official OSS-Fuzz build never reaches, so its `cp tests/fuzz/*.dict` aborted under `bash -eu`. 4. NightlyFuzzers claimed a cache hit on MasterCI's ARM release build but took a different job variant with untagged artifacts, so it rebuilt nightly and could downgrade MasterCI's artifact retention. Validated against a real binary: `update_dict.sh` aborts under a UTF-8 locale before the fix and succeeds after. 35 new `ci/tests` functions cover the four fixes, each with a mutation arm that reddens without its fix. Residual: `runner.py` still infers "fuzzer target" from the execute bit, so it is unchanged. The earlier dispatch showed defects 1 and 2; I cannot rule out more without a run. cc @yakov-olkhovskiy @maxknv @leshikus <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115307&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115307](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115307+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->
