signal.title: Fix flaky test 03100_lwu_22_detach_attach_patches
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110178 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Not for changelog. ### Description `03100_lwu_22_detach_attach_patches` hits the 60 second per-test cap in `Fast test` (`Timeout! Killing process group`). Measured over 30 days: 7 failures across 7 distinct pull requests, 0 on master. Example report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115234&sha=3d3a0b0cfb7379259dd3158099a5035c6d7099fe&name_0=PR&name_1=Fast%20test Root cause. Every merge-selection round that selects nothing multiplies the table's merge-selecting interval by `merge_selecting_sleep_slowdown_factor`, up to `max_merge_selecting_sleep_ms` (default 60000). Externally woken rounds count too, and `mutate()` schedules one for every `UPDATE` and `APPLY PATCHES`, so the interval saturates at the 60 second ceiling within a second of `CREATE TABLE`. Any later statement that has to wait for the next selection round then pays that interval. This test issues `APPLY PATCHES` under `mutations_sync = 2`, so a single such wait consumes the whole 60 second budget. Measured locally on one server, reading the interval the engine itself logs (`Scheduling next merge selecting task after Nms`): unpinned, the interval reaches 60000 ms and the longest observed wait between selection rounds is 54832 ms; with the pin the interval never exceeds 200 ms and the longest wait is 121 ms. Over 20 unpinned randomized runs, 7 took more than 30 seconds (max 57.51 s, i.e. a near miss of the cap); with the pin, 100 runs all finished in under 3 seconds. The fix pins `merge_selecting_sleep_ms` and `max_merge_selecting_sleep_ms` on the test's two tables, which is what the merged #110178 did for `02676_optimize_old_parts_replicated` and what `03047_on_fly_mutations_basics_rmt` already does. Test only, no product code change. I did not change the engine here. That the interval grows on externally woken rounds is a scheduling policy question that affects merge latency and Keeper load for every replicated table, and justifying a change to it needs multi-replica measurements this PR does not have. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115279&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115279](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115279+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Report which destination made the macOS self-extracting copy fail
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `Fast test (arm_darwin)` fails a few times a day on unrelated PRs with `Permission denied` on `ci/tmp/clickhouse`: [job 95461613722](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/actions/runs/32041145440/job/95461613722) ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114125&sha=88ab20e7768865da5426a0aaa8a204f6ad43e6f5&name_0=PR&name_1=Fast%20test%20%28arm_darwin%29)), also jobs `95537845886`, `95306463154`, `95222719292`, across three unrelated PRs. The binary is the self-extracting bundle and it destroys itself. In `decompressor.cpp` `unlink(self)` succeeds, the Darwin-only `std::filesystem::copy_file(tmp -> self)` then fails `EEXIST`, and the error return happens before the `chmod` restoring the executable bit, so the process exits having removed its own binary. The progress dots appear exactly once in the log, immediately followed by that `copy_file`'s `File exists`. Why the destination exists after a successful `unlink` is not established, and I could not reproduce it: this is macOS-only and I have no macOS host. Two mechanisms remain possible (path resolution through `_NSGetExecutablePath`/`realpath`/APFS naming a different entry than `unlink` removed, or a symlink-following equivalence match); an unlabelled `File exists` cannot tell them apart. So instead of guessing at a fix, this reports the destination's identity and keeps the failure closed: `lstat` and symlink-following `stat` for destination and source, the equivalence flag from the followed pair (what libc++ compares before returning `EEXIST`), and the original wrapper's dev/inode. It is confined to that failure branch plus an `OS_DARWIN`-only helper; one real occurrence identifies the mechanism. Two candidate fixes were dropped on measurement: `copy_options::overwrite_existing` is a no-op against the equivalence case and truncates an unknown object otherwise; staging the temp file executable would publish a partial executable. Validated by an oracle harness compiling this code verbatim over three destination shapes that must differ (they collapse without the change), a `-DOS_DARWIN` type-check with an injected-error control, byte-identical Linux `.text`, and a standalone self-extracting round trip unchanged before and after. A green `Fast test (arm_darwin)` here is not evidence the diagnostic works, since it only fires on failure: this makes the next occurrence diagnosable, not rarer. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115236&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115236](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115236+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Make the 01396 cleanup wait its own verdict
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108213 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `01396_inactive_replica_cleanup_nodes_zookeeper` failed on `Stateless tests (arm_binary, parallel)` with ``` cleanup wait did not converge: last count='49', last poll error: ``` CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115051&sha=dca080fd03ab3fd8be3a75a881ec4f6cb4c764d4&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28arm_binary%2C%20parallel%29 Root cause: the wait and the check were two independent samples of a moving value. The poll loop broke on its own observation of `49`, below the threshold of 50, then a **separate** query re-read the same node, returned `>= 50`, and that second read was the verdict. No query failed (the poll error was empty): inserts and merges append to `/log` while the cleanup thread trims it, and a burst landed in the gap. Cleanup was working; the test mis-sampled it. The fix makes the observation that ends the wait the verdict and deletes the second read, removing the gap rather than narrowing it. The threshold, the 120 s budget, the reference and the tags are unchanged. An observation counts only if the read both completed successfully and returned a number. The numeric test is the existing guard (`[[ "" -lt N ]]` is true in bash); the exit-status test is new here: the client can flush a data block and then fail, so a delivered row alone is not a successful read. The verdict therefore accepts the count having been observed below the threshold at any point in the wait, rather than at the end. Since `/log` moves, that is the property the test can assert. If cleanup does not run, no iteration observes it and the test still fails. Validated on release binary 26.8.1.1585 (`no-debug` skips on a debug build). Recreating the window deterministically: the old logic fails 16/16 with the CI signature, the new one passes 16/16. signal.title: Fix the Upgrade check silently validating against a stale previous release
signal.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description The Upgrade check starts a previous release, then upgrades to the build under test. `tests/ci/get_previous_release_tag.py` picks that baseline, and can silently pick one far too old. On PR #114376 commit `e1cb0dee5e9` it picked `v25.1.4.53` for a `26.8.1.1` build; that old server aborted on shutdown, reported as `Received signal 6` unrelated to the PR. Two commits earlier it resolved `v26.7.3.19`. 4 of 47 recent runs were affected. Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114376&sha=e1cb0dee5e9bd972e9bbbdd8cd8d971ad1e39ee1&name_0=PR&name_1=Upgrade%20check%20%28amd_release%29 Root cause: when no candidate on a page could be used, an unbounded `while not found:` advanced to page 2, 3 and answered from there. `/releases` returns entries roughly newest-created first, not in version order, and each later page's newest release is older than the previous page's newest (measured across all 9 pages), so page 1 holds the newest release overall. The only diagnostic was `logger.debug` under `basicConfig(level=INFO)`. This resolves from the first page only. A candidate still needs an uploaded package, so a release whose packages are still publishing keeps falling back to the previous patch release, now logged at WARNING rather than DEBUG. Three cases now raise: a first page with no usable candidate, a page shorter than the 100 requested, and an answer that is its page's oldest entry, which cannot show that no newer release precedes it. `upgrade_runner.sh` turns those nonzero exits into a job failure. No C++ change is needed: the abort is a use-after-free in `25.1`, fixed in `2920d338ea4` (#81473, released in `v25.6.1.3206`), so master and every active release branch carry the fix. Tests were removed at review request. The Upgrade check's digest now lists both release helpers `upgrade_runner.sh` runs, the resolver and `download_release_packages.py`; without them a change to either leaves the job cache-skippable, the same failure mode fixed here. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112974 (hardens the API helper; edits the same digest list, so whichever merges second rebases). <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115228&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115228](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115228+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Remove a duplicate decimal rescaling helper that did not check for overflow
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114886 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a signed integer overflow when a `Decimal` argument passed to `prometheusQuery` or `prometheusQueryRange` had to be rescaled to the table's timestamp scale. Such an argument returned an unrelated timestamp, or made the query attempt a huge allocation, instead of reporting `DECIMAL_OVERFLOW`. ### Description Found by the AST fuzzer, check `AST fuzzer (arm_asan_ubsan)`, STID `3715-3c49` ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=109480&sha=480e82b8b2a16cdfa145b984a2270ef95cf3d518&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28arm_asan_ubsan%29)): ``` src/Core/DecimalFunctions.h:444:55: runtime error: signed integer overflow: 9007199254740990976 * 1000000 cannot be represented in type 'long' ``` Reached from ordinary table-function argument parsing. Root cause is duplication rather than a missing check. `DecimalUtils::convertTo(to_scale, decimal, scale)` was a second implementation of decimal-to-decimal rescaling and the weaker of the two: it multiplied by the scale multiplier with a plain `*`, and narrowed through `Decimal::convertTo` (a bare `static_cast`) before multiplying. `convertDecimals` already did this correctly, promoting to the wider native type first, guarding the multiply with `common::mulOverflow`, and range-checking when narrowing. `FunctionsConversion.h` and `KeyCondition.cpp` both document no-wrap as this helper's contract, so the unguarded overload was the outlier. It is removed here and its four call sites go through `convertDecimals`, making the `src/` diff a net reduction. Without the fix a release build silently returns a wrapped timestamp (`toDecimal64(10000000000, 3)` against a `DateTime64(9)` table gives `1702-05-02 18:12:06.290448384`); for `prometheusQueryRange` the wrapped bounds inflate the step count until the query attempts an 8 GiB allocation. Validation: the UBSan abort reproduces on master and is gone after the change; 12 in-range values covering all three scale directions, both source widths and the exact `Int64` boundary are byte-identical before and after; new test `04926`. Known residual, not addressed here: `common::mulOverflow` does not detect `Int128`/`Int256` overflow (`base/base/arithmeticOverflow.h` says so), so a `Decimal128` rescale can still wrap. That is pre-existing, unreachable from these call sites (all `Int64`-native), and not regressed here. Complements #114886, which fixes the `UInt64` argument form in the same function and touches neither `DecimalFunctions.h` nor the decimal cases. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115220&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115220](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115220+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

Every failure is one of three assertion lines flipping `1` to `0`, for example `+normalized nullable 0`. [Sample report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=108431&sha=61e924073e8505f78ac3e3438e2a180a07c740df&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_debug%2C%20distributed%20plan%2C%20s3%20storage%2C%20parallel%29) (`Stateless tests (amd_debug, distributed plan, s3 storage, parallel)` on #108431). The test asserted `AdaptiveAggregationSealNormalizations > 0` separately for each of its three argument representations. That counter fires in `Aggregator::sealPendingChunks` only when the batches one producer buffered together disagree at an argument position, which needs two batches buffered in one producer, both representations reachable, and one producer holding blocks of both kinds. The test pins only the second; the others are a read pool decision and thread scheduling, so a non-zero count for a single query is not an engine guarantee. Randomization is not the cause: it also reproduces with randomization off and with `enable_lazy_columns_replication 0`. This sums the counter over the three arms instead, which is the property the engine does guarantee, and changes nothing else. The three queries stay separate, so each keeps its own value comparison and its own abort site; the `sealed chunks` assertion, the six value lines and the tags are untouched. Within one run the test no longer proves that every representation reached the normalization. `04654` already asserts the sibling `AdaptiveAggregationSealedChunks` in aggregate. Validation: in one interleaved loop the old form failed twice while the new form passed 300 of 300. Of 600 runs, 6 had an arm at zero and all 6 still had a non-zero total. With #115034's fix reverted the new form aborts 20 of 20 with `Bad cast from type DB::ColumnReplicated to DB::ColumnVector` in `sealPendingChunks`. 50 runs with randomized settings and 50 without both pass. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115204&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115204](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115204+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115061 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `Build profile diff` failed on #115061 with a message naming only the `gh` argv ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115061&sha=9a8c54a155a55828cef1e38c76a31aca80038099&name_0=PR&name_1=Build%20profile%20diff), [job log](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/actions/runs/32027518805/job/95431729878)): ``` CalledProcessError: Command '['gh', 'api', 'repos/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/commits?sha=a3f55f04… ``` Two things discarded the reason. `_list_commits_page` used `check=True`, and `CalledProcessError.__str__` renders only argv, so the captured `stderr`/`stdout` carrying the HTTP status were never read. The message then went through `md_code`, a table-cell *name* formatter (`MAX_NAME_LEN = 100`), which cut the tail. So 404, 403 and 5xx produced the same 102-character string, and the walk makes up to 60 calls without naming which one failed. Report it instead: exit code and endpoint first, then `stderr` and `stdout` each capped at 300 characters with an elision marker, in the field order `GH.get_output_with_retries` uses. `TimeoutExpired` is caught in the same place. `timeout=120` is kept deliberately - `gh` bounds connect and TLS handshake but not a stalled response body (measured 240 s unbounded), so the shared praktika helper, which passes no timeout, would unbound a bounded call site. `md_message` is added beside `md_code` for the comment path, bounded head+tail so the end of a message survives. `md_code` and `MAX_NAME_LEN` are untouched, so its 17 name callers are byte-identical. The bound matters beyond `gh`: a cluster query failure reaches the same handler carrying its whole inlined SQL, measured at 54952 characters against GitHub's 65536 limit. The `gh api` failure itself is environmental and out of scope: the byte-identical call succeeds 25 times out of 25 by hand. Validated with a throwaway harness, 30 assertions plus three mutation arms each reverting one hunk: 404, 403 and 5xx give three distinct messages where they gave one, and the success path, the `extend_master_shas` fail-close and the single-attempt contract are unchanged. `ci/tests/`: 711 passed, its 2 failures pre-existing on master. signal.title: Bound submodule cache population so it cannot kill the Config Workflow job
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114811 `Config Workflow` computes the workflow matrix, so when it dies no build and no test job is scheduled. On a submodule cache miss it clones 141 submodules inside its own `timeout=600` budget, and when that does not finish praktika SIGTERMs the job, silently dropping the matrix: the public `26.5` run at `f724d2da9360` recorded 4 checks against 102-155 on healthy commits, and the run still looks finished because `Finish Workflow` reports success afterwards. 7 occurrences over 7 refs in 30 days, including a release branch and three backport PRs. This bounds the clone with `timeout -s KILL` at 600s, above p99 494.5s and the slowest population that currently succeeds (517s), and raises the job cap to `SUBMODULE_CACHE_POPULATE_TIMEOUT_SEC + 600`, 1200s by default, above the 828s worst case (600 clone + 44 tar and upload + 184 rest of the job). Deriving the cap keeps it above the step bound under a per-repository override; were the two equal the job watchdog would fire first. A test pins that ordering. Per @ maxknv's review the step now fails when the cache cannot be populated, instead of reporting `OK` and accepting a miss. Accepting it only degrades cleanly if every dependant can run its own `git submodule update`; dependants clone unauthenticated while this path can use the App installation token, so under `ENABLE_SUBMODULE_CLONE_AUTH` a private submodule is unreachable to them and continuing would schedule checkout failures whose cause is no longer visible. The bound is what makes the timeout reportable: a job-level SIGTERM leaves no result at all. `retries` is dropped because `Shell.check` applies `timeout` per retry, not as a total. Verified by driving the real function both ways: an exhausted budget fails with the hash unset and nothing uploaded, a generous one still populates the cache. YAML regeneration is unchanged.

signal.title: Add a preliminary DISTINCT to UNION DISTINCT
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115104 (auto-closes the issue when this PR is merged into the default branch) Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114550 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115104 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114550 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): `A UNION DISTINCT B` now deduplicates each branch in parallel before merging them, the same way its `SELECT DISTINCT * FROM (A UNION ALL B)` rewrite already did. Previously every row funnelled through a single `DistinctTransform`, so the query did not scale with `max_threads`. ### Description `A UNION DISTINCT B` and `SELECT DISTINCT * FROM (A UNION ALL B)` are the same query but got different pipelines: the rewrite deduplicates each branch before the merge, `UNION DISTINCT` did not. **Root cause.** The union branch of `Planner::buildPlanForUnionNode` (and its old-analyzer twin in `InterpreterSelectWithUnionQuery::buildQueryPlan`) added one `DistinctStep` with `pre_distinct = false`. `DistinctStep::getTraits` sets `returns_single_stream = !pre_distinct`, so that one step both merged to one stream and deduplicated. The `SELECT DISTINCT` path adds two steps. **The change** adds a `pre_distinct = true` step before the existing one, in both planners. `liftUpUnion` then clones it into each branch, which is how the rewrite gets its per-branch distinct. No new setting, no change to `DistinctStep` or any pass. Scoped to `UNION_DISTINCT`: `INTERSECT`/`EXCEPT DISTINCT` share the `is_distinct` branch, but `IntersectOrExceptStep` already resizes every branch to one stream and `liftUpUnion` does not handle it, so a preliminary step there is overhead. Their plans are unchanged. **Measured** (release build, 8M rows/branch, 2000 distinct values, best of 7, `query_duration_ms`): | max_threads | before | after | |---|---|---| | 1 | 60 ms | 61 ms | | 8 | 44 ms | 13 ms | | 16 | 59 ms | 9 ms | The rewrite scores 13 ms / 8 ms here, so the two forms now agree. With all-distinct data the preliminary step is overhead, at the cost the rewrite already pays. A preliminary DISTINCT keeps one hash table per stream, and this one carries the same `max_rows_in_distinct` / `max_bytes_in_distinct`, so exactly as in the rewrite those limits now bind per stream as well as globally; both overflow modes measured identical to the rewrite. The new test asserts the plan shape, not timing, and checks results against the rewrite across `Nullable`, `LowCardinality`, `Array`, aggregate-state and coerced-type branches, chains, `LIMIT`/`LIMIT BY` and size limits. <details> <summary>Interaction with #114550 (measured)</summary> #114550 "Deduplicate the final DISTINCT in parallel" attacks the same bottleneck from the other side and edits the same two functions. Measured on its head `1e783f46`, same fixture and method: | arm | t1 | t8 | t16 | |---|---|---|---| | master | 60 ms | 44 ms | 59 ms | | #114550 alone | 57 ms | 22 ms | 17 ms | | this PR alone | 61 ms | 13 ms | 9 ms | | #114550 + this PR | 60 ms | 11 ms | 7 ms | #114550 parallelizes the final dedup; this PR reduces how many rows reach it. They stack, and #114550 alone does not close the reported gap. It keeps `pre_distinct = false` at the union site, so the conflict is textual only - whoever merges second rebases. </details>

signal.title: Support the delayed set-building step when decorrelating a subquery
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113182 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` error `Cannot decorrelate query, because 'DelayedCreatingSets' step is not supported` for a correlated subquery whose body contains an `IN (SELECT ...)` set. This included queries with no explicit `IN`, because `optimize_inverse_dictionary_lookup` (enabled by default) rewrites a `dictGet(...)` comparison into such a set. ### Description A valid query failed to plan when a correlated subquery body contained an `IN` set. ``` Code: 48. DB::Exception: Cannot decorrelate query, because 'DelayedCreatingSets' step is not supported. (NOT_IMPLEMENTED) ``` **Root cause.** The correlated body is planned by a nested `Planner`, which appends a `DelayedCreatingSetsStep` whenever the body used an `IN (subquery)` set. `decorrelateQueryPlan` has one handler per step type and throws for anything else. **The reported query is one spelling of it.** `optimize_inverse_dictionary_lookup` merely rewrites `dictGet(...) >= c` into a set, planting the step. A hand-written `IN (SELECT ...)` reproduces it with no dictionary, as do `GLOBAL IN`, `NOT IN`, correlated `NOT EXISTS` and the scalar form. Guarding the pass would leave those failing, so the fix is in the decorrelator. **The change** adds a handler for that step, mirroring the existing unary handlers: recurse into the child, refresh the header, re-add the step. The step is a planning-time placeholder whose output header equals its input, and a set reaching the decorrelator cannot reference the correlated columns, since a correlated subquery on either side of `IN` is already rejected during analysis. So it stays where the planner put it, and no set is rebuilt per outer row. **Validation.** New stateless test, both directions confirmed on locally built binaries. Every expected value comes from rewriting the query with an equivalent constant `IN`, never from the fixed binary's own output; the plan is asserted with `EXPLAIN` plus a positive control, since an empty step is optimized out and rows alone cannot witness it. 50 randomized runs pass, as do the `--replicated-database` and `optimize_inverse_dictionary_lookup=0` arms. Sibling issue #112030 is not covered: same producer, unrelated carrier, no decorrelator involvement. If you want the test smaller, tell me which cases to keep and I will trim it.

signal.title: Carry the join analyze mode into a SQL SECURITY view's context
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` losing the join statistics of a view declared `SQL SECURITY DEFINER` or `SQL SECURITY NONE` whose body contains a JOIN. In debug and sanitizer builds the query aborted with the logical error `JoinStep analyzed without the analyze mode`. ### Description The assertion is at `JoinStep.cpp:268`. In release it is compiled out, and the report is then built from statistics the join was never told to collect. `join_analyze_mode` is a `Context` member field, not a setting, and only `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` arms it. `Context::createCopy` carries it, which is why a bare JOIN, a plain view and an `INVOKER` view all report correctly. But `StorageInMemoryMetadata::getSQLSecurityOverriddenContext` rebuilds the context from the *global* one for `DEFINER` and `NONE`, then hand-carries a curated list of caller state onto it, and `join_analyze_mode` was missing from that list. The view's inner joins were planned with the mode off, and the walker then reached them. The fix carries the field across that rebuild: one line, above the `NONE` early return so it covers both branches, beside the existing `setNormalizedQueryHash` carry which exists for the same reason. It is inert unless `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` armed the outer context, and it cannot weaken the barrier the rebuild creates, because the mode selects diagnostic statistics, not identity or access rights. The failure is deterministic in six lines of SQL. New test `04926` covers `DEFINER`, `NONE`, a `DEFINER` view joining an `ENGINE = Join` table (the sibling assertion at `JoinStep.cpp:490`), and an `INVOKER` control. It asserts the statistics arrived rather than that nothing aborted, since a no-abort check passes vacuously in release. Unpatched, the first three arms abort and the control passes; with the fix all four pass, 50/50 under randomized settings. Two residuals. A second fuzzer shape reaches the same assertion through `prometheusQuery` with no view involved; it did not reproduce on either binary, so it is not root-caused. A deserialized remote plan also never sets the mode, but `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` refuses distributed plans. Found by the AST fuzzer: - https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114038&sha=cc2993d762348f09f324efc04cc1c8f43819da3e&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29 - https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114867&sha=f4c473e73f752fa079dc3caec5b0151adefe91e6&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29 <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1654` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: Fix wrong count and wrong DELETE when a NULL expression sits under NOT
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112242 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112242 Requested by @ nihalzp in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112242#issuecomment-5312306258 (reported by @ zlareb1). ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed wrong results when a `WHERE` clause contained a `NULL` expression under a `NOT`, for example `SELECT count() FROM t WHERE NOT (id >= 20 AND NULL)`. Index analysis treated such a condition as provably true for the whole range, so the filter was skipped: `count()` returned rows the query rejects, and `ALTER TABLE ... DELETE` with that condition removed rows it should have kept. ### Description ```sql CREATE TABLE t (id UInt32) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id; INSERT INTO t SELECT number FROM numbers(40); SELECT count() FROM t WHERE NOT (id >= 20 AND NULL); -- returned 40, correct is 20 ``` Reading the rows returned 20, so `count()` and the row set disagreed on one predicate. A mutation was worse: `ALTER TABLE t DELETE WHERE NOT (id >= 38 AND NULL)` deleted all 40 rows, although the predicate is `NULL` for `id` 38 and 39, so those two had to survive. **Root cause.** `cloneDAGWithInversionPushDown` pushes `NOT` to the leaves. For `NOT (id >= 20 AND NULL)`, De Morgan turns the `and` into an `or` and pushes the inversion into both children; the all-NULL leaf is not recognized, so the tail wraps it in a literal `not()`, which `RPNBuilder` complements classically into "provably true for every row". Both steps hold only in two-valued logic: `NOT NULL` is `NULL`, which `WHERE` must reject. **The change.** Before the node dispatch, an all-NULL node absorbs the inversion instead of receiving a `not()` wrapper, the same idiom the neighbouring `materialize` and trivial-cast branches use. It still folds to "never true" downstream, correct because `NULL` is not `TRUE`, and a non-negated `x AND NULL` keeps its exact fast path. Absorbing the inversion substitutes the operand's type for the `not()` result type, so the guard is confined to `boolean_context`, the existing flag for positions where the caller discards the value. In a value position a negation would otherwise change type and drop valid rows. The all-NULL test needs both a column and a type check: `toInt64OrNull('x')` is typed `Nullable(Int64)`, while `if(id % 2, NULL, NULL)` has no constant column. <details> <summary>Validation</summary> Debug build of the base commit vs the same build with the change. | probe | base | with change | correct | |---|---|---|---| | `count() WHERE NOT (id >= 20 AND NULL)` | 40 | 20 | 20 | | same with `toInt64OrNull('x')` | 40 | 20 | 20 | | same with `CAST(NULL, 'Nullable(UInt8)')` | 40 | 20 | 20 | | same with `if(id % 2, NULL, NULL)` | 40 | 20 | 20 | | same with `materialize(NULL)` | 40 | 20 | 20 | | `numbers(100) WHERE NOT (number = 5 AND NULL) LIMIT 10` | 9 | 10 | 10 | | minmax skip index, same predicate | 40 | 20 | 20 | | `ALTER DELETE WHERE NOT (id >= 38 AND NULL)`, survivors | `[]` | `[38,39]` | `[38,39]` | | `count() WHERE id >= 20 AND NULL` | 0 | 0 | 0 | | `numbers() WHERE number > 0 AND NULL LIMIT 10` | 0 fast | 0 fast | 0 fast | | value position, `ifNull(NOT materialize(CAST(NULL, 'Nullable(Int64)')), 0)`, rows | 40 | 40 | 40 | | same with `Nullable(Float64)`, rows | 40 | 40 | 40 | The new test fails on the base build, passes with the change, and passed 50/50 randomized runs. Deleting any one of the three parts of the guard makes it fail again on exactly the arms that part covers: the column test covers `toInt64OrNull` and `CAST`, the type test covers `if(id % 2, NULL, NULL)`, the `boolean_context` test covers the two value-position arms. The unbounded `numbers()` lines pin the positive direction, which an earlier attempt at this fix turned into a hang. The projection, `KeyCondition` and minmax test families were run on both builds: the same 23 tests fail either way, all on ZooKeeper and distributed connections unavailable in this sandbox, none mentioning the exact-count projection or `KeyCondition`. </details>

signal.title: Do not serve min/max from an unusable minmax_count projection bound
signal.text: Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/111938 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `min` and `max` returning a wrong value when the implicit `_minmax_count_projection` answered them from a part-level bound that is not a real row value: a `NULL` in a `Nullable` sorting key, a `NaN` in a float key, or a `Tuple` bound assembled component-wise. Such a query now reads rows instead of using the projection. ### Description `getMinMaxCountProjectionBlock` answers `min(col)`/`max(col)` from part-level bounds, feeding each straight into an aggregate state. That is only correct when the bound is a real row value, ordered as the aggregate orders it. Three ways it is not: - **NULL** (as reported): keys sort NULLS LAST so the top index entry is a NULL while `max` skips NULLs, and the `POSITIVE_INFINITY` pruning sentinel materializes as a SQL NULL. - **NaN**, no `Nullable` involved: the writer sorts NaN above every number while `max` skips it, so `Float64 ORDER BY k` over `(1),(200),(nan)` gives `nan`. - **Component-wise synthesis**, no NULL or NaN: `getExtremes` runs per column, so a `Tuple` bound envelopes each component's extreme and need not be any row. This breaks `min` too. Worse than the reported `NULL` is the silent shape: when the true maximum shares a part with a NULL, `max` returns the largest of the other parts, `4` instead of `200`. The fix declines the implicit projection for such a query, reusing the escape hatch this function already has earlier (`return {}` when a part has no final mark). A part whose bound pair is one repeated degenerate value stays exempt, since skipping it is the right contribution; for an index bound that exemption also requires a final mark, without which the index samples granule starts only and a repeated pair proves nothing. I rejected skipping only the poisoned part, which is the silent shape above, and changing the write path, since the sentinel is needed for `IS NULL` pruning and existing parts would stay broken. The new test covers each class across nullable, low-cardinality, tuple and float keys, ASC and DESC, one and several parts, and a part with no final mark. Issue #104412 is a different defect here, verified unaffected.

signal.title: Reduce the per-arm work of 04895_parquet_dictionary_source_prefetch_lifetime
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114668 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114668 (the use-after-free this test guards). @ PedroTadim asked for the per-arm work of this test to be trimmed. `04895` runs at 93.5% of the flaky check's 180 s per-arm cap on `Stateless tests (amd_asan_ubsan, flaky check)`: p50 141.5 s, p99 165.9 s, max 168.3 s over 50 arms in 21 days of public CIDB, so about 12 s of headroom. No duration breach yet, so this is headroom rather than a live failure. The fixture is larger than the mechanism needs. The detector requires many concurrent queued read ranges alive at throw time, and what supplies them is the row group count plus `input_format_parquet_local_file_min_bytes_for_seek = 1` and the 32 download / 32 parsing threads. None of that depends on payload size. Scaling `numbers()` and `output_format_parquet_row_group_size` by the same factor of 10 keeps the row group count at exactly 397 while cutting the file from 19,785,515 to 2,356,314 bytes. I did not shrink `repeat('y', 400)`: it is a single distinct value, so it is RLE_DICTIONARY encoded to about 0.25 B/row. `key` is 97.5% of the file and `val` 2.5%, and cutting the string width from 400 to 40 moves total bytes by only 18%. Validation. Against a binary with the `resetReadBuffer` override removed, the trimmed test fails 20/20 with the pure-virtual abort at `Prefetcher.cpp:116` in `readSync`, and passes 20/20 with the fix. Because both the trimmed and the untrimmed fixture saturate at 20/20 there, I lowered the thread counts until redness became fractional to get resolution: at 8 threads the trimmed fixture reddens 30/40 versus 4/40 untrimmed, so the trim makes the detector more sensitive, not less. All three oracles are unchanged and were each shown able to redden, `.reference` is untouched, and 50 randomized runs pass. <details> <summary>Measured duration, ASAN, trimmed vs current</summary> `tests/clickhouse-test`, randomized settings, 12 arms each against the same server: | arm | min | p50 | p90 | max | |---|---|---|---|---| | trimmed | 20.03 s | 20.84 s | 21.34 s | 21.90 s | | current | 21.14 s | 22.90 s | 23.49 s | 23.65 s | The serial gain is about 9% because the roughly 2000 row group reads per arm are deliberately kept. The gain grows with concurrency, which is the regime the flaky check runs in, since `allow_oversubscription` is False there and every worker runs the same test: | concurrent copies | trimmed p50 | current p50 | saving | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | 11.43 s | 12.51 s | 8.6% | | 8 | 12.31 s | 15.16 s | 18.8% | | 16 | 12.87 s | 19.44 s | 33.8% | | 20 | 13.66 s | 22.67 s | 39.7% | Server side, reload phase IO drops from 54.24 MiB to 13.99 MiB at an identical 1985 row group reads. These are local numbers on one box and do not predict a contended CI runner, so there is no timing assertion in the test. </details> <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115149&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115149](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115149+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1623` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: Fix THERE_IS_NO_COLUMN for DISTINCT with an aggregate projection
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112168 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `THERE_IS_NO_COLUMN` ("Cannot find column in source stream") for `SELECT DISTINCT expr(k) ... ORDER BY k` on a table that has an aggregate projection grouped on `k`. Closes #112168. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112168 `SELECT DISTINCT v * 2 FROM t ORDER BY v` works on an ordinary table, but throws as soon as `t` carries an aggregate projection grouped on `v`: ``` Code: 8. Cannot find column `__table1.v` in source stream, there are only columns: [multiply(__table1.v, 2_UInt8)]. (THERE_IS_NO_COLUMN) ``` **Root cause.** `DistinctStep` passes its input header through (`updateOutputHeader` assigns `input_headers.front()`), so that header carries the DISTINCT columns *plus* anything a later step needs, here the `ORDER BY` source column. The aggregate-projection matcher was handed only `DistinctStep::getColumnNames()`, so `foldActionsByProjection` emitted a subtree without the extra column, and the splice that must reproduce the step's full header then failed inside `ActionsDAG::makeConvertingActions`. Only `optimize_use_projections = 0` worked around it, because this pass is gated on `optimize_projection` rather than on `query_plan_enable_optimizations`. **The change** passes the step's output header names, the set the replacement subtree is actually required to produce. Matching then declines by itself when a required column is not computable from the projection keys, so those queries fall back to the ordinary read; queries whose extra column is a function of the projection keys keep using the projection. Names are taken verbatim without de-duplication, since `makeConvertingActions` consumes one input position per result column and `checkBlockStructure` compares positionally. **Validation.** Both directions on a debug build. Each arm compares the `optimize_use_projections = 1` result against the `= 0` result, asserting the value set rather than an ordering that `ORDER BY` on a column outside the DISTINCT list leaves ambiguous. Arms cover the reported query, a filter, an `ORDER BY` column the projection cannot produce, a two-key projection, partial projection data, `LowCardinality` and `Nullable` keys, and a repeated DISTINCT expression. Each also asserts via `EXPLAIN` that the projection is still selected where usable and declined where not, so a silent fallback cannot pass as a correct result.

signal.title: Accept LowCardinality(UInt64) as a dictionary simple primary key
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/104539 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `CREATE DICTIONARY` failing with `Incorrect type of ID column: must be UInt64, but it is LowCardinality` when the simple primary key is declared as `LowCardinality(UInt64)` and `dictionary_validate_primary_key_type` is enabled. Closes #104539. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/104539 With `dictionary_validate_primary_key_type = 1`, declaring a simple primary key as `LowCardinality(UInt64)` is rejected: ``` Code: 36. DB::Exception: Incorrect type of ID column: must be UInt64, but it is LowCardinality. (BAD_ARGUMENTS) ``` With the setting off (the default) the same dictionary is created, loads, and answers `dictGet`/`dictHas`/`SELECT *` correctly, with the key normalized to plain `UInt64`. So valid input is rejected. **Root cause.** `StorageDictionary::getNamesAndTypes` compared the raw outer `TypeIndex` of the declared key type against `TypeIndex::UInt64`. For `LowCardinality(UInt64)` that yields the wrapper's index, not the payload's. `LowCardinality` is a physical-representation wrapper, not a distinct logical type, so the validator answered a logical question with a physical predicate. **The change** unwraps one `LowCardinality` level before the comparison, for both the test and the message. The declared simple-key type is already advisory everywhere else: `getKeyTypes()` returns `{UInt64}` unconditionally and every other simple-key site constructs `DataTypeUInt64` directly, which is why the setting-off path already worked. This is the only site in `src/` that type-tests the declared key type. **Exactly one type changes behaviour:** `LowCardinality(UInt64)` becomes accepted. `Nullable(UInt64)` and `LowCardinality(Nullable(UInt64))` stay rejected, since a NULL key is meaningless for a lookup; one-level unwrap gives that for free, and the new test pins it so a later switch to `removeLowCardinalityAndNullable` cannot silently widen it. `LowCardinality(String)` also stays rejected, as a plain `String` key is rejected by design; its message now names the payload. The setting's default (`false`) is unchanged and nothing valid today becomes invalid, so no `SettingsChangesHistory.cpp` entry applies. Noted, not addressed here: `LowCardinality` keys are only constructible on `LAYOUT(FLAT())`, because `DictionaryStructure::getAttributes` strips `Nullable` but not `LowCardinality` and `AttributeUnderlyingType` has no `LowCardinality` member, so other layouts fail earlier with `UNKNOWN_TYPE` regardless of this setting.

signal.title: Do not read the master-only system.parts.files column in 04550_restore_fsync_after_insert
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111378 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115088 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `04550_restore_fsync_after_insert.sh` (added by #111378) read the `files` column of `system.parts` to size the encrypted-incremental-restore fsync assertion. That column was added by 476e9fcb3bb3f26 in January, after 25.8 forked, so the automated 25.8 backport #115088 fails at runtime even though the cherry-pick applied cleanly and the script is byte-identical: ``` Code: 47. Unknown expression identifier `files` in scope SELECT files FROM system.parts WHERE ... AND (`table` = 't_restore_fsync_enc'). (UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER) Code: 32. Attempt to read after eof: value cannot be parsed as UInt64 for query parameter 'files'. ``` CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115088&sha=980e9739e2ff0687cec113ed6460d38af75034f6&name_0=BackportPR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_asan%2C%20distributed%20plan%2C%20parallel%2C%201%2F2%29 The count the assertion wants is how many files RESTORE copies and must therefore fsync. The test already measures exactly that for its first table, with `SELECT path FROM system.parts` plus `find`. This drops the `system.parts.files` read and feeds the encrypted arm the same count. The two tables have identical schema, data and part-layout settings, so their parts hold the same file set; the assertion gets stronger, since the physical count also covers `checksums.txt`, `columns.txt` and the zero-byte `arr.bin` that the checksums map does not enumerate. `.reference` is unchanged. Validation: on the official 25.8 binary the old test reproduces both errors above and the new one runs to completion. On master the encrypted restore performs 20 `FileSync` events against a required 18, and the two arms' part file lists are identical on both branches (18 files on master, 15 on 25.8), so the reuse does not depend on a master-specific layout. Disabling `fsync_after_insert` on the encrypted table still fails the test, so the assertion is not vacuous. 50/50 runs green with randomized settings. Note that #115088 cannot pick this up by regeneration: the backport tree is built from #111378's merge commit, so a regenerated backport carries the same broken line. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1602` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: Bound the storage read output resize by the number of threads that consume it
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed excessive memory usage when reading from `File`, `URL`, object storage or any storage using the generic read path with a large `max_streams_to_max_threads_ratio`. The number of output ports created after reading is now bounded by `max_threads`, so a query over a tiny table no longer allocates tens of gigabytes while building the pipeline. ### Description A `SELECT` over a three-row table can exhaust server memory: ```sql CREATE TABLE t (n UInt64) ENGINE = File(TabSeparated); INSERT INTO t VALUES (1), (2), (3); SELECT sum(n) FROM t SETTINGS max_threads = 4, max_streams_to_max_threads_ratio = 1000000; -- Code: 241 ... would use 36.33 GiB ``` Uncapped, the server is OOM-killed. Found via a ThreadSanitizer out-of-memory report inside `ResizeProcessor` plus a `Server died` / `OOM in dmesg` storm, STID 3538-49e6 ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113382&sha=222f1691027d9ce7299c3ee404e9eea1a603a0d8&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_tsan%2C%20parallel%29)) -- not caused by that pull request, it reproduces on pristine master. **Root cause.** The planner computes the stream request as `max_threads * max_streams_to_max_threads_ratio`, checked only for `size_t` representability. Each storage read that parallelises its output passes that value verbatim to `pipe.resize()`, and `ResizeProcessor` builds one `OutputPort` list node per stream, so the allocation happens while building the pipeline, before any row is read. The ratio over-requests *sources*; it must not over-allocate *output ports*. **The change.** Bound each post-read resize target by the thread width, `min(requested_streams, max_threads)`, at the four sites that decide it: `ReadFromFile`, `ReadFromURL`, `ReadFromObjectStorageStep` and the generic `IStorage::read` (reached by e.g. `Join`, which discards `num_streams` and returns one source). The guard tests the clamped value, so no pointless resize is emitted. `clampClusterFunctionNumStreams` already bounds the same resize for the `*Cluster` table functions. At `ratio = 1` (the default) the pipeline is byte-identical; above 1 the surplus ports were already discarded immediately (table below). One case narrows: a remote read through `IStorage::read` with `async_socket_for_remote = 0`, where the planner requests `max_distributed_connections` (default 1024), now resizes to `max_threads`. That is `MongoDB` / `YTsaurus` / `BigQuery` only; `Distributed` and `Merge` override the plan-level `read()`. <details> <summary>Pipeline widths, before and after</summary> `EXPLAIN PIPELINE SELECT sum(n) FROM t`, `Resize` rows only: | max_threads | ratio | before | after | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | 1, 3 | *(no resize)* | *(no resize)* | | 2 | 1 | `Resize 2 → 2 ; Resize 1 → 2` | identical | | 2 | 3 | `Resize 6 → 2 ; Resize 1 → 6` | `Resize 2 → 2 ; Resize 1 → 2` | | 4 | 1 | `Resize 4 → 4 ; Resize 1 → 4` | identical | | 4 | 3 | `Resize 12 → 4 ; Resize 1 → 12` | `Resize 4 → 4 ; Resize 1 → 4` | </details>
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Copy a table function's AST per read of a Distributed table
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a data race when a `Remote`/`RemoteSecure` table (or a `Distributed` table over a table function) was read by several queries at once. A table function's arguments are rewritten in place while they are parsed, and every query parsed the same AST that the storage keeps for its lifetime, so a concurrent read could observe a partially rewritten argument. ### Description `StorageDistributed` keeps `remote_table_function_ptr` for the lifetime of the storage and passes it, unguarded, to `TableFunctionFactory::get` on every read. Argument parsing rewrites the argument slots in place: `TableFunctionMerge::parseArguments` assigns `args[0] = database_ast` after folding the database name to a literal. Two concurrent queries against the same table therefore write and read the same `ASTPtr` with no synchronization. The raced eight bytes are the `intrusive_ptr` pointer slot, whose `swap` and `operator->` are not atomic, so the consequence is a use-after-free rather than a torn value. `AST fuzzer (amd_tsan)` reported it as `ThreadSanitizer: data race (STID: 3616-438e)` between `StorageMerge::evaluateDatabaseName` (read, `intrusive_ptr::operator->`) and `TableFunctionMerge::parseArguments` (write, `intrusive_ptr::swap`), both under `SelectStreamFactory::createForShardImpl`: [CI report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112928&sha=06fd0bae7343ee9366f79bc6f2563e9f35f8432d&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_tsan%29). That commit touches none of the racing files and the mutation predates it, so it only exposed a latent race. The shard loop is sequential and already clones the query AST per shard, so the racing threads are two concurrent queries, not two shards. I fixed it at the owner: `StorageDistributed::read` takes one copy of the member per call and passes it to all three consumers, and `distributedWriteBetweenDistributedTables` does the same for the source storage's member. That covers every table function reachable through these paths, so no individual `parseArguments` changes. Parsing still rewrites its arguments in place, because that normalization is what a `CREATE` persists: `merge(currentDatabase(), '^t')` is still stored as `merge('db', '^t')`. Reachable from ordinary SQL: create `ENGINE = Remote('127.0.0.1', merge(currentDatabase(), '^t'))` and read it concurrently. Validated under ThreadSanitizer with four separately built binaries: 32 concurrent readers reproduce the race without the change and the run is clean with it, and each copy is witnessed on its own by reverting just that one. The new test covers concurrent reads and a concurrent parallel `INSERT SELECT` whose optimized route is asserted, not assumed.

signal.title: Keep the crash-report channel of clickhouse-local reachable
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed missing fatal-signal diagnostics from `clickhouse-local` when neither stdin nor stderr is attached to a terminal: a crash printed nothing at all, and `--client_logs_file` was never written. ### Description `clickhouse-local` built its crash-report channel and then discarded it: a fatal signal gave exit 134 with empty stderr and no report. `ClientApplicationBase::init` creates a splitter over stderr and binds the signal listener's logger to it. `LocalServer::processConfig` later calls `buildLoggers`, whose loop re-channels every existing logger by name, including that one. The replacement has no console child unless `logger.console` is set or a tty is attached, so the listener formatted the report into a channel with nowhere to go. `local` is the only program that is both a client and a `Loggers`, leaving `clickhouse-client` unaffected. Not CI-specific: the gate keys on `isatty` over stdin and stderr, so a run with neither on a terminal lost crash diagnostics. In CI it made 27 aborts across 7 tests undiagnosable, e.g. [PR 108078](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=108078&sha=a84b136d9ac4980b5ff9457eba8f3dbd3b1d09de&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_tsan%2C%20parallel%29). The channel is now rebound after `buildLoggers`: additively, so a configured log file keeps the report; at fatal severity only, since anything more verbose would pollute the program's own output; and dropping its own stderr child only when the configured console admits fatal records, so the report appears exactly once, never zero. File destinations go last, because the splitter walks children in order without catching a throw. Also fixed, since fatal records now route through it: `OwnSplitChannel::log` evaluated `logs_queue->isNeeded(...)` under `logs_queue == nullptr &&`, selecting the dereference rather than guarding it. Reachable with `--logger.async=0` and no log destination; the guard needs the `text_log` term its async counterpart has. Validated on x86_64 debug with a deterministic abort: stderr 0 -> 8544 bytes with the symbolized report, `--client_logs_file` created, and exactly one report with a console destination, even one whose level excludes fatal. A successful `SELECT 42` still prints only `42`, which matters for the 667 stateless tests using `clickhouse-local`. New test `04916_local_fatal_signal_report` covers ten configurations: 100/100 runs, red pre-fix, every assertion mutated. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115102&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115102](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115102+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix arrayROCAUC and arrayAUCPR returning order-dependent results for NaN scores
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/104763 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `arrayROCAUC` and `arrayAUCPR` (and their aliases `arrayAUC` and `arrayPRAUC`) returning a different result for the same data depending on the order of the array elements when a score was `NaN`. A `NaN` score now makes the result `NaN`. Closes [#104763](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/104763). ### Description Closes: #104763. **The problem.** These are pure functions of a set of (score, label) pairs, so permuting the pairs must not change the result. With a `NaN` score it did: `arrayAUCPR([nan, 0.5], [1, 1])` returned `nan` while `arrayAUCPR([0.5, nan], [1, 1])` returned `1`. No error was raised, so the metric was silently wrong. **Root cause.** Two independent defects in `FunctionArrayAUC::apply`, both reachable from a single `NaN`: 1. The descending-score comparator passed to `std::sort` is not a strict weak ordering when a score is `NaN` (every comparison with `NaN` is false, so incomparability is not transitive), so the sorted order, and the traversal with it, follows the input order. 2. `threshold` is seeded from the first sorted element so the first iteration never increments the area, but `nan != nan` is true, so the guard fires with `tp = fp = 0`, and the Precision-Recall precision term becomes `0 / 0`. **The change.** `apply` returns `NaN` if any score is `NaN`, before sorting. That removes both defects at once, and `std::sort`'s precondition then holds for every input reaching it. `NaN` in, `NaN` out matches `sum`, `avg`, `arraySum` and `corr`, and `arrayROCAUC` already used `NaN` for its undefined cases. Beyond the reported `arrayAUCPR` case this also fixes `arrayROCAUC`, both aliases, the `scale` argument and the 3- and 4-argument `partial_offsets` forms, all affected the same way. The intentional value change: any `NaN`-containing input now returns `NaN` instead of an order-dependent number, including the all-`NaN` case, where `arrayROCAUC` returned `1` or `0` depending on the label order. Infinities are ordered normally, so they are unaffected and have regression tests. A `NaN` label was already order independent. Rejecting `NaN` with an exception would be backward incompatible, so I did not pick it unilaterally. If a hard error is preferred, I will switch. Requested in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/104763#issuecomment-5312328708.

signal.title: Emit IF EXISTS when formatting ALTER ... MATERIALIZE INDEX/STATISTICS/PROJECTION
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114171 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed the formatting of `ALTER TABLE ... MATERIALIZE INDEX`, `MATERIALIZE STATISTICS` and `MATERIALIZE PROJECTION`, which dropped the `IF EXISTS` clause, so the formatted query was not the query that was parsed. Also rejected four `ALTER ... STATISTICS` AST JSON payloads that the SQL parser cannot produce and that formatted into a different command. ### Description `ParserAlterQuery` accepts and records `IF EXISTS` for `MATERIALIZE INDEX`, `MATERIALIZE STATISTICS` and `MATERIALIZE PROJECTION`, but `ASTAlterCommand::formatImpl` never emitted it, so formatting a parsed query produced a different query than the user wrote. The 11 sibling blocks in the same function all emit the clause already. Exactly these three of the 15 scalar `ASTAlterCommand` members fail a format-and-reparse preservation probe on master. The clause is not consumed for these three today, so no execution outcome changes. It is still user-visible: `system.mutations.command` reports exactly this formatted text, and so does the mutation entry persisted to ZooKeeper and disk. It surfaced as an `Inconsistent AST formatting` logical error in `Stateless tests (amd_debug, parallel)` from `02864_statistics_ddl.sql:194` ([CI report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114171&sha=105deb1ebf1fbc5dc4c3749df97ed590c3b9b30e&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_debug%2C%20parallel%29)). That run adds a tree hash over `if_exists`, and a member that is hashed but not formatted makes the round-trip check in `executeQuery.cpp` diverge and abort in debug builds. For `MATERIALIZE STATISTICS` the emission goes inside the column-list branch: the `ALL` form carries a null `statistics_decl`, and `MATERIALIZE STATISTICS IF EXISTS ALL` would reparse as the statistic on a column literally named `ALL`. The parser reads `IF EXISTS` and `IN PARTITION` only in that column-list branch, so on the `ALL` form neither is reachable from SQL, but both are constructible in AST JSON and both format into a different command. `readJSON` now rejects them for `MATERIALIZE STATISTICS` and `DROP/CLEAR STATISTICS`. Two were already wrong on master: `if_exists` formatted as `CLEAR STATISTICS IF EXISTS ALL` and reparsed as a column named `ALL`, and a `partition` was dropped, widening the mutation from one partition to every partition. Validation: the round-trips are pinned in `04126_parser_alter_query_variants` with the `ALL` forms asserted byte-unchanged, the rejections in `04350_ast_json_parser_impossible_field_combinations`. Every new assertion fails on a pre-fix binary.

signal.title: Reload a persisted `url()` table with the storage its creation selected
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104437 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a server that refuses to start after a table was created with `CREATE TABLE ... AS url('http://host/**/', ...)` while `allow_experimental_url_wildcard_from_index_pages` was enabled. Loading such a table's metadata re-evaluated the experimental check and failed with `SUPPORT_IS_DISABLED`, aborting startup. ### Description Reported by @ bacek on #104437, where `Stress test (amd_tsan)` failed with `Cannot start clickhouse-server` after a fuzzer created `url('/**/', JSONEachRow, 'x int')`. No fuzzer is needed: enable the setting, create such a table, restart with the default. Root cause is one defaulted parameter. `ITableFunction::execute` declares `bool is_insert_query = false`; `CREATE ... AS url(...)` passes `true` explicitly (`InterpreterCreateQuery.cpp:2403`), while metadata replay (`DatabaseOnDisk.cpp:117`) passes nothing. `TableFunctionURL::getStorage` computes `use_web_wildcard = !is_insert_query && ...`, so the two take opposite branches for the same stored table: creation builds a plain `StorageURL` and never reaches the experimental check, replay builds `StorageObjectStorage` and does. The check is dead at creation and live only on replay, and metadata loading rethrows. The fix treats a definition arriving with stored columns as a persisted one being replayed, so it resolves to the storage creation selected. The check is not suppressed, it becomes unreachable because the correct branch is taken. Suppressing it would instead enable index-page expansion with the setting disabled and give the table a read-only storage. `ENGINE = URL` was already fixed this way in 64abbdd31d85b15 ("Gate `URL` wildcard experiment check to creation"). Behaviour change: a persisted glob `url()` table that today rebuilds as `StorageObjectStorage` after a restart now rebuilds as the `StorageURL` its creation built. Both carriers are covered by the one change and both are tested: explicit structure, and `structure = 'auto'` via `StorageTableFunctionProxy` (the surface of an earlier `test_url_wildcard_schema_inference` failure). `urlCluster` cannot persist a table. The creation-time check in `getActualTableStructure` is deliberately untouched, since a columns-less `CREATE` reaches it before `execute`. Querying `url()` directly still requires the setting. Out of scope: the check stays dead at creation, so `CREATE` with a glob still succeeds with the setting off. `ytsaurus()` has the same problem by another mechanism. CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=104437&sha=bee15ffc5ec3d2a9b5479bd1fbc197ac6458eebc&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28amd_tsan%29 <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115095&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115095](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115095+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110479 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110479 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `Stateless tests (amd_tsan, flaky check)` on #110479 @ `038667a9c024` reported a single failing leaf `Server died` while its own aggregate said `Failed: 0, Passed: 3872`. The server did not die: no `<Fatal>` line, no sanitizer report, empty `dmesg`, clean shutdown. The `--hung-check` liveness probe failed and the run was aborted. Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110479&sha=038667a9c024695126415fe5f37b76f7a06662fa&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_tsan%2C%20flaky%20check%29 Root cause: `tests/clickhouse-test` collapses every in-band abort cause into `STOP_TESTING_EXIT_CODE = 2`, and the job side appends `Server died` for that code unconditionally. The aggregate stays FAIL, so bugfix validation still counts a hang as a repro. Not claimed: a remaining `Server died` row still does not prove a death. Code 2 is generic, and a worker seeing a `<Fatal>` line reaches the parent through `stop_tests()`, exiting 143 - correct there, but decided outside the carrier. Both touch the same region of `functional_tests_results.py`, so the second to merge needs a rebase.

signal.title: Do not attach a cache writer to a detached file segment
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110029 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a `LOGICAL_ERROR` (`Cache file segment is in detached state`) when reading through the filesystem cache with the experimental `use_reader_executor` setting. The regression was introduced by #110029 and is not in any release, so no backport is owed. ### Description Related: #110029 **The problem.** `BuzzHouse` aborts the server with `Cache file segment is in detached state, operation not allowed`, on two unrelated PRs, first seen 8h41m after #110029 merged. CIDB STID `4043-43b7`, [report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113382&sha=97396ecebc7bcb7ee4d4921c71d1cfdd071a2895&name_0=PR&name_1=BuzzHouse%20%28arm_asan_ubsan%29). **Root cause.** `FileCache::getOrSet` can hand back a synthetic `DETACHED` placeholder rather than a real segment: `getImpl` fabricates one when the covering segment is being evicted or removed, and another when the range exceeds `bypass_cache_threshold`. Such a placeholder is outside the cache metadata, holds no bytes, and the downloader role cannot be acquired on it. `DiskCacheProvider::resolve` classified it as a *writable* miss, because `segmentCommittedEnd` falls back to the write offset, which for a placeholder equals the segment start. It attached a `DiskCacheWriter`, and `ReaderExecutor::readThroughCaches` then called `claimLeadRole` on it, whose `getOrSetDownloader` hit `assertNotDetachedUnlocked`: a `LOGICAL_ERROR`, aborting the server in debug and sanitizer builds. **The change.** `resolve` now emits a writer-less miss for a detached segment, so those bytes are read from source and nothing is cached. The legacy paths already do this: `CachedOnDiskReadBufferFromFile` dispatches `State::DETACHED` to a cache bypass before acquiring any role, and `CachedOnDiskWriteBufferFromFile` skips write-through caching on `isDetached()`. `claimLeadRole` was the only one of the five non-test `getOrSetDownloader` callers reachable with a detached segment; the assertion is a correct caller contract and stays. **Reachability.** `src/IO/DiskCacheProvider.cpp` exists on no active release branch (25.8, 26.3-26.7), and #110029 is an ancestor of none of them, so no released version can reach this. `use_reader_executor` is experimental and off by default; the abort affects the `BuzzHouse` checks, which randomize it as a session setting, plus anyone opting into the experimental path. **Validation.** Deterministic, no fuzzer needed: the test arms the existing failpoint `file_cache_simulate_evicting_segment`, which makes every segment the cache reports a placeholder. Without the fix the server dies with the CI stack; with it the test passes, 50/50 randomized.

signal.title: Answer text-index materialization from the index read task
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109595 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115037 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109595 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115037 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a text index query silently returning too few rows when a part carries a `skp_idx_<index>.idx` file that `checksums.txt` does not account for. The read path decided which columns to read from file existence while the index reader was assigned from checksum accounting, so the affected part contributed no matches. Both are now answered by the same predicate. ### Description ```sql CREATE TABLE t (k UInt64, s String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY k; INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 'alpha'); ALTER TABLE t ADD INDEX tx s TYPE text(tokenizer = 'splitByNonAlpha') GRANULARITY 1; INSERT INTO t VALUES (2, 'alpha'); -- in all_1_1_0/: echo garbage > skp_idx_tx.idx DETACH TABLE t SYNC; ATTACH TABLE t; SELECT count() FROM t WHERE hasToken(s, 'alpha'); -- master: 1, expected 2 SELECT count() FROM t WHERE NOT hasToken(s, 'alpha'); -- master: 1, expected 0 ``` Default settings. The unaccounted file is the corrupted-part shape of #109595; its content is never decoded. Three read-path sites answer whether a text index is materialized in a part. `optimizeDirectReadFromTextIndex` and `getIndexReadTaskForReadStep` ask the index object via `getDeserializedFormat`, which requires the file to be accounted for and decodable. `hasMaterializedTextIndex` instead asked the part for a file on disk via `hasSecondaryIndex`, whose fallback is an unconditional `existsFile` with no accounting gate. An unaccounted file therefore reads as materialized only at that third site: `injectRequiredColumnsRecursively` takes its early return and never injects the base column, no index reader is created, and the virtual column's default expression is evaluated with its input missing. `getReadTaskColumns` already receives `index_read_tasks`, keyed by index name and carrying the index object the reader-assignment site uses. Threading the map through makes the two agree via a map lookup, with no index construction on the read path. `hasSecondaryIndex` is left alone: its mutation and merge callers want the file-existence answer. The reproducer needs one file write, so the test is an integration test (#111922 forbids fabricating part contents in a functional test). I found no pure-SQL carrier: `getDeserializedFormat`'s other two false routes are `isPartTypeCompatible`, where five SQL routes returned ground truth, and `isSystemColumnInvalidated`, which only covers `_block_number` / `_block_offset`, neither referenceable by a text index. The carrier test fails on master and passes with the fix. The `02346_text_index*` and `00990_hasToken*` families are unchanged.
