signal.title: A single test's timeout no longer aborts the whole clickhouse-test run
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/86768 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description **The problem.** `Fast test` on #86768 reported `Failed: 0, Passed: 73, Skipped: 23` yet failed with a synthetic `Server died` leaf. No core, no sanitizer report. [Report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=86768&sha=0927f057854f5e533b8ff833cf200e17db8005c5&name_0=PR&name_1=Fast%20test) | [job log](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/actions/runs/31943974132/job/95177622132) **Root cause.** The server saturated rather than died, so all 24 workers hit the 126 s alarm at once. The first into `timeout_handler` called `stop_tests()`, which `killpg`s our *own* group, shared by every worker and the parent. One test's deadline thus SIGTERMed the whole run, exiting -15, which `ABORTED_RUN_EXIT_CODES` makes the job side relabel `Server died`. The `Code: 76` on `run_r0/status` and the `Code: 159` from `SYSTEM FLUSH LOGS` are downstream of it. **The change.** `timeout_handler` now kills only the timing-out test's own out-of-group clients, via a per-child loop extracted from `cleanup_child_processes`. That broadcast is unchanged, so the whole-run callers are unaffected, as the `--max-failures` paths document. A surviving worker must then report the test, which needs a result built and stamped. The alarm can land before either, so the recovery arm completes what is missing, and `SIGALRM` is blocked across stamping so it cannot run twice: a doubled description matches the leaf pattern too, reporting a nonexistent test. Fast test just has the shortest fuse. This does not fix the saturation. **Validation.** Not SQL-observable. The new `ci/tests/` test drives the real handler and `run_tests_array`, faking `killpg`/`pgrep`: own-group broadcasts 0, the test's own client still killed, `cleanup_child_processes` still broadcasting, one parseable leaf per alarm window. No wall clock. `ci/tests/` is 663/665, both failures pre-existing. **Residuals.** A timed-out test's database and temporary directory survive into the worker's next test, as when the alarm killed the worker outright. An alarm can also be swallowed by an unrelated broad `except Exception`, after which saturation reports `SERVER_DIED`, as master did on every per-test timeout. Both want a private signal type, a larger change. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115061&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115061](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115061+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Record an index's absent columns when materializing it on a wide part
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114990 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112484 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes an unreleased regression from #112484 (`master` only): `ALTER TABLE ... MATERIALIZE INDEX` produced an index that never prunes when the indexed column had been added by a metadata-only `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` and the part is wide. No stable release carries #112484, so no changelog entry and no backport are owed. ### Description Reported by @ clickgapai. #112484 merged on 2026-08-15 and is an ancestor of no release branch, so only `master` is affected. **What breaks.** `ADD COLUMN c ... DEFAULT ...` on a wide part is metadata-only, so the part holds no bytes for `c`. A following `MATERIALIZE INDEX idx` writes the index files but does not add `c` to the part's column list, and since #112484 the reader refuses an index whose columns the part does not describe. The index occupies disk and never prunes: `Granules: 16/16` on the reporter's fixture versus `1/16` before, results correct both ways. **Root cause.** `splitAndModifyMutationCommands` has two branches. The compact one turns an index's required-but-absent columns into `READ_COLUMN` commands; the wide one had no such step, so `c` never enters `updated_header` and `getColumnsForNewDataPart` erases it. The missing type is the defect, so the fix belongs on the write side. **The change.** On a wide part, `MATERIALIZE INDEX` now also reads the index's absent columns, so the part records them at the type the granules were built from. The column list belongs to the part, so it records the column only when every other index holding files there either does not read it or has its granules rebuilt by this same mutation: a carried-over granule keeps its build-time type, so recording the column now would hand the reader a matching type for a stale granule. What the mutation rebuilds is decided from its own commands, and an undecidable index counts as carried over, keeping the pre-fix behaviour. Compact parts and the reader are untouched, so every #112484 refusal holds. **Cost.** The mutation now writes column data: +247 bytes before, +806,931 after on a 200k-row wide fixture; the next merge writes it anyway. No format, serialization or default change, so no `SettingsChangesHistory.cpp` entry. <details> <summary>Validation, rejected alternative, known-unfixed shape</summary> **Rejected alternative:** recording build-time types in a new per-part file - a format change needing ~9 seams, a protocol bump and upgrade/downgrade paths. **Known-unfixed:** on a part with orphan index files (#109595) `hasSecondaryIndex` is true, so the read is suppressed and the index stays inert - the status quo, never wrong results. | arm | absent arm | control arm | |---|---|---| | pristine master | `16/16` (inert) | 1/16 | | this PR | `1/16` | 1/16 | Counts identical with and without `use_skip_indexes` in every cell; the control prunes on both. Four mutation arms cover the restriction, each red on the build missing its guard: without it, a hardlinked granule's column is rewritten at the new type and the next read attempts a 4 EiB allocation; keyed to the index named in the command rather than the column, a second index over that column has its stale granules re-enabled and the next read aborts; without the rebuilt-sibling exemption, a batched update that does rebuild the sibling still suppresses it, leaving the new index inert - covered both for a sibling reached by a named column and for one reached via a TTL target. Tests: `04869_skip_index_stale_type_absent_column` gains cases 26 (the regression), 26b (subcolumn index, absent parent recorded), 27, 28 (two indices, one absent column), 29 and 30 (rebuilt sibling). Cases 11/22/23/24 moved from `ADD COLUMN` to a column TTL expiry, since the fix makes the old route no longer leave a column absent; each gained an `EXPLAIN indexes = 1` refusal assertion, and every such assertion now pins the granule count rather than matching a substring. `04246_materialize_index_force_recalc` (the #104872 compact tripwire), `04165`, `04870` and `04871` pass unchanged; 250/250 across a 50-run randomized loop. Unrelated columns stay hardlinked (by inode), so the mutation does not escalate to a full part rewrite. </details>

signal.title: Do not abort server startup when a database's named collection is missing
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110529 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed the server refusing to start when a database created with `S3`, `Remote`, `RemoteSecure`, `MySQL` or `PostgreSQL` referenced a named collection that no longer exists. Such a database is now skipped with a logged error and the server starts; recreating the collection and restarting brings the database back. ### Description A database whose engine arguments name a missing named collection stops the whole server from starting: `Caught exception while loading metadata: Code: 669 ... There is no named collection 'nc_cfg': while loading database 'db_cfg'`, then `shutting down`. Retiring a `config.d/*.xml` collection and restarting reaches this. Recovery meant moving `metadata/<db>.sql` aside by hand, since the collection cannot be recreated with the server down. A **table** in the same state does not: the server boots and only that table's load job fails, so an admin recovers with a plain `CREATE NAMED COLLECTION`. That asymmetry is the bug. `loadDatabase` runs with `create = true`, so `setForceAttach` is never called and databases derive `ATTACH` rather than the `FORCE_ATTACH` that gives tables their tolerance. The two startup loops in `loadMetadata` now skip such a database instead of aborting, under four conditions that must all hold: the process is `clickhouse-server`, the error is exactly `NAMED_COLLECTION_DOESNT_EXIST`, the database is not the configured default, and its engine is in an audited list of engines owning no local table metadata (`S3`, `Remote`, `RemoteSecure`, `MySQL`, `PostgreSQL`). Everything else is unchanged: other error codes still stop startup, `Replicated` and `MaterializedPostgreSQL` still do because they own local tables, `clickhouse-local` still fails, and `ATTACH DATABASE` still fails loudly. The metadata file is untouched, so recreating the collection and restarting restores the database. The *default* database is excluded because `assertDatabaseExists(default_database)` runs right after. Validated both directions on identical on-disk state: the pre-fix binary exits 157, the fixed one starts and logs the skip. `test_named_collections` passes 29/29 with 13 new cases, plus a `clickhouse-local` stateless test. Each of the four conditions has its own test that fails on a build with that one condition removed, so none is vacuous. The related PR fixes this class for URL **tables**, not databases.

signal.title: Fix the lost wakeup that hangs the BackgroundSchedulePool schedule tests
signal.text: Fix the lost wakeup that hangs the BackgroundSchedulePool schedule tests <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `TEST(BackgroundSchedulePool, Schedule)` can block forever. The unit tests run sequentially in a single binary, so one hang consumes the job's whole 90 minute budget and the binary is killed before it writes `gtest.json`: the job reported 2 rows instead of the usual ~20,285, losing every other gtest's result. `ScheduleAfter` has the same defect. Root cause: the task callback called `condvar.notify_one()` without holding the mutex the waiter uses, and the waiter's `condvar.wait` was unbounded. If the last iteration increments the counter and notifies after the waiter evaluated its predicate but before it blocked, the notification is dropped. That iteration is also the one that stops re-scheduling, so the pool goes idle and nothing can notify again; the wait is permanent rather than slow. The fix takes the mutex around the increment and the notify, closing that window, and bounds the wait at 60 seconds. `pool->join()` now runs before the assertions, because the pool's destructor requires `join()` and a fatal assertion before it would abort the binary on the timeout path. The bound waits on the wait's status, not on the predicate: the predicate overload of `wait_for` re-evaluates the predicate after the deadline and returns its value, so a dropped notification, which leaves the counter complete, would report success and keep the test green on the very regression the bound exists to catch. Validated by injecting a delay inside the waiter's predicate to force the losing interleaving: before the change the test hangs with a backtrace matching the reported one, after it the probe passes, and against that state the predicate overload passes in 301 ms while the status loop fails at the deadline. 50 repetitions of both arms pass in Debug and under TSan. Found on a private-repo `Unit tests (tsan)` run, so there is no public CI report to link. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1526` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: Spill the adaptive aggregator's learning-phase tables under memory pressure
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114987 --> Closes: #114987 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Requested by @ nihalzp in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114987#issuecomment-5307798148. **The problem.** `Aggregator::executeOnBlock` ends in a baseline tail that converts the table to two-level, checks limits and spills past `max_bytes_before_external_group_by`. The adaptive block returns before that tail. Its thaw arm stands down first and its frozen arm runs a drain valve, but the learning arm returned with no memory response at all. A producer leaves learning only by freezing at `adaptive_aggregator_freeze_threshold` keys or by giving up after 16x that many rows, so with the threshold raised neither bound fires inside one query and the table grows in RAM with no byte bound. **The change.** A learning table has no frozen twin to pair with and nothing staged, so under pressure it can stand down for good and spill through the branch that already exists below. Gating it on the pressure trigger matters: the tail can convert the table to two-level, after which `isConvertibleToTwoLevel()` is false and the producer could never freeze again, so an unconditional fall-through would disable the feature rather than fix it. **Reachability is narrower than the report implies.** At the default `adaptive_aggregator_freeze_threshold = 16384` the spill still works, so this needs a raised threshold, not stock settings. The reporter agreed on the issue. **Validation.** On the report's query with the threshold raised, `ExternalAggregationWritePart` goes from 0 to 46, matching the feature-off arm, and under `max_memory_usage = 700000000` the query changes from `MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` to completing. Each new defect cell fails on the unfixed binary, the freeze counters are byte-identical on the fast path, and the two files passed 100 randomized runs. Left alone deliberately: the stand-down reuses `Reason::TooFewDistinctKeys` rather than adding a `MemoryPressure` enumerator, since that field has no readers today; and a frozen local table stays unbounded in bytes for growing states such as `groupArray`, which the issue raises separately. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1521` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: Do not treat an unaccounted skip-index file as a materialized index
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109595 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104431 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a query failure on a part that carries both a `skp_idx.packed` archive and a leftover standalone skip-index file with no `checksums.txt` entry. The leftover file was counted as a materialized index, so a valid query was rejected with a `file_size` filesystem error. ### Description Reported on https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104431#issuecomment-5306256247, on the corrupted-part shape of https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109595 `indexFileExistsInChecksums` says whether a skip-index substream is materialized in a part. When the part carried `skp_idx.packed` it fell through to `storage->existsFile`, which tries the archive and then does a raw disk stat, and that one answer served two callers needing different ones. A read-time probe must not accept a file that neither `checksums.txt` nor the archive accounts for: it is an orphan, its index already dead, and counting it as materialized fails a valid query with `Code: 1001 ... in file_size: No such file or directory`. Mutation cleanup does need the wider answer, to strip the orphan from inherited checksums and keep it out of the hardlink loop; narrowing it there leaks the stale file forward and `CHECK TABLE` fails with `UNEXPECTED_FILE_IN_DATA_PART`. Each caller now asks by mode. One behaviour delta: read-time no longer calls generic part storage. The union answer is unchanged on every part, so nothing new reaches cleanup or `system.data_skipping_indices`. On a Keeper-backed metadata disk that stat reached Keeper with no component set, so the server threw `Current component is empty, please set it for your scope using Coordination::setCurrentComponent`. That is the private-sync failure in `Stress test (amd_tsan, SharedCatalog, meta in keeper)`, whose frames end in `DataPartStorageOnDiskFull::existsFileImpl`: the generic fallback, not the archive probe. I worked from those frames and cannot read the private logs. Asking the archive directly needs no new guard, since its loader already sets a component. This covers every unguarded probe of the class, not just the frame above: the rest of `getDeserializedFormat` is in-memory type comparison. Reachable on defaults: `packed_skip_index_max_bytes` is on and text indices are never packed. Building the shape needs a write into a part directory, so the test is `tests/integration/test_packed_skip_index_orphan`; each case fails on exactly the binary it targets.

signal.title: Fix out-of-bounds read in pointInPolygon on an unbounded bounding box
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/11375 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/11375 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed an out-of-bounds read in `pointInPolygon` with a constant polygon whose bounding box is unbounded, for example when a coordinate reaches `+-DBL_MAX`. Such a polygon is now rejected with `BAD_ARGUMENTS`, and a polygon with an empty ring is treated as having no interior. Previously the query could return a wrong result, or abort the server in builds with hardening or sanitizers enabled. ### Description `SELECT pointInPolygon((1e308, 1.), [(-1.7976931348623157e308, 0.), (1.7976931348623157e308, 0.), (0., 2.)])` reads a `cells` element out of range, on default settings and with no elevated privileges. With libc++ hardening or a sanitizer it aborts (`vector[] index out of bounds`); otherwise it switches on a garbage cell type. Found by the targeted AST fuzzer: [report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112930&sha=27e32067e2142071df32a1cd106e533e54ae645e&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29) (the carrier PR is unrelated to this code). **Root cause.** `calcGridAttributes` validated the derived scales for finiteness but tested the bounding-box span only for `== 0`. `1 / +-inf` is `+-0.0`, which is finite, so an infinite span passed validation; `contains` then computed `inf * 0.0 = NaN`, which compared false against both range guards, `static_cast<int>(NaN)` gave `INT_MIN`, and the cell index overflowed. **Change.** Classify the span where it is computed: non-positive means no interior (`has_empty_bound`), non-finite is rejected with `BAD_ARGUMENTS`. Six lines in the only writer of the grid scales, so every reader is covered at once. `<= 0` rather than `!(span > 0)` keeps a NaN span throwing, as it does today. **Scope.** Only the preprocessed grid used for constant polygons is changed. A non-constant polygon column takes the on-the-fly ray-casting path, which builds no grid and cannot reach this out-of-bounds read; it does lose precision on an unbounded span (`inf/inf` in the edge formula), a separate pre-existing issue deliberately left alone here. **Validation.** Measured against pristine HEAD. Three carriers stop aborting: the wide polygon above, an empty ring, and an empty ring inside a multipolygon (which tripped a boost R-tree assertion). A fourth, an unbounded span on the y axis, silently returned **wrong** answers (`1` where an affine analogue proves `0`). Wide but finite polygons (`1e200`) keep their results. 3 existing tests extended, each verified to fail before the change; the `polygon` suite is green. <details> <summary>Behavior matrix (pristine HEAD vs this PR)</summary> `01940_point_in_polygon_ubsan` changes expectation from `0` to `BAD_ARGUMENTS`: its polygon has an `inf` vertex, so the span is now rejected before `contains` runs, where its `0` came from the query point guard. That guard stays covered by `00500_point_in_polygon_nan`. | statement | settings | HEAD | this PR | |---|---|---|---| | `(1e308,1.)` vs `[(-M,0.),(M,0.),(0.,2.)]` | default | abort | `BAD_ARGUMENTS` | | same, multipolygon / with a hole | default | abort | `BAD_ARGUMENTS` | | empty ring, large point | `validate_polygons=0` | abort | `0` | | `[[[]]]` multipolygon | `validate_polygons=0` | boost assertion | `0` | | y-unbounded `[(0.,-M),(1.,M),(2.,0.)]`, `(1.,-1e308)` | `validate_polygons=0` | **`1` (wrong)** | `BAD_ARGUMENTS` | | NaN span `[(inf,0.),(inf,0.1),(inf,0.2)]` | `validate_polygons=0` | `BAD_ARGUMENTS` | `BAD_ARGUMENTS` | | `1e200` span, `(0.,1.)` / `(1e199,0.5)` | default | `1` / `1` | `1` / `1` | | zero span, point polygon | `validate_polygons=0` | `0` | `0` | | issue #11375 NaN-point repro | default | `0` | `0` | `M = 1.7976931348623157e308`. </details> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1524` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: Fix an adaptive aggregator abort on lazily replicated columns
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111459 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `Aggregator::sealPendingChunks` coalesces several staged mini-chunks into one, concatenating each aggregate argument column across the minis. It clones the destination from the first source and then calls `prepareForSquashing` and `insertRangeFrom`, both of which `assert_cast` every source to the destination's class. That assumes all minis share one physical representation per position. They do not. Lazy column replication is decided per block: a join materializes a block whose replication does not grow the output and leaves the others wrapped in `ColumnReplicated` (`HashJoinResult.cpp`), so one stream legitimately mixes wrapped and dense blocks for the same column. `recursiveRemoveSparse` in the staging path deliberately preserves the wrapper, so the mix reaches the seal and the cast aborts: ``` Logical error: 'Bad cast from type DB::ColumnReplicated to DB::ColumnVector<unsigned long>' Received signal Aborted (6) ``` Two sites abort, both reproduced locally: `insertRangeFrom` for the numeric vectors, which do not override `prepareForSquashing` (the signature above), and `prepareForSquashing` itself for String, Nullable, Array, Map, Tuple, Variant, Dynamic and Object. The fix normalizes the whole `sources` vector, including the front, before the destination is cloned, so one gate covers both sites and destination and sources stay drawn from the same normalized set. The `structureEquals` gate keeps the homogeneous case allocation-free, so lazy replication keeps its benefit where it is uniform, and mirrors what `Squashing.cpp` already does for the identical hazard. Reachable from ordinary SQL: a `JOIN` feeding a `GROUP BY` with `enable_adaptive_aggregator = 1` and `enable_lazy_columns_replication = 1`, both defaults. In a release build `assert_cast` degrades to `static_cast`, so the same input reads a `ColumnReplicated` through a `ColumnVector` layout and copies from a bogus data pointer instead of failing loudly. `AdaptiveAggregation.cpp` was added by #111459 and is on no release branch, so no backport applies. Found by CI in `Stress test (arm_msan)` on an unrelated pull request: [report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110838&sha=db62fd0ad673a4eaf5411e8b75df5b1750bdcb93&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_msan%29), [fatal.log](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/PRs/110838/db62fd0ad673a4eaf5411e8b75df5b1750bdcb93/stress_test_arm_msan/fatal.log). <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1525` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: Give Poco::Net::SocketAddress a noexcept move constructor
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110479 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Performance Improvement ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Appending to a system log queue no longer deep-copies the whole queue when it grows. `Poco::Net::SocketAddress` had no move constructor, which made `QueryLogElement` and three other element types not nothrow-move-constructible, so a `std::vector` reallocation copied every element (allocating per address) while the queue mutex was held, blocking every query that writes to `system.query_log`. ### Description Found while investigating a server that accepted and planned queries but executed none for 3.5 minutes on `Stateless tests (amd_tsan, flaky check)`: [CI report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=110479&sha=038667a9c024695126415fe5f37b76f7a06662fa&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_tsan%2C%20flaky%20check%29). The sampling profiler shows one thread inside `SystemLogQueue<QueryLogElement>::push` for 177 of 181 seconds, in `vector::__emplace_back_slow_path`, with 31 threads blocked on `std::mutex::lock()` in the same call. `push()` appends under `mutex`, so a `std::vector` reallocation happens in the critical section. libc++ relocates with `std::move_if_noexcept`, which falls back to **copying** every element when the type is not nothrow-move-constructible. `QueryLogElement` was not, for one reason: `Poco::Net::SocketAddress` declared copy operations only, and its copy heap-allocates a new `SocketAddressImpl`. `ClientInfo` holds three of those. The fix belongs in Poco because that is where the cause is: a refcounted-pointer wrapper whose move is nothing but a pointer transfer. The moves of `ClientInfo` and the log elements stay implicit, so their trait is derived. `AutoPtr::swap` is used because `AutoPtr` also declares no move, so assignment would bump the refcount and leave the source non-null. Measured over one reallocation of 8192 elements: 32769 allocations before, 1 after. Four element types were affected (`QueryLog`, `QueryThreadLog`, `SessionLog`, `ZooKeeperLog`); a `static_assert` in `SystemLogQueue` now enumerates every element type at build time (30 here, 32 in a cloud build) and fails on the unpatched tree. A moved-from `SocketAddress` has a null `_pImpl`; all seven accessors already route through `pImpl()`, which throws `NullPointerException`, so that state stays defined. Left out deliberately: the slow `query_log` flush that triggered the reallocation is a separate question, and a move on `Poco::AutoPtr` would be the broader fix. This is one mechanism proven on one artifact, not a claim about every `Server died` report. No SQL test, because a C++ relocation trait is not observable from SQL.

signal.title: Commit the recorded file sizes of a Log family write atomically
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/101796 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed an `INSERT` into a `Log`, `TinyLog` or `StripeLog` table that fails while committing the recorded file sizes. Such an insert could keep its rows in the table even though it reported an error, or leave the data files of an array column inconsistent with each other. Reading a `Log` or `TinyLog` table whose array column holds no elements while its offsets claim some now raises an error naming the column instead of reading past the end of the elements. A partially written elements column was already rejected. ### Description **The write commit was not atomic.** `StorageLog::saveFileSizes` recorded each stream's size separately, and each `FileChecker::update` does IO that can throw. A throw partway through left new sizes for some streams and old ones for the rest. The insert had not finished, so the sink destructor calls `FileChecker::repair`, which truncates every file to its recorded size, leaving adjacent streams of one array column at different generations: the outer offsets then described more elements than the inner ones held. A throw inside `save` instead left the files appended but the sizes unchanged, so a failed insert kept its rows. `FileChecker::updateAndSave` now collects the sizes into a candidate map, persists it, and adopts it only on success. `StorageStripeLog` is fixed likewise. The marks file is one of the recorded files, so a rollback truncates it while `num_marks_saved` stayed advanced, leaving in-memory marks that `removeUnsavedMarks` would not trim. The counter is now restored when the size commit fails, on both the insert and restore paths. **Reads no longer trust inconsistent array streams.** `LogSource::readData` already checked the deserialized column's type; it now also checks at every nesting level that the last offset matches the element count, raising `INCORRECT_DATA` naming the column. A short but non-empty elements column was already rejected with `CANNOT_READ_ALL_DATA`, so the empty case is the one that reached the pipeline and the one this check catches. I found the first defect while investigating a `ColumnArray::indexImpl` assertion failure in `BuzzHouse (amd_tsan)` (STID 2508-2944, [report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=101796&sha=628da3c387736525f6398b025afb900437a4f11a&name_0=PR&name_1=BuzzHouse%20%28amd_tsan%29)), where a sort indexed an array column whose offsets claimed more elements than it held. How that table reached the state is still unknown: the failing run's log shows no truncation by `repair`, so this commit path is not shown to have produced it. That is why the read side is hardened too. <details> <summary>Validation</summary> `tests/queries/0_stateless/04931_log_family_insert_commit_rollback.sh` covers the write half over `Log`, `TinyLog` and `StripeLog` and both failure windows, using two failpoints conditioned so they fire on the commit at the end of the insert and not on the empty baseline commit the sink makes when it starts. Reverting either half of the fix reddens it, with distinct symptoms: reverting the atomic commit aborts on `Invalid number of rows in Chunk`, while reverting only the counter restore leaves the table reporting 180 rows where 140 were written. `tests/integration/test_storage_log_damaged_array/` covers the read half for `Log` and `TinyLog`, over three damage shapes: a missing inner offsets stream, which the top-level check catches; a missing leaf elements stream, which only the recursion into nested levels catches; and a partially written elements stream, which fails earlier with `CANNOT_READ_ALL_DATA`. Deleting the recursion leaves the first and third passing and reddens the second. It edits the data files directly, so it cannot be a functional test. The new check was run against 1405 existing tests over `log`, `tinylog`, `stripelog`, `nested`, `array`, `object` and `json`; it did not fire once on data written normally. </details>
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Do not alias pre-aggregation states of a zero-size aggregate in arrayReduceInRanges
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108781 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/108781 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `arrayReduceInRanges` over an array whose elements are all NULL aborts a debug or sanitizer build with `Logical error: 'IAggregateFunction::merge called with the same source and destination state'`: ```sql SELECT arrayReduceInRanges('groupArray', [(1, 64)], arrayMap(x -> (x + NULL), range(64))); ``` Found by the AST fuzzer: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114747&sha=95a67283e1b33c000dba21cddefcd4418c4a2c94&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29 An all-NULL argument collapses the aggregate to `AggregateFunctionNothing`, whose `sizeOfData()` is 0. `Arena::alignedAlloc` advances the arena by `size`, so every zero-byte allocation returns the same address. The function allocates one pre-aggregation state per 64 rows plus one state per range from a single arena, so all of those states alias and both the pairwise level merge and the per-range merge become `merge(p, p)`. The fix allocates `max(sizeOfData(), 1)` bytes for the pre-aggregation states, so they are distinct and every merge still runs. The per-range state needs no padding: that merge only runs when the range spans a whole 64-row block, which is also the condition for a pre-aggregation state to exist, and its one-byte allocation has already advanced the arena. For an aggregate with a non-empty state the allocation is byte-identical to before. I deliberately did not suppress the merge for zero-size states. `sizeOfData() == 0` does not imply that merging is a no-op: `StatelessWindowFunction` is also zero-size and its `mergeImpl` throws. Since the aggregate is caller-supplied, a genuinely empty state cannot be told apart from one whose merge enforces a contract, so skipping the call could drop that enforcement. Two further places with the same allocation pattern are left alone. `ColumnAggregateFunction` can hold zero-size states (the test builds one via `nothingState`) but its `insertMergeFrom` merges across two different arenas. The `Aggregator` merge paths have one reported sighting of the sibling assertion (`mergeAndDestroyBatch`, on #111459) that 15 probes did not reproduce. Release behaviour is unchanged - the assertion compiles out and `Nothing::mergeImpl` is empty.

signal.title: Anchor the Build profile diff master baseline windows on the run's own event
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `Build profile diff` fails closed with `No master baseline with build profile data found - cannot compare` when CI is re-run days after it was triggered, even though the baseline rows are present. Failing run: [PR #113672 @ `494760825`](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113672&sha=494760825526a945d48dd1b90c9965dfd8721df9&name_0=PR&name_1=Build%20profile%20diff). `find_baseline` intersects two sets measured from different origins: the candidates are the frozen first-parent chain of the head's master parent (`master_track_commits_sha`, chain relative), while the row filter was `date >= today() - BASE_DAYS` (wall-clock relative). A re-run replays the frozen event payload, so the chain stays anchored on the old merge base while `today()` moves on, and once the gap exceeds `BASE_DAYS` the intersection is empty by construction. On the run above, `created_at` is `2026-08-06T13:03:49Z` against a `run_started_at` of `2026-08-16T01:28:41Z`: ten days, seven-day window. Eight more sites share the mismatch, so fixing only `find_baseline` relocates the error. Every master-side window now derives from `info.event_time`, frozen with the event, as a closed interval `[anchor - N, min(anchor + 4 days, today)]`. The first-parent walk takes the same anchor and stops a whole upload day further back, so the chain it returns is a superset of what those windows can match. Closed rather than half-open because `date` leads the primary key of the profile tables: the width is then fixed however old the event is, so the window slides rather than grows. The upper bound allows for profiles uploaded after their commit, measured at 4 hours p99 and 85 hours max over 673 master `arm_release` builds. Pull request side windows keep `today() - PR_DAYS`: those rows are uploaded by the run itself. An anchor at today emits the same windows as before, a local run keeps the wall-clock ones, and both fail-closes stand. Driving the job with that run's real values reproduces the error on the current module and resolves the baseline here. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1528` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: Fix a lambda argument taking the type of a table column with the same name
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/103584 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/103627 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes `LOGICAL_ERROR: Unexpected return type from FunctionExpression` when a higher-order function in `PREWHERE` has a lambda parameter named after a table column of a different type and the body reads that column before the parameter. The parameter took the column's type. A parameter whose name is also a generated expression name in the body is not covered. ### Description A lambda parameter named after a table column takes the column's type when the body reads the column first: ```sql CREATE TABLE t (v UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple(); INSERT INTO t SELECT 10 UNION ALL SELECT 20; SELECT v FROM t PREWHERE arrayExists(v -> (t.v != 0) AND (v = 7), [toNullable(toUInt64(7))]) ORDER BY v; -- Code: 49. Unexpected return type from FunctionExpression. Expected Nullable(UInt8). Got UInt8. ``` Renaming the parameter, or swapping the `AND` operands, returns `10, 20`. Reproduced on master 26.8.1.1454; debug builds abort. Found by the AST fuzzer, STID 2458-5396: [report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114721&sha=39164d61335228645d86f6613ff2bb2bfff00280&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%2C%20old_compatibility%29). Root cause: `ActionsScopeNode::addInputColumnIfNecessary` is a name-keyed get-or-create, called by `visitColumn` with the unqualified name (`use_column_identifier_as_action_node_name` is false in `PREWHERE`, mutations and `Merge`). The first visitor to reach the lambda scope decides its type. With the column first, the argument's INPUT takes the column's type, so the body yields `UInt8` while the declared return type stays `Nullable(UInt8)`. #103627 fixes the capture name, but runs later. Fix: before visiting the body, declare the arguments the body reads as a column as INPUTs of the lambda scope, so the name-keyed lookup finds them. The old interpreter does this in `ScopeStack::pushLevel`, so `enable_analyzer = 0` is unaffected. One scope map is shared by all node kinds, so the declaration is narrow: a candidate is matched through the same `calculateActionNodeName` the visitor uses, and a name bound by another lambda, or computed by the body, is left alone. A parameter whose name is also a generated expression name in the body is not covered, and still fails as on master. Validation: `arrayExists`, `arrayMap`, a `tuple()` body, nested lambdas, `LowCardinality(String)` and the inverted case failed before and pass now; `EXPLAIN actions = 1` is unchanged elsewhere.

signal.title: Fix reading a tuple element through a positional Tuple structure hint
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114991 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114991 Reading a tuple element through a positional structure hint returned default values instead of the file's data. Over a Parquet file written as `t Tuple(x UInt64, y String)`: ```sql SELECT tupleElement(t, 1) FROM file('p.parquet', Parquet, 't Tuple(UInt64, String)'); -- returned 0, 0, 0 instead of 0, 1, 2 ``` `WHERE tupleElement(t, 1) = 1` matched no rows, and with `input_format_parquet_allow_missing_columns = 0` the query failed with `THERE_IS_NO_COLUMN`. Silent wrong results, on default settings. Root cause: an unnamed tuple names its elements `1`, `2`, ..., so `optimize_functions_to_subcolumns` rewrote `tupleElement(t, 1)` to the subcolumn `t.1`. The existing guards there consult the storage snapshot, which is built from the structure argument and does contain `t.1`. The Parquet reader then resolves a flattened element name by string against the file's real field names `t.x`, `t.y`, found no match, and substituted a missing column filled with defaults. The fix suppresses the rewrite when the element name is a bare ordinal and the source resolves subcolumn names against a file schema. Named hints keep their pushdown, and storages serving subcolumns from their own metadata (MergeTree and friends) are unaffected. This regressed in #113383 and is master-only: that merge is an ancestor of no release branch and is in no release tag, hence `Not for changelog`. That category also skips `Bugfix validation`, so the reddening check below is the evidence. Validated on a Debug build, with a regression arm added to `04706_tuple_subcolumn_pushdown_parquet`: - Reddening: removing only the new guard term makes the new arm fail while the pre-existing arms stay green. - Preservation: `t.x` pushdown survives for a named hint by name and by ordinal, and `t.1` still pushes down for MergeTree's unnamed tuple. - `04706`, `04707`, `04708`, `04873` pass; a `subcolumn`/`tuple_element`/`functions_to_subcolumns` sweep has no failure absent from an unmodified-master control; 50 randomized runs pass.

signal.title: Allow Map data type for asynchronous metrics
signal.text: <!--- A technical comment, you are free to remove or leave it as it is when PR is created The following categories are used in the next scripts, update them accordingly utils/changelog/changelog.py tests/ci/cancel_and_rerun_workflow_lambda/app.py --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Backward Incompatible Change ### Changelog entry (a user-readable short description of the changes that goes to CHANGELOG.md): Asynchronous metrics can now have the `Map` data type, and the per-CPU-core and per-device metrics were converted to single key-value metrics: `OSUserTimeCPU0`, `OSUserTimeCPU1`, ... became a single `OSUserTimeCPU` metric with a map from the CPU core number to the value (and similarly for the other `OS*TimeCPU*` metrics, `CPUFrequencyMHz_*`, `Temperature*`, `EDAC*`, `Block*_*`, `Network(Receive|Send)*_*`, `Disk*_*`, `*BlobsQueueEstimate`, and `AsyncLogging*QueueSize`). `system.asynchronous_metrics` has a new `key_values Map(String, Float64)` column (the `value` column is `NaN` for such metrics), `system.asynchronous_metric_log` logs them as one row per key using a new `key` column, the Prometheus endpoint exports them with a label (e.g. `ClickHouseAsyncMetrics_BlockReadBytes{device="sda"}`), and the Graphite `MetricsTransmitter` sends them as `<prefix>.<Metric>.<key>`. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/115321 Some metrics are per CPU core or per device (block device, network interface, disk, temperature sensor, EDAC memory controller, logging channel), and they were published as separate metrics with the entity name mangled into the metric name (`CPUFrequencyMHz_0`, `BlockReadBytes_sda`, `DiskTotal_default`, ...). This pollutes the metric namespace (hundreds of metrics on large machines), makes the set of metric names unstable across servers, and makes aggregation across entities awkward. Now each such family is a single key-value metric. ### Details **Data model.** `AsynchronousMetricValue` gains `key_values` (an ordered map from the entity name to the value) and `key_label` (what the key means: `cpu`, `device`, `interface`, `disk`, `sensor`, `mc`, `channel`; it is also used as the Prometheus label name). A metric is either scalar or key-value. **`system.asynchronous_metrics`.** A new column `key_values Map(String, Float64)` holds the values of a key-value metric; the `value` column is `NaN` for them (an aggregate across entities like a sum is not meaningful for every metric, e.g. `CPUFrequencyMHz` or `Temperature`, so none is invented). Example: ``` SELECT metric, key_values FROM system.asynchronous_metrics WHERE metric = 'CPUFrequencyMHz' ``` I considered making the `value` column `Dynamic` (holding either `Float64` or `Map(String, Float64)`), but it breaks the most common query patterns: `WHERE value > 0` throws `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT` as soon as any row holds a Map, and `avg(value)` stops working. **`system.asynchronous_metric_log`.** A key-value metric is logged as one row per key via a new `key LowCardinality(String)` column (empty for scalar metrics). This keeps `value Float64` (and its compression), and time-series aggregation stays natural: `WHERE metric = 'BlockReadBytes' AND key = 'sda'`, or `sum(value) ... GROUP BY key`. The default `ORDER BY` of the table is now `metric, key, event_date, event_time`. On upgrade, the old table is renamed and a new one is created by the standard system-log schema-mismatch mechanism. **Prometheus.** Key-value metrics are exported as one line per key with a proper label instead of a mangled name: `ClickHouseAsyncMetrics_BlockReadBytes{device="sda"} 123` (merged with the configured constant labels; label values are escaped). **Graphite (`MetricsTransmitter`).** Key-value metrics are sent one path component deeper: `<prefix>.BlockReadBytes.sda`. **Converted metric families** ("change it where reasonable"): - `OS{User,Nice,System,Idle,IOWait,Irq,SoftIrq,Steal,Guest,GuestNice}TimeCPU<n>` → `OS*TimeCPU` keyed by the core number (the all-core sums `OSUserTime` etc. are unchanged) - `CPUFrequencyMHz_<n>` → `CPUFrequencyMHz` - `Temperature<n>` (thermal zones, numeric keys) and `Temperature_<hwmon>[_<sensor>]` (name keys) → a single `Temperature` metric - `EDAC<n>_{Correctable,Uncorrectable}` → `EDAC{Correctable,Uncorrectable}` keyed by the memory controller number - all 17 `Block*_<device>` families → `Block*` keyed by the device name - all 8 `Network{Receive,Send}*_<interface>` families → keyed by the interface name - `Disk{Total,Used,Available,Unreserved}_<disk>` and `Disk{Put,Get}ObjectThrottler{RPS,Available}_<disk>` → keyed by the disk name - `<disk>DeadBlobsQueueEstimate`, `<disk>MissingBlobsQueueEstimate` → `DeadBlobsQueueEstimate`, `MissingBlobsQueueEstimate` keyed by the disk name - `AsyncLogging<Channel>QueueSize` → `AsyncLoggingQueueSize` keyed by the channel name Left as-is (small bounded sets rather than per-device breakdowns): `PSI_*`, `NetworkTCPSockets_<STATE>`, per-protocol thread/rejected-connection metrics, `HTTPConnectionPool<Group>*`, jemalloc arena metrics. **Dashboards.** The only dashboard queries that used suffixed names are the four "Network receive/send bytes/sec" charts of the Cloud overview dashboards, which use `metric LIKE 'NetworkReceiveBytes%'` with `sum(value)` per time point. They are left unchanged deliberately: the `LIKE` pattern matches both the old suffixed rows and the new per-key rows, so the charts stay correct and continuous across the upgrade. The Web UI dashboard (`dashboard.html`) does not hardcode any metric names. **Docs.** The metric list in `docs/reference/system-tables/asynchronous_metrics.mdx` is regenerated by `utils/generate-async-metrics-docs`; the columns of both system tables are documented. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=115333&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/115333](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F115333+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Fix data race and silent data loss on the object-storage path list
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/90967 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed silent data loss when several `INSERT`s run concurrently into one non-partitioned `s3`, `azure` or `hdfs` table with `s3_create_new_file_on_insert = 1` or its per-storage equivalent, once the base object exists: the writers could derive the same new file name and overwrite each other's rows with no error. Also fixed the data race on the shared path list caused by the same sequence. ### Description Found by `La Casa Del Dolor (amd_tsan)`, STID `3437-4fb8`, on an unrelated PR: [report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=94148&sha=8eb1df1331f7fd5dcf93b4b0e975e56685b6f732&name_0=PR&name_1=La%20Casa%20Del%20Dolor%20%28amd_tsan%29), [log](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/PRs/94148/8eb1df1331f7fd5dcf93b4b0e975e56685b6f732/la_casa_del_dolor_amd_tsan/stderr0.log) `StorageObjectStorage::write()` read the configuration's path list, derived the next file name from it and published the result, unsynchronized. The configuration is created once per table and shared by every query, so two INSERT pipelines ran that sequence on one vector, which ThreadSanitizer reported in `std::vector::operator=`. The race is only the visible half. The new name is `<base>.<N>`, N from the length of the list the caller was handed, so the list is the name allocator: two concurrent INSERTs derive the same name, find it free, and open it with `WriteMode::Rewrite`, so one writer's rows silently replace the other's. With eight writers, two of nine rows survived. Fix: the concurrency moves into the class owning the state. `getPaths`/`setPaths` become non-virtual base methods taking a shared mutex and delegating to protected `*Impl` virtuals, so all five subclasses and the twelve `DataLakeConfiguration` instantiations inherit it, and `getPaths()` returns by value, since a reference into mutex-protected state protects nothing. Allocate-derive-publish becomes `allocatePathForWrite()` under a second, writer-only mutex, keeping the existence probes off the list's lock so a slow remote request cannot stall `SELECT`s. Three cases are left, so they are not mistaken for fixed: with no base object yet, nothing is reserved and both writers use the base path; wildcard-partitioned writes derive their name in the sink, so writers into one partition can still collide; and two `INSERT INTO FUNCTION s3(...)` queries build a configuration each, so there is no shared list. All three need an in-flight reservation, not a lock, as creating a sink creates no object to probe for. The new tests fail on master and pass 50/50 with the fix.

signal.title: Fix logical error for IN with an identical non-constant tuple on both sides in the old analyzer
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Not for changelog (changelog entry is not required) ### Description Found by the AST fuzzer, `AST fuzzer (arm_asan_ubsan)`, STID 2508-3457: ```sql EXPLAIN PIPELINE graph = 0, graph = 0, compact = 1 SELECT 'null', (SELECT tuple(materialize(NULL), NULL) GLOBAL IN (materialize(NULL), NULL)) GROUP BY ALL SETTINGS transform_null_in = 1 ``` Report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=111552&sha=38215c1758332de1ea8a4b5a620ba8364586f6c6&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28arm_asan_ubsan%29 It reaches the old interpreter through a scalar subquery, and reduces to `SELECT (materialize(1), 2) IN (materialize(1), 2) SETTINGS enable_analyzer = 0`. Release builds catch the exception but still reject the query with an empty identifier name: `Code: 47 ... Unknown identifier: ; there are columns: dummy, 1, materialize(1), 2, ...`. Root cause: a literal's `unique_column_name` is assigned lazily, only when `ActionsMatcher::visit(const ASTLiteral &)` runs, and `getNameAndTypeFromAST` requires it. The old interpreter's row-wise `IN` rewrite visits the left argument first, and here the right-hand `tuple` renders to the same column name as the left one, so `visit(right_argument, data)` takes the common-subexpression early return and never descends into the right-hand children. The loop that follows then asks for the name and type of each raw child, and a literal child is still unnamed. The fix visits each child before naming it. That call site was the only one of the eight `getNameAndTypeFromAST` callers in the file not already preceded by a `visit()` of the node it names. `visit` is idempotent, so the added call is a no-op when the child is already indexed. The abort is gone after the change, with the result now matching `enable_analyzer = 1` on 20 shapes (including `NULL` with `transform_null_in`, `nullIn`, `GLOBAL IN`, `LowCardinality`, array and tuple literal children, `indexHint`, and the query above). 13 shapes that already worked are unchanged, with byte-identical `EXPLAIN actions = 1` output. Removing the added line reinstates the abort. Introduced by #104993 and present only on master, so no backport is needed. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104993

signal.title: Do not drop the whole GROUP BY when unwrapping injective functions of constants
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/104863 (same logical error, closed earlier without this cause identified) ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix wrong results for a `GROUP BY` whose only key is an injective function of constants, for example `SELECT 1 FROM t GROUP BY materialize(NULL)`. Such a key was removed by `optimize_injective_functions_in_group_by`, which left the query with no `GROUP BY` and no aggregation at all, so it returned one row per input row instead of one row per group. Over a `Merge` table that mixes a local and a remote child the same cause also raised the logical error `Chunk info was not set for chunk in GroupingAggregatedTransform`. ### Description `unwrapInjectiveFunctionsInKeys` unwraps an injective function to its arguments and skips constant arguments, so a key that is an injective function *of a constant* unwraps to nothing and is dropped. `OptimizeGroupByInjectiveFunctionsPass` assigned that result unconditionally: when such a key was the only one and the query had no aggregate function, `GROUP BY` became empty and the query stopped aggregating. Under a `Merge` table mixing a child that aggregates with one that does not, the un-aggregated child's raw chunks reach a merge transform that requires aggregate state; both wordings of the message occur, `GroupingAggregatedTransform` and `MergingAggregatedTransform`, depending on `distributed_aggregation_memory_efficient`, and one fix closes both. Found by the fuzzers, e.g. [AST fuzzer (amd_debug)](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=94148&sha=8eb1df1331f7fd5dcf93b4b0e975e56685b6f732&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%29). The fix assigns the unwrapped list only when it is non-empty, which is what `OptimizeLimitByInjectiveFunctionsPass` already does for `LIMIT BY` and what the non-analyzer `TreeOptimizer::optimizeGroupBy` does via `appendUnusedGroupByColumn`. Of those three sibling paths only the analyzer's `GROUP BY` pass lacked the guard. The shared helper is unchanged, so `LIMIT BY` is unaffected. A per-key variant was deliberately not used: it would weaken the optimization when another key survives, and it is the branch added in 462445c2c201a5f and removed the next day in 355909eb3a415b7. `GROUP BY materialize(NULL), k` still groups by `k` alone. Affected queries now return a different row count, which is the point of the fix. Across 25 shapes the patched default is byte-identical to running with `optimize_injective_functions_in_group_by = 0`, where before it diverged on 7 of them; `enable_analyzer = 0` and a plain `GROUP BY NULL` key agree. The old behaviour stays reachable with that setting. The new test fails on master and passes here.

signal.title: Honour do_not_block_pipeline_on_failure for every non-ok job status
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/107115 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/109071 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description A job that sets `do_not_block_pipeline_on_failure` still blocked its whole downstream closure whenever it ended `ERROR` rather than `FAIL`. The two consumers disagreed. `hook_html.py:224` gates on `not result.is_ok()`, so dependees were correctly not marked `DROPPED`. `runner.py:910` gated on `result.is_failure()`, which is `FAIL`/`XPASS` only, so an `ERROR` was never exempted and the job emitted `pipeline_status=failure`. Every dependent job's guard is `!contains(needs.*.outputs.pipeline_status, 'failure')` over a transitive `needs`, so that one token skips the entire closure. The case that hits it: an integration shard exhausts its 7200 s parallel-phase budget and appends a synthetic `Timeout` child while every real test passes. One non-ok child means `force_ok_exit = True`, so the job declares itself non-blocking, but the same timeout sets the error flag and `set_error()` makes the status `ERROR`. That skipped 107 of 175 results on #107115 and 112 of 177 on #109071, including all five `Bugfix validation (*)` jobs. Because those never ran, `new_tests_check.py` read them as `PENDING` and failed `Finish Workflow` with "it's not actually a regression test for the fix", reporting a timeout in an unrelated shard as a verdict on the author's regression test. 8 occurrences across 8 PRs and 5 of the 6 shards in 30 days. `runner.py` now uses the same predicate as `hook_html`, extracted so it is reachable from a test. They have been asymmetric since the `runner.py` consumer was added in `b35b5fd41f28412`. `functional_tests.py:1527` passes the same flag after a path that can also end `ERROR`, so it is fixed by the same line. **Merge-blocking is unchanged.** `ready_for_merge` is computed from `job.allow_failure` alone (`native_jobs.py:1102-1117`) and never reads this flag; all six shards are `allow_failure=False`, so a failing shard still blocks the merge and still reports red. Only downstream dispatch changes. `new_tests_check.py` is left as it is: its strict check is correct once the jobs actually run. <details> <summary>Validation</summary> Every mutation below was applied to production code and the suite re-run. | arm | mutation | result | |---|---|---| | 0 | the fix | 45 passed | | A | predicate reverted to `is_failure()` (pre-fix behaviour) | 11 failed, incl. the end-to-end shard shape | | B | exemption made unconditional, flag ignored (negative control) | 14 failed (every `flag=False` row) | | C | `hook_html` predicate drifted to `is_failure()` | 1 failed (the agreement pin) | | D | output site re-derives the status inline, helper left unused | 1 failed (the delegation pin) | | E | merge gate made to read the flag | 1 failed (the merge-gate pin) | | F | emitted token hardcoded, or overridden after the call | 1 failed each (the emit pin) | Arm B is what rules out a vacuous oracle: a test that ignored the flag would stay green. Arms D, E and F each redden exactly one test, pinning the seams nothing else covers: the call site the extraction created, the token actually emitted, and the merge computation the paragraph above rests on. The new test parametrizes every non-ok member of `Result.Status` (`FAIL`, `ERROR`, `XPASS`, `DROPPED`, `UNKNOWN`, `PENDING`, `RUNNING`) and all three ok members against flag on/off, asserts the two consumers reach the same verdict, reproduces the measured production shape (903 `OK` + 17 `SKIPPED` + 1 `Timeout`), and pins `allow_failure=False` on the six shards. Full `ci/tests`: 972 passed / 31 skipped / 8 failed with the fix, versus 927 / 31 / 8 on pristine `runner.py`. The same 8 pre-existing environment failures on both arms (`clickhouse was not found in PATH`); the delta is the new tests. Exactly two production `complete_job(` call sites pass this flag, and both are covered by this one line. The only other writer of `pipeline_status` is the config job's unconditional `success`. The remaining `is_failure()` uses are test-level row filtering or rendering, not job-level gating. </details>

signal.title: Do not regenerate part names from part infos for tables with the deprecated syntax
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/87206 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/103537 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/112457 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix `BAD_DATA_PART_NAME` ("Trying to get part name in new format for old format version") on a `ReplicatedMergeTree` created with the deprecated positional syntax under `allow_deprecated_syntax_for_merge_tree`. A mutation could be reported as done on a replica that had not applied it, and the table could stay readonly after a restart. ### Description Reported by @ alexey-milovidov on #112457 ([`Upgrade check (amd_release)` report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=112457&sha=f888781eb610bfabdc8c8675d835b99482bec8a2&name_0=PR&name_1=Upgrade%20check%20%28amd_release%29)). No related open issue found. A table created with `ENGINE = ReplicatedMergeTree(date, key, granularity)` uses date-based (V0) part names. `MergeTreePartInfo::getPartNameAndCheckFormat` cannot produce one, because the min/max dates it needs are not part of a `MergeTreePartInfo`, so it throws. Two `ActiveDataPartSet` entry points take only an info and regenerate the name that way; each had exactly one caller, and both callers already held the name and threw it away. This change passes the name at both call sites, as in `536b611c96a757e`, which fixed the `ATTACH PARTITION` instance of this bug. V0 name formatting is untouched, and current-format tables are unaffected because the name-taking overload re-parses to the same info and runs the same insertion code. The linked report contains both failures: - `ReplicatedMergeTreeQueue::getPartNamesToMutate` builds `mutation.parts_to_do`. The throw left it empty, so a mutation reported `is_done` on a replica that never mutated its part, and `mutations_sync = 2` returned success while that replica still served pre-mutation values. Regressed by #87206, which changed `produced_parts` to hold infos instead of names. - `StorageReplicatedMergeTree::checkPartsImpl` builds the set of empty unexpected parts. The throw aborted `ReplicatedMergeTreeAttachThread`, leaving the table readonly. Regressed by my own #103537, which replaced a name-based call with an info-based one. The V0 gap in `MergeTreeData::restorePartFromBackup` that the throw-site comment describes is a different code path, absent from both stacks, and is not addressed. A new stateless test asserts `parts_to_do` on the frozen replica: it fails on master (`parts to do 0`) and passes here (`parts to do 2`), and 50/50 randomized runs pass. `checkPartsImpl`'s state needs parts fabricated on disk, so that half is covered by three V0 cases added to `gtest_active_data_part_set.cpp`, all of which fail with this change reverted. `00062_replicated_merge_tree_alter_zookeeper_long` and `00652_replicated_mutations_zookeeper` still pass.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Bound the waits in 02932_refreshable_materialized_views_1 and report refresh state on expiry
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/105987 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/105987 Requested by @ alexey-milovidov in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/105987#issuecomment-5302349211, after a private-sync run of `Stateless tests (amd_asan_ubsan, distributed cache, meta in keeper, s3 storage, parallel, 2/2)` hung in this test with the active query `select * from rmv_a order by x`. ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description **The problem.** Every wait in this test is an unbounded loop with no deadline and no diagnostic, and some predicates can never become true: the first waits for a refresh to succeed, but with `refresh every 2 second` a failing refresh retries forever, so the predicate never holds and the `exception` column that says why is never read. The test just times out, naming nothing. `-- $LINENO` was also single-quoted at two of the three sites emitting `select * from rmv_a order by x`, and the third had no marker, so the one query a report can quote was untraceable. **The change.** One `wait_for` helper for all ten client-side waits and the unguarded read. Each poll is capped by the budget remaining, a failing client fails the wait rather than being retried as a mismatch, and on expiry the test prints the awaited query, expected and actual values, why the wait expired and `system.view_refreshes` including `exception`, then exits 1. All three `order by x` sites now carry a line number. I bound every wait, not just the two loops I first offered on that thread: the observed hangs pin lines 42, 91 and 145. One wait costs at most 30s (20s polling, then SIGKILL grace and the bounded dump), inside the 60s Fast test cap, against a slowest measured wait of 2.65s on ASAN. It bounds one wait, not the script, since the harness timer is per-test. `SYSTEM WAIT VIEW` is left alone: `RefreshTask::wait` has no deadline and no cancellation check, so bounding it client-side would park a server thread. **Validation.** With a failing refresh armed, the test previously spun silently until killed; it now reports in 20s with the pinned line and the exception. Passing-path stdout is byte-identical to the unchanged `.reference`; 50/50 runs pass on debug and ASAN.

signal.title: Apply a row policy to a read shipped as a serialized query plan
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112891 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix a `SELECT` row policy on a shard-local table being ignored when the read is shipped to the executing replica as a serialized query plan (`serialize_query_plan = 1`, with `process_query_plan_packet` enabled there). Reads through a `Distributed` table with `prefer_localhost_replica = 0`, and reads over parallel replicas, returned rows the policy excludes. Closes #112891. ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/112891 **What breaks.** With a policy `USING y < 5` on a 10-row MergeTree table, `SELECT count()` through a `Distributed` table returns 10 instead of 5 and `SELECT DISTINCT y` returns 0..9. Parallel replicas leak the same way once remote replicas get read tasks. **Root cause.** The initiator resolves the policy into `SelectQueryInfo::row_level_filter`, since a MergeTree table accepts filter push-down into the read. When the plan is built for shipping, the leaf becomes a placeholder `ReadFromTableStep`, which has no field for that filter, so it is never serialized; on the executing node `replaceReadingFromTable` rebuilds the read with a hand-built `SelectQueryInfo` that never sets it. Each side assumes the other applied the policy. **The change.** Such a read is now rebuilt through the reconstructed-query path `resolveStorages` already uses for remote and `Merge` storages. That path runs the ordinary planner, so the policy is resolved in the executing node's own access context, and the read-column widening, the `FINAL` deferral and the PREWHERE ordering come with it. No wire format change and no version bump. Reads without a policy keep the direct path. The initiator cannot make this decision: effective policies resolve per node. **Residual, pre-existing and not introduced here.** A policy existing only on the receiver is still missed where the initiator pushes no policy into the read: storages without PREWHERE support (`Memory`, `View`) and those whose PREWHERE-column contract is not `nullopt` (`Buffer`, `File`, data lakes). Those behave exactly as on master. Replanning them would double-apply the filter step the initiator already shipped, and telling the two apart needs the plan to carry whether that step was emitted. So the fix assumes the shards behind one `Distributed` table use engines with the same PREWHERE contract. **Validation.** Three stateless tests (`Distributed`, parallel replicas, column grants), all failing on master. <details> <summary>Arms run on both binaries</summary> Measured on a debug build of base `63b0a472f4b62ac2` and of this branch. | arm | base | fix | |---|---|---| | `count()` / `sum(x)` / `sum(y)` / subquery, `serialize_query_plan = 1` | 10 / 45 / 45 / 10 | 5 / 10 / 10 / 5 | | `SELECT DISTINCT y` | 0..9 | 0..4 | | parallel replicas `sum(x)` / `count()` / `max(y)` | 548895757384 / 1046417 / 1111952 | correct on all three | | explicit `PREWHERE` + policy | 8 | 3 | | policy on `LowCardinality` / `Nullable` / `Array` / `ALIAS` / `MATERIALIZED` column | 10 each | matches the non-serialized result | | always-false policy | 10 | 0 | | `FINAL`, both `apply_row_policy_after_final` values | disagrees with the non-serialized path | agrees | | policy on `Memory` (push-down refused, must keep the direct path) | 5 | 5, and a nondeterministic policy is applied exactly once | | `additional_table_filters` on the read table, nondeterministic | applied once | applied once | | `additional_table_filters` on a table only the policy's subquery reads | n/a, policy not applied at all | applied, agreeing with `serialize_query_plan = 0` | | policy on the `Distributed` table itself | `ILLEGAL_PREWHERE` | same code and outcome; the message drops its now-stale `serialize_query_plan` advice | | `max_rows_to_read = 1` | returns 10 silently | `TOO_MANY_ROWS`, matching the non-serialized path | | no policy, `serialize_query_plan` 1 and 0 | 10 / 10 | 10 / 10 | Existing row-policy and serialized-plan tests pass unchanged, including `03743_apply_row_policy_after_final_safety`, `04652_prewhere_final_move_skipped_when_deferred`, `03006_parallel_replicas_prewhere` and `03302_analyzer_distributed_filter_push_down`. The new `Distributed` test is 50/50 stable under randomized settings. </details>
