signal.title: Fix an unkillable hang when dropping a low-sorting-name TimeSeries table
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114259 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a hang when dropping a `TimeSeries` table whose name sorts lexicographically below its inner tables' names, for example `` DROP TABLE `-ts` `` or dropping a materialized view declared with `ENGINE = TimeSeries`. The drop self-deadlocked on the DDL guard and could not be cancelled with `KILL QUERY`. ### Description `DROP TABLE` of a `TimeSeries` table never returned and could not be killed when the table's own qualified name sorted below its inner tables' names: ```sql SET allow_experimental_time_series_table = 1; CREATE TABLE `-ts` ENGINE = TimeSeries; DROP TABLE `-ts`; -- hung forever ``` A materialized view's inner name is `.inner_id.<uuid>`, which always sorts below `.inner_id.metrics.<uuid>`, so dropping an `MV ... ENGINE = TimeSeries` hung too. **Root cause.** `executeDropQuery` takes the DDL guard for the inner table, then synthesizes an `ASTDropQuery` for that same table without setting `no_ddl_lock`, so the nested interpreter takes the guard for the identical name again. `DDLGuard::table_lock` wraps a non-recursive `std::mutex`, so the thread deadlocks against itself. A mutex wait is not a cancellation point, so `KILL QUERY` could not land and the guard stayed held for the server's lifetime. `need_ddl_guard = true` comes from one call site, `StorageTimeSeries::dropInnerTableIfAny`, which requests the inner guard only when the parent name sorts first. That predicate is correct and is kept: guards must be taken in increasing name order. Only its comment was wrong, claiming the inner name is "almost always less", which holds for `MaterializedView` but not `TimeSeries`. **The change.** `executeDropQuery` now sets `no_ddl_lock = need_ddl_guard`, so the inner name is guarded exactly once, by the caller, across the nested execute. `InterpreterCreateQuery` sets the same field for the same reason. The fix is inert for the other ten call sites, which all take the `need_ddl_guard = false` default. The `ddl_guard` null check is pre-existing hardening. **Validation.** Both shapes time out before the fix and succeed after, while a high-sorting-name control passes on both builds. Eight concurrent drops serialize and complete and the name is reusable afterwards, so the guard is still taken and released. New test `04920` covers both shapes and asserts no inner table is left behind.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Report RabbitMQ container recreation attempts made by the startup retry
signal.text: Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114415 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114434 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description #114415 made the RabbitMQ readiness waiter recreate a container that fails to start and try again, turning a 21-case module abort into a passing run. When the second attempt succeeds, every channel that could record the first failure closes at once: artifact collection is gated on a failing suite (`if failed_suits:`), the report log strips setup logs from passed tests (`--report-log-exclude-logs-on-passed-tests`), and `job.log` never carried harness logging. The recovered failure survives only as an anomalous duration on the module's first test: +123.5 s against a p99 of 13.4 s over 7774 runs of that test and lane. So a retry-absorbed run discards exactly the diagnostics #114415 added to show where a hang is stuck. Now: - the waiter copies the failed attempt's `rabbit.log` out of the instance directory before recreating the container (that directory is removed on teardown) and emits a stable `RABBITMQ_RECREATE` token. The copy is named per process, cluster, waiter call and attempt, because S3 upload keys use the basename alone; - at job end the script counts those tokens across the per-worker pytest logs, puts the count in `Result.info` and attaches the preserved logs, whatever the outcome. The failure-gated paths are left alone. A recreation is not itself a verdict, so only `info` and `files` are touched: status and labels stay as the test results set them, and the count is appended after the job's own `Failures: N/M` summary rather than replacing it. Forcing a retry on a healthy host passes, and the count reaches `result_*.json` with the 107,336 B broker log attached. The same run with the reporting removed attaches nothing; a run that never retried writes no count; a forced-red run keeps its `Failures: 1/1`. `test_system_stop.py` is 21 passed. Both sides are unit-tested, each arm checked against a mutation of the code it pins. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114947&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114947](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114947+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: -->

signal.title: Coordinate a read with pinned block numbers in classic parallel replicas
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114263 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/97557 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fix wrong results when a `SELECT` with `select_sequential_consistency = 1` on a `ReplicatedMergeTree` table runs with classic (task-based) parallel replicas. Every replica performed a complete local read clamped to the quorum boundary instead of a coordinator-assigned slice, so rows were returned once per participating replica. ### Description `StorageReplicatedMergeTree::read` routes a `select_sequential_consistency = 1` query into `readLocalSequentialConsistencyImpl`, which called `MergeTreeDataSelectExecutor::read` with `enable_parallel_reading` hardcoded to `false`. The setting is propagated to the followers, so each follower took that same branch: `read_task_callback` was never installed, the follower never announced its parts, and it read the whole pinned range locally. The initiator then merged N complete copies. On a 5-part `ReplicatedMergeTree` with a pinned boundary of 12000 rows and `max_parallel_replicas = 3`, `count()` returned 36000 and `sum()` was likewise tripled, with no exception and no warning. It scaled exactly linearly with `max_parallel_replicas`, and `uniqExact` stayed correct, confirming pure per-replica duplication. Reaching the defect requires turning off one of the optimizations that would otherwise bypass this read path: `optimize_trivial_count_query = 0` for `count()`, since at its default the planner serves the count from `totalRows()` and disables parallel replicas, or `parallel_replicas_local_plan = 0` or `parallel_replicas_prefer_local_replica = 0` for data reads. All three are documented, settable per query, and leave the wrong result silent. The fix passes `canUseParallelReplicasOnFollower()` at that call site, exactly as the sibling `readLocalImpl` already does for the non-pinned path, so the pinned read participates in coordination instead of being silently excluded from it. The boundary stays computed and applied: when it binds it comes from ZooKeeper and is identical on every replica (measured on two replicas holding different part sets, 7 and 6 active parts, both clamping to the same block), and with no quorum node it is the replica's own maximum, which excludes nothing it owns. Validation: new test `04912_pr_classic_pinned_block_numbers` fails on master and passes with the change, 50/50 green under randomized settings. Full matrix in the validation-gate comment below. Out of scope, neither introduced nor altered here: the plan-based path with `parallel_replicas_local_plan = 0` (#114263), and divergent part sets with no quorum node (#105710).
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Keep 04896_orfill_merge_group_by_overflow_any on the projection merge path at any granularity
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114740 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `04896_orfill_merge_group_by_overflow_any` fails deterministically whenever the test runner randomizes `index_granularity_bytes` small: ``` Code: 117. DB::Exception: Projection p is specified in setting force_optimize_projection_name but not used. (INCORRECT_DATA) ``` Seen at four different values (7801, 9281, 49209 and locally at 1024), so it reds unrelated PRs' CI (most recently #112889 and #76867), and the arm stops covering the null-place `mergeBatch` segfault it was added for in #114740. A throw is not coverage. The optimizer is correct here. The table declares two projections, and `p` stores four aggregate states where `p2` stores one; granule sizing charges an aggregate-state column at its serialized width, so at small `index_granularity_bytes` `p` reads more marks than the base table and than `p2`, and is dropped (`optimizeUseAggregateProjection.cpp:1036` and `:1048`). At coarse granularity every candidate floors to one granule per part, the marks tie, and `p` wins only because it is declared first. The fix removes both comparisons from the fixture rather than constraining the randomizer: `index_granularity_bytes = 0` turns off adaptive granularity on the table, so a projection's mark count no longer depends on state width. The `sumOrNull` arm, the only one where `p2` is a candidate at all, also names `p` as preferred, which reduces the candidate list to one entry before any cost comparison. `force_optimize_projection_name = 'p'` is kept, so each arm still asserts that `p` specifically was used. `index_granularity_bytes`, `min_bytes_for_wide_part` and `use_const_adaptive_granularity` stay randomized. This matches `04063` and `04365`, the other tests using this pin. Validated: all four culprit values pass; 5 arms x 36 setting combinations (Compact and Wide) pass with the pinned projection applied; 50/50 runs with and without randomization; and the pre-fix binary still segfaults in `AggregateFunctionOrFill::mergeBatch` with this fixture, so the defect stays covered. `.reference` is unchanged. <!-- CI automatic block start :ci_links: --> --- Workflow [[PR](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114943&sha=latest&name_0=PR)] Sync PR [[sync-upstream/pr/114943](https://github.com/search?q=head%3Async-upstream%2Fpr%2F114943+org%3AClickHouse+type%3Apr&type=pullrequests)] <!-- CI automatic block end :ci_links: --> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1619` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: Apply HAVING without aggregation in the old analyzer
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113760 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed wrong results with `enable_analyzer = 0` when a query has a `HAVING` clause but no aggregation: the condition was silently ignored and excluded rows were returned. `HAVING` is now merged into `WHERE` for such queries, matching the new analyzer. ### Description With `enable_analyzer = 0`, a `SELECT` that has a `HAVING` clause but no aggregation silently discarded the condition and returned rows it excludes. Over a MergeTree table holding 1, 2, 3: ```sql SELECT a FROM t HAVING a > 999 SETTINGS enable_analyzer = 0, enable_optimize_predicate_expression = 0; -- returned 1, 2, 3; the new analyzer returns nothing ``` Root cause: the old analyzer builds and executes a `HAVING` filter only in its aggregation branch (`appendHaving` is called under `if (need_aggregate)`, and `executeHaving` is reachable only from inside `else if (expressions.need_aggregate)`), so without aggregation the clause is never applied. What normally hides this is `PredicateExpressionsOptimizer` moving non-aggregate conjuncts to `WHERE`, i.e. a performance optimizer was load-bearing for correctness with no interpreter fallback. It also fails at default settings when a stateful conjunct makes `tryMovePredicatesFromHavingToWhere` bail out, so `HAVING a > 999 AND blockNumber() >= 0` reproduces with `enable_analyzer = 0` alone. This merges `HAVING` into `WHERE` in `TreeRewriter::analyzeSelect` when the query does not aggregate, the canonicalization the new analyzer already performs in `Planner.cpp:2231-2238`. The interpreter, `ExpressionAnalyzer` and `PredicateExpressionsOptimizer` are unchanged. The site sits after `getAggregates` and `getWindowFunctions` so `NOT_AN_AGGREGATE` and `ILLEGAL_AGGREGATION` keep being raised, after `PredicateExpressionsOptimizer` so the default path is a no-op, and outside the `ast_optimizations_allowed` gate so it also applies on shards. Validation: `EXPLAIN` shows no `Filter` step before; after the fix the predicate reaches the storage and prunes (`Parts: 0/1`). 33 query shapes now agree across the old analyzer, the old analyzer with the rewrite enabled and the new analyzer; 20 disagreed before. `NOT_AN_AGGREGATE`, `ILLEGAL_AGGREGATION` and the `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` for `WITH TOTALS` without aggregation are unchanged and pinned by the new test. Distributed and `remote()` queries were checked on a two-shard cluster. The 44 stateless tests setting `enable_optimize_predicate_expression` pass, 589 further `HAVING` and `*analyzer*` tests show no regression.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Share one referenced input subplan across sibling correlated subqueries
signal.text: ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed a query plan growing exponentially with the number of correlated subqueries in one expression when `correlated_subqueries_use_in_memory_buffer` is disabled, which made such a query spend minutes in planning and consume tens of gigabytes. A query with eight sibling correlated subqueries now builds 226 plan steps instead of 6895. ### Description A `WHERE`/`SELECT` expression containing several correlated subqueries decorrelates them one at a time. `addExpressionStep` validates all of them against the header captured *before* that loop, but each subquery referenced the input subplan root as it stood *during* its own iteration, so subquery `k` referenced a subtree already containing subqueries `1..k-1`. When the referenced result is not buffered, the materialization pass clones each referenced root together with the references nested inside it, and the node count doubles per subquery. Measured plan steps for N sibling subqueries (`correlated_subqueries_use_in_memory_buffer = 0`): 415 at N = 4 rising to 6895 at N = 8, i.e. exactly `2^N`, reaching 68 GB of resident memory at N = 8. The buffer is also disabled whenever `correlated_subqueries_default_join_kind = 'left'`, so the blow-up is reachable by changing that one setting alone; `make_distributed_plan = 1` forces the buffer off as well (`SettingsQuirks.cpp`). Found as a `Stress test (arm_tsan)` hung check, where a cancelled `INSERT ... SELECT` sat 426 s in plan optimization with 1,670,597 plan nodes (N of about 17, for a `SELECT` repeating one correlated alias 20 times). CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114072&sha=08c0cd1e799e63d9cf42a2402776fa2ce09c9bc7&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_tsan%29 The fix creates one referenced root per expression and reuses it for every sibling. It is used only when the in-memory buffer is not in play, because the buffer optimization replaces the referenced step in place, and only when the shared root's header already carries the subquery's correlated columns. Both cases fall back to today's per-subquery root. After the fix the same plans are 226 steps at N = 8 and grow linearly. The default buffered path is untouched, and results are unchanged over both settings values. Cancellation inside the materialization pass is still not checked; with the plan now linear that pass takes milliseconds, so it is not addressed here.
signal.author: groeneai

signal.title: Do not run 04726_kill_undrop_table_busy_wait on database engines without UNDROP support
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/56062 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `04726_kill_undrop_table_busy_wait.sh` has no `# Tags:` line, so the stateless runner admits it into the `--replicated-database` lane. There `InterpreterUndropQuery::executeToTable` rejects the query outright with `SUPPORT_IS_DISABLED` before the busy-wait the test exists to exercise ever starts, so the test's own assertion fires with `UNDROP TABLE was not cancelled with QUERY_WAS_CANCELLED`. Deterministic, not flaky: in that check 1771 of its 1776 `OK` results carry the failure text, against 0 of the 27000+ results in every other check, continuously since the explicit assertion was added on 2026-08-09. It stays invisible because that coverage job relabels diagnosed-flaky results to `OK`; the [master report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=432b1ae96183f5b085835f4b0aece8d95ce9ce73&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_llvm_coverage%2C%20old%20analyzer%2C%20s3%20storage%2C%20DBReplicated%2C%20WasmEdge%2C%20parallel%2C%202%2F3%29) that exposed it escaped only because a concurrent server death skipped the diagnostics rerun. That relabel is pre-existing and intentional; noted as disclosure, not touched here. `Ordinary` is a second carrier: `DatabaseAtomic` is the only engine that registers dropped tables for undrop, and `Ordinary` does not override `DatabaseOnDisk::dropTable`, so nothing is put into `tables_marked_dropped` and the undrop throws `UNKNOWN_TABLE`. Both rejections verified directly against a server. All three sibling UNDROP tests already tag both engines; 04726 was the only omission. Validation on one binary: the failure reproduces 100% on the pre-fix tree through the real runner; with the tag the test is `SKIPPED` in that lane and under `--db-engine Ordinary`, and still passes in the default `Atomic` lane, 50 of 50 with randomization. Negative controls (tag names typo'd, or the reason comment kept while the `# Tags:` line is deleted) re-admit the test and it fails again, so the tag is load-bearing rather than silently inert. `Related:` is context only; this PR does not implement UNDROP for Replicated. @ alexey-milovidov reached the same conclusion from the same report in PR 114884, which was closed unmerged over its unrelated `ThreadGroup` half, so this tag never landed.

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109909 --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/109909 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description `test_rabbitmq_mv_combo` intermittently fails `Time limit of 180 seconds reached` on master, most recently on `amd_msan, 6/8` ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?REF=master&sha=236b530a8018049fb73c0417cceebbf346888949&name_0=MasterCI&name_1=Integration%20tests%20%28amd_msan%2C%206%2F8%29)). The run is not stalled: consumption strictly increases at every poll, zero no-progress polls. It is too slow because `rabbitmq_max_block_size = 100` makes every consumer flush a 100-row part, so each of the 5 materialized-view targets accumulates ~2,000 level-0 parts and every merge round re-reads the growing `all_1_*` base part - ~300 times over (final merge level 295-316). In the failing job merges read 124M rows to consume the 693k reached before the deadline (~179x); locally, same signature, 122M rows for the full 1M (~122x), ~96% base-part re-reads. This raises `rabbitmq_max_block_size` to 10000 for this test's table only, matching `test_nats_overloaded_insert` (the same high-volume MV fan-out shape). It reduces the work rather than relaxing the budget: the 180s deadline is unchanged and the `parallel_view_processing` setting from #110224 is retained. `rabbitmq_flush_interval_ms` stays at 1000, so partial blocks still flush every second - measured block sizes stay between 538 and 6168 rows and never reach the new cap, so the test cannot wait on a full block. The final exact-count assertion is untouched. 10000 is still 52x below the engine default for this table (`max_insert_block_size / rabbitmq_num_consumers`). Validated with 12 interleaved A/B pairs on an MSAN build (the failing configuration, same binary both arms, order alternated). Amplification drops 122.11x -> 12.43x with non-overlapping ranges, and the consumption loop the deadline measures is faster in 12/12 pairs (median 77.2s -> 66.6s). A Debug build cannot show this: there merges use 0.23 of 384 cores, so the amplification is free. 9 tests in the module pass, including `test_rabbitmq_flush_by_block_size`; the other 31 occurrences are unchanged. One residual, not addressed here: the test's `SELECT count() FROM merge(...)` poll still scans rows (~590k per poll) rather than using the trivial-count path. <details> <summary>Per-arm measurements (12 interleaved MSAN pairs)</summary> | metric | base (n=12) | fix (n=12) | delta | |---|---|---|---| | consumption loop (s), median (range) | 77.2 (69.1-81.0) | 66.6 (52.0-71.2) | -13.8% | | merge read amplification (x) | 122.11 (120.51-124.50) | 12.43 (10.90-13.25) | -89.8% | | merge rows read | 122,101,440 | 12,430,342 | -89.8% | | max merge level | 295 (291-301) | 25 (20-27) | -91.5% | | level-0 parts per table | 2000 | 142 (117-152) | -92.9% | Level-0 part size is exactly 100 rows for 9,989 of 9,989 parts before the change; after it, sizes range 538-6168 and reach the 10000 cap in 0 of 2,090 parts. </details> <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1551` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: Fix server abort on a corrupt ORC stripe footer
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/114674 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/orc/pull/25 Reading a corrupt ORC blob aborts a debug or sanitizer server instead of raising `INCORRECT_DATA`: ``` generated_message_tctable_lite.cc:228] Check failed: VerifyHasBitConsistency(msg, table) is OK (INTERNAL: Has bits mismatch for Type=orc.proto.StripeFooter Field=1 ``` Found by the AST fuzzer (`AST fuzzer (amd_debug, targeted)`, [report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=114267&sha=08273e65417c8b6a4fe95d2c2cdad899ea17d041&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29)), and reproduced on pristine master with default settings by `SELECT c0 FROM format(ORC, 'c0 DateTime64(3)', unhex('4f524311...524317'))`, so any user-supplied ORC bytes reach it. **Root cause.** ORC's `DecompressionStream` throws where protobuf's `ZeroCopyInputStream::Next` contract requires a `false` return, so the exception originates inside protobuf's parse loop. `TcParser` keeps has-bits in a register-cached local and writes them back only on its own exit paths, so the unwind skips that write-back and leaves `StripeFooter` with the repeated field `streams` appended to and its has-bit clear. Since the v35.1 protobuf bump the generated destructor checks that invariant, so destroying it aborts. `DebugHardenCheckHasBitConsistency()` gates it on `!NDEBUG` or a sanitizer, so release builds are unaffected, hence a CI fix. **Change.** A submodule bump only. ORC's parse boundary now wraps the caller's stream in an adapter that captures anything escaping `Next`/`BackUp`/`Skip`/`ByteCount`, returns the contract's failure value, and rethrows the original exception once the parser has returned consistent. One header covers all nine `parseProtobufFromStream` call sites, including embedder streams such as ClickHouse's `ORCInputStream`. **Validation.** The blob aborts (RC 134) before the change and afterwards reports `Code: 117 ... Read past EOF in DecompressionStream::readBuffer ... (INCORRECT_DATA)`, byte-identical to master release today, so no user-visible message or code changes. New test `04856_orc_corrupt_stripe_footer` passes 50/50 randomized and fails on the unfixed binary with the has-bits tokens. A 183-case corruption sweep and the full `orc` suite show no behaviour change. `ProtobufZeroCopyInputStreamFromReadBuffer` (Prometheus remote-write) has the same shape, but is unreported and I could not reproduce a failure there, so it is untouched.

signal.title: Show why a job failed when it never uploaded its own report
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113382 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Not user-facing: CI report only. ### Description Two jobs on #113382 lost their runner mid-`Run`, and both report pages render nothing, so the failure looks like a 0-second job with no output: - https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113382&sha=f7f79281458bd4558f12725868c0035cbc7b8f5d&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%29 - https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=113382&sha=f7f79281458bd4558f12725868c0035cbc7b8f5d&name_0=PR&name_1=AST%20fuzzer%20%28amd_debug%2C%20targeted%2C%20old_compatibility%29 praktika did detect the failure and record the reason, but three defects hide it. `_finish_workflow` reported such a job only through `env.add_workflow_error(..., source=result.name)`. `source=` sets the `from` label, not the destination, so the message landed on the workflow node while the job's own node kept an empty `info`, and the page renders notifications from the node it resolved, which is the job. The `Status.ERROR` sites in `runner.py` already call `add_error` on the job's own result; this site did not. A job uploads its own `result_<job>.json` from inside the job, so a job that dies never uploads one and S3 answers 403. The page turned that 403 into "Report does not exist or expired" and returned, discarding the workflow report it had already fetched, which does contain the job's node. That early return is gone, and the cached per-job report is now overwritten on every fetch that came back, so a page polling `sha=latest` cannot keep showing an older commit's node. Rendering that node exposed a third defect, already on master: the auto-reload predicate asked whether the per-job report was running, so a null one read as still loading and the page refetched S3 every 30 seconds forever. It now asks the node the page actually renders. The runner loss is not fixable here and this does not try to. A test drives `_finish_workflow` against a stubbed environment and asserts the reason reaches the uploaded workflow report. For the page, a script extracts the relevant functions from `json.html` and replays the measured S3 responses. Reverting any one fix alone reintroduces its symptom; the healthy and expired paths stay byte-identical.

signal.title: Fix coordination mode mismatch with a parameterized view subquery
signal.text: <!-- Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106039 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113622 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/106039 Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/113622 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed `Coordination mode mismatch for stream <table>: got Default, expected WithOrder` when a parameterized view is used as an `IN`-subquery of an ordered query with parallel replicas enabled. A parameterized view used this way no longer plans its inner read with parallel replicas coordination on a replica. ### Description `SELECT ... FROM t WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM pv(id = 'a')) AND id IN (SELECT id FROM pv(id = 'b')) ORDER BY id` with parallel replicas enabled aborted the server in debug and sanitizer builds, and threw in release. Root cause. A parameterized view resolves as a `TableFunctionNode`, so its arguments land in `skip_children` in `Planner/CollectSets.cpp` and the view call survives verbatim into the text sent to the replicas. The initiator plans the outer read in order from the sort key and announces `WithOrder`; each replica re-plans the view body, an unordered scan, and announces `Default`. Both key on the bare table name, so the second announcement reaches the first's coordinator and throws. `PlannerJoinTree.cpp` already guards a view planning its own read on a follower, but it compares `table_node` against the chosen `parallel_replicas_table`, and both are null, so it concludes "this is the chosen table" and leaves coordination enabled for the view. A table expression that is not a `TableNode` is now treated as not chosen, which is always correct: `parallel_replicas_table` is a `const TableNode *`, and both walks in `findTableForParallelReplicas` bail out on a table function. The union-children comparison is skipped for the same reason. A view referenced by name is a `TableNode`, so `parallel_replicas_allow_view_over_mergetree = 1` is unaffected. Validation. The test pins the five settings the divergence depends on, three of which the runner randomizes; each of the four that can vary was confirmed load-bearing by a negative control on the unfixed binary. It fails 8 of 8 randomized runs on master with the reported error and passes 100 of 100 here. Expected rows are parallel-replicas-off ground truth, so each query also asserts `ParallelReplicasHandleAnnouncementMicroseconds > 0` to show coordination was reached. The in-tree view, parameterized-view, trivial-view-pushdown and table-function tests are unchanged.

signal.title: Set the current Keeper component in TextIndexCountSource::generate
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/113295 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Related: #113295 `SELECT count() FROM t WHERE hasAllTokens(str, [...])` is rewritten by the trivial-count-from-text-index optimization into a `ReadFromTextIndexCount` step (added in #111494). Its source runs on a pipeline execution thread: `TextIndexCountSource::generate` -> `computeCountForPart` -> `makeTextIndexInputStream` -> `IMergeTreeDataPart::getStreamNameOrHash(..., IDataPartStorage &)`, whose body probes the part storage with `existsFile`. On a disk that keeps part metadata in Keeper that probe is a real Keeper request, and `Coordination::ZooKeeper::pushRequest` throws `LOGICAL_ERROR` when no component is set for the scope. `generate()` is the outermost scope this step owns on that thread, and it set none: the step builds its own `Pipe`, so unlike the ordinary read path it never inherits the guard from `MergeTreeSource::tryGenerate`. This adds the one-line RAII guard at the top of `generate()`. The guard is a nesting-safe thread-local stack and every Keeper-reaching call above is a descendant of that scope, so no deeper placement is needed. Same shape as #113295 for `MergeTreeCodecBlockCountsSource::generate` and the sibling `MergeTreeTextIndexSource::generate`. Of the four callers of `makeTextIndexInputStream`, the other three already have an ancestor guard (`MergeTreeSource::tryGenerate` for both `MergeTreeReaderTextIndex` sites, the mutate/merge task guards for `MergeTextIndexesTask`); this step was the only gap. Category is `CI Fix or Improvement`, as in #113295 and #113386: the metadata-in-Keeper storage type is registered only under `#if CLICKHOUSE_CLOUD`, and `LOGICAL_ERROR` aborts only in debug and sanitizer builds, so this cannot happen in an official stable build. For the same reason no test is added: no public build reaches Keeper through `existsFile`. Validated with the existing `02346_text_index*` suite (plus 50/50 randomized runs of `02346_text_index_optimize_trivial_count`), an `EXPLAIN` assertion that the modified scope is the one the query executes, and a run with `enforce_keeper_component_tracking = 1`. Left alone: the plan-time `getDeserializedFormat` path can also reach `existsFile` for packed skip-index parts and is likewise unguarded, but it predates this step by three weeks and is not this failure's carrier.

signal.title: Scope WITH aliases to the SELECT that declares them when adding the default database
signal.text: Scope WITH aliases to the SELECT that declares them when adding the default database <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/104972 --> Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/104972 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixed table names not being qualified with the default database when a `WITH` alias elsewhere in the same query happened to share the name. `ALTER TABLE other_db.t UPDATE v = (WITH RECURSIVE src AS (SELECT 7 AS id) SELECT max(id) FROM src) + (SELECT max(id) FROM src)` failed with `UNKNOWN_DATABASE`, the same expression through `UPDATE ... SET` silently read the session's `src` instead of `other_db.src`, and a view whose `UNION` branch referenced such a table could not be read from another database. Closes #104972. ### Description `AddDefaultDatabaseVisitor` records `WITH RECURSIVE` aliases so it does not qualify a name that is a CTE rather than a table. That record was one set shared by the whole visitor instance and never cleared, so an alias declared inside one `SELECT` kept suppressing qualification for every identifier seen afterwards, including a genuine physical table. The leak is forward-only: a colliding name before the CTE is fine. The set becomes a stack of scopes, one pushed per `ASTSelectQuery` and popped by a destructor, so a `SELECT`'s subtree inherits the enclosing aliases and nothing outside it does. Lookups walk it innermost-first. Three cases follow: - The `WITH` list is now walked in the non-recursive case too. A recursive alias is registered before its element is visited, since it may reference itself; a plain alias after, so inside its own definition the name still denotes a table. This mirrors `ApplyWithSubqueryVisitor`, and matters because `ApplyWithGlobalVisitor` copies a first branch's `WITH` list into later `UNION` branches without the `RECURSIVE` flag. - Enclosing scopes are searched for a plain name only when `enable_global_with_statement` is set, matching the resolver: without it the analyzer clears `allow_to_check_cte` for parent scopes. A recursive name is searched unconditionally, since its self-reference resolves inside its own definition. The setting is read per `SELECT`, by replaying the clauses reaching it as `QueryTreeBuilder` does, so a repeated setting takes its last value and `compatibility` is honoured. - `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY QUERY` and `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW` expand a plain CTE reference into a copy of its body first. Inside that copy the name denotes a table, so that binding is masked. Fixing the visitor covers all 13 construction sites at once. Validated on 40 arms, with eight mutants pinning the scope stack, the clone mask, the registration and lookup order, and the setting handling.

signal.title: Do not abort the server when a loader worker cannot be spawned
signal.text: <!-- Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110174 --> ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a server abort that happens when the global thread pool is momentarily saturated while tables are still loading. `AsyncLoader` now keeps running if it cannot spawn an extra loader worker and some worker will still drain the queued jobs, instead of calling `std::terminate`. ### Description `AsyncLoader::spawn` wrapped `scheduleOrThrowOnError` in `NOEXCEPT_SCOPE`, whose handler is unconditionally `std::terminate()`. A transient `CANNOT_SCHEDULE_TASK` from a saturated global thread pool therefore killed the server (`Received signal 6`) during table loading. Seen 4 times over 4 unrelated PRs and 4 build flavours in 30 days, e.g. [`Stress test (arm_tsan)`](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=108468&sha=27a154474608ee82636207020a9bd13beb8c9449&name_0=PR&name_1=Stress%20test%20%28arm_tsan%29), whose stack is `terminate_handler()` -> `std::terminate()` -> `AsyncLoader.cpp:908` `spawn()` -> `:744` `enqueue()`. A spawn must succeed only when nothing else will drain the pool's ready queue, so it now tells three states apart: - a worker that entered `worker()` and is not inside `wait()` drains the queue now; - a worker inside `wait()` on *another* pool's job resumes draining once that job runs; - neither of those means nobody ever will. In the first two cases `spawn` uses the non-throwing `trySchedule`, rolls back its `Pool::workers` increment on failure, warns and returns false. Only the last case keeps the fatal path, byte for byte: the queued jobs would be stranded, and throwing is not an option because `schedule` marks that region non-exception-safe. Covering it needs rollback-and-retry across the loading DAG, out of scope here. All 4 observed rows are recoverable. `BackgroundSchedulePool` narrows the same way (`929227464f9736b`). Two counters are added because `Pool::workers` also counts a worker still queued in the global pool, which drains nothing, and one blocked in `wait()`, which cannot take its own pool's jobs. A saturated pool is remembered so the failing thread creation happens once per episode, not once per queued job, counted by the new `AsyncLoaderSpawnFailures` event; entering `wait()` clears the memo. Tests are gtests asserting which branch was taken, not just that the process survived. A SQL test cannot reach the line: on master the whole call sits under `blockFaultInjections()`. Related: #110174, which removed the mask that hid this exception. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Backported to: `26.7.4.53` <!-- ch-version-info:end -->

signal.title: Hold the table lock across a lightweight UPDATE pipeline
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/104431 ### Changelog category (leave one): - Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): Fixes a server abort (`Logical error: Part patch-... doesn't exist`) when a `DROP TABLE` runs concurrently with a lightweight `UPDATE` on a `ReplicatedMergeTree` table. The update now holds the table's shared lock until its patch part is committed, so the `DROP` waits instead of removing it. ### Description Reported by @ alexey-milovidov on #104431: an `Upgrade check (amd_release)` abort with no fix on master, STID `3208-458f`, 4 hits on 4 unrelated PRs in 6 days ([report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=104431&sha=7970f08a82eaf2ad5217d57a7796ae1c5e920030&name_0=PR&name_1=Upgrade+check+%28amd_release%29)). **What breaks.** A lightweight `UPDATE` racing a `DROP TABLE` aborts the server, release builds included: `Transaction::commit`'s `modifyPartState` sits in `NOEXCEPT_SCOPE`, whose catch-all is `std::terminate`. **Root cause.** `InterpreterUpdateQuery::execute` takes `lockForShare` into a function-local holder and parks only the *storage* in the returned pipeline; `QueryPlanResourceHolder` keeps `storage_holders` and `table_locks` separately, so the lock dies when `execute()` returns, long before the sink commits the patch part. A concurrent `DROP` then takes the exclusive lock, `dropAllData()` clears `data_parts_indexes`, and the commit cannot find its own part. It needs a UUID-less database (`Memory`/`Ordinary`), where `DROP` removes data inline, hence the intermittency. **The change.** Move the already-acquired lock into the pipeline's resources, as the INSERT path does at `InterpreterInsertQuery.cpp:1297`. Three entry points: `InterpreterUpdateQuery::execute`, `InterpreterAlterQuery::executeToTable`, and `StorageAlias::updateLightweight`, which resolves a *different* storage and so needs the target's own lock, as `StorageAlias::read` does. `DELETE FROM` rewrites to `UPDATE` and is covered transitively. A concurrent `DROP` or `DETACH` now waits for an in-flight lightweight update, as it already does for `INSERT`. `TRUNCATE` takes no exclusive lock for `MergeTree`. **Validation.** New test `04905_lwu_drop_race_table_lock.sh`, one arm per fixed carrier. A pauseable failpoint parks the replicated sink between the patch-part rename and the commit, while the update still holds the lock; the arm then drops the table and waits for the drop to block on that lock. Nothing is timed, so an arm cannot miss a window or pass quietly. Aborts without the fix, passes with it, 50/50 green. <details> <summary>Both-directions matrix (every cell measured, Build IDs asserted against the running server)</summary> | binary | `UPDATE` | `ALTER ... UPDATE` | via `Alias` | |---|---|---|---| | base (fix reverted) `ea8e869d` | ABORT | ABORT | ABORT | | interpreters only `3651f11d` | pass | pass | ABORT | | full fix `1884b944` | pass | pass | pass | The middle row is the control that shows the `StorageAlias` change is necessary: with both interpreter fixes applied, the alias arm is the only one that still aborts. The lock demonstrably serializes the two queries: with the sink parked after the patch-part rename, the `DROP` becomes a waiting writer and stays one until the sink is released, then completes. Deadlock check: the change only extends the lifetime of a *Read* acquisition, and no sink on this path takes the table lock. `update_sequential_consistency = 1` and a following `OPTIMIZE TABLE ... FINAL` both complete normally. </details>

signal.title: Fix flaky 00632_get_sample_block_cache (300s timeout under TSAN)
signal.text: <!-- Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need. --> Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/41240 ### Changelog category (leave one): - CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required) ### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md): ... ### Description Seen under `Stateless tests (amd_tsan, parallel)`: ``` Code: 159. DB::Exception: Timeout exceeded: elapsed 300200.551 ms, maximum: 300000 ms. (TIMEOUT_EXCEEDED) (query 20, line 69) ``` [CI report](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/PRs/114731/a5daee0848c43176efa72907a99ab173c49a6297/result_pr.json) **Root cause.** The bound that fires is the test's own `SET max_execution_time = 300`, and it sits at the top of the healthy distribution. Nothing else bounds the query: the server default is unlimited, and `tests/config` sets the setting only in `users.d/limits_fast.yaml`, linked for Fast test alone (`install.sh:293`). Measured on this check over the 90 days to 2026-08-14, n = 12736 passing runs: p50 23.4 s, p99 128 s, max 289.1 s, so 4% headroom. TSAN plus parallel-suite contention supplies the rest. Three CIDB timeouts share the signature, one on master. **Change.** I cut the fixture's row volume only (`LIMIT 65536` to `LIMIT 4096`); `4095` asserts the same `distinct x > 0` property `65535` did. Query-20 cost is row-linear over a fixed ~50 ms analysis floor (medians 655 ms at 65536 rows, 108 ms at 4096), and the cache under test is keyed on query text, so cutting rows removes execution noise only. All 100 `UNION ALL` branches, `max_threads = 32`, the 300 s bound and all four tags stay, and `EXPLAIN PIPELINE` is byte-identical. Sensitivity drops from ~13x the p50 to ~150x; the regression it names, its own "tens of minutes", is still caught. **Validation.** The failure is contention-driven and does not reproduce on an idle box, so I proved the mechanism deterministically: with the oracle tightened to 0.3 s, between the two medians, the unchanged file fails with the exact CI signature and the fixed file passes. 200 further runs pass across both files, randomization on and off. Side note, not fixed here: under this test's `enable_analyzer = 1` query 20 never reaches the sample-block cache, which only `InterpreterSelectWithUnionQuery` reads. <!-- ch-version-info:start --> ### Version info - Merged into: `26.8.1.1441` (included in `26.8` and later) <!-- ch-version-info:end -->
